title: 湯姆歷險記
author: Mark Twain 馬克·吐溫
description: 《The Adventures of Tom Sawyer》(1876)。密西西比河畔小鎮聖彼得堡,頑皮機靈的湯姆·索亞與哈克貝利·費恩闖過墓地目擊命案、扮海盜、尋寶、迷失山洞的種種歷險。英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: Preface 序言

passages.original: CH Most of the adventures recorded in this book really occurred; one or two were experiences of my own, the rest those of boys who were schoolmates of mine.
passages.vernacular: 呢本書裡記載嘅大部分冒險確實發生過;有一兩件係我自己嘅經歷,其餘係我同學嘅經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這本書裡記載的大部分冒險確實發生過;有一兩件是我自己的經歷,其餘是我同學的經歷。

passages.original: Huck Finn is drawn from life; Tom Sawyer also, but not from an individual—he is a combination of the characteristics of three boys whom I knew, and therefore belongs to the composite order of architecture.
passages.vernacular: 哈克·費恩係根據生活中嘅人寫嘅;湯姆·索亞都係,但唔係來自某一個人——佢係我認識嘅三個男孩嘅特點嘅結合,因此屬於混合式建築嘅類型。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克·費恩是根據生活中的人寫的;湯姆·索亞也是,但不是來自某一個人——他是我認識的三個男孩的特點的結合,因此屬於混合式建築的類型。

passages.original: The odd superstitions touched upon were all prevalent among children and slaves in the West at the period of this story—that is to say, thirty or forty years ago.
passages.vernacular: 書中提到嘅嗰啲古怪迷信,喺本故事所處嘅時代——都就係三四十年前——西部嘅細路哋同奴隸哋中間都好流行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 書中提到的那些古怪迷信,在本故事所處的時代——也就是三四十年前——西部的孩子們和奴隸們中間都很流行。

passages.original: Although my book is intended mainly for the entertainment of boys and girls, I hope it will not be shunned by men and women on that account, for part of my plan has been to try to pleasantly remind adults of what they once were themselves, and of how they felt and thought and talked, and what queer enterprises they sometimes engaged in.
passages.vernacular: 雖然我嘅書主要係為了畀男孩女孩消遣而寫,我希望男人女人唔會因此而迴避佢,因為我嘅計畫嘅一部分,係試圖愉快地提醒成年人佢哋自己曾經係乜嘢樣子,佢哋當時點樣感覺、思考同談話,以及佢哋有時做過乜嘢古怪嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然我的書主要是為了給男孩女孩消遣而寫,我希望男人女人不會因此而迴避它,因為我的計畫的一部分,是試圖愉快地提醒成年人他們自己曾經是什麼樣子,他們當時怎樣感覺、思考和談話,以及他們有時做過什麼古怪的事。

passages.original: THE AUTHOR.
passages.vernacular: 作者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 作者。

passages.original: HARTFORD, 1876.
passages.vernacular: 哈特福德,一八七六年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈特福德,一八七六年。

chapters.title: Chapter I: Y-o-u-u Tom 第一章:湯姆!

passages.original: CH “Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆!」

passages.original: No answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇人應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒人應。

passages.original: “TOM!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆!」

passages.original: No answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇人應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒人應。

passages.original: “What’s gone with that boy, I wonder?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰細路跑到邊度去喇,我真想知道?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那孩子跑到哪裡去了,我真想知道?

passages.original: You TOM!”
passages.vernacular: 你呢湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這湯姆!」

passages.original: No answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇人應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒人應。

passages.original: The old lady pulled her spectacles down and looked over them about the room; then she put them up and looked out under them.
passages.vernacular: 老太太把眼鏡拉到鼻尖,從上面望住屋子四周;然後又把眼鏡推上去,從下面往外睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太把眼鏡拉到鼻尖,從上面望著屋子四周;然後又把眼鏡推上去,從下面往外看。

passages.original: She seldom or never looked through them for so small a thing as a boy; they were her state pair, the pride of her heart, and were built for “style,” not service—she could have seen through a pair of stove-lids just as well.
passages.vernacular: 為了一個細路咁小嘅嘢,佢好少或從不透過眼鏡去睇;嗰個係佢嘅盛裝眼鏡,係佢心頭嘅驕傲,係為「時髦」而造嘅,唔係為了實用——佢透過一對爐蓋都一樣睇得清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了一個孩子這麼小的東西,她很少或從不透過眼鏡去看;那是她的盛裝眼鏡,是她心頭的驕傲,是為「時髦」而造的,不是為了實用——她透過一對爐蓋也一樣看得清楚。

passages.original: She looked perplexed for a moment, and then said, not fiercely, but still loud enough for the furniture to hear:
passages.vernacular: 佢困惑地睇咗一會兒,然後講,唔係凶狠地,但仍然大聲到足以讓傢俱聽到:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她困惑地看了一會兒,然後說,不是凶狠地,但仍然大聲到足以讓傢俱聽到:

passages.original: “Well, I lay if I get hold of you I’ll—”
passages.vernacular: 「哼,我敢講要係讓我抓到你,我就——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,我敢說要是讓我抓到你,我就——」

passages.original: She did not finish, for by this time she was bending down and punching under the bed with the broom, and so she needed breath to punctuate the punches with.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇講完,因為呢陣佢正彎下腰,用掃帚喺床底下捅,需要喘氣嚟為捅嘅動作加標點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沒說完,因為這時她正彎下腰,用掃帚在床底下捅,需要喘氣來為捅的動作加標點。

passages.original: She resurrected nothing but the cat.
passages.vernacular: 佢捅出嚟嘅只有貓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她捅出來的只有貓。

passages.original: “I never did see the beat of that boy!”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇見過咁難纏嘅細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒見過這麼難纏的孩子!」

passages.original: She went to the open door and stood in it and looked out among the tomato vines and “jimpson” weeds that constituted the garden.
passages.vernacular: 佢走到敞開嘅門口,站喺嗰度,望住構成花園嘅番茄藤同「曼陀羅」野草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走到敞開的門口,站在那裡,望著構成花園的番茄藤和「曼陀羅」野草。

passages.original: No Tom.
passages.vernacular: 冇湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有湯姆。

passages.original: So she lifted up her voice at an angle calculated for distance and shouted:
passages.vernacular: 於是佢提高聲音,用適合遠距離嘅角度喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是她提高聲音,用適合遠距離的角度喊道:

passages.original: “Y-o-u-u TOM!”
There was a slight noise behind her and she turned just in time to seize a small boy by the slack of his roundabout and arrest his flight.
passages.vernacular: 佢身後有輕微嘅聲音,佢轉過身,恰好抓住一個小男孩外衣嘅鬆處,制止咗佢嘅逃跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她身後有輕微的聲音,她轉過身,恰好抓住一個小男孩外衣的鬆處,制止了他的逃跑。

passages.original: “There!
I might ’a’ thought of that closet.
passages.vernacular: 我早該想到嗰個櫃子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早該想到那個櫃子。

passages.original: What you been doing in there?”
passages.vernacular: 你喺裡面幹乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在裡面幹什麼?」

passages.original: “Nothing.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇幹乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒幹什麼。」

passages.original: “Nothing!
passages.vernacular: 「冇幹乜嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒幹什麼!

passages.original: Look at your hands.
passages.vernacular: 睇你嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看你的手。

passages.original: And look at your mouth.
passages.vernacular: 仲有你嘅嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有你的嘴。

passages.original: What is that truck?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係乜嘢嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是什麼東西?」

passages.original: “I don’t know, aunt.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,姨媽。」

passages.original: “Well, I know.
passages.vernacular: 「哼,我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,我知道。

passages.original: It’s jam—that’s what it is.
passages.vernacular: 係果醬——就係嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是果醬——就是那個。

passages.original: Forty times I’ve said if you didn’t let that jam alone I’d skin you.
passages.vernacular: 我講過四十次,你要係不動嗰果醬,我就剝你嘅皮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說過四十次,你要是不動那果醬,我就剝你的皮。

passages.original: Hand me that switch.”
passages.vernacular: 把嗰根鞭子遞畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把那根鞭子遞給我。」

passages.original: The switch hovered in the air—the peril was desperate—
passages.vernacular: 鞭子懸喺空中——危險萬分——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鞭子懸在空中——危險萬分——

passages.original: “My!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!

passages.original: Look behind you, aunt!”
passages.vernacular: 睇你後面,姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看你後面,姨媽!」

passages.original: The old lady whirled round, and snatched her skirts out of danger.
passages.vernacular: 老太太猛地轉身,把裙子從危險中拉開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太猛地轉身,把裙子從危險中拉開。

passages.original: The lad fled on the instant, scrambled up the high board-fence, and disappeared over it.
passages.vernacular: 細路即刻逃走喇,爬上高高嘅木板籬笆,翻過去唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子立刻逃走了,爬上高高的木板籬笆,翻過去不見了。

passages.original: His aunt Polly stood surprised a moment, and then broke into a gentle laugh.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅波莉姨媽驚訝地站咗一會兒,然後輕輕笑咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的波莉姨媽驚訝地站了一會兒,然後輕輕笑了起來。

passages.original: “Hang the boy, can’t I never learn anything?
passages.vernacular: 「呢細路,真該死,我就唔能夠學乖嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這孩子,真該死,我就不能學乖嗎?

passages.original: Ain’t he played me tricks enough like that for me to be looking out for him by this time?
passages.vernacular: 佢咁樣捉弄我嘅把戲仲少嗎,到呢陣我仲不留神佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他這樣捉弄我的把戲還少嗎,到這時我還不留神他?

passages.original: But old fools is the biggest fools there is.
passages.vernacular: 但老糊塗係最糊塗嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但老糊塗是最糊塗的。

passages.original: Can’t learn an old dog new tricks, as the saying is.
passages.vernacular: 正如俗話講嘅,老狗學唔會新把戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正如俗話說的,老狗學不會新把戲。

passages.original: But my goodness, he never plays them alike, two days, and how is a body to know what’s coming?
passages.vernacular: 不過我嘅天,佢從不連住兩天耍同樣嘅把戲,邊個知道下一步係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我的天,他從不連著兩天耍同樣的把戲,誰知道下一步是什麼?

passages.original: He ’pears to know just how long he can torment me before I get my dander up, and he knows if he can make out to put me off for a minute or make me laugh, it’s all down again and I can’t hit him a lick.
passages.vernacular: 佢好像確切知道佢能折磨我多久,才會讓我火冒三丈,佢仲知道只要佢能設法拖我一分鐘,或讓我發笑,一切就煙消雲散,我連打佢一下都打不下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他好像確切知道他能折磨我多久,才會讓我火冒三丈,他還知道只要他能設法拖我一分鐘,或讓我發笑,一切就煙消雲散,我連打他一下都打不下去。

passages.original: I ain’t doing my duty by that boy, and that’s the Lord’s truth, goodness knows.
passages.vernacular: 我冇盡到對嗰細路嘅責任,呢個係千真萬確嘅,天知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有盡到對那孩子的責任,這是千真萬確的,天知道。

passages.original: Spare the rod and spile the child, as the Good Book says.
passages.vernacular: 正如聖經講嘅,不打不成器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正如聖經說的,不打不成器。

passages.original: I’m a laying up sin and suffering for us both, I know.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我係喺為我哋倆積累罪孽同痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我是在為我們倆積累罪孽和痛苦。

passages.original: He’s full of the Old Scratch, but laws-a-me! he’s my own dead sister’s boy, poor thing, and I ain’t got the heart to lash him, somehow.
passages.vernacular: 佢滿肚子鬼主意,但係天呀!佢係我死去嘅姐姐嘅細路,可憐嘅嘢,我唔知怎嘅就係不忍心抽佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他滿肚子鬼主意,但是天哪!他是我死去的姐姐的孩子,可憐的東西,我不知怎的就是不忍心抽他。

passages.original: Every time I let him off, my conscience does hurt me so, and every time I hit him my old heart most breaks.
passages.vernacular: 每次我放過佢,我嘅良心就好痛,每次我打佢,我呢顆老心就差點碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每次我放過他,我的良心就很痛,每次我打他,我這顆老心就差點碎了。

passages.original: Well-a-well, man that is born of woman is of few days and full of trouble, as the Scripture says, and I reckon it’s so.
passages.vernacular: 唉,正如聖經講嘅,婦人所生嘅人,日子短少,多有患難,我想確實如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,正如聖經說的,婦人所生的人,日子短少,多有患難,我想確實如此。

passages.original: He’ll play hookey this evening,[*] and I’ll just be obleeged to make him work, tomorrow, to punish him.
passages.vernacular: 佢今日下午會逃學,[*]聽日我只好逼佢做工嚟懲罰佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他今天下午會逃學,[*]明天我只好逼他做工來懲罰他。

passages.original: It’s mighty hard to make him work Saturdays, when all the boys is having holiday, but he hates work more than he hates anything else, and I’ve got to do some of my duty by him, or I’ll be the ruination of the child.”
passages.vernacular: 星期六,別嘅男孩都放假時,逼佢做工真難,但佢恨工作勝過恨任何別嘅嘢,而我必須對佢盡啲責任,否則我會毀咗呢細路嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期六,別的男孩都放假時,逼他做工真難,但他恨工作勝過恨任何別的東西,而我必須對他盡一點責任,否則我會毀了這孩子的。」

passages.original: [*] Southwestern for “afternoon”
passages.vernacular: [*] 西南部方言,指「下午」
passages.vernacularMandarin: [*] 西南部方言,指「下午」

passages.original: Tom did play hookey, and he had a very good time.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆確實逃學喇,而且玩得好痛快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆確實逃學了,而且玩得很痛快。

passages.original: He got back home barely in season to help Jim, the small colored boy, saw next-day’s wood and split the kindlings before supper—at least he was there in time to tell his adventures to Jim while Jim did three-fourths of the work.
passages.vernacular: 佢回到家剛好趕上幫黑人小男孩吉姆鋸第二天用嘅柴火,喺晚飯前劈好引火柴——至少佢及時趕到,可以把佢嘅冒險講畀吉姆聽,而吉姆做咗四分之三嘅活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回到家剛好趕上幫黑人小男孩吉姆鋸第二天用的柴火,在晚飯前劈好引火柴——至少他及時趕到,可以把他的冒險講給吉姆聽,而吉姆做了四分之三的活。

passages.original: Tom’s younger brother (or rather half-brother) Sid was already through with his part of the work (picking up chips), for he was a quiet boy, and had no adventurous, trouble-some ways.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅弟弟(確切講係同母異父嘅弟弟)希德已經做完咗佢嗰份活(撿木屑),因為佢係個安靜嘅細路,冇愛冒險、惹麻煩嘅習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的弟弟(確切說是同母異父的弟弟)希德已經做完了他那份活(撿木屑),因為他是個安靜的孩子,沒有愛冒險、惹麻煩的習慣。

passages.original: While Tom was eating his supper, and stealing sugar as opportunity offered, Aunt Polly asked him questions that were full of guile, and very deep—for she wanted to trap him into damaging revealments.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆食晚飯時,一有機會就偷糖,波莉姨媽問佢啲充滿詭計、好有深度嘅問題——因為佢想引佢落入圈套,透露對佢不利嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆吃晚飯時,一有機會就偷糖,波莉姨媽問他一些充滿詭計、很有深度的問題——因為她想引他落入圈套,透露對他不利的事。

passages.original: Like many other simple-hearted souls, it was her pet vanity to believe she was endowed with a talent for dark and mysterious diplomacy, and she loved to contemplate her most transparent devices as marvels of low cunning.
passages.vernacular: 像許多其他心地單純嘅人一樣,佢嘅虛榮係相信自己天賦有一種陰暗神祕嘅外交才能,佢鍾意把自己最透明嘅計謀當作低級狡猾嘅奇蹟嚟欣賞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像許多其他心地單純的人一樣,她的虛榮是相信自己天賦有一種陰暗神祕的外交才能,她喜歡把自己最透明的計謀當作低級狡猾的奇蹟來欣賞。

passages.original: Said she:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說:

passages.original: “Tom, it was middling warm in school, warn’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,學校裡仲算熱,係吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,學校裡還算熱,是吧?」

passages.original: “Yes’m.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,姨媽。」

passages.original: “Powerful warm, warn’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 「熱得厲害,係吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「熱得厲害,是吧?」

passages.original: “Yes’m.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,姨媽。」

passages.original: “Didn’t you want to go in a-swimming, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 「你唔係想去游泳嗎,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不是想去游泳嗎,湯姆?」

passages.original: A bit of a scare shot through Tom—a touch of uncomfortable suspicion.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆心裡閃過一絲驚慌——啲不舒服嘅懷疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆心裡閃過一絲驚慌——一點不舒服的懷疑。

passages.original: He searched Aunt Polly’s face, but it told him nothing.
passages.vernacular: 佢搜索波莉姨媽嘅臉,但乜嘢都睇不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他搜索波莉姨媽的臉,但什麼也看不出來。

passages.original: So he said:
passages.vernacular: 於是佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他說:

passages.original: “No’m—well, not very much.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔想,姨媽——嗯,不太想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不想,姨媽——嗯,不太想。」

passages.original: The old lady reached out her hand and felt Tom’s shirt, and said:
passages.vernacular: 老太太伸出手,摸咗摸湯姆嘅襯衫,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太伸出手,摸了摸湯姆的襯衫,說:

passages.original: “But you ain’t too warm now, though.”
passages.vernacular: 「但你而家不太熱,對吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你現在不太熱,對吧。」

passages.original: And it flattered her to reflect that she had discovered that the shirt was dry without anybody knowing that that was what she had in her mind.
passages.vernacular: 佢想到自己發現咗襯衫係乾嘅,而冇人知道佢心裡想嘅就係呢個,感到好得意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她想到自己發現了襯衫是乾的,而沒有人知道她心裡想的就是這個,感到很得意。

passages.original: But in spite of her, Tom knew where the wind lay, now.
passages.vernacular: 但不管佢點樣,湯姆而家知道風向喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不管她怎麼樣,湯姆現在知道風向了。

passages.original: So he forestalled what might be the next move:
passages.vernacular: 所以佢預先防備咗佢可能嘅下一步:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他預先防備了她可能的下一步:

passages.original: “Some of us pumped on our heads—mine’s damp yet.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋有些人往頭上打水——我嘅仲濕住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們有些人往頭上打水——我的還濕著。

passages.original: See?”
Aunt Polly was vexed to think she had overlooked that bit of circumstantial evidence, and missed a trick.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽想到自己忽略咗嗰點間接證據,漏掉咗一招,好惱火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽想到自己忽略了那點間接證據,漏掉了一招,很惱火。

passages.original: Then she had a new inspiration:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢又有咗新靈感:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她又有了新靈感:

passages.original: “Tom, you didn’t have to undo your shirt collar where I sewed it, to pump on your head, did you?
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,你往頭上打水,唔使解開我縫嘅襯衫領子吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,你往頭上打水,不用解開我縫的襯衫領子吧?

passages.original: Unbutton your jacket!”
passages.vernacular: 解開你嘅外套!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 解開你的外套!」

passages.original: The trouble vanished out of Tom’s face.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆臉上嘅麻煩消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆臉上的麻煩消失了。

passages.original: He opened his jacket.
passages.vernacular: 佢打開外套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他打開外套。

passages.original: His shirt collar was securely sewed.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅襯衫領子縫得牢牢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的襯衫領子縫得牢牢的。

passages.original: “Bother!
passages.vernacular: 「真討厭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真討厭!

passages.original: Well, go ’long with you.
passages.vernacular: 好吧,走開吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,走開吧。

passages.original: I’d made sure you’d played hookey and been a-swimming.
passages.vernacular: 我本來肯定你逃學去游泳喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我本來肯定你逃學去游泳了。

passages.original: But I forgive ye, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 但我原諒你,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我原諒你,湯姆。

passages.original: I reckon you’re a kind of a singed cat, as the saying is—better’n you look.
passages.vernacular: 我想你係嗰種被燒焦嘅貓,正如俗話講嘅——比睇起嚟好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你是那種被燒焦的貓,正如俗話說的——比看起來好。

passages.original: This time.”
passages.vernacular: 呢次。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次。」

passages.original: She was half sorry her sagacity had miscarried, and half glad that Tom had stumbled into obedient conduct for once.
passages.vernacular: 佢一半為自己嘅洞察力落空而遺憾,一半為湯姆偶然表現出順從而高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一半為自己的洞察力落空而遺憾,一半為湯姆偶然表現出順從而高興。

passages.original: But Sidney said:
passages.vernacular: 但希德講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但希德說:

passages.original: “Well, now, if I didn’t think you sewed his collar with white thread, but it’s black.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎,我本來仲以為你用白線縫佢嘅領子,不過佢係黑嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎,我本來還以為你用白線縫他的領子,可是它是黑的。」

passages.original: “Why, I did sew it with white!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我係用白線縫嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我是用白線縫的!

passages.original: Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆!」

passages.original: But Tom did not wait for the rest.
passages.vernacular: 但湯姆冇等聽下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但湯姆沒等聽下去。

passages.original: As he went out at the door he said:
passages.vernacular: 佢走出門時講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走出門時說:

passages.original: “Siddy, I’ll lick you for that.”
passages.vernacular: 「希迪,我為呢個要揍你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「希迪,我為這個要揍你。」

passages.original: In a safe place Tom examined two large needles which were thrust into the lapels of his jacket, and had thread bound about them—one needle carried white thread and the other black.
passages.vernacular: 喺一個安全嘅地方,湯姆檢查咗插喺佢外套翻領上嘅兩根大針,上面纏住線——一根針係白線,另一根係黑線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一個安全的地方,湯姆檢查了插在他外套翻領上的兩根大針,上面纏著線——一根針是白線,另一根是黑線。

passages.original: He said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “She’d never noticed if it hadn’t been for Sid.
passages.vernacular: 「要唔係希德,佢永遠唔會發現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要不是希德,她永遠不會發現。

passages.original: Confound it! sometimes she sews it with white, and sometimes she sews it with black.
passages.vernacular: 真該死!有時佢用白線縫,有時用黑線縫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真該死!有時她用白線縫,有時用黑線縫。

passages.original: I wish to gee-miny she’d stick to one or t’other—I can’t keep the run of ’em.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望佢堅持用其中一種——我記不清喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望她堅持用其中一種——我記不清了。

passages.original: But I bet you I’ll lam Sid for that.
passages.vernacular: 但我打賭我要為呢個揍希德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我打賭我要為這個揍希德。

passages.original: I’ll learn him!”
passages.vernacular: 我要教訓佢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要教訓他!」

passages.original: He was not the Model Boy of the village.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係村裡嘅模範男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是村裡的模範男孩。

passages.original: He knew the model boy very well though—and loathed him.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢好了解模範男孩——並且討厭佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過他很了解模範男孩——並且討厭他。

passages.original: Within two minutes, or even less, he had forgotten all his troubles.
passages.vernacular: 唔到兩分鐘,甚至更短,佢就忘記咗所有嘅煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不到兩分鐘,甚至更短,他就忘記了所有的煩惱。

passages.original: Not because his troubles were one whit less heavy and bitter to him than a man’s are to a man, but because a new and powerful interest bore them down and drove them out of his mind for the time—just as men’s misfortunes are forgotten in the excitement of new enterprises.
passages.vernacular: 並唔係因為佢嘅煩惱對佢來講比成年人嘅煩惱輕咗啲點或冇咁苦,而係因為一個新嘅強烈興趣壓倒咗佢哋,暫時把佢哋趕出咗佢嘅腦子——就像人哋嘅不幸喺新事業嘅興奮中被忘記一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並不是因為他的煩惱對他來說比成年人的煩惱輕了一點點或沒那麼苦,而是因為一個新的強烈興趣壓倒了它們,暫時把它們趕出了他的腦子——就像人們的不幸在新事業的興奮中被忘記一樣。

passages.original: This new interest was a valued novelty in whistling, which he had just acquired from a negro, and he was suffering to practise it undisturbed.
passages.vernacular: 呢個新興趣係佢剛從一個黑人嗰度學到嘅一種有價值嘅新奇口哨,佢渴望不受打擾地練習佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個新興趣是他剛從一個黑人那裡學到的一種有價值的新奇口哨,他渴望不受打擾地練習它。

passages.original: It consisted in a peculiar bird-like turn, a sort of liquid warble, produced by touching the tongue to the roof of the mouth at short intervals in the midst of the music—the reader probably remembers how to do it, if he has ever been a boy.
passages.vernacular: 佢包括一種特殊嘅鳥鳴般嘅轉音,一種流水般嘅顫音,係喺音樂中間每隔一小段時間用舌頭碰上顎產生嘅——讀者如果曾經係男孩,大概記得點做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它包括一種特殊的鳥鳴般的轉音,一種流水般的顫音,是在音樂中間每隔一小段時間用舌頭碰上顎產生的——讀者如果曾經是男孩,大概記得怎麼做。

passages.original: Diligence and attention soon gave him the knack of it, and he strode down the street with his mouth full of harmony and his soul full of gratitude.
passages.vernacular: 勤奮同專注好快讓佢掌握咗竅門,佢大步走喺街上,嘴裡充滿和諧,心裡充滿感激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 勤奮和專注很快讓他掌握了竅門,他大步走在街上,嘴裡充滿和諧,心裡充滿感激。

passages.original: He felt much as an astronomer feels who has discovered a new planet—no doubt, as far as strong, deep, unalloyed pleasure is concerned, the advantage was with the boy, not the astronomer.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅感覺好像一位發現咗新行星嘅天文學家——毫無疑問,就強烈、深刻、純粹嘅快樂而言,優勢屬於呢個男孩,而唔係天文學家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的感覺很像一位發現了新行星的天文學家——毫無疑問,就強烈、深刻、純粹的快樂而言,優勢屬於這個男孩,而不是天文學家。

passages.original: The summer evenings were long.
passages.vernacular: 夏天嘅黃昏好長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏天的黃昏很長。

passages.original: It was not dark, yet.
passages.vernacular: 天仲冇黑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天還沒黑。

passages.original: Presently Tom checked his whistle.
passages.vernacular: 不久,湯姆止住咗口哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,湯姆止住了口哨。

passages.original: A stranger was before him—a boy a shade larger than himself.
passages.vernacular: 一個陌生人站喺佢面前——一個比佢稍大啲嘅男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個陌生人站在他面前——一個比他稍大一點的男孩。

passages.original: A new-comer of any age or either sex was an impressive curiosity in the poor little shabby village of St. Petersburg.
passages.vernacular: 喺聖彼得堡呢個破舊嘅小村子裡,任何年齡、任何性別嘅新嚟者都係令人印象深刻嘅稀奇事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在聖彼得堡這個破舊的小村子裡,任何年齡、任何性別的新來者都是令人印象深刻的稀奇事。

passages.original: This boy was well dressed, too—well dressed on a week-day.
passages.vernacular: 呢個男孩穿得都好好——喺平日裡穿得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個男孩穿得也很好——在平日裡穿得很好。

passages.original: This was simply astounding.
passages.vernacular: 呢簡直令人震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這簡直令人震驚。

passages.original: His cap was a dainty thing, his close-buttoned blue cloth roundabout was new and natty, and so were his pantaloons.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅帽子係精緻嘅嘢,佢緊扣住嘅藍布外衣又新又整潔,佢嘅褲子都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的帽子是精緻的東西,他緊扣著的藍布外衣又新又整潔,他的褲子也是。

passages.original: He had shoes on—and it was only Friday.
passages.vernacular: 佢穿住鞋——而今日才星期五。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他穿著鞋——而今天才星期五。

passages.original: He even wore a necktie, a bright bit of ribbon.
passages.vernacular: 佢甚至仲繫住領帶,一小段鮮豔嘅絲帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他甚至還繫著領帶,一小段鮮豔的絲帶。

passages.original: He had a citified air about him that ate into Tom’s vitals.
passages.vernacular: 佢身上有一種城裡人嘅派頭,啃噬住湯姆嘅五臟六腑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他身上有一種城裡人的派頭,啃噬著湯姆的五臟六腑。

passages.original: The more Tom stared at the splendid marvel, the higher he turned up his nose at his finery and the shabbier and shabbier his own outfit seemed to him to grow.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆越盯住呢個華麗嘅奇觀,對佢嘅華服越係嗤之以鼻,覺得自己嘅衣住越嚟越破舊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆越盯著這個華麗的奇觀,對他的華服越是嗤之以鼻,覺得自己的衣著越來越破舊。

passages.original: Neither boy spoke.
passages.vernacular: 兩個男孩都冇講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個男孩都沒說話。

passages.original: If one moved, the other moved—but only sidewise, in a circle; they kept face to face and eye to eye all the time.
passages.vernacular: 一個動,另一個就跟住動——但只係側住走,繞住圈子;佢哋始終面對面、眼對眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個動,另一個就跟著動——但只是側著走,繞著圈子;他們始終面對面、眼對眼。

passages.original: Finally Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 終於湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於湯姆說:

passages.original: “I can lick you!”
passages.vernacular: 「我能揍你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能揍你!」

passages.original: “I’d like to see you try it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我倒想睇你試試。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我倒想看你試試。」

passages.original: “Well, I can do it.”
passages.vernacular: 「哼,我能做到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,我能做到。」

passages.original: “No you can’t, either.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,你都唔能夠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,你也不能。」

passages.original: “Yes I can.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅我能。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的我能。」

passages.original: “No you can’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,你唔能夠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,你不能。」

passages.original: “I can.”
passages.vernacular: 「我能。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能。」

passages.original: “You can’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「你唔能夠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不能。」

passages.original: “Can!”
“Can’t!”
passages.vernacular: 「唔能夠!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不能!」

passages.original: An uncomfortable pause.
passages.vernacular: 一陣不舒服嘅停頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣不舒服的停頓。

passages.original: Then Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆說:

passages.original: “What’s your name?”
passages.vernacular: 「你叫乜嘢名字?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你叫什麼名字?」

passages.original: “’Tisn’t any of your business, maybe.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者不關你嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許不關你的事。」

passages.original: “Well I ’low I’ll make it my business.”
passages.vernacular: 「哼,我準備讓佢關我嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,我準備讓它關我的事。」

passages.original: “Well why don’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你點解不?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你為什麼不?」

passages.original: “If you say much, I will.”
passages.vernacular: 「你再多嘴,我就嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你再多嘴,我就來。」

passages.original: “Much—much—much.
passages.vernacular: 「多嘴——多嘴——多嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多嘴——多嘴——多嘴。

passages.original: There now.”
passages.vernacular: 呢下好喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這下好了。」

passages.original: “Oh, you think you’re mighty smart, don’t you?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你以為你好聰明,係吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你以為你很聰明,是吧?

passages.original: I could lick you with one hand tied behind me, if I wanted to.”
passages.vernacular: 我要係想,可以把一隻手綁喺背後揍你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要是想,可以把一隻手綁在背後揍你。」

passages.original: “Well why don’t you do it?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你點解不揍?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你為什麼不揍?

passages.original: You say you can do it.”
passages.vernacular: 你講你能做到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說你能做到。」

passages.original: “Well I will, if you fool with me.”
passages.vernacular: 「你要係惹我,我就揍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要是惹我,我就揍。」

passages.original: “Oh yes—I’ve seen whole families in the same fix.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅——我見過整家人都係咁樣嘅處境。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的——我見過整家人都是這樣的處境。」

passages.original: “Smarty!
passages.vernacular: 「自作聰明!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「自作聰明!

passages.original: You think you’re some, now, don’t you?
passages.vernacular: 你而家以為自己係個人物,對吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在以為自己是個人物,對吧?

passages.original: Oh, what a hat!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,幾咁好嘅一頂帽子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,多麼好的一頂帽子!」

passages.original: “You can lump that hat if you don’t like it.
passages.vernacular: 「你不鍾意嗰頂帽子就湊合住吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不喜歡那頂帽子就湊合著吧。

passages.original: I dare you to knock it off—and anybody that’ll take a dare will suck eggs.”
passages.vernacular: 我敢你把佢打掉——敢接受挑戰嘅人都會去吸蛋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢你把它打掉——敢接受挑戰的人都會去吸蛋。」

passages.original: “You’re a liar!”
passages.vernacular: 「你係個騙子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是個騙子!」

passages.original: “You’re another.”
passages.vernacular: 「你才係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你才是。」

passages.original: “You’re a fighting liar and dasn’t take it up.”
passages.vernacular: 「你係個好鬥嘅騙子,又唔敢動手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是個好鬥的騙子,又不敢動手。」

passages.original: “Aw—take a walk!”
“Say—if you give me much more of your sass I’ll take and bounce a rock off’n your head.”
passages.vernacular: 「喂——你再多對我無禮,我就攞石頭砸你嘅頭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂——你再多對我無禮,我就拿石頭砸你的頭。」

passages.original: “Oh, of course you will.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,當然你會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,當然你會。」

passages.original: “Well I will.”
passages.vernacular: 「哼,我會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,我會。」

passages.original: “Well why don’t you do it then?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你點解不做?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你為什麼不做?

passages.original: What do you keep saying you will for?
passages.vernacular: 你老係講你會,點解?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你老是說你會,為什麼?

passages.original: Why don’t you do it?
passages.vernacular: 你點解不做?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼不做?

passages.original: It’s because you’re afraid.”
passages.vernacular: 因為你害怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你害怕。」

passages.original: “I ain’t afraid.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不怕。」

passages.original: “You are.”
passages.vernacular: 「你怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怕。」

passages.original: “I ain’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不怕。」

passages.original: “You are.”
passages.vernacular: 「你怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怕。」

passages.original: Another pause, and more eying and sidling around each other.
passages.vernacular: 又一次停頓,更多嘅對視,互相側住繞圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一次停頓,更多的對視,互相側著繞圈。

passages.original: Presently they were shoulder to shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋肩並肩喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們肩並肩了。

passages.original: Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說:

passages.original: “Get away from here!”
passages.vernacular: 「從呢度滾開!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從這裡滾開!」

passages.original: “Go away yourself!”
passages.vernacular: 「你自己滾開!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你自己滾開!」

passages.original: “I won’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不。」

passages.original: “I won’t either.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都不。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也不。」

passages.original: So they stood, each with a foot placed at an angle as a brace, and both shoving with might and main, and glowering at each other with hate.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋站住,各自把一隻腳斜放住當支撐,兩人拼盡全力推擠,憎恨地互相瞪住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們站著,各自把一隻腳斜放著當支撐,兩人拼盡全力推擠,憎恨地互相瞪著。

passages.original: But neither could get an advantage.
passages.vernacular: 但邊個都占唔到上風。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但誰也占不到上風。

passages.original: After struggling till both were hot and flushed, each relaxed his strain with watchful caution, and Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 搏鬥到兩人都熱得臉紅,各自小心翼翼地放鬆力道,湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 搏鬥到兩人都熱得臉紅,各自小心翼翼地放鬆力道,湯姆說:

passages.original: “You’re a coward and a pup.
passages.vernacular: 「你係個膽小鬼同小狗崽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是個膽小鬼和小狗崽。

passages.original: I’ll tell my big brother on you, and he can thrash you with his little finger, and I’ll make him do it, too.”
passages.vernacular: 我要告訴我大哥嚟收拾你,佢用小指頭就能揍你,我都要讓佢咁樣做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要告訴我大哥來收拾你,他用小指頭就能揍你,我也要讓他這樣做。」

passages.original: “What do I care for your big brother?
passages.vernacular: 「我在乎你大哥乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在乎你大哥什麼?

passages.original: I’ve got a brother that’s bigger than he is—and what’s more, he can throw him over that fence, too.”
passages.vernacular: 我有個哥哥比佢仲大——而且,佢仲能把佢扔過嗰道籬笆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有個哥哥比他還大——而且,他還能把他扔過那道籬笆。」

passages.original: [Both brothers were imaginary.]
passages.vernacular: [兩個哥哥都係想像出嚟嘅。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [兩個哥哥都是想像出來的。]

passages.original: “That’s a lie.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係謊話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是謊話。」

passages.original: “Your saying so don’t make it so.”
passages.vernacular: 「你講咗並不代表佢係真嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說了並不代表它是真的。」

passages.original: Tom drew a line in the dust with his big toe, and said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆用大腳趾喺灰塵裡劃咗一條線,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆用大腳趾在灰塵裡劃了一條線,說:

passages.original: “I dare you to step over that, and I’ll lick you till you can’t stand up.
passages.vernacular: 「我敢你跨過去,我就揍你,揍到你站不起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢你跨過去,我就揍你,揍到你站不起來。

passages.original: Anybody that’ll take a dare will steal sheep.”
passages.vernacular: 敢接受挑戰嘅人都會偷羊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 敢接受挑戰的人都會偷羊。」

passages.original: The new boy stepped over promptly, and said:
passages.vernacular: 新嚟嘅男孩即刻跨咗過去,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新來的男孩馬上跨了過去,說:

passages.original: “Now you said you’d do it, now let’s see you do it.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家你講過你會做,而家讓我哋睇睇你做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你說過你會做,現在讓我們看看你做。」

passages.original: “Don’t you crowd me now; you better look out.”
passages.vernacular: 「你別擠我;你最好小心點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你別擠我;你最好小心點。」

passages.original: “Well, you said you’d do it—why don’t you do it?”
passages.vernacular: 「哼,你講你會做——你點解不做?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,你說你會做——你為什麼不做?」

passages.original: “By jingo! for two cents I will do it.”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!畀我兩個銅板我就做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!給我兩個銅板我就做。」

passages.original: The new boy took two broad coppers out of his pocket and held them out with derision.
passages.vernacular: 新男孩從口袋裡掏出兩枚大銅板,嘲弄地伸出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新男孩從口袋裡掏出兩枚大銅板,嘲弄地伸出來。

passages.original: Tom struck them to the ground.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆把佢哋打落喺地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆把它們打落在地。

passages.original: In an instant both boys were rolling and tumbling in the dirt, gripped together like cats; and for the space of a minute they tugged and tore at each other’s hair and clothes, punched and scratched each other’s nose, and covered themselves with dust and glory.
passages.vernacular: 轉眼間兩個男孩喺泥土裡翻滾,像貓一樣扭喺一起;有一分鐘佢哋互相扯頭髮、扯衣服,互相打鼻子、抓鼻子,把自己弄得滿身塵土同榮耀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉眼間兩個男孩在泥土裡翻滾,像貓一樣扭在一起;有一分鐘他們互相扯頭髮、扯衣服,互相打鼻子、抓鼻子,把自己弄得滿身塵土和榮耀。

passages.original: Presently the confusion took form, and through the fog of battle Tom appeared, seated astride the new boy, and pounding him with his fists.
passages.vernacular: 不久混亂有咗形狀,穿過戰鬥嘅煙霧,湯姆出現喇,騎喺新男孩身上,用拳頭捶佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久混亂有了形狀,穿過戰鬥的煙霧,湯姆出現了,騎在新男孩身上,用拳頭捶他。

passages.original: “Holler ’nuff!” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「喊夠喇!」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喊夠了!」他說。

passages.original: The boy only struggled to free himself.
passages.vernacular: 男孩只係掙扎著想擺脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩只是掙扎著想擺脫。

passages.original: He was crying—mainly from rage.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺哭——主要係出於憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在哭——主要是出於憤怒。

passages.original: “Holler ’nuff!”—and the pounding went on.
passages.vernacular: 「喊夠喇!」——捶打繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喊夠了!」——捶打繼續。

passages.original: At last the stranger got out a smothered “’Nuff!” and Tom let him up and said:
passages.vernacular: 最後陌生人悶聲喊出一聲「夠喇!」湯姆放佢起嚟,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後陌生人悶聲喊出一聲「夠了!」湯姆放他起來,說:

passages.original: “Now that’ll learn you.
passages.vernacular: 「呢下會教你嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這下會教你的。

passages.original: Better look out who you’re fooling with next time.”
passages.vernacular: 下次最好睇睇你喺跟邊個作對。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下次最好看看你在跟誰作對。」

passages.original: The new boy went off brushing the dust from his clothes, sobbing, snuffling, and occasionally looking back and shaking his head and threatening what he would do to Tom the “next time he caught him out.”
passages.vernacular: 新男孩走喇,拍掉衣服上嘅灰,抽泣住、吸住鼻子,時而回頭搖頭,威脅講「下次抓到佢喺外面」要對湯姆點樣點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 新男孩走了,拍掉衣服上的灰,抽泣著、吸著鼻子,時而回頭搖頭,威脅說「下次抓到他在外面」要對湯姆怎樣怎樣。

passages.original: To which Tom responded with jeers, and started off in high feather, and as soon as his back was turned the new boy snatched up a stone, threw it and hit him between the shoulders and then turned tail and ran like an antelope.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆報以嘲笑,興高采烈地走喇,佢一轉身,新男孩就抓起一塊石頭,扔過去,打中咗佢嘅肩胛骨之間,然後掉頭像羚羊一樣跑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆報以嘲笑,興高采烈地走了,他一轉身,新男孩就抓起一塊石頭,扔過去,打中了他的肩胛骨之間,然後掉頭像羚羊一樣跑了。

passages.original: Tom chased the traitor home, and thus found out where he lived.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆追住呢個叛徒回家,咁樣就知道咗佢住喺邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆追著這個叛徒回家,這樣就知道了他住在哪裡。

passages.original: He then held a position at the gate for some time, daring the enemy to come outside, but the enemy only made faces at him through the window and declined.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢喺大門口守咗一會兒,向敵人挑戰,讓佢出嚟,但敵人只係隔住窗子對佢做鬼臉,拒絕出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他在大門口守了一會兒,向敵人挑戰,讓他出來,但敵人只是隔著窗子對他做鬼臉,拒絕出來。

passages.original: At last the enemy’s mother appeared, and called Tom a bad, vicious, vulgar child, and ordered him away.
passages.vernacular: 最後敵人嘅母親出現喇,罵湯姆係個壞嘅、惡毒嘅、粗俗嘅細路,命令佢走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後敵人的母親出現了,罵湯姆是個壞的、惡毒的、粗俗的孩子,命令他走開。

passages.original: So he went away; but he said he “’lowed” to “lay” for that boy.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢走喇;但佢講佢「打算」要「埋伏」嗰個男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他走了;但他說他「打算」要「埋伏」那個男孩。

passages.original: He got home pretty late that night, and when he climbed cautiously in at the window, he uncovered an ambuscade, in the person of his aunt; and when she saw the state his clothes were in her resolution to turn his Saturday holiday into captivity at hard labor became adamantine in its firmness.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上佢回家好晚,佢小心地從窗子爬進去時,發現咗一個埋伏,係佢姨媽本人;佢睇到佢衣服嘅狀態,把佢星期六假日變成苦役監禁嘅決心,堅定得像鑽石一樣不可動搖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上他回家很晚,他小心地從窗子爬進去時,發現了一個埋伏,是他姨媽本人;她看到他衣服的狀態,把他星期六假日變成苦役監禁的決心,堅定得像鑽石一樣不可動搖。

chapters.title: Chapter II: Strong Temptations 第二章:粉刷圍欄

passages.original: CH Saturday morning was come, and all the summer world was bright and fresh, and brimming with life.
passages.vernacular: 星期六早晨到喇,整個夏天嘅世界明亮而清新,充滿生機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期六早晨到了,整個夏天的世界明亮而清新,充滿生機。

passages.original: There was a song in every heart; and if the heart was young the music issued at the lips.
passages.vernacular: 每顆心裡都有一首歌;如果心係年輕嘅,音樂就從嘴唇流出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每顆心裡都有一首歌;如果心是年輕的,音樂就從嘴唇流出來。

passages.original: There was cheer in every face and a spring in every step.
passages.vernacular: 每張臉上都有歡樂,每一步都有彈性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每張臉上都有歡樂,每一步都有彈性。

passages.original: The locust-trees were in bloom and the fragrance of the blossoms filled the air.
passages.vernacular: 刺槐樹正在開花,花香瀰漫喺空氣中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 刺槐樹正在開花,花香瀰漫在空氣中。

passages.original: Cardiff Hill, beyond the village and above it, was green with vegetation and it lay just far enough away to seem a Delectable Land, dreamy, reposeful, and inviting.
passages.vernacular: 村子外面、高高喺上嘅卡迪夫山,長滿綠色植物,離得剛好夠遠,睇起嚟像一片樂土,夢幻、寧靜而誘人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 村子外面、高高在上的卡迪夫山,長滿綠色植物,離得剛好夠遠,看起來像一片樂土,夢幻、寧靜而誘人。

passages.original: Tom appeared on the sidewalk with a bucket of whitewash and a long-handled brush.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆出而家人行道上,提住一桶石灰水同一把長柄刷子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆出現在人行道上,提著一桶石灰水和一把長柄刷子。

passages.original: He surveyed the fence, and all gladness left him and a deep melancholy settled down upon his spirit.
passages.vernacular: 佢察睇咗圍欄,所有嘅歡樂都離佢而去,一種深深嘅憂鬱落喺佢嘅心上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他察看了圍欄,所有的歡樂都離他而去,一種深深的憂鬱落在他的心上。

passages.original: Thirty yards of board fence nine feet high.
passages.vernacular: 三十碼長、九呎高嘅木板圍欄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三十碼長、九呎高的木板圍欄。

passages.original: Life to him seemed hollow, and existence but a burden.
passages.vernacular: 生活對佢似乎係空虛嘅,存在只係一種負擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 生活對他似乎是空虛的,存在只是一種負擔。

passages.original: Sighing, he dipped his brush and passed it along the topmost plank; repeated the operation; did it again; compared the insignificant whitewashed streak with the far-reaching continent of unwhitewashed fence, and sat down on a tree-box discouraged.
passages.vernacular: 佢歎住氣,蘸咗蘸刷子,沿住最上面嘅木板刷過去;重複呢個動作;又刷咗一次;把微不足道嘅一道白色同廣闊無垠嘅未刷圍欄大陸相比,沮喪地坐喺一個樹箱上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他歎著氣,蘸了蘸刷子,沿著最上面的木板刷過去;重複這個動作;又刷了一次;把微不足道的一道白色與廣闊無垠的未刷圍欄大陸相比,沮喪地坐在一個樹箱上。

passages.original: Jim came skipping out at the gate with a tin pail, and singing Buffalo Gals.
passages.vernacular: 吉姆提住一個鐵皮桶,唱住《水牛姑娘》,蹦蹦跳跳地從大門出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉姆提著一個鐵皮桶,唱著《水牛姑娘》,蹦蹦跳跳地從大門出來。

passages.original: Bringing water from the town pump had always been hateful work in Tom’s eyes, before, but now it did not strike him so.
passages.vernacular: 以前,從鎮上嘅水泵打水喺湯姆眼中一直係討厭嘅活,但而家佢不咁覺得喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以前,從鎮上的水泵打水在湯姆眼中一直是討厭的活,但現在他不這麼覺得了。

passages.original: He remembered that there was company at the pump.
passages.vernacular: 佢記起水泵嗰度有夥伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他記起水泵那裡有夥伴。

passages.original: White, mulatto, and negro boys and girls were always there waiting their turns, resting, trading playthings, quarrelling, fighting, skylarking.
passages.vernacular: 白人、混血同黑人嘅男孩女孩總喺嗰度等住輪到佢哋,休息、交換玩具、爭吵、打架、嬉鬧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白人、混血和黑人的男孩女孩總在那裡等著輪到他們,休息、交換玩具、爭吵、打架、嬉鬧。

passages.original: And he remembered that although the pump was only a hundred and fifty yards off, Jim never got back with a bucket of water under an hour—and even then somebody generally had to go after him.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲記得,雖然水泵只有一百五十碼遠,吉姆提一桶水回嚟從冇少於一個小時——即使咁樣,通常仲得有人去找佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他還記得,雖然水泵只有一百五十碼遠,吉姆提一桶水回來從沒少於一個小時——即使這樣,通常還得有人去找他。

passages.original: Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說:

passages.original: “Say, Jim, I’ll fetch the water if you’ll whitewash some.”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,吉姆,你要係替我刷點石灰水,我就去打水。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,吉姆,你要是替我刷點石灰水,我就去打水。」

passages.original: Jim shook his head and said:
passages.vernacular: 吉姆搖搖頭講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉姆搖搖頭說:

passages.original: “Can’t, Mars Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「不行,湯姆少爺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不行,湯姆少爺。

passages.original: Ole missis, she tole me I got to go an’ git dis water an’ not stop foolin’ roun’ wid anybody.
passages.vernacular: 老太太跟我講,我得去打水,不許跟任何人瞎混。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太跟我說,我得去打水,不許跟任何人瞎混。

passages.original: She say she spec’ Mars Tom gwine to ax me to whitewash, an’ so she tole me go ’long an’ ’tend to my own business—she ’lowed she’d ’tend to de whitewashin’.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢猜湯姆少爺會叫我刷石灰水,所以佢叫我走自己嘅路——佢講刷石灰水嘅事佢自己嚟管。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她猜湯姆少爺會叫我刷石灰水,所以她叫我走自己的路——她說刷石灰水的事她自己來管。」

passages.original: “Oh, never you mind what she said, Jim.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別管佢講乜嘢,吉姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別管她說什麼,吉姆。

passages.original: That’s the way she always talks.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是嗰樣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她總是那樣說。

passages.original: Gimme the bucket—I won’t be gone only a a minute.
passages.vernacular: 把桶畀我——我只去一分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把桶給我——我只去一分鐘。

passages.original: She won’t ever know.”
passages.vernacular: 佢永遠唔會知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她永遠不會知道。」

passages.original: “Oh, I dasn’t, Mars Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我唔敢,湯姆少爺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我不敢,湯姆少爺。

passages.original: Ole missis she’d take an’ tar de head off’n me. ’Deed she would.”
passages.vernacular: 老太太會把我嘅頭擰下嚟。真嘅,佢會嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太會把我的頭擰下來。真的,她會的。」

passages.original: “She!
She never licks anybody—whacks ’em over the head with her thimble—and who cares for that, I’d like to know.
passages.vernacular: 佢從不打人——只係用頂針敲人嘅頭——邊個在乎嗰個,我倒想知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從不打人——只是用頂針敲人的頭——誰在乎那個,我倒想知道。

passages.original: She talks awful, but talk don’t hurt—anyways it don’t if she don’t cry.
passages.vernacular: 佢講得好凶,但講講唔會傷人——至少佢不哭就唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說得很凶,但說說不會傷人——至少她不哭就不會。

passages.original: Jim, I’ll give you a marvel.
passages.vernacular: 吉姆,我畀你一顆彈珠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉姆,我給你一顆彈珠。

passages.original: I’ll give you a white alley!”
passages.vernacular: 我畀你一顆白色嘅大理石彈珠!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給你一顆白色的大理石彈珠!」

passages.original: Jim began to waver.
passages.vernacular: 吉姆開始動搖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉姆開始動搖。

passages.original: “White alley, Jim!
passages.vernacular: 「白色大理石彈珠,吉姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「白色大理石彈珠,吉姆!

passages.original: And it’s a bully taw.”
passages.vernacular: 而且係個好棒嘅彈珠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且是個很棒的彈珠。」

passages.original: “My!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!

passages.original: Dat’s a mighty gay marvel, I tell you!
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個好漂亮嘅彈珠,我告訴你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個非常漂亮的彈珠,我告訴你!

passages.original: But Mars Tom I’s powerful ’fraid ole missis—”
passages.vernacular: 不過湯姆少爺,我好怕老太太——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是湯姆少爺,我非常怕老太太——」

passages.original: “And besides, if you will I’ll show you my sore toe.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且,如果你肯,我畀你睇我嘅痛腳趾。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且,如果你肯,我給你看我的痛腳趾。」

passages.original: Jim was only human—this attraction was too much for him.
passages.vernacular: 吉姆只係個人——呢個誘惑對佢太大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉姆只是個人——這個誘惑對他太大了。

passages.original: He put down his pail, took the white alley, and bent over the toe with absorbing interest while the bandage was being unwound.
passages.vernacular: 佢放下水桶,攞咗嗰顆白色彈珠,喺繃帶被解開時,全神貫注地彎腰睇嗰個腳趾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他放下水桶,拿了那顆白色彈珠,在繃帶被解開時,全神貫注地彎腰看那個腳趾。

passages.original: In another moment he was flying down the street with his pail and a tingling rear, Tom was whitewashing with vigor, and Aunt Polly was retiring from the field with a slipper in her hand and triumph in her eye.
passages.vernacular: 轉眼佢就提住水桶飛奔喺街上,屁股火辣辣嘅,湯姆起勁地刷住石灰水,波莉姨媽手裡攞住拖鞋,眼裡帶住勝利,從戰場撤退。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 轉眼他就提著水桶飛奔在街上,屁股火辣辣的,湯姆起勁地刷著石灰水,波莉姨媽手裡拿著拖鞋,眼裡帶著勝利,從戰場撤退。

passages.original: But Tom’s energy did not last.
passages.vernacular: 但湯姆嘅精力冇持續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但湯姆的精力沒有持續。

passages.original: He began to think of the fun he had planned for this day, and his sorrows multiplied.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始想佢為呢一天計畫好嘅樂趣,佢嘅悲傷成倍增加。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他開始想他為這一天計畫好的樂趣,他的悲傷成倍增加。

passages.original: Soon the free boys would come tripping along on all sorts of delicious expeditions, and they would make a world of fun of him for having to work—the very thought of it burnt him like fire.
passages.vernacular: 好快自由嘅男孩哋就會輕快地走嚟,去進行各種美妙嘅遠足,佢哋會因佢唔得不工作而大大地取笑佢——一想到呢個,佢就像被火燒一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很快自由的男孩們就會輕快地走來,去進行各種美妙的遠足,他們會因他不得不工作而大大地取笑他——一想到這個,他就像被火燒一樣。

passages.original: He got out his worldly wealth and examined it—bits of toys, marbles, and trash; enough to buy an exchange of work, maybe, but not half enough to buy so much as half an hour of pure freedom.
passages.vernacular: 佢攞出自己嘅全部家當查睇——零碎嘅玩具、彈珠同垃圾;或者夠買一次工作嘅交換,但仲唔夠買半個鐘頭嘅純粹自由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拿出自己的全部家當查看——零碎的玩具、彈珠和垃圾;也許夠買一次工作的交換,但還不夠買半個鐘頭的純粹自由。

passages.original: So he returned his straitened means to his pocket, and gave up the idea of trying to buy the boys.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢把拮据嘅財產放回口袋,放棄咗買通男孩哋嘅念頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他把拮据的財產放回口袋,放棄了買通男孩們的念頭。

passages.original: At this dark and hopeless moment an inspiration burst upon him!
passages.vernacular: 喺呢個黑暗而絕望嘅時刻,一個靈感閃電般降臨喺佢身上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這個黑暗而絕望的時刻,一個靈感閃電般降臨在他身上!

passages.original: Nothing less than a great, magnificent inspiration.
passages.vernacular: 不亞於一個偉大、輝煌嘅靈感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不亞於一個偉大、輝煌的靈感。

passages.original: He took up his brush and went tranquilly to work.
passages.vernacular: 佢攞起刷子,平靜地開始工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拿起刷子,平靜地開始工作。

passages.original: Ben Rogers hove in sight presently—the very boy, of all boys, whose ridicule he had been dreading.
passages.vernacular: 不久本·羅傑斯出而家視野中——所有男孩中,正是佢一直怕被嘲笑嘅嗰個男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久本·羅傑斯出現在視野中——所有男孩中,正是他一直怕被嘲笑的那個男孩。

passages.original: Ben’s gait was the hop-skip-and-jump—proof enough that his heart was light and his anticipations high.
passages.vernacular: 本嘅步態係單腳跳加跨步跳——足以證明佢心情輕鬆,期望好高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本的步態是單腳跳加跨步跳——足以證明他心情輕鬆,期望很高。

passages.original: He was eating an apple, and giving a long, melodious whoop, at intervals, followed by a deep-toned ding-dong-dong, ding-dong-dong, for he was personating a steamboat.
passages.vernacular: 佢正在食蘋果,不時發出一聲長長嘅悅耳嘅呼喊,接住係低沉嘅叮咚咚,叮咚咚,因為佢喺扮演一艘汽船。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他正在吃蘋果,不時發出一聲長長的悅耳的呼喊,接著是低沉的叮咚咚,叮咚咚,因為他在扮演一艘汽船。

passages.original: As he drew near, he slackened speed, took the middle of the street, leaned far over to starboard and rounded to ponderously and with laborious pomp and circumstance—for he was personating the Big Missouri, and considered himself to be drawing nine feet of water.
passages.vernacular: 佢走近時,放慢速度,走喺街道中央,向右舷大幅傾斜,莊重而費力地、帶住排場轉彎——因為佢喺扮演「大密蘇里號」,認為自己食水九呎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走近時,放慢速度,走在街道中央,向右舷大幅傾斜,莊重而費力地、帶著排場轉彎——因為他在扮演「大密蘇里號」,認為自己吃水九呎。

passages.original: He was boat and captain and engine-bells combined, so he had to imagine himself standing on his own hurricane-deck giving the orders and executing them:
passages.vernacular: 佢係船、船長同機艙鈴嘅合體,所以佢得想像自己站喺自己嘅颶風甲板上發號施令並執行:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是船、船長和機艙鈴的合體,所以他得想像自己站在自己的颶風甲板上發號施令並執行:

passages.original: “Stop her, sir!
passages.vernacular: 「停船,先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「停船,先生!

passages.original: Ting-a-ling-ling!”
passages.vernacular: 叮鈴鈴!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮鈴鈴!」

passages.original: The headway ran almost out, and he drew up slowly toward the sidewalk.
passages.vernacular: 前進嘅勢頭幾乎用完喇,佢慢慢地向人行道靠攏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前進的勢頭幾乎用完了,他慢慢地向人行道靠攏。

passages.original: “Ship up to back!
passages.vernacular: 「倒車!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「倒車!

passages.original: Ting-a-ling-ling!”
passages.vernacular: 叮鈴鈴!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮鈴鈴!」

passages.original: His arms straightened and stiffened down his sides.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅手臂伸直,僵硬地垂喺身側。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的手臂伸直,僵硬地垂在身側。

passages.original: “Set her back on the stabboard!
passages.vernacular: 「右舷倒車!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「右舷倒車!

passages.original: Ting-a-ling-ling!
passages.vernacular: 叮鈴鈴!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮鈴鈴!

passages.original: Chow! ch-chow-wow!
passages.vernacular: 嘎!嘎嘎嘎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘎!嘎嘎嘎!

passages.original: Chow!”
His right hand, mean-time, describing stately circles—for it was representing a forty-foot wheel.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅右手同時畫住莊嚴嘅圓圈——因為佢代表一個四十呎嘅明輪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的右手同時畫著莊嚴的圓圈——因為它代表一個四十呎的明輪。

passages.original: “Let her go back on the labboard!
passages.vernacular: 「左舷倒車!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「左舷倒車!

passages.original: Ting-a-ling-ling!
passages.vernacular: 叮鈴鈴!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮鈴鈴!

passages.original: Chow-ch-chow-chow!”
passages.vernacular: 嘎嘎嘎嘎!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘎嘎嘎嘎!」

passages.original: The left hand began to describe circles.
passages.vernacular: 左手開始畫圓圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 左手開始畫圓圈。

passages.original: “Stop the stabboard!
passages.vernacular: 「右舷停車!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「右舷停車!

passages.original: Ting-a-ling-ling!
passages.vernacular: 叮鈴鈴!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮鈴鈴!

passages.original: Stop the labboard!
passages.vernacular: 左舷停車!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 左舷停車!

passages.original: Come ahead on the stabboard!
passages.vernacular: 右舷前進!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 右舷前進!

passages.original: Stop her!
passages.vernacular: 停船!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 停船!

passages.original: Let your outside turn over slow!
passages.vernacular: 讓外輪慢轉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓外輪慢轉!

passages.original: Ting-a-ling-ling!
passages.vernacular: 叮鈴鈴!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮鈴鈴!

passages.original: Chow-ow-ow!
passages.vernacular: 嘎嗚嗚!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘎嗚嗚!

passages.original: Get out that head-line! lively now!
passages.vernacular: 拋出頭纜!快!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拋出頭纜!快!

passages.original: Come—out with your spring-line—what’re you about there!
passages.vernacular: 嚟——把你嘅船纜拋出——你哋喺嗰度幹乜嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來——把你的船纜拋出——你們在那裡幹什麼!

passages.original: Take a turn round that stump with the bight of it!
passages.vernacular: 用纜繩嘅彎處喺嗰個樹樁上繞一圈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用纜繩的彎處在那個樹樁上繞一圈!

passages.original: Stand by that stage, now—let her go!
passages.vernacular: 站穩嗰個跳板——放下!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站穩那個跳板——放下!

passages.original: Done with the engines, sir!
passages.vernacular: 引擎停止,先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 引擎停止,先生!

passages.original: Ting-a-ling-ling!
passages.vernacular: 叮鈴鈴!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮鈴鈴!

passages.original: SH’T!
passages.vernacular: 嘶!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘶!

passages.original: S’H’T!
passages.vernacular: 嘶!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘶!

passages.original: SH’T!”
(trying the gauge-cocks).
passages.vernacular: (試放汽缸旋塞)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: (試放汽缸旋塞)。

passages.original: Tom went on whitewashing—paid no attention to the steamboat.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆繼續刷石灰水——不理汽船。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆繼續刷石灰水——不理汽船。

passages.original: Ben stared a moment and then said: “Hi-Yi!
passages.vernacular: 本瞪咗一會兒,然後講:「嗨呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本瞪了一會兒,然後說:「嗨呀!

passages.original: You’re up a stump, ain’t you!”
passages.vernacular: 你被難住喇,係吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你被難住了,是吧!」

passages.original: No answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: Tom surveyed his last touch with the eye of an artist, then he gave his brush another gentle sweep and surveyed the result, as before.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆用藝術家嘅眼光察睇咗佢嘅最後一筆,然後又輕輕刷咗一下,像之前嗰樣察睇結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆用藝術家的眼光察看了他的最後一筆,然後又輕輕刷了一下,像之前那樣察看結果。

passages.original: Ben ranged up alongside of him.
passages.vernacular: 本走到佢身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本走到他身邊。

passages.original: Tom’s mouth watered for the apple, but he stuck to his work.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆為嗰個蘋果流口水,但堅持佢嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆為那個蘋果流口水,但堅持他的工作。

passages.original: Ben said:
passages.vernacular: 本講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本說:

passages.original: “Hello, old chap, you got to work, hey?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,老夥計,你得做工,係吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,老夥計,你得做工,是吧?」

passages.original: Tom wheeled suddenly and said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆突然轉過身講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆突然轉過身說:

passages.original: “Why, it’s you, Ben!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,係你,本!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,是你,本!

passages.original: I warn’t noticing.”
passages.vernacular: 我冇注意到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒注意到。」

passages.original: “Say—I’m going in a-swimming, I am.
passages.vernacular: 「喂——我要去游泳喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂——我要去游泳了。

passages.original: Don’t you wish you could?
passages.vernacular: 你不希望你能去嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不希望你能去嗎?

passages.original: But of course you’d druther work—wouldn’t you?
passages.vernacular: 但當然你寧願做工——對吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但當然你寧願做工——對吧?

passages.original: Course you would!”
passages.vernacular: 當然你願意!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然你願意!」

passages.original: Tom contemplated the boy a bit, and said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆打量咗呢個男孩一會兒,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆打量了這個男孩一會兒,說:

passages.original: “What do you call work?”
passages.vernacular: 「你把乜嘢叫做工?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你把什麼叫做工?」

passages.original: “Why, ain’t that work?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,嗰唔係工作嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,那不是工作嗎?」

passages.original: Tom resumed his whitewashing, and answered carelessly:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆繼續刷石灰水,隨意地回答:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆繼續刷石灰水,隨意地回答:

passages.original: “Well, maybe it is, and maybe it ain’t.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,或者係,或者唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,也許是,也許不是。

passages.original: All I know, is, it suits Tom Sawyer.”
passages.vernacular: 我只知道,佢適合湯姆·索亞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只知道,它適合湯姆·索亞。」

passages.original: “Oh come, now, you don’t mean to let on that you like it?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦得喇,你唔係要裝作你鍾意呢個吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦得了,你不是要裝作你喜歡這個吧?」

passages.original: The brush continued to move.
passages.vernacular: 刷子繼續動住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 刷子繼續動著。

passages.original: “Like it?
passages.vernacular: 「鍾意?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喜歡?

passages.original: Well, I don’t see why I oughtn’t to like it.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我睇不出點解我唔應該該鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我看不出為什麼我不應該喜歡。

passages.original: Does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence every day?”
passages.vernacular: 一個男孩有機會每天刷圍欄嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個男孩有機會每天刷圍欄嗎?」

passages.original: That put the thing in a new light.
passages.vernacular: 呢使事情有咗新嘅面貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使事情有了新的面貌。

passages.original: Ben stopped nibbling his apple.
passages.vernacular: 本停止咬佢嘅蘋果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本停止咬他的蘋果。

passages.original: Tom swept his brush daintily back and forth—stepped back to note the effect—added a touch here and there—criticised the effect again—Ben watching every move and getting more and more interested, more and more absorbed.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆優雅地嚟回揮動佢嘅刷子——退後一步查睇效果——呢度嗰度添一筆——又批評咗效果——本睇住佢嘅每一個動作,越嚟越感興趣,越嚟越入迷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆優雅地來回揮動他的刷子——退後一步查看效果——這裡那裡添一筆——又批評了效果——本看著他的每一個動作,越來越感興趣,越來越入迷。

passages.original: Presently he said:
passages.vernacular: 不久佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他說:

passages.original: “Say, Tom, let me whitewash a little.”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,湯姆,讓我刷啲石灰水。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,湯姆,讓我刷一點石灰水。」

passages.original: Tom considered, was about to consent; but he altered his mind:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆考慮咗一下,正要同意;但佢改變咗主意:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆考慮了一下,正要同意;但他改變了主意:

passages.original: “No—no—I reckon it wouldn’t hardly do, Ben.
passages.vernacular: 「不——不——我想不行,本。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——不——我想不行,本。

passages.original: You see, Aunt Polly’s awful particular about this fence—right here on the street, you know—but if it was the back fence I wouldn’t mind and she wouldn’t.
passages.vernacular: 你睇,波莉姨媽對呢道圍欄特唔好講究——就喺街上,你知道——但如果係後面嘅圍欄,我不介意,佢都唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,波莉姨媽對這道圍欄特別講究——就在街上,你知道——但如果是後面的圍欄,我不介意,她也不會。

passages.original: Yes, she’s awful particular about this fence; it’s got to be done very careful; I reckon there ain’t one boy in a thousand, maybe two thousand, that can do it the way it’s got to be done.”
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,佢對呢道圍欄特唔好講究;必須好小心地刷;我想一千個男孩裡,或者兩千個,冇一個能按要求嘅方式去做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,她對這道圍欄特別講究;必須非常小心地刷;我想一千個男孩裡,也許兩千個,沒有一個能按要求的方式去做。」

passages.original: “No—is that so?
passages.vernacular: 「不——真嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——真的嗎?

passages.original: Oh come, now—lemme just try.
passages.vernacular: 哦得喇——讓我試試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦得了——讓我試試。

passages.original: Only just a little—I’d let you, if you was me, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 就啲點——如果我係你,湯姆,我會讓你試嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就一點點——如果我是你,湯姆,我會讓你試的。」

passages.original: “Ben, I’d like to, honest injun; but Aunt Polly—well, Jim wanted to do it, but she wouldn’t let him; Sid wanted to do it, and she wouldn’t let Sid.
passages.vernacular: 「本,我真想,講實話;但波莉姨媽——嗯,吉姆想做,佢不讓佢;希德想做,佢不讓希德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「本,我真想,說實話;但波莉姨媽——嗯,吉姆想做,她不讓他;希德想做,她不讓希德。

passages.original: Now don’t you see how I’m fixed?
passages.vernacular: 而家你睇不出我嘅處境嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你看不出我的處境嗎?

passages.original: If you was to tackle this fence and anything was to happen to it—”
passages.vernacular: 如果你嚟弄呢道圍欄,圍欄出咗乜嘢事——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你來弄這道圍欄,圍欄出了什麼事——」

passages.original: “Oh, shucks, I’ll be just as careful.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,唔好講喇,我會一樣小心嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別說了,我會一樣小心的。

passages.original: Now lemme try.
passages.vernacular: 而家讓我試試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在讓我試試。

passages.original: Say—I’ll give you the core of my apple.”
passages.vernacular: 喂——我把我蘋果嘅核畀你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂——我把我蘋果的核給你。」

passages.original: “Well, here—No, Ben, now don’t.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,畀——不,本,別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,給——不,本,別。

passages.original: I’m afeard—”
passages.vernacular: 我怕——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕——」

passages.original: “I’ll give you all of it!”
passages.vernacular: 「我把整個都畀你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我把整個都給你!」

passages.original: Tom gave up the brush with reluctance in his face, but alacrity in his heart.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆臉上帶住不情願,心裡卻好快樂地交出咗刷子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆臉上帶著不情願,心裡卻很快樂地交出了刷子。

passages.original: And while the late steamer Big Missouri worked and sweated in the sun, the retired artist sat on a barrel in the shade close by, dangled his legs, munched his apple, and planned the slaughter of more innocents.
passages.vernacular: 已故嘅汽船大密蘇里號喺陽光下工作流汗時,退休嘅藝術家坐喺附近陰涼處嘅一個桶上,晃住腿,嚼住佢嘅蘋果,策劃屠殺更多嘅無辜者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已故的汽船大密蘇里號在陽光下工作流汗時,退休的藝術家坐在附近陰涼處的一個桶上,晃著腿,嚼著他的蘋果,策劃屠殺更多的無辜者。

passages.original: There was no lack of material; boys happened along every little while; they came to jeer, but remained to whitewash.
passages.vernacular: 材料不缺;男孩哋每隔一會兒就碰巧走過嚟;佢哋嚟時係嘲笑嘅,留下時卻去刷石灰水喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 材料不缺;男孩們每隔一會兒就碰巧走過來;他們來時是嘲笑的,留下時卻去刷石灰水了。

passages.original: By the time Ben was fagged out, Tom had traded the next chance to Billy Fisher for a kite, in good repair; and when he played out, Johnny Miller bought in for a dead rat and a string to swing it with—and so on, and so on, hour after hour.
passages.vernacular: 等本累垮時,湯姆已經把下一次機會以一個狀態完好嘅風箏換畀咗比利·費舍爾;佢玩累喇,強尼·米勒用一隻死老鼠同一根甩佢嘅繩子買咗進嚟——如此呢般,一個鐘頭又一個鐘頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等本累垮時,湯姆已經把下一次機會以一個狀態完好的風箏換給了比利·費舍爾;他玩累了,強尼·米勒用一隻死老鼠和一根甩它的繩子買了進來——如此這般,一個鐘頭又一個鐘頭。

passages.original: And when the middle of the afternoon came, from being a poor poverty-stricken boy in the morning, Tom was literally rolling in wealth.
passages.vernacular: 到下午過半時,湯姆從早晨一個窮困潦倒嘅男孩,字面意義上地變成咗滾喺財富裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到下午過半時,湯姆從早晨一個窮困潦倒的男孩,字面意義上地變成了滾在財富裡。

passages.original: He had besides the things before mentioned, twelve marbles, part of a jews-harp, a piece of blue bottle-glass to look through, a spool cannon, a key that wouldn’t unlock anything, a fragment of chalk, a glass stopper of a decanter, a tin soldier, a couple of tadpoles, six fire-crackers, a kitten with only one eye, a brass door-knob, a dog-collar—but no dog—the handle of a knife, four pieces of orange-peel, and a dilapidated old window sash.
passages.vernacular: 除咗前面提到嘅嘢,佢有十二顆彈珠、一把口簧琴嘅一部分、一塊用嚟透視嘅藍色瓶玻璃、一個線軸砲、一把乜嘢都打不開嘅鑰匙、一小塊粉筆、一個酒瓶嘅玻璃塞子、一個錫兵、兩隻蝌蚪、六個爆竹、一隻只有一隻眼睛嘅小貓、一個黃銅門把手、一個狗項圈——但冇狗——一把刀嘅柄、四片橘子皮,同一個破舊嘅老窗框。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了前面提到的東西,他有十二顆彈珠、一把口簧琴的一部分、一塊用來透視的藍色瓶玻璃、一個線軸砲、一把什麼也打不開的鑰匙、一小塊粉筆、一個酒瓶的玻璃塞子、一個錫兵、兩隻蝌蚪、六個爆竹、一隻只有一隻眼睛的小貓、一個黃銅門把手、一個狗項圈——但沒有狗——一把刀的柄、四片橘子皮,和一個破舊的老窗框。

passages.original: He had had a nice, good, idle time all the while—plenty of company—and the fence had three coats of whitewash on it!
passages.vernacular: 佢一直過得又好又悠閒——有好多伙伴——而圍欄上已經刷咗三層石灰水!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一直過得又好又悠閒——有很多伙伴——而圍欄上已經刷了三層石灰水!

passages.original: If he hadn’t run out of whitewash he would have bankrupted every boy in the village.
passages.vernacular: 如果冇用完石灰水,佢會讓村裡每個男孩破產。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果沒有用完石灰水,他會讓村裡每個男孩破產。

passages.original: Tom said to himself that it was not such a hollow world, after all.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆對自己講,呢個世界畢竟唔係咁空虛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆對自己說,這個世界畢竟不是那麼空虛。

passages.original: He had discovered a great law of human action, without knowing it—namely, that in order to make a man or a boy covet a thing, it is only necessary to make the thing difficult to attain.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺唔知不覺中發現咗人類行為嘅一條偉大法則——就係,要讓一個男人或男孩渴望一樣嘢,只需讓咁樣嘢難以得到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在不知不覺中發現了人類行為的一條偉大法則——就是,要讓一個男人或男孩渴望一樣東西,只需讓這樣東西難以得到。

passages.original: If he had been a great and wise philosopher, like the writer of this book, he would now have comprehended that Work consists of whatever a body is obliged to do, and that Play consists of whatever a body is not obliged to do.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢係一位偉大而智慧嘅哲學家,像本書作者一樣,佢而家就會明白,工作係一個人被迫去做嘅一切,玩耍係一個人不被迫去做嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他是一位偉大而智慧的哲學家,像本書作者一樣,他現在就會明白,工作是一個人被迫去做的一切,玩耍是一個人不被迫去做的一切。

passages.original: And this would help him to understand why constructing artificial flowers or performing on a tread-mill is work, while rolling ten-pins or climbing Mont Blanc is only amusement.
passages.vernacular: 呢會幫助佢明白點解做人造花或喺踏車上表演係工作,而滾木球或爬勃朗峰只係消遣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這會幫助他明白為什麼做人造花或在踏車上表演是工作,而滾木球或爬勃朗峰只是消遣。

passages.original: There are wealthy gentlemen in England who drive four-horse passenger-coaches twenty or thirty miles on a daily line, in the summer, because the privilege costs them considerable money; but if they were offered wages for the service, that would turn it into work and then they would resign.
passages.vernacular: 英國有些富有嘅紳士,夏天每天駕駛四匹馬拉嘅載客馬車,跑二三十英里嘅路線,因為呢個特權花咗佢哋相當多嘅錢;但如果有人提出為呢項服務付工資,嗰會把佢變成工作,嗰時佢哋就會辭職。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 英國有些富有的紳士,夏天每天駕駛四匹馬拉的載客馬車,跑二三十英里的路線,因為這個特權花了他們相當多的錢;但如果有人提出為這項服務付工資,那會把它變成工作,那時他們就會辭職。

passages.original: The boy mused awhile over the substantial change which had taken place in his worldly circumstances, and then wended toward headquarters to report.
passages.vernacular: 男孩對佢世俗處境發生嘅實質性變化沉思咗一會兒,然後向總部走去報告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩對他世俗處境發生的實質性變化沉思了一會兒,然後向總部走去報告。

chapters.title: Chapter III: Tom as a General 第三章:湯姆當將軍

passages.original: CH Tom presented himself before Aunt Polly, who was sitting by an open window in a pleasant rearward apartment, which was bedroom, breakfast-room, dining-room, and library, combined.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆出而家波莉姨媽面前,佢坐喺一扇敞開嘅窗邊,喺一間愜意嘅後屋裡,嗰度兼作臥室、早餐室、餐廳同書房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆出現在波莉姨媽面前,她坐在一扇敞開的窗邊,在一間愜意的後屋裡,那裡兼作臥室、早餐室、餐廳和書房。

passages.original: The balmy summer air, the restful quiet, the odor of the flowers, and the drowsing murmur of the bees had had their effect, and she was nodding over her knitting—for she had no company but the cat, and it was asleep in her lap.
passages.vernacular: 溫和嘅夏日空氣、安靜嘅休息、花嘅香氣同蜜蜂昏昏欲瞓嘅嗡嗡聲都起咗作用,佢正在打盹,織物喺手裡——因為佢冇伴,只有貓,而貓瞓喺佢嘅腿上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫和的夏日空氣、安靜的休息、花的香氣和蜜蜂昏昏欲睡的嗡嗡聲都起了作用,她正在打盹,織物在手裡——因為她沒有伴,只有貓,而貓睡在她的腿上。

passages.original: Her spectacles were propped up on her gray head for safety.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼鏡為了安全架喺佢灰白嘅頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼鏡為了安全架在她灰白的頭上。

passages.original: She had thought that of course Tom had deserted long ago, and she wondered at seeing him place himself in her power again in this intrepid way.
passages.vernacular: 佢以為湯姆當然早就逃跑喇,佢對睇到佢以呢種無畏嘅方式再次把自己放喺佢嘅掌握中感到驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她以為湯姆當然早就逃跑了,她對看到他以這種無畏的方式再次把自己放在她的掌握中感到驚訝。

passages.original: He said: “Mayn’t I go and play now, aunt?”
passages.vernacular: 佢講:「我而家可以去玩咗嗎,姨媽?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:「我現在可以去玩了嗎,姨媽?」

passages.original: “What, a’ready?
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢,已經?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼,已經?

passages.original: How much have you done?”
passages.vernacular: 你做咗多少?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你做了多少?」

passages.original: “It’s all done, aunt.”
passages.vernacular: 「全做完喇,姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「全做完了,姨媽。」

passages.original: “Tom, don’t lie to me—I can’t bear it.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,別對我撒謊——我受不喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,別對我撒謊——我受不了。」

passages.original: “I ain’t, aunt; it is all done.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇,姨媽;真嘅全做完喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有,姨媽;真的全做完了。」

passages.original: Aunt Polly placed small trust in such evidence.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽對呢種證據好少信任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽對這種證據很少信任。

passages.original: She went out to see for herself; and she would have been content to find twenty per cent. of Tom’s statement true.
passages.vernacular: 佢出去自己睇;如果發現湯姆嘅話有百分之二十係真嘅,佢就滿足喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她出去自己看;如果發現湯姆的話有百分之二十是真的,她就滿足了。

passages.original: When she found the entire fence white-washed, and not only whitewashed but elaborately coated and recoated, and even a streak added to the ground, her astonishment was almost unspeakable.
passages.vernacular: 當佢發現整道圍欄都刷咗石灰水,而且不僅刷喇,仲精心地塗咗又塗,甚至地上仲加咗一道,佢嘅驚訝幾乎無法形容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當她發現整道圍欄都刷了石灰水,而且不僅刷了,還精心地塗了又塗,甚至地上還加了一道,她的驚訝幾乎無法形容。

passages.original: She said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說:

passages.original: “Well, I never!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我真冇想到!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我真沒想到!

passages.original: There’s no getting round it, you can work when you’re a mind to, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係冇法否認嘅,你願意嘅時候,你係能工作嘅,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是沒法否認的,你願意的時候,你是能工作的,湯姆。」

passages.original: And then she diluted the compliment by adding, “But it’s powerful seldom you’re a mind to, I’m bound to say.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢又沖淡咗呢句讚美,補充講:「但係你願意嘅時候真係少得好,我唔得不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她又沖淡了這句讚美,補充說:「但是你願意的時候真是少得很,我不得不說。

passages.original: Well, go ’long and play; but mind you get back some time in a week, or I’ll tan you.”
passages.vernacular: 好喇,去玩吧;但記得一個星期之內某個時候回嚟,否則我揍你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,去玩吧;但記得一個星期之內某個時候回來,否則我揍你。」

passages.original: She was so overcome by the splendor of his achievement that she took him into the closet and selected a choice apple and delivered it to him, along with an improving lecture upon the added value and flavor a treat took to itself when it came without sin through virtuous effort.
passages.vernacular: 佢被佢成就嘅輝煌弄得太激動,佢把佢帶進櫃子,挑咗一個上好嘅蘋果畀咗佢,仲附帶一番教益性嘅講話,講通過美德嘅努力、無罪過得嚟嘅款待,味道同價值都要更高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她被他成就的輝煌弄得太激動,她把他帶進櫃子,挑了一個上好的蘋果給了他,還附帶一番教益性的講話,說通過美德的努力、無罪過得來的款待,味道和價值都要更高。

passages.original: And while she closed with a happy Scriptural flourish, he “hooked” a doughnut.
passages.vernacular: 佢以一個快樂嘅聖經式嘅華麗結語結束時,佢「順手牽羊」攞咗一個甜甜圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她以一個快樂的聖經式的華麗結語結束時,他「順手牽羊」拿了一個甜甜圈。

passages.original: Then he skipped out, and saw Sid just starting up the outside stairway that led to the back rooms on the second floor.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢蹦跳住跑出去,睇到希德剛要走上通向二樓後面房間嘅外樓梯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他蹦跳著跑出去,看到希德剛要走上通向二樓後面房間的外樓梯。

passages.original: Clods were handy and the air was full of them in a twinkling.
passages.vernacular: 土塊好順手,轉眼間空中到處係土塊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 土塊很順手,轉眼間空中到處是土塊。

passages.original: They raged around Sid like a hail-storm; and before Aunt Polly could collect her surprised faculties and sally to the rescue, six or seven clods had taken personal effect, and Tom was over the fence and gone.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋像冰雹一樣喺希德周圍怒吼;喺波莉姨媽集中佢食驚嘅神志、出擊營救之前,六七塊土塊已經親身起咗作用,湯姆翻過圍欄走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們像冰雹一樣在希德周圍怒吼;在波莉姨媽集中她吃驚的神志、出擊營救之前,六七塊土塊已經親身起了作用,湯姆翻過圍欄走了。

passages.original: There was a gate, but as a general thing he was too crowded for time to make use of it.
passages.vernacular: 有扇門,但一般來講佢時間太緊,冇法利用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有扇門,但一般來說他時間太緊,沒法利用。

passages.original: His soul was at peace, now that he had settled with Sid for calling attention to his black thread and getting him into trouble.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅靈魂而家平靜喇,因為佢已經同希德算清咗佢提起佢嘅黑線、讓佢惹上麻煩嘅帳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的靈魂現在平靜了,因為他已經和希德算清了他提起他的黑線、讓他惹上麻煩的帳。

passages.original: Tom skirted the block, and came round into a muddy alley that led by the back of his aunt’s cow-stable.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆繞過嗰個街區,拐進通向佢姨媽牛棚後面嘅一條泥濘嘅小巷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆繞過那個街區,拐進通向他姨媽牛棚後面的一條泥濘的小巷。

passages.original: He presently got safely beyond the reach of capture and punishment, and hastened toward the public square of the village, where two “military” companies of boys had met for conflict, according to previous appointment.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢安全地離開咗被抓同受懲罰嘅範圍,匆匆趕往村子嘅公共廣場,嗰度有兩支男孩嘅「軍隊」按事先嘅約定相會交戰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他安全地離開了被抓和受懲罰的範圍,匆匆趕往村子的公共廣場,那裡有兩支男孩的「軍隊」按事先的約定相會交戰。

passages.original: Tom was General of one of these armies, Joe Harper (a bosom friend) General of the other.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆係其中一支軍隊嘅將軍,喬·哈珀(一位知心朋友)係另一支嘅將軍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆是其中一支軍隊的將軍,喬·哈珀(一位知心朋友)是另一支的將軍。

passages.original: These two great commanders did not condescend to fight in person—that being better suited to the still smaller fry—but sat together on an eminence and conducted the field operations by orders delivered through aides-de-camp.
passages.vernacular: 呢兩位偉大嘅指揮官不屑親自作戰——嗰更適合更小嘅小傢伙——而係一起坐喺一個高處,通過副官傳達命令指揮野戰行動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這兩位偉大的指揮官不屑親自作戰——那更適合更小的小傢伙——而是一起坐在一個高處,通過副官傳達命令指揮野戰行動。

passages.original: Tom’s army won a great victory, after a long and hard-fought battle.
passages.vernacular: 經過一場漫長而艱苦嘅戰鬥,湯姆嘅軍隊獲得咗大勝利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過一場漫長而艱苦的戰鬥,湯姆的軍隊獲得了大勝利。

passages.original: Then the dead were counted, prisoners exchanged, the terms of the next disagreement agreed upon, and the day for the necessary battle appointed; after which the armies fell into line and marched away, and Tom turned homeward alone.
passages.vernacular: 然後清點咗死者,交換咗俘虜,商定咗下一次分歧嘅條件,約定咗必要戰鬥嘅日期;然後軍隊排好隊,開走喇,湯姆獨自回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後清點了死者,交換了俘虜,商定了下一次分歧的條件,約定了必要戰鬥的日期;然後軍隊排好隊,開走了,湯姆獨自回家。

passages.original: As he was passing by the house where Jeff Thatcher lived, he saw a new girl in the garden—a lovely little blue-eyed creature with yellow hair plaited into two long-tails, white summer frock and embroidered pantalettes.
passages.vernacular: 佢經過傑夫·撒切爾住嘅房子時,睇到花園裡有個新嚟嘅女孩——一個可愛嘅藍眼睛小人兒,黃頭髮梳成兩條長辮子,穿住白色夏裝同繡花長內褲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他經過傑夫·撒切爾住的房子時,看到花園裡有個新來的女孩——一個可愛的藍眼睛小人兒,黃頭髮梳成兩條長辮子,穿著白色夏裝和繡花長內褲。

passages.original: The fresh-crowned hero fell without firing a shot.
passages.vernacular: 呢位啱啱加冕嘅英雄不戰而敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位剛剛加冕的英雄不戰而敗。

passages.original: A certain Amy Lawrence vanished out of his heart and left not even a memory of herself behind.
passages.vernacular: 一個叫艾米·勞倫斯嘅人從佢心裡消失喇,連佢嘅記憶都冇留下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個叫艾米·勞倫斯的人從他心裡消失了,連她的記憶也沒留下。

passages.original: He had thought he loved her to distraction; he had regarded his passion as adoration; and behold it was only a poor little evanescent partiality.
passages.vernacular: 佢曾以為佢愛佢愛到發狂;佢曾把自己嘅激情睇作崇拜;不過睇邊,嗰只係一種可憐嘅、轉瞬即逝嘅偏愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他曾以為他愛她愛到發狂;他曾把自己的激情看作崇拜;可是看哪,那只是一種可憐的、轉瞬即逝的偏愛。

passages.original: He had been months winning her; she had confessed hardly a week ago; he had been the happiest and the proudest boy in the world only seven short days, and here in one instant of time she had gone out of his heart like a casual stranger whose visit is done.
passages.vernacular: 佢花咗幾個月才贏得佢;佢幾乎一星期前才承認;佢只做咗短短七天世界上最幸福最驕傲嘅男孩,而喺一剎嗰之間,佢就像一個拜訪結束嘅偶然陌生人一樣,從佢嘅心裡走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他花了幾個月才贏得她;她幾乎一星期前才承認;他只做了短短七天世界上最幸福最驕傲的男孩,而在一剎那之間,她就像一個拜訪結束的偶然陌生人一樣,從他的心裡走了。

passages.original: He worshipped this new angel with furtive eye, till he saw that she had discovered him; then he pretended he did not know she was present, and began to “show off” in all sorts of absurd boyish ways, in order to win her admiration.
passages.vernacular: 佢用偷偷嘅眼光崇拜呢位新天使,直到睇到佢發現咗佢;然後佢假裝唔知道佢在場,開始用各種荒唐嘅男孩方式「表演」,以贏得佢嘅欣賞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他用偷偷的眼光崇拜這位新天使,直到看到她發現了他;然後他假裝不知道她在場,開始用各種荒唐的男孩方式「表演」,以贏得她的欣賞。

passages.original: He kept up this grotesque foolishness for some time; but by-and-by, while he was in the midst of some dangerous gymnastic performances, he glanced aside and saw that the little girl was wending her way toward the house.
passages.vernacular: 佢持續咗呢種滑稽嘅愚蠢行為一會兒;但不久,正當佢做啲危險嘅體操表演時,佢瞥向旁邊,睇到小女孩正往房子走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他持續了這種滑稽的愚蠢行為一會兒;但不久,正當他做一些危險的體操表演時,他瞥向旁邊,看到小女孩正往房子走去。

passages.original: Tom came up to the fence and leaned on it, grieving, and hoping she would tarry yet awhile longer.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆走到圍欄邊靠喺上面,悲傷,希望佢再多停留一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆走到圍欄邊靠在上面,悲傷,希望她再多停留一會兒。

passages.original: She halted a moment on the steps and then moved toward the door.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺台階上停咗一下,然後走向門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在台階上停了一下,然後走向門。

passages.original: Tom heaved a great sigh as she put her foot on the threshold.
passages.vernacular: 佢把腳放喺門檻上時,湯姆深深歎咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把腳放在門檻上時,湯姆深深歎了口氣。

passages.original: But his face lit up, right away, for she tossed a pansy over the fence a moment before she disappeared.
passages.vernacular: 但佢嘅臉即刻亮咗起嚟,因為佢喺消失前一刻把一朵三色堇拋過咗圍欄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他的臉馬上亮了起來,因為她在消失前一刻把一朵三色堇拋過了圍欄。

passages.original: The boy ran around and stopped within a foot or two of the flower, and then shaded his eyes with his hand and began to look down street as if he had discovered something of interest going on in that direction.
passages.vernacular: 男孩跑過去,喺離花一兩呎嘅地方停住,然後用手遮住眼睛,開始往街下睇,好像發現嗰個方向有乜嘢有趣嘅事喺發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩跑過去,在離花一兩呎的地方停住,然後用手遮住眼睛,開始往街下看,好像發現那個方向有什麼有趣的事在發生。

passages.original: Presently he picked up a straw and began trying to balance it on his nose, with his head tilted far back; and as he moved from side to side, in his efforts, he edged nearer and nearer toward the pansy; finally his bare foot rested upon it, his pliant toes closed upon it, and he hopped away with the treasure and disappeared round the corner.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢撿起一根稻草,開始試住把佢平衡喺鼻子上,頭向後仰得好遠;佢為此努力左右移動時,慢慢靠近三色堇;最後佢嘅赤腳踩喺咗佢上面,佢靈活嘅腳趾夾住咗佢,佢帶住寶物蹦跳住走喇,消失喺拐角。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他撿起一根稻草,開始試著把它平衡在鼻子上,頭向後仰得很遠;他為此努力左右移動時,慢慢靠近三色堇;最後他的赤腳踩在了它上面,他靈活的腳趾夾住了它,他帶著寶物蹦跳著走了,消失在拐角。

passages.original: But only for a minute—only while he could button the flower inside his jacket, next his heart—or next his stomach, possibly, for he was not much posted in anatomy, and not hypercritical, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 但只有一分鐘——只夠佢把花扣喺外套裡面,靠近佢嘅心——或者或者靠近佢嘅胃,因為佢對解剖學不太了解,而且無論如何都不挑剔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但只有一分鐘——只夠他把花扣在外套裡面,靠近他的心——或者也許靠近他的胃,因為他對解剖學不太了解,而且無論如何也不挑剔。

passages.original: He returned, now, and hung about the fence till nightfall, “showing off,” as before; but the girl never exhibited herself again, though Tom comforted himself a little with the hope that she had been near some window, meantime, and been aware of his attentions.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家回嚟喇,喺圍欄邊逗留到天黑,像以前一樣「表演」;但女孩冇再出現,雖然湯姆稍微安慰自己,希望佢其間喺某個窗口附近,知道佢嘅殷勤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在回來了,在圍欄邊逗留到天黑,像以前一樣「表演」;但女孩沒有再出現,雖然湯姆稍微安慰自己,希望她其間在某個窗口附近,知道他的殷勤。

passages.original: Finally he strode home reluctantly, with his poor head full of visions.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢不情願地大步回家,可憐嘅腦袋裡充滿咗幻象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他不情願地大步回家,可憐的腦袋裡充滿了幻象。

passages.original: All through supper his spirits were so high that his aunt wondered “what had got into the child.”
passages.vernacular: 整個晚餐期間佢嘅情緒咁高,佢姨媽納悶「呢細路係點喇」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個晚餐期間他的情緒那麼高,他姨媽納悶「這孩子是怎麼了」。

passages.original: He took a good scolding about clodding Sid, and did not seem to mind it in the least.
passages.vernacular: 佢因為用土塊丟希德挨咗一頓好罵,似乎啲都不介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他因為用土塊丟希德挨了一頓好罵,似乎一點也不介意。

passages.original: He tried to steal sugar under his aunt’s very nose, and got his knuckles rapped for it.
passages.vernacular: 佢試圖喺佢姨媽鼻子底下偷糖,為此被敲咗指關節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他試圖在他姨媽鼻子底下偷糖,為此被敲了指關節。

passages.original: He said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “Aunt, you don’t whack Sid when he takes it.”
passages.vernacular: 「姨媽,希德攞糖時你不打佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「姨媽,希德拿糖時你不打他。」

passages.original: “Well, Sid don’t torment a body the way you do.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,希德不像你嗰樣折磨人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,希德不像你那樣折磨人。

passages.original: You’d be always into that sugar if I warn’t watching you.”
passages.vernacular: 要唔係我睇住你,你總是會動嗰糖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是我看著你,你總是會動那糖。」

passages.original: Presently she stepped into the kitchen, and Sid, happy in his immunity, reached for the sugar-bowl—a sort of glorying over Tom which was wellnigh unbearable.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢走進廚房,希德為自己嘅豁免而高興,伸手去攞糖碗——呢個係對湯姆嘅一種得意,幾乎令人無法忍受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久她走進廚房,希德為自己的豁免而高興,伸手去拿糖碗——這是對湯姆的一種得意,幾乎令人無法忍受。

passages.original: But Sid’s fingers slipped and the bowl dropped and broke.
passages.vernacular: 但希德嘅手指滑喇,碗掉下去摔碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但希德的手指滑了,碗掉下去摔碎了。

passages.original: Tom was in ecstasies.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆欣喜若狂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆欣喜若狂。

passages.original: In such ecstasies that he even controlled his tongue and was silent.
passages.vernacular: 欣喜若狂到佢甚至控制住舌頭保持沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 欣喜若狂到他甚至控制住舌頭保持沉默。

passages.original: He said to himself that he would not speak a word, even when his aunt came in, but would sit perfectly still till she asked who did the mischief; and then he would tell, and there would be nothing so good in the world as to see that pet model “catch it.”
