passages.vernacular: 佢對自己講,即使姨媽進嚟,佢都一個字不講,而係完全靜坐,等到佢問係邊個幹嘅壞事;然後佢會講出嚟,世界上冇乜嘢比睇到嗰個寵兒「挨罵」更好嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對自己說,即使姨媽進來,他也一個字不說,而是完全靜坐,等到她問是誰幹的壞事;然後他會說出來,世界上沒有什麼比看到那個寵兒「挨罵」更好的了。

passages.original: He was so brimful of exultation that he could hardly hold himself when the old lady came back and stood above the wreck discharging lightnings of wrath from over her spectacles.
passages.vernacular: 老太太回嚟站喺殘骸上方,從眼鏡上方射出憤怒嘅閃電時,佢滿溢住得意,幾乎控制不住自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太回來站在殘骸上方,從眼鏡上方射出憤怒的閃電時,他滿溢著得意,幾乎控制不住自己。

passages.original: He said to himself, “Now it’s coming!”
passages.vernacular: 佢對自己講:「而家嚟喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對自己說:「現在來了!」

passages.original: And the next instant he was sprawling on the floor!
passages.vernacular: 下一刻佢已經趴喺地板上喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻他已經趴在地板上了!

passages.original: The potent palm was uplifted to strike again when Tom cried out:
passages.vernacular: 嗰強有力嘅手掌又舉起嚟要打時,湯姆喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那強有力的手掌又舉起來要打時,湯姆喊道:

passages.original: “Hold on, now, what ’er you belting me for?—Sid broke it!”
passages.vernacular: 「等一下,你點解打我?——係希德打破嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等一下,你為什麼打我?——是希德打破的!」

passages.original: Aunt Polly paused, perplexed, and Tom looked for healing pity.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽停下嚟,困惑,湯姆期待住撫慰嘅憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽停下來,困惑,湯姆期待著撫慰的憐憫。

passages.original: But when she got her tongue again, she only said:
passages.vernacular: 但佢恢復講話後,只講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她恢復說話後,只說:

passages.original: “Umf!
Well, you didn’t get a lick amiss, I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 好吧,我想你冇挨冤枉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,我想你沒挨冤枉。

passages.original: You been into some other audacious mischief when I wasn’t around, like enough.”
passages.vernacular: 我不喺時你大概幹咗別嘅乜嘢大膽嘅壞事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不在時你大概幹了別的什麼大膽的壞事。」

passages.original: Then her conscience reproached her, and she yearned to say something kind and loving; but she judged that this would be construed into a confession that she had been in the wrong, and discipline forbade that.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢嘅良心責備佢,佢渴望講些善意同愛嘅話;但佢判斷呢會被理解為承認佢錯喇,而紀律禁止咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她的良心責備她,她渴望說些善意和愛的話;但她判斷這會被理解為承認她錯了,而紀律禁止這樣。

passages.original: So she kept silence, and went about her affairs with a troubled heart.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢保持沉默,帶住不安嘅心去做佢嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以她保持沉默,帶著不安的心去做她的事。

passages.original: Tom sulked in a corner and exalted his woes.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喺角落裡生悶氣,抬高佢嘅悲哀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆在角落裡生悶氣,抬高他的悲哀。

passages.original: He knew that in her heart his aunt was on her knees to him, and he was morosely gratified by the consciousness of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道喺佢姨媽心裡正向佢下跪,佢為意識到呢點而陰鬱地滿足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他知道在他姨媽心裡正向他下跪,他為意識到這點而陰鬱地滿足。

passages.original: He would hang out no signals, he would take notice of none.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔會掛出任何信號,佢唔會注意任何信號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不會掛出任何信號,他不會注意任何信號。

passages.original: He knew that a yearning glance fell upon him, now and then, through a film of tears, but he refused recognition of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道有時一道渴望嘅目光透過一層淚霧落喺佢身上,但佢拒絕承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他知道有時一道渴望的目光透過一層淚霧落在他身上,但他拒絕承認。

passages.original: He pictured himself lying sick unto death and his aunt bending over him beseeching one little forgiving word, but he would turn his face to the wall, and die with that word unsaid.
passages.vernacular: 佢想像自己病得快死,佢姨媽俯身懇求一句小小嘅原諒嘅話,但佢會把臉轉向牆,帶住嗰句話冇講就死去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想像自己病得快死,他姨媽俯身懇求一句小小的原諒的話,但他會把臉轉向牆,帶著那句話沒說就死去。

passages.original: Ah, how would she feel then?
passages.vernacular: 啊,嗰時佢會有乜嘢感覺?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,那時她會有什麼感覺?

passages.original: And he pictured himself brought home from the river, dead, with his curls all wet, and his sore heart at rest.
passages.vernacular: 佢想像自己從河裡被抬回家,死喇,捲髮全濕喇,佢受傷嘅心安息喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想像自己從河裡被抬回家,死了,捲髮全濕了,他受傷的心安息了。

passages.original: How she would throw herself upon him, and how her tears would fall like rain, and her lips pray God to give her back her boy and she would never, never abuse him any more!
passages.vernacular: 佢會點樣撲到佢身上,佢嘅眼淚會點樣如雨落下,佢嘅嘴唇會點樣祈求上帝把佢嘅細路還畀佢,佢再都唔會、再都唔會虐待佢喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會怎樣撲到他身上,她的眼淚會怎樣如雨落下,她的嘴唇會怎樣祈求上帝把她的孩子還給她,她再也不會、再也不會虐待他了!

passages.original: But he would lie there cold and white and make no sign—a poor little sufferer, whose griefs were at an end.
passages.vernacular: 但佢會躺喺嗰度,冰冷而蒼白,不作任何表示——一個可憐嘅小受難者,佢嘅悲傷已經結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他會躺在那裡,冰冷而蒼白,不作任何表示——一個可憐的小受難者,他的悲傷已經結束。

passages.original: He so worked upon his feelings with the pathos of these dreams, that he had to keep swallowing, he was so like to choke; and his eyes swam in a blur of water, which overflowed when he winked, and ran down and trickled from the end of his nose.
passages.vernacular: 佢用呢啲夢嘅悲壯感動自己嘅情感,以致佢唔得不一直吞嚥,佢快窒息喇;佢嘅眼睛游喺模糊嘅水中,眨眼時溢出嚟,從鼻尖流下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他用這些夢的悲壯感動自己的情感,以致他不得不一直吞嚥,他快窒息了;他的眼睛游在模糊的水中,眨眼時溢出來,從鼻尖流下來。

passages.original: And such a luxury to him was this petting of his sorrows, that he could not bear to have any worldly cheeriness or any grating delight intrude upon it; it was too sacred for such contact; and so, presently, when his cousin Mary danced in, all alive with the joy of seeing home again after an age-long visit of one week to the country, he got up and moved in clouds and darkness out at one door as she brought song and sunshine in at the other.
passages.vernacular: 對佢來講,呢種寵愛自己嘅悲傷係咁樣一種享受,佢唔能夠忍受任何世俗嘅歡樂或刺耳嘅愉悅闖入其中;佢太神聖喇,唔能夠同呢種接觸;所以不久,佢嘅表姐瑪麗跳舞般進嚟,為經過一星期漫長嘅鄉下探訪後再見到家而充滿活力,佢站起嚟,喺雲同黑暗中從一扇門出去,而佢從另一扇門帶嚟歌聲同陽光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對他來說,這種寵愛自己的悲傷是這樣一種享受,他不能忍受任何世俗的歡樂或刺耳的愉悅闖入其中;它太神聖了,不能與這種接觸;所以不久,他的表姐瑪麗跳舞般進來,為經過一星期漫長的鄉下探訪後再見到家而充滿活力,他站起來,在雲和黑暗中從一扇門出去,而她從另一扇門帶來歌聲和陽光。

passages.original: He wandered far from the accustomed haunts of boys, and sought desolate places that were in harmony with his spirit.
passages.vernacular: 佢遠遠走離男孩哋慣常出冇嘅地方,尋找同佢嘅精神和諧嘅荒涼之地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他遠遠走離男孩們慣常出沒的地方,尋找與他的精神和諧的荒涼之地。

passages.original: A log raft in the river invited him, and he seated himself on its outer edge and contemplated the dreary vastness of the stream, wishing, the while, that he could only be drowned, all at once and unconsciously, without undergoing the uncomfortable routine devised by nature.
passages.vernacular: 河裡嘅一個木筏邀請咗佢,佢坐喺佢嘅外沿,凝視住河流淒涼嘅廣闊,同時希望自己能被淹死,一下子、無意識地,而唔使經歷自然設計嘅不舒服嘅過程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 河裡的一個木筏邀請了他,他坐在它的外沿,凝視著河流淒涼的廣闊,同時希望自己能被淹死,一下子、無意識地,而不必經歷自然設計的不舒服的過程。

passages.original: Then he thought of his flower.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢想起咗佢嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他想起了他的花。

passages.original: He got it out, rumpled and wilted, and it mightily increased his dismal felicity.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢攞出嚟,皺巴巴、枯萎嘅,呢極大地增加咗佢陰鬱嘅幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把它拿出來,皺巴巴、枯萎的,這極大地增加了他陰鬱的幸福。

passages.original: He wondered if she would pity him if she knew?
passages.vernacular: 佢想,如果佢知道,佢會可憐佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想,如果她知道,她會可憐他嗎?

passages.original: Would she cry, and wish that she had a right to put her arms around his neck and comfort him?
passages.vernacular: 佢會哭,希望自己有權利用手臂摟住佢嘅脖子安慰佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會哭,希望自己有權利用手臂摟住他的脖子安慰他嗎?

passages.original: Or would she turn coldly away like all the hollow world?
passages.vernacular: 定係佢會像整個空虛嘅世界一樣冷冷地轉身走開?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是她會像整個空虛的世界一樣冷冷地轉身走開?

passages.original: This picture brought such an agony of pleasurable suffering that he worked it over and over again in his mind and set it up in new and varied lights, till he wore it threadbare.
passages.vernacular: 呢個畫面帶嚟咁一種愉快嘅痛苦劇痛,佢一遍又一遍地喺腦子裡加工,從新嘅各種光線裡把佢擺出嚟,直到把佢磨得薄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個畫面帶來那麼一種愉快的痛苦劇痛,他一遍又一遍地在腦子裡加工,從新的各種光線裡把它擺出來,直到把它磨得薄了。

passages.original: At last he rose up sighing and departed in the darkness.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢歎住氣站起嚟,喺黑暗中離去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他歎著氣站起來,在黑暗中離去。

passages.original: About half-past nine or ten o’clock he came along the deserted street to where the Adored Unknown lived; he paused a moment; no sound fell upon his listening ear; a candle was casting a dull glow upon the curtain of a second-story window.
passages.vernacular: 大約九點半或十點,佢沿住空蕩蕩嘅街道嚟到嗰位被崇拜嘅陌生人住嘅地方;佢停咗一下;佢傾聽嘅耳朵裡冇聲音;一支蠟燭喺二樓窗子嘅窗簾上投下暗淡嘅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約九點半或十點,他沿著空蕩蕩的街道來到那位被崇拜的陌生人住的地方;他停了一下;他傾聽的耳朵裡沒有聲音;一支蠟燭在二樓窗子的窗簾上投下暗淡的光。

passages.original: Was the sacred presence there?
passages.vernacular: 神聖嘅存在喺嗰度嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 神聖的存在在那裡嗎?

passages.original: He climbed the fence, threaded his stealthy way through the plants, till he stood under that window; he looked up at it long, and with emotion; then he laid him down on the ground under it, disposing himself upon his back, with his hands clasped upon his breast and holding his poor wilted flower.
passages.vernacular: 佢爬過圍欄,悄悄穿過植物,直到站喺嗰扇窗下;佢久久地、動情地抬頭睇住佢;然後佢躺喺佢下面嘅地上,仰臥住,雙手交叉喺胸前,攞住佢可憐嘅枯萎嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他爬過圍欄,悄悄穿過植物,直到站在那扇窗下;他久久地、動情地抬頭看著它;然後他躺在它下面的地上,仰臥著,雙手交叉在胸前,拿著他可憐的枯萎的花。

passages.original: And thus he would die—out in the cold world, with no shelter over his homeless head, no friendly hand to wipe the death-damps from his brow, no loving face to bend pityingly over him when the great agony came.
passages.vernacular: 佢就咁樣死去——喺冷酷嘅世界裡,頭頂冇遮蔽,無家可歸,冇友善嘅手擦去佢額頭嘅死亡冷汗,大痛苦來臨時冇慈愛嘅臉憐憫地俯身睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他就這樣死去——在冷酷的世界裡,頭頂沒有遮蔽,無家可歸,沒有友善的手擦去他額頭的死亡冷汗,大痛苦來臨時沒有慈愛的臉憐憫地俯身看他。

passages.original: And thus she would see him when she looked out upon the glad morning, and oh! would she drop one little tear upon his poor, lifeless form, would she heave one little sigh to see a bright young life so rudely blighted, so untimely cut down?
passages.vernacular: 佢喺歡樂嘅早晨向外睇時,就會咁樣睇到佢,哦!佢會對佢可憐嘅毫無生氣嘅身體落下一滴小小嘅眼淚嗎?佢會為睇到一個明亮嘅年輕生命如此粗暴地凋謝、如此不合時宜地被砍倒而發出一聲小小嘅歎息嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在歡樂的早晨向外看時,就會這樣看到他,哦!她會對他可憐的毫無生氣的身體落下一滴小小的眼淚嗎?她會為看到一個明亮的年輕生命如此粗暴地凋謝、如此不合時宜地被砍倒而發出一聲小小的歎息嗎?

passages.original: The window went up, a maid-servant’s discordant voice profaned the holy calm, and a deluge of water drenched the prone martyr’s remains!
passages.vernacular: 窗子打開喇,一個女傭刺耳嘅聲音褻瀆咗神聖嘅寧靜,一大盆水澆喺伏地嘅殉道者嘅遺體上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗子打開了,一個女傭刺耳的聲音褻瀆了神聖的寧靜,一大盆水澆在伏地的殉道者的遺體上!

passages.original: The strangling hero sprang up with a relieving snort.
passages.vernacular: 被嗆得半窒息嘅英雄帶住解脫嘅哼聲跳起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被嗆得半窒息的英雄帶著解脫的哼聲跳起來。

passages.original: There was a whiz as of a missile in the air, mingled with the murmur of a curse, a sound as of shivering glass followed, and a small, vague form went over the fence and shot away in the gloom.
passages.vernacular: 空中傳嚟像飛彈似嘅嗖嘅一聲,夾雜住咒罵嘅低語,接住係玻璃破碎嘅聲音,一個小而模糊嘅身影翻過咗圍欄,消失喺黑暗中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空中傳來像飛彈似的嗖的一聲,夾雜著咒罵的低語,接著是玻璃破碎的聲音,一個小而模糊的身影翻過了圍欄,消失在黑暗中。

passages.original: Not long after, as Tom, all undressed for bed, was surveying his drenched garments by the light of a tallow dip, Sid woke up; but if he had any dim idea of making any “references to allusions,” he thought better of it and held his peace, for there was danger in Tom’s eye.
passages.vernacular: 不久後,湯姆脫光準備上床,喺牛油燭光下察睇佢被淋濕嘅衣服時,希德醒喇;但如果佢有任何模糊嘅念頭要作「對暗示嘅引述」,佢想想定係閉咗嘴,因為湯姆嘅眼睛裡有危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久後,湯姆脫光準備上床,在牛油燭光下察看他被淋濕的衣服時,希德醒了;但如果他有任何模糊的念頭要作「對暗示的引述」,他想想還是閉了嘴,因為湯姆的眼睛裡有危險。

passages.original: Tom turned in without the added vexation of prayers, and Sid made mental note of the omission.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆冇再增添祈禱嘅煩惱就上咗床,希德喺心裡記下咗呢個疏漏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆沒有再增添祈禱的煩惱就上了床,希德在心裡記下了這個疏漏。

chapters.title: Chapter IV: Mental Acrobatics 第四章:主日學校

passages.original: CH The sun rose upon a tranquil world, and beamed down upon the peaceful village like a benediction.
passages.vernacular: 太陽升起喺一個寧靜嘅世界上,像祝福一樣照耀住平靜嘅村莊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽升起在一個寧靜的世界上,像祝福一樣照耀著平靜的村莊。

passages.original: Breakfast over, Aunt Polly had family worship: it began with a prayer built from the ground up of solid courses of Scriptural quotations, welded together with a thin mortar of originality; and from the summit of this she delivered a grim chapter of the Mosaic Law, as from Sinai.
passages.vernacular: 早餐後,波莉姨媽進行家庭禮拜:開始係一篇用聖經引文嘅堅實層次從地基建起、用一層薄薄嘅原創灰漿焊接起嚟嘅禱告;佢從呢個頂峰宣讀咗一段嚴峻嘅摩西律法,如同從西奈山上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐後,波莉姨媽進行家庭禮拜:開始是一篇用聖經引文的堅實層次從地基建起、用一層薄薄的原創灰漿焊接起來的禱告;她從這個頂峰宣讀了一段嚴峻的摩西律法,如同從西奈山上。

passages.original: Then Tom girded up his loins, so to speak, and went to work to “get his verses.”
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆,可以講,束緊咗腰,去「背佢嘅經文」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆,可以說,束緊了腰,去「背他的經文」。

passages.original: Sid had learned his lesson days before.
passages.vernacular: 希德幾天前就學會咗佢嘅功課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德幾天前就學會了他的功課。

passages.original: Tom bent all his energies to the memorizing of five verses, and he chose part of the Sermon on the Mount, because he could find no verses that were shorter.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆用盡全力去記五節經文,佢選咗登山寶訓嘅一部分,因為佢找唔到更短嘅經文喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆用盡全力去記五節經文,他選了登山寶訓的一部分,因為他找不到更短的經文了。

passages.original: At the end of half an hour Tom had a vague general idea of his lesson, but no more, for his mind was traversing the whole field of human thought, and his hands were busy with distracting recreations.
passages.vernacular: 半個小時後湯姆對佢嘅功課有咗一個模糊嘅大概,僅此而已,因為佢嘅腦子喺整個人類思想領域遊蕩,佢嘅雙手忙住分散注意力嘅娛樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 半個小時後湯姆對他的功課有了一個模糊的大概,僅此而已,因為他的腦子在整個人類思想領域遊蕩,他的雙手忙著分散注意力的娛樂。

passages.original: Mary took his book to hear him recite, and he tried to find his way through the fog:
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗攞咗佢嘅書聽佢背誦,佢試圖穿過迷霧找到路:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗拿了他的書聽他背誦,他試圖穿過迷霧找到路:

passages.original: “Blessed are the—a—a—”
passages.vernacular: 「虛心嘅人有福喇——嗯——嗯——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「虛心的人有福了——嗯——嗯——」

passages.original: “Poor”—
“Yes—poor; blessed are the poor—a—a—”
passages.vernacular: 「對——窮;虛心嘅人有福喇——嗯——嗯——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對——窮;虛心的人有福了——嗯——嗯——」

passages.original: “In spirit—”
passages.vernacular: 「喺心靈上——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在心靈上——」

passages.original: “In spirit; blessed are the poor in spirit, for they—they—”
passages.vernacular: 「喺心靈上;窮嘅人有福喇,因為佢哋——佢哋——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在心靈上;窮的人有福了,因為他們——他們——」

passages.original: “Theirs—”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋嘅——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們的——」

passages.original: “For theirs.
passages.vernacular: 「因為佢哋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為他們的。

passages.original: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
passages.vernacular: 喺心靈上窮嘅人有福喇,因為天國係佢哋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在心靈上窮的人有福了,因為天國是他們的。

passages.original: Blessed are they that mourn, for they—they—”
passages.vernacular: 哀慟嘅人有福喇,因為佢哋——佢哋——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哀慟的人有福了,因為他們——他們——」

passages.original: “Sh—”
“For they—a—”
passages.vernacular: 「因為佢哋——嗯——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為他們——嗯——」

passages.original: “For they S, H—Oh, I don’t know what it is!”
passages.vernacular: 「因為佢哋將、將——哦,我唔知道係乜嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為他們將、將——哦,我不知道是什麼!」

passages.original: “Shall!”
passages.vernacular: 「將要!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「將要!」

passages.original: “Oh, shall! for they shall—for they shall—a—a—shall mourn—a—a—blessed are they that shall—they that—a—they that shall mourn, for they shall—a—shall what?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,將要!因為佢哋將要——因為佢哋將要——嗯——嗯——將要哀慟——嗯——嗯——哀慟嘅人有福喇,佢哋將要——佢哋——嗯——佢哋將要哀慟,因為佢哋將要——嗯——將要乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,將要!因為他們將要——因為他們將要——嗯——嗯——將要哀慟——嗯——嗯——哀慟的人有福了,他們將要——他們——嗯——他們將要哀慟,因為他們將要——嗯——將要什麼?

passages.original: Why don’t you tell me, Mary?—what do you want to be so mean for?”
passages.vernacular: 你點解不告訴我,瑪麗?——你點解咁壞?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼不告訴我,瑪麗?——你為什麼那麼壞?」

passages.original: “Oh, Tom, you poor thick-headed thing, I’m not teasing you.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆,你呢個可憐嘅笨腦袋,我唔係喺逗你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆,你這個可憐的笨腦袋,我不是在逗你。

passages.original: I wouldn’t do that.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會嗰樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會那樣做。

passages.original: You must go and learn it again.
passages.vernacular: 你必須去重新學。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你必須去重新學。

passages.original: Don’t you be discouraged, Tom, you’ll manage it—and if you do, I’ll give you something ever so nice.
passages.vernacular: 別灰心,湯姆,你會成功嘅——如果你成功喇,我畀你一樣好好嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別灰心,湯姆,你會成功的——如果你成功了,我給你一樣非常好的東西。

passages.original: There, now, that’s a good boy.”
passages.vernacular: 好喇,真係個好細路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,真是個好孩子。」

passages.original: “All right!
passages.vernacular: 「好吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧!

passages.original: What is it, Mary, tell me what it is.”
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢,瑪麗,告訴我係乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼,瑪麗,告訴我是什麼。」

passages.original: “Never you mind, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「別管,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別管,湯姆。

passages.original: You know if I say it’s nice, it is nice.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道如果我講好,就係好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道如果我說好,就是好。」

passages.original: “You bet you that’s so, Mary.
passages.vernacular: 「你講得對,瑪麗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說得對,瑪麗。

passages.original: All right, I’ll tackle it again.”
passages.vernacular: 好吧,我再試試。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,我再試試。」

passages.original: And he did “tackle it again”—and under the double pressure of curiosity and prospective gain he did it with such spirit that he accomplished a shining success.
passages.vernacular: 佢真嘅「再試」喇——喺好奇心同預期得益嘅雙重壓力下,佢咁有精神地做喇,取得咗輝煌嘅成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他真的「再試」了——在好奇心和預期得益的雙重壓力下,他那麼有精神地做了,取得了輝煌的成功。

passages.original: Mary gave him a brand-new “Barlow” knife worth twelve and a half cents; and the convulsion of delight that swept his system shook him to his foundations.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗畀咗佢一把全新嘅「巴洛」刀,值十二分半;嗰陣席捲佢全身嘅狂喜痙攣把佢震得根基動搖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗給了他一把全新的「巴洛」刀,值十二分半;那陣席捲他全身的狂喜痙攣把他震得根基動搖。

passages.original: True, the knife would not cut anything, but it was a “sure-enough” Barlow, and there was inconceivable grandeur in that—though where the Western boys ever got the idea that such a weapon could possibly be counterfeited to its injury is an imposing mystery and will always remain so, perhaps.
passages.vernacular: 誠然,呢把刀乜嘢都切不喇,但佢係貨真價實嘅巴洛刀,其中有難以想像嘅宏偉——雖然西部嘅男孩哋從邊度得嚟呢種念頭,認為呢種武器可能被偽造,從而損害佢,呢個係一個令人印象深刻嘅謎,或者永遠都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠然,這把刀什麼也切不了,但它是貨真價實的巴洛刀,其中有難以想像的宏偉——雖然西部的男孩們從哪裡得來這種念頭,認為這種武器可能被偽造,從而損害它,這是一個令人印象深刻的謎,也許永遠都是。

passages.original: Tom contrived to scarify the cupboard with it, and was arranging to begin on the bureau, when he was called off to dress for Sunday-school.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆設法用佢喺碗櫃上劃咗道道,正在準備開始喺衣櫥上動手,呢陣佢被叫去換衣服上主日學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆設法用它在碗櫃上劃了道道,正在準備開始在衣櫥上動手,這時他被叫去換衣服上主日學校。

passages.original: Mary gave him a tin basin of water and a piece of soap, and he went outside the door and set the basin on a little bench there; then he dipped the soap in the water and laid it down; turned up his sleeves; poured out the water on the ground, gently, and then entered the kitchen and began to wipe his face diligently on the towel behind the door.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗畀咗佢一個錫盆水同一塊肥皂,佢走到門外,把盆放喺嗰度一張小凳上;然後佢把肥皂浸喺水裡,放下;捲起袖子;輕輕地把水倒喺地上,然後進咗廚房,開始認真地喺門後嘅毛巾上擦臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗給了他一個錫盆水和一塊肥皂,他走到門外,把盆放在那裡一張小凳上;然後他把肥皂浸在水裡,放下;捲起袖子;輕輕地把水倒在地上,然後進了廚房,開始認真地在門後的毛巾上擦臉。

passages.original: But Mary removed the towel and said:
passages.vernacular: 但瑪麗攞走咗毛巾,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但瑪麗拿走了毛巾,說:

passages.original: “Now ain’t you ashamed, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「你不覺得羞恥嗎,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不覺得羞恥嗎,湯姆。

passages.original: You mustn’t be so bad.
passages.vernacular: 你不可以咁壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不可以這麼壞。

passages.original: Water won’t hurt you.”
passages.vernacular: 水唔會傷害你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 水不會傷害你。」

passages.original: Tom was a trifle disconcerted.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆有點唔知所措。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆有點不知所措。

passages.original: The basin was refilled, and this time he stood over it a little while, gathering resolution; took in a big breath and began.
passages.vernacular: 盆又裝滿咗水,呢次佢站喺上面一會兒,鼓足決心;深吸咗一大口氣,開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 盆又裝滿了水,這次他站在上面一會兒,鼓足決心;深吸了一大口氣,開始了。

passages.original: When he entered the kitchen presently, with both eyes shut and groping for the towel with his hands, an honorable testimony of suds and water was dripping from his face.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢進廚房時,雙眼緊閉,用手摸索住毛巾,一份肥皂泡同水嘅光榮證明正從佢臉上滴下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他進廚房時,雙眼緊閉,用手摸索著毛巾,一份肥皂泡和水的光榮證明正從他臉上滴下。

passages.original: But when he emerged from the towel, he was not yet satisfactory, for the clean territory stopped short at his chin and his jaws, like a mask; below and beyond this line there was a dark expanse of unirrigated soil that spread downward in front and backward around his neck.
passages.vernacular: 但佢從毛巾後出嚟時,仍然不令人滿意,因為乾淨嘅區域喺下巴同兩腮就停住喇,像個面具;呢條線以下同以外係一大片未灌溉嘅黑土,向下蔓延到前面,向後環繞佢嘅脖子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他從毛巾後出來時,仍然不令人滿意,因為乾淨的區域在下巴和兩腮就停住了,像個面具;這條線以下和以外是一大片未灌溉的黑土,向下蔓延到前面,向後環繞他的脖子。

passages.original: Mary took him in hand, and when she was done with him he was a man and a brother, without distinction of color, and his saturated hair was neatly brushed, and its short curls wrought into a dainty and symmetrical general effect.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗接手管佢,佢弄完後,佢成咗個人同兄弟,不分膚色,佢濕透嘅頭髮被整齊地刷好,短捲髮被弄出一種精緻對稱嘅整體效果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗接手管他,她弄完後,他成了個人和兄弟,不分膚色,他濕透的頭髮被整齊地刷好,短捲髮被弄出一種精緻對稱的整體效果。

passages.original: [He privately smoothed out the curls, with labor and difficulty, and plastered his hair close down to his head; for he held curls to be effeminate, and his own filled his life with bitterness.]
passages.vernacular: [佢私下費力艱難地把捲髮弄平,把頭髮緊貼喺頭上抹平;因為佢認為捲髮係女氣嘅,而佢自己嘅捲髮使佢嘅生活充滿苦澀。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [他私下費力艱難地把捲髮弄平,把頭髮緊貼在頭上抹平;因為他認為捲髮是女氣的,而他自己的捲髮使他的生活充滿苦澀。]

passages.original: Then Mary got out a suit of his clothing that had been used only on Sundays during two years—they were simply called his “other clothes”—and so by that we know the size of his wardrobe.
passages.vernacular: 然後瑪麗攞出一套佢嘅衣服,兩年嚟只喺星期日穿過——佢哋被簡單稱為佢嘅「另一套衣服」——由此我哋知道佢嘅衣櫥有多大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後瑪麗拿出一套他的衣服,兩年來只在星期日穿過——它們被簡單稱為他的「另一套衣服」——由此我們知道他的衣櫥有多大。

passages.original: The girl “put him to rights” after he had dressed himself; she buttoned his neat roundabout up to his chin, turned his vast shirt collar down over his shoulders, brushed him off and crowned him with his speckled straw hat.
passages.vernacular: 女孩喺佢穿好衣服後「把佢整理好」;佢把佢整潔嘅外衣扣到下巴,把佢寬大嘅襯衫領子翻下蓋住肩膀,畀佢拍掉灰塵,畀佢戴上有斑點嘅草帽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩在他穿好衣服後「把他整理好」;她把他整潔的外衣扣到下巴,把他寬大的襯衫領子翻下蓋住肩膀,給他拍掉灰塵,給他戴上有斑點的草帽。

passages.original: He now looked exceedingly improved and uncomfortable.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家睇起嚟大有改進,而且極不舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在看起來大有改進,而且極不舒服。

passages.original: He was fully as uncomfortable as he looked; for there was a restraint about whole clothes and cleanliness that galled him.
passages.vernacular: 佢都確實像睇起嚟嗰樣不舒服;因為穿住完整嘅衣服同乾淨有一種拘束,使佢難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他也確實像看起來那樣不舒服;因為穿著完整的衣服和乾淨有一種拘束,使他難受。

passages.original: He hoped that Mary would forget his shoes, but the hope was blighted; she coated them thoroughly with tallow, as was the custom, and brought them out.
passages.vernacular: 佢希望瑪麗會忘咗佢嘅鞋子,但希望落空;佢按習慣喺上面徹底塗咗牛油,攞咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他希望瑪麗會忘了他的鞋子,但希望落空;她按習慣在上面徹底塗了牛油,拿了出來。

passages.original: He lost his temper and said he was always being made to do everything he didn’t want to do.
passages.vernacular: 佢發咗脾氣,講佢總是被迫做所有佢唔想做嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他發了脾氣,說他總是被迫做所有他不想做的事。

passages.original: But Mary said, persuasively:
passages.vernacular: 但瑪麗勸講道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但瑪麗勸說道:

passages.original: “Please, Tom—that’s a good boy.”
passages.vernacular: 「求你,湯姆——呢才係好細路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「求你,湯姆——這才是好孩子。」

passages.original: So he got into the shoes snarling.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢咆哮住穿上咗鞋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他咆哮著穿上了鞋。

passages.original: Mary was soon ready, and the three children set out for Sunday-school—a place that Tom hated with his whole heart; but Sid and Mary were fond of it.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗好快準備好,三個細路出發去主日學校——湯姆全心恨嘅地方;但希德同瑪麗鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗很快準備好,三個孩子出發去主日學校——湯姆全心恨的地方;但希德和瑪麗喜歡它。

passages.original: Sabbath-school hours were from nine to half-past ten; and then church service.
passages.vernacular: 安息日學校嘅時間係九點到十點半;然後係教堂禮拜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安息日學校的時間是九點到十點半;然後是教堂禮拜。

passages.original: Two of the children always remained for the sermon voluntarily, and the other always remained too—for stronger reasons.
passages.vernacular: 兩個細路總是自願留下聽講道,另一個都總是留下——出於更強嘅理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個孩子總是自願留下聽講道,另一個也總是留下——出於更強的理由。

passages.original: The church’s high-backed, uncushioned pews would seat about three hundred persons; the edifice was but a small, plain affair, with a sort of pine board tree-box on top of it for a steeple.
passages.vernacular: 教堂高背無墊嘅長椅可坐三百人左右;建築只係個小而樸素嘅嘢,頂上有一個像松木板樹箱似嘅嘢當尖塔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 教堂高背無墊的長椅可坐三百人左右;建築只是個小而樸素的東西,頂上有一個像松木板樹箱似的東西當尖塔。

passages.original: At the door Tom dropped back a step and accosted a Sunday-dressed comrade:
passages.vernacular: 喺門口湯姆落後一步,向一個穿住主日服嘅同伴搭話:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在門口湯姆落後一步,向一個穿著主日服的同伴搭話:

passages.original: “Say, Billy, got a yaller ticket?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,比利,有黃票嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,比利,有黃票嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
“What’ll you take for her?”
passages.vernacular: 「你要乜嘢才肯賣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要什麼才肯賣?」

passages.original: “What’ll you give?”
passages.vernacular: 「你畀乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你給什麼?」

passages.original: “Piece of lickrish and a fish-hook.”
passages.vernacular: 「一片甘草糖同一個魚鉤。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一片甘草糖和一個魚鉤。」

passages.original: “Less see ’em.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看看。」

passages.original: Tom exhibited.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆展示喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆展示了。

passages.original: They were satisfactory, and the property changed hands.
passages.vernacular: 令人滿意,財產易手喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令人滿意,財產易手了。

passages.original: Then Tom traded a couple of white alleys for three red tickets, and some small trifle or other for a couple of blue ones.
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆用兩顆白色大理石彈珠換咗三張紅票,用一件小玩意換咗兩張藍票。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆用兩顆白色大理石彈珠換了三張紅票,用一件小玩意換了兩張藍票。

passages.original: He waylaid other boys as they came, and went on buying tickets of various colors ten or fifteen minutes longer.
passages.vernacular: 佢攔截其他嚟嘅男孩,繼續買咗各種顏色嘅票好鐘或十五分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他攔截其他來的男孩,繼續買了各種顏色的票十分鐘或十五分鐘。

passages.original: He entered the church, now, with a swarm of clean and noisy boys and girls, proceeded to his seat and started a quarrel with the first boy that came handy.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家隨住一群乾淨而吵鬧嘅男孩女孩進咗教堂,走到座位上,同第一個順手嘅男孩吵咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在隨著一群乾淨而吵鬧的男孩女孩進了教堂,走到座位上,同第一個順手的男孩吵了起來。

passages.original: The teacher, a grave, elderly man, interfered; then turned his back a moment and Tom pulled a boy’s hair in the next bench, and was absorbed in his book when the boy turned around; stuck a pin in another boy, presently, in order to hear him say “Ouch!” and got a new reprimand from his teacher.
passages.vernacular: 老師,一位嚴肅嘅年長男人,介入喇;然後佢轉身一會兒,湯姆扯咗下一排長椅一個男孩嘅頭髮,男孩轉過身時,佢正埋頭睇書;不久又用針扎另一個男孩,為了聽佢講「哎喲!」,佢又受到老師新一輪嘅訓斥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師,一位嚴肅的年長男人,介入了;然後他轉身一會兒,湯姆扯了下一排長椅一個男孩的頭髮,男孩轉過身時,他正埋頭看書;不久又用針扎另一個男孩,為了聽他說「哎喲!」,他又受到老師新一輪的訓斥。

passages.original: Tom’s whole class were of a pattern—restless, noisy, and troublesome.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆整個班都係一個模式——坐不住、吵鬧、愛惹麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆整個班都是一個模式——坐不住、吵鬧、愛惹麻煩。

passages.original: When they came to recite their lessons, not one of them knew his verses perfectly, but had to be prompted all along.
passages.vernacular: 輪到背誦功課時,佢哋冇一個人完美地記得經文,而係一直需要提示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輪到背誦功課時,他們沒有一個人完美地記得經文,而是一直需要提示。

passages.original: However, they worried through, and each got his reward—in small blue tickets, each with a passage of Scripture on it; each blue ticket was pay for two verses of the recitation.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢哋勉強通過,每個人得到咗獎勵——小藍票,每張上面有一段聖經經文;每張藍票係兩節背誦嘅報酬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,他們勉強通過,每個人得到了獎勵——小藍票,每張上面有一段聖經經文;每張藍票是兩節背誦的報酬。

passages.original: Ten blue tickets equalled a red one, and could be exchanged for it; ten red tickets equalled a yellow one; for ten yellow tickets the superintendent gave a very plainly bound Bible (worth forty cents in those easy times) to the pupil.
passages.vernacular: 十張藍票等於一張紅票,可以換;十張紅票等於一張黃票;十張黃票,監督畀學生一本裝訂好樸素嘅聖經(喺嗰個容易嘅時代值四好)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十張藍票等於一張紅票,可以換;十張紅票等於一張黃票;十張黃票,監督給學生一本裝訂非常樸素的聖經(在那個容易的時代值四十分)。

passages.original: How many of my readers would have the industry and application to memorize two thousand verses, even for a Doré Bible?
passages.vernacular: 我嘅讀者中有多少人有勤奮同專注去背兩千節經文,即使為了一本多雷插圖聖經?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的讀者中有多少人有勤奮和專注去背兩千節經文,即使為了一本多雷插圖聖經?

passages.original: And yet Mary had acquired two Bibles in this way—it was the patient work of two years—and a boy of German parentage had won four or five.
passages.vernacular: 然而瑪麗就係咁樣得到咗兩本聖經——呢個係兩年嘅耐心工作——一個德國籍父母嘅男孩贏咗四五本。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而瑪麗就是這樣得到了兩本聖經——這是兩年的耐心工作——一個德國籍父母的男孩贏了四五本。

passages.original: He once recited three thousand verses without stopping; but the strain upon his mental faculties was too great, and he was little better than an idiot from that day forth—a grievous misfortune for the school, for on great occasions, before company, the superintendent (as Tom expressed it) had always made this boy come out and “spread himself.”
passages.vernacular: 佢曾經不停地背誦三千節經文;但對佢智力嘅壓力太大,從嗰天起佢比白癡好不咗多少——呢對學校係慘重嘅不幸,因為喺重大場合,有賓客在場時,監督(如湯姆所講)總是叫呢個男孩出嚟「大展身手」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他曾經不停地背誦三千節經文;但對他智力的壓力太大,從那天起他比白癡好不了多少——這對學校是慘重的不幸,因為在重大場合,有賓客在場時,監督(如湯姆所說)總是叫這個男孩出來「大展身手」。

passages.original: Only the older pupils managed to keep their tickets and stick to their tedious work long enough to get a Bible, and so the delivery of one of these prizes was a rare and noteworthy circumstance; the successful pupil was so great and conspicuous for that day that on the spot every scholar’s heart was fired with a fresh ambition that often lasted a couple of weeks.
passages.vernacular: 只有較大嘅學生設法保存佢哋嘅票、堅持佢哋單調嘅工作足夠長嘅時間得到一本聖經,所以頒發呢啲獎品之一係罕見而值得注意嘅情況;成功嘅學生喺嗰天係咁偉大顯眼,以致當場每個學生嘅心都燃起新嘅野心,往往持續一兩個星期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有較大的學生設法保存他們的票、堅持他們單調的工作足夠長的時間得到一本聖經,所以頒發這些獎品之一是罕見而值得注意的情況;成功的學生在那天是那麼偉大顯眼,以致當場每個學生的心都燃起新的野心,往往持續一兩個星期。

passages.original: It is possible that Tom’s mental stomach had never really hungered for one of those prizes, but unquestionably his entire being had for many a day longed for the glory and the eclat that came with it.
passages.vernacular: 或者湯姆嘅精神胃口從未真正渴望過呢啲獎品,但毫無疑問佢整個人多日以來渴望隨之而嚟嘅榮耀同光彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許湯姆的精神胃口從未真正渴望過這些獎品,但毫無疑問他整個人多日以來渴望隨之而來的榮耀和光彩。

passages.original: In due course the superintendent stood up in front of the pulpit, with a closed hymn-book in his hand and his forefinger inserted between its leaves, and commanded attention.
passages.vernacular: 不久監督站喺講壇前,手裡攞住合上嘅讚美詩集,食指夾喺書頁間,要求注意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久監督站在講壇前,手裡拿著合上的讚美詩集,食指夾在書頁間,要求注意。

passages.original: When a Sunday-school superintendent makes his customary little speech, a hymn-book in the hand is as necessary as is the inevitable sheet of music in the hand of a singer who stands forward on the platform and sings a solo at a concert—though why, is a mystery: for neither the hymn-book nor the sheet of music is ever referred to by the sufferer.
passages.vernacular: 主日學校監督發表佢慣常嘅小演講時,手裡攞一本讚美詩集,就像站喺台前喺音樂會上獨唱嘅歌手手裡攞住不可避免嘅樂譜一樣必要——雖然點解,係個謎:因為受難者從不參考讚美詩集或樂譜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主日學校監督發表他慣常的小演講時,手裡拿一本讚美詩集,就像站在台前在音樂會上獨唱的歌手手裡拿著不可避免的樂譜一樣必要——雖然為什麼,是個謎:因為受難者從不參考讚美詩集或樂譜。

passages.original: This superintendent was a slim creature of thirty-five, with a sandy goatee and short sandy hair; he wore a stiff standing-collar whose upper edge almost reached his ears and whose sharp points curved forward abreast the corners of his mouth—a fence that compelled a straight lookout ahead, and a turning of the whole body when a side view was required; his chin was propped on a spreading cravat which was as broad and as long as a bank-note, and had fringed ends; his boot toes were turned sharply up, in the fashion of the day, like sleigh-runners—an effect patiently and laboriously produced by the young men by sitting with their toes pressed against a wall for hours together.
passages.vernacular: 呢位監督係個三十五歲嘅瘦削生物,留住沙色山羊鬍同短短嘅沙色頭髮;佢戴住一個硬立領,上緣幾乎到耳朵,尖角向前彎曲到同嘴角平齊——一道迫使人只能向前直視嘅籬笆,需要睇側面時要轉動整個身體;佢嘅下巴撐喺一條張開嘅領巾上,領巾像鈔票一樣寬、一樣長,末端有流蘇;佢嘅靴尖急劇上翹,按當時嘅時尚,像雪橇滑板——呢個效果係年輕人通過把腳趾壓喺牆上坐上好幾個小時而耐心辛苦造出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位監督是個三十五歲的瘦削生物,留著沙色山羊鬍和短短的沙色頭髮;他戴著一個硬立領,上緣幾乎到耳朵,尖角向前彎曲到與嘴角平齊——一道迫使人只能向前直視的籬笆,需要看側面時要轉動整個身體;他的下巴撐在一條張開的領巾上,領巾像鈔票一樣寬、一樣長,末端有流蘇;他的靴尖急劇上翹,按當時的時尚,像雪橇滑板——這個效果是年輕人通過把腳趾壓在牆上坐上好幾個小時而耐心辛苦造出來的。

passages.original: Mr. Walters was very earnest of mien, and very sincere and honest at heart; and he held sacred things and places in such reverence, and so separated them from worldly matters, that unconsciously to himself his Sunday-school voice had acquired a peculiar intonation which was wholly absent on week-days.
passages.vernacular: 沃爾特斯先生神態好認真,內心好真誠誠實;佢對神聖嘅事物同地方如此崇敬,並把佢哋同世俗事務分得咁開,以致佢自己唔知不覺地,佢嘅主日學校聲音獲得咗一種特殊嘅語調,呢喺平日完全冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沃爾特斯先生神態非常認真,內心非常真誠誠實;他對神聖的事物和地方如此崇敬,並把它們與世俗事務分得那麼開,以致他自己不知不覺地,他的主日學校聲音獲得了一種特殊的語調,這在平日完全沒有。

passages.original: He began after this fashion:
passages.vernacular: 佢以呢種方式開始:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他以這種方式開始:

passages.original: “Now, children, I want you all to sit up just as straight and pretty as you can and give me all your attention for a minute or two.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,細路哋,我要你哋都盡可能坐得又直又漂亮,畀我一兩分鐘嘅全部注意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,孩子們,我要你們都盡可能坐得又直又漂亮,給我一兩分鐘的全部注意。

passages.original: There—that is it.
passages.vernacular: 好——就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好——就是這樣。

passages.original: That is the way good little boys and girls should do.
passages.vernacular: 好小孩應該就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好小孩應該就是這樣。

passages.original: I see one little girl who is looking out of the window—I am afraid she thinks I am out there somewhere—perhaps up in one of the trees making a speech to the little birds.
passages.vernacular: 我睇到一個小女孩喺睇窗外——我怕佢以為我喺外面某個地方——或者喺一棵樹上對小鳥發表演講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看到一個小女孩在看窗外——我怕她以為我在外面某個地方——也許在一棵樹上對小鳥發表演講。

passages.original: [Applausive titter.]
passages.vernacular: [讚許嘅竊笑。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [讚許的竊笑。]

passages.original: I want to tell you how good it makes me feel to see so many bright, clean little faces assembled in a place like this, learning to do right and be good.”
passages.vernacular: 我想告訴你哋,睇到咁多明亮乾淨嘅小臉聚集喺咁樣嘅地方,學習做正確嘅事、做好人,我感到幾咁好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想告訴你們,看到這麼多明亮乾淨的小臉聚集在這樣的地方,學習做正確的事、做好人,我感到多麼好。」

passages.original: And so forth and so on.
passages.vernacular: 諸如此類。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 諸如此類。

passages.original: It is not necessary to set down the rest of the oration.
passages.vernacular: 冇必要記下演講嘅其餘部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有必要記下演說的其餘部分。

passages.original: It was of a pattern which does not vary, and so it is familiar to us all.
passages.vernacular: 佢屬於一種永不變嘅模式,所以我哋都好熟悉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它屬於一種永不變的模式,所以我們都很熟悉。

passages.original: The latter third of the speech was marred by the resumption of fights and other recreations among certain of the bad boys, and by fidgetings and whisperings that extended far and wide, washing even to the bases of isolated and incorruptible rocks like Sid and Mary.
passages.vernacular: 演講嘅後三分之一被啲壞男孩又開始打架同其他消遣所破壞,被廣泛蔓延嘅坐立不安同竊竊私語所破壞,甚至沖刷到像希德同瑪麗咁樣孤立不可腐蝕嘅岩石腳下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 演講的後三分之一被一些壞男孩又開始打架和其他消遣所破壞,被廣泛蔓延的坐立不安和竊竊私語所破壞,甚至沖刷到像希德和瑪麗這樣孤立不可腐蝕的岩石腳下。

passages.original: But now every sound ceased suddenly, with the subsidence of Mr. Walters’ voice, and the conclusion of the speech was received with a burst of silent gratitude.
passages.vernacular: 但而家隨住沃爾特斯先生聲音嘅平息,所有聲音突然停止,演講嘅結束得到一陣無聲嘅感激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在隨著沃爾特斯先生聲音的平息,所有聲音突然停止,演講的結束得到一陣無聲的感激。

passages.original: A good part of the whispering had been occasioned by an event which was more or less rare—the entrance of visitors: lawyer Thatcher, accompanied by a very feeble and aged man; a fine, portly, middle-aged gentleman with iron-gray hair; and a dignified lady who was doubtless the latter’s wife.
passages.vernacular: 相當多嘅竊竊私語係由一個比較罕見嘅事件引起嘅——訪客嘅進入:撒切爾律師,陪住一位好虛弱年老嘅男人;一位儀表堂堂、身材魁梧、頭髮鐵灰色嘅中年紳士;同一位威嚴嘅女士,毫無疑問係後者嘅妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相當多的竊竊私語是由一個比較罕見的事件引起的——訪客的進入:撒切爾律師,陪著一位非常虛弱年老的男人;一位儀表堂堂、身材魁梧、頭髮鐵灰色的中年紳士;和一位威嚴的女士,毫無疑問是後者的妻子。

passages.original: The lady was leading a child.
passages.vernacular: 女士牽住一個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女士牽著一個孩子。

passages.original: Tom had been restless and full of chafings and repinings; conscience-smitten, too—he could not meet Amy Lawrence’s eye, he could not brook her loving gaze.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆一直坐立不安,充滿惱怒同不滿;都受到良心嘅譴責——佢唔敢面對艾米·勞倫斯嘅眼睛,佢唔能夠忍受佢深情嘅凝視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆一直坐立不安,充滿惱怒和不滿;也受到良心的譴責——他不敢面對艾米·勞倫斯的眼睛,他不能忍受她深情的凝視。

passages.original: But when he saw this small newcomer his soul was all ablaze with bliss in a moment.
passages.vernacular: 但佢睇到呢個小新嚟者時,轉眼間佢嘅靈魂全被喜悅燃燒起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他看到這個小新來者時,轉眼間他的靈魂全被喜悅燃燒起來。

passages.original: The next moment he was “showing off” with all his might—cuffing boys, pulling hair, making faces—in a word, using every art that seemed likely to fascinate a girl and win her applause.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻佢拼命地「表演」——打男孩哋嘅頭、扯頭髮、做鬼臉——一句話,使用似乎可能迷住女孩、贏得佢掌聲嘅一切手段。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻他拼命地「表演」——打男孩們的頭、扯頭髮、做鬼臉——一句話,使用似乎可能迷住女孩、贏得她掌聲的一切手段。

passages.original: His exaltation had but one alloy—the memory of his humiliation in this angel’s garden—and that record in sand was fast washing out, under the waves of happiness that were sweeping over it now.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅興奮只有一種雜質——記得佢喺呢位天使嘅花園裡嘅羞辱——而嗰沙上嘅記錄,喺而家席捲佢嘅幸福浪潮下,正迅速被沖掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的興奮只有一種雜質——記得他在這位天使的花園裡的羞辱——而那沙上的記錄,在現在席捲它的幸福浪潮下,正迅速被沖掉。

passages.original: The visitors were given the highest seat of honor, and as soon as Mr. Walters’ speech was finished, he introduced them to the school.
passages.vernacular: 訪客被安排喺最尊貴嘅位置,沃爾特斯先生嘅演講一結束,佢就向學校介紹佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 訪客被安排在最尊貴的位置,沃爾特斯先生的演講一結束,他就向學校介紹他們。

passages.original: The middle-aged man turned out to be a prodigious personage—no less a one than the county judge—altogether the most august creation these children had ever looked upon—and they wondered what kind of material he was made of—and they half wanted to hear him roar, and were half afraid he might, too.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位中年男人原來係個了不起嘅人物——唔係別人,正是縣法官——係呢啲細路見過嘅最威嚴嘅創造物——佢哋想知道佢係由乜嘢材料做成嘅——佢哋半想聽佢咆哮,又半怕佢會咆哮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位中年男人原來是個了不起的人物——不是別人,正是縣法官——是這些孩子見過的最威嚴的創造物——他們想知道他是由什麼材料做成的——他們半想聽他咆哮,又半怕他會咆哮。

passages.original: He was from Constantinople, twelve miles away—so he had travelled, and seen the world—these very eyes had looked upon the county court-house—which was said to have a tin roof.
passages.vernacular: 佢來自十二英里外嘅君士坦丁堡——所以佢旅行過,見過世面——呢雙眼睛睇過縣法院——據講佢有個錫皮屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來自十二英里外的君士坦丁堡——所以他旅行過,見過世面——這雙眼睛看過縣法院——據說它有個錫皮屋頂。

passages.original: The awe which these reflections inspired was attested by the impressive silence and the ranks of staring eyes.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲思考激起嘅敬畏,由令人印象深刻嘅沉默同一排排瞪大嘅眼睛證明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些思考激起的敬畏,由令人印象深刻的沉默和一排排瞪大的眼睛證明。

passages.original: This was the great Judge Thatcher, brother of their own lawyer.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係偉大嘅撒切爾法官,佢哋自己律師嘅兄弟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是偉大的撒切爾法官,他們自己律師的兄弟。

passages.original: Jeff Thatcher immediately went forward, to be familiar with the great man and be envied by the school.
passages.vernacular: 傑夫·撒切爾即刻走上前,同呢位大人物親近,並被學校羨慕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑夫·撒切爾馬上走上前,同這位大人物親近,並被學校羨慕。

passages.original: It would have been music to his soul to hear the whisperings:
passages.vernacular: 聽到竊竊私語對佢嘅靈魂來講係音樂:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到竊竊私語對他的靈魂來說是音樂:

passages.original: “Look at him, Jim!
passages.vernacular: 「睇佢,吉姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看他,吉姆!

passages.original: He’s a going up there.
passages.vernacular: 佢正走上去呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他正走上去呢。

passages.original: Say—look! he’s a going to shake hands with him—he is shaking hands with him!
passages.vernacular: 喂——睇!佢要同佢握手喇——佢正在同佢握手!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂——看!他要同他握手了——他正在同他握手!

passages.original: By jings, don’t you wish you was Jeff?”
passages.vernacular: 天呀,你不希望你係傑夫嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,你不希望你是傑夫嗎?」

passages.original: Mr. Walters fell to “showing off,” with all sorts of official bustlings and activities, giving orders, delivering judgments, discharging directions here, there, everywhere that he could find a target.
passages.vernacular: 沃爾特斯先生開始「表演」,忙忙碌碌地做各種官方活動,發命令、作判斷、喺佢能找到靶子嘅各處發布指示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沃爾特斯先生開始「表演」,忙忙碌碌地做各種官方活動,發命令、作判斷、在他能找到靶子的各處發布指示。

passages.original: The librarian “showed off”—running hither and thither with his arms full of books and making a deal of the splutter and fuss that insect authority delights in.
passages.vernacular: 圖書管理員「表演」——抱住滿懷嘅書跑嚟跑去,製造許多昆蟲權威鍾意嘅噴濺同忙亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 圖書管理員「表演」——抱著滿懷的書跑來跑去,製造許多昆蟲權威喜歡的噴濺和忙亂。

passages.original: The young lady teachers “showed off”—bending sweetly over pupils that were lately being boxed, lifting pretty warning fingers at bad little boys and patting good ones lovingly.
passages.vernacular: 年輕嘅女教師哋「表演」——甜美地俯身向最近剛被打過耳光嘅學生,對壞小男孩舉起漂亮嘅警告手指,愛撫好男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕的女教師們「表演」——甜美地俯身向最近剛被打過耳光的學生,對壞小男孩舉起漂亮的警告手指,愛撫好男孩。

passages.original: The young gentlemen teachers “showed off” with small scoldings and other little displays of authority and fine attention to discipline—and most of the teachers, of both sexes, found business up at the library, by the pulpit; and it was business that frequently had to be done over again two or three times (with much seeming vexation).
passages.vernacular: 年輕嘅男教師哋「表演」,小小嘅責備同其他小小嘅權威展示、對紀律嘅精細關注——大部分教師,不論男女,都喺講壇邊嘅圖書館找到咗事務;而呢啲事務常常要重做兩三次(帶住許多假裝嘅煩惱)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕的男教師們「表演」,小小的責備和其他小小的權威展示、對紀律的精細關注——大部分教師,不論男女,都在講壇邊的圖書館找到了事務;而這些事務常常要重做兩三次(帶著許多假裝的煩惱)。

passages.original: The little girls “showed off” in various ways, and the little boys “showed off” with such diligence that the air was thick with paper wads and the murmur of scufflings.
passages.vernacular: 小女孩哋以各種方式「表演」,小男孩哋咁勤奮地「表演」,空氣裡到處係紙團同扭打嘅嘈雜聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小女孩們以各種方式「表演」,小男孩們那麼勤奮地「表演」,空氣裡到處是紙團和扭打的嘈雜聲。

passages.original: And above it all the great man sat and beamed a majestic judicial smile upon all the house, and warmed himself in the sun of his own grandeur—for he was “showing off,” too.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢一切之上,大人物坐住,對全場露出威嚴嘅法官式微笑,喺自己偉大嘅陽光下取暖——因為佢都喺「表演」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這一切之上,大人物坐著,對全場露出威嚴的法官式微笑,在自己偉大的陽光下取暖——因為他也在「表演」。

passages.original: There was only one thing wanting to make Mr. Walters’ ecstasy complete, and that was a chance to deliver a Bible-prize and exhibit a prodigy.
passages.vernacular: 要使沃爾特斯先生嘅狂喜完整,只缺一件事,就係有機會頒發一本聖經獎並展示一個天才。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要使沃爾特斯先生的狂喜完整,只缺一件事,就是有機會頒發一本聖經獎並展示一個天才。

passages.original: Several pupils had a few yellow tickets, but none had enough—he had been around among the star pupils inquiring.
passages.vernacular: 幾個學生有幾張黃票,但冇人夠——佢喺明星學生中問過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾個學生有幾張黃票,但沒有人夠——他在明星學生中問過。

passages.original: He would have given worlds, now, to have that German lad back again with a sound mind.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家願意付出整個世界,把嗰個德國細路頭腦健全地找回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在願意付出整個世界,把那個德國孩子頭腦健全地找回來。

passages.original: And now at this moment, when hope was dead, Tom Sawyer came forward with nine yellow tickets, nine red tickets, and ten blue ones, and demanded a Bible.
passages.vernacular: 而而家呢一刻,希望已死時,湯姆·索亞攞住九張黃票、九張紅票同十張藍票走上前,要求一本聖經。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而現在這一刻,希望已死時,湯姆·索亞拿著九張黃票、九張紅票和十張藍票走上前,要求一本聖經。

passages.original: This was a thunderbolt out of a clear sky.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係晴天霹靂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是晴天霹靂。

passages.original: Walters was not expecting an application from this source for the next ten years.
passages.vernacular: 沃爾特斯冇指望呢個來源喺未來十年內提出申請。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沃爾特斯沒指望這個來源在未來十年內提出申請。

passages.original: But there was no getting around it—here were the certified checks, and they were good for their face.
passages.vernacular: 但冇辦法迴避——呢度係有證明嘅支票,而且按票面價值係有效嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有辦法迴避——這裡是有證明的支票,而且按票面價值是有效的。

passages.original: Tom was therefore elevated to a place with the Judge and the other elect, and the great news was announced from headquarters.
passages.vernacular: 因此湯姆被提升到法官同其他貴賓嘅位置,偉大嘅消息從總部宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此湯姆被提升到法官和其他貴賓的位置,偉大的消息從總部宣布。

passages.original: It was the most stunning surprise of the decade, and so profound was the sensation that it lifted the new hero up to the judicial one’s altitude, and the school had two marvels to gaze upon in place of one.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係呢個十年最驚人嘅意外,轟動如此之深,以致把新英雄提升到司法嘅高度,學校有兩個奇觀可睇,而唔係一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是這個十年最驚人的意外,轟動如此之深,以致把新英雄提升到司法的高度,學校有兩個奇觀可看,而不是一個。

passages.original: The boys were all eaten up with envy—but those that suffered the bitterest pangs were those who perceived too late that they themselves had contributed to this hated splendor by trading tickets to Tom for the wealth he had amassed in selling whitewashing privileges.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋都被嫉妒啃噬——但承受最痛苦嘅人係嗰啲太遲才察覺自己為呢可恨嘅光彩作出咗貢獻嘅人,佢哋為湯姆通過出售刷石灰水特權積累嘅財富而把票換畀咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們都被嫉妒啃噬——但承受最痛苦的人是那些太遲才察覺自己為這可恨的光彩作出了貢獻的人,他們為湯姆通過出售刷石灰水特權積累的財富而把票換給了他。

passages.original: These despised themselves, as being the dupes of a wily fraud, a guileful snake in the grass.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲人鄙視自己,覺得係狡猾騙局、草叢裡奸詐嘅蛇嘅受騙者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些人鄙視自己,覺得是狡猾騙局、草叢裡奸詐的蛇的受騙者。

passages.original: The prize was delivered to Tom with as much effusion as the superintendent could pump up under the circumstances; but it lacked somewhat of the true gush, for the poor fellow’s instinct taught him that there was a mystery here that could not well bear the light, perhaps; it was simply preposterous that this boy had warehoused two thousand sheaves of Scriptural wisdom on his premises—a dozen would strain his capacity, without a doubt.
passages.vernacular: 獎品以監督喺呢種情況下能擠出嘅盡可能多嘅熱情頒畀咗湯姆;但佢缺少啲真正嘅湧流,因為嗰可憐人嘅直覺告訴佢呢度有個或者經不起光照嘅謎;呢個男孩喺佢場地裡貯存咗兩千捆聖經智慧,簡直荒唐——十二捆毫無疑問會使佢嘅容量食緊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獎品以監督在這種情況下能擠出的盡可能多的熱情頒給了湯姆;但它缺少一些真正的湧流,因為那可憐人的直覺告訴他這裡有個也許經不起光照的謎;這個男孩在他場地裡貯存了兩千捆聖經智慧,簡直荒唐——十二捆毫無疑問會使他的容量吃緊。

passages.original: Amy Lawrence was proud and glad, and she tried to make Tom see it in her face—but he wouldn’t look.
passages.vernacular: 艾米·勞倫斯又驕傲又高興,佢試圖讓湯姆喺佢臉上睇到——但佢不睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾米·勞倫斯又驕傲又高興,她試圖讓湯姆在她臉上看到——但他不看。

passages.original: She wondered; then she was just a grain troubled; next a dim suspicion came and went—came again; she watched; a furtive glance told her worlds—and then her heart broke, and she was jealous, and angry, and the tears came and she hated everybody.
passages.vernacular: 佢感到奇怪;然後有點兒不安;接住一個模糊嘅懷疑嚟咗又去喇——又嚟喇;佢睇住;偷偷嘅一瞥告訴咗佢好多——然後佢嘅心碎喇,佢嫉妒、生氣,眼淚嚟喇,佢恨每個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她感到奇怪;然後有點兒不安;接著一個模糊的懷疑來了又去了——又來了;她看著;偷偷的一瞥告訴了她很多——然後她的心碎了,她嫉妒、生氣,眼淚來了,她恨每個人。

passages.original: Tom most of all (she thought).
passages.vernacular: 最恨湯姆(佢想)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最恨湯姆(她想)。

passages.original: Tom was introduced to the Judge; but his tongue was tied, his breath would hardly come, his heart quaked—partly because of the awful greatness of the man, but mainly because he was her parent.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆被介紹畀法官;但佢舌頭打結,呼吸幾乎出不嚟,心喺顫抖——部分係因為呢位大人物嘅可怕偉大,但主要係因為佢係佢嘅父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆被介紹給法官;但他舌頭打結,呼吸幾乎出不來,心在顫抖——部分是因為這位大人物的可怕偉大,但主要是因為他是她的父親。

passages.original: He would have liked to fall down and worship him, if it were in the dark.
passages.vernacular: 如果係喺黑暗中,佢會好想倒下對佢膜拜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是在黑暗中,他會很想倒下對他膜拜。

passages.original: The Judge put his hand on Tom’s head and called him a fine little man, and asked him what his name was.
passages.vernacular: 法官把手放喺湯姆頭上,稱佢為好小伙子,問佢叫乜嘢名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法官把手放在湯姆頭上,稱他為好小伙子,問他叫什麼名字。

passages.original: The boy stammered, gasped, and got it out:
passages.vernacular: 男孩結結巴巴、喘住氣,講咗出嚟:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩結結巴巴、喘著氣,說了出來:

passages.original: “Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆。」

passages.original: “Oh, no, not Tom—it is—”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,唔係湯姆——係——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,不是湯姆——是——」

passages.original: “Thomas.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯瑪斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯瑪斯。」

passages.original: “Ah, that’s it.
passages.vernacular: 「啊,就係呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,就是這個。

passages.original: I thought there was more to it, maybe.
passages.vernacular: 我想或者仲有更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想也許還有更多。

passages.original: That’s very well.
passages.vernacular: 好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很好。

passages.original: But you’ve another one I daresay, and you’ll tell it to me, won’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 但我敢講你仲有另一個,你會告訴我嘅,係吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我敢說你還有另一個,你會告訴我的,是吧?」

passages.original: “Tell the gentleman your other name, Thomas,” said Walters, “and say sir.
passages.vernacular: 「告訴呢位先生你嘅另一個名字,湯瑪斯,」沃爾特斯講,「仲要講先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴這位先生你的另一個名字,湯瑪斯,」沃爾特斯說,「還要說先生。

passages.original: You mustn’t forget your manners.”
passages.vernacular: 你唔能夠忘咗禮貌。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不能忘了禮貌。」

passages.original: “Thomas Sawyer—sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯瑪斯·索亞——先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯瑪斯·索亞——先生。」

passages.original: “That’s it!
passages.vernacular: 「就係喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是了!

passages.original: That’s a good boy.
passages.vernacular: 好細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好孩子。

passages.original: Fine boy.
passages.vernacular: 好男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好男孩。

passages.original: Fine, manly little fellow.
passages.vernacular: 好嘅、有男子氣概嘅小伙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好的、有男子氣概的小伙子。

passages.original: Two thousand verses is a great many—very, very great many.
passages.vernacular: 兩千節經文係好多——好、好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩千節經文是很多——非常、非常多。

passages.original: And you never can be sorry for the trouble you took to learn them; for knowledge is worth more than anything there is in the world; it’s what makes great men and good men; you’ll be a great man and a good man yourself, some day, Thomas, and then you’ll look back and say, It’s all owing to the precious Sunday-school privileges of my boyhood—it’s all owing to my dear teachers that taught me to learn—it’s all owing to the good superintendent, who encouraged me, and watched over me, and gave me a beautiful Bible—a splendid elegant Bible—to keep and have it all for my own, always—it’s all owing to right bringing up!
passages.vernacular: 你永遠唔會為學習佢哋所費嘅功夫後悔;因為知識比世界上任何嘢都更有價值;係佢造就偉大嘅人同好人;有一天你自己都會成為偉大嘅人同好人,湯瑪斯,嗰時你會回顧講,呢全歸功於我童年寶貴嘅主日學校嘅恩典——全歸功於教我學習嘅親愛嘅老師哋——全歸功於鼓勵我、睇顧我、畀咗我一本美麗嘅聖經——一本華麗優雅嘅聖經——讓我永遠全部保存、擁有嘅好監督——呢全歸功於正確嘅教養!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你永遠不會為學習它們所費的功夫後悔;因為知識比世界上任何東西都更有價值;是它造就偉大的人和好人;有一天你自己也會成為偉大的人和好人,湯瑪斯,那時你會回顧說,這全歸功於我童年寶貴的主日學校的恩典——全歸功於教我學習的親愛的老師們——全歸功於鼓勵我、看顧我、給了我一本美麗的聖經——一本華麗優雅的聖經——讓我永遠全部保存、擁有的好監督——這全歸功於正確的教養!

passages.original: That is what you will say, Thomas—and you wouldn’t take any money for those two thousand verses—no indeed you wouldn’t.
passages.vernacular: 湯瑪斯,你會咁樣講——你唔會為嗰兩千節經文攞任何錢——不,你確實唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯瑪斯,你會這樣說——你不會為那兩千節經文拿任何錢——不,你確實不會。

passages.original: And now you wouldn’t mind telling me and this lady some of the things you’ve learned—no, I know you wouldn’t—for we are proud of little boys that learn.
passages.vernacular: 而家你唔會介意告訴我同呢位女士你學到嘅啲嘢吧——不,我知道你唔會——因為我哋為學習嘅小男孩驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你不會介意告訴我和這位女士你學到的一些東西吧——不,我知道你不會——因為我們為學習的小男孩驕傲。

passages.original: Now, no doubt you know the names of all the twelve disciples.
passages.vernacular: 而家,毫無疑問你知道十二門徒嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,毫無疑問你知道十二門徒的名字。

passages.original: Won’t you tell us the names of the first two that were appointed?”
passages.vernacular: 你願意告訴我哋最先被任命嘅兩位嘅名字嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你願意告訴我們最先被任命的兩位的名字嗎?」

passages.original: Tom was tugging at a button-hole and looking sheepish.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喺拉扯一個鈕扣孔,顯得羞怯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆在拉扯一個鈕扣孔,顯得羞怯。

passages.original: He blushed, now, and his eyes fell.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家臉紅喇,眼睛垂下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在臉紅了,眼睛垂下。

passages.original: Mr. Walters’ heart sank within him.
passages.vernacular: 沃爾特斯先生嘅心沉咗下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沃爾特斯先生的心沉了下去。

passages.original: He said to himself, it is not possible that the boy can answer the simplest question—why did the Judge ask him?
passages.vernacular: 佢對自己講,呢個男孩唔可能回答最簡單嘅問題——法官點解要問佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對自己說,這個男孩不可能回答最簡單的問題——法官為什麼要問他?

passages.original: Yet he felt obliged to speak up and say:
passages.vernacular: 然而佢覺得有義務開口講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而他覺得有義務開口說:

passages.original: “Answer the gentleman, Thomas—don’t be afraid.”
passages.vernacular: 「回答呢位先生,湯瑪斯——別怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回答這位先生,湯瑪斯——別怕。」

passages.original: Tom still hung fire.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆仍然遲遲不答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆仍然遲遲不答。

passages.original: “Now I know you’ll tell me,” said the lady.
passages.vernacular: 「而家我知道你會告訴我,」女士講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我知道你會告訴我,」女士說。

passages.original: “The names of the first two disciples were—”
passages.vernacular: 「最先兩位門徒嘅名字係——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最先兩位門徒的名字是——」

passages.original: “David and Goliah!”
passages.vernacular: 「大衛同歌利亞!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大衛和歌利亞!」

passages.original: Let us draw the curtain of charity over the rest of the scene.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋為呢一幕嘅其餘部分拉上仁慈嘅帷幕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們為這一幕的其餘部分拉上仁慈的帷幕。

chapters.title: Chapter V: A Useful Minister 第五章:教堂裡

passages.original: CH About half-past ten the cracked bell of the small church began to ring, and presently the people began to gather for the morning sermon.
passages.vernacular: 大約十點半,小教堂嗰口破鐘開始響喇,不久人哋開始聚集聽早晨嘅講道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約十點半,小教堂那口破鐘開始響了,不久人們開始聚集聽早晨的講道。

passages.original: The Sunday-school children distributed themselves about the house and occupied pews with their parents, so as to be under supervision.
passages.vernacular: 主日學校嘅細路哋分散喺教堂各處,同父母佔據長椅,以便受到監管。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主日學校的孩子們分散在教堂各處,同父母佔據長椅,以便受到監管。

passages.original: Aunt Polly came, and Tom and Sid and Mary sat with her—Tom being placed next the aisle, in order that he might be as far away from the open window and the seductive outside summer scenes as possible.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽嚟喇,湯姆、希德同瑪麗同佢坐喺一起——湯姆被安排喺靠過道嘅位置,以便盡可能遠離敞開嘅窗子同外面夏景嘅誘惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽來了,湯姆、希德和瑪麗同她坐在一起——湯姆被安排在靠過道的位置,以便盡可能遠離敞開的窗子和外面夏景的誘惑。

passages.original: The crowd filed up the aisles: the aged and needy postmaster, who had seen better days; the mayor and his wife—for they had a mayor there, among other unnecessaries; the justice of the peace; the widow Douglas, fair, smart, and forty, a generous, good-hearted soul and well-to-do, her hill mansion the only palace in the town, and the most hospitable and much the most lavish in the matter of festivities that St. Petersburg could boast; the bent and venerable Major and Mrs. Ward; lawyer Riverson, the new notable from a distance; next the belle of the village, followed by a troop of lawn-clad and ribbon-decked young heart-breakers; then all the young clerks in town in a body—for they had stood in the vestibule sucking their cane-heads, a circling wall of oiled and simpering admirers, till the last girl had run their gantlet; and last of all came the Model Boy, Willie Mufferson, taking as heedful care of his mother as if she were cut glass.
passages.vernacular: 人群沿住過道魚貫而入:年老而貧困嘅郵政局長,佢見過更好嘅日子;市長同佢嘅妻子——因為佢哋嗰度有市長,同其他唔使要嘅嘢;治安法官;道格拉斯寡婦,美麗、聰明、四十歲,一個慷慨、心地善良又富有嘅靈魂,佢山上嘅大宅係鎮上唯一嘅宮殿,喺聖彼得堡所能誇耀嘅款待同慶典嘅奢華上首屈一指;彎腰嘅令人尊敬嘅沃德少校及夫人;律師里弗森,遠方嚟嘅新名人;接下嚟係村裡嘅美人,後面跟住一群穿細麻布、戴絲帶裝飾嘅年輕「傷心製造者」;然後係鎮上所有嘅年輕店員成群結隊——因為佢哋站喺前廳吸著手杖頭,一道旋轉嘅、抹咗油嘅傻笑嘅仰慕者嘅牆,直到最後一個女孩穿過佢哋嘅夾道;最後來嘅係模範男孩,威利·馬弗森,像照顧一件切割玻璃一樣仔細地照顧住佢嘅母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人群沿著過道魚貫而入:年老而貧困的郵政局長,他見過更好的日子;市長和他的妻子——因為他們那裡有市長,和其他不必要的東西;治安法官;道格拉斯寡婦,美麗、聰明、四十歲,一個慷慨、心地善良又富有的靈魂,她山上的大宅是鎮上唯一的宮殿,在聖彼得堡所能誇耀的款待和慶典的奢華上首屈一指;彎腰的令人尊敬的沃德少校及夫人;律師里弗森,遠方來的新名人;接下來是村裡的美人,後面跟著一群穿細麻布、戴絲帶裝飾的年輕「傷心製造者」;然後是鎮上所有的年輕店員成群結隊——因為他們站在前廳吸著手杖頭,一道旋轉的、抹了油的傻笑的仰慕者的牆,直到最後一個女孩穿過他們的夾道;最後來的是模範男孩,威利·馬弗森,像照顧一件切割玻璃一樣仔細地照顧著他的母親。

passages.original: He always brought his mother to church, and was the pride of all the matrons.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是帶母親嚟教堂,係所有主婦嘅驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他總是帶母親來教堂,是所有主婦的驕傲。

passages.original: The boys all hated him, he was so good.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋都恨佢,佢太好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們都恨他,他太好了。

passages.original: And besides, he had been “thrown up to them” so much.
passages.vernacular: 而且,佢一直被「攞嚟畀佢哋比較」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,他一直被「拿來給他們比較」。

passages.original: His white handkerchief was hanging out of his pocket behind, as usual on Sundays—accidentally.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅白手帕像往常嘅星期日一樣從後面嘅口袋裡露出嚟——係偶然嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的白手帕像往常的星期日一樣從後面的口袋裡露出來——是偶然的。

passages.original: Tom had no handkerchief, and he looked upon boys who had as snobs.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆冇手帕,佢把有手帕嘅男孩睇作勢利小人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆沒有手帕,他把有手帕的男孩看作勢利小人。

passages.original: The congregation being fully assembled, now, the bell rang once more, to warn laggards and stragglers, and then a solemn hush fell upon the church which was only broken by the tittering and whispering of the choir in the gallery.
passages.vernacular: 會眾而家全部到齊,鐘又響咗一次,警告遲到者同落後者,然後一陣莊嚴嘅寂靜降臨教堂,只被樓座上唱詩班嘅竊笑同耳語打破。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 會眾現在全部到齊,鐘又響了一次,警告遲到者和落後者,然後一陣莊嚴的寂靜降臨教堂,只被樓座上唱詩班的竊笑和耳語打破。

passages.original: The choir always tittered and whispered all through service.
passages.vernacular: 唱詩班總是整個禮拜都喺竊笑同耳語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唱詩班總是整個禮拜都在竊笑和耳語。

passages.original: There was once a church choir that was not ill-bred, but I have forgotten where it was, now.
passages.vernacular: 曾經有一個教堂唱詩班冇教養不好,但我而家忘咗佢喺邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 曾經有一個教堂唱詩班沒有教養不好,但我現在忘了它在哪裡。

passages.original: It was a great many years ago, and I can scarcely remember anything about it, but I think it was in some foreign country.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係好多年前喇,我幾乎不記得關於佢嘅任何事,但我想嗰個係喺某個外國。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是很多年前了,我幾乎不記得關於它的任何事,但我想那是在某個外國。

passages.original: The minister gave out the hymn, and read it through with a relish, in a peculiar style which was much admired in that part of the country.
passages.vernacular: 牧師報咗讚美詩,津津有味地用一種獨特嘅風格讀咗一遍,呢種風格喺嗰一帶好受欣賞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師報了讚美詩,津津有味地用一種獨特的風格讀了一遍,這種風格在那一帶很受欣賞。

passages.original: His voice began on a medium key and climbed steadily up till it reached a certain point, where it bore with strong emphasis upon the topmost word and then plunged down as if from a spring-board:
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅聲音從中間嘅音調開始,穩步攀升,直到某個點,喺嗰度佢用強烈嘅重音強調最高嘅字,然後像從跳板上一樣俯衝下嚟:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的聲音從中間的音調開始,穩步攀升,直到某個點,在那裡他用強烈的重音強調最高的字,然後像從跳板上一樣俯衝下來:

passages.original: Shall I be car-ri-ed toe the skies, on flow’ry beds of ease,
passages.vernacular: 我會被帶到天上去嗎,躺喺鮮花盛開嘅安逸床上,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會被帶到天上去嗎,躺在鮮花盛開的安逸床上,

passages.original: Whilst others fight to win the prize, and sail thro’ blood -y seas?
passages.vernacular: 而別人奮鬥贏取獎賞,乘住血腥嘅海洋航行?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而別人奮鬥贏取獎賞,乘著血腥的海洋航行?

passages.original: He was regarded as a wonderful reader.
passages.vernacular: 佢被認為係一位出色嘅朗讀者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他被認為是一位出色的朗讀者。

passages.original: At church “sociables” he was always called upon to read poetry; and when he was through, the ladies would lift up their hands and let them fall helplessly in their laps, and “wall” their eyes, and shake their heads, as much as to say, “Words cannot express it; it is too beautiful, TOO beautiful for this mortal earth.”
passages.vernacular: 喺教堂嘅「聯誼會」上,總是請佢讀詩;佢讀完後,女士哋會舉起雙手,讓佢哋無助地落喺腿上,「翻」住眼睛,搖住頭,好像喺講:「言語無法表達;佢太美喇,對呢塵世太美喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在教堂的「聯誼會」上,總是請他讀詩;他讀完後,女士們會舉起雙手,讓它們無助地落在腿上,「翻」著眼睛,搖著頭,好像在說:「言語無法表達;它太美了,對這塵世太美了。」

passages.original: After the hymn had been sung, the Rev. Mr. Sprague turned himself into a bulletin-board, and read off “notices” of meetings and societies and things till it seemed that the list would stretch out to the crack of doom—a queer custom which is still kept up in America, even in cities, away here in this age of abundant newspapers.
passages.vernacular: 讚美詩唱完後,斯普拉格牧師把自己變成一塊公告板,宣讀會議、社團等等嘅「通告」,似乎名單要延伸到世界末日——呢個係一種古怪嘅習俗,喺美國至今仍保持住,即使喺城市裡,遠喺呢個報紙豐富嘅時代。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讚美詩唱完後,斯普拉格牧師把自己變成一塊公告板,宣讀會議、社團等等的「通告」,似乎名單要延伸到世界末日——這是一種古怪的習俗,在美國至今仍保持著,即使在城市裡,遠在這個報紙豐富的時代。

passages.original: Often, the less there is to justify a traditional custom, the harder it is to get rid of it.
passages.vernacular: 常常,一個傳統習俗越係缺乏理由,越難以擺脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 常常,一個傳統習俗越是缺乏理由,越難以擺脫。

passages.original: And now the minister prayed.
passages.vernacular: 而家牧師禱告喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在牧師禱告了。

passages.original: A good, generous prayer it was, and went into details: it pleaded for the church, and the little children of the church; for the other churches of the village; for the village itself; for the county; for the State; for the State officers; for the United States; for the churches of the United States; for Congress; for the President; for the officers of the Government; for poor sailors, tossed by stormy seas; for the oppressed millions groaning under the heel of European monarchies and Oriental despotisms; for such as have the light and the good tidings, and yet have not eyes to see nor ears to hear withal; for the heathen in the far islands of the sea; and closed with a supplication that the words he was about to speak might find grace and favor, and be as seed sown in fertile ground, yielding in time a grateful harvest of good.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一篇好嘅、慷慨嘅禱告,涉及細節:為教會同教會嘅小細路哋祈求;為村裡其他教會;為村子本身;為縣;為州;為州官員;為合眾國;為合眾國嘅各教會;為國會;為總統;為政府官員;為被暴風雨嘅海洋顛簸嘅可憐水手;為喺歐洲君主制同東方專制嘅腳跟下呻吟嘅受壓迫嘅數百萬人;為嗰啲有光同好消息,卻冇眼睛去睇、冇耳朵去聽嘅人;為遙遠海島嘅異教徒;最後以一個懇求結束,希望佢即將講嘅話能找到恩典同恩惠,像播種喺肥沃土壤裡嘅種子,時候到了結出感恩嘅善果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一篇好的、慷慨的禱告,涉及細節:為教會和教會的小孩子們祈求;為村裡其他教會;為村子本身;為縣;為州;為州官員;為合眾國;為合眾國的各教會;為國會;為總統;為政府官員;為被暴風雨的海洋顛簸的可憐水手;為在歐洲君主制和東方專制的腳跟下呻吟的受壓迫的數百萬人;為那些有光和好消息,卻沒有眼睛去看、沒有耳朵去聽的人;為遙遠海島的異教徒;最後以一個懇求結束,希望他即將說的話能找到恩典和恩惠,像播種在肥沃土壤裡的種子,時候到了結出感恩的善果。

passages.original: Amen.
passages.vernacular: 阿哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿們。

passages.original: There was a rustling of dresses, and the standing congregation sat down.
passages.vernacular: 一陣衣服窸窣聲,站住嘅會眾坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣衣服窸窣聲,站著的會眾坐下。

passages.original: The boy whose history this book relates did not enjoy the prayer, he only endured it—if he even did that much.
passages.vernacular: 本書所記述其歷史嘅男孩不鍾意呢個禱告,佢只係忍受佢——如果佢連呢個都做到嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本書所記述其歷史的男孩不喜歡這個禱告,他只是忍受它——如果他連這個也做到的話。

passages.original: He was restive all through it; he kept tally of the details of the prayer, unconsciously—for he was not listening, but he knew the ground of old, and the clergyman’s regular route over it—and when a little trifle of new matter was interlarded, his ear detected it and his whole nature resented it; he considered additions unfair, and scoundrelly.
passages.vernacular: 整個禱告期間佢都坐立不安;佢無意識地記錄禱告嘅細節——因為佢冇喺聽,但佢熟悉呢片土地,同牧師喺上面固定嘅路線——當啲新嘅小材料被夾進去時,佢嘅耳朵察覺到喇,佢整個天性都憤慨;佢認為增添不公平,而且係無賴行為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個禱告期間他都坐立不安;他無意識地記錄禱告的細節——因為他沒有在聽,但他熟悉這片土地,和牧師在上面固定的路線——當一點新的小材料被夾進去時,他的耳朵察覺到了,他整個天性都憤慨;他認為增添不公平,而且是無賴行為。

passages.original: In the midst of the prayer a fly had lit on the back of the pew in front of him and tortured his spirit by calmly rubbing its hands together, embracing its head with its arms, and polishing it so vigorously that it seemed to almost part company with the body, and the slender thread of a neck was exposed to view; scraping its wings with its hind legs and smoothing them to its body as if they had been coat-tails; going through its whole toilet as tranquilly as if it knew it was perfectly safe.
passages.vernacular: 禱告中間,一隻蒼蠅落喺佢前面長椅嘅靠背上,平靜地搓住雙手,用手臂抱住頭,咁猛烈地擦亮佢,似乎幾乎要同身體分離,纖細嘅脖子線露出嚟;用後腿刮翅膀,把佢哋撫平貼喺身體上像外衣嘅下擺;平靜地完成佢全部嘅梳洗,好像知道自己完全安全,折磨住佢嘅精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 禱告中間,一隻蒼蠅落在他前面長椅的靠背上,平靜地搓著雙手,用手臂抱著頭,那麼猛烈地擦亮它,似乎幾乎要與身體分離,纖細的脖子線露出來;用後腿刮翅膀,把它們撫平貼在身體上像外衣的下擺;平靜地完成它全部的梳洗,好像知道自己完全安全,折磨著他的精神。

passages.original: As indeed it was; for as sorely as Tom’s hands itched to grab for it they did not dare—he believed his soul would be instantly destroyed if he did such a thing while the prayer was going on.
passages.vernacular: 確實都係如此;因為不管湯姆嘅手多癢想去抓佢,佢哋都唔敢——佢相信如果喺禱告進行時做咁樣嘅事,佢嘅靈魂會立即被毀滅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實也是如此;因為不管湯姆的手多癢想去抓它,它們都不敢——他相信如果在禱告進行時做這樣的事,他的靈魂會立即被毀滅。

passages.original: But with the closing sentence his hand began to curve and steal forward; and the instant the “Amen” was out the fly was a prisoner of war.
passages.vernacular: 但隨住結束句,佢嘅手開始彎曲向前偷偷移動;「阿哋」一出口,蒼蠅就成咗戰俘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但隨著結束句,他的手開始彎曲向前偷偷移動;「阿們」一出口,蒼蠅就成了戰俘。

passages.original: His aunt detected the act and made him let it go.
passages.vernacular: 佢姨媽察覺到呢個動作,叫佢放咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他姨媽察覺到這個動作,叫他放了它。

passages.original: The minister gave out his text and droned along monotonously through an argument that was so prosy that many a head by and by began to nod—and yet it was an argument that dealt in limitless fire and brimstone and thinned the predestined elect down to a company so small as to be hardly worth the saving.
passages.vernacular: 牧師報咗經文,單調地嗡嗡講下去,一個咁枯燥嘅論證,不久好多腦袋都開始打瞌瞓——然而嗰個係一個涉及無邊火同硫磺、把預定嘅選民削減到少得幾乎不值得拯救嘅一群人嘅論證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師報了經文,單調地嗡嗡講下去,一個那麼枯燥的論證,不久很多腦袋都開始打瞌睡——然而那是一個涉及無邊火與硫磺、把預定的選民削減到少得幾乎不值得拯救的一群人的論證。

passages.original: Tom counted the pages of the sermon; after church he always knew how many pages there had been, but he seldom knew anything else about the discourse.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆數講道嘅頁數;禮拜後佢總是知道有多少頁,但好少知道講道嘅其他任何嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆數講道的頁數;禮拜後他總是知道有多少頁,但很少知道講道的其他任何東西。

passages.original: However, this time he was really interested for a little while.
passages.vernacular: 不過,呢次佢真嘅感咗一會兒興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,這次他真的感了一會兒興趣。

passages.original: The minister made a grand and moving picture of the assembling together of the world’s hosts at the millennium when the lion and the lamb should lie down together and a little child should lead them.
passages.vernacular: 牧師描繪咗一幅宏大而動人嘅圖畫,千年盛世時世界嘅大軍聚集喺一起,獅子同羔羊一起躺臥,一個小孩領住佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師描繪了一幅宏大而動人的圖畫,千年盛世時世界的大軍聚集在一起,獅子和羔羊一起躺臥,一個小孩領著他們。

passages.original: But the pathos, the lesson, the moral of the great spectacle were lost upon the boy; he only thought of the conspicuousness of the principal character before the on-looking nations; his face lit with the thought, and he said to himself that he wished he could be that child, if it was a tame lion.
passages.vernacular: 但呢個偉大場景嘅悲壯、教訓同寓意對男孩都白費喇;佢只想到主角喺注視住嘅萬國面前係幾咁顯眼;佢嘅臉因呢個念頭亮咗起嚟,佢對自己講,如果係一頭馴服嘅獅子,佢希望自己係嗰個小孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這個偉大場景的悲壯、教訓和寓意對男孩都白費了;他只想到主角在注視著的萬國面前是多麼顯眼;他的臉因這個念頭亮了起來,他對自己說,如果是一頭馴服的獅子,他希望自己是那個小孩。

passages.original: Now he lapsed into suffering again, as the dry argument was resumed.
passages.vernacular: 而家乾燥嘅論證繼續,佢又陷入痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在乾燥的論證繼續,他又陷入痛苦。

passages.original: Presently he bethought him of a treasure he had and got it out.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢想起咗佢有一件寶貝,把佢攞咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他想起了他有一件寶貝,把它拿了出來。

passages.original: It was a large black beetle with formidable jaws—a “pinchbug,” he called it.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一隻大黑甲蟲,有可怕嘅顎——佢稱佢為「夾子蟲」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一隻大黑甲蟲,有可怕的顎——他稱它為「夾子蟲」。

passages.original: It was in a percussion-cap box.
passages.vernacular: 佢裝喺一個雷管盒子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它裝在一個雷管盒子裡。

passages.original: The first thing the beetle did was to take him by the finger.
passages.vernacular: 甲蟲做嘅第一件事係咬住咗佢嘅手指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甲蟲做的第一件事是咬住了他的手指。

passages.original: A natural fillip followed, the beetle went floundering into the aisle and lit on its back, and the hurt finger went into the boy’s mouth.
passages.vernacular: 隨之而嚟嘅係自然嘅一彈,甲蟲掙扎住掉進過道,背朝下落地,受傷嘅手指進咗男孩嘅嘴裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨之而來的是自然的一彈,甲蟲掙扎著掉進過道,背朝下落地,受傷的手指進了男孩的嘴裡。

passages.original: The beetle lay there working its helpless legs, unable to turn over.
passages.vernacular: 甲蟲躺喺嗰度,無助嘅腿喺動,翻不過身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 甲蟲躺在那裡,無助的腿在動,翻不過身。

passages.original: Tom eyed it, and longed for it; but it was safe out of his reach.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆睇住佢,渴望得到佢;但佢安全地喺佢夠不住嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆看著它,渴望得到它;但它安全地在他夠不著的地方。

passages.original: Other people uninterested in the sermon found relief in the beetle, and they eyed it too.
passages.vernacular: 其他對講道不感興趣嘅人喺甲蟲身上找到了解脫,佢哋都睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他對講道不感興趣的人在甲蟲身上找到了解脫,他們也看著它。

passages.original: Presently a vagrant poodle dog came idling along, sad at heart, lazy with the summer softness and the quiet, weary of captivity, sighing for change.
passages.vernacular: 不久一隻流浪嘅捲毛狗閒逛過嚟,心裡悲傷,對夏天嘅溫柔和安靜感到懶散,厭倦咗囚禁,渴望變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久一隻流浪的捲毛狗閒逛過來,心裡悲傷,對夏天的溫柔和安靜感到懶散,厭倦了囚禁,渴望變化。

passages.original: He spied the beetle; the drooping tail lifted and wagged.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現咗甲蟲;下垂嘅尾巴抬起嚟搖咗搖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它發現了甲蟲;下垂的尾巴抬起來搖了搖。

passages.original: He surveyed the prize; walked around it; smelt at it from a safe distance; walked around it again; grew bolder, and took a closer smell; then lifted his lip and made a gingerly snatch at it, just missing it; made another, and another; began to enjoy the diversion; subsided to his stomach with the beetle between his paws, and continued his experiments; grew weary at last, and then indifferent and absent-minded.
passages.vernacular: 佢察睇咗呢份獎品;繞住佢走;從安全嘅距離聞佢;又繞住佢走;膽子大喇,近前聞;然後掀起嘴唇,小心翼翼地去抓佢,剛好冇抓到;又抓一次,又一次;開始享受呢種消遣;趴下肚子,把甲蟲放喺兩爪之間,繼續佢嘅實驗;最後累喇,變得漠不關心、心不喺焉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它察看了這份獎品;繞著它走;從安全的距離聞它;又繞著它走;膽子大了,近前聞;然後掀起嘴唇,小心翼翼地去抓它,剛好沒抓到;又抓一次,又一次;開始享受這種消遣;趴下肚子,把甲蟲放在兩爪之間,繼續它的實驗;最後累了,變得漠不關心、心不在焉。

passages.original: His head nodded, and little by little his chin descended and touched the enemy, who seized it.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅頭點住,下巴啲啲垂下,碰到咗敵人,敵人咬住咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它的頭點著,下巴一點一點垂下,碰到了敵人,敵人咬住了它。

passages.original: There was a sharp yelp, a flirt of the poodle’s head, and the beetle fell a couple of yards away, and lit on its back once more.
passages.vernacular: 一聲尖銳嘅哀叫,捲毛狗嘅頭一甩,甲蟲掉到兩碼外,又一次背朝下落地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一聲尖銳的哀叫,捲毛狗的頭一甩,甲蟲掉到兩碼外,又一次背朝下落地。

passages.original: The neighboring spectators shook with a gentle inward joy, several faces went behind fans and hand-kerchiefs, and Tom was entirely happy.
passages.vernacular: 鄰近嘅觀眾輕輕地內心喜悅地發抖,幾張臉躲到扇子同手帕後面,湯姆完全幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鄰近的觀眾輕輕地內心喜悅地發抖,幾張臉躲到扇子和手帕後面,湯姆完全幸福。

passages.original: The dog looked foolish, and probably felt so; but there was resentment in his heart, too, and a craving for revenge.
passages.vernacular: 狗顯得傻,大概都覺得傻;但佢心裡都有怨恨,渴望復仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗顯得傻,大概也覺得傻;但它心裡也有怨恨,渴望復仇。

passages.original: So he went to the beetle and began a wary attack on it again; jumping at it from every point of a circle, lighting with his fore-paws within an inch of the creature, making even closer snatches at it with his teeth, and jerking his head till his ears flapped again.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢走到甲蟲嗰度,又開始小心地攻擊佢;從圓周嘅各個點向佢跳,前爪落喺離呢生物一寸之內,用牙齒更靠近地抓佢,猛甩頭,直到耳朵又啪啪拍起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以它走到甲蟲那裡,又開始小心地攻擊它;從圓周的各個點向它跳,前爪落在離這生物一寸之內,用牙齒更靠近地抓它,猛甩頭,直到耳朵又啪啪拍起來。

passages.original: But he grew tired once more, after a while; tried to amuse himself with a fly but found no relief; followed an ant around, with his nose close to the floor, and quickly wearied of that; yawned, sighed, forgot the beetle entirely, and sat down on it.
passages.vernacular: 但過咗一會兒佢又累喇;試住用一隻蒼蠅消遣,但冇找到解脫;跟住一隻螞蟻轉,鼻子貼住地板,好快對呢個都厭倦喇;打咗個呵欠,歎咗口氣,完全忘咗甲蟲,坐咗下去,坐喺佢上面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但過了一會兒它又累了;試著用一隻蒼蠅消遣,但沒找到解脫;跟著一隻螞蟻轉,鼻子貼著地板,很快對這個也厭倦了;打了個呵欠,歎了口氣,完全忘了甲蟲,坐了下去,坐在它上面。

passages.original: Then there was a wild yelp of agony and the poodle went sailing up the aisle; the yelps continued, and so did the dog; he crossed the house in front of the altar; he flew down the other aisle; he crossed before the doors; he clamored up the home-stretch; his anguish grew with his progress, till presently he was but a woolly comet moving in its orbit with the gleam and the speed of light.
passages.vernacular: 於是響起一聲狂野嘅痛苦哀嚎,捲毛狗飛過過道;哀叫繼續,狗都繼續;佢穿過祭壇前嘅教堂;佢飛下另一條過道;佢喺門前穿過;佢喺回家嘅直路上叫喊;佢嘅痛苦隨住佢嘅前進增加,直到不久佢只係一顆毛茸茸嘅彗星,喺佢嘅軌道上以光嘅閃耀同速度運行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是響起一聲狂野的痛苦哀嚎,捲毛狗飛過過道;哀叫繼續,狗也繼續;它穿過祭壇前的教堂;它飛下另一條過道;它在門前穿過;它在回家的直路上叫喊;它的痛苦隨著它的前進增加,直到不久它只是一顆毛茸茸的彗星,在它的軌道上以光的閃耀和速度運行。

passages.original: At last the frantic sufferer sheered from its course, and sprang into its master’s lap; he flung it out of the window, and the voice of distress quickly thinned away and died in the distance.
passages.vernacular: 最後呢個瘋狂嘅受難者偏離咗佢嘅路線,跳進佢主人嘅腿上;佢把佢扔出窗外,痛苦嘅聲音好快變細,消失喺遠處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後這個瘋狂的受難者偏離了它的路線,跳進它主人的腿上;他把它扔出窗外,痛苦的聲音很快變細,消失在遠處。

passages.original: By this time the whole church was red-faced and suffocating with suppressed laughter, and the sermon had come to a dead standstill.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣整個教堂臉都紅喇,被壓抑嘅笑聲憋得喘不過氣,講道已經完全停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時整個教堂臉都紅了,被壓抑的笑聲憋得喘不過氣,講道已經完全停下。

passages.original: The discourse was resumed presently, but it went lame and halting, all possibility of impressiveness being at an end; for even the gravest sentiments were constantly being received with a smothered burst of unholy mirth, under cover of some remote pew-back, as if the poor parson had said a rarely facetious thing.
passages.vernacular: 講道不久後繼續,但跛腳而躊躇,所有畀人深刻印象嘅可能性都結束喇;因為即使最嚴肅嘅情感都不斷地喺某個遠處長椅靠背嘅掩護下,被一陣被扼殺嘅不神聖嘅歡笑所接收,好像可憐嘅牧師講咗一件罕見嘅詼諧話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講道不久後繼續,但跛腳而躊躇,所有給人深刻印象的可能性都結束了;因為即使最嚴肅的情感也不斷地在某個遠處長椅靠背的掩護下,被一陣被扼殺的不神聖的歡笑所接收,好像可憐的牧師說了一件罕見的詼諧話。

passages.original: It was a genuine relief to the whole congregation when the ordeal was over and the benediction pronounced.
passages.vernacular: 當折磨結束、祝福宣布時,呢對整個會眾係真正嘅解脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當折磨結束、祝福宣布時,這對整個會眾是真正的解脫。

passages.original: Tom Sawyer went home quite cheerful, thinking to himself that there was some satisfaction about divine service when there was a bit of variety in it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆·索亞相當愉快地回家,心裡想,當禮拜中有啲變化時,神聖嘅禮拜係有些令人滿意嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆·索亞相當愉快地回家,心裡想,當禮拜中有一點變化時,神聖的禮拜是有些令人滿意的。

passages.original: He had but one marring thought; he was willing that the dog should play with his pinchbug, but he did not think it was upright in him to carry it off.
passages.vernacular: 佢只有一個令佢掃興嘅念頭;佢願意讓狗玩佢嘅夾子蟲,但佢認為佢把佢攞走咗係不正直嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只有一個令他掃興的念頭;他願意讓狗玩他的夾子蟲,但他認為它把它拿走了是不正直的。

chapters.title: Chapter VI: Self-Examination 第六章:自我檢查

passages.original: CH Monday morning found Tom Sawyer miserable.
passages.vernacular: 星期一早晨,湯姆·索亞好悲慘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期一早晨,湯姆·索亞很悲慘。

passages.original: Monday morning always found him so—because it began another week’s slow suffering in school.
passages.vernacular: 星期一早晨總是發現佢咁樣——因為佢開始咗又一個星期喺學校裡嘅緩慢受苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期一早晨總是發現他這樣——因為它開始了又一個星期在學校裡的緩慢受苦。

passages.original: He generally began that day with wishing he had had no intervening holiday, it made the going into captivity and fetters again so much more odious.
passages.vernacular: 佢通常以希望中間冇假日嚟開始呢一天,呢使得再次進入囚禁同鐐銬更加可憎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他通常以希望中間沒有假日來開始這一天,這使得再次進入囚禁和鐐銬更加可憎。

passages.original: Tom lay thinking.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆躺住思考。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆躺著思考。

passages.original: Presently it occurred to him that he wished he was sick; then he could stay home from school.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢想到,佢希望自己生病喇;嗰樣佢就可以待喺家裡不去學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他想到,他希望自己生病了;那樣他就可以待在家裡不去學校。

passages.original: Here was a vague possibility.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一種模糊嘅可能性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一種模糊的可能性。

passages.original: He canvassed his system.
passages.vernacular: 佢檢查自己嘅身體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他檢查自己的身體。

passages.original: No ailment was found, and he investigated again.
passages.vernacular: 冇發現任何疾病,佢又檢查咗一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有發現任何疾病,他又檢查了一次。

passages.original: This time he thought he could detect colicky symptoms, and he began to encourage them with considerable hope.
passages.vernacular: 呢次佢以為能查出絞痛嘅症狀,佢帶住相當大嘅希望開始鼓勵佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次他以為能查出絞痛的症狀,他帶著相當大的希望開始鼓勵它們。

passages.original: But they soon grew feeble, and presently died wholly away.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋好快變弱,不久完全消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們很快變弱,不久完全消失了。

passages.original: He reflected further.
passages.vernacular: 佢進一步思考。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他進一步思考。

passages.original: Suddenly he discovered something.
passages.vernacular: 突然佢發現咗點乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然他發現了點什麼。

passages.original: One of his upper front teeth was loose.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅一顆上門牙鬆喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的一顆上門牙鬆了。

passages.original: This was lucky; he was about to begin to groan, as a “starter,” as he called it, when it occurred to him that if he came into court with that argument, his aunt would pull it out, and that would hurt.
passages.vernacular: 呢個好幸運;佢正要開始呻吟,佢稱之為「開場」,呢陣佢想到,如果佢帶住呢個論據出庭,佢姨媽會把佢拔掉,嗰會好痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這很幸運;他正要開始呻吟,他稱之為「開場」,這時他想到,如果他帶著這個論據出庭,他姨媽會把它拔掉,那會很痛。

passages.original: So he thought he would hold the tooth in reserve for the present, and seek further.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢想佢暫時把呢顆牙留作後備,再去尋找別嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他想他暫時把這顆牙留作後備,再去尋找別的。

passages.original: Nothing offered for some little time, and then he remembered hearing the doctor tell about a certain thing that laid up a patient for two or three weeks and threatened to make him lose a finger.
passages.vernacular: 有一小會兒乜嘢都冇出現,然後佢想起聽醫生講過某件事,使病人臥床兩三個星期,仲威脅要讓佢失去一根手指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一小會兒什麼也沒有出現,然後他想起聽醫生說過某件事,使病人臥床兩三個星期,還威脅要讓他失去一根手指。

passages.original: So the boy eagerly drew his sore toe from under the sheet and held it up for inspection.
passages.vernacular: 於是男孩急切地從被單下拉出佢嘅痛腳趾,舉起嚟檢查。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是男孩急切地從被單下拉出他的痛腳趾,舉起來檢查。

passages.original: But now he did not know the necessary symptoms.
passages.vernacular: 但而家佢唔知道必要嘅症狀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在他不知道必要的症狀。

passages.original: However, it seemed well worth while to chance it, so he fell to groaning with considerable spirit.
passages.vernacular: 不過,似乎好值得冒險一試,所以佢相當有精神地開始呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,似乎很值得冒險一試,所以他相當有精神地開始呻吟。

passages.original: But Sid slept on unconscious.
passages.vernacular: 但希德繼續瞓住,毫無知覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但希德繼續睡著,毫無知覺。

passages.original: Tom groaned louder, and fancied that he began to feel pain in the toe.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆呻吟得更大聲,幻想自己開始感到腳趾疼痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆呻吟得更大聲,幻想自己開始感到腳趾疼痛。

passages.original: No result from Sid.
passages.vernacular: 希德冇反應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德沒有反應。

passages.original: Tom was panting with his exertions by this time.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆此時已為佢嘅努力喘氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆此時已為他的努力喘氣。

passages.original: He took a rest and then swelled himself up and fetched a succession of admirable groans.
passages.vernacular: 佢休息咗一下,然後把自己鼓起嚟,發出一連串令人欽佩嘅呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他休息了一下,然後把自己鼓起來,發出一連串令人欽佩的呻吟。

passages.original: Sid snored on.
passages.vernacular: 希德繼續打鼾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德繼續打鼾。

passages.original: Tom was aggravated.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆氣惱喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆氣惱了。

passages.original: He said, “Sid, Sid!” and shook him.
passages.vernacular: 佢講:「希德,希德!」搖佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:「希德,希德!」搖他。

passages.original: This course worked well, and Tom began to groan again.
passages.vernacular: 呢個辦法好有效,湯姆又開始呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個辦法很有效,湯姆又開始呻吟。

passages.original: Sid yawned, stretched, then brought himself up on his elbow with a snort, and began to stare at Tom.
passages.vernacular: 希德打咗個呵欠,伸咗個懶腰,然後哼咗一聲用手肘撐起身子,開始盯住湯姆睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德打了個呵欠,伸了個懶腰,然後哼了一聲用手肘撐起身子,開始盯著湯姆看。

passages.original: Tom went on groaning.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆繼續呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆繼續呻吟。

passages.original: Sid said:
passages.vernacular: 希德講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德說:
