passages.original: “Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆!

passages.original: Say, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 喂,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,湯姆!」

passages.original: [No response.]
passages.vernacular: [冇回應。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [沒有回應。]

passages.original: “Here, Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「喂,湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,湯姆!

passages.original: TOM!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆!

passages.original: What is the matter, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 點喇,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,湯姆?」

passages.original: And he shook him and looked in his face anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 佢搖佢,焦急地睇住佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他搖他,焦急地看著他的臉。

passages.original: Tom moaned out:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆呻吟住講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆呻吟著說:

passages.original: “Oh, don’t, Sid.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別,希德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別,希德。

passages.original: Don’t joggle me.”
passages.vernacular: 別搖我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別搖我。」

passages.original: “Why, what’s the matter, Tom?
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,點喇,湯姆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,怎麼了,湯姆?

passages.original: I must call auntie.”
passages.vernacular: 我必須叫姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須叫姨媽。」

passages.original: “No—never mind.
passages.vernacular: 「不——別管。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——別管。

passages.original: It’ll be over by and by, maybe.
passages.vernacular: 或者過一會兒就過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許過一會兒就過去了。

passages.original: Don’t call anybody.”
passages.vernacular: 別叫任何人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別叫任何人。」

passages.original: “But I must!
passages.vernacular: 「但我必須!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我必須!

passages.original: Don’t groan so, Tom, it’s awful.
passages.vernacular: 別咁樣呻吟,湯姆,太可怕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別這樣呻吟,湯姆,太可怕了。

passages.original: How long you been this way?”
passages.vernacular: 你咁樣多久喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這樣多久了?」

passages.original: “Hours.
passages.vernacular: 「幾個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「幾個小時。

passages.original: Ouch!
passages.vernacular: 哎喲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎喲!

passages.original: Oh, don’t stir so, Sid, you’ll kill me.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,別動,希德,你會殺咗我嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,別動,希德,你會殺了我的。」

passages.original: “Tom, why didn’t you wake me sooner?
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,你點解不早點叫醒我?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,你為什麼不早點叫醒我?

passages.original: Oh, Tom, don’t!
passages.vernacular: 哦,湯姆,別!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,湯姆,別!

passages.original: It makes my flesh crawl to hear you.
passages.vernacular: 聽你咁樣我渾身起雞皮疙瘩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽你這樣我渾身起雞皮疙瘩。

passages.original: Tom, what is the matter?”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,怎麼了?」

passages.original: “I forgive you everything, Sid.
passages.vernacular: 「我原諒你一切,希德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我原諒你一切,希德。

passages.original: [Groan.]
passages.vernacular: [呻吟。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [呻吟。]

passages.original: Everything you’ve ever done to me.
passages.vernacular: 你對我做過嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對我做過的一切。

passages.original: When I’m gone—”
passages.vernacular: 等我走喇——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我走了——」

passages.original: “Oh, Tom, you ain’t dying, are you?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆,你唔係要死咗吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆,你不是要死了吧?

passages.original: Don’t, Tom—oh, don’t.
passages.vernacular: 別,湯姆——哦,別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別,湯姆——哦,別。

passages.original: Maybe—”
passages.vernacular: 或者——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許——」

passages.original: “I forgive everybody, Sid.
passages.vernacular: 「我原諒每個人,希德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我原諒每個人,希德。

passages.original: [Groan.]
passages.vernacular: [呻吟。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [呻吟。]

passages.original: Tell ’em so, Sid.
passages.vernacular: 告訴佢哋,希德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴他們,希德。

passages.original: And Sid, you give my window-sash and my cat with one eye to that new girl that’s come to town, and tell her—”
passages.vernacular: 仲有希德,你把我嘅窗框同我嗰隻獨眼貓畀嗰個新嚟鎮上嘅女孩,告訴佢——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有希德,你把我的窗框和我那隻獨眼貓給那個新來鎮上的女孩,告訴她——」

passages.original: But Sid had snatched his clothes and gone.
passages.vernacular: 但希德已經抓起衣服走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但希德已經抓起衣服走了。

passages.original: Tom was suffering in reality, now, so handsomely was his imagination working, and so his groans had gathered quite a genuine tone.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆而家真嘅喺受苦,佢嘅想像力運作得咁好,所以佢嘅呻吟已經帶上相當真實嘅語調。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆現在真的在受苦,他的想像力運作得這麼好,所以他的呻吟已經帶上相當真實的語調。

passages.original: Sid flew downstairs and said:
passages.vernacular: 希德飛下樓講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德飛下樓說:

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, come!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,快嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,快來!

passages.original: Tom’s dying!”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆要死喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆要死了!」

passages.original: “Dying!”
passages.vernacular: 「要死喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要死了!」

passages.original: “Yes’m.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,姨媽。

passages.original: Don’t wait—come quick!”
passages.vernacular: 別等喇——快嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別等了——快來!」

passages.original: “Rubbage!
passages.vernacular: 「胡講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說!

passages.original: I don’t believe it!”
passages.vernacular: 我不信!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不信!」

passages.original: But she fled upstairs, nevertheless, with Sid and Mary at her heels.
passages.vernacular: 但佢仍然跑上樓,希德同瑪麗緊跟喺後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她仍然跑上樓,希德和瑪麗緊跟在後。

passages.original: And her face grew white, too, and her lip trembled.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉都變白喇,嘴唇發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉也變白了,嘴唇發抖。

passages.original: When she reached the bedside she gasped out:
passages.vernacular: 佢到咗床邊,喘住氣講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她到了床邊,喘著氣說:

passages.original: “You, Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「你,湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你,湯姆!

passages.original: Tom, what’s the matter with you?”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,你點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,你怎麼了?」

passages.original: “Oh, auntie, I’m—”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,姨媽,我——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,姨媽,我——」

passages.original: “What’s the matter with you—what is the matter with you, child?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點喇——你到底點喇,細路?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼了——你到底怎麼了,孩子?」

passages.original: “Oh, auntie, my sore toe’s mortified!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,姨媽,我嘅痛腳趾壞死喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,姨媽,我的痛腳趾壞死了!」

passages.original: The old lady sank down into a chair and laughed a little, then cried a little, then did both together.
passages.vernacular: 老太太跌坐喺椅子上,笑咗一下,然後哭咗一下,然後兩者同時發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太跌坐在椅子上,笑了一下,然後哭了一下,然後兩者同時發生。

passages.original: This restored her and she said:
passages.vernacular: 呢使佢恢復過嚟,佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使她恢復過來,她說:

passages.original: “Tom, what a turn you did give me.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,你真把我嚇咗一大跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,你真把我嚇了一大跳。

passages.original: Now you shut up that nonsense and climb out of this.”
passages.vernacular: 而家你住嘴唔好講呢種廢話,從嗰度爬出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你住嘴別說這種廢話,從那裡爬出來。」

passages.original: The groans ceased and the pain vanished from the toe.
passages.vernacular: 呻吟停止喇,腳趾嘅痛都消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呻吟停止了,腳趾的痛也消失了。

passages.original: The boy felt a little foolish, and he said:
passages.vernacular: 男孩感到有點傻,佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩感到有點傻,他說:

passages.original: “Aunt Polly, it seemed mortified, and it hurt so I never minded my tooth at all.”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽,佢好像壞死喇,痛得我完全冇在意我嘅牙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽,它好像壞死了,痛得我完全沒在意我的牙。」

passages.original: “Your tooth, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅牙,真係嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的牙,真是的!

passages.original: What’s the matter with your tooth?”
passages.vernacular: 你嘅牙點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的牙怎麼了?」

passages.original: “One of them’s loose, and it aches perfectly awful.”
passages.vernacular: 「有一顆鬆喇,痛得可怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一顆鬆了,痛得可怕。」

passages.original: “There, there, now, don’t begin that groaning again.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,別又開始呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,別又開始呻吟。

passages.original: Open your mouth.
passages.vernacular: 張開嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 張開嘴。

passages.original: Well—your tooth is loose, but you’re not going to die about that.
passages.vernacular: 嗯——你嘅牙係鬆喇,但你唔會為呢個死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯——你的牙是鬆了,但你不會為這個死。

passages.original: Mary, get me a silk thread, and a chunk of fire out of the kitchen.”
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗,畀我攞一根絲線,同廚房裡嘅一塊火炭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗,給我拿一根絲線,和廚房裡的一塊火炭。」

passages.original: Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說:

passages.original: “Oh, please, auntie, don’t pull it out.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,求你,姨媽,別拔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,求你,姨媽,別拔。

passages.original: It don’t hurt any more.
passages.vernacular: 佢不痛喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不痛了。

passages.original: I wish I may never stir if it does.
passages.vernacular: 我敢發誓,如果痛我就永遠不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢發誓,如果痛我就永遠不動。

passages.original: Please don’t, auntie.
passages.vernacular: 求你別,姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求你別,姨媽。

passages.original: I don’t want to stay home from school.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔想待喺家裡不去學校。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想待在家裡不去學校。」

passages.original: “Oh, you don’t, don’t you?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你唔想,係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你不想,是嗎?

passages.original: So all this row was because you thought you’d get to stay home from school and go a-fishing?
passages.vernacular: 所以呢一切吵鬧係因為你以為可以待喺家不上學去釣魚?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以這一切吵鬧是因為你以為可以待在家不上學去釣魚?

passages.original: Tom, Tom, I love you so, and you seem to try every way you can to break my old heart with your outrageousness.”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,湯姆,我咁愛你,而你似乎用盡一切辦法,用你嘅荒唐傷我呢顆老心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,湯姆,我那麼愛你,而你似乎用盡一切辦法,用你的荒唐傷我這顆老心。」

passages.original: By this time the dental instruments were ready.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣牙科器械準備好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時牙科器械準備好了。

passages.original: The old lady made one end of the silk thread fast to Tom’s tooth with a loop and tied the other to the bedpost.
passages.vernacular: 老太太把絲線嘅一端用一個圈牢牢系喺湯姆嘅牙上,另一端綁喺床柱上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太把絲線的一端用一個圈牢牢系在湯姆的牙上,另一端綁在床柱上。

passages.original: Then she seized the chunk of fire and suddenly thrust it almost into the boy’s face.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢抓起嗰塊火炭,突然幾乎戳到男孩臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她抓起那塊火炭,突然幾乎戳到男孩臉上。

passages.original: The tooth hung dangling by the bedpost, now.
passages.vernacular: 牙而家晃晃蕩蕩地掛喺床柱上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牙現在晃晃蕩蕩地掛在床柱上。

passages.original: But all trials bring their compensations.
passages.vernacular: 但所有考驗都有補償。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但所有考驗都有補償。

passages.original: As Tom wended to school after breakfast, he was the envy of every boy he met because the gap in his upper row of teeth enabled him to expectorate in a new and admirable way.
passages.vernacular: 早餐後湯姆去學校時,佢係佢遇到嘅每個男孩嘅羨慕對象,因為佢上排牙齒嘅缺口讓佢能以一種新嘅令人欽佩嘅方式吐口水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐後湯姆去學校時,他是他遇到的每個男孩的羨慕對象,因為他上排牙齒的缺口讓他能以一種新的令人欽佩的方式吐口水。

passages.original: He gathered quite a following of lads interested in the exhibition; and one that had cut his finger and had been a centre of fascination and homage up to this time, now found himself suddenly without an adherent, and shorn of his glory.
passages.vernacular: 佢聚集咗相當多對呢個表演感興趣嘅小伙子;一個割破咗手指、直到嗰時一直係迷戀同敬意中心嘅男孩,而家發現自己突然冇咗追隨者,都失去咗榮耀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他聚集了相當多對這個表演感興趣的小伙子;一個割破了手指、直到那時一直是迷戀和敬意中心的男孩,現在發現自己突然沒有了追隨者,也失去了榮耀。

passages.original: His heart was heavy, and he said with a disdain which he did not feel that it wasn’t anything to spit like Tom Sawyer; but another boy said, “Sour grapes!” and he wandered away a dismantled hero.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅心情沉重,佢帶住並非真實感受嘅輕蔑講,像湯姆·索亞嗰樣吐口水不算乜嘢;但另一個男孩講:「酸葡萄!」佢徘徊住走開,成咗個被拆除嘅英雄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的心情沉重,他帶著並非真實感受的輕蔑說,像湯姆·索亞那樣吐口水不算什麼;但另一個男孩說:「酸葡萄!」他徘徊著走開,成了個被拆除的英雄。

passages.original: Shortly Tom came upon the juvenile pariah of the village, Huckleberry Finn, son of the town drunkard.
passages.vernacular: 不久湯姆遇到咗村裡嘅少年賤民,哈克貝利·費恩,鎮上酒鬼嘅兒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久湯姆遇到了村裡的少年賤民,哈克貝利·費恩,鎮上酒鬼的兒子。

passages.original: Huckleberry was cordially hated and dreaded by all the mothers of the town, because he was idle and lawless and vulgar and bad—and because all their children admired him so, and delighted in his forbidden society, and wished they dared to be like him.
passages.vernacular: 哈克貝利被鎮上所有嘅母親誠摯地憎恨同害怕,因為佢懶散、無法無天、粗俗又壞——都因為佢哋所有嘅細路都咁欽佩佢,鍾意佢被禁止嘅陪伴,希望自己敢像佢一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克貝利被鎮上所有的母親誠摯地憎恨和害怕,因為他懶散、無法無天、粗俗又壞——也因為她們所有的孩子都那麼欽佩他,喜歡他被禁止的陪伴,希望自己敢像他一樣。

passages.original: Tom was like the rest of the respectable boys, in that he envied Huckleberry his gaudy outcast condition, and was under strict orders not to play with him.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆像其他體面嘅男孩一樣,羨慕哈克貝利嗰華麗嘅被遺棄嘅處境,並且被嚴格命令不許同佢玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆像其他體面的男孩一樣,羨慕哈克貝利那華麗的被遺棄的處境,並且被嚴格命令不許同他玩。

passages.original: So he played with him every time he got a chance.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢一有機會就同佢玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他一有機會就同他玩。

passages.original: Huckleberry was always dressed in the cast-off clothes of full-grown men, and they were in perennial bloom and fluttering with rags.
passages.vernacular: 哈克貝利總是穿成年男人丟棄嘅衣服,佢哋終年開花,破布飄揚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克貝利總是穿成年男人丟棄的衣服,它們終年開花,破布飄揚。

passages.original: His hat was a vast ruin with a wide crescent lopped out of its brim; his coat, when he wore one, hung nearly to his heels and had the rearward buttons far down the back; but one suspender supported his trousers; the seat of the trousers bagged low and contained nothing, the fringed legs dragged in the dirt when not rolled up.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅帽子係一個巨大嘅廢墟,帽簷被砍掉一個寬寬嘅月牙;佢嘅外套,穿嘅時候,幾乎垂到腳跟,後面嘅鈕扣遠遠喺背上;只有一根吊褲帶撐住佢嘅褲子;褲子嘅臀部低低地垂住,裡面乜嘢都冇,有流蘇嘅褲腿不捲起嚟時就拖喺泥裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的帽子是一個巨大的廢墟,帽簷被砍掉一個寬寬的月牙;他的外套,穿的時候,幾乎垂到腳跟,後面的鈕扣遠遠在背上;只有一根吊褲帶撐著他的褲子;褲子的臀部低低地垂著,裡面什麼也沒有,有流蘇的褲腿不捲起來時就拖在泥裡。

passages.original: Huckleberry came and went, at his own free will.
passages.vernacular: 哈克貝利隨自己嘅自由意志嚟去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克貝利隨自己的自由意志來去。

passages.original: He slept on doorsteps in fine weather and in empty hogsheads in wet; he did not have to go to school or to church, or call any being master or obey anybody; he could go fishing or swimming when and where he chose, and stay as long as it suited him; nobody forbade him to fight; he could sit up as late as he pleased; he was always the first boy that went barefoot in the spring and the last to resume leather in the fall; he never had to wash, nor put on clean clothes; he could swear wonderfully.
passages.vernacular: 天氣好時佢瞓喺門階上,下雨時瞓喺空桶裡;佢唔使去學校或教堂,唔使叫任何人主人或服從任何人;佢可以隨時隨地去釣魚或游泳,待多久都隨佢高興;冇人禁止佢打架;佢可以隨佢鍾意熬夜到多晚;春天佢總是第一個赤腳嘅男孩,秋天總是最後一個重新穿皮鞋;佢從唔使洗澡,都唔使穿乾淨衣服;佢能罵得好精彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天氣好時他睡在門階上,下雨時睡在空桶裡;他不必去學校或教堂,不必叫任何人主人或服從任何人;他可以隨時隨地去釣魚或游泳,待多久都隨他高興;沒有人禁止他打架;他可以隨他喜歡熬夜到多晚;春天他總是第一個赤腳的男孩,秋天總是最後一個重新穿皮鞋;他從不必洗澡,也不必穿乾淨衣服;他能罵得很精彩。

passages.original: In a word, everything that goes to make life precious that boy had.
passages.vernacular: 一句話,使生活珍貴嘅一切,嗰個男孩都有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一句話,使生活珍貴的一切,那個男孩都有。

passages.original: So thought every harassed, hampered, respectable boy in St. Petersburg.
passages.vernacular: 聖彼得堡每個受騷擾、受束縛嘅體面男孩都咁想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖彼得堡每個受騷擾、受束縛的體面男孩都這麼想。

passages.original: Tom hailed the romantic outcast:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆向呢個浪漫嘅被遺棄者打招呼:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆向這個浪漫的被遺棄者打招呼:

passages.original: “Hello, Huckleberry!”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,哈克貝利!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,哈克貝利!」

passages.original: “Hello yourself, and see how you like it.”
passages.vernacular: 「你自己喂,睇你鍾意不鍾意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你自己喂,看你喜歡不喜歡。」

passages.original: “What’s that you got?”
passages.vernacular: 「你攞嘅係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你拿的是什麼?」

passages.original: “Dead cat.”
passages.vernacular: 「死貓。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「死貓。」

passages.original: “Lemme see him, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我睇睇,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我看看,哈克。

passages.original: My, he’s pretty stiff.
passages.vernacular: 天呀,佢相當僵硬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,他相當僵硬。

passages.original: Where’d you get him?”
passages.vernacular: 你從邊度弄嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從哪裡弄來的?」

passages.original: “Bought him off’n a boy.”
passages.vernacular: 「從一個男孩嗰度買嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從一個男孩那裡買的。」

passages.original: “What did you give?”
passages.vernacular: 「你畀咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你給了什麼?」

passages.original: “I give a blue ticket and a bladder that I got at the slaughter-house.”
passages.vernacular: 「我畀咗一張藍票同一個我喺屠宰場得到嘅膀胱。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我給了一張藍票和一個我在屠宰場得到的膀胱。」

passages.original: “Where’d you get the blue ticket?”
passages.vernacular: 「你從邊度得到藍票嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你從哪裡得到藍票的?」

passages.original: “Bought it off’n Ben Rogers two weeks ago for a hoop-stick.”
passages.vernacular: 「兩個星期前從本·羅傑斯嗰度用一根箍棒買嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「兩個星期前從本·羅傑斯那裡用一根箍棒買的。」

passages.original: “Say—what is dead cats good for, Huck?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂——死貓有乜嘢用,哈克?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂——死貓有什麼用,哈克?」

passages.original: “Good for?
passages.vernacular: 「有乜嘢用?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有什麼用?

passages.original: Cure warts with.”
passages.vernacular: 治疣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 治疣。」

passages.original: “No!
passages.vernacular: 「唔會吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會吧!

passages.original: Is that so?
passages.vernacular: 係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是嗎?

passages.original: I know something that’s better.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道一個更好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道一個更好的。」

passages.original: “I bet you don’t.
passages.vernacular: 「我打賭你唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我打賭你不知道。

passages.original: What is it?”
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, spunk-water.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,朽木水。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,朽木水。」

passages.original: “Spunk-water!
passages.vernacular: 「朽木水!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「朽木水!

passages.original: I wouldn’t give a dern for spunk-water.”
passages.vernacular: 我才不稀罕朽木水。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我才不稀罕朽木水。」

passages.original: “You wouldn’t, wouldn’t you?
passages.vernacular: 「你不稀罕,係吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不稀罕,是吧?

passages.original: D’you ever try it?”
passages.vernacular: 你試過嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你試過嗎?」

passages.original: “No, I hain’t.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我沒有。

passages.original: But Bob Tanner did.”
passages.vernacular: 但鮑勃·坦納試過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但鮑勃·坦納試過。」

passages.original: “Who told you so!”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個告訴你嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰告訴你的!」

passages.original: “Why, he told Jeff Thatcher, and Jeff told Johnny Baker, and Johnny told Jim Hollis, and Jim told Ben Rogers, and Ben told a nigger, and the nigger told me.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,佢告訴傑夫·撒切爾,傑夫告訴強尼·貝克,強尼告訴吉姆·霍利斯,吉姆告訴本·羅傑斯,本告訴一個黑人,嗰個黑人告訴我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,他告訴傑夫·撒切爾,傑夫告訴強尼·貝克,強尼告訴吉姆·霍利斯,吉姆告訴本·羅傑斯,本告訴一個黑人,那個黑人告訴我。

passages.original: There now!”
passages.vernacular: 睇吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看吧!」

passages.original: “Well, what of it?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那又怎樣?

passages.original: They’ll all lie.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都會撒謊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都會撒謊。

passages.original: Leastways all but the nigger.
passages.vernacular: 至少除咗嗰個黑人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少除了那個黑人。

passages.original: I don’t know him.
passages.vernacular: 我不認識佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不認識他。

passages.original: But I never see a nigger that wouldn’t lie.
passages.vernacular: 但我從冇見過一個不撒謊嘅黑人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我從沒見過一個不撒謊的黑人。

passages.original: Shucks!
passages.vernacular: 算喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 算了!

passages.original: Now you tell me how Bob Tanner done it, Huck.”
passages.vernacular: 而家你告訴我鮑勃·坦納係點做嘅,哈克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你告訴我鮑勃·坦納是怎麼做的,哈克。」

passages.original: “Why, he took and dipped his hand in a rotten stump where the rain-water was.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,佢把手伸進一個有雨水嘅腐爛樹樁裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,他把手伸進一個有雨水的腐爛樹樁裡。」

passages.original: “In the daytime?”
passages.vernacular: 「白天嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「白天嗎?」

passages.original: “Certainly.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。」

passages.original: “With his face to the stump?”
passages.vernacular: 「臉對住樹樁嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「臉對著樹樁嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.
Least I reckon so.”
passages.vernacular: 至少我想係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少我想是。」

passages.original: “Did he say anything?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講咗乜嘢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說了什麼嗎?」

passages.original: “I don’t reckon he did.
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想他沒說。

passages.original: I don’t know.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道。」

passages.original: “Aha!
passages.vernacular: 「啊哈!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊哈!

passages.original: Talk about trying to cure warts with spunk-water such a blame fool way as that!
passages.vernacular: 仲講用朽木水治疣,用咁一種該死嘅蠢方法!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還說用朽木水治疣,用這麼一種該死的蠢方法!

passages.original: Why, that ain’t a-going to do any good.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,嗰唔會有啲好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,那不會有一點好處。

passages.original: You got to go all by yourself, to the middle of the woods, where you know there’s a spunk-water stump, and just as it’s midnight you back up against the stump and jam your hand in and say:
passages.vernacular: 你得一個人去,到樹林中間,你知道嗰度有朽木水樹樁,就喺午夜時背靠樹樁,把手塞進去,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得一個人去,到樹林中間,你知道那裡有朽木水樹樁,就在午夜時背靠樹樁,把手塞進去,說:

passages.original: ‘Barley-corn, barley-corn, injun-meal shorts, Spunk-water, spunk-water, swaller these warts,’
passages.vernacular: 『大麥,大麥,印第安玉米粉,朽木水,朽木水,吞掉呢啲疣,』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『大麥,大麥,印第安玉米粉,朽木水,朽木水,吞掉這些疣,』

passages.original: and then walk away quick, eleven steps, with your eyes shut, and then turn around three times and walk home without speaking to anybody.
passages.vernacular: 然後閉住眼睛快步走開,十一步,然後轉三圈,不同任何人講話走回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後閉著眼睛快步走開,十一步,然後轉三圈,不同任何人說話走回家。

passages.original: Because if you speak the charm’s busted.”
passages.vernacular: 因為你一講話,咒語就破喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你一說話,咒語就破了。」

passages.original: “Well, that sounds like a good way; but that ain’t the way Bob Tanner done.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,聽起嚟係個好辦法;但鮑勃·坦納唔係咁樣做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,聽起來是個好辦法;但鮑勃·坦納不是這樣做的。」

passages.original: “No, sir, you can bet he didn’t, becuz he’s the wartiest boy in this town; and he wouldn’t have a wart on him if he’d knowed how to work spunk-water.
passages.vernacular: 「不,先生,你可以打賭佢唔係,因為佢係呢個鎮上長疣最多嘅男孩;如果佢知道點用朽木水,佢身上就唔會有疣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,先生,你可以打賭他不是,因為他是這個鎮上長疣最多的男孩;如果他知道怎麼用朽木水,他身上就不會有疣了。

passages.original: I’ve took off thousands of warts off of my hands that way, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 我用嗰種方法從手上去掉過上千個疣,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我用那種方法從手上去掉過上千個疣,哈克。

passages.original: I play with frogs so much that I’ve always got considerable many warts.
passages.vernacular: 我玩青蛙玩得太多,總是有相當多嘅疣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我玩青蛙玩得太多,總是有相當多的疣。

passages.original: Sometimes I take ’em off with a bean.”
passages.vernacular: 有時我用豆子把佢哋去掉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時我用豆子把它們去掉。」

passages.original: “Yes, bean’s good.
passages.vernacular: 「對,豆子好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,豆子很好。

passages.original: I’ve done that.”
passages.vernacular: 我做過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我做過。」

passages.original: “Have you?
passages.vernacular: 「你做過?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做過?

passages.original: What’s your way?”
passages.vernacular: 你嘅方法係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的方法是什麼?」

passages.original: “You take and split the bean, and cut the wart so as to get some blood, and then you put the blood on one piece of the bean and take and dig a hole and bury it ’bout midnight at the crossroads in the dark of the moon, and then you burn up the rest of the bean.
passages.vernacular: 「你把豆子劈開,把疣割破,弄出些血,然後把血塗喺豆子嘅一半上,挖個洞,喺月黑時分大約午夜時喺十字路口把佢埋掉,然後把剩下嘅豆子燒掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你把豆子劈開,把疣割破,弄出些血,然後把血塗在豆子的一半上,挖個洞,在月黑時分大約午夜時在十字路口把它埋掉,然後把剩下的豆子燒掉。

passages.original: You see that piece that’s got the blood on it will keep drawing and drawing, trying to fetch the other piece to it, and so that helps the blood to draw the wart, and pretty soon off she comes.”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,有血嘅嗰一半會不停地吸,不停地吸,想把另一半拉到佢嗰度,咁樣幫助血把疣吸走,不久佢就掉喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,有血的那一半會不停地吸,不停地吸,想把另一半拉到它那裡,這樣幫助血把疣吸走,不久它就掉了。」

passages.original: “Yes, that’s it, Huck—that’s it; though when you’re burying it if you say ‘Down bean; off wart; come no more to bother me!’ it’s better.
passages.vernacular: 「對,就係嗰樣,哈克——就係嗰樣;不過你埋嘅時候,如果你講『豆子下去;疣離開;唔好再嚟煩我!』更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,就是那樣,哈克——就是那樣;不過你埋的時候,如果你說『豆子下去;疣離開;不要再來煩我!』更好。

passages.original: That’s the way Joe Harper does, and he’s been nearly to Coonville and most everywheres.
passages.vernacular: 喬·哈珀就係咁樣做嘅,佢幾乎去過庫恩維爾,幾乎到過各處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬·哈珀就是這樣做的,他幾乎去過庫恩維爾,幾乎到過各處。

passages.original: But say—how do you cure ’em with dead cats?”
passages.vernacular: 但係,喂——你點用死貓治佢哋?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,喂——你怎麼用死貓治它們?」

passages.original: “Why, you take your cat and go and get in the grave-yard ’long about midnight when somebody that was wicked has been buried; and when it’s midnight a devil will come, or maybe two or three, but you can’t see ’em, you can only hear something like the wind, or maybe hear ’em talk; and when they’re taking that feller away, you heave your cat after ’em and say, ‘Devil follow corpse, cat follow devil, warts follow cat, I’m done with ye!’
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,你帶住你嘅貓,喺某個壞人被埋葬嘅大約午夜時分到墳場去;到午夜時,一個魔鬼會嚟,或者兩三個,但你睇唔見佢哋,你只能聽到像風一樣嘅嘢,或者或者聽到佢哋講話;佢哋把嗰傢伙帶走時,你把貓扔向佢哋,講:『魔鬼跟住屍體,貓跟住魔鬼,疣跟住貓,我同你哋冇關係喇!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,你帶著你的貓,在某個壞人被埋葬的大約午夜時分到墳場去;到午夜時,一個魔鬼會來,也許兩三個,但你看不見它們,你只能聽到像風一樣的東西,或者也許聽到它們說話;它們把那傢伙帶走時,你把貓扔向它們,說:『魔鬼跟著屍體,貓跟著魔鬼,疣跟著貓,我同你們沒關係了!』

passages.original: That’ll fetch any wart.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰會把任何疣弄掉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會把任何疣弄掉。」

passages.original: “Sounds right.
passages.vernacular: 「聽起嚟對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽起來對。

passages.original: D’you ever try it, Huck?”
passages.vernacular: 你試過嗎,哈克?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你試過嗎,哈克?」

passages.original: “No, but old Mother Hopkins told me.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,但老霍普金斯媽媽告訴我嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,但老霍普金斯媽媽告訴我的。」

passages.original: “Well, I reckon it’s so, then.
passages.vernacular: 「咁我想係真嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我想是真的了。

passages.original: Becuz they say she’s a witch.”
passages.vernacular: 因為佢哋講佢係個女巫。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為他們說她是個女巫。」

passages.original: “Say!
Why, Tom, I know she is.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,湯姆,我知道佢係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,湯姆,我知道她是。

passages.original: She witched pap.
passages.vernacular: 佢對爸爸施咗巫術。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對爸爸施了巫術。

passages.original: Pap says so his own self.
passages.vernacular: 爸爸自己咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸自己這麼說。

passages.original: He come along one day, and he see she was a-witching him, so he took up a rock, and if she hadn’t dodged, he’d a got her.
passages.vernacular: 有一天佢走過,睇到佢喺對佢施巫術,所以佢撿起一塊石頭,如果佢冇躲開,佢就砸到佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天他走過,看到她在對他施巫術,所以他撿起一塊石頭,如果她沒躲開,他就砸到她了。

passages.original: Well, that very night he rolled off’n a shed wher’ he was a layin drunk, and broke his arm.”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,就喺嗰天晚上佢從棚子上滾下嚟,佢當時醉倒躺喺嗰上面,摔斷咗手臂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,就在那天晚上他從棚子上滾下來,他當時醉倒躺在那上面,摔斷了手臂。」

passages.original: “Why, that’s awful.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,太可怕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,太可怕了。

passages.original: How did he know she was a-witching him?”
passages.vernacular: 佢點知道佢喺對佢施巫術?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他怎麼知道她在對他施巫術?」

passages.original: “Lord, pap can tell, easy.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,爸爸好容易睇出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,爸爸很容易看出來。

passages.original: Pap says when they keep looking at you right stiddy, they’re a-witching you.
passages.vernacular: 爸爸講,當佢哋一直直直地盯住你睇,佢哋就係喺對你施巫術。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸說,當他們一直直直地盯著你看,他們就是在對你施巫術。

passages.original: Specially if they mumble.
passages.vernacular: 特別係如果佢哋喃喃自語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 特別是如果他們喃喃自語。

passages.original: Becuz when they mumble they’re saying the Lord’s Prayer backards.”
passages.vernacular: 因為佢哋喃喃自語時,係喺倒住念主禱文。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為他們喃喃自語時,是在倒著念主禱文。」

passages.original: “Say, Hucky, when you going to try the cat?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,哈克,你乜嘢時候試貓?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,哈克,你什麼時候試貓?」

passages.original: “To-night.
passages.vernacular: 「今晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今晚。

passages.original: I reckon they’ll come after old Hoss Williams to-night.”
passages.vernacular: 我想今晚佢哋會嚟接老霍斯·威廉斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想今晚他們會來接老霍斯·威廉斯。」

passages.original: “But they buried him Saturday.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢哋星期六埋葬咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是他們星期六埋葬了他。

passages.original: Didn’t they get him Saturday night?”
passages.vernacular: 星期六晚上佢哋冇把佢帶走嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期六晚上他們沒把他帶走嗎?」

passages.original: “Why, how you talk!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,你點講話嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,你怎麼說話的!

passages.original: How could their charms work till midnight?—and then it’s Sunday.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅咒語點能喺午夜前起作用?——然後就係星期日喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們的咒語怎麼能在午夜前起作用?——然後就是星期日了。

passages.original: Devils don’t slosh around much of a Sunday, I don’t reckon.”
passages.vernacular: 我想魔鬼喺星期日唔會到處亂跑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想魔鬼在星期日不會到處亂跑。」

passages.original: “I never thought of that.
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇想到呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒想到這個。

passages.original: That’s so.
passages.vernacular: 對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對。

passages.original: Lemme go with you?”
passages.vernacular: 讓我同你去好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我同你去好嗎?」

passages.original: “Of course—if you ain’t afeard.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然——如果你不害怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然——如果你不害怕。」

passages.original: “Afeard! ’Tain’t likely.
passages.vernacular: 「害怕!唔可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「害怕!不可能。

passages.original: Will you meow?”
passages.vernacular: 你會喵喵叫嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會喵喵叫嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes—and you meow back, if you get a chance.
passages.vernacular: 「會——如果你有機會,你喵回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「會——如果你有機會,你喵回來。

passages.original: Last time, you kep’ me a-meowing around till old Hays went to throwing rocks at me and says ‘Dern that cat!’ and so I hove a brick through his window—but don’t you tell.”
passages.vernacular: 上次,你讓我喵咗好久,直到老海斯開始向我扔石頭,講『該死嘅貓!』所以我扔咗一塊磚頭穿過佢嘅窗子——不過你別告訴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上次,你讓我喵了很久,直到老海斯開始向我扔石頭,說『該死的貓!』所以我扔了一塊磚頭穿過他的窗子——可是你別告訴。」

passages.original: “I won’t.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不會。

passages.original: I couldn’t meow that night, becuz auntie was watching me, but I’ll meow this time.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上我唔能夠喵,因為姨媽喺睇住我,但呢次我會喵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上我不能喵,因為姨媽在看著我,但這次我會喵。

passages.original: Say—what’s that?”
passages.vernacular: 喂——嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂——那是什麼?」

passages.original: “Nothing but a tick.”
passages.vernacular: 「只係一隻扁蝨。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是一隻扁蝨。」

passages.original: “Where’d you get him?”
passages.vernacular: 「你從邊度弄嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你從哪裡弄來的?」

passages.original: “Out in the woods.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺樹林裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在樹林裡。」

passages.original: “What’ll you take for him?”
passages.vernacular: 「你要乜嘢才肯賣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要什麼才肯賣?」

passages.original: “I don’t know.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: I don’t want to sell him.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔想賣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想賣。」

passages.original: “All right.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧。

passages.original: It’s a mighty small tick, anyway.”
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,佢係隻好小嘅扁蝨。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,它是隻很小的扁蝨。」

passages.original: “Oh, anybody can run a tick down that don’t belong to them.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,任何人都可以追捕不屬於自己嘅扁蝨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,任何人都可以追捕不屬於自己的扁蝨。

passages.original: I’m satisfied with it.
passages.vernacular: 我對佢滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對它滿意。

passages.original: It’s a good enough tick for me.”
passages.vernacular: 對我來講佢係夠好嘅扁蝨。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我來說它是夠好的扁蝨。」

passages.original: “Sho, there’s ticks a plenty.
passages.vernacular: 「呸,扁蝨多得好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「呸,扁蝨多得很。

passages.original: I could have a thousand of ’em if I wanted to.”
passages.vernacular: 我想要嘅話可以有一千隻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想要的話可以有一千隻。」

passages.original: “Well, why don’t you?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你點解唔好?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你為什麼不要?

passages.original: Becuz you know mighty well you can’t.
passages.vernacular: 因為你好清楚你唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你很清楚你不能。

passages.original: This is a pretty early tick, I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係隻相當早嘅扁蝨,我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是隻相當早的扁蝨,我想。

passages.original: It’s the first one I’ve seen this year.”
passages.vernacular: 係我今年見到嘅第一隻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是我今年見到的第一隻。」

passages.original: “Say, Huck—I’ll give you my tooth for him.”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,哈克——我把我嘅牙畀你換佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,哈克——我把我的牙給你換它。」

passages.original: “Less see it.”
passages.vernacular: 「讓我睇睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我看看。」

passages.original: Tom got out a bit of paper and carefully unrolled it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆攞出一小張紙,小心地打開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拿出一小張紙,小心地打開。

passages.original: Huckleberry viewed it wistfully.
passages.vernacular: 哈克貝利渴望地睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克貝利渴望地看著它。

passages.original: The temptation was very strong.
passages.vernacular: 誘惑好強。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誘惑非常強。

passages.original: At last he said:
passages.vernacular: 最後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他說:

passages.original: “Is it genuwyne?”
passages.vernacular: 「係真嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是真的嗎?」

passages.original: Tom lifted his lip and showed the vacancy.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆掀起嘴唇,露出空缺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆掀起嘴唇,露出空缺。

passages.original: “Well, all right,” said Huckleberry, “it’s a trade.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」哈克貝利講,「成交。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」哈克貝利說,「成交。」

passages.original: Tom enclosed the tick in the percussion-cap box that had lately been the pinchbug’s prison, and the boys separated, each feeling wealthier than before.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆把扁蝨裝進最近啱啱係夾子蟲牢房嘅雷管盒子裡,男孩哋分手喇,各自覺得比以前富有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆把扁蝨裝進最近剛剛是夾子蟲牢房的雷管盒子裡,男孩們分手了,各自覺得比以前富有。

passages.original: When Tom reached the little isolated frame school-house, he strode in briskly, with the manner of one who had come with all honest speed.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆到咗嗰間孤立嘅小木框校舍,佢大步走進去,帶住一個以全部誠實速度趕嚟嘅人嘅神態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆到了那間孤立的小木框校舍,他大步走進去,帶著一個以全部誠實速度趕來的人的神態。

passages.original: He hung his hat on a peg and flung himself into his seat with business-like alacrity.
passages.vernacular: 佢把帽子掛喺釘子上,以辦事般嘅敏捷把自己扔到座位上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把帽子掛在釘子上,以辦事般的敏捷把自己扔到座位上。

passages.original: The master, throned on high in his great splint-bottom arm-chair, was dozing, lulled by the drowsy hum of study.
passages.vernacular: 老師高高坐喺佢嘅大木片底扶手椅上,被學習嘅昏昏欲瞓嘅嗡嗡聲催眠,正在打盹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師高高坐在他的大木片底扶手椅上,被學習的昏昏欲睡的嗡嗡聲催眠,正在打盹。

passages.original: The interruption roused him.
passages.vernacular: 呢個打斷驚醒咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個打斷驚醒了他。

passages.original: “Thomas Sawyer!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯瑪斯·索亞!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯瑪斯·索亞!」

passages.original: Tom knew that when his name was pronounced in full, it meant trouble.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆知道,佢嘅全名被喊出嚟,意味住麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆知道,他的全名被喊出來,意味著麻煩。

passages.original: “Sir!”
passages.vernacular: 「先生!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「先生!」

passages.original: “Come up here.
passages.vernacular: 「到呢度嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「到這裡來。

passages.original: Now, sir, why are you late again, as usual?”
passages.vernacular: 而家,先生,你點解又遲到喇,像往常一樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,先生,你為什麼又遲到了,像往常一樣?」

passages.original: Tom was about to take refuge in a lie, when he saw two long tails of yellow hair hanging down a back that he recognized by the electric sympathy of love; and by that form was the only vacant place on the girls’ side of the school-house.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆正要躲進一個謊言,呢陣佢睇到兩條黃色頭髮嘅長辮子垂喺一個背上,嗰背影佢憑愛嘅電感應認出嚟;嗰個身影旁邊係校舍女生嗰邊唯一嘅空位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆正要躲進一個謊言,這時他看到兩條黃色頭髮的長辮子垂在一個背上,那背影他憑愛的電感應認出來;那個身影旁邊是校舍女生那邊唯一的空位。

passages.original: He instantly said:
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他立刻說:

passages.original: “I stopped to talk with Huckleberry Finn!”
passages.vernacular: 「我停下嚟同哈克貝利·費恩講話!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我停下來同哈克貝利·費恩說話!」

passages.original: The master’s pulse stood still, and he stared helplessly.
passages.vernacular: 老師嘅脈搏停止喇,佢無助地瞪住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師的脈搏停止了,他無助地瞪著。

passages.original: The buzz of study ceased.
passages.vernacular: 學習嘅嗡嗡聲停止喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學習的嗡嗡聲停止了。

passages.original: The pupils wondered if this foolhardy boy had lost his mind.
passages.vernacular: 學生哋想,呢個魯莽嘅男孩係唔係瘋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學生們想,這個魯莽的男孩是不是瘋了。

passages.original: The master said:
passages.vernacular: 老師講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師說:

passages.original: “You—you did what?”
passages.vernacular: 「你——你做咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你——你做了什麼?」

passages.original: “Stopped to talk with Huckleberry Finn.”
passages.vernacular: 「停下嚟同哈克貝利·費恩講話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「停下來同哈克貝利·費恩說話。」

passages.original: There was no mistaking the words.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲話唔會聽錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些話不會聽錯。

passages.original: “Thomas Sawyer, this is the most astounding confession I have ever listened to.
passages.vernacular: 「湯瑪斯·索亞,呢個係我聽過嘅最驚人嘅供認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯瑪斯·索亞,這是我聽過的最驚人的供認。

passages.original: No mere ferule will answer for this offence.
passages.vernacular: 單單戒尺不足以懲罰呢種罪行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 單單戒尺不足以懲罰這種罪行。

passages.original: Take off your jacket.”
passages.vernacular: 脫掉你嘅外套。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 脫掉你的外套。」

passages.original: The master’s arm performed until it was tired and the stock of switches notably diminished.
passages.vernacular: 老師嘅手臂表演,直到累喇,細枝鞭嘅存貨明顯減少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師的手臂表演,直到累了,細枝鞭的存貨明顯減少。

passages.original: Then the order followed:
passages.vernacular: 然後命令跟住嚟喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後命令跟著來了:

passages.original: “Now, sir, go and sit with the girls!
passages.vernacular: 「而家,先生,去同女生坐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,先生,去同女生坐!

passages.original: And let this be a warning to you.”
passages.vernacular: 讓呢個成為對你嘅警告。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓這個成為對你的警告。」

passages.original: The titter that rippled around the room appeared to abash the boy, but in reality that result was caused rather more by his worshipful awe of his unknown idol and the dread pleasure that lay in his high good fortune.
passages.vernacular: 喺整個教室裡蕩漾嘅竊笑似乎使男孩尷尬,但事實上呢個結果更多係由於佢對佢唔知名嘅偶像虔誠嘅敬畏,同佢嘅大好運所包含嘅可怕快樂造成嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在整個教室裡蕩漾的竊笑似乎使男孩尷尬,但事實上這個結果更多是由於他對他不知名的偶像虔誠的敬畏,和他的大好運所包含的可怕快樂造成的。

passages.original: He sat down upon the end of the pine bench and the girl hitched herself away from him with a toss of her head.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐喺松木長凳嘅末端,女孩把自己挪離佢,甩咗甩頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐在松木長凳的末端,女孩把自己挪離他,甩了甩頭。

passages.original: Nudges and winks and whispers traversed the room, but Tom sat still, with his arms upon the long, low desk before him, and seemed to study his book.
passages.vernacular: 擠眉弄眼同竊竊私語穿過房間,但湯姆坐住不動,雙臂放喺面前又長又矮嘅桌上,似乎喺睇書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 擠眉弄眼和竊竊私語穿過房間,但湯姆坐著不動,雙臂放在面前又長又矮的桌上,似乎在看書。

passages.original: By and by attention ceased from him, and the accustomed school murmur rose upon the dull air once more.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地人哋唔再注意佢,慣常嘅學校嗡嗡聲又喺沉悶嘅空氣中升起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地人們不再注意他,慣常的學校嗡嗡聲又在沉悶的空氣中升起。

passages.original: Presently the boy began to steal furtive glances at the girl.
passages.vernacular: 不久男孩開始偷偷地瞥女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久男孩開始偷偷地瞥女孩。

passages.original: She observed it, “made a mouth” at him and gave him the back of her head for the space of a minute.
passages.vernacular: 佢察覺喇,對佢「撇咗嘴」,把後腦勺畀咗佢一分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她察覺了,對他「撇了嘴」,把後腦勺給了他一分鐘。

passages.original: When she cautiously faced around again, a peach lay before her.
passages.vernacular: 佢小心地再轉過頭時,一個桃子躺喺佢面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她小心地再轉過頭時,一個桃子躺在她面前。

passages.original: She thrust it away.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢推開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把它推開。

passages.original: Tom gently put it back.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆輕輕把佢放回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆輕輕把它放回去。

passages.original: She thrust it away again, but with less animosity.
passages.vernacular: 佢又把佢推開,但敵意少咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她又把它推開,但敵意少了一些。

passages.original: Tom patiently returned it to its place.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆耐心地把佢放回原位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆耐心地把它放回原位。

passages.original: Then she let it remain.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢讓佢留喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她讓它留在那裡。

passages.original: Tom scrawled on his slate, “Please take it—I got more.”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喺石板上塗寫:「請攞去——我仲有。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆在石板上塗寫:「請拿去——我還有。」

passages.original: The girl glanced at the words, but made no sign.
passages.vernacular: 女孩瞥咗一眼呢啲字,但冇表示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩瞥了一眼這些字,但沒有表示。

passages.original: Now the boy began to draw something on the slate, hiding his work with his left hand.
passages.vernacular: 而家男孩開始喺石板上畫些乜嘢,用左手遮住佢嘅作品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在男孩開始在石板上畫些什麼,用左手遮住他的作品。

passages.original: For a time the girl refused to notice; but her human curiosity presently began to manifest itself by hardly perceptible signs.
passages.vernacular: 有一陣子女孩拒絕注意;但佢人類嘅好奇心不久開始以幾乎察覺不出嘅跡象表現出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一陣子女孩拒絕注意;但她人類的好奇心不久開始以幾乎察覺不出的跡象表現出來。

passages.original: The boy worked on, apparently unconscious.
passages.vernacular: 男孩繼續畫,顯然毫無意識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩繼續畫,顯然毫無意識。

passages.original: The girl made a sort of non-committal attempt to see, but the boy did not betray that he was aware of it.
passages.vernacular: 女孩做咗一種不置可否嘅嘗試去睇,但男孩冇暴露佢知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩做了一種不置可否的嘗試去看,但男孩沒有暴露他知道。

passages.original: At last she gave in and hesitatingly whispered:
passages.vernacular: 最後佢屈服喇,猶豫地低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後她屈服了,猶豫地低聲說:

passages.original: “Let me see it.”
passages.vernacular: 「讓我睇睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我看看。」

passages.original: Tom partly uncovered a dismal caricature of a house with two gable ends to it and a corkscrew of smoke issuing from the chimney.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆部分揭開咗一幅陰森嘅房子漫畫,有兩個山牆,煙囪裡冒出一縷像開瓶器似嘅煙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆部分揭開了一幅陰森的房子漫畫,有兩個山牆,煙囪裡冒出一縷像開瓶器似的煙。

passages.original: Then the girl’s interest began to fasten itself upon the work and she forgot everything else.
passages.vernacular: 然後女孩嘅興趣開始集中喺呢作品上,佢忘咗其他一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後女孩的興趣開始集中在這作品上,她忘了其他一切。

passages.original: When it was finished, she gazed a moment, then whispered:
passages.vernacular: 畫完後,佢凝視咗一會兒,然後低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 畫完後,她凝視了一會兒,然後低聲說:

passages.original: “It’s nice—make a man.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好睇——畫個人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好看——畫個人。」

passages.original: The artist erected a man in the front yard, that resembled a derrick.
passages.vernacular: 畫家喺前院豎起咗一個人,像個起重機。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 畫家在前院豎起了一個人,像個起重機。

passages.original: He could have stepped over the house; but the girl was not hypercritical; she was satisfied with the monster, and whispered:
passages.vernacular: 佢可以跨過房子;但女孩不挑剔;佢對呢個怪物滿意,低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他可以跨過房子;但女孩不挑剔;她對這個怪物滿意,低聲說:

passages.original: “It’s a beautiful man—now make me coming along.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個美麗嘅人——而家畫我走過嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個美麗的人——現在畫我走過來。」

passages.original: Tom drew an hour-glass with a full moon and straw limbs to it and armed the spreading fingers with a portentous fan.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆畫咗個沙漏,加上滿月同稻草嘅四肢,喺張開嘅手指上武裝咗一把不祥嘅扇子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆畫了個沙漏,加上滿月和稻草的四肢,在張開的手指上武裝了一把不祥的扇子。

passages.original: The girl said:
passages.vernacular: 女孩講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩說:

passages.original: “It’s ever so nice—I wish I could draw.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好睇——我希望我會畫。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「非常好看——我希望我會畫。」

passages.original: “It’s easy,” whispered Tom, “I’ll learn you.”
passages.vernacular: 「好容易,」湯姆低聲講,「我教你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很容易,」湯姆低聲說,「我教你。」

passages.original: “Oh, will you?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你願意嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你願意嗎?

passages.original: When?”
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢時候?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼時候?」

passages.original: “At noon.
passages.vernacular: 「中午。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「中午。

passages.original: Do you go home to dinner?”
passages.vernacular: 你回家食午飯嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你回家吃午飯嗎?」

passages.original: “I’ll stay if you will.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你留下,我就留下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你留下,我就留下。」

passages.original: “Good—that’s a whack.
passages.vernacular: 「好——講定喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好——說定了。

passages.original: What’s your name?”
passages.vernacular: 你叫乜嘢名字?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫什麼名字?」

passages.original: “Becky Thatcher.
passages.vernacular: 「貝琪·撒切爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貝琪·撒切爾。

passages.original: What’s yours?
passages.vernacular: 你呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你呢?

passages.original: Oh, I know.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我知道。

passages.original: It’s Thomas Sawyer.”
passages.vernacular: 係湯瑪斯·索亞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是湯瑪斯·索亞。」

passages.original: “That’s the name they lick me by.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係佢哋揍我時用嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是他們揍我時用的名字。

passages.original: I’m Tom when I’m good.
passages.vernacular: 我乖嘅時候叫湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我乖的時候叫湯姆。

passages.original: You call me Tom, will you?”
passages.vernacular: 你叫我湯姆,好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫我湯姆,好嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
Now Tom began to scrawl something on the slate, hiding the words from the girl.
passages.vernacular: 而家湯姆開始喺石板上塗寫些乜嘢,把字藏起嚟不讓女孩睇到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在湯姆開始在石板上塗寫些什麼,把字藏起來不讓女孩看到。

passages.original: But she was not backward this time.
passages.vernacular: 但呢次佢不退縮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這次她不退縮。

passages.original: She begged to see.
passages.vernacular: 佢央求睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她央求看。

passages.original: Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說:

passages.original: “Oh, it ain’t anything.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,冇乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,沒什麼。」

passages.original: “Yes it is.”
passages.vernacular: 「有嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有的。」

passages.original: “No it ain’t.
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。

passages.original: You don’t want to see.”
passages.vernacular: 你唔會想睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不會想看。」

passages.original: “Yes I do, indeed I do.
passages.vernacular: 「我想,真嘅想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想,真的想。

passages.original: Please let me.”
passages.vernacular: 求你讓我睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求你讓我看。」

passages.original: “You’ll tell.”
passages.vernacular: 「你會講出去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會說出去。」

passages.original: “No I won’t—deed and deed and double deed won’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,我唔會——絕對、絕對、絕對唔會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我不會——絕對、絕對、絕對不會。」

passages.original: “You won’t tell anybody at all?
passages.vernacular: 「你完全唔會告訴任何人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你完全不會告訴任何人?

passages.original: Ever, as long as you live?”
passages.vernacular: 永遠,只要你活住?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永遠,只要你活著?」

passages.original: “No, I won’t ever tell anybody.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我永遠唔會告訴任何人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我永遠不會告訴任何人。

passages.original: Now let me.”
passages.vernacular: 而家讓我睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在讓我看。」

passages.original: “Oh, you don’t want to see!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你唔想睇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你不想看!」

passages.original: “Now that you treat me so, I will see.”
passages.vernacular: 「既然你咁樣對我,我就要睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「既然你這樣對我,我就要看。」

passages.original: And she put her small hand upon his and a little scuffle ensued, Tom pretending to resist in earnest but letting his hand slip by degrees till these words were revealed: “I love you.”
passages.vernacular: 佢把小手放喺佢嘅手上,一場小小嘅扭打隨之而嚟,湯姆假裝認真地抵抗,卻讓手啲啲滑開,直到呢幾個字露出嚟:「我愛你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把小手放在他的手上,一場小小的扭打隨之而來,湯姆假裝認真地抵抗,卻讓手一點一點滑開,直到這幾個字露出來:「我愛你。」

passages.original: “Oh, you bad thing!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你呢壞傢伙!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你這壞傢伙!」

passages.original: And she hit his hand a smart rap, but reddened and looked pleased, nevertheless.
passages.vernacular: 佢狠狠拍咗一下佢嘅手,但臉紅喇,而且睇起嚟高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她狠狠拍了一下他的手,但臉紅了,而且看起來高興。

passages.original: Just at this juncture the boy felt a slow, fateful grip closing on his ear, and a steady lifting impulse.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,男孩感到一個緩慢嘅、命運般嘅夾握喺佢嘅耳朵上收緊,仲有一股穩定嘅上提嘅力量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,男孩感到一個緩慢的、命運般的夾握在他的耳朵上收緊,還有一股穩定的上提的力量。

passages.original: In that wise he was borne across the house and deposited in his own seat, under a peppering fire of giggles from the whole school.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣佢被帶過整個房子,放喺自己嘅座位上,全校嘅咯咯笑聲像胡椒般密集地向佢開火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣他被帶過整個房子,放在自己的座位上,全校的咯咯笑聲像胡椒般密集地向他開火。

passages.original: Then the master stood over him during a few awful moments, and finally moved away to his throne without saying a word.
passages.vernacular: 然後老師站喺佢面前度過咗可怕嘅幾分鐘,最後一言不發地走回佢嘅寶座。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後老師站在他面前度過了可怕的幾分鐘,最後一言不發地走回他的寶座。

passages.original: But although Tom’s ear tingled, his heart was jubilant.
passages.vernacular: 但雖然湯姆嘅耳朵發燙,佢嘅心卻歡騰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但雖然湯姆的耳朵發燙,他的心卻歡騰。

passages.original: As the school quieted down Tom made an honest effort to study, but the turmoil within him was too great.
passages.vernacular: 學校安靜下嚟時,湯姆誠實地努力學習,但佢內心嘅混亂太大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學校安靜下來時,湯姆誠實地努力學習,但他內心的混亂太大了。

passages.original: In turn he took his place in the reading class and made a botch of it; then in the geography class and turned lakes into mountains, mountains into rivers, and rivers into continents, till chaos was come again; then in the spelling class, and got “turned down,” by a succession of mere baby words, till he brought up at the foot and yielded up the pewter medal which he had worn with ostentation for months.
passages.vernacular: 佢依次坐到閱讀班,搞得一團糟;然後地理班,把湖變成山,山變成河,河變成大陸,直到混沌重現;然後拼字班,被一連串嬰兒般嘅字「打下去」,直到墊底,交出咗佢炫耀地戴咗幾個月嘅白鑞獎章。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他依次坐到閱讀班,搞得一團糟;然後地理班,把湖變成山,山變成河,河變成大陸,直到混沌重現;然後拼字班,被一連串嬰兒般的字「打下去」,直到墊底,交出了他炫耀地戴了幾個月的白鑞獎章。

chapters.title: Chapter VII: A Treaty Entered Into 第七章:訂立盟約

passages.original: CH The harder Tom tried to fasten his mind on his book, the more his ideas wandered.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆越努力把心思放喺書上,佢嘅思緒就越游離。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆越努力把心思放在書上,他的思緒就越游離。

passages.original: So at last, with a sigh and a yawn, he gave it up.
passages.vernacular: 於是最後,佢歎咗口氣,打咗個呵欠,放棄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是最後,他歎了口氣,打了個呵欠,放棄了。

passages.original: It seemed to him that the noon recess would never come.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得中午嘅休息時間永遠唔會嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他覺得中午的休息時間永遠不會來。

passages.original: The air was utterly dead.
passages.vernacular: 空氣完全係死嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空氣完全是死的。

passages.original: There was not a breath stirring.
passages.vernacular: 冇一絲風喺動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一絲風在動。

passages.original: It was the sleepiest of sleepy days.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係最昏昏欲瞓嘅昏瞓日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是最昏昏欲睡的昏睡日。

passages.original: The drowsing murmur of the five and twenty studying scholars soothed the soul like the spell that is in the murmur of bees.
passages.vernacular: 二十五個學習嘅學生嘅催眠般嘅嗡嗡聲,像蜜蜂嗡嗡聲裡嘅咒語一樣撫慰住靈魂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 二十五個學習的學生的催眠般的嗡嗡聲,像蜜蜂嗡嗡聲裡的咒語一樣撫慰著靈魂。

passages.original: Away off in the flaming sunshine, Cardiff Hill lifted its soft green sides through a shimmering veil of heat, tinted with the purple of distance; a few birds floated on lazy wing high in the air; no other living thing was visible but some cows, and they were asleep.
passages.vernacular: 遠處喺熾熱嘅陽光下,卡迪夫山透過一層帶住遠方紫色嘅閃爍熱氣面紗,抬起佢柔和嘅綠色山坡;幾隻鳥喺高空懶洋洋地翅膀漂浮;除咗幾頭牛,睇唔到其他活物,而牠哋喺瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠處在熾熱的陽光下,卡迪夫山透過一層帶著遠方紫色的閃爍熱氣面紗,抬起它柔和的綠色山坡;幾隻鳥在高空懶洋洋地翅膀漂浮;除了幾頭牛,看不到其他活物,而牠們在睡覺。

passages.original: Tom’s heart ached to be free, or else to have something of interest to do to pass the dreary time.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅心渴望自由,或者有乜嘢有趣嘅事可做嚟打發呢沉悶嘅時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的心渴望自由,或者有什麼有趣的事可做來打發這沉悶的時間。

passages.original: His hand wandered into his pocket and his face lit up with a glow of gratitude that was prayer, though he did not know it.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅手游進口袋,臉上亮起一道感激嘅光輝,嗰個係祈禱,雖然佢自己唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的手游進口袋,臉上亮起一道感激的光輝,那是祈禱,雖然他自己不知道。

passages.original: Then furtively the percussion-cap box came out.
passages.vernacular: 然後嗰個雷管盒子偷偷攞咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後那個雷管盒子偷偷拿了出來。

passages.original: He released the tick and put him on the long flat desk.
passages.vernacular: 佢放出扁蝨,把佢放喺長長嘅平桌上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他放出扁蝨,把它放在長長的平桌上。

passages.original: The creature probably glowed with a gratitude that amounted to prayer, too, at this moment, but it was premature: for when he started thankfully to travel off, Tom turned him aside with a pin and made him take a new direction.
passages.vernacular: 呢生物此刻大概都閃耀住相當於祈禱嘅感激,但呢個係過早嘅:因為佢開始感激地走開時,湯姆用一根針把佢撥開,讓佢走一個新方向。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這生物此刻大概也閃耀著相當於祈禱的感激,但這是過早的:因為它開始感激地走開時,湯姆用一根針把它撥開,讓它走一個新方向。

passages.original: Tom’s bosom friend sat next him, suffering just as Tom had been, and now he was deeply and gratefully interested in this entertainment in an instant.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅知心朋友坐喺佢旁邊,正像湯姆一樣受苦,而家轉眼間佢深深地、感激地對呢項娛樂產生咗興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的知心朋友坐在他旁邊,正像湯姆一樣受苦,現在轉眼間他深深地、感激地對這項娛樂產生了興趣。

passages.original: This bosom friend was Joe Harper.
passages.vernacular: 呢個知心朋友係喬·哈珀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個知心朋友是喬·哈珀。

passages.original: The two boys were sworn friends all the week, and embattled enemies on Saturdays.
passages.vernacular: 兩個男孩一星期都係宣誓嘅朋友,星期六則係交戰嘅敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個男孩一星期都是宣誓的朋友,星期六則是交戰的敵人。

passages.original: Joe took a pin out of his lapel and began to assist in exercising the prisoner.
passages.vernacular: 喬從翻領上取下一根針,開始幫忙訓練呢個俘虜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬從翻領上取下一根針,開始幫忙訓練這個俘虜。

passages.original: The sport grew in interest momently.
passages.vernacular: 呢項運動嘅趣味時時增加。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這項運動的趣味時時增加。

passages.original: Soon Tom said that they were interfering with each other, and neither getting the fullest benefit of the tick.
passages.vernacular: 不久湯姆講佢哋喺互相干擾,邊個都冇充分利用扁蝨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久湯姆說他們在互相干擾,誰也沒有充分利用扁蝨。

passages.original: So he put Joe’s slate on the desk and drew a line down the middle of it from top to bottom.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢把喬嘅石板放喺桌上,從上到下喺中間畫咗一條線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他把喬的石板放在桌上,從上到下在中間畫了一條線。

passages.original: “Now,” said he, “as long as he is on your side you can stir him up and I’ll let him alone; but if you let him get away and get on my side, you’re to leave him alone as long as I can keep him from crossing over.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,」佢講,「只要佢喺你呢邊,你可以撥弄佢,我不管;但如果你讓佢跑掉到我呢邊,只要我能讓佢不越過去,你就不許碰佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,」他說,「只要它在你這邊,你可以撥弄它,我不管;但如果你讓它跑掉到我這邊,只要我能讓它不越過去,你就不許碰它。」

passages.original: “All right, go ahead; start him up.”
passages.vernacular: 「好,開始吧;讓佢動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,開始吧;讓它動。」

passages.original: The tick escaped from Tom, presently, and crossed the equator.
passages.vernacular: 不久扁蝨從湯姆嗰邊逃咗出去,越過咗赤道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久扁蝨從湯姆那邊逃了出去,越過了赤道。

passages.original: Joe harassed him awhile, and then he got away and crossed back again.
passages.vernacular: 喬騷擾咗佢一會兒,然後佢逃走又越回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬騷擾了它一會兒,然後它逃走又越回來。

passages.original: This change of base occurred often.
passages.vernacular: 呢種換基地常常發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種換基地常常發生。

passages.original: While one boy was worrying the tick with absorbing interest, the other would look on with interest as strong, the two heads bowed together over the slate, and the two souls dead to all things else.
passages.vernacular: 一個男孩以全神貫注嘅興趣折磨扁蝨時,另一個都以同樣強烈嘅興趣睇住,兩個頭一起彎喺石板上,兩個靈魂對其他一切毫無知覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個男孩以全神貫注的興趣折磨扁蝨時,另一個也以同樣強烈的興趣看著,兩個頭一起彎在石板上,兩個靈魂對其他一切毫無知覺。

passages.original: At last luck seemed to settle and abide with Joe.
passages.vernacular: 最後運氣似乎喺喬嗰邊安頓下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後運氣似乎在喬那邊安頓下來了。

passages.original: The tick tried this, that, and the other course, and got as excited and as anxious as the boys themselves, but time and again just as he would have victory in his very grasp, so to speak, and Tom’s fingers would be twitching to begin, Joe’s pin would deftly head him off, and keep possession.
passages.vernacular: 扁蝨試咗呢條路、嗰條路同另一條路,變得同男孩哋一樣激動同焦急,但一次又一次,正當佢可以講勝利就喺掌握之中,湯姆嘅手指抽動住要開始時,喬嘅針就巧妙地攔住佢,保持佔有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 扁蝨試了這條路、那條路和另一條路,變得和男孩們一樣激動和焦急,但一次又一次,正當它可以說勝利就在掌握之中,湯姆的手指抽動著要開始時,喬的針就巧妙地攔住它,保持佔有。

passages.original: At last Tom could stand it no longer.
passages.vernacular: 最後湯姆再都忍受不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後湯姆再也忍受不了。

passages.original: The temptation was too strong.
passages.vernacular: 誘惑太強喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誘惑太強了。

passages.original: So he reached out and lent a hand with his pin.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢伸出手用針幫忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他伸出手用針幫忙。

passages.original: Joe was angry in a moment.
passages.vernacular: 喬即刻生氣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬立刻生氣了。

passages.original: Said he:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “Tom, you let him alone.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,你別管佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,你別管它。」

passages.original: “I only just want to stir him up a little, Joe.”
passages.vernacular: 「我只想把佢撥動啲點,喬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只想把它撥動一點點,喬。」

passages.original: “No, sir, it ain’t fair; you just let him alone.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,先生,呢不公平;你別管佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,先生,這不公平;你別管它。」

passages.original: “Blame it, I ain’t going to stir him much.”
passages.vernacular: 「真該死,我唔會點撥佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真該死,我不會怎麼撥它。」

passages.original: “Let him alone, I tell you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我告訴你別管佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我告訴你別管它。」

passages.original: “I won’t!”
passages.vernacular: 「我不!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不!」

passages.original: “You shall—he’s on my side of the line.”
passages.vernacular: 「你必須——佢喺我呢邊嘅線上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你必須——它在我這邊的線上。」

passages.original: “Look here, Joe Harper, whose is that tick?”
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,喬·哈珀,嗰扁蝨係邊個嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,喬·哈珀,那扁蝨是誰的?」

passages.original: “I don’t care whose tick he is—he’s on my side of the line, and you sha’n’t touch him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不管佢係邊個嘅扁蝨——佢喺我呢邊嘅線上,你不許碰佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不管它是誰的扁蝨——它在我這邊的線上,你不許碰它。」

passages.original: “Well, I’ll just bet I will, though.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我敢打賭我要碰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我敢打賭我要碰。

passages.original: He’s my tick and I’ll do what I blame please with him, or die!”
passages.vernacular: 佢係我嘅扁蝨,我愛點樣就點樣,否則我就死!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是我的扁蝨,我愛怎麼樣就怎麼樣,否則我就死!」

passages.original: A tremendous whack came down on Tom’s shoulders, and its duplicate on Joe’s; and for the space of two minutes the dust continued to fly from the two jackets and the whole school to enjoy it.
passages.vernacular: 一記巨大嘅鞭打落喺湯姆肩上,同樣嘅一記落喺喬身上;兩分鐘內塵土不斷從兩件外衣上飛出,全校都喺享受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一記巨大的鞭打落在湯姆肩上,同樣的一記落在喬身上;兩分鐘內塵土不斷從兩件外衣上飛出,全校都在享受。

passages.original: The boys had been too absorbed to notice the hush that had stolen upon the school awhile before when the master came tiptoeing down the room and stood over them.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋太專注喇,冇注意到不久前老師踮住腳尖沿房間走嚟、站喺佢哋上方時悄悄降臨學校嘅寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們太專注了,沒注意到不久前老師踮著腳尖沿房間走來、站在他們上方時悄悄降臨學校的寂靜。

passages.original: He had contemplated a good part of the performance before he contributed his bit of variety to it.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺畀佢加入佢嗰點變化之前,已經欣賞咗相當一部分表演。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在給它加入他那點變化之前,已經欣賞了相當一部分表演。

passages.original: When school broke up at noon, Tom flew to Becky Thatcher, and whispered in her ear:
passages.vernacular: 中午放學時,湯姆飛奔到貝琪·撒切爾嗰度,喺佢耳邊低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 中午放學時,湯姆飛奔到貝琪·撒切爾那裡,在她耳邊低聲說:

passages.original: “Put on your bonnet and let on you’re going home; and when you get to the corner, give the rest of ’em the slip, and turn down through the lane and come back.
passages.vernacular: 「戴上你嘅帽子,假裝你要回家;到轉角時,把其他人甩掉,拐下小巷再回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「戴上你的帽子,假裝你要回家;到轉角時,把其他人甩掉,拐下小巷再回來。

passages.original: I’ll go the other way and come it over ’em the same way.”
passages.vernacular: 我走另一條路,用同樣嘅方法甩掉佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我走另一條路,用同樣的方法甩掉他們。」

passages.original: So the one went off with one group of scholars, and the other with another.
passages.vernacular: 於是一個同一群學生走喇,另一個同另一群走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是一個同一群學生走了,另一個同另一群走了。

passages.original: In a little while the two met at the bottom of the lane, and when they reached the school they had it all to themselves.
passages.vernacular: 不久兩人喺小巷嘅盡頭會合,等佢哋回到學校時,學校完全屬於佢哋自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久兩人在小巷的盡頭會合,等他們回到學校時,學校完全屬於他們自己。

passages.original: Then they sat together, with a slate before them, and Tom gave Becky the pencil and held her hand in his, guiding it, and so created another surprising house.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋坐喺一起,面前一塊石板,湯姆把鉛筆畀貝琪,握住佢嘅手,引導住佢,咁樣創造咗又一座令人驚奇嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們坐在一起,面前一塊石板,湯姆把鉛筆給貝琪,握著她的手,引導著它,這樣創造了又一座令人驚奇的房子。

passages.original: When the interest in art began to wane, the two fell to talking.
passages.vernacular: 當對藝術嘅興趣開始減退,兩人開始談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當對藝術的興趣開始減退,兩人開始談話。

passages.original: Tom was swimming in bliss.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆浸喺幸福裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆浸在幸福裡。

passages.original: He said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “Do you love rats?”
passages.vernacular: 「你愛老鼠嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你愛老鼠嗎?」

passages.original: “No!
I hate them!”
passages.vernacular: 我恨牠哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我恨牠們!」

passages.original: “Well, I do, too—live ones.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我都係——活嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我也是——活的。

passages.original: But I mean dead ones, to swing round your head with a string.”
passages.vernacular: 但我係講死嘅,用一根繩子喺你頭上甩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我是說死的,用一根繩子在你頭上甩。」

passages.original: “No, I don’t care for rats much, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 「不,無論如何我不太鍾意老鼠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,無論如何我不太喜歡老鼠。

passages.original: What I like is chewing-gum.”
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意嘅係口香糖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡的是口香糖。」

passages.original: “Oh, I should say so!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我應該講係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我應該說是!

passages.original: I wish I had some now.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望我而家有啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我現在有一些。」

passages.original: “Do you?
passages.vernacular: 「你想嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想嗎?

passages.original: I’ve got some.
passages.vernacular: 我有啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一些。

passages.original: I’ll let you chew it awhile, but you must give it back to me.”
passages.vernacular: 我讓你嚼一會兒,但你必須還畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讓你嚼一會兒,但你必須還給我。」

passages.original: That was agreeable, so they chewed it turn about, and dangled their legs against the bench in excess of contentment.
passages.vernacular: 呢個好好,於是佢哋輪流嚼,滿足過度地用腿拍打長凳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這很好,於是他們輪流嚼,滿足過度地用腿拍打長凳。

passages.original: “Was you ever at a circus?” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「你去過馬戲團嗎?」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你去過馬戲團嗎?」湯姆說。

passages.original: “Yes, and my pa’s going to take me again some time, if I’m good.”
passages.vernacular: 「去過,我爸爸有時間仲要帶我去,如果我乖嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去過,我爸爸有時間還要帶我去,如果我乖的話。」

passages.original: “I been to the circus three or four times—lots of times.
passages.vernacular: 「我去過三四次馬戲團——好多次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我去過三四次馬戲團——很多次。

passages.original: Church ain’t shucks to a circus.
passages.vernacular: 教堂跟馬戲團比根本不算乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 教堂跟馬戲團比根本不算什麼。

passages.original: There’s things going on at a circus all the time.
passages.vernacular: 馬戲團裡一直有事情喺進行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬戲團裡一直有事情在進行。

passages.original: I’m going to be a clown in a circus when I grow up.”
passages.vernacular: 我長大後要喺馬戲團裡當小丑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我長大後要在馬戲團裡當小丑。」

passages.original: “Oh, are you!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是嗎!

passages.original: That will be nice.
passages.vernacular: 嗰會好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會很好。

passages.original: They’re so lovely, all spotted up.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋咁可愛,渾身斑點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們那麼可愛,渾身斑點。」

passages.original: “Yes, that’s so.
passages.vernacular: 「對,係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,是的。

passages.original: And they get slathers of money—most a dollar a day, Ben Rogers says.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢哋賺大把嘅錢——差不多每天一塊錢,本·羅傑斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且他們賺大把的錢——差不多每天一塊錢,本·羅傑斯說。

passages.original: Say, Becky, was you ever engaged?”
passages.vernacular: 喂,貝琪,你訂過婚嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,貝琪,你訂過婚嗎?」

passages.original: “What’s that?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, engaged to be married.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,訂婚結婚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,訂婚結婚。」

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。」

passages.original: “Would you like to?”
passages.vernacular: 「你想嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想嗎?」

passages.original: “I reckon so.
passages.vernacular: 「我想係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是的。

passages.original: I don’t know.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道。

passages.original: What is it like?”
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢樣嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼樣的?」

passages.original: “Like?
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼樣?

passages.original: Why it ain’t like anything.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,佢不像任何嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,它不像任何東西。

passages.original: You only just tell a boy you won’t ever have anybody but him, ever ever ever, and then you kiss and that’s all.
passages.vernacular: 你只係告訴一個男孩你永遠唔會有別人只有佢,永遠永遠永遠,然後你哋親吻,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只是告訴一個男孩你永遠不會有別人只有他,永遠永遠永遠,然後你們親吻,就是這樣。

passages.original: Anybody can do it.”
passages.vernacular: 任何人都可以做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何人都可以做。」

passages.original: “Kiss?
passages.vernacular: 「親吻?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親吻?

passages.original: What do you kiss for?”
passages.vernacular: 點解要親吻?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼要親吻?」

passages.original: “Why, that, you know, is to—well, they always do that.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,嗰,你知道,係為喇——嗯,佢哋總是咁樣做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,那,你知道,是為了——嗯,他們總是這樣做。」

passages.original: “Everybody?”
passages.vernacular: 「每個人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「每個人?」

passages.original: “Why, yes, everybody that’s in love with each other.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,係嘅,每個互相相愛嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,是的,每個互相相愛的人。

passages.original: Do you remember what I wrote on the slate?”
passages.vernacular: 你記得我喺石板上寫咗乜嘢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你記得我在石板上寫了什麼嗎?」

passages.original: “Ye—yes.”
“What was it?”
passages.vernacular: 「係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是什麼?」

passages.original: “I sha’n’t tell you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不告訴你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不告訴你。」

passages.original: “Shall I tell you?”
passages.vernacular: 「我告訴你好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我告訴你好嗎?」

passages.original: “Ye—yes—but some other time.”
passages.vernacular: 「好——好——但改天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好——好——但改天。」

passages.original: “No, now.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,而家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,現在。」

passages.original: “No, not now—to-morrow.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,唔係而家——聽日。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不是現在——明天。」

passages.original: “Oh, no, now.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,而家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,現在。

passages.original: Please, Becky—I’ll whisper it, I’ll whisper it ever so easy.”
passages.vernacular: 求你,貝琪——我低聲講,我講得好輕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求你,貝琪——我低聲說,我說得非常輕。」

passages.original: Becky hesitating, Tom took silence for consent, and passed his arm about her waist and whispered the tale ever so softly, with his mouth close to her ear.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪猶豫住,湯姆把沉默當作同意,用手臂環住佢嘅腰,把嘴貼近佢嘅耳朵,好輕地低聲講出嗰個故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪猶豫著,湯姆把沉默當作同意,用手臂環住她的腰,把嘴貼近她的耳朵,非常輕地低聲說出那個故事。

passages.original: And then he added:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢補充講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他補充說:

passages.original: “Now you whisper it to me—just the same.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家你低聲講畀我聽——一樣嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你低聲說給我聽——一樣的。」

passages.original: She resisted, for a while, and then said:
passages.vernacular: 佢抗拒咗一會兒,然後講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她抗拒了一會兒,然後說:

passages.original: “You turn your face away so you can’t see, and then I will.
passages.vernacular: 「你把臉轉開,咁樣你睇唔見,我就講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你把臉轉開,這樣你看不見,我就說。

passages.original: But you mustn’t ever tell anybody—will you, Tom?
passages.vernacular: 但你絕不許告訴任何人——你會嗎,湯姆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你絕不許告訴任何人——你會嗎,湯姆?

passages.original: Now you won’t, will you?”
passages.vernacular: 你唔會,對吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不會,對吧?」

passages.original: “No, indeed, indeed I won’t.
passages.vernacular: 「不,真嘅,真嘅我唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,真的,真的我不會。

passages.original: Now, Becky.”
passages.vernacular: 而家,貝琪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,貝琪。」

passages.original: He turned his face away.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉過臉去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他轉過臉去。

passages.original: She bent timidly around till her breath stirred his curls and whispered, “I—love—you!”
passages.vernacular: 佢膽怯地彎過嚟,直到佢嘅氣息撥動佢嘅捲髮,低聲講:「我——愛——你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她膽怯地彎過來,直到她的氣息撥動他的捲髮,低聲說:「我——愛——你!」

passages.original: Then she sprang away and ran around and around the desks and benches, with Tom after her, and took refuge in a corner at last, with her little white apron to her face.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢跳開,繞住桌子同長凳一圈又一圈地跑,湯姆追住佢,最後躲進一個角落,把佢嘅小白圍裙捂喺臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她跳開,繞著桌子和長凳一圈又一圈地跑,湯姆追著她,最後躲進一個角落,把她的小白圍裙捂在臉上。

passages.original: Tom clasped her about her neck and pleaded:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆摟住佢嘅脖子,懇求講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆摟住她的脖子,懇求說:

passages.original: “Now, Becky, it’s all done—all over but the kiss.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,貝琪,都做完喇——只剩下吻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,貝琪,都做完了——只剩下吻。

passages.original: Don’t you be afraid of that—it ain’t anything at all.
passages.vernacular: 你別怕嗰個——佢根本不算乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你別怕那個——它根本不算什麼。

passages.original: Please, Becky.”
passages.vernacular: 求你,貝琪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求你,貝琪。」

passages.original: And he tugged at her apron and the hands.
passages.vernacular: 佢拉扯住佢嘅圍裙同手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拉扯著她的圍裙和手。

passages.original: By and by she gave up, and let her hands drop; her face, all glowing with the struggle, came up and submitted.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地佢放棄喇,讓雙手落下;佢嘅臉因掙扎而發光,抬起嚟,屈服喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地她放棄了,讓雙手落下;她的臉因掙扎而發光,抬起來,屈服了。

passages.original: Tom kissed the red lips and said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆吻咗紅唇,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆吻了紅唇,說:

passages.original: “Now it’s all done, Becky.
passages.vernacular: 「而家都做完喇,貝琪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在都做完了,貝琪。

passages.original: And always after this, you know, you ain’t ever to love anybody but me, and you ain’t ever to marry anybody but me, ever never and forever.
passages.vernacular: 而且從此以後,你知道,你永遠唔能夠愛任何人只愛我,永遠唔能夠嫁任何人只嫁我,永遠永遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且從此以後,你知道,你永遠不能愛任何人只愛我,永遠不能嫁任何人只嫁我,永遠永遠。

passages.original: Will you?”
passages.vernacular: 你願意嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你願意嗎?」

passages.original: “No, I’ll never love anybody but you, Tom, and I’ll never marry anybody but you—and you ain’t to ever marry anybody but me, either.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,我永遠唔會愛任何人只愛你,湯姆,我永遠唔會嫁任何人只嫁你——你都永遠唔能夠娶任何人只娶我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我永遠不會愛任何人只愛你,湯姆,我永遠不會嫁任何人只嫁你——你也永遠不能娶任何人只娶我。」

passages.original: “Certainly.
passages.vernacular: 「當然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。

passages.original: Of course.
passages.vernacular: 當然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然。

passages.original: That’s part of it.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係其中嘅一部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是其中的一部分。

passages.original: And always coming to school or when we’re going home, you’re to walk with me, when there ain’t anybody looking—and you choose me and I choose you at parties, because that’s the way you do when you’re engaged.”
passages.vernacular: 而且總是嚟學校或回家時,你要同我一起走,喺冇人睇嘅時候——而且喺聚會時你選我我選你,因為訂咗婚就係咁樣做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且總是來學校或回家時,你要同我一起走,在沒有人看的時候——而且在聚會時你選我我選你,因為訂了婚就是這樣做的。」

passages.original: “It’s so nice.
passages.vernacular: 「真好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真好。

passages.original: I never heard of it before.”
passages.vernacular: 我以前從冇聽講過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前從沒聽說過。」

passages.original: “Oh, it’s ever so gay!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,好有趣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,非常有趣!

passages.original: Why, me and Amy Lawrence—”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,我同艾米·勞倫斯——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,我和艾米·勞倫斯——」

passages.original: The big eyes told Tom his blunder and he stopped, confused.
passages.vernacular: 大眼睛告訴湯姆佢嘅失誤,佢停住喇,慌亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大眼睛告訴湯姆他的失誤,他停住了,慌亂。

passages.original: “Oh, Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆!

passages.original: Then I ain’t the first you’ve ever been engaged to!”
passages.vernacular: 嗰我唔係你第一個訂婚嘅人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我不是你第一個訂婚的人!」

passages.original: The child began to cry.
passages.vernacular: 細路開始哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子開始哭。

passages.original: Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說:

passages.original: “Oh, don’t cry, Becky, I don’t care for her any more.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別哭,貝琪,我唔再在乎佢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別哭,貝琪,我不再在乎她了。」

passages.original: “Yes, you do, Tom—you know you do.”
passages.vernacular: 「你在乎,湯姆——你知道你在乎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在乎,湯姆——你知道你在乎。」

passages.original: Tom tried to put his arm about her neck, but she pushed him away and turned her face to the wall, and went on crying.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆試圖用手臂摟住佢嘅脖子,但佢把佢推開,把臉轉向牆壁,繼續哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆試圖用手臂摟住她的脖子,但她把他推開,把臉轉向牆壁,繼續哭。

passages.original: Tom tried again, with soothing words in his mouth, and was repulsed again.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆又試咗一次,嘴裡帶住安慰嘅話,又被推開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆又試了一次,嘴裡帶著安慰的話,又被推開。

passages.original: Then his pride was up, and he strode away and went outside.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢嘅自尊心起嚟喇,佢大步走開,走到外面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他的自尊心起來了,他大步走開,走到外面。

passages.original: He stood about, restless and uneasy, for a while, glancing at the door, every now and then, hoping she would repent and come to find him.
passages.vernacular: 佢站咗一會兒,不安而焦躁,不時瞥向門,希望佢後悔,嚟找佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他站了一會兒,不安而焦躁,不時瞥向門,希望她後悔,來找他。

passages.original: But she did not.
passages.vernacular: 但佢冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她沒有。

passages.original: Then he began to feel badly and fear that he was in the wrong.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢開始感到難受,害怕自己錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他開始感到難受,害怕自己錯了。

passages.original: It was a hard struggle with him to make new advances, now, but he nerved himself to it and entered.
passages.vernacular: 而家再主動係好艱難嘅事,但佢鼓起勇氣,進去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在再主動是很艱難的事,但他鼓起勇氣,進去了。

passages.original: She was still standing back there in the corner, sobbing, with her face to the wall.
passages.vernacular: 佢仍然站喺嗰邊角落裡抽泣,臉對住牆壁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她仍然站在那邊角落裡抽泣,臉對著牆壁。

passages.original: Tom’s heart smote him.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅心受到責備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的心受到責備。

passages.original: He went to her and stood a moment, not knowing exactly how to proceed.
passages.vernacular: 佢走到佢嗰度,站咗一會兒,唔知道確切該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走到她那裡,站了一會兒,不知道確切該怎麼辦。

passages.original: Then he said hesitatingly:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢猶豫地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他猶豫地說:

passages.original: “Becky, I—I don’t care for anybody but you.”
passages.vernacular: 「貝琪,我——我不在乎任何人,只在乎你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貝琪,我——我不在乎任何人,只在乎你。」

passages.original: No reply—but sobs.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答——只有抽泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答——只有抽泣。

passages.original: “Becky”—pleadingly.
passages.vernacular: 「貝琪」——懇求地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貝琪」——懇求地。

passages.original: “Becky, won’t you say something?”
passages.vernacular: 「貝琪,你不講句話嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貝琪,你不說句話嗎?」

passages.original: More sobs.
passages.vernacular: 更多嘅抽泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 更多的抽泣。

passages.original: Tom got out his chiefest jewel, a brass knob from the top of an andiron, and passed it around her so that she could see it, and said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆攞出咗佢最主要嘅珠寶,從柴架頂上攞下嘅一個黃銅球,喺佢周圍遞過去,讓佢睇見,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆拿出了他最主要的珠寶,從柴架頂上拿下的一個黃銅球,在她周圍遞過去,讓她看見,說:

passages.original: “Please, Becky, won’t you take it?”
passages.vernacular: 「求你,貝琪,你不收下嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「求你,貝琪,你不收下嗎?」

passages.original: She struck it to the floor.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢打落喺地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把它打落在地。

passages.original: Then Tom marched out of the house and over the hills and far away, to return to school no more that day.
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆昂首走出屋子,翻過山丘,走得遠遠嘅,嗰天唔再回學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆昂首走出屋子,翻過山丘,走得遠遠的,那天不再回學校。

passages.original: Presently Becky began to suspect.
passages.vernacular: 不久貝琪開始懷疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久貝琪開始懷疑。

passages.original: She ran to the door; he was not in sight; she flew around to the play-yard; he was not there.
passages.vernacular: 佢跑到門口;佢不喺視線內;佢飛跑到操場;佢不喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她跑到門口;他不在視線內;她飛跑到操場;他不在那裡。

passages.original: Then she called:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她喊道:

passages.original: “Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆!

passages.original: Come back, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 回嚟,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回來,湯姆!」

passages.original: She listened intently, but there was no answer.
passages.vernacular: 佢專注地聽住,但冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她專注地聽著,但沒有回答。

passages.original: She had no companions but silence and loneliness.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇伴,只有沉默同孤獨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她沒有伴,只有沉默和孤獨。

passages.original: So she sat down to cry again and upbraid herself; and by this time the scholars began to gather again, and she had to hide her griefs and still her broken heart and take up the cross of a long, dreary, aching afternoon, with none among the strangers about her to exchange sorrows with.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢坐下又哭,責備自己;呢陣學生哋又開始聚集,佢唔得不藏起悲傷,安撫破碎嘅心,背起漫長、沉悶、痛苦嘅下午呢個十字架,周圍嘅陌生人當中,冇一個人可以同佢交換悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是她坐下又哭,責備自己;這時學生們又開始聚集,她不得不藏起悲傷,安撫破碎的心,背起漫長、沉悶、痛苦的下午這個十字架,周圍的陌生人當中,沒有一個人可以同她交換悲傷。

chapters.title: Chapter VIII: Tom Decides on his Course 第八章:湯姆決定當海盜

passages.original: CH Tom dodged hither and thither through lanes until he was well out of the track of returning scholars, and then fell into a moody jog.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喺小巷裡東躲西閃,直到遠離返回嘅學生嘅路線,然後陷入悶悶不樂嘅慢跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆在小巷裡東躲西閃,直到遠離返回的學生的路線,然後陷入悶悶不樂的慢跑。
