passages.original: He crossed a small “branch” two or three times, because of a prevailing juvenile superstition that to cross water baffled pursuit.
passages.vernacular: 佢兩三次穿過一條小「支流」,因為流行一種少年迷信,認為過水能使追蹤者摸不住頭腦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他兩三次穿過一條小「支流」,因為流行一種少年迷信,認為過水能使追蹤者摸不著頭腦。

passages.original: Half an hour later he was disappearing behind the Douglas mansion on the summit of Cardiff Hill, and the school-house was hardly distinguishable away off in the valley behind him.
passages.vernacular: 半個小時後,佢消失喺卡迪夫山頂嘅道格拉斯大宅後面,校舍喺佢身後遠處嘅山谷中幾乎睇不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 半個小時後,他消失在卡迪夫山頂的道格拉斯大宅後面,校舍在他身後遠處的山谷中幾乎看不出來。

passages.original: He entered a dense wood, picked his pathless way to the centre of it, and sat down on a mossy spot under a spreading oak.
passages.vernacular: 佢進入一片茂密嘅樹林,摸索住冇路徑走到中心,坐喺一棵枝葉伸展嘅橡樹下一塊長滿苔蘚嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他進入一片茂密的樹林,摸索著沒有路徑走到中心,坐在一棵枝葉伸展的橡樹下一塊長滿苔蘚的地方。

passages.original: There was not even a zephyr stirring; the dead noonday heat had even stilled the songs of the birds; nature lay in a trance that was broken by no sound but the occasional far-off hammering of a wood-pecker, and this seemed to render the pervading silence and sense of loneliness the more profound.
passages.vernacular: 連一絲微風都冇;死寂嘅正午熱氣甚至使鳥聲都靜止喇;大自然處喺一種出神狀態,除咗偶爾遠處啄木鳥嘅敲擊聲,冇別嘅聲音打破,呢似乎使瀰漫嘅寂靜同孤獨感更加深沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連一絲微風也沒有;死寂的正午熱氣甚至使鳥聲也靜止了;大自然處在一種出神狀態,除了偶爾遠處啄木鳥的敲擊聲,沒有別的聲音打破,這似乎使瀰漫的寂靜和孤獨感更加深沉。

passages.original: The boy’s soul was steeped in melancholy; his feelings were in happy accord with his surroundings.
passages.vernacular: 男孩嘅靈魂浸喺憂鬱中;佢嘅感覺同周圍環境愉快地和諧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩的靈魂浸在憂鬱中;他的感覺與周圍環境愉快地和諧。

passages.original: He sat long with his elbows on his knees and his chin in his hands, meditating.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐咗好久,手肘放喺膝蓋上,下巴放喺手裡,沉思住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐了很久,手肘放在膝蓋上,下巴放在手裡,沉思著。

passages.original: It seemed to him that life was but a trouble, at best, and he more than half envied Jimmy Hodges, so lately released; it must be very peaceful, he thought, to lie and slumber and dream forever and ever, with the wind whispering through the trees and caressing the grass and the flowers over the grave, and nothing to bother and grieve about, ever any more.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得生命至多只係一種麻煩,佢有一大半羨慕不久前才解脫嘅吉米·霍奇斯;佢想,永遠永遠地躺住、瞓住、做夢,風喺樹間低語,撫摸墳上嘅草同花,再都冇乜嘢煩惱同悲傷,一定好平靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他覺得生命至多只是一種麻煩,他有一大半羨慕不久前才解脫的吉米·霍奇斯;他想,永遠永遠地躺著、睡著、做夢,風在樹間低語,撫摸墳上的草和花,再也沒有什麼煩惱和悲傷,一定非常平靜。

passages.original: If he only had a clean Sunday-school record he could be willing to go, and be done with it all.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢只有一份乾淨嘅主日學校記錄,佢可以願意走,結束呢一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他只有一份乾淨的主日學校記錄,他可以願意走,結束這一切。

passages.original: Now as to this girl.
passages.vernacular: 而家講到呢個女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在說到這個女孩。

passages.original: What had he done?
passages.vernacular: 佢做咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他做了什麼?

passages.original: Nothing.
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼也沒有。

passages.original: He had meant the best in the world, and been treated like a dog—like a very dog.
passages.vernacular: 佢懷住世界上最好嘅意思,卻被當狗對待——簡直係狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他懷著世界上最好的意思,卻被當狗對待——簡直是狗。

passages.original: She would be sorry some day—maybe when it was too late.
passages.vernacular: 有一天佢會後悔——或者太遲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天她會後悔——也許太遲了。

passages.original: Ah, if he could only die temporarily!
passages.vernacular: 啊,要係佢能暫時死去就好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,要是他能暫時死去就好了!

passages.original: But the elastic heart of youth cannot be compressed into one constrained shape long at a time.
passages.vernacular: 但青春有彈性嘅心唔能夠長時間壓縮成一個受限制嘅形狀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但青春有彈性的心不能長時間壓縮成一個受限制的形狀。

passages.original: Tom presently began to drift insensibly back into the concerns of this life again.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆不久開始唔知不覺地漂回呢一生嘅牽掛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆不久開始不知不覺地漂回這一生的牽掛。

passages.original: What if he turned his back, now, and disappeared mysteriously?
passages.vernacular: 如果佢而家轉身,神祕地消失呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他現在轉身,神祕地消失呢?

passages.original: What if he went away—ever so far away, into unknown countries beyond the seas—and never came back any more!
passages.vernacular: 如果佢離開——遠遠地,去海外未知嘅國家——再都不回嚟呢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他離開——遠遠地,去海外未知的國家——再也不回來呢!

passages.original: How would she feel then!
passages.vernacular: 嗰時佢會有乜嘢感覺!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時她會有什麼感覺!

passages.original: The idea of being a clown recurred to him now, only to fill him with disgust.
passages.vernacular: 當小丑嘅想法而家又回嚟喇,只係讓佢充滿厭惡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當小丑的想法現在又回來了,只是讓他充滿厭惡。

passages.original: For frivolity and jokes and spotted tights were an offense, when they intruded themselves upon a spirit that was exalted into the vague august realm of the romantic.
passages.vernacular: 因為輕浮、笑話同斑點緊身衣,當佢哋闖入一個被提升到浪漫嘅模糊崇高領域嘅精神時,係一種冒犯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為輕浮、笑話和斑點緊身衣,當它們闖入一個被提升到浪漫的模糊崇高領域的精神時,是一種冒犯。

passages.original: No, he would be a soldier, and return after long years, all war-worn and illustrious.
passages.vernacular: 不,佢要當士兵,多年後歸嚟,戰績累累、聲名顯赫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,他要當士兵,多年後歸來,戰績累累、聲名顯赫。

passages.original: No—better still, he would join the Indians, and hunt buffaloes and go on the warpath in the mountain ranges and the trackless great plains of the Far West, and away in the future come back a great chief, bristling with feathers, hideous with paint, and prance into Sunday-school, some drowsy summer morning, with a blood-curdling war-whoop, and sear the eyeballs of all his companions with unappeasable envy.
passages.vernacular: 不——更好,佢要加入印第安人,獵水牛,喺遠西嘅山脈同無路嘅大平原上走上戰爭路,並喺遙遠嘅未來回嚟做一位大酋長,滿身羽毛,塗住可怕嘅油彩,喺某個昏昏欲瞓嘅夏日早晨跳進主日學校,發出令人毛骨悚然嘅戰吼,以無法平息嘅嫉妒灼傷所有同伴嘅眼球。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不——更好,他要加入印第安人,獵水牛,在遠西的山脈和無路的大平原上走上戰爭路,並在遙遠的未來回來做一位大酋長,滿身羽毛,塗著可怕的油彩,在某個昏昏欲睡的夏日早晨跳進主日學校,發出令人毛骨悚然的戰吼,以無法平息的嫉妒灼傷所有同伴的眼球。

passages.original: But no, there was something gaudier even than this.
passages.vernacular: 但不,仲有比呢更華麗嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不,還有比這更華麗的。

passages.original: He would be a pirate!
passages.vernacular: 佢要當海盜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要當海盜!

passages.original: That was it! now his future lay plain before him, and glowing with unimaginable splendor.
passages.vernacular: 就係呢個!而家佢嘅未來清楚地展而家佢面前,閃耀住難以想像嘅輝煌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這個!現在他的未來清楚地展現在他面前,閃耀著難以想像的輝煌。

passages.original: How his name would fill the world, and make people shudder!
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅名字將如何充滿世界,令人戰慄!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的名字將如何充滿世界,令人戰慄!

passages.original: How gloriously he would go plowing the dancing seas, in his long, low, black-hulled racer, the Spirit of the Storm, with his grisly flag flying at the fore!
passages.vernacular: 佢將幾咁光榮地駕住佢長長嘅、低矮嘅、黑色船身嘅快船「風暴之魂」,犁過舞動嘅海洋,佢可怕嘅旗幟喺前桅飄揚!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他將多麼光榮地駕著他長長的、低矮的、黑色船身的快船「風暴之魂」,犁過舞動的海洋,他可怕的旗幟在前桅飄揚!

passages.original: And at the zenith of his fame, how he would suddenly appear at the old village and stalk into church, brown and weather-beaten, in his black velvet doublet and trunks, his great jack-boots, his crimson sash, his belt bristling with horse-pistols, his crime-rusted cutlass at his side, his slouch hat with waving plumes, his black flag unfurled, with the skull and crossbones on it, and hear with swelling ecstasy the whisperings, “It’s Tom Sawyer the Pirate!—the Black Avenger of the Spanish Main!”
passages.vernacular: 而喺佢名聲嘅頂峰,佢將如何突然出而家老村莊,大步走進教堂,黝黑、飽經風霜,穿住佢嘅黑天鵝絨緊身上衣同短褲,佢嘅大馬靴,佢嘅深紅色腰帶,佢嘅皮帶上插滿馬槍,佢嘅腰側掛住染滿罪惡鏽跡嘅短彎刀,佢嘅寬邊帽上羽毛飄揚,佢嘅黑旗展開,上面有骷髏同交叉骨頭,並帶住膨脹嘅狂喜聽到竊竊私語:「係海盜湯姆·索亞!——西班牙海嘅黑色復仇者!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而在他名聲的頂峰,他將如何突然出現在老村莊,大步走進教堂,黝黑、飽經風霜,穿著他的黑天鵝絨緊身上衣和短褲,他的大馬靴,他的深紅色腰帶,他的皮帶上插滿馬槍,他的腰側掛著染滿罪惡鏽跡的短彎刀,他的寬邊帽上羽毛飄揚,他的黑旗展開,上面有骷髏和交叉骨頭,並帶著膨脹的狂喜聽到竊竊私語:「是海盜湯姆·索亞!——西班牙海的黑色復仇者!」

passages.original: Yes, it was settled; his career was determined.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,決定喇;佢嘅職業確定喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,決定了;他的職業確定了。

passages.original: He would run away from home and enter upon it.
passages.vernacular: 佢要離家出走,開始呢個職業。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要離家出走,開始這個職業。

passages.original: He would start the very next morning.
passages.vernacular: 佢聽日一早就出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他明天一早就出發。

passages.original: Therefore he must now begin to get ready.
passages.vernacular: 因此佢而家必須開始準備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此他現在必須開始準備。

passages.original: He would collect his resources together.
passages.vernacular: 佢要把佢嘅資源集中起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要把他的資源集中起來。

passages.original: He went to a rotten log near at hand and began to dig under one end of it with his Barlow knife.
passages.vernacular: 佢走到附近一根腐爛嘅原木旁,開始用佢嘅巴洛刀喺佢一端下面挖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走到附近一根腐爛的原木旁,開始用他的巴洛刀在它一端下面挖。

passages.original: He soon struck wood that sounded hollow.
passages.vernacular: 佢好快碰到咗聽起嚟係空心嘅木頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很快碰到了聽起來是空心的木頭。

passages.original: He put his hand there and uttered this incantation impressively:
passages.vernacular: 佢把手放喺嗰度,莊嚴地唸咗呢段咒語:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把手放在那裡,莊嚴地唸了這段咒語:

passages.original: “What hasn’t come here, come!
passages.vernacular: 「冇嚟嘅,嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒來的,來!

passages.original: What’s here, stay here!”
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度嘅,留喺呢度!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡的,留在這裡!」

passages.original: Then he scraped away the dirt, and exposed a pine shingle.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢刮掉泥土,露出一塊松木薄板。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他刮掉泥土,露出一塊松木薄板。

passages.original: He took it up and disclosed a shapely little treasure-house whose bottom and sides were of shingles.
passages.vernacular: 佢攞起佢,露出一個形狀勻稱嘅小寶庫,底部同側面都係薄木片。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拿起它,露出一個形狀勻稱的小寶庫,底部和側面都是薄木片。

passages.original: In it lay a marble.
passages.vernacular: 裡面躺住一顆彈珠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 裡面躺著一顆彈珠。

passages.original: Tom’s astonishment was boundless!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅驚訝係無邊嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的驚訝是無邊的!

passages.original: He scratched his head with a perplexed air, and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢困惑地撓住頭,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他困惑地撓著頭,說:

passages.original: “Well, that beats anything!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢比乜嘢都奇怪!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這比什麼都奇怪!」

passages.original: Then he tossed the marble away pettishly, and stood cogitating.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢氣惱地把彈珠扔掉,站住思考。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他氣惱地把彈珠扔掉,站著思考。

passages.original: The truth was, that a superstition of his had failed, here, which he and all his comrades had always looked upon as infallible.
passages.vernacular: 事實係,佢嘅一種迷信喺呢度失敗喇,佢同所有嘅同伴一直把佢睇作絕對可靠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實是,他的一種迷信在這裡失敗了,他和所有的同伴一直把它看作絕對可靠。

passages.original: If you buried a marble with certain necessary incantations, and left it alone a fortnight, and then opened the place with the incantation he had just used, you would find that all the marbles you had ever lost had gathered themselves together there, meantime, no matter how widely they had been separated.
passages.vernacular: 如果你用某些必要嘅咒語埋一顆彈珠,放住兩個星期,然後用佢頭先用嘅咒語打開嗰個地方,你會發現你以前丟失嘅所有彈珠,不管佢哋分開得多遠,同時都聚集到嗰度喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你用某些必要的咒語埋一顆彈珠,放著兩個星期,然後用他剛才用的咒語打開那個地方,你會發現你以前丟失的所有彈珠,不管它們分開得多遠,同時都聚集到那裡了。

passages.original: But now, this thing had actually and unquestionably failed.
passages.vernacular: 但而家,呢件事確實無疑地失敗喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在,這件事確實無疑地失敗了。

passages.original: Tom’s whole structure of faith was shaken to its foundations.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆整個信仰嘅結構被震動到根基。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆整個信仰的結構被震動到根基。

passages.original: He had many a time heard of this thing succeeding but never of its failing before.
passages.vernacular: 佢多次聽講呢件事成功,但以前從冇聽講過失敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他多次聽說這件事成功,但以前從沒聽說過失敗。

passages.original: It did not occur to him that he had tried it several times before, himself, but could never find the hiding-places afterward.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇想到佢自己以前試過幾次,但事後從未能找到藏匿處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有想到他自己以前試過幾次,但事後從未能找到藏匿處。

passages.original: He puzzled over the matter some time, and finally decided that some witch had interfered and broken the charm.
passages.vernacular: 佢為此困惑咗啲時間,最後斷定係某個女巫干擾,破壞咗咒語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他為此困惑了一些時間,最後斷定是某個女巫干擾,破壞了咒語。

passages.original: He thought he would satisfy himself on that point; so he searched around till he found a small sandy spot with a little funnel-shaped depression in it.
passages.vernacular: 佢想就呢啲讓自己滿意;於是佢四處搜尋,直到找到一小塊沙地,上面有一個小漏斗形嘅凹陷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想就這一點讓自己滿意;於是他四處搜尋,直到找到一小塊沙地,上面有一個小漏斗形的凹陷。

passages.original: He laid himself down and put his mouth close to this depression and called—
passages.vernacular: 佢躺下,把嘴貼近呢個凹陷,喊道——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他躺下,把嘴貼近這個凹陷,喊道——

passages.original: “Doodle-bug, doodle-bug, tell me what I want to know!
passages.vernacular: 「蟻獅,蟻獅,告訴我我想知道嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蟻獅,蟻獅,告訴我我想知道的!

passages.original: Doodle-bug, doodle-bug, tell me what I want to know!”
passages.vernacular: 蟻獅,蟻獅,告訴我我想知道嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蟻獅,蟻獅,告訴我我想知道的!」

passages.original: The sand began to work, and presently a small black bug appeared for a second and then darted under again in a fright.
passages.vernacular: 沙子開始動,不久一隻小黑蟲出現咗一秒,然後驚恐地又鑽下去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沙子開始動,不久一隻小黑蟲出現了一秒,然後驚恐地又鑽下去了。

passages.original: “He dasn’t tell!
passages.vernacular: 「佢唔敢講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它不敢說!

passages.original: So it was a witch that done it.
passages.vernacular: 所以係女巫幹嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以是女巫幹的。

passages.original: I just knowed it.”
passages.vernacular: 我就知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就知道。」

passages.original: He well knew the futility of trying to contend against witches, so he gave up discouraged.
passages.vernacular: 佢好清楚同女巫對抗嘅徒勞,所以沮喪地放棄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很清楚同女巫對抗的徒勞,所以沮喪地放棄了。

passages.original: But it occurred to him that he might as well have the marble he had just thrown away, and therefore he went and made a patient search for it.
passages.vernacular: 但佢想到,佢不妨攞回頭先扔掉嘅彈珠,於是佢去耐心地尋找佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他想到,他不妨拿回剛才扔掉的彈珠,於是他去耐心地尋找它。

passages.original: But he could not find it.
passages.vernacular: 但佢找唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他找不到。

passages.original: Now he went back to his treasure-house and carefully placed himself just as he had been standing when he tossed the marble away; then he took another marble from his pocket and tossed it in the same way, saying:
passages.vernacular: 而家佢回到佢嘅寶庫,小心地站喺佢扔彈珠時站嘅位置;然後佢從口袋裡又攞出一顆彈珠,以同樣嘅方式扔,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他回到他的寶庫,小心地站在他扔彈珠時站的位置;然後他從口袋裡又拿出一顆彈珠,以同樣的方式扔,說:

passages.original: “Brother, go find your brother!”
passages.vernacular: 「兄弟,去找你嘅兄弟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「兄弟,去找你的兄弟!」

passages.original: He watched where it stopped, and went there and looked.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇住佢停喺邊度,走到嗰度睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看著它停在哪裡,走到那裡看。

passages.original: But it must have fallen short or gone too far; so he tried twice more.
passages.vernacular: 但佢一定係落短咗或飛得太遠;所以佢又試咗兩次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它一定是落短了或飛得太遠;所以他又試了兩次。

passages.original: The last repetition was successful.
passages.vernacular: 最後一次重複成功喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後一次重複成功了。

passages.original: The two marbles lay within a foot of each other.
passages.vernacular: 兩顆彈珠躺喺一呎以內。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩顆彈珠躺在一呎以內。

passages.original: Just here the blast of a toy tin trumpet came faintly down the green aisles of the forest.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,玩具錫喇叭嘅聲音微弱地從森林嘅綠色走道傳嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,玩具錫喇叭的聲音微弱地從森林的綠色走道傳來。

passages.original: Tom flung off his jacket and trousers, turned a suspender into a belt, raked away some brush behind the rotten log, disclosing a rude bow and arrow, a lath sword and a tin trumpet, and in a moment had seized these things and bounded away, barelegged, with fluttering shirt.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆甩掉外套同褲子,把一根吊褲帶變成腰帶,扒開腐爛原木後面嘅啲灌木叢,露出一把簡陋嘅弓同箭、一把板條劍同一個錫喇叭,轉眼佢抓起呢啲嘢,光住腿、襯衫飄動住蹦跳住走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆甩掉外套和褲子,把一根吊褲帶變成腰帶,扒開腐爛原木後面的一些灌木叢,露出一把簡陋的弓和箭、一把板條劍和一個錫喇叭,轉眼他抓起這些東西,光著腿、襯衫飄動著蹦跳著走了。

passages.original: He presently halted under a great elm, blew an answering blast, and then began to tiptoe and look warily out, this way and that.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢喺一棵大榆樹下停住,吹咗個回應嘅喇叭,然後開始踮住腳,警惕地向呢邊嗰邊張望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他在一棵大榆樹下停住,吹了個回應的喇叭,然後開始踮著腳,警惕地向這邊那邊張望。

passages.original: He said cautiously—to an imaginary company:
passages.vernacular: 佢謹慎地講——對一個想像出嚟嘅隊伍:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他謹慎地說——對一個想像出來的隊伍:

passages.original: “Hold, my merry men!
passages.vernacular: 「站住,我嘅快樂弟兄哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「站住,我的快樂弟兄們!

passages.original: Keep hid till I blow.”
passages.vernacular: 喺我吹號前保持隱蔽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我吹號前保持隱蔽。」

passages.original: Now appeared Joe Harper, as airily clad and elaborately armed as Tom.
passages.vernacular: 而家喬·哈珀出現喇,穿得像湯姆一樣輕便,武裝得像湯姆一樣精細。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在喬·哈珀出現了,穿得像湯姆一樣輕便,武裝得像湯姆一樣精細。

passages.original: Tom called:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆喊道:

passages.original: “Hold!
passages.vernacular: 「站住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「站住!

passages.original: Who comes here into Sherwood Forest without my pass?”
passages.vernacular: 邊個冇我嘅通行證就進入舍伍德森林?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰沒有我的通行證就進入舍伍德森林?」

passages.original: “Guy of Guisborne wants no man’s pass.
passages.vernacular: 「吉斯伯恩嘅蓋伊不需要任何人嘅通行證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉斯伯恩的蓋伊不需要任何人的通行證。

passages.original: Who art thou that—that—”
passages.vernacular: 你係邊個,竟敢——竟敢——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是誰,竟敢——竟敢——」

passages.original: “Dares to hold such language,” said Tom, prompting—for they talked “by the book,” from memory.
passages.vernacular: 「講咁樣嘅話,」湯姆提示講——因為佢哋「照書」講話,憑記憶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說這樣的話,」湯姆提示說——因為他們「照書」說話,憑記憶。

passages.original: “Who art thou that dares to hold such language?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個,竟敢講咁樣嘅話?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰,竟敢說這樣的話?」

passages.original: “I, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「我,真嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我,真的!

passages.original: I am Robin Hood, as thy caitiff carcase soon shall know.”
passages.vernacular: 我係羅賓漢,你呢卑鄙嘅身軀好快就會知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是羅賓漢,你這卑鄙的身軀很快就會知道。」

passages.original: “Then art thou indeed that famous outlaw?
passages.vernacular: 「咁你真係嗰著名嘅亡命之徒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼你真是那著名的亡命之徒?

passages.original: Right gladly will I dispute with thee the passes of the merry wood.
passages.vernacular: 我好樂意同你爭奪呢快樂樹林嘅通道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很樂意同你爭奪這快樂樹林的通道。

passages.original: Have at thee!”
passages.vernacular: 睇劍!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看劍!」

passages.original: They took their lath swords, dumped their other traps on the ground, struck a fencing attitude, foot to foot, and began a grave, careful combat, “two up and two down.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋攞起板條劍,把其他裝備扔喺地上,擺出擊劍姿勢,腳對腳,開始一場嚴肅、小心嘅戰鬥,「兩上兩下」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們拿起板條劍,把其他裝備扔在地上,擺出擊劍姿勢,腳對腳,開始一場嚴肅、小心的戰鬥,「兩上兩下」。

passages.original: Presently Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 不久湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久湯姆說:

passages.original: “Now, if you’ve got the hang, go it lively!”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,如果你掌握咗竅門,就快點打!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,如果你掌握了竅門,就快點打!」

passages.original: So they “went it lively,” panting and perspiring with the work.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋「快點打」,為呢活動喘氣流汗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們「快點打」,為這活動喘氣流汗。

passages.original: By and by Tom shouted:
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地湯姆喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地湯姆喊道:

passages.original: “Fall! fall!
passages.vernacular: 「倒下!倒下!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「倒下!倒下!

passages.original: Why don’t you fall?”
passages.vernacular: 你點解不倒下?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼不倒下?」

passages.original: “I sha’n’t!
passages.vernacular: 「我不!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不!

passages.original: Why don’t you fall yourself?
passages.vernacular: 你點解不自己倒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼不自己倒?

passages.original: You’re getting the worst of it.”
passages.vernacular: 你佔下風喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你佔下風了。」

passages.original: “Why, that ain’t anything.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,嗰不算乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,那不算什麼。

passages.original: I can’t fall; that ain’t the way it is in the book.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠倒下;書上唔係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能倒下;書上不是這樣。

passages.original: The book says, ‘Then with one back-handed stroke he slew poor Guy of Guisborne.’
passages.vernacular: 書上講:『然後佢反手一擊,殺死咗可憐嘅吉斯伯恩嘅蓋伊。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 書上說:『然後他反手一擊,殺死了可憐的吉斯伯恩的蓋伊。』

passages.original: You’re to turn around and let me hit you in the back.”
passages.vernacular: 你要轉身讓我打你嘅背。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要轉身讓我打你的背。」

passages.original: There was no getting around the authorities, so Joe turned, received the whack and fell.
passages.vernacular: 冇辦法繞過權威,喬轉身,挨咗一擊,倒下喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有辦法繞過權威,喬轉身,挨了一擊,倒下了。

passages.original: “Now,” said Joe, getting up, “you got to let me kill you.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,」喬站起來講,「你得讓我殺你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,」喬站起來說,「你得讓我殺你。

passages.original: That’s fair.”
passages.vernacular: 呢才公平。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這才公平。」

passages.original: “Why, I can’t do that, it ain’t in the book.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我唔能夠嗰樣,書上冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我不能那樣,書上沒有。」

passages.original: “Well, it’s blamed mean—that’s all.”
passages.vernacular: 「哼,呢太卑鄙喇——就咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼,這太卑鄙了——就這樣。」

passages.original: “Well, say, Joe, you can be Friar Tuck or Much the miller’s son, and lam me with a quarter-staff; or I’ll be the Sheriff of Nottingham and you be Robin Hood a little while and kill me.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,喂,喬,你可以當塔克修士或磨坊主嘅兒子馬奇,用棍棒揍我;或者我當諾丁漢郡長,你當一會兒羅賓漢殺我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,喂,喬,你可以當塔克修士或磨坊主的兒子馬奇,用棍棒揍我;或者我當諾丁漢郡長,你當一會兒羅賓漢殺我。」

passages.original: This was satisfactory, and so these adventures were carried out.
passages.vernacular: 呢令人滿意,於是呢啲冒險都演咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這令人滿意,於是這些冒險都演了出來。

passages.original: Then Tom became Robin Hood again, and was allowed by the treacherous nun to bleed his strength away through his neglected wound.
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆又成咗羅賓漢,被背信嘅修女允許讓佢嘅力量從被忽視嘅傷口中流失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆又成了羅賓漢,被背信的修女允許讓他的力量從被忽視的傷口中流失。

passages.original: And at last Joe, representing a whole tribe of weeping outlaws, dragged him sadly forth, gave his bow into his feeble hands, and Tom said, “Where this arrow falls, there bury poor Robin Hood under the greenwood tree.”
passages.vernacular: 最後喬代表整個哭泣嘅亡命之徒部落,悲傷地把佢拖出嚟,把佢嘅弓交到佢虛弱嘅手裡,湯姆講:「呢支箭落喺邊度,就把可憐嘅羅賓漢埋喺邊度嘅綠林樹下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後喬代表整個哭泣的亡命之徒部落,悲傷地把他拖出來,把他的弓交到他虛弱的手裡,湯姆說:「這支箭落在哪裡,就把可憐的羅賓漢埋在哪裡的綠林樹下。」

passages.original: Then he shot the arrow and fell back and would have died, but he lit on a nettle and sprang up too gaily for a corpse.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢射咗箭,向後倒下,本來就要死喇,但佢落喺一叢蕁麻上,跳起嚟對屍體來講太快活喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他射了箭,向後倒下,本來就要死了,但他落在一叢蕁麻上,跳起來對屍體來說太快活了。

passages.original: The boys dressed themselves, hid their accoutrements, and went off grieving that there were no outlaws any more, and wondering what modern civilization could claim to have done to compensate for their loss.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋穿好衣服,藏起裝備,悲傷地離開,因為再都冇亡命之徒喇,並納悶現代文明能宣稱做咗乜嘢嚟彌補佢哋嘅損失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們穿好衣服,藏起裝備,悲傷地離開,因為再也沒有亡命之徒了,並納悶現代文明能宣稱做了什麼來彌補他們的損失。

passages.original: They said they would rather be outlaws a year in Sherwood Forest than President of the United States forever.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋講,佢哋寧願喺舍伍德森林當一年亡命之徒,都唔願永遠當美國總統。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們說,他們寧願在舍伍德森林當一年亡命之徒,也不願永遠當美國總統。

chapters.title: Chapter IX: A Solemn Situation 第九章:墓地的一夜

passages.original: CH At half-past nine, that night, Tom and Sid were sent to bed, as usual.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上九點半,湯姆同希德像往常一樣被打發上床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上九點半,湯姆和希德像往常一樣被打發上床。

passages.original: They said their prayers, and Sid was soon asleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋做咗禱告,希德好快瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們做了禱告,希德很快睡著了。

passages.original: Tom lay awake and waited, in restless impatience.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆醒住躺住等待,焦躁不耐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆醒著躺著等待,焦躁不耐。

passages.original: When it seemed to him that it must be nearly daylight, he heard the clock strike ten!
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得好像一定快天亮喇,卻聽到鐘敲十點!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他覺得好像一定快天亮了,卻聽到鐘敲十點!

passages.original: This was despair.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係絕望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是絕望。

passages.original: He would have tossed and fidgeted, as his nerves demanded, but he was afraid he might wake Sid.
passages.vernacular: 佢本想翻嚟覆去、坐立不安,正如佢嘅神經所要求嘅,但佢怕會吵醒希德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他本想翻來覆去、坐立不安,正如他的神經所要求的,但他怕會吵醒希德。

passages.original: So he lay still, and stared up into the dark.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢靜靜躺住,瞪住黑暗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他靜靜躺著,瞪著黑暗。

passages.original: Everything was dismally still.
passages.vernacular: 一切都淒涼地寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切都淒涼地寂靜。

passages.original: By and by, out of the stillness, little, scarcely perceptible noises began to emphasize themselves.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地,從寂靜中,啲細小嘅、幾乎察覺唔到嘅聲音開始突顯出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地,從寂靜中,一些細小的、幾乎察覺不到的聲音開始突顯出來。

passages.original: The ticking of the clock began to bring itself into notice.
passages.vernacular: 鐘嘅滴答聲開始引起注意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鐘的滴答聲開始引起注意。

passages.original: Old beams began to crack mysteriously.
passages.vernacular: 老屋樑開始神祕地噼啪作響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老屋樑開始神祕地噼啪作響。

passages.original: The stairs creaked faintly.
passages.vernacular: 樓梯微弱地吱嘎響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樓梯微弱地吱嘎響。

passages.original: Evidently spirits were abroad.
passages.vernacular: 顯然鬼魂出動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顯然鬼魂出動了。

passages.original: A measured, muffled snore issued from Aunt Polly’s chamber.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽房間傳嚟有節奏嘅、被悶住嘅鼾聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽房間傳來有節奏的、被悶住的鼾聲。

passages.original: And now the tiresome chirping of a cricket that no human ingenuity could locate, began.
passages.vernacular: 而家開始咗一隻蟋蟀惱人嘅唧唧聲,冇人類嘅聰明才智能找到佢嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在開始了一隻蟋蟀惱人的唧唧聲,沒有人類的聰明才智能找到它的位置。

passages.original: Next the ghastly ticking of a death-watch in the wall at the bed’s head made Tom shudder—it meant that somebody’s days were numbered.
passages.vernacular: 接住床頭牆壁裡報死蟲可怕嘅滴答聲使湯姆發抖——呢意味住某人嘅日子有限喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著床頭牆壁裡報死蟲可怕的滴答聲使湯姆發抖——這意味著某人的日子有限了。

passages.original: Then the howl of a far-off dog rose on the night air, and was answered by a fainter howl from a remoter distance.
passages.vernacular: 然後遠處一隻狗嘅嚎叫喺夜空中升起,從更遠嘅地方傳嚟更微弱嘅嚎叫回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後遠處一隻狗的嚎叫在夜空中升起,從更遠的地方傳來更微弱的嚎叫回答。

passages.original: Tom was in an agony.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆痛苦萬分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆痛苦萬分。

passages.original: At last he was satisfied that time had ceased and eternity begun; he began to doze, in spite of himself; the clock chimed eleven, but he did not hear it.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢確信時間已停止,永恆已開始;佢不由自主地開始打盹;鐘敲咗十啲,但佢冇聽到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他確信時間已停止,永恆已開始;他不由自主地開始打盹;鐘敲了十一點,但他沒聽到。

passages.original: And then there came, mingling with his half-formed dreams, a most melancholy caterwauling.
passages.vernacular: 然後傳嚟,同佢半成形嘅夢混合喺一起,最憂傷嘅貓叫春。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後傳來,與他半成形的夢混合在一起,最憂傷的貓叫春。

passages.original: The raising of a neighboring window disturbed him.
passages.vernacular: 鄰居一扇窗子被抬起嘅聲音驚擾咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鄰居一扇窗子被抬起的聲音驚擾了他。

passages.original: A cry of “Scat! you devil!” and the crash of an empty bottle against the back of his aunt’s woodshed brought him wide awake, and a single minute later he was dressed and out of the window and creeping along the roof of the “ell” on all fours.
passages.vernacular: 一聲「噓!你呢魔鬼!」嘅喊叫同一個空瓶子砸喺佢姨媽柴棚背面嘅碎裂聲使佢完全清醒,一分鐘後,佢穿好衣服,出咗窗子,四肢住地沿住「側屋」嘅屋頂爬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一聲「噓!你這魔鬼!」的喊叫和一個空瓶子砸在他姨媽柴棚背面的碎裂聲使他完全清醒,一分鐘後,他穿好衣服,出了窗子,四肢著地沿著「側屋」的屋頂爬。

passages.original: He “meow’d” with caution once or twice, as he went; then jumped to the roof of the woodshed and thence to the ground.
passages.vernacular: 佢一路謹慎地「喵」咗一兩聲;然後跳到柴棚頂,從嗰度跳到地面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一路謹慎地「喵」了一兩聲;然後跳到柴棚頂,從那裡跳到地面。

passages.original: Huckleberry Finn was there, with his dead cat.
passages.vernacular: 哈克貝利·費恩喺嗰度,帶住佢嘅死貓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克貝利·費恩在那裡,帶著他的死貓。

passages.original: The boys moved off and disappeared in the gloom.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋走開,消失喺昏暗中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們走開,消失在昏暗中。

passages.original: At the end of half an hour they were wading through the tall grass of the graveyard.
passages.vernacular: 半個鐘頭後,佢哋正涉過墳場嘅高草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 半個鐘頭後,他們正涉過墳場的高草。

passages.original: It was a graveyard of the old-fashioned Western kind.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一個西部老式嘅墳場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一個西部老式的墳場。

passages.original: It was on a hill, about a mile and a half from the village.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺一座山上,離村子約一英里半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它在一座山上,離村子約一英里半。

passages.original: It had a crazy board fence around it, which leaned inward in places, and outward the rest of the time, but stood upright nowhere.
passages.vernacular: 周圍有一道搖搖欲墜嘅木板圍欄,有些地方向內傾斜,其餘時間向外傾斜,但邊度都不直立。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 周圍有一道搖搖欲墜的木板圍欄,有些地方向內傾斜,其餘時間向外傾斜,但哪裡也不直立。

passages.original: Grass and weeds grew rank over the whole cemetery.
passages.vernacular: 草同雜草喺整個墓地茂盛生長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 草和雜草在整個墓地茂盛生長。

passages.original: All the old graves were sunken in, there was not a tombstone on the place; round-topped, worm-eaten boards staggered over the graves, leaning for support and finding none.
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅老墳都下陷喇,地方上冇一塊墓碑;圓頂嘅、被蟲蛀嘅木板喺墳上搖搖晃晃,靠住要支撐卻找唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的老墳都下陷了,地方上沒有一塊墓碑;圓頂的、被蟲蛀的木板在墳上搖搖晃晃,靠著要支撐卻找不到。

passages.original: “Sacred to the memory of” So-and-So had been painted on them once, but it could no longer have been read, on the most of them, now, even if there had been light.
passages.vernacular: 「紀念某某神聖之記」曾經漆喺上面,但即使有光,而家大部分都已經讀不出嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「紀念某某神聖之記」曾經漆在上面,但即使有光,現在大部分也已經讀不出來了。

passages.original: A faint wind moaned through the trees, and Tom feared it might be the spirits of the dead, complaining at being disturbed.
passages.vernacular: 一陣微風喺樹間呻吟,湯姆擔心嗰可能係死人嘅靈魂,抱怨被打擾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣微風在樹間呻吟,湯姆擔心那可能是死人的靈魂,抱怨被打擾。

passages.original: The boys talked little, and only under their breath, for the time and the place and the pervading solemnity and silence oppressed their spirits.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋好少講話,都只係壓低聲音,因為時間、地點同瀰漫嘅莊嚴同寂靜壓抑住佢哋嘅精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們很少說話,也只是壓低聲音,因為時間、地點和瀰漫的莊嚴與寂靜壓抑著他們的精神。

passages.original: They found the sharp new heap they were seeking, and ensconced themselves within the protection of three great elms that grew in a bunch within a few feet of the grave.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋找到咗佢哋尋找嘅新堆起嘅尖尖土堆,藏喺三棵長喺一起嘅大榆樹嘅保護之下,離墳只有幾呎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們找到了他們尋找的新堆起的尖尖土堆,藏在三棵長在一起的大榆樹的保護之下,離墳只有幾呎。

passages.original: Then they waited in silence for what seemed a long time.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋喺沉默中等待,似乎好長一段時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們在沉默中等待,似乎很長一段時間。

passages.original: The hooting of a distant owl was all the sound that troubled the dead stillness.
passages.vernacular: 遠處貓頭鷹嘅叫聲係唯一擾亂死寂嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠處貓頭鷹的叫聲是唯一擾亂死寂的聲音。

passages.original: Tom’s reflections grew oppressive.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅思緒越嚟越壓抑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的思緒越來越壓抑。

passages.original: He must force some talk.
passages.vernacular: 佢必須強迫講點話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他必須強迫說點話。

passages.original: So he said in a whisper:
passages.vernacular: 所以佢低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他低聲說:

passages.original: “Hucky, do you believe the dead people like it for us to be here?”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,你相信死人鍾意我哋喺呢度嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,你相信死人喜歡我們在這裡嗎?」

passages.original: Huckleberry whispered:
passages.vernacular: 哈克貝利低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克貝利低聲說:

passages.original: “I wisht I knowed.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望我知道。

passages.original: It’s awful solemn like, ain’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 呢種莊嚴得可怕,唔係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種莊嚴得可怕,不是嗎?」

passages.original: “I bet it is.”
passages.vernacular: 「我打賭係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我打賭是。」

passages.original: There was a considerable pause, while the boys canvassed this matter inwardly.
passages.vernacular: 有一段相當長嘅停頓,男孩哋在內心考慮呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一段相當長的停頓,男孩們在內心考慮這件事。

passages.original: Then Tom whispered:
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆低聲說:

passages.original: “Say, Hucky—do you reckon Hoss Williams hears us talking?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,哈克——你想霍斯·威廉斯聽得到我哋講話嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,哈克——你想霍斯·威廉斯聽得到我們說話嗎?」

passages.original: “O’ course he does.
passages.vernacular: 「當然聽得到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然聽得到。

passages.original: Least his sperrit does.”
passages.vernacular: 至少佢嘅靈魂聽得到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少他的靈魂聽得到。」

passages.original: Tom, after a pause:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆停頓後:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆停頓後:

passages.original: “I wish I’d said Mister Williams.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望我頭先講嘅係威廉斯先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望我剛才說的是威廉斯先生。

passages.original: But I never meant any harm.
passages.vernacular: 但我冇惡意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我沒有惡意。

passages.original: Everybody calls him Hoss.”
passages.vernacular: 大家都叫佢霍斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大家都叫他霍斯。」

passages.original: “A body can’t be too partic’lar how they talk ’bout these-yer dead people, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「談論呢啲死人時,點講話都唔能夠太小心,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「談論這些死人時,怎麼說話都不能太小心,湯姆。」

passages.original: This was a damper, and conversation died again.
passages.vernacular: 呢潑咗冷水,談話又死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這潑了冷水,談話又死了。

passages.original: Presently Tom seized his comrade’s arm and said:
passages.vernacular: 不久湯姆抓住同伴嘅手臂講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久湯姆抓住同伴的手臂說:

passages.original: “Sh!”
“What is it, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 「點喇,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了,湯姆?」

passages.original: And the two clung together with beating hearts.
passages.vernacular: 兩人緊緊靠喺一起,心怦怦地跳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩人緊緊靠在一起,心怦怦地跳。

passages.original: “Sh!
There ’tis again!
passages.vernacular: 又嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又來了!

passages.original: Didn’t you hear it?”
passages.vernacular: 你冇聽到嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒聽到嗎?」

passages.original: “There!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那裡!

passages.original: Now you hear it.”
passages.vernacular: 而家你聽到喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你聽到了。」

passages.original: “Lord, Tom, they’re coming!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,湯姆,佢哋嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,湯姆,他們來了!

passages.original: They’re coming, sure.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋肯定嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們肯定來了。

passages.original: What’ll we do?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “I dono.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: Think they’ll see us?”
passages.vernacular: 你想佢哋會睇到我哋嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想他們會看到我們嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, Tom, they can see in the dark, same as cats.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆,佢哋喺黑暗中睇得見,像貓一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆,他們在黑暗中看得見,像貓一樣。

passages.original: I wisht I hadn’t come.”
passages.vernacular: 我真希望我冇嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望我沒來。」

passages.original: “Oh, don’t be afeard.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別怕。

passages.original: I don’t believe they’ll bother us.
passages.vernacular: 我不相信佢哋會打擾我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不相信他們會打擾我們。

passages.original: We ain’t doing any harm.
passages.vernacular: 我哋冇做任何壞事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們沒有做任何壞事。

passages.original: If we keep perfectly still, maybe they won’t notice us at all.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋完全靜止,或者佢哋根本唔會注意到我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們完全靜止,也許他們根本不會注意到我們。」

passages.original: “I’ll try to, Tom, but, Lord, I’m all of a shiver.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會試試,湯姆,但係,天呀,我渾身發抖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會試試,湯姆,但是,天哪,我渾身發抖。」

passages.original: “Listen!”
The boys bent their heads together and scarcely breathed.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋把頭湊喺一起,幾乎不呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們把頭湊在一起,幾乎不呼吸。

passages.original: A muffled sound of voices floated up from the far end of the graveyard.
passages.vernacular: 一陣被悶住嘅講話聲從墳場遠端飄上嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣被悶住的說話聲從墳場遠端飄上來。

passages.original: “Look!
See there!” whispered Tom.
passages.vernacular: 睇嗰邊!」湯姆低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看那邊!」湯姆低聲說。

passages.original: “What is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」

passages.original: “It’s devil-fire.
passages.vernacular: 「係鬼火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是鬼火。

passages.original: Oh, Tom, this is awful.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,湯姆,呢太可怕喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,湯姆,這太可怕了。」

passages.original: Some vague figures approached through the gloom, swinging an old-fashioned tin lantern that freckled the ground with innumerable little spangles of light.
passages.vernacular: 啲模糊嘅人影穿過昏暗走近,搖晃住一盞老式錫燈籠,喺地面上灑下無數小小嘅光點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一些模糊的人影穿過昏暗走近,搖晃著一盞老式錫燈籠,在地面上灑下無數小小的光點。

passages.original: Presently Huckleberry whispered with a shudder:
passages.vernacular: 不久哈克貝利顫抖住低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久哈克貝利顫抖著低聲說:

passages.original: “It’s the devils sure enough.
passages.vernacular: 「肯定係魔鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「肯定是魔鬼。

passages.original: Three of ’em!
passages.vernacular: 三個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三個!

passages.original: Lordy, Tom, we’re goners!
passages.vernacular: 天呀,湯姆,我哋完喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,湯姆,我們完了!

passages.original: Can you pray?”
passages.vernacular: 你會禱告嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會禱告嗎?」

passages.original: “I’ll try, but don’t you be afeard.
passages.vernacular: 「我會試試,但你別怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會試試,但你別怕。

passages.original: They ain’t going to hurt us.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔會傷害我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不會傷害我們。

passages.original: ‘Now I lay me down to sleep, I—’”
passages.vernacular: 『而家我躺下瞓覺,我——』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『現在我躺下睡覺,我——』」

passages.original: “Sh!”
“What is it, Huck?”
passages.vernacular: 「點喇,哈克?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了,哈克?」

passages.original: “They’re humans!
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋係人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們是人!

passages.original: One of ’em is, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 至少其中一個係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少其中一個是。

passages.original: One of ’em’s old Muff Potter’s voice.”
passages.vernacular: 其中一個係老馬夫·波特嘅聲音。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一個是老馬夫·波特的聲音。」

passages.original: “No—’tain’t so, is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「不——唔係吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——不是吧?」

passages.original: “I bet I know it.
passages.vernacular: 「我打賭我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我打賭我知道。

passages.original: Don’t you stir nor budge.
passages.vernacular: 你別動都別挪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你別動也別挪。

passages.original: He ain’t sharp enough to notice us.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔夠敏銳,注意唔到我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不夠敏銳,注意不到我們。

passages.original: Drunk, the same as usual, likely—blamed old rip!”
passages.vernacular: 像往常一樣醉喇,大概——該死嘅老流氓!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像往常一樣醉了,大概——該死的老流氓!」

passages.original: “All right, I’ll keep still.
passages.vernacular: 「好,我保持不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,我保持不動。

passages.original: Now they’re stuck.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢哋卡住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他們卡住了。

passages.original: Can’t find it.
passages.vernacular: 找唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 找不到。

passages.original: Here they come again.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋又嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們又來了。

passages.original: Now they’re hot.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢哋接近喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他們接近了。

passages.original: Cold again.
passages.vernacular: 又冷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又冷了。

passages.original: Hot again.
passages.vernacular: 又熱喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又熱了。

passages.original: Red hot!
passages.vernacular: 滾熱!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾熱!

passages.original: They’re p’inted right, this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢次佢哋指對喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次他們指對了。

passages.original: Say, Huck, I know another o’ them voices; it’s Injun Joe.”
passages.vernacular: 喂,哈克,我知道另一個聲音;係印第安喬。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,哈克,我知道另一個聲音;是印第安喬。」

passages.original: “That’s so—that murderin’ half-breed!
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——嗰個殺人嘅混血兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——那個殺人的混血兒!

passages.original: I’d druther they was devils a dern sight.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願佢哋係魔鬼,好得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願他們是魔鬼,好得多。

passages.original: What kin they be up to?”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋能幹乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們能幹什麼?」

passages.original: The whisper died wholly out, now, for the three men had reached the grave and stood within a few feet of the boys’ hiding-place.
passages.vernacular: 耳語而家完全消失喇,因為三個男人已經到咗墳邊,站喺男孩藏身處幾呎之內。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 耳語現在完全消失了,因為三個男人已經到了墳邊,站在男孩藏身處幾呎之內。

passages.original: “Here it is,” said the third voice; and the owner of it held the lantern up and revealed the face of young Doctor Robinson.
passages.vernacular: 「就係呢度,」第三個聲音講;佢嘅主人舉起燈籠,露出咗年輕嘅羅賓遜醫生嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是這裡,」第三個聲音說;它的主人舉起燈籠,露出了年輕的羅賓遜醫生的臉。

passages.original: Potter and Injun Joe were carrying a handbarrow with a rope and a couple of shovels on it.
passages.vernacular: 波特同印第安喬抬住一輛手推車,上面有一根繩子同兩把鏟子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特和印第安喬抬著一輛手推車,上面有一根繩子和兩把鏟子。

passages.original: They cast down their load and began to open the grave.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋放下貨物,開始挖墳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們放下貨物,開始挖墳。

passages.original: The doctor put the lantern at the head of the grave and came and sat down with his back against one of the elm trees.
passages.vernacular: 醫生把燈籠放喺墳頭,過嚟坐下,背靠住一棵榆樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生把燈籠放在墳頭,過來坐下,背靠著一棵榆樹。

passages.original: He was so close the boys could have touched him.
passages.vernacular: 佢離得咁近,男孩哋能碰到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他離得那麼近,男孩們能碰到他。

passages.original: “Hurry, men!” he said, in a low voice; “the moon might come out at any moment.”
passages.vernacular: 「快點,夥計哋!」佢低聲講;「月亮隨時可能出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快點,夥計們!」他低聲說;「月亮隨時可能出來。」

passages.original: They growled a response and went on digging.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋咆哮住回應,繼續挖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們咆哮著回應,繼續挖。

passages.original: For some time there was no noise but the grating sound of the spades discharging their freight of mould and gravel.
passages.vernacular: 有一段時間除咗鏟子倒出泥土同碎石嘅刮擦聲外冇噪音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一段時間除了鏟子倒出泥土和碎石的刮擦聲外沒有噪音。

passages.original: It was very monotonous.
passages.vernacular: 好單調。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 非常單調。

passages.original: Finally a spade struck upon the coffin with a dull woody accent, and within another minute or two the men had hoisted it out on the ground.
passages.vernacular: 最後一把鏟子以沉悶嘅木頭音調碰到咗棺材,再過一兩分鐘,人哋把佢吊出放喺地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後一把鏟子以沉悶的木頭音調碰到了棺材,再過一兩分鐘,人們把它吊出放在地上。

passages.original: They pried off the lid with their shovels, got out the body and dumped it rudely on the ground.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋用鏟子撬開蓋子,取出屍體,粗魯地扔喺地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們用鏟子撬開蓋子,取出屍體,粗魯地扔在地上。

passages.original: The moon drifted from behind the clouds and exposed the pallid face.
passages.vernacular: 月亮從雲後飄出嚟,露出蒼白嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月亮從雲後飄出來,露出蒼白的臉。

passages.original: The barrow was got ready and the corpse placed on it, covered with a blanket, and bound to its place with the rope.
passages.vernacular: 手推車準備好喇,屍體放喺上面,蓋上毯子,用繩子綁在位置上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 手推車準備好了,屍體放在上面,蓋上毯子,用繩子綁在位置上。

passages.original: Potter took out a large spring-knife and cut off the dangling end of the rope and then said:
passages.vernacular: 波特攞出一把大彈簧刀,割掉繩子垂下嘅一端,然後講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特拿出一把大彈簧刀,割掉繩子垂下的一端,然後說:

passages.original: “Now the cussed thing’s ready, Sawbones, and you’ll just out with another five, or here she stays.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家呢該死嘅嘢準備好喇,外科大夫,你再攞出五塊嚟,否則佢就留喺呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在這該死的東西準備好了,外科大夫,你再拿出五塊來,否則它就留在這裡。」

passages.original: “That’s the talk!” said Injun Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「就係咁講!」印第安喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是這麼說!」印第安喬說。

passages.original: “Look here, what does this mean?” said the doctor.
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,呢個係乜嘢意思?」醫生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,這是什麼意思?」醫生說。

passages.original: “You required your pay in advance, and I’ve paid you.”
passages.vernacular: 「你要求預付酬金,我已經付畀你喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要求預付酬金,我已經付給你了。」

passages.original: “Yes, and you done more than that,” said Injun Joe, approaching the doctor, who was now standing.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,而你做得不止嗰啲,」印第安喬講,走近醫生,醫生呢陣站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,而你做得不止那些,」印第安喬說,走近醫生,醫生這時站著。

passages.original: “Five years ago you drove me away from your father’s kitchen one night, when I come to ask for something to eat, and you said I warn’t there for any good; and when I swore I’d get even with you if it took a hundred years, your father had me jailed for a vagrant.
passages.vernacular: 「五年前,一個晚上,我嚟要點食嘅,你把我從你父親嘅廚房趕走,講我唔係為了乜嘢好事嚟嘅;我發誓即使花一百年都要同你算帳時,你父親把我當流浪漢關進咗監獄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「五年前,一個晚上,我來要點吃的,你把我從你父親的廚房趕走,說我不是為了什麼好事來的;我發誓即使花一百年也要同你算帳時,你父親把我當流浪漢關進了監獄。

passages.original: Did you think I’d forget?
passages.vernacular: 你以為我會忘記嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以為我會忘記嗎?

passages.original: The Injun blood ain’t in me for nothing.
passages.vernacular: 我身上嘅印第安血唔係白流嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我身上的印第安血不是白流的。

passages.original: And now I’ve got you, and you got to settle, you know!”
passages.vernacular: 而家我抓到你喇,你得算清,你知道!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我抓到你了,你得算清,你知道!」

passages.original: He was threatening the doctor, with his fist in his face, by this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣佢正用拳頭抵住醫生嘅臉威脅佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時他正用拳頭抵著醫生的臉威脅他。

passages.original: The doctor struck out suddenly and stretched the ruffian on the ground.
passages.vernacular: 醫生突然一拳打出,把惡棍打倒喺地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生突然一拳打出,把惡棍打倒在地。

passages.original: Potter dropped his knife, and exclaimed:
passages.vernacular: 波特扔下刀,喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特扔下刀,喊道:

passages.original: “Here, now, don’t you hit my pard!” and the next moment he had grappled with the doctor and the two were struggling with might and main, trampling the grass and tearing the ground with their heels.
passages.vernacular: 「喂,別打我夥計!」下一刻佢已經同醫生扭打,兩人拼盡全力搏鬥,踐踏草地,用腳跟撕裂土地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,別打我夥計!」下一刻他已經同醫生扭打,兩人拼盡全力搏鬥,踐踏草地,用腳跟撕裂土地。

passages.original: Injun Joe sprang to his feet, his eyes flaming with passion, snatched up Potter’s knife, and went creeping, catlike and stooping, round and round about the combatants, seeking an opportunity.
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬一躍而起,眼睛因激怒而燃燒,抓起波特嘅刀,貓一樣彎住腰繞住搏鬥者一圈又一圈地潛行,尋找機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬一躍而起,眼睛因激怒而燃燒,抓起波特的刀,貓一樣彎著腰繞著搏鬥者一圈又一圈地潛行,尋找機會。

passages.original: All at once the doctor flung himself free, seized the heavy headboard of Williams’ grave and felled Potter to the earth with it—and in the same instant the half-breed saw his chance and drove the knife to the hilt in the young man’s breast.
passages.vernacular: 突然醫生掙脫喇,抓起威廉斯墳上沉重嘅墓板,把波特打倒喺地——就喺同一瞬間,混血兒睇到機會,把刀直插到柄,刺入年輕人嘅胸膛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然醫生掙脫了,抓起威廉斯墳上沉重的墓板,把波特打倒在地——就在同一瞬間,混血兒看到機會,把刀直插到柄,刺入年輕人的胸膛。

passages.original: He reeled and fell partly upon Potter, flooding him with his blood, and in the same moment the clouds blotted out the dreadful spectacle and the two frightened boys went speeding away in the dark.
passages.vernacular: 佢踉蹌住倒下,部分壓喺波特身上,把佢浸喺佢嘅血中,同一時刻雲遮住咗呢個可怕嘅場面,兩個受驚嘅男孩喺黑暗中飛奔而去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他踉蹌著倒下,部分壓在波特身上,把他浸在他的血中,同一時刻雲遮住了這可怕的場面,兩個受驚的男孩在黑暗中飛奔而去。

passages.original: Presently, when the moon emerged again, Injun Joe was standing over the two forms, contemplating them.
passages.vernacular: 不久,月亮再次露面時,印第安喬正站喺兩個身體上方,凝視住佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,月亮再次露面時,印第安喬正站在兩個身體上方,凝視著他們。

passages.original: The doctor murmured inarticulately, gave a long gasp or two and was still.
passages.vernacular: 醫生含糊地低語,長長地喘咗一兩口氣,就靜止喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生含糊地低語,長長地喘了一兩口氣,就靜止了。

passages.original: The half-breed muttered:
passages.vernacular: 混血兒喃喃講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 混血兒喃喃說:

passages.original: “That score is settled—damn you.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰筆帳算清喇——該死嘅你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那筆帳算清了——該死的你。」

passages.original: Then he robbed the body.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢搜劫咗屍體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他搜劫了屍體。

passages.original: After which he put the fatal knife in Potter’s open right hand, and sat down on the dismantled coffin.
passages.vernacular: 之後佢把致命嘅刀放喺波特張開嘅右手裡,坐喺被拆開嘅棺材上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後他把致命的刀放在波特張開的右手裡,坐在被拆開的棺材上。

passages.original: Three—four—five minutes passed, and then Potter began to stir and moan.
passages.vernacular: 三——四——五分鐘過去喇,然後波特開始動並呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三——四——五分鐘過去了,然後波特開始動並呻吟。

passages.original: His hand closed upon the knife; he raised it, glanced at it, and let it fall, with a shudder.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅手握住咗刀;佢舉起佢,瞥咗一眼,顫抖住讓佢掉下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的手握住了刀;他舉起它,瞥了一眼,顫抖著讓它掉下。

passages.original: Then he sat up, pushing the body from him, and gazed at it, and then around him, confusedly.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢坐起嚟,把屍體從身邊推開,凝視住佢,然後困惑地睇住四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他坐起來,把屍體從身邊推開,凝視著它,然後困惑地看著四周。

passages.original: His eyes met Joe’s.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛遇到咗喬嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的眼睛遇到了喬的。

passages.original: “Lord, how is this, Joe?” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,呢個係點回事,喬?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,這是怎麼回事,喬?」他說。

passages.original: “It’s a dirty business,” said Joe, without moving.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係件骯髒嘅事,」喬講,冇動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是件骯髒的事,」喬說,沒有動。

passages.original: “What did you do it for?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點解咁樣做?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼這樣做?」

passages.original: I never done it!”
passages.vernacular: 我冇做!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒做!」

passages.original: “Look here!
passages.vernacular: 「聽住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著!

passages.original: That kind of talk won’t wash.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰種話行不通。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那種話行不通。」

passages.original: Potter trembled and grew white.
passages.vernacular: 波特顫抖住,變白喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特顫抖著,變白了。

passages.original: “I thought I’d got sober.
passages.vernacular: 「我以為我酒醒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以為我酒醒了。

passages.original: I’d no business to drink to-night.
passages.vernacular: 我今晚不該飲酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我今晚不該喝酒。

passages.original: But it’s in my head yet—worse’n when we started here.
passages.vernacular: 但佢仲喺我腦子裡——比我哋開始嚟呢度時更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它還在我腦子裡——比我們開始來這裡時更糟。

passages.original: I’m all in a muddle; can’t recollect anything of it, hardly.
passages.vernacular: 我完全糊塗喇;幾乎乜嘢都記唔得喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我完全糊塗了;幾乎什麼也記不得了。

passages.original: Tell me, Joe—honest, now, old feller—did I do it?
passages.vernacular: 告訴我,喬——老實講,老夥計——係我幹嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我,喬——老實說,老夥計——是我幹的嗎?

passages.original: Joe, I never meant to—’pon my soul and honor, I never meant to, Joe.
passages.vernacular: 喬,我唔係有意嘅——我以靈魂同榮譽發誓,我唔係有意嘅,喬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬,我不是有意的——我以靈魂和榮譽發誓,我不是有意的,喬。

passages.original: Tell me how it was, Joe.
passages.vernacular: 告訴我係點回事,喬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我是怎麼回事,喬。

passages.original: Oh, it’s awful—and him so young and promising.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,太可怕喇——佢咁年輕,前途無量。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,太可怕了——他那麼年輕,前途無量。」

passages.original: “Why, you two was scuffling, and he fetched you one with the headboard and you fell flat; and then up you come, all reeling and staggering like, and snatched the knife and jammed it into him, just as he fetched you another awful clip—and here you’ve laid, as dead as a wedge til now.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,你哋倆喺扭打,佢用墓板畀咗你一下,你直挺挺地倒下喇;然後你站起嚟,搖搖晃晃、踉踉蹌蹌嘅,抓起刀子捅進佢身上,正好佢又畀你可怕嘅一擊——然後你就躺喺呢度,像楔子一樣死喇,直到而家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,你們倆在扭打,他用墓板給了你一下,你直挺挺地倒下了;然後你站起來,搖搖晃晃、踉踉蹌蹌的,抓起刀子捅進他身上,正好他又給你可怕的一擊——然後你就躺在這裡,像楔子一樣死了,直到現在。」

passages.original: “Oh, I didn’t know what I was a-doing.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我唔知道我喺幹乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我不知道我在幹什麼。

passages.original: I wish I may die this minute if I did.
passages.vernacular: 我希望我此刻就死,如果我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我此刻就死,如果我知道。

passages.original: It was all on account of the whiskey and the excitement, I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 呢都係因為威士忌同興奮,我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這都是因為威士忌和興奮,我想。

passages.original: I never used a weepon in my life before, Joe.
passages.vernacular: 我一輩子從冇用過武器,喬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一輩子從沒用過武器,喬。

passages.original: I’ve fought, but never with weepons.
passages.vernacular: 我打過架,但從冇用過武器。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打過架,但從沒用過武器。

passages.original: They’ll all say that.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都會咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都會這麼說。

passages.original: Joe, don’t tell!
passages.vernacular: 喬,唔好講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬,別說!

passages.original: Say you won’t tell, Joe—that’s a good feller.
passages.vernacular: 講你唔會講,喬——呢才係好夥計。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說你不會說,喬——這才是好夥計。

passages.original: I always liked you, Joe, and stood up for you, too.
passages.vernacular: 我一直鍾意你,喬,都替你講過話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直喜歡你,喬,也替你說過話。

passages.original: Don’t you remember?
passages.vernacular: 你不記得嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不記得嗎?

passages.original: You won’t tell, will you, Joe?”
passages.vernacular: 你唔會講嘅,對吧,喬?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不會說的,對吧,喬?」

passages.original: And the poor creature dropped on his knees before the stolid murderer, and clasped his appealing hands.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅人跪喺冷漠嘅兇手面前,雙手合十懇求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的人跪在冷漠的兇手面前,雙手合十懇求。

passages.original: “No, you’ve always been fair and square with me, Muff Potter, and I won’t go back on you.
passages.vernacular: 「不,你一直對我公平正直,馬夫·波特,我唔會背棄你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,你一直對我公平正直,馬夫·波特,我不會背棄你。

passages.original: There, now, that’s as fair as a man can say.”
passages.vernacular: 好喇,呢個係一個人能講嘅最公平嘅話喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,這是一個人能說的最公平的話了。」

passages.original: “Oh, Joe, you’re an angel.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,喬,你係天使。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,喬,你是天使。

passages.original: I’ll bless you for this the longest day I live.”
passages.vernacular: 我活住嘅最長一天我都會為此祝福你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我活著的最長一天我都會為此祝福你。」

passages.original: And Potter began to cry.
passages.vernacular: 波特開始哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特開始哭。

passages.original: “Come, now, that’s enough of that.
passages.vernacular: 「嚟,夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來,夠了。

passages.original: This ain’t any time for blubbering.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係啼哭嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是啼哭的時候。

passages.original: You be off yonder way and I’ll go this.
passages.vernacular: 你往嗰邊走,我走呢邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你往那邊走,我走這邊。

passages.original: Move, now, and don’t leave any tracks behind you.”
passages.vernacular: 動吧,別留下痕跡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 動吧,別留下痕跡。」

passages.original: Potter started on a trot that quickly increased to a run.
passages.vernacular: 波特開始小跑,好快加快為跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特開始小跑,很快加快為跑。

passages.original: The half-breed stood looking after him.
passages.vernacular: 混血兒站住睇住佢嘅背影。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 混血兒站著看著他的背影。

passages.original: He muttered:
passages.vernacular: 佢喃喃講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他喃喃說:

passages.original: “If he’s as much stunned with the lick and fuddled with the rum as he had the look of being, he won’t think of the knife till he’s gone so far he’ll be afraid to come back after it to such a place by himself—chicken-heart!”
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢像睇起嚟嗰樣被打暈同被朗姆酒弄糊塗,佢唔會想起嗰把刀,直到佢走得太遠,唔敢自己回到咁樣嘅地方嚟取——膽小鬼!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果他像看起來那樣被打暈和被朗姆酒弄糊塗,他不會想起那把刀,直到他走得太遠,不敢自己回到這樣的地方來取——膽小鬼!」

passages.original: Two or three minutes later the murdered man, the blanketed corpse, the lidless coffin, and the open grave were under no inspection but the moon’s.
passages.vernacular: 兩三分鐘後,被謀殺嘅人、蓋住毯子嘅屍體、冇蓋嘅棺材同敞開嘅墳墓,唔再受任何人檢視,只有月亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩三分鐘後,被謀殺的人、蓋著毯子的屍體、沒有蓋的棺材和敞開的墳墓,不再受任何人檢視,只有月亮。

passages.original: The stillness was complete again, too.
passages.vernacular: 寂靜又完全恢復喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寂靜又完全恢復了。

chapters.title: Chapter X: The Solemn Oath 第十章:莊嚴的誓言

passages.original: CH The two boys flew on and on, toward the village, speechless with horror.
passages.vernacular: 兩個男孩一直飛奔,向村子跑去,嚇得講不出話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個男孩一直飛奔,向村子跑去,嚇得說不出話。

passages.original: They glanced backward over their shoulders from time to time, apprehensively, as if they feared they might be followed.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不時恐懼地回頭睇,好像怕被人跟蹤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不時恐懼地回頭看,好像怕被人跟蹤。

passages.original: Every stump that started up in their path seemed a man and an enemy, and made them catch their breath; and as they sped by some outlying cottages that lay near the village, the barking of the aroused watch-dogs seemed to give wings to their feet.
passages.vernacular: 路上冒出嘅每個樹樁似乎都係一個人、一個敵人,使佢哋屏住呼吸;佢哋飛快地經過靠近村子嘅啲偏遠小屋時,被驚醒嘅睇門狗嘅叫聲似乎畀佢哋嘅腳添上咗翅膀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路上冒出的每個樹樁似乎都是一個人、一個敵人,使他們屏住呼吸;他們飛快地經過靠近村子的一些偏遠小屋時,被驚醒的看門狗的叫聲似乎給他們的腳添上了翅膀。

passages.original: “If we can only get to the old tannery before we break down!” whispered Tom, in short catches between breaths.
passages.vernacular: 「只要我哋喺垮掉之前到達老製革廠就好喇!」湯姆喺呼吸之間斷斷續續地低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要我們在垮掉之前到達老製革廠就好了!」湯姆在呼吸之間斷斷續續地低聲說。

passages.original: “I can’t stand it much longer.”
passages.vernacular: 「我再都支撐不咗多久喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我再也支撐不了多久了。」

passages.original: Huckleberry’s hard pantings were his only reply, and the boys fixed their eyes on the goal of their hopes and bent to their work to win it.
passages.vernacular: 哈克貝利粗重嘅喘息係佢唯一嘅回答,男孩哋把眼睛盯住佢哋希望嘅目標,埋頭努力去贏得佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克貝利粗重的喘息是他唯一的回答,男孩們把眼睛盯著他們希望的目標,埋頭努力去贏得它。

passages.original: They gained steadily on it, and at last, breast to breast, they burst through the open door and fell grateful and exhausted in the sheltering shadows beyond.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋穩定地逼近佢,最後肩並肩地衝進敞開嘅門,感激地、筋疲力盡地倒喺嗰邊遮蔽嘅陰影中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們穩定地逼近它,最後肩並肩地衝進敞開的門,感激地、筋疲力盡地倒在那邊遮蔽的陰影中。

passages.original: By and by their pulses slowed down, and Tom whispered:
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地佢哋嘅脈搏慢下嚟,湯姆低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地他們的脈搏慢下來,湯姆低聲說:

passages.original: “Huckleberry, what do you reckon’ll come of this?”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克貝利,你想呢件事會點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克貝利,你想這件事會怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “If Doctor Robinson dies, I reckon hanging’ll come of it.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果羅賓遜醫生死喇,我想結果就係絞刑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果羅賓遜醫生死了,我想結果就是絞刑。」

passages.original: “Do you though?”
passages.vernacular: 「你真咁想嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真這麼想嗎?」

passages.original: “Why, I know it, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我知道,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我知道,湯姆。」

passages.original: Tom thought a while, then he said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆想咗一會兒,然後講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆想了一會兒,然後說:

passages.original: “Who’ll tell?
passages.vernacular: 「邊個會講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰會說?

passages.original: We?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們?」

passages.original: “What are you talking about?
passages.vernacular: 「你喺講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在說什麼?

passages.original: S’pose something happened and Injun Joe didn’t hang?
passages.vernacular: 假設發生咗乜嘢事,印第安喬冇被絞死呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假設發生了什麼事,印第安喬沒被絞死呢?

passages.original: Why, he’d kill us some time or other, just as dead sure as we’re a laying here.”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,佢遲早會殺死我哋,就像我哋躺喺呢度一樣肯定。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,他遲早會殺死我們,就像我們躺在這裡一樣肯定。」

passages.original: “That’s just what I was thinking to myself, Huck.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰正是我心裡想嘅,哈克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那正是我心裡想的,哈克。」

passages.original: “If anybody tells, let Muff Potter do it, if he’s fool enough.
passages.vernacular: 「如果有人講,讓馬夫·波特講吧,如果佢傻到講嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果有人說,讓馬夫·波特說吧,如果他傻到說的話。

passages.original: He’s generally drunk enough.”
passages.vernacular: 佢通常夠醉嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他通常夠醉的。」

passages.original: Tom said nothing—went on thinking.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆乜嘢都冇講——繼續想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆什麼也沒說——繼續想。

passages.original: Presently he whispered:
passages.vernacular: 不久佢低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他低聲說:

passages.original: “Huck, Muff Potter don’t know it.
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,馬夫·波特唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,馬夫·波特不知道。

passages.original: How can he tell?”
passages.vernacular: 佢點能講?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他怎麼能說?」

passages.original: “What’s the reason he don’t know it?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢點解唔知道?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他為什麼不知道?」

passages.original: “Because he’d just got that whack when Injun Joe done it.
passages.vernacular: 「因為印第安喬動手時,佢剛挨咗嗰一擊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為印第安喬動手時,他剛挨了那一擊。

passages.original: D’you reckon he could see anything?
passages.vernacular: 你想佢能睇到乜嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想他能看到什麼嗎?

passages.original: D’you reckon he knowed anything?”
passages.vernacular: 你想佢知道乜嘢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想他知道什麼嗎?」

passages.original: “By hokey, that’s so, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,係咁樣,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,是這樣,湯姆!」

passages.original: “And besides, look-a-here—maybe that whack done for him!”
passages.vernacular: 「而且,聽住——或者嗰一擊把佢打死喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且,聽著——也許那一擊把他打死了!」

passages.original: “No, ’taint likely, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「不,不太可能,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不太可能,湯姆。

passages.original: He had liquor in him; I could see that; and besides, he always has.
passages.vernacular: 佢體內有酒;我睇得出嚟;而且,佢總是咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他體內有酒;我看得出來;而且,他總是這樣。

passages.original: Well, when pap’s full, you might take and belt him over the head with a church and you couldn’t phase him.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,爸爸飲醉時,你可以攞一座教堂打佢嘅頭,都打不暈佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,爸爸喝醉時,你可以拿一座教堂打他的頭,也打不暈他。

passages.original: He says so, his own self.
passages.vernacular: 佢自己咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他自己這麼說。

passages.original: So it’s the same with Muff Potter, of course.
passages.vernacular: 所以馬夫·波特當然都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以馬夫·波特當然也一樣。

passages.original: But if a man was dead sober, I reckon maybe that whack might fetch him; I dono.”
passages.vernacular: 但如果一個人完全清醒,我想或者嗰一擊可以打倒佢;我唔知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果一個人完全清醒,我想也許那一擊可以打倒他;我不知道。」

passages.original: After another reflective silence, Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 又一陣沉思嘅沉默後,湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一陣沉思的沉默後,湯姆說:

passages.original: “Hucky, you sure you can keep mum?”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,你確定你能保持沉默嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,你確定你能保持沉默嗎?」

passages.original: “Tom, we got to keep mum.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我哋必須保持沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我們必須保持沉默。

passages.original: You know that.
passages.vernacular: 你知道嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道的。

passages.original: That Injun devil wouldn’t make any more of drownding us than a couple of cats, if we was to squeak ’bout this and they didn’t hang him.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋吭一聲,而佢哋冇絞死佢,嗰個印第安魔鬼淹死我哋就像淹死一對貓一樣不當回事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們吭一聲,而他們沒有絞死他,那個印第安魔鬼淹死我們就像淹死一對貓一樣不當回事。

passages.original: Now, look-a-here, Tom, less take and swear to one another—that’s what we got to do—swear to keep mum.”
passages.vernacular: 而家,聽住,湯姆,讓我哋互相發誓——呢個係我哋必須做嘅——發誓保持沉默。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,聽著,湯姆,讓我們互相發誓——這是我們必須做的——發誓保持沉默。」

passages.original: “I’m agreed.
passages.vernacular: 「我同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我同意。

passages.original: It’s the best thing.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係最好嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是最好的辦法。

passages.original: Would you just hold hands and swear that we—”
passages.vernacular: 你只係握手然後發誓我哋——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只是握手然後發誓我們——」

passages.original: “Oh no, that wouldn’t do for this.
passages.vernacular: 「哦不,呢件事唔能夠嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦不,這件事不能那樣。

passages.original: That’s good enough for little rubbishy common things—specially with gals, cuz they go back on you anyway, and blab if they get in a huff—but there orter be writing ’bout a big thing like this.
passages.vernacular: 嗰適合小小嘅、不值一提嘅平常事——尤其係對女孩,因為佢哋反正會反悔,一生氣就亂講——但像咁大嘅事應該有書面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那適合小小的、不值一提的平常事——尤其是對女孩,因為她們反正會反悔,一生氣就亂說——但像這麼大的事應該有書面。

passages.original: And blood.”
passages.vernacular: 仲有血。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有血。」

passages.original: Tom’s whole being applauded this idea.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆整個人都贊同呢個主意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆整個人都贊同這個主意。

passages.original: It was deep, and dark, and awful; the hour, the circumstances, the surroundings, were in keeping with it.
passages.vernacular: 佢深沉、黑暗、可怕;時辰、環境、周圍都同佢相稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它深沉、黑暗、可怕;時辰、環境、周圍都與它相稱。

passages.original: He picked up a clean pine shingle that lay in the moon-light, took a little fragment of “red keel” out of his pocket, got the moon on his work, and painfully scrawled these lines, emphasizing each slow down-stroke by clamping his tongue between his teeth, and letting up the pressure on the up-strokes.
passages.vernacular: 佢撿起躺喺月光下嘅一塊乾淨嘅松木薄板,從口袋裡攞出一小塊「紅粉筆」,讓月亮照喺佢嘅作品上,痛苦地潦草寫下呢幾行,每慢慢往下嘅一筆都用牙齒夾住舌頭強調,向上嘅筆畫時放鬆壓力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他撿起躺在月光下的一塊乾淨的松木薄板,從口袋裡拿出一小塊「紅粉筆」,讓月亮照在他的作品上,痛苦地潦草寫下這幾行,每慢慢往下的一筆都用牙齒夾住舌頭強調,向上的筆畫時放鬆壓力。

passages.original: “Huck Finn and Tom Sawyer swears they will keep mum about This and They wish They may Drop down dead in Their Tracks if They ever Tell and Rot.”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克·費恩同湯姆·索亞發誓佢哋將對此事保持沉默,如果佢哋講出去,願佢哋當場倒地而死,爛掉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克·費恩和湯姆·索亞發誓他們將對此事保持沉默,如果他們說出去,願他們當場倒地而死,爛掉。」

passages.original: Huckleberry was filled with admiration of Tom’s facility in writing, and the sublimity of his language.
passages.vernacular: 哈克貝利對湯姆寫字嘅流利同語言嘅崇高充滿欽佩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克貝利對湯姆寫字的流利和語言的崇高充滿欽佩。

passages.original: He at once took a pin from his lapel and was going to prick his flesh, but Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻從翻領上取下一根針,準備刺破自己嘅皮肉,但湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他立刻從翻領上取下一根針,準備刺破自己的皮肉,但湯姆說:

passages.original: “Hold on!
passages.vernacular: 「等一下!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等一下!

passages.original: Don’t do that.
passages.vernacular: 別嗰樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別那樣做。

passages.original: A pin’s brass.
passages.vernacular: 針係黃銅嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 針是黃銅的。

passages.original: It might have verdigrease on it.”
passages.vernacular: 上面可能有銅綠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面可能有銅綠。」

passages.original: “What’s verdigrease?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢係銅綠?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼是銅綠?」

passages.original: “It’s p’ison.
passages.vernacular: 「係毒藥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是毒藥。

passages.original: That’s what it is.
passages.vernacular: 就係嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是那樣。

passages.original: You just swaller some of it once—you’ll see.”
passages.vernacular: 你吞下啲試試——你就知道喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你吞下一點試試——你就知道了。」

passages.original: So Tom unwound the thread from one of his needles, and each boy pricked the ball of his thumb and squeezed out a drop of blood.
passages.vernacular: 於是湯姆從一根針上解下線,每個男孩刺破拇指球,擠出一滴血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是湯姆從一根針上解下線,每個男孩刺破拇指球,擠出一滴血。

passages.original: In time, after many squeezes, Tom managed to sign his initials, using the ball of his little finger for a pen.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,擠咗好多次後,湯姆設法簽上咗佢嘅姓名縮寫,用佢小指嘅指球當筆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,擠了很多次後,湯姆設法簽上了他的姓名縮寫,用他小指的指球當筆。

passages.original: Then he showed Huckleberry how to make an H and an F, and the oath was complete.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢教哈克貝利點寫H同F,誓言就完成喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他教哈克貝利怎麼寫H和F,誓言就完成了。

passages.original: They buried the shingle close to the wall, with some dismal ceremonies and incantations, and the fetters that bound their tongues were considered to be locked and the key thrown away.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把薄板埋喺牆邊,舉行咗啲陰鬱嘅儀式同咒語,束縛佢哋舌頭嘅鐐銬被認為鎖上喇,鑰匙都扔掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把薄板埋在牆邊,舉行了一些陰鬱的儀式和咒語,束縛他們舌頭的鐐銬被認為鎖上了,鑰匙也扔掉了。

passages.original: A figure crept stealthily through a break in the other end of the ruined building, now, but they did not notice it.
passages.vernacular: 一個身影從廢墟建築另一端嘅破口悄悄爬進嚟,但佢哋冇注意到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個身影從廢墟建築另一端的破口悄悄爬進來,但他們沒有注意到。

passages.original: “Tom,” whispered Huckleberry, “does this keep us from ever telling—always?”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,」哈克貝利低聲講,「呢能讓我哋永遠不講——一直不講嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,」哈克貝利低聲說,「這能讓我們永遠不說——一直不說嗎?」

passages.original: “Of course it does.
passages.vernacular: 「當然能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然能。

passages.original: It don’t make any difference what happens, we got to keep mum.
passages.vernacular: 不管發生乜嘢,我哋都必須保持沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管發生什麼,我們都必須保持沉默。

passages.original: We’d drop down dead—don’t you know that?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋會當場倒地而死——你唔知道嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會當場倒地而死——你不知道嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, I reckon that’s so.”
passages.vernacular: 「對,我想係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,我想是的。」

passages.original: They continued to whisper for some little time.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋繼續低聲講話咗一小會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們繼續低聲說話了一小會兒。

passages.original: Presently a dog set up a long, lugubrious howl just outside—within ten feet of them.
passages.vernacular: 不久一隻狗喺外面——離佢哋十呎以內——發出一聲悠長、淒厲嘅嚎叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久一隻狗在外面——離他們十呎以內——發出一聲悠長、淒厲的嚎叫。

passages.original: The boys clasped each other suddenly, in an agony of fright.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋突然緊緊抱喺一起,喺恐懼中痛苦萬分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們突然緊緊抱在一起,在恐懼中痛苦萬分。

passages.original: “Which of us does he mean?” gasped Huckleberry.
passages.vernacular: 「佢指嘅係我哋邊一個?」哈克貝利喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他指的是我們哪一個?」哈克貝利喘著氣說。

passages.original: “I dono—peep through the crack.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道——從縫裡偷睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道——從縫裡偷看。

passages.original: Quick!”
“No, you, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 「不,你,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,你,湯姆!」

passages.original: “I can’t—I can’t do it, Huck!”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠——我唔敢,哈克!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能——我不敢,哈克!」

passages.original: “Please, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「求你,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「求你,湯姆。

passages.original: There ’tis again!”
passages.vernacular: 又嚟喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又來了!」

passages.original: “Oh, lordy, I’m thankful!” whispered Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,天呀,我感謝!」湯姆低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,天哪,我感謝!」湯姆低聲說。

passages.original: “I know his voice.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道佢嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道他的聲音。

passages.original: It’s Bull Harbison.”
passages.vernacular: 係布爾·哈比森。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是布爾·哈比森。」

passages.original: [* If Mr. Harbison owned a slave named Bull, Tom would have spoken of him as “Harbison’s Bull,” but a son or a dog of that name was “Bull Harbison.”]
passages.vernacular: [*如果哈比森先生有個叫布爾嘅奴隸,湯姆會稱佢為「哈比森嘅布爾」,但呢個名字嘅兒子或狗叫「布爾·哈比森」。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [*如果哈比森先生有個叫布爾的奴隸,湯姆會稱他為「哈比森的布爾」,但這個名字的兒子或狗叫「布爾·哈比森」。]

passages.original: “Oh, that’s good—I tell you, Tom, I was most scared to death; I’d a bet anything it was a stray dog.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰好——我告訴你,湯姆,我差點嚇死;我敢打賭任何嘢佢係流浪狗。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那好——我告訴你,湯姆,我差點嚇死;我敢打賭任何東西它是流浪狗。」

passages.original: The dog howled again.
passages.vernacular: 狗又嚎叫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗又嚎叫了。

passages.original: The boys’ hearts sank once more.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋嘅心又沉咗下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們的心又沉了下去。

passages.original: “Oh, my! that ain’t no Bull Harbison!” whispered Huckleberry.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,天呀!嗰唔係布爾·哈比森!」哈克貝利低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,天哪!那不是布爾·哈比森!」哈克貝利低聲說。

passages.original: “Do, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 「睇吧,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看吧,湯姆!」

passages.original: Tom, quaking with fear, yielded, and put his eye to the crack.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嚇得發抖,屈服喇,把眼睛貼喺縫上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆嚇得發抖,屈服了,把眼睛貼在縫上。

passages.original: His whisper was hardly audible when he said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講話時低語幾乎聽唔見:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說話時低語幾乎聽不見:

passages.original: “Oh, Huck, it’s a stray dog!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,哈克,係流浪狗!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,哈克,是流浪狗!」

passages.original: “Quick, Tom, quick!
passages.vernacular: 「快,湯姆,快!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快,湯姆,快!

passages.original: Who does he mean?”
passages.vernacular: 佢指嘅係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他指的是誰?」

passages.original: “Huck, he must mean us both—we’re right together.”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,佢一定指我哋兩個——我哋就喺一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,他一定指我們兩個——我們就在一起。」

passages.original: “Oh, Tom, I reckon we’re goners.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆,我想我哋完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆,我想我們完了。

passages.original: I reckon there ain’t no mistake ’bout where I’ll go to.
passages.vernacular: 我想我要去邊度毫無疑問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我要去哪裡毫無疑問。

passages.original: I been so wicked.”
passages.vernacular: 我太壞喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太壞了。」

passages.original: “Dad fetch it!
passages.vernacular: 「該死!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「該死!

passages.original: This comes of playing hookey and doing everything a feller’s told not to do.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係逃學同做一切人家叫別做嘅事嘅結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是逃學和做一切人家叫別做的事的結果。

passages.original: I might a been good, like Sid, if I’d a tried—but no, I wouldn’t, of course.
passages.vernacular: 如果我試過,我可能像希德一樣好——不過不,當然我唔肯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我試過,我可能像希德一樣好——可是不,當然我不肯。

passages.original: But if ever I get off this time, I lay I’ll just waller in Sunday-schools!”
passages.vernacular: 但如果呢次我能脫身,我發誓我要沉浸喺主日學校裡!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果這次我能脫身,我發誓我要沉浸在主日學校裡!」

passages.original: And Tom began to snuffle a little.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆開始有點抽鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆開始有點抽鼻子。

passages.original: “You bad!” and Huckleberry began to snuffle too.
passages.vernacular: 「你壞!」哈克貝利都開始抽鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你壞!」哈克貝利也開始抽鼻子。

passages.original: “Consound it, Tom Sawyer, you’re just old pie, ’long-side o’ what I am.
passages.vernacular: 「真該死,湯姆·索亞,同我比,你只係老好人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真該死,湯姆·索亞,同我比,你只是老好人。

passages.original: Oh, lordy, lordy, lordy, I wisht I only had half your chance.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,天呀,天呀,天呀,我真希望我只有你一半嘅機會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,天哪,天哪,天哪,我真希望我只有你一半的機會。」

passages.original: Tom choked off and whispered:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆止住咗哽咽,低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆止住了哽咽,低聲說:

passages.original: “Look, Hucky, look!
passages.vernacular: 「睇,哈克,睇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看,哈克,看!

passages.original: He’s got his back to us!”
passages.vernacular: 佢背對住我哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他背對著我們!」

passages.original: Hucky looked, with joy in his heart.
passages.vernacular: 哈克睇喇,心裡充滿喜悅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克看了,心裡充滿喜悅。

passages.original: “Well, he has, by jingoes!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,佢確實係,天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,他確實是,天哪!

passages.original: Did he before?”
passages.vernacular: 佢之前係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他之前是嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, he did.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是。

passages.original: But I, like a fool, never thought.
passages.vernacular: 但我像個傻瓜,冇想到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我像個傻瓜,沒想到。

passages.original: Oh, this is bully, you know.
passages.vernacular: 哦,呢太棒喇,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,這太棒了,你知道。

passages.original: Now who can he mean?”
passages.vernacular: 而家佢指嘅係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他指的是誰?」

passages.original: The howling stopped.
passages.vernacular: 嚎叫停止喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嚎叫停止了。

passages.original: Tom pricked up his ears.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆豎起耳朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆豎起耳朵。

passages.original: “Sh!
What’s that?” he whispered.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係乜嘢?」佢低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是什麼?」他低聲說。

passages.original: “Sounds like—like hogs grunting.
passages.vernacular: 「聽起嚟像——像豬哼哼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽起來像——像豬哼哼。

passages.original: No—it’s somebody snoring, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 不——係有人喺打鼾,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不——是有人在打鼾,湯姆。」

passages.original: “That is it!
passages.vernacular: 「就係嗰個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是那個!

passages.original: Where ’bouts is it, Huck?”
passages.vernacular: 喺邊度,哈克?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在哪裡,哈克?」

passages.original: “I bleeve it’s down at ’tother end.
passages.vernacular: 「我相信喺另一端。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信在另一端。

passages.original: Sounds so, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 無論如何聽起嚟係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何聽起來是。

passages.original: Pap used to sleep there, sometimes, ’long with the hogs, but laws bless you, he just lifts things when he snores.
passages.vernacular: 爸爸有時瞓喺嗰度,同豬一起,但天呀,佢一打鼾就把嘢抬起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸有時睡在那裡,同豬一起,但天哪,他一打鼾就把東西抬起來。

passages.original: Besides, I reckon he ain’t ever coming back to this town any more.”
passages.vernacular: 而且,我想佢永遠唔會再回呢個鎮喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,我想他永遠不會再回這個鎮了。」

passages.original: The spirit of adventure rose in the boys’ souls once more.
passages.vernacular: 冒險精神喺男孩哋嘅靈魂中又升起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冒險精神在男孩們的靈魂中又升起。

passages.original: “Hucky, do you das’t to go if I lead?”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,如果我帶頭,你敢去嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,如果我帶頭,你敢去嗎?」

passages.original: “I don’t like to, much.
passages.vernacular: 「我不太想去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不太想去。

passages.original: Tom, s’pose it’s Injun Joe!”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,假如係印第安喬呢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,假如是印第安喬呢!」

passages.original: Tom quailed.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆畏縮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆畏縮了。

passages.original: But presently the temptation rose up strong again and the boys agreed to try, with the understanding that they would take to their heels if the snoring stopped.
passages.vernacular: 但不久誘惑又強烈地升起,男孩哋同意試試,約定如果鼾聲停咗就拔腿就跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不久誘惑又強烈地升起,男孩們同意試試,約定如果鼾聲停了就拔腿就跑。

passages.original: So they went tiptoeing stealthily down, the one behind the other.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋踮住腳尖悄悄走下去,一個接一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們踮著腳尖悄悄走下去,一個接一個。

passages.original: When they had got to within five steps of the snorer, Tom stepped on a stick, and it broke with a sharp snap.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋走到離打鼾者只有五步時,湯姆踩到一根棍子,佢發出尖銳嘅啪嘅一聲斷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們走到離打鼾者只有五步時,湯姆踩到一根棍子,它發出尖銳的啪的一聲斷了。

passages.original: The man moaned, writhed a little, and his face came into the moonlight.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人呻吟,扭動咗一下,佢嘅臉進入咗月光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人呻吟,扭動了一下,他的臉進入了月光。

passages.original: It was Muff Potter.
passages.vernacular: 係馬夫·波特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是馬夫·波特。

passages.original: The boys’ hearts had stood still, and their hopes too, when the man moved, but their fears passed away now.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人動時,男孩哋嘅心停止咗跳動,佢哋嘅希望都係,但佢哋嘅恐懼而家消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人動時,男孩們的心停止了跳動,他們的希望也是,但他們的恐懼現在消失了。

passages.original: They tip-toed out, through the broken weather-boarding, and stopped at a little distance to exchange a parting word.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋踮住腳尖從破損嘅護牆板出去,喺一小段距離外停下嚟,交換臨別話語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們踮著腳尖從破損的護牆板出去,在一小段距離外停下來,交換臨別話語。

passages.original: That long, lugubrious howl rose on the night air again!
passages.vernacular: 嗰悠長淒厲嘅嚎叫又喺夜空中升起!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那悠長淒厲的嚎叫又在夜空中升起!

passages.original: They turned and saw the strange dog standing within a few feet of where Potter was lying, and facing Potter, with his nose pointing heavenward.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋轉身,睇到嗰條陌生狗站喺離波特躺住嘅地方幾呎以內,面對住波特,鼻子指向天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們轉身,看到那條陌生狗站在離波特躺著的地方幾呎以內,面對著波特,鼻子指向天空。

passages.original: “Oh, geeminy, it’s him!” exclaimed both boys, in a breath.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,天呀,係佢!」兩個男孩同時喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,天哪,是他!」兩個男孩同時喊道。
