passages.original: “Say, Tom—they say a stray dog come howling around Johnny Miller’s house, ’bout midnight, as much as two weeks ago; and a whippoorwill come in and lit on the banisters and sung, the very same evening; and there ain’t anybody dead there yet.”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,湯姆——佢哋講兩個星期前大約午夜時,一條流浪狗嚎叫住嚟到強尼·米勒家周圍;一隻夜鷹同一天晚上進嚟落喺欄杆上唱歌;嗰度仲冇人死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,湯姆——他們說兩個星期前大約午夜時,一條流浪狗嚎叫著來到強尼·米勒家周圍;一隻夜鷹同一天晚上進來落在欄杆上唱歌;那裡還沒有人死。」

passages.original: “Well, I know that.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我知道。

passages.original: And suppose there ain’t.
passages.vernacular: 假設冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假設沒有。

passages.original: Didn’t Gracie Miller fall in the kitchen fire and burn herself terrible the very next Saturday?”
passages.vernacular: 格雷西·米勒唔係下個星期六掉進廚房火裡把自己燒傷得好厲害嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格雷西·米勒不是下個星期六掉進廚房火裡把自己燒傷得很厲害嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, but she ain’t dead.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,但佢冇死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,但她沒死。

passages.original: And what’s more, she’s getting better, too.”
passages.vernacular: 而且,佢仲喺好轉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,她還在好轉。」

passages.original: “All right, you wait and see.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,你等住瞧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,你等著瞧。

passages.original: She’s a goner, just as dead sure as Muff Potter’s a goner.
passages.vernacular: 佢完喇,同馬夫·波特完咗一樣肯定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她完了,和馬夫·波特完了一樣肯定。

passages.original: That’s what the niggers say, and they know all about these kind of things, Huck.”
passages.vernacular: 黑人哋咁講,佢哋對呢類事情乜嘢都知道,哈克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑人們這麼說,他們對這類事情什麼都知道,哈克。」

passages.original: Then they separated, cogitating.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋分手喇,各自思索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們分手了,各自思索。

passages.original: When Tom crept in at his bedroom window the night was almost spent.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆爬進臥室窗子時,夜幾乎過完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆爬進臥室窗子時,夜幾乎過完了。

passages.original: He undressed with excessive caution, and fell asleep congratulating himself that nobody knew of his escapade.
passages.vernacular: 佢極其小心地脫咗衣服,瞓住喇,慶幸冇人知道佢嘅出走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他極其小心地脫了衣服,睡著了,慶幸沒有人知道他的出走。

passages.original: He was not aware that the gently-snoring Sid was awake, and had been so for an hour.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔知道輕輕打鼾嘅希德係醒住嘅,而且已經醒咗一個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不知道輕輕打鼾的希德是醒著的,而且已經醒了一個小時。

passages.original: When Tom awoke, Sid was dressed and gone.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆醒嚟時,希德已穿好衣服走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆醒來時,希德已穿好衣服走了。

passages.original: There was a late look in the light, a late sense in the atmosphere.
passages.vernacular: 光線有點晚嘅樣子,空氣有種晚嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 光線有點晚的樣子,空氣有種晚的感覺。

passages.original: He was startled.
passages.vernacular: 佢食咗一驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他吃了一驚。

passages.original: Why had he not been called—persecuted till he was up, as usual?
passages.vernacular: 點解冇叫佢——像往常一樣迫害佢起床?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼沒有叫他——像往常一樣迫害他起床?

passages.original: The thought filled him with bodings.
passages.vernacular: 呢個念頭使佢充滿不祥嘅預感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個念頭使他充滿不祥的預感。

passages.original: Within five minutes he was dressed and down-stairs, feeling sore and drowsy.
passages.vernacular: 五分鐘內佢穿好衣服下咗樓,覺得痛楚同昏沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 五分鐘內他穿好衣服下了樓,覺得痛楚和昏沉。

passages.original: The family were still at table, but they had finished breakfast.
passages.vernacular: 家人仲喺桌旁,但已食完早餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 家人還在桌旁,但已吃完早餐。

passages.original: There was no voice of rebuke; but there were averted eyes; there was a silence and an air of solemnity that struck a chill to the culprit’s heart.
passages.vernacular: 冇責備嘅聲音;但有避開嘅眼睛;一種沉默同嚴肅嘅氣氛,使罪犯嘅心感到一陣寒意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有責備的聲音;但有避開的眼睛;一種沉默和嚴肅的氣氛,使罪犯的心感到一陣寒意。

passages.original: He sat down and tried to seem gay, but it was up-hill work; it roused no smile, no response, and he lapsed into silence and let his heart sink down to the depths.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐下,試圖顯得快樂,但呢個係食力嘅工作;冇引起微笑,冇回應,佢陷入沉默,讓心沉入深處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐下,試圖顯得快樂,但這是吃力的工作;沒有引起微笑,沒有回應,他陷入沉默,讓心沉入深處。

passages.original: After breakfast his aunt took him aside, and Tom almost brightened in the hope that he was going to be flogged; but it was not so.
passages.vernacular: 早餐後佢姨媽把佢拉到一邊,湯姆幾乎高興起嚟,希望佢要被鞭打喇;但唔係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐後他姨媽把他拉到一邊,湯姆幾乎高興起來,希望他要被鞭打了;但不是這樣。

passages.original: His aunt wept over him and asked him how he could go and break her old heart so; and finally told him to go on, and ruin himself and bring her gray hairs with sorrow to the grave, for it was no use for her to try any more.
passages.vernacular: 佢姨媽對佢哭泣,問佢點能咁樣傷佢嘅老心;最後告訴佢去吧,去毀掉自己,讓佢嘅白髮帶住悲傷進墳墓,因為佢再試都冇用喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他姨媽對他哭泣,問他怎麼能這樣傷她的老心;最後告訴他去吧,去毀掉自己,讓她的白髮帶著悲傷進墳墓,因為她再試也沒有用了。

passages.original: This was worse than a thousand whippings, and Tom’s heart was sorer now than his body.
passages.vernacular: 呢比一千次鞭打仲糟,湯姆嘅心而家比佢嘅身體更痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這比一千次鞭打還糟,湯姆的心現在比他的身體更痛。

passages.original: He cried, he pleaded for forgiveness, promised to reform over and over again, and then received his dismissal, feeling that he had won but an imperfect forgiveness and established but a feeble confidence.
passages.vernacular: 佢哭喇,佢懇求原諒,一遍又一遍地承諾改過,然後得到佢嘅遣散,覺得自己只贏得咗不完全嘅原諒,建立咗微弱嘅信任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他哭了,他懇求原諒,一遍又一遍地承諾改過,然後得到他的遣散,覺得自己只贏得了不完全的原諒,建立了微弱的信任。

passages.original: He left the presence too miserable to even feel revengeful toward Sid; and so the latter’s prompt retreat through the back gate was unnecessary.
passages.vernacular: 佢離開佢嘅面前,太悲慘喇,甚至不覺得要報復希德;所以後者從後門迅速撤退係唔使要嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他離開她的面前,太悲慘了,甚至不覺得要報復希德;所以後者從後門迅速撤退是不必要的。

passages.original: He moped to school gloomy and sad, and took his flogging, along with Joe Harper, for playing hookey the day before, with the air of one whose heart was busy with heavier woes and wholly dead to trifles.
passages.vernacular: 佢悶悶不樂、悲傷地走去學校,同喬·哈珀一起因為前一天逃學挨咗鞭打,神態像一個心思忙於更重嘅悲痛、對瑣事完全死心嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他悶悶不樂、悲傷地走去學校,和喬·哈珀一起因為前一天逃學挨了鞭打,神態像一個心思忙於更重的悲痛、對瑣事完全死心的人。

passages.original: Then he betook himself to his seat, rested his elbows on his desk and his jaws in his hands, and stared at the wall with the stony stare of suffering that has reached the limit and can no further go.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢走到座位上,手肘放喺桌上,下巴放喺手裡,以苦難已達極限、無法再進一步嘅石頭般嘅凝視盯住牆壁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他走到座位上,手肘放在桌上,下巴放在手裡,以苦難已達極限、無法再進一步的石頭般的凝視盯著牆壁。

passages.original: His elbow was pressing against some hard substance.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅手肘壓喺某個硬嘢上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的手肘壓在某個硬東西上。

passages.original: After a long time he slowly and sadly changed his position, and took up this object with a sigh.
passages.vernacular: 過咗好久,佢緩慢而悲傷地改變姿勢,歎住氣攞起呢個物件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了很久,他緩慢而悲傷地改變姿勢,歎著氣拿起這個物件。

passages.original: It was in a paper.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺一張紙裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它在一張紙裡。

passages.original: He unrolled it.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢打開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把它打開。

passages.original: A long, lingering, colossal sigh followed, and his heart broke.
passages.vernacular: 隨之係一聲長長嘅、持續嘅、巨大嘅歎息,佢嘅心碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨之是一聲長長的、持續的、巨大的歎息,他的心碎了。

passages.original: It was his brass andiron knob!
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係佢嘅黃銅柴架球!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是他的黃銅柴架球!

passages.original: This final feather broke the camel’s back.
passages.vernacular: 呢個最後一根羽毛壓斷咗駱駝嘅背。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這最後一根羽毛壓斷了駱駝的背。

chapters.title: Chapter XI: Muff Potter Comes Himself 第十一章:馬夫·波特自己來了

passages.original: CH Close upon the hour of noon the whole village was suddenly electrified with the ghastly news.
passages.vernacular: 臨近正午,整個村子突然被可怕嘅消息震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 臨近正午,整個村子突然被可怕的消息震驚。

passages.original: No need of the as yet un-dreamed-of telegraph; the tale flew from man to man, from group to group, from house to house, with little less than telegraphic speed.
passages.vernacular: 不需要當時仲想唔到嘅電報;消息從人傳到人,從一群傳到另一群,從一戶傳到另一戶,速度幾乎同電報一樣快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不需要當時還想不到的電報;消息從人傳到人,從一群傳到另一群,從一戶傳到另一戶,速度幾乎和電報一樣快。

passages.original: Of course the schoolmaster gave holiday for that afternoon; the town would have thought strangely of him if he had not.
passages.vernacular: 當然校長嗰天下午放咗假;如果佢不放,鎮上會覺得佢好奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然校長那天下午放了假;如果他不放,鎮上會覺得他很奇怪。

passages.original: A gory knife had been found close to the murdered man, and it had been recognized by somebody as belonging to Muff Potter—so the story ran.
passages.vernacular: 喺被謀殺嘅人身邊發現咗一把血淋淋嘅刀,並被某人認出係屬於馬夫·波特嘅——故事係咁樣傳嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在被謀殺的人身邊發現了一把血淋淋的刀,並被某人認出是屬於馬夫·波特的——故事是這樣傳的。

passages.original: And it was said that a belated citizen had come upon Potter washing himself in the “branch” about one or two o’clock in the morning, and that Potter had at once sneaked off—suspicious circumstances, especially the washing which was not a habit with Potter.
passages.vernacular: 仲有人講,一個遲歸嘅公民喺早晨一兩點撞見波特喺「支流」裡洗澡,波特立即溜走喇——可疑嘅情況,尤其係洗澡,呢唔係波特嘅習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有人說,一個遲歸的公民在早晨一兩點撞見波特在「支流」裡洗澡,波特立即溜走了——可疑的情況,尤其是洗澡,這不是波特的習慣。

passages.original: It was also said that the town had been ransacked for this “murderer” (the public are not slow in the matter of sifting evidence and arriving at a verdict), but that he could not be found.
passages.vernacular: 仲有人講,全鎮都為呢個「兇手」被搜查過(公眾喺篩選證據同得出判決方面並不遲緩),但找唔到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有人說,全鎮都為這個「兇手」被搜查過(公眾在篩選證據和得出判決方面並不遲緩),但找不到他。

passages.original: Horsemen had departed down all the roads in every direction, and the Sheriff “was confident” that he would be captured before night.
passages.vernacular: 騎馬嘅人已沿住所有道路向各個方向出發,郡長「有信心」佢會喺天黑前被捕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 騎馬的人已沿著所有道路向各個方向出發,郡長「有信心」他會在天黑前被捕。

passages.original: All the town was drifting toward the graveyard.
passages.vernacular: 全鎮嘅人都朝墳場湧去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全鎮的人都朝墳場湧去。

passages.original: Tom’s heartbreak vanished and he joined the procession, not because he would not a thousand times rather go anywhere else, but because an awful, unaccountable fascination drew him on.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅傷心消失喇,佢加入咗呢支隊伍,唔係因為佢唔係千百倍地寧願去別嘅任何地方,而係因為一種可怕嘅、無法解釋嘅魔力把佢吸引過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的傷心消失了,他加入了這支隊伍,不是因為他不是千百倍地寧願去別的任何地方,而是因為一種可怕的、無法解釋的魔力把他吸引過去。

passages.original: Arrived at the dreadful place, he wormed his small body through the crowd and saw the dismal spectacle.
passages.vernacular: 到咗可怕嘅地方,佢把小小嘅身體從人群中擠過去,睇到咗淒慘嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到了可怕的地方,他把小小的身體從人群中擠過去,看到了淒慘的景象。

passages.original: It seemed to him an age since he was there before.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得離佢上次喺呢度已經過咗一個世紀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他覺得離他上次在這裡已經過了一個世紀。

passages.original: Somebody pinched his arm.
passages.vernacular: 有人捏咗佢嘅手臂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人捏了他的手臂。

passages.original: He turned, and his eyes met Huckleberry’s.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉身,眼睛遇到咗哈克貝利嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他轉身,眼睛遇到了哈克貝利的。

passages.original: Then both looked elsewhere at once, and wondered if anybody had noticed anything in their mutual glance.
passages.vernacular: 然後兩人即刻睇向別處,想知道有冇人從佢哋互相嘅一瞥中察覺到乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後兩人立刻看向別處,想知道有沒有人從他們互相的一瞥中察覺到什麼。

passages.original: But everybody was talking, and intent upon the grisly spectacle before them.
passages.vernacular: 但每個人都喺講話,專注於佢哋面前嘅可怕景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但每個人都在說話,專注於他們面前的可怕景象。

passages.original: “Poor fellow!”
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的人!」

passages.original: “Poor young fellow!”
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅年輕人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的年輕人!」

passages.original: “This ought to be a lesson to grave robbers!”
passages.vernacular: 「呢應該畀盜墓者一個教訓!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這應該給盜墓者一個教訓!」

passages.original: “Muff Potter’ll hang for this if they catch him!”
passages.vernacular: 「如果抓到馬夫·波特,佢會為此被絞死!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果抓到馬夫·波特,他會為此被絞死!」

passages.original: This was the drift of remark; and the minister said, “It was a judgment; His hand is here.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係議論嘅大意;牧師講:「呢個係一個審判;祂嘅手喺呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是議論的大意;牧師說:「這是一個審判;祂的手在這裡。」

passages.original: Now Tom shivered from head to heel; for his eye fell upon the stolid face of Injun Joe.
passages.vernacular: 而家湯姆從頭到腳顫抖;因為佢嘅目光落喺印第安喬嗰張木然嘅臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在湯姆從頭到腳顫抖;因為他的目光落在印第安喬那張木然的臉上。

passages.original: At this moment the crowd began to sway and struggle, and voices shouted, “It’s him! it’s him! he’s coming himself!”
passages.vernacular: 呢陣人群開始搖擺掙扎,聲音喊道:「係佢!係佢!佢自己嚟喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時人群開始搖擺掙扎,聲音喊道:「是他!是他!他自己來了!」

passages.original: “Who?
passages.vernacular: 「邊個?

passages.original: Who?” from twenty voices.
passages.vernacular: 邊個?」二十個聲音喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰?」二十個聲音喊道。

passages.original: “Muff Potter!”
passages.vernacular: 「馬夫·波特!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬夫·波特!」

passages.original: “Hallo, he’s stopped!—Look out, he’s turning!
passages.vernacular: 「喂,佢停喇!——小心,佢喺轉身!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,他停了!——小心,他在轉身!

passages.original: Don’t let him get away!”
passages.vernacular: 唔好畀佢跑喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別讓他跑了!」

passages.original: People in the branches of the trees over Tom’s head said he wasn’t trying to get away—he only looked doubtful and perplexed.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆頭上樹枝裡嘅人講佢冇想跑——佢只係睇起嚟猶豫同困惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆頭上樹枝裡的人說他沒有想跑——他只是看起來猶豫和困惑。

passages.original: “Infernal impudence!” said a bystander; “wanted to come and take a quiet look at his work, I reckon—didn’t expect any company.”
passages.vernacular: 「該死嘅厚臉皮!」一個旁觀者講;「想嚟安靜地睇睇自己嘅傑作,我想——冇料到有人喺。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「該死的厚臉皮!」一個旁觀者說;「想來安靜地看看自己的傑作,我想——沒料到有人在。」

passages.original: The crowd fell apart, now, and the Sheriff came through, ostentatiously leading Potter by the arm.
passages.vernacular: 人群而家散開,郡長走過嚟,炫耀地拉住波特嘅手臂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人群現在散開,郡長走過來,炫耀地拉著波特的手臂。

passages.original: The poor fellow’s face was haggard, and his eyes showed the fear that was upon him.
passages.vernacular: 嗰可憐人嘅臉憔悴不堪,眼睛流露出佢嘅恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那可憐人的臉憔悴不堪,眼睛流露出他的恐懼。

passages.original: When he stood before the murdered man, he shook as with a palsy, and he put his face in his hands and burst into tears.
passages.vernacular: 佢站喺被謀殺嘅人面前時,像得咗癱瘓似嘅發抖,把臉埋喺手裡,淚如泉湧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他站在被謀殺的人面前時,像得了癱瘓似的發抖,把臉埋在手裡,淚如泉湧。

passages.original: “I didn’t do it, friends,” he sobbed; “’pon my word and honor I never done it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇做,朋友哋,」佢抽泣住講;「我以靈魂同榮譽發誓我從冇做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒做,朋友們,」他抽泣著說;「我以靈魂和榮譽發誓我從沒做。」

passages.original: “Who’s accused you?” shouted a voice.
passages.vernacular: 「邊個指控你喇?」一個聲音喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰指控你了?」一個聲音喊道。

passages.original: This shot seemed to carry home.
passages.vernacular: 呢一槍似乎擊中咗要害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一槍似乎擊中了要害。

passages.original: Potter lifted his face and looked around him with a pathetic hopelessness in his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 波特抬起臉,環視四周,眼睛裡帶住可憐嘅絕望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特抬起臉,環視四周,眼睛裡帶著可憐的絕望。

passages.original: He saw Injun Joe, and exclaimed:
passages.vernacular: 佢睇到印第安喬,喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看到印第安喬,喊道:

passages.original: “Oh, Injun Joe, you promised me you’d never—”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,印第安喬,你答應過我你永遠唔會——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,印第安喬,你答應過我你永遠不會——」

passages.original: “Is that your knife?” and it was thrust before him by the Sheriff.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係你嘅刀嗎?」郡長把佢遞到佢面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是你的刀嗎?」郡長把它遞到他面前。

passages.original: Potter would have fallen if they had not caught him and eased him to the ground.
passages.vernacular: 波特如果冇被扶住、緩緩放到地上,就會倒下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特如果沒有被扶住、緩緩放到地上,就會倒下。

passages.original: Then he said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他說:

passages.original: “Something told me ’t if I didn’t come back and get—” He shuddered; then waved his nerveless hand with a vanquished gesture and said, “Tell ’em, Joe, tell ’em—it ain’t any use any more.”
passages.vernacular: 「有乜嘢嘢告訴我,如果我不回嚟攞——」佢顫抖;然後無力嘅手以被擊敗嘅姿態揮咗揮,講:「告訴佢哋,喬,告訴佢哋——再都冇用喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有什麼東西告訴我,如果我不回來拿——」他顫抖;然後無力的手以被擊敗的姿態揮了揮,說:「告訴他們,喬,告訴他們——再也沒有用了。」

passages.original: Then Huckleberry and Tom stood dumb and staring, and heard the stony-hearted liar reel off his serene statement, they expecting every moment that the clear sky would deliver God’s lightnings upon his head, and wondering to see how long the stroke was delayed.
passages.vernacular: 然後哈克貝利同湯姆站住,啞口無言地瞪住,聽鐵石心腸嘅騙子滔滔不絕地講佢平靜嘅陳述,佢哋每一刻都期待晴朗嘅天空把上帝嘅閃電落喺佢頭上,並納悶呢一擊延遲咗多久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後哈克貝利和湯姆站著,啞口無言地瞪著,聽鐵石心腸的騙子滔滔不絕地說他平靜的陳述,他們每一刻都期待晴朗的天空把上帝的閃電落在他頭上,並納悶這一擊延遲了多久。

passages.original: And when he had finished and still stood alive and whole, their wavering impulse to break their oath and save the poor betrayed prisoner’s life faded and vanished away, for plainly this miscreant had sold himself to Satan and it would be fatal to meddle with the property of such a power as that.
passages.vernacular: 等佢講完,仍然活住,完好無損,佢哋動搖嘅想打破誓言、救呢可憐被出賣嘅囚犯性命嘅衝動消退消失喇,因為好明顯呢個惡棍已把自己賣畀咗撒旦,干預呢種力量嘅財產會係致命嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等他說完,仍然活著,完好無損,他們動搖的想打破誓言、救這可憐被出賣的囚犯性命的衝動消退消失了,因為很明顯這個惡棍已把自己賣給了撒旦,干預這種力量的財產會是致命的。

passages.original: “Why didn’t you leave?
passages.vernacular: 「你點解不走?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼不走?

passages.original: What did you want to come here for?” somebody said.
passages.vernacular: 你點解要到呢度嚟?」有人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼要到這裡來?」有人說。

passages.original: “I couldn’t help it—I couldn’t help it,” Potter moaned.
passages.vernacular: 「我控制不喇——我控制不喇,」波特呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我控制不了——我控制不了,」波特呻吟。

passages.original: “I wanted to run away, but I couldn’t seem to come anywhere but here.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想逃跑,但似乎邊度都去不喇,只能嚟呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想逃跑,但似乎哪裡也去不了,只能來這裡。」

passages.original: And he fell to sobbing again.
passages.vernacular: 佢又開始抽泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他又開始抽泣。

passages.original: Injun Joe repeated his statement, just as calmly, a few minutes afterward on the inquest, under oath; and the boys, seeing that the lightnings were still withheld, were confirmed in their belief that Joe had sold himself to the devil.
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘後,喺驗屍調查中,印第安喬宣誓後,同樣平靜地重複咗佢嘅陳述;男孩哋睇到閃電仍然被扣住,更加確信喬已把自己賣畀咗魔鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘後,在驗屍調查中,印第安喬宣誓後,同樣平靜地重複了他的陳述;男孩們看到閃電仍然被扣住,更加確信喬已把自己賣給了魔鬼。

passages.original: He was now become, to them, the most balefully interesting object they had ever looked upon, and they could not take their fascinated eyes from his face.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家對佢哋來講成咗佢哋見過嘅最邪惡有趣嘅對象,佢哋無法把著迷嘅眼睛從佢嘅臉上移開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在對他們來說成了他們見過的最邪惡有趣的對象,他們無法把著迷的眼睛從他的臉上移開。

passages.original: They inwardly resolved to watch him nights, when opportunity should offer, in the hope of getting a glimpse of his dread master.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋心裡決定,有機會時夜裡要監視佢,希望瞥見佢可怕嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們心裡決定,有機會時夜裡要監視他,希望瞥見他可怕的主人。

passages.original: Injun Joe helped to raise the body of the murdered man and put it in a wagon for removal; and it was whispered through the shuddering crowd that the wound bled a little!
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬幫忙抬起被謀殺者嘅屍體,把佢放進一輛馬車運走;戰慄嘅人群中有人低聲講傷口流咗啲血!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬幫忙抬起被謀殺者的屍體,把它放進一輛馬車運走;戰慄的人群中有人低聲說傷口流了一點血!

passages.original: The boys thought that this happy circumstance would turn suspicion in the right direction; but they were disappointed, for more than one villager remarked:
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋認為呢個幸運嘅情況會把懷疑轉向正確嘅方向;但佢哋失望喇,因為不止一個村民講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們認為這個幸運的情況會把懷疑轉向正確的方向;但他們失望了,因為不止一個村民說:

passages.original: “It was within three feet of Muff Potter when it done it.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢動手時離馬夫·波特只有三呎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他動手時離馬夫·波特只有三呎。」

passages.original: Tom’s fearful secret and gnawing conscience disturbed his sleep for as much as a week after this; and at breakfast one morning Sid said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆可怕嘅祕密同啃噬嘅良心擾亂咗佢之後整整一個星期嘅瞓眠;一天早晨食早餐時希德講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆可怕的祕密和啃噬的良心擾亂了他之後整整一個星期的睡眠;一天早晨吃早餐時希德說:

passages.original: “Tom, you pitch around and talk in your sleep so much that you keep me awake half the time.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,你瞓覺時翻嚟覆去、講夢話講得咁多,有一半時間吵得我瞓不住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,你睡覺時翻來覆去、說夢話說得那麼多,有一半時間吵得我睡不著。」

passages.original: Tom blanched and dropped his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆臉色發白,垂下眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆臉色發白,垂下眼睛。

passages.original: “It’s a bad sign,” said Aunt Polly, gravely.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個壞兆頭,」波莉姨媽嚴肅地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個壞兆頭,」波莉姨媽嚴肅地說。

passages.original: “What you got on your mind, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 「你心裡有乜嘢事,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你心裡有什麼事,湯姆?」

passages.original: “Nothing.
passages.vernacular: 「冇乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒什麼。

passages.original: Nothing ’t I know of.”
passages.vernacular: 我所知道嘅冇乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我所知道的沒什麼。」

passages.original: But the boy’s hand shook so that he spilled his coffee.
passages.vernacular: 但男孩嘅手發抖,灑咗咖啡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但男孩的手發抖,灑了咖啡。

passages.original: “And you do talk such stuff,” Sid said.
passages.vernacular: 「你講嘅真係咁樣嘅話,」希德講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說的真是這樣的話,」希德說。

passages.original: “Last night you said, ‘It’s blood, it’s blood, that’s what it is!’
passages.vernacular: 「琴晚你講:『係血,係血,就係呢個!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「昨晚你說:『是血,是血,就是這個!』

passages.original: You said that over and over.
passages.vernacular: 你一遍又一遍地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一遍又一遍地說。

passages.original: And you said, ‘Don’t torment me so—I’ll tell!’
passages.vernacular: 你仲講:『別咁樣折磨我——我要講喇!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還說:『別這樣折磨我——我要說了!』

passages.original: Tell what?
passages.vernacular: 講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說什麼?

passages.original: What is it you’ll tell?”
passages.vernacular: 你要講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要說什麼?」

passages.original: Everything was swimming before Tom.
passages.vernacular: 一切都喺湯姆面前打轉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切都在湯姆面前打轉。

passages.original: There is no telling what might have happened, now, but luckily the concern passed out of Aunt Polly’s face and she came to Tom’s relief without knowing it.
passages.vernacular: 而家難講會發生乜嘢,但幸運嘅係,憂慮從波莉姨媽臉上過去喇,佢喺唔知不覺中為湯姆解咗圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在難說會發生什麼,但幸運的是,憂慮從波莉姨媽臉上過去了,她在不知不覺中為湯姆解了圍。

passages.original: She said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說:

passages.original: “Sho!
It’s that dreadful murder.
passages.vernacular: 係嗰可怕嘅謀殺案。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是那可怕的謀殺案。

passages.original: I dream about it most every night myself.
passages.vernacular: 我自己幾乎每晚都夢見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己幾乎每晚都夢見。

passages.original: Sometimes I dream it’s me that done it.”
passages.vernacular: 有時我夢見係我幹嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時我夢見是我幹的。」

passages.original: Mary said she had been affected much the same way.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗講佢都受到差不多嘅影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗說她也受到差不多的影響。

passages.original: Sid seemed satisfied.
passages.vernacular: 希德似乎滿意喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德似乎滿意了。

passages.original: Tom got out of the presence as quick as he plausibly could, and after that he complained of toothache for a week, and tied up his jaws every night.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆盡可能自然地盡快離開咗佢哋面前,此後佢抱怨牙痛一星期,每晚把下巴綁起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆盡可能自然地盡快離開了她們面前,此後他抱怨牙痛一星期,每晚把下巴綁起來。

passages.original: He never knew that Sid lay nightly watching, and frequently slipped the bandage free and then leaned on his elbow listening a good while at a time, and afterward slipped the bandage back to its place again.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔知道希德每晚躺住監視,經常把繃帶弄鬆,然後用手肘支住聽好久,之後又把繃帶放回原位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不知道希德每晚躺著監視,經常把繃帶弄鬆,然後用手肘支著聽很久,之後又把繃帶放回原位。

passages.original: Tom’s distress of mind wore off gradually and the toothache grew irksome and was discarded.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅心理痛苦逐漸消退,牙痛變得討厭,就放棄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的心理痛苦逐漸消退,牙痛變得討厭,就放棄了。

passages.original: If Sid really managed to make anything out of Tom’s disjointed mutterings, he kept it to himself.
passages.vernacular: 如果希德真嘅設法從湯姆斷斷續續嘅喃喃自語中弄明白咗乜嘢,佢都藏喺心裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果希德真的設法從湯姆斷斷續續的喃喃自語中弄明白了什麼,他也藏在心裡。

passages.original: It seemed to Tom that his schoolmates never would get done holding inquests on dead cats, and thus keeping his trouble present to his mind.
passages.vernacular: 喺湯姆睇來,佢嘅同學哋永遠唔會停止對死貓舉行驗屍調查,咁樣使佢嘅煩惱一直喺佢心裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在湯姆看來,他的同學們永遠不會停止對死貓舉行驗屍調查,這樣使他的煩惱一直在他心裡。

passages.original: Sid noticed that Tom never was coroner at one of these inquiries, though it had been his habit to take the lead in all new enterprises; he noticed, too, that Tom never acted as a witness—and that was strange; and Sid did not overlook the fact that Tom even showed a marked aversion to these inquests, and always avoided them when he could.
passages.vernacular: 希德注意到湯姆喺呢啲調查中從不當驗屍官,雖然佢習慣喺所有新事業中帶頭;佢仲注意到,湯姆從不做證人——呢個好奇怪;希德冇忽略,湯姆甚至對呢啲驗屍調查表現出明顯嘅反感,總是盡可能避開佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德注意到湯姆在這些調查中從不當驗屍官,雖然他習慣在所有新事業中帶頭;他還注意到,湯姆從不做證人——這很奇怪;希德沒有忽略,湯姆甚至對這些驗屍調查表現出明顯的反感,總是盡可能避開它們。

passages.original: Sid marvelled, but said nothing.
passages.vernacular: 希德感到驚奇,但乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德感到驚奇,但什麼也沒說。

passages.original: However, even inquests went out of vogue at last, and ceased to torture Tom’s conscience.
passages.vernacular: 不過,驗屍調查最終都過時喇,唔再折磨湯姆嘅良心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,驗屍調查最終也過時了,不再折磨湯姆的良心。

passages.original: Every day or two, during this time of sorrow, Tom watched his opportunity and went to the little grated jail-window and smuggled such small comforts through to the “murderer” as he could get hold of.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢段悲傷嘅時間裡,每隔一兩天,湯姆睇準機會,到小鐵窗嘅監獄窗邊,把佢能弄到嘅啲小小安慰品偷偷遞畀嗰個「兇手」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這段悲傷的時間裡,每隔一兩天,湯姆看準機會,到小鐵窗的監獄窗邊,把他能弄到的一些小小安慰品偷偷遞給那個「兇手」。

passages.original: The jail was a trifling little brick den that stood in a marsh at the edge of the village, and no guards were afforded for it; indeed, it was seldom occupied.
passages.vernacular: 監獄係一個微不足道嘅小磚屋,立喺村邊嘅沼澤地裡,冇安排睇守;其實佢好少被佔用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 監獄是一個微不足道的小磚屋,立在村邊的沼澤地裡,沒有安排看守;其實它很少被佔用。

passages.original: These offerings greatly helped to ease Tom’s conscience.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲禮物極大地幫助減輕咗湯姆嘅良心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些禮物極大地幫助減輕了湯姆的良心。

passages.original: The villagers had a strong desire to tar-and-feather Injun Joe and ride him on a rail, for body-snatching, but so formidable was his character that nobody could be found who was willing to take the lead in the matter, so it was dropped.
passages.vernacular: 村民哋強烈希望對印第安喬施以柏油羽毛刑並騎喺欄杆上遊街,因為佢盜屍,但佢嘅性格如此可怕,找唔到願意喺呢件事上帶頭嘅人,所以呢件事作罷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 村民們強烈希望對印第安喬施以柏油羽毛刑並騎在欄杆上遊街,因為他盜屍,但他的性格如此可怕,找不到願意在這件事上帶頭的人,所以這件事作罷了。

passages.original: He had been careful to begin both of his inquest-statements with the fight, without confessing the grave-robbery that preceded it; therefore it was deemed wisest not to try the case in the courts at present.
passages.vernacular: 佢小心地以打架開始佢兩次驗屍陳述,而不承認之前嘅盜墓;因此認為目前最明智嘅係不喺法院審理此案。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他小心地以打架開始他兩次驗屍陳述,而不承認之前的盜墓;因此認為目前最明智的是不在法院審理此案。

chapters.title: Chapter XII: Tom Shows his Generosity 第十二章:湯姆的慷慨

passages.original: CH One of the reasons why Tom’s mind had drifted away from its secret troubles was, that it had found a new and weighty matter to interest itself about.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅心思從佢嘅祕密煩惱中飄走嘅原因之一,係佢找到咗一件新嘅、重大嘅事情去關心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的心思從他的祕密煩惱中飄走的原因之一,是它找到了一件新的、重大的事情去關心。

passages.original: Becky Thatcher had stopped coming to school.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪·撒切爾唔再嚟上學喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪·撒切爾不再來上學了。

passages.original: Tom had struggled with his pride a few days, and tried to “whistle her down the wind,” but failed.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆同自己嘅自尊心掙扎咗幾天,試圖「隨風把佢吹走」,但失敗喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆與自己的自尊心掙扎了幾天,試圖「隨風把她吹走」,但失敗了。

passages.original: He began to find himself hanging around her father’s house, nights, and feeling very miserable.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始發現自己夜裡喺佢父親房子周圍徘徊,感到好悲慘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他開始發現自己夜裡在她父親房子周圍徘徊,感到非常悲慘。

passages.original: She was ill.
passages.vernacular: 佢病喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她病了。

passages.original: What if she should die!
passages.vernacular: 如果佢死咗點算!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她死了怎麼辦!

passages.original: There was distraction in the thought.
passages.vernacular: 呢個念頭使人發狂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個念頭使人發狂。

passages.original: He no longer took an interest in war, nor even in piracy.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔再對戰爭有興趣,甚至對海盜都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不再對戰爭有興趣,甚至對海盜也沒有。

passages.original: The charm of life was gone; there was nothing but dreariness left.
passages.vernacular: 生活嘅魅力消失喇;只剩下淒涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 生活的魅力消失了;只剩下淒涼。

passages.original: He put his hoop away, and his bat; there was no joy in them any more.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢嘅鐵環同球拍收起嚟;佢哋唔再有任何樂趣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把他的鐵環和球拍收起來;它們不再有任何樂趣了。

passages.original: His aunt was concerned.
passages.vernacular: 佢姨媽好擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他姨媽很擔心。

passages.original: She began to try all manner of remedies on him.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始對佢試各種各樣嘅療法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她開始對他試各種各樣的療法。

passages.original: She was one of those people who are infatuated with patent medicines and all new-fangled methods of producing health or mending it.
passages.vernacular: 佢係嗰種迷戀專利藥品同一切新奇嘅製造或恢復健康嘅方法嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是那種迷戀專利藥品和一切新奇的製造或恢復健康的方法的人。

passages.original: She was an inveterate experimenter in these things.
passages.vernacular: 佢係呢啲事嘅積習難改嘅實驗者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是這些事的積習難改的實驗者。

passages.original: When something fresh in this line came out she was in a fever, right away, to try it; not on herself, for she was never ailing, but on anybody else that came handy.
passages.vernacular: 當呢方面有新嘢出嚟,佢即刻發燒似嘅想試;唔係喺佢自己身上,因為佢從不生病,而係喺任何手邊嘅其他人身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當這方面有新東西出來,她馬上發燒似的想試;不是在她自己身上,因為她從不生病,而是在任何手邊的其他人身上。

passages.original: She was a subscriber for all the “Health” periodicals and phrenological frauds; and the solemn ignorance they were inflated with was breath to her nostrils.
passages.vernacular: 佢訂閱咗所有「健康」期刊同骨相學騙局;佢哋所鼓吹嘅莊嚴嘅無知,對佢就像鼻孔嘅呼吸一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她訂閱了所有「健康」期刊和骨相學騙局;它們所鼓吹的莊嚴的無知,對她就像鼻孔的呼吸一樣。

passages.original: All the “rot” they contained about ventilation, and how to go to bed, and how to get up, and what to eat, and what to drink, and how much exercise to take, and what frame of mind to keep one’s self in, and what sort of clothing to wear, was all gospel to her, and she never observed that her health-journals of the current month customarily upset everything they had recommended the month before.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋所包含嘅所有關於通風、點樣上床、點樣起床、食乜嘢、飲乜嘢、做多少運動、保持乜嘢心態、穿乜嘢衣服嘅「廢話」,對佢來講都係福音,佢從冇注意到,佢當月嘅健康雜誌通常推翻咗上個月推薦嘅一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們所包含的所有關於通風、怎樣上床、怎樣起床、吃什麼、喝什麼、做多少運動、保持什麼心態、穿什麼衣服的「廢話」,對她來說都是福音,她從沒有注意到,她當月的健康雜誌通常推翻了上個月推薦的一切。

passages.original: She was as simple-hearted and honest as the day was long, and so she was an easy victim.
passages.vernacular: 佢像白晝一樣長地單純、誠實,所以佢係個容易上當嘅受害者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她像白晝一樣長地單純、誠實,所以她是個容易上當的受害者。

passages.original: She gathered together her quack periodicals and her quack medicines, and thus armed with death, went about on her pale horse, metaphorically speaking, with “hell following after.”
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢嘅江湖期刊同江湖藥品聚集喺一起,咁樣帶住死亡嘅武裝,騎住佢嘅灰白馬到處走,象徵性地講,「陰間跟喺後面」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把她的江湖期刊和江湖藥品聚集在一起,這樣帶著死亡的武裝,騎著她的灰白馬到處走,象徵性地說,「陰間跟在後面」。

passages.original: But she never suspected that she was not an angel of healing and the balm of Gilead in disguise, to the suffering neighbors.
passages.vernacular: 但佢從冇懷疑過佢唔係對受苦鄰居哋嘅治癒天使同基列嘅香膏嘅化身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她從沒懷疑過她不是對受苦鄰居們的治癒天使和基列的香膏的化身。

passages.original: The water treatment was new, now, and Tom’s low condition was a windfall to her.
passages.vernacular: 水療法而家係新嘅,湯姆嘅低落狀態對佢係意外之財。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 水療法現在是新的,湯姆的低落狀態對她是意外之財。

passages.original: She had him out at daylight every morning, stood him up in the wood-shed and drowned him with a deluge of cold water; then she scrubbed him down with a towel like a file, and so brought him to; then she rolled him up in a wet sheet and put him away under blankets till she sweated his soul clean and “the yellow stains of it came through his pores”—as Tom said.
passages.vernacular: 佢每天天一亮就把佢帶出嚟,讓佢站喺柴棚裡,用一陣洪水般嘅冷水淹沒佢;然後用像銼刀一樣嘅毛巾把佢擦下嚟,咁樣使佢醒過嚟;然後把佢捲喺一張濕床單裡,放喺毯子下,直到把佢嘅靈魂汗洗乾淨,「佢嘅黃色污漬從佢嘅毛孔裡透出嚟」——如湯姆所講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她每天天一亮就把他帶出來,讓他站在柴棚裡,用一陣洪水般的冷水淹沒他;然後用像銼刀一樣的毛巾把他擦下來,這樣使他醒過來;然後把他捲在一張濕床單裡,放在毯子下,直到把他的靈魂汗洗乾淨,「它的黃色污漬從他的毛孔裡透出來」——如湯姆所說。

passages.original: Yet notwithstanding all this, the boy grew more and more melancholy and pale and dejected.
passages.vernacular: 然而儘管呢一切,男孩變得越嚟越憂鬱、蒼白、沮喪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而儘管這一切,男孩變得越來越憂鬱、蒼白、沮喪。

passages.original: She added hot baths, sitz baths, shower baths, and plunges.
passages.vernacular: 佢加咗熱水浴、坐浴、淋浴同浸泡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她加了熱水浴、坐浴、淋浴和浸泡。

passages.original: The boy remained as dismal as a hearse.
passages.vernacular: 男孩仍像靈車一樣淒涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩仍像靈車一樣淒涼。

passages.original: She began to assist the water with a slim oatmeal diet and blister-plasters.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始用清淡嘅燕麥飲食同發泡膏幫助水療。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她開始用清淡的燕麥飲食和發泡膏幫助水療。

passages.original: She calculated his capacity as she would a jug’s, and filled him up every day with quack cure-alls.
passages.vernacular: 佢像計算一個壺嘅容量一樣計算佢嘅容量,每天用江湖包治百病嘅藥把佢灌滿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她像計算一個壺的容量一樣計算他的容量,每天用江湖包治百病的藥把他灌滿。

passages.original: Tom had become indifferent to persecution by this time.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆此時已對迫害無動於衷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆此時已對迫害無動於衷。

passages.original: This phase filled the old lady’s heart with consternation.
passages.vernacular: 呢個階段使老太太嘅心充滿驚愕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個階段使老太太的心充滿驚愕。

passages.original: This indifference must be broken up at any cost.
passages.vernacular: 呢種冷漠必須不惜代價打破。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種冷漠必須不惜代價打破。

passages.original: Now she heard of Pain-killer for the first time.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢第一次聽講咗「痛靈」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在她第一次聽說了「痛靈」。

passages.original: She ordered a lot at once.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻訂咗好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她馬上訂了很多。

passages.original: She tasted it and was filled with gratitude.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚐咗嚐,充滿感激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她嚐了嚐,充滿感激。

passages.original: It was simply fire in a liquid form.
passages.vernacular: 佢簡直係液體形式嘅火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它簡直是液體形式的火。

passages.original: She dropped the water treatment and everything else, and pinned her faith to Pain-killer.
passages.vernacular: 佢放棄咗水療法同其他一切,把信心寄託喺「痛靈」上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她放棄了水療法和其他一切,把信心寄託在「痛靈」上。

passages.original: She gave Tom a teaspoonful and watched with the deepest anxiety for the result.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀咗湯姆一茶匙,懷住最深嘅焦慮睇住結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她給了湯姆一茶匙,懷著最深的焦慮看著結果。

passages.original: Her troubles were instantly at rest, her soul at peace again; for the “indifference” was broken up.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅煩惱立即平息,佢嘅靈魂再次平靜;因為「冷漠」被打破喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的煩惱立即平息,她的靈魂再次平靜;因為「冷漠」被打破了。

passages.original: The boy could not have shown a wilder, heartier interest, if she had built a fire under him.
passages.vernacular: 即使佢喺佢下面生一堆火,男孩都唔可能表現出更狂野、更熱切嘅興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使她在他下面生一堆火,男孩也不可能表現出更狂野、更熱切的興趣。

passages.original: Tom felt that it was time to wake up; this sort of life might be romantic enough, in his blighted condition, but it was getting to have too little sentiment and too much distracting variety about it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆覺得係該醒嚟嘅時候喇;呢種生活喺佢受挫嘅狀態下或者夠浪漫,但佢漸漸變得情感太少、令人分心嘅變化太多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆覺得是該醒來的時候了;這種生活在他受挫的狀態下也許夠浪漫,但它漸漸變得情感太少、令人分心的變化太多。

passages.original: So he thought over various plans for relief, and finally hit upon that of professing to be fond of Pain-killer.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢想咗各種解脫嘅計畫,最後想到咗假裝鍾意「痛靈」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他想了各種解脫的計畫,最後想到了假裝喜歡「痛靈」。

passages.original: He asked for it so often that he became a nuisance, and his aunt ended by telling him to help himself and quit bothering her.
passages.vernacular: 佢咁頻繁地要,以致成咗討厭鬼,佢姨媽最後告訴佢自己攞,唔好再煩佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他那麼頻繁地要,以致成了討厭鬼,他姨媽最後告訴他自己拿,別再煩她。

passages.original: If it had been Sid, she would have had no misgivings to alloy her delight; but since it was Tom, she watched the bottle clandestinely.
passages.vernacular: 如果係希德,佢唔會有任何疑慮嚟摻雜佢嘅喜悅;但因為係湯姆,佢暗中睇住嗰個瓶子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是希德,她不會有任何疑慮來摻雜她的喜悅;但因為是湯姆,她暗中看著那個瓶子。

passages.original: She found that the medicine did really diminish, but it did not occur to her that the boy was mending the health of a crack in the sitting-room floor with it.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現藥確實在減少,但佢冇想到男孩喺用佢修補客廳地板上一條裂縫嘅健康。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她發現藥確實在減少,但她沒想到男孩在用它修補客廳地板上一條裂縫的健康。

passages.original: One day Tom was in the act of dosing the crack when his aunt’s yellow cat came along, purring, eyeing the teaspoon avariciously, and begging for a taste.
passages.vernacular: 一天,湯姆正在畀裂縫服藥時,佢姨媽嘅黃貓走過嚟,呼嚕住,貪婪地睇住茶匙,求嚐一口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一天,湯姆正在給裂縫服藥時,他姨媽的黃貓走過來,呼嚕著,貪婪地看著茶匙,求嚐一口。

passages.original: Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說:

passages.original: “Don’t ask for it unless you want it, Peter.”
passages.vernacular: 「除非你想要,否則別要,彼得。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「除非你想要,否則別要,彼得。」

passages.original: But Peter signified that he did want it.
passages.vernacular: 但彼得表示牠確實想要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但彼得表示牠確實想要。

passages.original: “You better make sure.”
passages.vernacular: 「你最好確定。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你最好確定。」

passages.original: Peter was sure.
passages.vernacular: 彼得確定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得確定。

passages.original: “Now you’ve asked for it, and I’ll give it to you, because there ain’t anything mean about me; but if you find you don’t like it, you mustn’t blame anybody but your own self.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家你要喇,我就畀你,因為我呢個人冇乜嘢小氣;但如果你發現你不鍾意,你唔能夠怪任何人,只能怪你自己。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你要了,我就給你,因為我這個人沒有什麼小氣;但如果你發現你不喜歡,你不能怪任何人,只能怪你自己。」

passages.original: Peter was agreeable.
passages.vernacular: 彼得同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得同意。

passages.original: So Tom pried his mouth open and poured down the Pain-killer.
passages.vernacular: 於是湯姆撬開牠嘅嘴,灌下咗「痛靈」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是湯姆撬開牠的嘴,灌下了「痛靈」。

passages.original: Peter sprang a couple of yards in the air, and then delivered a war-whoop and set off round and round the room, banging against furniture, upsetting flower-pots, and making general havoc.
passages.vernacular: 彼得向空中跳咗兩碼,然後發出一聲戰吼,繞住房間一圈又一圈地跑,撞到傢俱、打翻花盆、造成全面破壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彼得向空中跳了兩碼,然後發出一聲戰吼,繞著房間一圈又一圈地跑,撞到傢俱、打翻花盆、造成全面破壞。

passages.original: Next he rose on his hind feet and pranced around, in a frenzy of enjoyment, with his head over his shoulder and his voice proclaiming his unappeasable happiness.
passages.vernacular: 接住牠用後腿站起嚟蹦跳,處喺享受嘅狂亂中,頭轉到肩上,聲音宣告住無法平息嘅快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著牠用後腿站起來蹦跳,處在享受的狂亂中,頭轉到肩上,聲音宣告著無法平息的快樂。

passages.original: Then he went tearing around the house again spreading chaos and destruction in his path.
passages.vernacular: 然後牠又撕扯住繞房子跑,喺路上散布混亂同破壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後牠又撕扯著繞房子跑,在路上散布混亂和破壞。

passages.original: Aunt Polly entered in time to see him throw a few double summersets, deliver a final mighty hurrah, and sail through the open window, carrying the rest of the flower-pots with him.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽進嚟時,剛好睇到牠翻咗幾個雙跟斗,發出最後一聲響亮嘅歡呼,穿過敞開嘅窗子飛出去,把其餘嘅花盆都帶走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽進來時,剛好看到牠翻了幾個雙跟斗,發出最後一聲響亮的歡呼,穿過敞開的窗子飛出去,把其餘的花盆也帶走了。

passages.original: The old lady stood petrified with astonishment, peering over her glasses; Tom lay on the floor expiring with laughter.
passages.vernacular: 老太太驚訝得呆若木雞,從眼鏡上方窺視;湯姆躺喺地板上笑得快斷氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太驚訝得呆若木雞,從眼鏡上方窺視;湯姆躺在地板上笑得快斷氣。

passages.original: “Tom, what on earth ails that cat?”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,嗰隻貓到底點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,那隻貓到底怎麼了?」

passages.original: “I don’t know, aunt,” gasped the boy.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,姨媽,」男孩喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,姨媽,」男孩喘著氣說。

passages.original: “Why, I never see anything like it.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我從冇見過咁樣嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我從沒見過這樣的。

passages.original: What did make him act so?”
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢讓牠咁樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼讓牠這樣?」

passages.original: “Deed I don’t know, Aunt Polly; cats always act so when they’re having a good time.”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅我唔知道,波莉姨媽;貓玩得開心時總是咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的我不知道,波莉姨媽;貓玩得開心時總是這樣。」

passages.original: “They do, do they?”
passages.vernacular: 「牠哋係咁樣,係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「牠們是這樣,是嗎?」

passages.original: There was something in the tone that made Tom apprehensive.
passages.vernacular: 語氣裡有種嘢使湯姆擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 語氣裡有種東西使湯姆擔心。

passages.original: “Yes’m.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,姨媽。

passages.original: That is, I believe they do.”
passages.vernacular: 就係講,我相信係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是說,我相信是。」

passages.original: “You do?”
passages.vernacular: 「你相信?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你相信?」

passages.original: “Yes’m.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,姨媽。」

passages.original: The old lady was bending down, Tom watching, with interest emphasized by anxiety.
passages.vernacular: 老太太正彎下腰,湯姆睇住,興趣因焦慮而加強。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太正彎下腰,湯姆看著,興趣因焦慮而加強。

passages.original: Too late he divined her “drift.”
passages.vernacular: 佢太遲才猜到佢嘅「用意」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他太遲才猜到她的「用意」。

passages.original: The handle of the telltale tea-spoon was visible under the bed-valance.
passages.vernacular: 揭穿底細嘅茶匙柄從床幔下露出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 揭穿底細的茶匙柄從床幔下露出來。

passages.original: Aunt Polly took it, held it up.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽攞起佢,舉起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽拿起它,舉起來。

passages.original: Tom winced, and dropped his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆畏縮喇,垂下眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆畏縮了,垂下眼睛。

passages.original: Aunt Polly raised him by the usual handle—his ear—and cracked his head soundly with her thimble.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽用通常嘅把手——佢嘅耳朵——把佢提起嚟,用頂針狠狠敲佢嘅頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽用通常的把手——他的耳朵——把他提起來,用頂針狠狠敲他的頭。

passages.original: “Now, sir, what did you want to treat that poor dumb beast so, for?”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,先生,你點解要嗰樣對待嗰可憐嘅啞巴動物?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,先生,你為什麼要那樣對待那可憐的啞巴動物?」

passages.original: “I done it out of pity for him—because he hadn’t any aunt.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係出於對牠嘅憐憫——因為牠冇姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是出於對牠的憐憫——因為牠沒有姨媽。」

passages.original: “Hadn’t any aunt!—you numskull.
passages.vernacular: 「冇姨媽!——你呢笨蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有姨媽!——你這笨蛋。

passages.original: What has that got to do with it?”
passages.vernacular: 呢同佢有乜嘢關係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這同它有什麼關係?」

passages.original: “Heaps.
passages.vernacular: 「關係大住呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「關係大著呢。

passages.original: Because if he’d had one she’d a burnt him out herself!
passages.vernacular: 因為如果牠有一個,佢自己會把牠燒掉嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果牠有一個,她自己會把牠燒掉的!

passages.original: She’d a roasted his bowels out of him ’thout any more feeling than if he was a human!”
passages.vernacular: 佢會把牠嘅腸子烤出嚟,毫無感覺,好像牠係人一樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會把牠的腸子烤出來,毫無感覺,好像牠是人一樣!」

passages.original: Aunt Polly felt a sudden pang of remorse.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽突然感到一陣悔恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽突然感到一陣悔恨。

passages.original: This was putting the thing in a new light; what was cruelty to a cat might be cruelty to a boy, too.
passages.vernacular: 呢使事情有咗新嘅面貌;對貓殘忍,都可能係對男孩殘忍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使事情有了新的面貌;對貓殘忍,也可能是對男孩殘忍。

passages.original: She began to soften; she felt sorry.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始軟化;佢感到抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她開始軟化;她感到抱歉。

passages.original: Her eyes watered a little, and she put her hand on Tom’s head and said gently:
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛有點濕,佢把手放喺湯姆頭上,溫柔地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛有點濕,她把手放在湯姆頭上,溫柔地說:

passages.original: “I was meaning for the best, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「我係一番好意,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是一番好意,湯姆。

passages.original: And, Tom, it did do you good.”
passages.vernacular: 而且,湯姆,佢確實對你有好處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,湯姆,它確實對你有好處。」

passages.original: Tom looked up in her face with just a perceptible twinkle peeping through his gravity.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆抬頭睇住佢嘅臉,佢嘅嚴肅中只透出一絲可察覺嘅閃光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆抬頭看著她的臉,他的嚴肅中只透出一絲可察覺的閃光。

passages.original: “I know you was meaning for the best, aunty, and so was I with Peter.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道你係一番好意,姨媽,我對彼得都係一番好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道你是一番好意,姨媽,我對彼得也是一番好意。

passages.original: It done him good, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢對牠都有好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它對牠也有好處。

passages.original: I never see him get around so since—”
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見牠咁樣跑嚟跑去,自從——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見牠這樣跑來跑去,自從——」

passages.original: “Oh, go ’long with you, Tom, before you aggravate me again.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,走開吧,湯姆,趁你仲冇又惹我生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,走開吧,湯姆,趁你還沒又惹我生氣。

passages.original: And you try and see if you can’t be a good boy, for once, and you needn’t take any more medicine.”
passages.vernacular: 你試住睇睇能唔能夠乖一次,你就唔使再食藥喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你試著看看能不能乖一次,你就不用再吃藥了。」

passages.original: Tom reached school ahead of time.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆提前到咗學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆提前到了學校。

passages.original: It was noticed that this strange thing had been occurring every day latterly.
passages.vernacular: 人哋注意到,呢種奇怪嘅事最近每天都喺發生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們注意到,這種奇怪的事最近每天都在發生。

passages.original: And now, as usual of late, he hung about the gate of the schoolyard instead of playing with his comrades.
passages.vernacular: 而家,像最近一樣,佢喺校園門口閒逛,而唔係同夥伴玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,像最近一樣,他在校園門口閒逛,而不是同夥伴玩。

passages.original: He was sick, he said, and he looked it.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢病喇,睇起嚟都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他病了,看起來也是。

passages.original: He tried to seem to be looking everywhere but whither he really was looking—down the road.
passages.vernacular: 佢試圖顯得向各個地方睇,除咗佢真正睇嘅地方——路嘅盡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他試圖顯得向各個地方看,除了他真正看的地方——路的盡頭。

passages.original: Presently Jeff Thatcher hove in sight, and Tom’s face lighted; he gazed a moment, and then turned sorrowfully away.
passages.vernacular: 不久傑夫·撒切爾出而家視野中,湯姆嘅臉亮喇;佢睇咗一會兒,然後悲傷地轉開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久傑夫·撒切爾出現在視野中,湯姆的臉亮了;他看了一會兒,然後悲傷地轉開。

passages.original: When Jeff arrived, Tom accosted him; and “led up” warily to opportunities for remark about Becky, but the giddy lad never could see the bait.
passages.vernacular: 傑夫到達時,湯姆向佢搭話;並謹慎地「引導」出談論貝琪嘅機會,但呢個輕浮嘅小伙子始終睇不出誘餌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傑夫到達時,湯姆向他搭話;並謹慎地「引導」出談論貝琪的機會,但這個輕浮的小伙子始終看不出誘餌。

passages.original: Tom watched and watched, hoping whenever a frisking frock came in sight, and hating the owner of it as soon as he saw she was not the right one.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆睇咗又睇,每當一件活潑嘅裙子出而家視野中就抱希望,一睇到唔係嗰件就恨佢嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆看了又看,每當一件活潑的裙子出現在視野中就抱希望,一看到不是那件就恨它的主人。

passages.original: At last frocks ceased to appear, and he dropped hopelessly into the dumps; he entered the empty schoolhouse and sat down to suffer.
passages.vernacular: 最後裙子唔再出現,佢毫無希望地陷入沮喪;佢走進空蕩蕩嘅校舍,坐下嚟受苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後裙子不再出現,他毫無希望地陷入沮喪;他走進空蕩蕩的校舍,坐下來受苦。

passages.original: Then one more frock passed in at the gate, and Tom’s heart gave a great bound.
passages.vernacular: 然後又一件裙子從門口進嚟,湯姆嘅心大大地跳咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後又一件裙子從門口進來,湯姆的心大大地跳了一下。

passages.original: The next instant he was out, and “going on” like an Indian; yelling, laughing, chasing boys, jumping over the fence at risk of life and limb, throwing handsprings, standing on his head—doing all the heroic things he could conceive of, and keeping a furtive eye out, all the while, to see if Becky Thatcher was noticing.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻佢已經出去,像印第安人一樣「鬧」起嚟;大叫、大笑、追男孩、冒生命同四肢嘅危險跳過圍欄、翻筋斗、倒立——做一切佢能想到嘅英雄事跡,同時一直偷偷留意睇貝琪·撒切爾係咪注意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻他已經出去,像印第安人一樣「鬧」起來;大叫、大笑、追男孩、冒生命和四肢的危險跳過圍欄、翻筋斗、倒立——做一切他能想到的英雄事跡,同時一直偷偷留意看貝琪·撒切爾是否注意。

passages.original: But she seemed to be unconscious of it all; she never looked.
passages.vernacular: 但佢似乎對呢一切毫無意識;佢從不睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她似乎對這一切毫無意識;她從不看。

passages.original: Could it be possible that she was not aware that he was there?
passages.vernacular: 佢有可能唔知道佢喺嗰度嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有可能不知道他在那裡嗎?

passages.original: He carried his exploits to her immediate vicinity; came war-whooping around, snatched a boy’s cap, hurled it to the roof of the schoolhouse, broke through a group of boys, tumbling them in every direction, and fell sprawling, himself, under Becky’s nose, almost upsetting her—and she turned, with her nose in the air, and he heard her say: “Mf! some people think they’re mighty smart—always showing off!”
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢嘅功績帶到佢附近;戰吼住繞過嚟,搶咗一個男孩嘅帽子,把佢扔到校舍嘅屋頂上,衝破一群男孩,把佢哋撞向各個方向,自己四仰八叉地倒喺貝琪鼻子底下,幾乎撞翻佢——佢轉過身,鼻子朝天,佢聽到佢講:「哼!有些人以為自己好聰明——總是炫耀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把他的功績帶到她附近;戰吼著繞過來,搶了一個男孩的帽子,把它扔到校舍的屋頂上,衝破一群男孩,把他們撞向各個方向,自己四仰八叉地倒在貝琪鼻子底下,幾乎撞翻她——她轉過身,鼻子朝天,他聽到她說:「哼!有些人以為自己很聰明——總是炫耀!」

passages.original: Tom’s cheeks burned.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅臉頰發燙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的臉頰發燙。

passages.original: He gathered himself up and sneaked off, crushed and crestfallen.
passages.vernacular: 佢爬起嚟溜走喇,被壓垮,垂頭喪氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他爬起來溜走了,被壓垮,垂頭喪氣。

chapters.title: Chapter XIII: The Young Pirates 第十三章:年輕的海盜

passages.original: CH Tom’s mind was made up now.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆而家下定咗決心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆現在下定了決心。

passages.original: He was gloomy and desperate.
passages.vernacular: 佢陰鬱而絕望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他陰鬱而絕望。

passages.original: He was a forsaken, friendless boy, he said; nobody loved him; when they found out what they had driven him to, perhaps they would be sorry; he had tried to do right and get along, but they would not let him; since nothing would do them but to be rid of him, let it be so; and let them blame him for the consequences—why shouldn’t they?
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢係個被拋棄、冇朋友嘅男孩;冇人愛佢;等佢哋發現把佢逼成咗乜嘢樣子,或者佢哋會後悔;佢曾努力做對、相處融洽,但佢哋不讓佢;既然佢哋非要擺脫佢不可,就讓佢咁樣吧;讓佢哋為後果責怪佢吧——佢哋點解不呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他是個被拋棄、沒有朋友的男孩;沒有人愛他;等他們發現把他逼成了什麼樣子,也許他們會後悔;他曾努力做對、相處融洽,但他們不讓他;既然他們非要擺脫他不可,就讓它這樣吧;讓他們為後果責怪他吧——他們為什麼不呢?

passages.original: What right had the friendless to complain?
passages.vernacular: 冇朋友嘅人有乜嘢權利抱怨?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有朋友的人有什麼權利抱怨?

passages.original: Yes, they had forced him to it at last: he would lead a life of crime.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,佢哋終於逼佢走到呢一步喇:佢要過犯罪嘅生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,他們終於逼他走到這一步了:他要過犯罪的生活。

passages.original: There was no choice.
passages.vernacular: 冇選擇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有選擇。

passages.original: By this time he was far down Meadow Lane, and the bell for school to “take up” tinkled faintly upon his ear.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣佢已走到草地巷嘅盡頭,學校「開課」嘅鐘聲微弱地叮噹傳入佢嘅耳朵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時他已走到草地巷的盡頭,學校「開課」的鐘聲微弱地叮噹傳入他的耳朵。

passages.original: He sobbed, now, to think he should never, never hear that old familiar sound any more—it was very hard, but it was forced on him; since he was driven out into the cold world, he must submit—but he forgave them.
passages.vernacular: 想到佢再都、再都聽唔到嗰熟悉嘅老聲音,佢抽泣起嚟——呢個好難,但呢個係強加於佢嘅;既然佢被趕入寒冷嘅世界,佢必須服從——但佢原諒佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到他再也、再也聽不到那熟悉的老聲音,他抽泣起來——這很難,但這是強加於他的;既然他被趕入寒冷的世界,他必須服從——但他原諒他們。

passages.original: Then the sobs came thick and fast.
passages.vernacular: 然後抽泣又急又密地嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後抽泣又急又密地來了。

passages.original: Just at this point he met his soul’s sworn comrade, Joe Harper—hard-eyed, and with evidently a great and dismal purpose in his heart.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣佢遇到咗佢靈魂宣誓嘅夥伴喬·哈珀——眼神堅硬,心裡顯然有一個偉大而陰鬱嘅目的。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時他遇到了他靈魂宣誓的夥伴喬·哈珀——眼神堅硬,心裡顯然有一個偉大而陰鬱的目的。

passages.original: Plainly here were “two souls with but a single thought.”
passages.vernacular: 顯然呢度係「兩個靈魂,一個思想」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顯然這裡是「兩個靈魂,一個思想」。

passages.original: Tom, wiping his eyes with his sleeve, began to blubber out something about a resolution to escape from hard usage and lack of sympathy at home by roaming abroad into the great world never to return; and ended by hoping that Joe would not forget him.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆用袖子擦住眼睛,開始嗚咽住講咗啲關於下決心逃離家裡嘅虐待同缺乏同情,流浪到廣闊嘅世界,永不回嚟;最後希望喬唔會忘記佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆用袖子擦著眼睛,開始嗚咽著說了一些關於下決心逃離家裡的虐待和缺乏同情,流浪到廣闊的世界,永不回來;最後希望喬不會忘記他。

passages.original: But it transpired that this was a request which Joe had just been going to make of Tom, and had come to hunt him up for that purpose.
passages.vernacular: 但原來呢個係喬頭先正要向湯姆提出嘅請求,佢係為此嚟找佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但原來這是喬剛才正要向湯姆提出的請求,他是為此來找他的。

passages.original: His mother had whipped him for drinking some cream which he had never tasted and knew nothing about; it was plain that she was tired of him and wished him to go; if she felt that way, there was nothing for him to do but succumb; he hoped she would be happy, and never regret having driven her poor boy out into the unfeeling world to suffer and die.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅母親因為佢飲咗奶油而打咗佢,佢從冇嚐過,都一無所知;好明顯佢厭倦咗佢,希望佢走;如果佢咁覺得,佢除咗屈服無事可做;佢希望佢會快樂,永遠唔會後悔把佢可憐嘅細路趕入無情嘅世界去受苦同死去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的母親因為他喝了奶油而打了他,他從沒嚐過,也一無所知;很明顯她厭倦了他,希望他走;如果她那麼覺得,他除了屈服無事可做;他希望她會快樂,永遠不會後悔把她可憐的孩子趕入無情的世界去受苦和死去。

passages.original: As the two boys walked sorrowing along, they made a new compact to stand by each other and be brothers and never separate till death relieved them of their troubles.
passages.vernacular: 兩個男孩悲傷地一路走住,訂立咗一個新嘅盟約,互相支持、做兄弟,喺死亡解除佢哋嘅煩惱之前永不分離。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個男孩悲傷地一路走著,訂立了一個新的盟約,互相支持、做兄弟,在死亡解除他們的煩惱之前永不分離。

passages.original: Then they began to lay their plans.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋開始制定計畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們開始制定計畫。

passages.original: Joe was for being a hermit, and living on crusts in a remote cave, and dying, some time, of cold and want and grief; but after listening to Tom, he conceded that there were some conspicuous advantages about a life of crime, and so he consented to be a pirate.
passages.vernacular: 喬想當隱士,喺遙遠嘅山洞裡靠麵包皮活住,有朝一日死於寒冷、窮困同悲傷;但聽咗湯姆嘅話之後,佢承認犯罪生活有些顯著嘅好處,於是佢同意當海盜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬想當隱士,在遙遠的山洞裡靠麵包皮活著,有朝一日死於寒冷、窮困和悲傷;但聽了湯姆的話之後,他承認犯罪生活有些顯著的好處,於是他同意當海盜。

passages.original: Three miles below St. Petersburg, at a point where the Mississippi River was a trifle over a mile wide, there was a long, narrow, wooded island, with a shallow bar at the head of it, and this offered well as a rendezvous.
passages.vernacular: 喺聖彼得堡下游三英里處,密西西比河寬度略超過一英里嘅一個點上,有一座長長嘅、狹窄嘅、樹木繁茂嘅島,島頭有一道淺沙洲,呢作為會合地點好合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在聖彼得堡下游三英里處,密西西比河寬度略超過一英里的一個點上,有一座長長的、狹窄的、樹木繁茂的島,島頭有一道淺沙洲,這作為會合地點很合適。

passages.original: It was not inhabited; it lay far over toward the further shore, abreast a dense and almost wholly unpeopled forest.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇人居住;佢遠遠地躺喺對岸嗰邊,同一片茂密嘅、幾乎完全冇人煙嘅森林相對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它沒有人居住;它遠遠地躺在對岸那邊,與一片茂密的、幾乎完全沒有人煙的森林相對。

passages.original: So Jackson’s Island was chosen.
passages.vernacular: 於是選定咗傑克森島。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是選定了傑克森島。

passages.original: Who were to be the subjects of their piracies was a matter that did not occur to them.
passages.vernacular: 邊個將係佢哋劫掠嘅對象,係佢哋冇想到嘅問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰將是他們劫掠的對象,是他們沒有想到的問題。

passages.original: Then they hunted up Huckleberry Finn, and he joined them promptly, for all careers were one to him; he was indifferent.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋去找哈克貝利·費恩,佢即刻加入咗佢哋,因為所有職業對佢都一樣;佢無所謂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們去找哈克貝利·費恩,他馬上加入了他們,因為所有職業對他都一樣;他無所謂。

passages.original: They presently separated to meet at a lonely spot on the river-bank two miles above the village at the favorite hour—which was midnight.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋分開,約好喺午夜呢個最鍾意嘅時刻,喺村子上游兩英里河岸嘅一處荒涼地方會合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們分開,約好在午夜這個最喜歡的時刻,在村子上游兩英里河岸的一處荒涼地方會合。

passages.original: There was a small log raft there which they meant to capture.
passages.vernacular: 嗰度有一個小原木筏,佢哋打算奪取佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡有一個小原木筏,他們打算奪取它。

passages.original: Each would bring hooks and lines, and such provision as he could steal in the most dark and mysterious way—as became outlaws.
passages.vernacular: 每人將帶魚鉤同釣線,以及佢能以最黑暗、最神祕嘅方式偷嚟嘅糧食——呢個係亡命之徒應有嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每人將帶魚鉤和釣線,以及他能以最黑暗、最神祕的方式偷來的糧食——這是亡命之徒應有的。

passages.original: And before the afternoon was done, they had all managed to enjoy the sweet glory of spreading the fact that pretty soon the town would “hear something.”
passages.vernacular: 下午仲冇結束,佢哋都設法享受咗散布消息嘅甜美光榮,講不久鎮上就會「聽到點乜嘢」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午還沒結束,他們都設法享受了散布消息的甜美光榮,說不久鎮上就會「聽到點什麼」。

passages.original: All who got this vague hint were cautioned to “be mum and wait.”
passages.vernacular: 所有得到呢個模糊暗示嘅人都被告誡「保持沉默,等住」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有得到這個模糊暗示的人都被告誡「保持沉默,等著」。

passages.original: About midnight Tom arrived with a boiled ham and a few trifles, and stopped in a dense undergrowth on a small bluff overlooking the meeting-place.
passages.vernacular: 大約午夜,湯姆帶住一隻煮熟嘅火腿同啲零碎嘢到達,停喺俯瞰會合地嘅小懸崖上一片茂密嘅灌木叢中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約午夜,湯姆帶著一隻煮熟的火腿和一些零碎東西到達,停在俯瞰會合地的小懸崖上一片茂密的灌木叢中。

passages.original: It was starlight, and very still.
passages.vernacular: 星光燦爛,好安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星光燦爛,非常安靜。

passages.original: The mighty river lay like an ocean at rest.
passages.vernacular: 大河像休息中嘅海洋一樣躺住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大河像休息中的海洋一樣躺著。

passages.original: Tom listened a moment, but no sound disturbed the quiet.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆聽咗一會兒,冇聲音擾亂寧靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆聽了一會兒,沒有聲音擾亂寧靜。

passages.original: Then he gave a low, distinct whistle.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢發出一聲低低嘅清晰口哨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他發出一聲低低的清晰口哨。

passages.original: It was answered from under the bluff.
passages.vernacular: 從懸崖下回應喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從懸崖下回應了。

passages.original: Tom whistled twice more; these signals were answered in the same way.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆又吹咗兩聲;呢啲信號同樣得到咗回應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆又吹了兩聲;這些信號同樣得到了回應。

passages.original: Then a guarded voice said:
passages.vernacular: 然後一個謹慎嘅聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一個謹慎的聲音說:

passages.original: “Who goes there?”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個喺嗰度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰在那裡?」

passages.original: “Tom Sawyer, the Black Avenger of the Spanish Main.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆·索亞,西班牙海嘅黑色復仇者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆·索亞,西班牙海的黑色復仇者。

passages.original: Name your names.”
passages.vernacular: 報上你哋嘅名字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 報上你們的名字。」

passages.original: “Huck Finn the Red-Handed, and Joe Harper the Terror of the Seas.”
passages.vernacular: 「紅手哈克·費恩,同海上恐怖喬·哈珀。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「紅手哈克·費恩,和海上恐怖喬·哈珀。」

passages.original: Tom had furnished these titles, from his favorite literature.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆從佢最愛嘅文學中提供咗呢啲頭銜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆從他最愛的文學中提供了這些頭銜。

passages.original: “’Tis well.
passages.vernacular: 「好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好。

passages.original: Give the countersign.”
passages.vernacular: 講出暗號。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說出暗號。」

passages.original: Two hoarse whispers delivered the same awful word simultaneously to the brooding night:
passages.vernacular: 兩個嘶啞嘅低語同時向沉思嘅夜晚講出咗同一個可怕嘅詞:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個嘶啞的低語同時向沉思的夜晚說出了同一個可怕的詞:

passages.original: “Blood!”
Then Tom tumbled his ham over the bluff and let himself down after it, tearing both skin and clothes to some extent in the effort.
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆把火腿翻過懸崖,自己跟住滑下去,為此喺皮膚同衣服上都撕破咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆把火腿翻過懸崖,自己跟著滑下去,為此在皮膚和衣服上都撕破了一些。

passages.original: There was an easy, comfortable path along the shore under the bluff, but it lacked the advantages of difficulty and danger so valued by a pirate.
passages.vernacular: 懸崖下沿住岸邊有一條輕鬆舒適嘅小路,但佢缺少海盜所睇重嘅困難同危險嘅優點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懸崖下沿著岸邊有一條輕鬆舒適的小路,但它缺少海盜所看重的困難和危險的優點。

passages.original: The Terror of the Seas had brought a side of bacon, and had about worn himself out with getting it there.
passages.vernacular: 海上恐怖帶咗一大片培根,為了把佢弄到嗰度幾乎累壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海上恐怖帶了一大片培根,為了把它弄到那裡幾乎累壞了。

passages.original: Finn the Red-Handed had stolen a skillet and a quantity of half-cured leaf tobacco, and had also brought a few corn-cobs to make pipes with.
passages.vernacular: 紅手費恩偷咗一個平底鍋同一大堆半醃製嘅煙葉,仲帶咗幾個玉米棒子做菸斗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紅手費恩偷了一個平底鍋和一大堆半醃製的煙葉,還帶了幾個玉米棒子做菸斗。

passages.original: But none of the pirates smoked or “chewed” but himself.
passages.vernacular: 但海盜裡除咗佢冇一個抽菸或「嚼」菸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但海盜裡除了他沒有一個抽菸或「嚼」菸。

passages.original: The Black Avenger of the Spanish Main said it would never do to start without some fire.
passages.vernacular: 西班牙海嘅黑色復仇者講,冇啲火就出發係不行嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 西班牙海的黑色復仇者說,沒有一點火就出發是不行的。

passages.original: That was a wise thought; matches were hardly known there in that day.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個明智嘅想法;嗰時嗰度幾乎唔知道火柴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個明智的想法;那時那裡幾乎不知道火柴。

passages.original: They saw a fire smouldering upon a great raft a hundred yards above, and they went stealthily thither and helped themselves to a chunk.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋睇到一百碼外上游一個大木筏上有火喺悶燒,佢哋悄悄走過去,取咗一塊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們看到一百碼外上游一個大木筏上有火在悶燒,他們悄悄走過去,取了一塊。

passages.original: They made an imposing adventure of it, saying, “Hist!” every now and then, and suddenly halting with finger on lip; moving with hands on imaginary dagger-hilts; and giving orders in dismal whispers that if “the foe” stirred, to “let him have it to the hilt,” because “dead men tell no tales.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把佢做成一次令人印象深刻嘅冒險,不時講「噓!」,突然停住,手指放喺唇上;手放喺想像嘅匕首柄上移動;用陰沉嘅低語下命令,如果「敵人」動,就「讓佢嚐到劍柄」,因為「死人唔會講故事」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把它做成一次令人印象深刻的冒險,不時說「噓!」,突然停住,手指放在唇上;手放在想像的匕首柄上移動;用陰沉的低語下命令,如果「敵人」動,就「讓他嚐到劍柄」,因為「死人不會講故事」。

passages.original: They knew well enough that the raftsmen were all down at the village laying in stores or having a spree, but still that was no excuse for their conducting this thing in an unpiratical way.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好清楚筏工哋都喺村子裡採購物資或狂歡,但呢仍唔係佢哋以非海盜方式處理此事嘅藉口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們很清楚筏工們都在村子裡採購物資或狂歡,但這仍不是他們以非海盜方式處理此事的藉口。

passages.original: They shoved off, presently, Tom in command, Huck at the after oar and Joe at the forward.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋撐開,湯姆指揮,哈克喺後槳,喬喺前槳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們撐開,湯姆指揮,哈克在後槳,喬在前槳。

passages.original: Tom stood amidships, gloomy-browed, and with folded arms, and gave his orders in a low, stern whisper:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆站喺船中央,眉頭陰沉,雙臂交叉,用低沉嚴厲嘅耳語下達命令:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆站在船中央,眉頭陰沉,雙臂交叉,用低沉嚴厲的耳語下達命令:

passages.original: “Luff, and bring her to the wind!”
passages.vernacular: 「搶風,讓佢迎風!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「搶風,讓她迎風!」

passages.original: “Aye-aye, sir!”
passages.vernacular: 「係,係,長官!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是,長官!」

passages.original: “Steady, steady-y-y-y!”
“Steady it is, sir!”
passages.vernacular: 「穩住喇,長官!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「穩住了,長官!」

passages.original: “Let her go off a point!”
passages.vernacular: 「讓佢偏啲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓她偏一點!」

passages.original: “Point it is, sir!”
passages.vernacular: 「偏啲喇,長官!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「偏一點了,長官!」

passages.original: As the boys steadily and monotonously drove the raft toward mid-stream it was no doubt understood that these orders were given only for “style,” and were not intended to mean anything in particular.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋穩定而單調地把木筏推向河中心時,毫無疑問理解呢啲命令只係為了「派頭」,並不特指任何意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們穩定而單調地把木筏推向河中心時,毫無疑問理解這些命令只是為了「派頭」,並不特指任何意思。

passages.original: “What sail’s she carrying?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢掛嘅乜嘢帆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她掛的什麼帆?」

passages.original: “Courses, tops’ls, and flying-jib, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「主帆、上桅帆同飛艏帆,長官。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「主帆、上桅帆和飛艏帆,長官。」

passages.original: “Send the r’yals up!
passages.vernacular: 「把皇家帆升起嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把皇家帆升起來!

passages.original: Lay out aloft, there, half a dozen of ye—foretopmaststuns’l!
passages.vernacular: 你哋,幾個人到上面去——前上桅副帆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們,幾個人到上面去——前上桅副帆!

passages.original: Lively, now!”
passages.vernacular: 快,而家!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快,現在!」

passages.original: “Aye-aye, sir!”
passages.vernacular: 「係,係,長官!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是,長官!」

passages.original: “Shake out that maintogalans’l!
passages.vernacular: 「展開主上桅帆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「展開主上桅帆!

passages.original: Sheets and braces! now my hearties!”
passages.vernacular: 帆腳索同轉帆索!而家我嘅好小子哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帆腳索和轉帆索!現在我的好小子們!」

passages.original: “Aye-aye, sir!”
passages.vernacular: 「係,係,長官!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是,長官!」

passages.original: “Hellum-a-lee—hard a port!
passages.vernacular: 「舵向下風——硬左舵!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「舵向下風——硬左舵!

passages.original: Stand by to meet her when she comes!
passages.vernacular: 準備迎接佢嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 準備迎接它來!

passages.original: Port, port!
passages.vernacular: 左舵,左舵!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 左舵,左舵!

passages.original: Now, men!
passages.vernacular: 而家,夥計哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,夥計們!

passages.original: With a will!
passages.vernacular: 使勁!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 使勁!

passages.original: Stead-y-y-y!”
“Steady it is, sir!”
passages.vernacular: 「穩住喇,長官!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「穩住了,長官!」

passages.original: The raft drew beyond the middle of the river; the boys pointed her head right, and then lay on their oars.
passages.vernacular: 木筏越過河中間;男孩哋把佢嘅頭擺正,然後躺喺槳上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 木筏越過河中間;男孩們把她的頭擺正,然後躺在槳上。

passages.original: The river was not high, so there was not more than a two or three mile current.
passages.vernacular: 河水不高,所以水流不超過兩三英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 河水不高,所以水流不超過兩三英里。

passages.original: Hardly a word was said during the next three-quarters of an hour.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟嘅四十五分鐘幾乎冇講一句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來的四十五分鐘幾乎沒說一句話。

passages.original: Now the raft was passing before the distant town.
passages.vernacular: 而家木筏經過遠處嘅鎮子前面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在木筏經過遠處的鎮子前面。

passages.original: Two or three glimmering lights showed where it lay, peacefully sleeping, beyond the vague vast sweep of star-gemmed water, unconscious of the tremendous event that was happening.
passages.vernacular: 兩三點閃爍嘅燈光顯示佢躺喺嗰度,平靜地沉瞓,喺模糊嘅、浩瀚嘅、星光點點嘅水面之外,對正在發生嘅巨大事件毫無察覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩三點閃爍的燈光顯示它躺在那裡,平靜地沉睡,在模糊的、浩瀚的、星光點點的水面之外,對正在發生的巨大事件毫無察覺。

passages.original: The Black Avenger stood still with folded arms, “looking his last” upon the scene of his former joys and his later sufferings, and wishing “she” could see him now, abroad on the wild sea, facing peril and death with dauntless heart, going to his doom with a grim smile on his lips.
passages.vernacular: 黑色復仇者站住不動,雙臂交叉,對佢從前歡樂同後來受苦嘅場景「作最後一瞥」,希望「佢」而家能睇到佢,喺狂野嘅海上,以無畏嘅心面對危險同死亡,嘴唇上帶住嚴峻嘅微笑走向佢嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑色復仇者站著不動,雙臂交叉,對他從前歡樂和後來受苦的場景「作最後一瞥」,希望「她」現在能看到他,在狂野的海上,以無畏的心面對危險和死亡,嘴唇上帶著嚴峻的微笑走向他的命運。

passages.original: It was but a small strain on his imagination to remove Jackson’s Island beyond eye-shot of the village, and so he “looked his last” with a broken and satisfied heart.
passages.vernacular: 佢只需稍稍費力想像,就把傑克森島移到村子視線之外,於是佢以一顆破碎而滿足嘅心「作最後一瞥」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只需稍稍費力想像,就把傑克森島移到村子視線之外,於是他以一顆破碎而滿足的心「作最後一瞥」。

passages.original: The other pirates were looking their last, too; and they all looked so long that they came near letting the current drift them out of the range of the island.
passages.vernacular: 其他海盜都喺作最後一瞥;佢哋都睇咗咁久,差點讓水流把佢哋漂出島嶼嘅範圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他海盜也在作最後一瞥;他們都看了那麼久,差點讓水流把他們漂出島嶼的範圍。

passages.original: But they discovered the danger in time, and made shift to avert it.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋及時發現咗危險,設法避開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們及時發現了危險,設法避開了。

passages.original: About two o’clock in the morning the raft grounded on the bar two hundred yards above the head of the island, and they waded back and forth until they had landed their freight.
passages.vernacular: 大約凌晨兩點,木筏喺島頭上游兩百碼嘅沙洲上擱淺,佢哋嚟回涉水,直到卸完貨物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約凌晨兩點,木筏在島頭上游兩百碼的沙洲上擱淺,他們來回涉水,直到卸完貨物。

passages.original: Part of the little raft’s belongings consisted of an old sail, and this they spread over a nook in the bushes for a tent to shelter their provisions; but they themselves would sleep in the open air in good weather, as became outlaws.
passages.vernacular: 小木筏嘅部分物品包括一張舊帆,佢哋把佢撐喺灌木叢嘅一個角落當帳篷,遮蔽佢哋嘅糧食;但天氣好時佢哋自己將瞓喺露天,呢個係亡命之徒應有嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小木筏的部分物品包括一張舊帆,他們把它撐在灌木叢的一個角落當帳篷,遮蔽他們的糧食;但天氣好時他們自己將睡在露天,這是亡命之徒應有的。

passages.original: They built a fire against the side of a great log twenty or thirty steps within the sombre depths of the forest, and then cooked some bacon in the frying-pan for supper, and used up half of the corn “pone” stock they had brought.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺森林陰沉深處二三十步,靠住一根大原木嘅側面生咗火,然後喺煎鍋裡煮咗些培根當晚餐,用掉咗佢哋帶嚟嘅一半玉米「餅」存貨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在森林陰沉深處二三十步,靠著一根大原木的側面生了火,然後在煎鍋裡煮了些培根當晚餐,用掉了他們帶來的一半玉米「餅」存貨。

passages.original: It seemed glorious sport to be feasting in that wild, free way in the virgin forest of an unexplored and uninhabited island, far from the haunts of men, and they said they never would return to civilization.
passages.vernacular: 喺一座未勘探、無人居住嘅島嘅原始森林裡,以嗰種野性自由嘅方式盛宴,似乎係光榮嘅樂事,佢哋講佢哋永遠不回文明喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一座未勘探、無人居住的島的原始森林裡,以那種野性自由的方式盛宴,似乎是光榮的樂事,他們說他們永遠不回文明了。

passages.original: The climbing fire lit up their faces and threw its ruddy glare upon the pillared tree-trunks of their forest temple, and upon the varnished foliage and festooning vines.
passages.vernacular: 升騰嘅火光照亮咗佢哋嘅臉,把紅色嘅光投喺佢哋森林殿堂嘅柱狀樹幹上,投喺有光澤嘅樹葉同垂掛嘅藤蔓上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 升騰的火光照亮了他們的臉,把紅色的光投在他們森林殿堂的柱狀樹幹上,投在有光澤的樹葉和垂掛的藤蔓上。

passages.original: When the last crisp slice of bacon was gone, and the last allowance of corn pone devoured, the boys stretched themselves out on the grass, filled with contentment.
passages.vernacular: 最後一片脆培根食完,最後一份玉米餅吞下,男孩哋伸展開躺喺草地上,心滿意足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後一片脆培根吃完,最後一份玉米餅吞下,男孩們伸展開躺在草地上,心滿意足。

passages.original: They could have found a cooler place, but they would not deny themselves such a romantic feature as the roasting campfire.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋本可以找到一個更涼快嘅地方,但佢哋唔願拒絕烤人嘅營火呢種浪漫嘅特色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們本可以找到一個更涼快的地方,但他們不願拒絕烤人的營火這種浪漫的特色。

passages.original: “Ain’t it gay?” said Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係好愉快嗎?」喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是很愉快嗎?」喬說。

passages.original: “It’s nuts!” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「棒極喇!」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「棒極了!」湯姆說。

passages.original: “What would the boys say if they could see us?”
passages.vernacular: 「如果男孩哋能睇到我哋,佢哋會講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果男孩們能看到我們,他們會說什麼?」

passages.original: “Say?
Well, they’d just die to be here—hey, Hucky!”
passages.vernacular: 哼,佢哋會渴望嚟呢度渴望得要死——係吧,哈克!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哼,他們會渴望來這裡渴望得要死——是吧,哈克!」

passages.original: “I reckon so,” said Huckleberry; “anyways, I’m suited.
passages.vernacular: 「我想係,」哈克貝利講;「無論如何,我滿意喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是,」哈克貝利說;「無論如何,我滿意了。

passages.original: I don’t want nothing better’n this.
passages.vernacular: 我唔想要比呢更好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想要比這更好的。

passages.original: I don’t ever get enough to eat, gen’ally—and here they can’t come and pick at a feller and bullyrag him so.”
passages.vernacular: 我通常永遠食不飽——而喺呢度佢哋唔能夠嚟挑剔人、欺負人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我通常永遠吃不飽——而在這裡他們不能來挑剔人、欺負人。」

passages.original: “It’s just the life for me,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「呢正是我嘅生活,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這正是我的生活,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “You don’t have to get up, mornings, and you don’t have to go to school, and wash, and all that blame foolishness.
passages.vernacular: 「你早晨唔使起床,唔使上學、洗臉同所有嗰啲該死嘅蠢事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你早晨不用起床,不用上學、洗臉和所有那些該死的蠢事。

passages.original: You see a pirate don’t have to do anything, Joe, when he’s ashore, but a hermit he has to be praying considerable, and then he don’t have any fun, anyway, all by himself that way.”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,海盜上岸時乜嘢都唔使做,但隱士佢得相當多禱告,而且,無論如何,嗰樣自己一個人冇任何樂趣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,海盜上岸時什麼也不用做,但隱士他得相當多禱告,而且,無論如何,那樣自己一個人沒有任何樂趣。」

passages.original: “Oh yes, that’s so,” said Joe, “but I hadn’t thought much about it, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,」喬講,「但我冇點想過,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,」喬說,「但我沒怎麼想過,你知道。

passages.original: I’d a good deal rather be a pirate, now that I’ve tried it.”
passages.vernacular: 既然我試過喇,我寧願當海盜好多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然我試過了,我寧願當海盜好多。」

passages.original: “You see,” said Tom, “people don’t go much on hermits, nowadays, like they used to in old times, but a pirate’s always respected.
passages.vernacular: 「你睇,」湯姆講,「而家人哋不像古時候嗰樣睇重隱士喇,但海盜總是受人尊敬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看,」湯姆說,「現在人們不像古時候那樣看重隱士了,但海盜總是受人尊敬。

passages.original: And a hermit’s got to sleep on the hardest place he can find, and put sackcloth and ashes on his head, and stand out in the rain, and—”
passages.vernacular: 而隱士得瞓喺佢能找到嘅最硬嘅地方,頭上放麻布同灰,站喺雨裡,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而隱士得睡在他能找到的最硬的地方,頭上放麻布和灰,站在雨裡,而且——」

passages.original: “What does he put sackcloth and ashes on his head for?” inquired Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「佢點解頭上放麻布同灰?」哈克問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他為什麼頭上放麻布和灰?」哈克問。

passages.original: “I dono.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: But they’ve got to do it.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋必須咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們必須這樣。

passages.original: Hermits always do.
passages.vernacular: 隱士總是咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隱士總是這樣。

passages.original: You’d have to do that if you was a hermit.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你係隱士你都得咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你是隱士你也得這樣。」

passages.original: “Dern’d if I would,” said Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「我才不呢,」哈克講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我才不呢,」哈克說。

passages.original: “Well, what would you do?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你會點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你會怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “I dono.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: But I wouldn’t do that.”
passages.vernacular: 但我不做嗰個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不做那個。」

passages.original: “Why, Huck, you’d have to.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,哈克,你必須。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,哈克,你必須。

passages.original: How’d you get around it?”
passages.vernacular: 你點繞過去?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼繞過去?」

passages.original: “Why, I just wouldn’t stand it.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我就係不忍受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我就是不忍受。

passages.original: I’d run away.”
passages.vernacular: 我會逃跑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會逃跑。」

passages.original: “Run away!
passages.vernacular: 「逃跑!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「逃跑!

passages.original: Well, you would be a nice old slouch of a hermit.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,你會係個好好嘅老邋遢隱士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,你會是個很好的老邋遢隱士。

passages.original: You’d be a disgrace.”
passages.vernacular: 你會係個恥辱。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會是個恥辱。」

passages.original: The Red-Handed made no response, being better employed.
passages.vernacular: 紅手冇回答,正忙住更好嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紅手沒有回答,正忙著更好的事。

passages.original: He had finished gouging out a cob, and now he fitted a weed stem to it, loaded it with tobacco, and was pressing a coal to the charge and blowing a cloud of fragrant smoke—he was in the full bloom of luxurious contentment.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經挖完一個玉米棒子,而家畀佢裝上一根草莖,裝上煙草,把一塊炭壓喺裝填物上,吹出一團芬芳嘅煙雲——佢正處喺豪華滿足嘅盛開期。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他已經挖完一個玉米棒子,現在給它裝上一根草莖,裝上煙草,把一塊炭壓在裝填物上,吹出一團芬芳的煙雲——他正處在豪華滿足的盛開期。

passages.original: The other pirates envied him this majestic vice, and secretly resolved to acquire it shortly.
passages.vernacular: 其他海盜羨慕佢呢個威嚴嘅惡習,暗中決定不久都要學會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他海盜羨慕他這個威嚴的惡習,暗中決定不久也要學會。

passages.original: Presently Huck said:
passages.vernacular: 不久哈克講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久哈克說:

passages.original: “What does pirates have to do?”
passages.vernacular: 「海盜要做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「海盜要做什麼?」

passages.original: Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說:

passages.original: “Oh, they have just a bully time—take ships and burn them, and get the money and bury it in awful places in their island where there’s ghosts and things to watch it, and kill everybody in the ships—make ’em walk a plank.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢哋有最好嘅時光——劫掠船隻並燒掉佢哋,攞到錢,埋喺島上可怕嘅地方,嗰度有鬼同嘢睇守,殺死船上所有人——叫佢哋走跳板。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他們有最好的時光——劫掠船隻並燒掉它們,拿到錢,埋在島上可怕的地方,那裡有鬼和東西看守,殺死船上所有人——叫他們走跳板。」

passages.original: “And they carry the women to the island,” said Joe; “they don’t kill the women.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋把女人帶到島上,」喬講;「佢哋不殺女人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們把女人帶到島上,」喬說;「他們不殺女人。」

passages.original: “No,” assented Tom, “they don’t kill the women—they’re too noble.
passages.vernacular: 「不,」湯姆同意,「佢哋不殺女人——佢哋太高貴喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」湯姆同意,「他們不殺女人——他們太高貴了。

passages.original: And the women’s always beautiful, too.”
passages.vernacular: 而且女人總是好美。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且女人總是很美。」

passages.original: “And don’t they wear the bulliest clothes!
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋穿嘅衣服唔係最棒嘅嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們穿的衣服不是最棒的嗎!

passages.original: Oh no!
passages.vernacular: 哦不!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦不!

passages.original: All gold and silver and di’monds,” said Joe, with enthusiasm.
passages.vernacular: 全係金銀同鑽石,」喬熱情地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全是金銀和鑽石,」喬熱情地說。

passages.original: “Who?” said Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「邊個?」哈克講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰?」哈克說。

passages.original: “Why, the pirates.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,海盜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,海盜。」

passages.original: Huck scanned his own clothing forlornly.
passages.vernacular: 哈克悲哀地打量住自己嘅衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克悲哀地打量著自己的衣服。

passages.original: “I reckon I ain’t dressed fitten for a pirate,” said he, with a regretful pathos in his voice; “but I ain’t got none but these.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想我穿嘅不適合當海盜,」佢講,聲音裡帶住遺憾嘅悲壯;「但我只有呢啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我穿的不適合當海盜,」他說,聲音裡帶著遺憾的悲壯;「但我只有這些。」

passages.original: But the other boys told him the fine clothes would come fast enough, after they should have begun their adventures.
passages.vernacular: 但其他男孩告訴佢,佢哋開始冒險後,好衣服好快就會嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但其他男孩告訴他,他們開始冒險後,好衣服很快就會來。

passages.original: They made him understand that his poor rags would do to begin with, though it was customary for wealthy pirates to start with a proper wardrobe.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋讓佢明白,佢可憐嘅破衣服開始時都將就,雖然富有嘅海盜一般以像樣嘅衣櫥開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們讓他明白,他可憐的破衣服開始時也將就,雖然富有的海盜一般以像樣的衣櫥開始。

passages.original: Gradually their talk died out and drowsiness began to steal upon the eyelids of the little waifs.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地佢哋嘅談話停喇,睏倦開始悄悄爬上呢啲小流浪兒嘅眼皮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地他們的談話停了,睏倦開始悄悄爬上這些小流浪兒的眼皮。

passages.original: The pipe dropped from the fingers of the Red-Handed, and he slept the sleep of the conscience-free and the weary.
passages.vernacular: 菸斗從紅手嘅手指間滑落,佢瞓了無愧良心者同疲倦者嘅覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 菸斗從紅手的手指間滑落,他睡了無愧良心者和疲倦者的覺。

passages.original: The Terror of the Seas and the Black Avenger of the Spanish Main had more difficulty in getting to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 海上恐怖同西班牙海嘅黑色復仇者更難入瞓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海上恐怖和西班牙海的黑色復仇者更難入睡。

passages.original: They said their prayers inwardly, and lying down, since there was nobody there with authority to make them kneel and recite aloud; in truth, they had a mind not to say them at all, but they were afraid to proceed to such lengths as that, lest they might call down a sudden and special thunderbolt from heaven.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋躺住喺心裡禱告,因為嗰度冇有權威嘅人叫佢哋跪住大聲背誦;事實上,佢哋本想根本不講,但佢哋怕走得咁遠,免得召嚟上天突然而特別嘅雷霆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們躺著在心裡禱告,因為那裡沒有有權威的人叫他們跪著大聲背誦;事實上,他們本想根本不說,但他們怕走得那麼遠,免得召來上天突然而特別的雷霆。

passages.original: Then at once they reached and hovered upon the imminent verge of sleep—but an intruder came, now, that would not “down.”
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋即刻到達並徘徊喺瞓眠嘅迫近邊緣——但一個闖入者嚟喇,唔肯「下去」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們立刻到達並徘徊在睡眠的迫近邊緣——但一個闖入者來了,不肯「下去」。

passages.original: It was conscience.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係良心。
