passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是良心。

passages.original: They began to feel a vague fear that they had been doing wrong to run away; and next they thought of the stolen meat, and then the real torture came.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋開始隱約感到恐懼,覺得逃跑係做錯喇;接住佢哋想到偷嘅肉,然後真正嘅折磨嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們開始隱約感到恐懼,覺得逃跑是做錯了;接著他們想到偷的肉,然後真正的折磨來了。

passages.original: They tried to argue it away by reminding conscience that they had purloined sweetmeats and apples scores of times; but conscience was not to be appeased by such thin plausibilities; it seemed to them, in the end, that there was no getting around the stubborn fact that taking sweetmeats was only “hooking,” while taking bacon and hams and such valuables was plain simple stealing—and there was a command against that in the Bible.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋試圖通過提醒良心,佢哋偷過幾十次糖果同蘋果,嚟辯駁掉佢;但良心唔係呢種單薄嘅似係而非能安撫嘅;最後佢哋似乎無法繞過呢個頑固嘅事實:攞糖果只係「順手牽羊」,而攞培根、火腿同呢類貴重物品係純粹嘅偷竊——而聖經裡有一條誡命禁止呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們試圖通過提醒良心,他們偷過幾十次糖果和蘋果,來辯駁掉它;但良心不是這種單薄的似是而非能安撫的;最後他們似乎無法繞過這個頑固的事實:拿糖果只是「順手牽羊」,而拿培根、火腿和這類貴重物品是純粹的偷竊——而聖經裡有一條誡命禁止這個。

passages.original: So they inwardly resolved that so long as they remained in the business, their piracies should not again be sullied with the crime of stealing.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋喺心裡決定,只要佢哋仲喺呢一行,佢哋嘅海盜行為唔應該再被偷竊嘅罪行玷污。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們在心裡決定,只要他們還在這一行,他們的海盜行為不應再被偷竊的罪行玷污。

passages.original: Then conscience granted a truce, and these curiously inconsistent pirates fell peacefully to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 然後良心批准咗休戰,呢啲奇怪地自相矛盾嘅海盜平靜地瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後良心批准了休戰,這些奇怪地自相矛盾的海盜平靜地睡著了。

chapters.title: Chapter XIV: Camp-Life 第十四章:營地生活

passages.original: CH When Tom awoke in the morning, he wondered where he was.
passages.vernacular: 早晨湯姆醒嚟時,納悶自己喺邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨湯姆醒來時,納悶自己在哪裡。

passages.original: He sat up and rubbed his eyes and looked around.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐起嚟,揉揉眼睛,環顧四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐起來,揉揉眼睛,環顧四周。

passages.original: Then he comprehended.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢明白喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他明白了。

passages.original: It was the cool gray dawn, and there was a delicious sense of repose and peace in the deep pervading calm and silence of the woods.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係涼爽嘅灰色黎明,喺森林深沉瀰漫嘅平靜同寂靜中,有一種美妙嘅休息同安寧嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是涼爽的灰色黎明,在森林深沉瀰漫的平靜與寂靜中,有一種美妙的休息與安寧的感覺。

passages.original: Not a leaf stirred; not a sound obtruded upon great Nature’s meditation.
passages.vernacular: 冇一片葉子動;冇啲聲音打擾大自然嘅沉思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一片葉子動;沒有一點聲音打擾大自然的沉思。

passages.original: Beaded dewdrops stood upon the leaves and grasses.
passages.vernacular: 露珠像串珠一樣停喺葉子同草上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 露珠像串珠一樣停在葉子和草上。

passages.original: A white layer of ashes covered the fire, and a thin blue breath of smoke rose straight into the air.
passages.vernacular: 一層白色嘅灰燼覆蓋住火堆,一縷淡淡嘅藍煙直直升入空中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一層白色的灰燼覆蓋著火堆,一縷淡淡的藍煙直直升入空中。

passages.original: Joe and Huck still slept.
passages.vernacular: 喬同哈克仲瞓住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬和哈克還睡著。

passages.original: Now, far away in the woods a bird called; another answered; presently the hammering of a woodpecker was heard.
passages.vernacular: 而家,遠處嘅樹林裡一隻鳥喺叫;另一隻回答;不久聽到咗啄木鳥嘅敲擊聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,遠處的樹林裡一隻鳥在叫;另一隻回答;不久聽到了啄木鳥的敲擊聲。

passages.original: Gradually the cool dim gray of the morning whitened, and as gradually sounds multiplied and life manifested itself.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地早晨涼爽朦朧嘅灰色變白喇,聲音都漸漸增多,生命顯現出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地早晨涼爽朦朧的灰色變白了,聲音也漸漸增多,生命顯現出來。

passages.original: The marvel of Nature shaking off sleep and going to work unfolded itself to the musing boy.
passages.vernacular: 大自然抖掉瞓意、開始工作嘅奇妙,向沉思嘅男孩展開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大自然抖掉睡意、開始工作的奇妙,向沉思的男孩展開了。

passages.original: A little green worm came crawling over a dewy leaf, lifting two-thirds of his body into the air from time to time and “sniffing around,” then proceeding again—for he was measuring, Tom said; and when the worm approached him, of its own accord, he sat as still as a stone, with his hopes rising and falling, by turns, as the creature still came toward him or seemed inclined to go elsewhere; and when at last it considered a painful moment with its curved body in the air and then came decisively down upon Tom’s leg and began a journey over him, his whole heart was glad—for that meant that he was going to have a new suit of clothes—without the shadow of a doubt a gaudy piratical uniform.
passages.vernacular: 一條小綠蟲爬過一片帶露嘅葉子,不時把身體嘅三分之二抬到空中「四處嗅」,然後又繼續前進——因為佢喺量,湯姆講;嗰蟲子自己向佢靠近時,佢像石頭一樣坐住不動,佢嘅希望隨住嗰生物仍朝佢嚟或似乎想去別處而起伏;最後佢考慮咗痛苦嘅一刻,身體彎曲喺空中,然後果斷地落喺湯姆嘅腿上,開始喺佢身上旅行,佢整個心都高興——因為呢意味住佢要有一套新衣服喇——毫無疑問係一套華麗嘅海盜制服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一條小綠蟲爬過一片帶露的葉子,不時把身體的三分之二抬到空中「四處嗅」,然後又繼續前進——因為它在量,湯姆說;那蟲子自己向他靠近時,他像石頭一樣坐著不動,他的希望隨著那生物仍朝他來或似乎想去別處而起伏;最後它考慮了痛苦的一刻,身體彎曲在空中,然後果斷地落在湯姆的腿上,開始在他身上旅行,他整個心都高興——因為這意味著他要有一套新衣服了——毫無疑問是一套華麗的海盜制服。

passages.original: Now a procession of ants appeared, from nowhere in particular, and went about their labors; one struggled manfully by with a dead spider five times as big as itself in its arms, and lugged it straight up a tree-trunk.
passages.vernacular: 而家一列螞蟻從冇特定嘅地方出現,忙住幹活;一隻英勇地掙扎住走過,懷裡抱住比自己大五倍嘅死蜘蛛,把佢直拖上樹幹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在一列螞蟻從沒有特定的地方出現,忙著幹活;一隻英勇地掙扎著走過,懷裡抱著比自己大五倍的死蜘蛛,把它直拖上樹幹。

passages.original: A brown spotted lady-bug climbed the dizzy height of a grass blade, and Tom bent down close to it and said, “Lady-bug, lady-bug, fly away home, your house is on fire, your children’s alone,” and she took wing and went off to see about it—which did not surprise the boy, for he knew of old that this insect was credulous about conflagrations, and he had practised upon its simplicity more than once.
passages.vernacular: 一隻褐色斑點嘅瓢蟲爬上草葉令人頭暈嘅高度,湯姆俯身靠近佢,講:「瓢蟲,瓢蟲,飛回家,你家住火喇,你細路哋孤單」,佢展翅飛走去睇個究竟——呢並冇讓男孩感到驚訝,因為佢早就知道呢種昆蟲對火災輕信,佢不止一次利用過佢嘅單純。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻褐色斑點的瓢蟲爬上草葉令人頭暈的高度,湯姆俯身靠近它,說:「瓢蟲,瓢蟲,飛回家,你家著火了,你孩子們孤單」,她展翅飛走去看個究竟——這並沒有讓男孩感到驚訝,因為他早就知道這種昆蟲對火災輕信,他不止一次利用過它的單純。

passages.original: A tumblebug came next, heaving sturdily at its ball, and Tom touched the creature, to see it shut its legs against its body and pretend to be dead.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟係一隻蜣螂,堅強地推佢嘅球,湯姆碰咗碰呢生物,睇佢把腿縮喺身體上裝死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來是一隻蜣螂,堅強地推它的球,湯姆碰了碰這生物,看它把腿縮在身體上裝死。

passages.original: The birds were fairly rioting by this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣鳥兒哋幾乎喺狂歡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時鳥兒們幾乎在狂歡。

passages.original: A catbird, the Northern mocker, lit in a tree over Tom’s head, and trilled out her imitations of her neighbors in a rapture of enjoyment; then a shrill jay swept down, a flash of blue flame, and stopped on a twig almost within the boy’s reach, cocked his head to one side and eyed the strangers with a consuming curiosity; a gray squirrel and a big fellow of the “fox” kind came skurrying along, sitting up at intervals to inspect and chatter at the boys, for the wild things had probably never seen a human being before and scarcely knew whether to be afraid or not.
passages.vernacular: 一隻貓鵲,北方嘅模仿鳥,落喺湯姆頭上嘅一棵樹上,狂喜地顫聲模仿佢嘅鄰居;然後一隻尖叫嘅松鴉俯衝下嚟,一道藍色火焰嘅閃光,停喺幾乎喺男孩手邊嘅一根小枝上,把頭歪到一邊,以吞噬般嘅好奇心打量呢啲陌生人;一隻灰松鼠同一隻「狐」種嘅大傢伙匆匆跑過,不時坐起嚟檢查男孩哋並對佢哋吱吱叫,因為呢啲野生動物大概從冇見過人類,幾乎唔知道該不該害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻貓鵲,北方的模仿鳥,落在湯姆頭上的一棵樹上,狂喜地顫聲模仿她的鄰居;然後一隻尖叫的松鴉俯衝下來,一道藍色火焰的閃光,停在幾乎在男孩手邊的一根小枝上,把頭歪到一邊,以吞噬般的好奇心打量這些陌生人;一隻灰松鼠和一隻「狐」種的大傢伙匆匆跑過,不時坐起來檢查男孩們並對他們吱吱叫,因為這些野生動物大概從沒見過人類,幾乎不知道該不該害怕。

passages.original: All Nature was wide awake and stirring, now; long lances of sunlight pierced down through the dense foliage far and near, and a few butterflies came fluttering upon the scene.
passages.vernacular: 而家整個大自然完全醒喇,忙碌起嚟;長長嘅陽光矛穿過茂密嘅樹葉,遠近都有,幾隻蝴蝶翩翩飛到場上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在整個大自然完全醒了,忙碌起來;長長的陽光矛穿過茂密的樹葉,遠近都有,幾隻蝴蝶翩翩飛到場上。

passages.original: Tom stirred up the other pirates and they all clattered away with a shout, and in a minute or two were stripped and chasing after and tumbling over each other in the shallow limpid water of the white sandbar.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆叫醒其他海盜,佢哋喊叫住嘩啦跑開,唔到一兩分鐘就脫光衣服,喺白色沙洲清澈嘅淺水中互相追逐翻滾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆叫醒其他海盜,他們喊叫著嘩啦跑開,不到一兩分鐘就脫光衣服,在白色沙洲清澈的淺水中互相追逐翻滾。

passages.original: They felt no longing for the little village sleeping in the distance beyond the majestic waste of water.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋對遠處壯觀嘅水面嗰邊沉瞓嘅小村子冇任何思念。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們對遠處壯觀的水面那邊沉睡的小村子沒有任何思念。

passages.original: A vagrant current or a slight rise in the river had carried off their raft, but this only gratified them, since its going was something like burning the bridge between them and civilization.
passages.vernacular: 一道漂移嘅水流或河水嘅輕微上漲帶走咗佢哋嘅木筏,但呢只讓佢哋高興,因為佢嘅離去有點像燒掉咗佢哋同文明之間嘅橋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一道漂移的水流或河水的輕微上漲帶走了他們的木筏,但這只讓他們高興,因為它的離去有點像燒掉了他們與文明之間的橋。

passages.original: They came back to camp wonderfully refreshed, glad-hearted, and ravenous; and they soon had the camp-fire blazing up again.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋回到營地,精神極其振作,心情愉快,飢腸轆轆;好快佢哋就把營火重新燒旺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們回到營地,精神極其振作,心情愉快,飢腸轆轆;很快他們就把營火重新燒旺。

passages.original: Huck found a spring of clear cold water close by, and the boys made cups of broad oak or hickory leaves, and felt that water, sweetened with such a wildwood charm as that, would be a good enough substitute for coffee.
passages.vernacular: 哈克喺附近找到一股清冷嘅泉水,男孩哋用寬大嘅橡樹或山核桃樹葉做杯子,覺得呢種帶住荒野魅力而甜美嘅水,可以好好地代替咖啡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克在附近找到一股清冷的泉水,男孩們用寬大的橡樹或山核桃樹葉做杯子,覺得這種帶著荒野魅力而甜美的水,可以很好地代替咖啡。

passages.original: While Joe was slicing bacon for breakfast, Tom and Huck asked him to hold on a minute; they stepped to a promising nook in the river-bank and threw in their lines; almost immediately they had reward.
passages.vernacular: 喬喺切早餐用嘅培根時,湯姆同哈克請佢稍等;佢哋走到河岸一個有希望嘅角落,拋下釣線;幾乎即刻有咗收穫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬在切早餐用的培根時,湯姆和哈克請他稍等;他們走到河岸一個有希望的角落,拋下釣線;幾乎立刻有了收穫。

passages.original: Joe had not had time to get impatient before they were back again with some handsome bass, a couple of sun-perch and a small catfish—provisions enough for quite a family.
passages.vernacular: 喬仲冇嚟得及不耐煩,佢哋就帶住啲漂亮嘅鱸魚、幾條太陽魚同一條小鯰魚回嚟喇——夠一整個家庭嘅食物喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬還沒來得及不耐煩,他們就帶著一些漂亮的鱸魚、幾條太陽魚和一條小鯰魚回來了——夠一整個家庭的食物了。

passages.original: They fried the fish with the bacon, and were astonished; for no fish had ever seemed so delicious before.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把魚同培根一起煎,驚呆喇;因為從冇邊種魚似乎咁樣美味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把魚同培根一起煎,驚呆了;因為從沒有哪種魚似乎這樣美味。

passages.original: They did not know that the quicker a fresh-water fish is on the fire after he is caught the better he is; and they reflected little upon what a sauce open-air sleeping, open-air exercise, bathing, and a large ingredient of hunger make, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔知道淡水魚釣上嚟後越快上火越好;佢哋都好少想到,露天瞓覺、露天運動、洗澡同大量飢餓呢啲佐料都起咗作用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不知道淡水魚釣上來後越快上火越好;他們也很少想到,露天睡覺、露天運動、洗澡和大量飢餓這些佐料也起了作用。

passages.original: They lay around in the shade, after breakfast, while Huck had a smoke, and then went off through the woods on an exploring expedition.
passages.vernacular: 早餐後佢哋躺喺陰涼處,哈克抽咗一管菸,然後穿過樹林去探險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐後他們躺在陰涼處,哈克抽了一管菸,然後穿過樹林去探險。

passages.original: They tramped gayly along, over decaying logs, through tangled underbrush, among solemn monarchs of the forest, hung from their crowns to the ground with a drooping regalia of grape-vines.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋快活地大步走過腐爛嘅原木,穿過糾結嘅灌木叢,喺莊嚴嘅森林君王之間,佢哋從樹冠到地面掛住下垂嘅葡萄藤皇家飾物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們快活地大步走過腐爛的原木,穿過糾結的灌木叢,在莊嚴的森林君王之間,它們從樹冠到地面掛著下垂的葡萄藤皇家飾物。

passages.original: Now and then they came upon snug nooks carpeted with grass and jeweled with flowers.
passages.vernacular: 不時佢哋碰到鋪住草、鑲住花嘅舒適角落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不時他們碰到鋪著草、鑲著花的舒適角落。

passages.original: They found plenty of things to be delighted with, but nothing to be astonished at.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋發現好多令人高興嘅嘢,但冇令人驚訝嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們發現很多令人高興的東西,但沒有令人驚訝的。

passages.original: They discovered that the island was about three miles long and a quarter of a mile wide, and that the shore it lay closest to was only separated from it by a narrow channel hardly two hundred yards wide.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋發現呢座島大約三英里長、四分之一英里寬,離佢最近嘅岸只隔住一條幾乎唔到兩百碼寬嘅狹窄水道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們發現這座島大約三英里長、四分之一英里寬,離它最近的岸只隔著一條幾乎不到兩百碼寬的狹窄水道。

passages.original: They took a swim about every hour, so it was close upon the middle of the afternoon when they got back to camp.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋大約每小時游一次泳,所以佢哋回到營地時已接近下午過半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們大約每小時游一次泳,所以他們回到營地時已接近下午過半。

passages.original: They were too hungry to stop to fish, but they fared sumptuously upon cold ham, and then threw themselves down in the shade to talk.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋餓得唔能夠停下嚟釣魚,但佢哋食咗一頓豐盛嘅冷火腿,然後倒喺陰涼處聊天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們餓得不能停下來釣魚,但他們吃了一頓豐盛的冷火腿,然後倒在陰涼處聊天。

passages.original: But the talk soon began to drag, and then died.
passages.vernacular: 但談話好快開始拖沓,然後死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但談話很快開始拖沓,然後死了。

passages.original: The stillness, the solemnity that brooded in the woods, and the sense of loneliness, began to tell upon the spirits of the boys.
passages.vernacular: 森林裡籠罩嘅寂靜、莊嚴,同孤獨感開始影響男孩哋嘅精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 森林裡籠罩的寂靜、莊嚴,和孤獨感開始影響男孩們的精神。

passages.original: They fell to thinking.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋開始思考。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們開始思考。

passages.original: A sort of undefined longing crept upon them.
passages.vernacular: 一種未明確嘅渴望悄悄爬上佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種未明確的渴望悄悄爬上他們。

passages.original: This took dim shape, presently—it was budding homesickness.
passages.vernacular: 呢不久有咗模糊嘅形狀——佢係正在萌芽嘅思鄉病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不久有了模糊的形狀——它是正在萌芽的思鄉病。

passages.original: Even Finn the Red-Handed was dreaming of his doorsteps and empty hogsheads.
passages.vernacular: 連紅手費恩都喺夢想佢嘅門階同空桶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連紅手費恩也在夢想他的門階和空桶。

passages.original: But they were all ashamed of their weakness, and none was brave enough to speak his thought.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋都為自己嘅軟弱感到羞愧,冇一個勇敢到講出自己嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們都為自己的軟弱感到羞愧,沒有一個勇敢到說出自己的想法。

passages.original: For some time, now, the boys had been dully conscious of a peculiar sound in the distance, just as one sometimes is of the ticking of a clock which he takes no distinct note of.
passages.vernacular: 有一陣子,男孩哋隱約意識到遠處有一種奇怪嘅聲音,就像人有時對一個冇清楚注意嘅鐘嘅滴答聲有意識一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一陣子,男孩們隱約意識到遠處有一種奇怪的聲音,就像人有時對一個沒有清楚注意的鐘的滴答聲有意識一樣。

passages.original: But now this mysterious sound became more pronounced, and forced a recognition.
passages.vernacular: 但而家呢個神祕嘅聲音變得更明顯,迫使人承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在這個神祕的聲音變得更明顯,迫使人承認。

passages.original: The boys started, glanced at each other, and then each assumed a listening attitude.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋一驚,互相瞥咗一眼,然後每個人擺出聆聽嘅姿態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們一驚,互相瞥了一眼,然後每個人擺出聆聽的姿態。

passages.original: There was a long silence, profound and unbroken; then a deep, sullen boom came floating down out of the distance.
passages.vernacular: 一陣長長嘅沉默,深沉而不間斷;然後一聲低沉、陰鬱嘅轟鳴從遠處飄嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣長長的沉默,深沉而不間斷;然後一聲低沉、陰鬱的轟鳴從遠處飄來。

passages.original: “What is it!” exclaimed Joe, under his breath.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢!」喬屏住呼吸講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼!」喬屏住呼吸說。

passages.original: “I wonder,” said Tom in a whisper.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺想,」湯姆低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在想,」湯姆低聲說。

passages.original: “’Tain’t thunder,” said Huckleberry, in an awed tone, “becuz thunder—”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係雷,」哈克貝利用敬畏嘅語氣講,「因為雷——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是雷,」哈克貝利用敬畏的語氣說,「因為雷——」

passages.original: “Hark!” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「聽!」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽!」湯姆說。

passages.original: “Listen—don’t talk.”
passages.vernacular: 「聽——唔好講話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽——別說話。」

passages.original: They waited a time that seemed an age, and then the same muffled boom troubled the solemn hush.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋等咗似乎一個世紀,然後同樣被悶住嘅轟鳴擾亂咗莊嚴嘅寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們等了似乎一個世紀,然後同樣被悶住的轟鳴擾亂了莊嚴的寂靜。

passages.original: “Let’s go and see.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋去睇睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們去看看。」

passages.original: They sprang to their feet and hurried to the shore toward the town.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋跳起嚟,匆忙跑到朝鎮子嘅岸邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們跳起來,匆忙跑到朝鎮子的岸邊。

passages.original: They parted the bushes on the bank and peered out over the water.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋撥開岸上嘅灌木,從水面窺視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們撥開岸上的灌木,從水面窺視。

passages.original: The little steam ferry-boat was about a mile below the village, drifting with the current.
passages.vernacular: 小汽輪渡船喺村子下游約一英里處,隨水流漂移。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小汽輪渡船在村子下游約一英里處,隨水流漂移。

passages.original: Her broad deck seemed crowded with people.
passages.vernacular: 佢寬闊嘅甲板上似乎擠滿咗人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她寬闊的甲板上似乎擠滿了人。

passages.original: There were a great many skiffs rowing about or floating with the stream in the neighborhood of the ferryboat, but the boys could not determine what the men in them were doing.
passages.vernacular: 渡船附近有許多小艇喺划行或隨流漂浮,但男孩哋睇不出裡面嘅人喺做乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 渡船附近有許多小艇在划行或隨流漂浮,但男孩們看不出裡面的人在做什麼。

passages.original: Presently a great jet of white smoke burst from the ferryboat’s side, and as it expanded and rose in a lazy cloud, that same dull throb of sound was borne to the listeners again.
passages.vernacular: 不久渡船側面噴出一大股白煙,佢擴散、升起成一朵懶散嘅雲時,同樣沉悶嘅聲響又傳畀咗聽者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久渡船側面噴出一大股白煙,它擴散、升起成一朵懶散的雲時,同樣沉悶的聲響又傳給了聽者。

passages.original: “I know now!” exclaimed Tom; “somebody’s drownded!”
passages.vernacular: 「我而家知道喇!」湯姆喊道;「有人淹死喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在知道了!」湯姆喊道;「有人淹死了!」

passages.original: “That’s it!” said Huck; “they done that last summer, when Bill Turner got drownded; they shoot a cannon over the water, and that makes him come up to the top.
passages.vernacular: 「就係嗰樣!」哈克講;「去年夏天比爾·特納淹死時,佢哋就咁樣做過;佢哋喺水面上開炮,嗰使佢浮上嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是那樣!」哈克說;「去年夏天比爾·特納淹死時,他們就這樣做過;他們在水面上開炮,那使他浮上來。

passages.original: Yes, and they take loaves of bread and put quicksilver in ’em and set ’em afloat, and wherever there’s anybody that’s drownded, they’ll float right there and stop.”
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,而且佢哋攞麵包,放進水銀,讓佢哋漂浮,邊度有淹死嘅人,佢哋就會漂到嗰度停住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,而且他們拿麵包,放進水銀,讓它們漂浮,哪裡有淹死的人,它們就會漂到那裡停住。」

passages.original: “Yes, I’ve heard about that,” said Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我聽講過,」喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我聽說過,」喬說。

passages.original: “I wonder what makes the bread do that.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想知道係乜嘢使麵包嗰樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想知道是什麼使麵包那樣。」

passages.original: “Oh, it ain’t the bread, so much,” said Tom; “I reckon it’s mostly what they say over it before they start it out.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,主要唔係麵包,」湯姆講;「我想主要係佢哋喺放出去之前喺上面講嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,主要不是麵包,」湯姆說;「我想主要是他們在放出去之前在上面說的話。」

passages.original: “But they don’t say anything over it,” said Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢哋喺上面乜嘢都不講,」哈克講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但他們在上面什麼也不說,」哈克說。

passages.original: “I’ve seen ’em and they don’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「我睇過佢哋,佢哋不講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看過他們,他們不說。」

passages.original: “Well, that’s funny,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰好奇怪,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那很奇怪,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “But maybe they say it to themselves.
passages.vernacular: 「但或者佢哋喺心裡講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但也許他們在心裡說。

passages.original: Of course they do.
passages.vernacular: 當然佢哋講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然他們說。

passages.original: Anybody might know that.”
passages.vernacular: 任何人都能知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何人都能知道。」

passages.original: The other boys agreed that there was reason in what Tom said, because an ignorant lump of bread, uninstructed by an incantation, could not be expected to act very intelligently when set upon an errand of such gravity.
passages.vernacular: 其他男孩同意湯姆嘅話有道理,因為一塊無知嘅麵包,冇被咒語指導,被派去執行咁重大嘅任務時,唔能夠指望佢表現得好聰明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他男孩同意湯姆的話有道理,因為一塊無知的麵包,沒有被咒語指導,被派去執行這麼重大的任務時,不能指望它表現得很聰明。

passages.original: “By jings, I wish I was over there, now,” said Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,我真希望我而家喺嗰邊,」喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,我真希望我現在在那邊,」喬說。

passages.original: “I do too,” said Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「我都係,」哈克講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是,」哈克說。

passages.original: “I’d give heaps to know who it is.”
passages.vernacular: 「我願意花好多錢去知道係邊個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我願意花很多錢去知道是誰。」

passages.original: The boys still listened and watched.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋仍喺聽住、睇住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們仍在聽著、看著。

passages.original: Presently a revealing thought flashed through Tom’s mind, and he exclaimed:
passages.vernacular: 不久一個揭示性嘅念頭閃過湯姆嘅腦子,佢喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久一個揭示性的念頭閃過湯姆的腦子,他喊道:

passages.original: “Boys, I know who’s drownded—it’s us!”
passages.vernacular: 「夥計哋,我知道邊個淹死喇——係我哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夥計們,我知道誰淹死了——是我們!」

passages.original: They felt like heroes in an instant.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋轉眼覺得像英雄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們轉眼覺得像英雄。

passages.original: Here was a gorgeous triumph; they were missed; they were mourned; hearts were breaking on their account; tears were being shed; accusing memories of unkindness to these poor lost lads were rising up, and unavailing regrets and remorse were being indulged; and best of all, the departed were the talk of the whole town, and the envy of all the boys, as far as this dazzling notoriety was concerned.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一場輝煌嘅勝利;佢哋被想念喇;佢哋被哀悼喇;因為佢哋,心喺碎;眼淚喺流;對呢啲可憐嘅失蹤男孩不好嘅指責性回憶正在升起,無濟於事嘅後悔同悔恨正在被放縱;最好嘅係,逝者成咗全鎮嘅話題,就呢耀眼嘅聲名而言,成咗所有男孩羨慕嘅對象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一場輝煌的勝利;他們被想念了;他們被哀悼了;因為他們,心在碎;眼淚在流;對這些可憐的失蹤男孩不好的指責性回憶正在升起,無濟於事的後悔和悔恨正在被放縱;最好的是,逝者成了全鎮的話題,就這耀眼的聲名而言,成了所有男孩羨慕的對象。

passages.original: This was fine.
passages.vernacular: 呢個好棒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這很棒。

passages.original: It was worth while to be a pirate, after all.
passages.vernacular: 畢竟當海盜係值得嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 畢竟當海盜是值得的。

passages.original: As twilight drew on, the ferryboat went back to her accustomed business and the skiffs disappeared.
passages.vernacular: 暮色降臨時,渡船回到佢平常嘅工作,小艇消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暮色降臨時,渡船回到她平常的工作,小艇消失了。

passages.original: The pirates returned to camp.
passages.vernacular: 海盜哋回到營地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 海盜們回到營地。

passages.original: They were jubilant with vanity over their new grandeur and the illustrious trouble they were making.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋因對新嘅偉大同佢哋製造嘅顯赫嘅麻煩而虛榮地歡欣鼓舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們因對新的偉大和他們製造的顯赫的麻煩而虛榮地歡欣鼓舞。

passages.original: They caught fish, cooked supper and ate it, and then fell to guessing at what the village was thinking and saying about them; and the pictures they drew of the public distress on their account were gratifying to look upon—from their point of view.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋釣咗魚,煮咗晚餐食喇,然後開始猜測村子喺想乜嘢、喺講乜嘢;佢哋畫出嘅公眾因佢哋而悲痛嘅畫面,從佢哋嘅觀點嚟睇,係令人滿意嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們釣了魚,煮了晚餐吃了,然後開始猜測村子在想什麼、在說什麼;他們畫出的公眾因他們而悲痛的畫面,從他們的觀點來看,是令人滿意的。

passages.original: But when the shadows of night closed them in, they gradually ceased to talk, and sat gazing into the fire, with their minds evidently wandering elsewhere.
passages.vernacular: 但夜晚嘅陰影籠罩佢哋時,佢哋漸漸唔再講話,坐住凝視火焰,心顯然游蕩到別處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但夜晚的陰影籠罩他們時,他們漸漸不再說話,坐著凝視火焰,心顯然游蕩到別處。

passages.original: The excitement was gone, now, and Tom and Joe could not keep back thoughts of certain persons at home who were not enjoying this fine frolic as much as they were.
passages.vernacular: 興奮而家消失喇,湯姆同喬無法抑制對家裡某些人嘅想念,嗰啲人並冇像佢哋嗰樣享受呢場美好嘅嬉戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 興奮現在消失了,湯姆和喬無法抑制對家裡某些人的想念,那些人並沒有像他們那樣享受這場美好的嬉戲。

passages.original: Misgivings came; they grew troubled and unhappy; a sigh or two escaped, unawares.
passages.vernacular: 疑慮嚟喇;佢哋變得煩惱不快樂;一兩聲歎息不自覺地溜出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 疑慮來了;他們變得煩惱不快樂;一兩聲歎息不自覺地溜出。

passages.original: By and by Joe timidly ventured upon a roundabout “feeler” as to how the others might look upon a return to civilization—not right now, but—
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地喬膽怯地冒險拐彎抹角地「試探」,其他人會點樣睇待回到文明——唔係而家,但係——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地喬膽怯地冒險拐彎抹角地「試探」,其他人會怎樣看待回到文明——不是現在,但是——

passages.original: Tom withered him with derision!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆用嘲笑讓佢枯萎喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆用嘲笑讓他枯萎了!

passages.original: Huck, being uncommitted as yet, joined in with Tom, and the waverer quickly “explained,” and was glad to get out of the scrape with as little taint of chicken-hearted home-sickness clinging to his garments as he could.
passages.vernacular: 哈克仲冇表態,附和咗湯姆,動搖者好快「解釋」,好高興能擺脫呢個困境,衣服上盡可能少沾上膽小思鄉嘅污點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克還沒有表態,附和了湯姆,動搖者很快「解釋」,很高興能擺脫這個困境,衣服上盡可能少沾上膽小思鄉的污點。

passages.original: Mutiny was effectually laid to rest for the moment.
passages.vernacular: 叛變暫時有效地被平息喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叛變暫時有效地被平息了。

passages.original: As the night deepened, Huck began to nod, and presently to snore.
passages.vernacular: 夜深時,哈克開始打盹,不久開始打鼾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜深時,哈克開始打盹,不久開始打鼾。

passages.original: Joe followed next.
passages.vernacular: 接住係喬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著是喬。

passages.original: Tom lay upon his elbow motionless, for some time, watching the two intently.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆用手肘撐住一動不動地躺咗一會兒,專注地睇住兩人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆用手肘撐著一動不動地躺了一會兒,專注地看著兩人。

passages.original: At last he got up cautiously, on his knees, and went searching among the grass and the flickering reflections flung by the campfire.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢謹慎地跪起嚟,喺草叢同營火投下嘅閃爍倒影中搜尋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他謹慎地跪起來,在草叢和營火投下的閃爍倒影中搜尋。

passages.original: He picked up and inspected several large semi-cylinders of the thin white bark of a sycamore, and finally chose two which seemed to suit him.
passages.vernacular: 佢撿起並檢查咗幾個梧桐樹薄白樹皮嘅大半圓筒,最後選咗兩個似乎適合佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他撿起並檢查了幾個梧桐樹薄白樹皮的大半圓筒,最後選了兩個似乎適合他的。

passages.original: Then he knelt by the fire and painfully wrote something upon each of these with his “red keel”; one he rolled up and put in his jacket pocket, and the other he put in Joe’s hat and removed it to a little distance from the owner.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢跪喺火邊,用佢嘅「紅粉筆」費力地喺每個上面寫咗些乜嘢;一個佢捲起嚟放進外套口袋,另一個放進喬嘅帽子,並把佢移到離主人一小段距離處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他跪在火邊,用他的「紅粉筆」費力地在每個上面寫了些什麼;一個他捲起來放進外套口袋,另一個放進喬的帽子,並把它移到離主人一小段距離處。

passages.original: And he also put into the hat certain schoolboy treasures of almost inestimable value—among them a lump of chalk, an India-rubber ball, three fishhooks, and one of that kind of marbles known as a “sure ’nough crystal.”
passages.vernacular: 佢仲喺帽子裡放咗某些幾乎無價嘅小學生寶物——其中有一塊粉筆、一個橡皮球、三個魚鉤同一顆被稱為「貨真價實水晶」嘅嗰種彈珠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他還在帽子裡放了某些幾乎無價的小學生寶物——其中有一塊粉筆、一個橡皮球、三個魚鉤和一顆被稱為「貨真價實水晶」的那種彈珠。

passages.original: Then he tiptoed his way cautiously among the trees till he felt that he was out of hearing, and straightway broke into a keen run in the direction of the sandbar.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢踮住腳尖小心地穿過樹林,直到覺得已經聽唔到喇,隨即向沙洲嘅方向全速飛奔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他踮著腳尖小心地穿過樹林,直到覺得已經聽不到了,隨即向沙洲的方向全速飛奔。

chapters.title: Chapter XV: Tom Reconnoiters 第十五章:湯姆偵察

passages.original: CH A few minutes later Tom was in the shoal water of the bar, wading toward the Illinois shore.
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘後,湯姆喺沙洲嘅淺水裡,涉水朝伊利諾州嘅岸走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘後,湯姆在沙洲的淺水裡,涉水朝伊利諾州的岸走去。

passages.original: Before the depth reached his middle he was halfway over; the current would permit no more wading, now, so he struck out confidently to swim the remaining hundred yards.
passages.vernacular: 水深到佢腰部之前佢已走過一半;水流而家不允許再涉水,所以佢信心十足地開始游泳,游剩下嘅一百碼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 水深到他腰部之前他已走過一半;水流現在不允許再涉水,所以他信心十足地開始游泳,游剩下的一百碼。

passages.original: He swam quartering upstream, but still was swept downward rather faster than he had expected.
passages.vernacular: 佢斜住逆流游,但仍然被沖向下游,比佢預料嘅快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他斜著逆流游,但仍然被沖向下游,比他預料的快。

passages.original: However, he reached the shore finally, and drifted along till he found a low place and drew himself out.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢終於到達岸邊,順流漂住,直到找到一個低處把自己拉咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,他終於到達岸邊,順流漂著,直到找到一個低處把自己拉了出來。

passages.original: He put his hand on his jacket pocket, found his piece of bark safe, and then struck through the woods, following the shore, with streaming garments.
passages.vernacular: 佢把手放喺外套口袋上,發現佢嗰塊樹皮安全無恙,然後穿過樹林,沿住岸邊,衣服淌住水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把手放在外套口袋上,發現他那塊樹皮安全無恙,然後穿過樹林,沿著岸邊,衣服淌著水。

passages.original: Shortly before ten o’clock he came out into an open place opposite the village, and saw the ferryboat lying in the shadow of the trees and the high bank.
passages.vernacular: 將近十點時,佢嚟到村子對面一塊空地上,睇到渡船停喺樹同高岸嘅陰影裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將近十點時,他來到村子對面一塊空地上,看到渡船停在樹和高岸的陰影裡。

passages.original: Everything was quiet under the blinking stars.
passages.vernacular: 眨眼嘅星星下一切都好安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 眨眼的星星下一切都很安靜。

passages.original: He crept down the bank, watching with all his eyes, slipped into the water, swam three or four strokes and climbed into the skiff that did “yawl” duty at the boat’s stern.
passages.vernacular: 佢爬下河岸,睜大眼睛觀察,滑進水裡,游咗三四下,爬上充當船尾「小艇」嘅嗰艘小艇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他爬下河岸,睜大眼睛觀察,滑進水裡,游了三四下,爬上充當船尾「小艇」的那艘小艇。

passages.original: He laid himself down under the thwarts and waited, panting.
passages.vernacular: 佢躺喺橫板下,喘住氣等待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他躺在橫板下,喘著氣等待。

passages.original: Presently the cracked bell tapped and a voice gave the order to “cast off.”
passages.vernacular: 不久嗰口破鐘敲響,一個聲音下令「解纜」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久那口破鐘敲響,一個聲音下令「解纜」。

passages.original: A minute or two later the skiff’s head was standing high up, against the boat’s swell, and the voyage was begun.
passages.vernacular: 一兩分鐘後,小艇嘅船頭喺船嘅浪頭中高高翹起,航行開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一兩分鐘後,小艇的船頭在船的浪頭中高高翹起,航行開始了。

passages.original: Tom felt happy in his success, for he knew it was the boat’s last trip for the night.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆為佢嘅成功感到高興,因為佢知道呢個係渡船今晚嘅最後一趟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆為他的成功感到高興,因為他知道這是渡船今晚的最後一趟。

passages.original: At the end of a long twelve or fifteen minutes the wheels stopped, and Tom slipped overboard and swam ashore in the dusk, landing fifty yards downstream, out of danger of possible stragglers.
passages.vernacular: 漫長嘅十二或十五分鐘結束時,輪子停喇,湯姆溜出船外,喺暮色中游上岸,喺下游五十碼處上岸,避開可能有落後者嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漫長的十二或十五分鐘結束時,輪子停了,湯姆溜出船外,在暮色中游上岸,在下游五十碼處上岸,避開可能有落後者的危險。

passages.original: He flew along unfrequented alleys, and shortly found himself at his aunt’s back fence.
passages.vernacular: 佢沿住人跡罕至嘅小巷飛奔,不久就到咗佢姨媽嘅後圍欄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沿著人跡罕至的小巷飛奔,不久就到了他姨媽的後圍欄。

passages.original: He climbed over, approached the “ell,” and looked in at the sitting-room window, for a light was burning there.
passages.vernacular: 佢翻過去,接近「側屋」,從起居室嘅窗子往裡睇,因為嗰度點住燈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他翻過去,接近「側屋」,從起居室的窗子往裡看,因為那裡點著燈。

passages.original: There sat Aunt Polly, Sid, Mary, and Joe Harper’s mother, grouped together, talking.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽、希德、瑪麗同喬·哈珀嘅母親坐喺一起,喺談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽、希德、瑪麗和喬·哈珀的母親坐在一起,在談話。

passages.original: They were by the bed, and the bed was between them and the door.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺床邊,床喺佢哋同門之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在床邊,床在他們和門之間。

passages.original: Tom went to the door and began to softly lift the latch; then he pressed gently and the door yielded a crack; he continued pushing cautiously, and quaking every time it creaked, till he judged he might squeeze through on his knees; so he put his head through and began, warily.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆走到門邊,開始輕輕抬起門閂;然後輕輕推,門開咗一道縫;佢繼續謹慎地推,每次佢吱嘎響都發抖,直到佢判斷自己可以跪住擠進去;於是佢把頭伸進去,小心地開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆走到門邊,開始輕輕抬起門閂;然後輕輕推,門開了一道縫;他繼續謹慎地推,每次它吱嘎響都發抖,直到他判斷自己可以跪著擠進去;於是他把頭伸進去,小心地開始。

passages.original: “What makes the candle blow so?” said Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「蠟燭點解咁樣吹?」波莉姨媽講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蠟燭為什麼這樣吹?」波莉姨媽說。

passages.original: Tom hurried up.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆急忙加快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆急忙加快。

passages.original: “Why, that door’s open, I believe.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,嗰門開住,我相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,那門開著,我相信。

passages.original: Why, of course it is.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,當然係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,當然是的。

passages.original: No end of strange things now.
passages.vernacular: 而家奇怪嘅事冇完冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在奇怪的事沒完沒了。

passages.original: Go ’long and shut it, Sid.”
passages.vernacular: 去把佢關上,希德。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去把它關上,希德。」

passages.original: Tom disappeared under the bed just in time.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆剛好及時消失喺床下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆剛好及時消失在床下。

passages.original: He lay and “breathed” himself for a time, and then crept to where he could almost touch his aunt’s foot.
passages.vernacular: 佢躺住「喘」咗一會兒,然後爬到幾乎能碰到佢姨媽嘅腳嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他躺著「喘」了一會兒,然後爬到幾乎能碰到他姨媽的腳的地方。

passages.original: “But as I was saying,” said Aunt Polly, “he warn’t bad, so to say—only mischeevous.
passages.vernacular: 「但正如我講嘅,」波莉姨媽講,「佢不壞,可以咁講——只係淘氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但正如我說的,」波莉姨媽說,「他不壞,可以這麼說——只是淘氣。

passages.original: Only just giddy, and harum-scarum, you know.
passages.vernacular: 只係輕浮,魯莽,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是輕浮,魯莽,你知道。

passages.original: He warn’t any more responsible than a colt.
passages.vernacular: 佢不比一匹小馬更負責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不比一匹小馬更負責任。

passages.original: He never meant any harm, and he was the best-hearted boy that ever was”—and she began to cry.
passages.vernacular: 佢從冇惡意,佢係有史以來心地最好嘅細路」——佢開始哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從沒有惡意,他是有史以來心地最好的孩子」——她開始哭了。

passages.original: “It was just so with my Joe—always full of his devilment, and up to every kind of mischief, but he was just as unselfish and kind as he could be—and laws bless me, to think I went and whipped him for taking that cream, never once recollecting that I throwed it out myself because it was sour, and I never to see him again in this world, never, never, never, poor abused boy!”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅喬都係咁樣——總是滿肚子嘅鬼主意,幹各種各樣嘅惡作劇,但佢無私和善良得唔能夠再無私善良喇——天呀,想想我竟然去為了佢攞奶油鞭打佢,一次都冇記起嗰個係我自己因為酸咗才倒掉嘅,而我喺呢個世界上再都見唔到佢喇,永遠、永遠、永遠,可憐被冤枉嘅細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的喬也是這樣——總是滿肚子的鬼主意,幹各種各樣的惡作劇,但他無私和善良得不能再無私善良了——天哪,想想我竟然去為了他拿奶油鞭打他,一次也沒記起那是我自己因為酸了才倒掉的,而我在這個世界上再也見不到他了,永遠、永遠、永遠,可憐被冤枉的孩子!」

passages.original: And Mrs. Harper sobbed as if her heart would break.
passages.vernacular: 哈珀太太抽泣住,好像心都要碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈珀太太抽泣著,好像心都要碎了。

passages.original: “I hope Tom’s better off where he is,” said Sid, “but if he’d been better in some ways—”
passages.vernacular: 「我希望湯姆喺佢所在嘅地方過得更好,」希德講,「但如果佢喺某些方面更好啲——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望湯姆在他所在的地方過得更好,」希德說,「但如果他在某些方面更好一些——」

passages.original: “Sid!”
passages.vernacular: 「希德!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「希德!」

passages.original: Tom felt the glare of the old lady’s eye, though he could not see it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆感到老太太眼睛嘅目光,雖然佢睇唔見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆感到老太太眼睛的目光,雖然他看不見。

passages.original: “Not a word against my Tom, now that he’s gone!
passages.vernacular: 「佢走喇,不許講一句反對我嘅湯姆嘅話!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他走了,不許說一句反對我的湯姆的話!

passages.original: God’ll take care of him—never you trouble yourself, sir!
passages.vernacular: 上帝會照顧佢——你別操心,先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝會照顧他——你別操心,先生!

passages.original: Oh, Mrs. Harper, I don’t know how to give him up!
passages.vernacular: 哦,哈珀太太,我唔知道點放棄佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,哈珀太太,我不知道怎麼放棄他!

passages.original: I don’t know how to give him up!
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道點放棄佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道怎麼放棄他!

passages.original: He was such a comfort to me, although he tormented my old heart out of me, ’most.”
passages.vernacular: 佢畀咗我咁大嘅安慰,雖然佢幾乎把我老心都折磨掉喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給了我這麼大的安慰,雖然他幾乎把我老心都折磨掉了。」

passages.original: “The Lord giveth and the Lord hath taken away—Blessed be the name of the Lord!
passages.vernacular: 「主賜予,主收回——主嘅名係應當稱頌嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「主賜予,主收回——主的名是應當稱頌的!

passages.original: But it’s so hard—Oh, it’s so hard!
passages.vernacular: 但係咁難——哦,咁難!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是這麼難——哦,這麼難!

passages.original: Only last Saturday my Joe busted a firecracker right under my nose and I knocked him sprawling.
passages.vernacular: 就喺上星期六,我嘅喬就喺我鼻子底下炸響咗一個爆竹,我把佢打得四腳朝天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在上星期六,我的喬就在我鼻子底下炸響了一個爆竹,我把他打得四腳朝天。

passages.original: Little did I know then, how soon—Oh, if it was to do over again I’d hug him and bless him for it.”
passages.vernacular: 我嗰時邊度知道多快——哦,如果能重嚟一次,我會擁抱佢,為此祝福佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我那時哪裡知道多快——哦,如果能重來一次,我會擁抱他,為此祝福他。」

passages.original: “Yes, yes, yes, I know just how you feel, Mrs. Harper, I know just exactly how you feel.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係嘅,係嘅,我確切知道你嘅感受,哈珀太太,我確切知道你嘅感受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是的,是的,我確切知道你的感受,哈珀太太,我確切知道你的感受。

passages.original: No longer ago than yesterday noon, my Tom took and filled the cat full of Pain-killer, and I did think the cretur would tear the house down.
passages.vernacular: 就喺尋日中午,我嘅湯姆攞「痛靈」灌咗貓一肚子,我真以為嗰畜生要把房子拆喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在昨天中午,我的湯姆拿「痛靈」灌了貓一肚子,我真以為那畜生要把房子拆了。

passages.original: And God forgive me, I cracked Tom’s head with my thimble, poor boy, poor dead boy.
passages.vernacular: 求上帝原諒我,我用頂針敲咗湯姆嘅頭,可憐嘅細路,可憐死咗嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求上帝原諒我,我用頂針敲了湯姆的頭,可憐的孩子,可憐死了的孩子。

passages.original: But he’s out of all his troubles now.
passages.vernacular: 但佢而家擺脫咗佢所有嘅煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他現在擺脫了他所有的煩惱。

passages.original: And the last words I ever heard him say was to reproach—”
passages.vernacular: 我最後聽到佢講嘅話係責備——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最後聽到他說的話是責備——」

passages.original: But this memory was too much for the old lady, and she broke entirely down.
passages.vernacular: 但呢個回憶對老太太太過分喇,佢完全崩潰喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這個回憶對老太太太過分了,她完全崩潰了。

passages.original: Tom was snuffling, now, himself—and more in pity of himself than anybody else.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆而家都喺抽鼻子——更多係為了可憐佢自己,而唔係別人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆現在也在抽鼻子——更多是為了可憐他自己,而不是別人。

passages.original: He could hear Mary crying, and putting in a kindly word for him from time to time.
passages.vernacular: 佢聽到瑪麗喺哭,不時替佢講一句好話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他聽到瑪麗在哭,不時替他說一句好話。

passages.original: He began to have a nobler opinion of himself than ever before.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始對自己有比以往更高尚嘅睇法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他開始對自己有比以往更高尚的看法。

passages.original: Still, he was sufficiently touched by his aunt’s grief to long to rush out from under the bed and overwhelm her with joy—and the theatrical gorgeousness of the thing appealed strongly to his nature, too, but he resisted and lay still.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,佢被佢姨媽嘅悲傷深深觸動,渴望從床下衝出嚟,用喜悅淹沒佢——呢件事嘅戲劇性華麗都強烈吸引咗佢嘅天性,但佢抵制喇,靜靜躺住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,他被他姨媽的悲傷深深觸動,渴望從床下衝出來,用喜悅淹沒她——這件事的戲劇性華麗也強烈吸引了他的天性,但他抵制了,靜靜躺著。

passages.original: He went on listening, and gathered by odds and ends that it was conjectured at first that the boys had got drowned while taking a swim; then the small raft had been missed; next, certain boys said the missing lads had promised that the village should “hear something” soon; the wise-heads had “put this and that together” and decided that the lads had gone off on that raft and would turn up at the next town below, presently; but toward noon the raft had been found, lodged against the Missouri shore some five or six miles below the village—and then hope perished; they must be drowned, else hunger would have driven them home by nightfall if not sooner.
passages.vernacular: 佢繼續聽住,零零碎碎地拼湊出:起初推測男孩哋係游泳時淹死喇;然後發現小木筏唔見喇;接住,某些男孩講失蹤嘅小伙子答應過村子不久就會「聽到點乜嘢」;聰明人「把呢個嗰個放喺一起」,斷定小伙子哋乘嗰木筏走喇,不久會喺下面嘅下一個鎮子出現;但將近中午時發現咗木筏,擱淺喺村子下游五六英里嘅密蘇里岸邊——於是希望破滅喇;佢哋一定淹死喇,否則飢餓會迫使佢哋即使不早都喺夜幕降臨前回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他繼續聽著,零零碎碎地拼湊出:起初推測男孩們是游泳時淹死了;然後發現小木筏不見了;接著,某些男孩說失蹤的小伙子答應過村子不久就會「聽到點什麼」;聰明人「把這個那個放在一起」,斷定小伙子們乘那木筏走了,不久會在下面的下一個鎮子出現;但將近中午時發現了木筏,擱淺在村子下游五六英里的密蘇里岸邊——於是希望破滅了;他們一定淹死了,否則飢餓會迫使他們即使不早也在夜幕降臨前回家。

passages.original: It was believed that the search for the bodies had been a fruitless effort merely because the drowning must have occurred in mid-channel, since the boys, being good swimmers, would otherwise have escaped to shore.
passages.vernacular: 人哋相信尋找屍體嘅努力係徒勞嘅,僅僅因為溺水一定發生喺河道中央,否則男孩哋係好游泳手,本可以逃到岸上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們相信尋找屍體的努力是徒勞的,僅僅因為溺水一定發生在河道中央,否則男孩們是好游泳手,本可以逃到岸上。

passages.original: This was Wednesday night.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係星期三晚上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是星期三晚上。

passages.original: If the bodies continued missing until Sunday, all hope would be given over, and the funerals would be preached on that morning.
passages.vernacular: 如果屍體一直失蹤到星期日,所有希望就放棄,嗰天早晨就宣講葬禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果屍體一直失蹤到星期日,所有希望就放棄,那天早晨就宣講葬禮。

passages.original: Tom shuddered.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆戰慄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆戰慄。

passages.original: Mrs. Harper gave a sobbing goodnight and turned to go.
passages.vernacular: 哈珀太太抽泣住道咗晚安,轉身要走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈珀太太抽泣著道了晚安,轉身要走。

passages.original: Then with a mutual impulse the two bereaved women flung themselves into each other’s arms and had a good, consoling cry, and then parted.
passages.vernacular: 然後出於共同嘅衝動,兩位喪子嘅婦人撲進彼此嘅懷抱,痛痛快快地哭咗一場安慰嘅眼淚,然後分開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後出於共同的衝動,兩位喪子的婦人撲進彼此的懷抱,痛痛快快地哭了一場安慰的眼淚,然後分開。

passages.original: Aunt Polly was tender far beyond her wont, in her goodnight to Sid and Mary.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽對希德同瑪麗道晚安時,溫柔得遠超平常。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽對希德和瑪麗道晚安時,溫柔得遠超平常。

passages.original: Sid snuffled a bit and Mary went off crying with all her heart.
passages.vernacular: 希德抽咗抽鼻子,瑪麗全心哭住離開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德抽了抽鼻子,瑪麗全心哭著離開了。

passages.original: Aunt Polly knelt down and prayed for Tom so touchingly, so appealingly, and with such measureless love in her words and her old trembling voice, that he was weltering in tears again, long before she was through.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽跪下為湯姆禱告,咁動人,咁懇切,佢嘅話同佢顫抖嘅老聲音裡有咁無量嘅愛,喺佢仲冇結束之前好久,佢又淚流滿面喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽跪下為湯姆禱告,那麼動人,那麼懇切,她的話和她顫抖的老聲音裡有那麼無量的愛,在她還沒結束之前很久,他又淚流滿面了。

passages.original: He had to keep still long after she went to bed, for she kept making broken-hearted ejaculations from time to time, tossing unrestfully, and turning over.
passages.vernacular: 佢上床後佢唔得不靜止好久,因為佢不時發出傷心嘅感嘆,不安地輾轉翻身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她上床後他不得不靜止很久,因為她不時發出傷心的感嘆,不安地輾轉翻身。

passages.original: But at last she was still, only moaning a little in her sleep.
passages.vernacular: 但最後佢安靜喇,只喺瞓夢中輕輕呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但最後她安靜了,只在睡夢中輕輕呻吟。

passages.original: Now the boy stole out, rose gradually by the bedside, shaded the candle-light with his hand, and stood regarding her.
passages.vernacular: 而家男孩溜出嚟,慢慢從床邊站起,用手遮住燭光,站住睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在男孩溜出來,慢慢從床邊站起,用手遮住燭光,站著看著她。

passages.original: His heart was full of pity for her.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅心充滿對佢嘅憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的心充滿對她的憐憫。

passages.original: He took out his sycamore scroll and placed it by the candle.
passages.vernacular: 佢攞出佢嘅梧桐樹皮卷,放喺蠟燭旁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拿出他的梧桐樹皮卷,放在蠟燭旁。

passages.original: But something occurred to him, and he lingered considering.
passages.vernacular: 但佢想到咗乜嘢,佢停留住考慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他想到了什麼,他停留著考慮。

passages.original: His face lighted with a happy solution of his thought; he put the bark hastily in his pocket.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉因佢思想嘅一個快樂嘅解決而亮起嚟;佢匆忙把樹皮放進口袋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的臉因他思想的一個快樂的解決而亮起來;他匆忙把樹皮放進口袋。

passages.original: Then he bent over and kissed the faded lips, and straightway made his stealthy exit, latching the door behind him.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢彎下腰,吻咗嗰褪色嘅嘴唇,隨即悄悄出去,喺身後閂上咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他彎下腰,吻了那褪色的嘴唇,隨即悄悄出去,在身後閂上了門。

passages.original: He threaded his way back to the ferry landing, found nobody at large there, and walked boldly on board the boat, for he knew she was tenantless except that there was a watchman, who always turned in and slept like a graven image.
passages.vernacular: 佢摸索住回到渡口碼頭,發現嗰度冇人喺外面,大膽地走上船,因為佢知道佢冇人,除咗一個睇守,佢總是一上床就瞓得像雕像一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他摸索著回到渡口碼頭,發現那裡沒有人在外面,大膽地走上船,因為他知道她沒有人,除了一個看守,他總是一上床就睡得像雕像一樣。

passages.original: He untied the skiff at the stern, slipped into it, and was soon rowing cautiously upstream.
passages.vernacular: 佢解開船尾嘅小艇,滑進去,不久就小心地逆流划行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他解開船尾的小艇,滑進去,不久就小心地逆流划行。

passages.original: When he had pulled a mile above the village, he started quartering across and bent himself stoutly to his work.
passages.vernacular: 佢划到村子上游一英里時,開始斜住橫渡,用力埋頭幹活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他划到村子上游一英里時,開始斜著橫渡,用力埋頭幹活。

passages.original: He hit the landing on the other side neatly, for this was a familiar bit of work to him.
passages.vernacular: 佢乾淨利落地到達對岸碼頭,因為呢對佢係熟悉嘅活兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他乾淨利落地到達對岸碼頭,因為這對他是熟悉的活兒。

passages.original: He was moved to capture the skiff, arguing that it might be considered a ship and therefore legitimate prey for a pirate, but he knew a thorough search would be made for it and that might end in revelations.
passages.vernacular: 佢想要劫掠呢艘小艇,爭辯講佢可被視為一艘船,因此係海盜嘅合法獵物,但佢知道會有人徹底搜查佢,嗰可能導致洩露。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想要劫掠這艘小艇,爭辯說它可被視為一艘船,因此是海盜的合法獵物,但他知道會有人徹底搜查它,那可能導致洩露。

passages.original: So he stepped ashore and entered the woods.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢上咗岸,進咗樹林。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他上了岸,進了樹林。

passages.original: He sat down and took a long rest, torturing himself meanwhile to keep awake, and then started warily down the home-stretch.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐下嚟,長長地休息,同時折磨自己以保持清醒,然後謹慎地向回家嘅路走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐下來,長長地休息,同時折磨自己以保持清醒,然後謹慎地向回家的路走去。

passages.original: The night was far spent.
passages.vernacular: 夜已過咗大半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夜已過了大半。

passages.original: It was broad daylight before he found himself fairly abreast the island bar.
passages.vernacular: 直到天大亮,佢才發現自己正好同島上嘅沙洲相對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到天大亮,他才發現自己正好與島上的沙洲相對。

passages.original: He rested again until the sun was well up and gilding the great river with its splendor, and then he plunged into the stream.
passages.vernacular: 佢又休息咗一陣,直到太陽高升,用佢嘅光輝為大河鍍金,然後佢跳進水流。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他又休息了一陣,直到太陽高升,用它的光輝為大河鍍金,然後他跳進水流。

passages.original: A little later he paused, dripping, upon the threshold of the camp, and heard Joe say:
passages.vernacular: 稍後,佢渾身滴水,停喺營地門檻上,聽到喬講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍後,他渾身滴水,停在營地門檻上,聽到喬說:

passages.original: “No, Tom’s true-blue, Huck, and he’ll come back.
passages.vernacular: 「不,湯姆係忠實嘅,哈克,佢會回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,湯姆是忠實的,哈克,他會回來。

passages.original: He won’t desert.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔會逃走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不會逃走。

passages.original: He knows that would be a disgrace to a pirate, and Tom’s too proud for that sort of thing.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道嗰對海盜係恥辱,而湯姆太驕傲喇,唔會做嗰種事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他知道那對海盜是恥辱,而湯姆太驕傲了,不會做那種事。

passages.original: He’s up to something or other.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺搞乜嘢名堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在搞什麼名堂。

passages.original: Now I wonder what?”
passages.vernacular: 而家我想知道係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我想知道是什麼?」

passages.original: “Well, the things is ours, anyway, ain’t they?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢啲嘢無論如何係我哋嘅,唔係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這些東西無論如何是我們的,不是嗎?」

passages.original: “Pretty near, but not yet, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「差不多,但仲唔係,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「差不多,但還不是,哈克。

passages.original: The writing says they are if he ain’t back here to breakfast.”
passages.vernacular: 字上講,如果佢不回嚟食早飯,佢哋就係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 字上說,如果他不回來吃早飯,它們就是。」

passages.original: “Which he is!” exclaimed Tom, with fine dramatic effect, stepping grandly into camp.
passages.vernacular: 「佢回嚟喇!」湯姆帶住精彩嘅戲劇效果喊道,威風凜凜地走進營地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他回來了!」湯姆帶著精彩的戲劇效果喊道,威風凜凜地走進營地。

passages.original: A sumptuous breakfast of bacon and fish was shortly provided, and as the boys set to work upon it, Tom recounted (and adorned) his adventures.
passages.vernacular: 一頓豐盛嘅培根同魚嘅早餐好快準備好,男孩哋開始食時,湯姆敘述(並修飾)咗佢嘅冒險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一頓豐盛的培根和魚的早餐很快準備好,男孩們開始吃時,湯姆敘述(並修飾)了他的冒險。

passages.original: They were a vain and boastful company of heroes when the tale was done.
passages.vernacular: 故事講完時,佢哋係一夥虛榮自誇嘅英雄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 故事講完時,他們是一夥虛榮自誇的英雄。

passages.original: Then Tom hid himself away in a shady nook to sleep till noon, and the other pirates got ready to fish and explore.
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆躲到一個陰涼嘅角落瞓到中午,其他海盜準備去釣魚同探險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆躲到一個陰涼的角落睡到中午,其他海盜準備去釣魚和探險。

chapters.title: Chapter XVI: A Day's Amusements 第十六章:一天的消遣

passages.original: CH After dinner all the gang turned out to hunt for turtle eggs on the bar.
passages.vernacular: 午飯後,全夥人出動去沙洲上找龜蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 午飯後,全夥人出動去沙洲上找龜蛋。

passages.original: They went about poking sticks into the sand, and when they found a soft place they went down on their knees and dug with their hands.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋四處用棍子戳沙子,找到鬆軟嘅地方就跪下用手挖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們四處用棍子戳沙子,找到鬆軟的地方就跪下用手挖。

passages.original: Sometimes they would take fifty or sixty eggs out of one hole.
passages.vernacular: 有時佢哋一個洞裡就能取出五六十個蛋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時他們一個洞裡就能取出五六十個蛋。

passages.original: They were perfectly round white things a trifle smaller than an English walnut.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係完全圓形嘅白色嘢,比一個英國核桃略小。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們是完全圓形的白色東西,比一個英國核桃略小。

passages.original: They had a famous fried-egg feast that night, and another on Friday morning.
passages.vernacular: 嗰晚佢哋食咗著名嘅煎蛋大餐,星期五早晨又食咗一頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那晚他們吃了著名的煎蛋大餐,星期五早晨又吃了一頓。

passages.original: After breakfast they went whooping and prancing out on the bar, and chased each other round and round, shedding clothes as they went, until they were naked, and then continued the frolic far away up the shoal water of the bar, against the stiff current, which latter tripped their legs from under them from time to time and greatly increased the fun.
passages.vernacular: 早餐後佢哋叫喊住、蹦蹦跳跳地跑到沙洲上,一圈又一圈互相追逐,邊跑邊脫衣服,直到赤身裸體,然後繼續遠遠地喺沙洲淺水裡逆住強勁嘅水流嬉戲,水流不時把佢哋嘅腿絆倒,大大增加咗樂趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐後他們叫喊著、蹦蹦跳跳地跑到沙洲上,一圈又一圈互相追逐,邊跑邊脫衣服,直到赤身裸體,然後繼續遠遠地在沙洲淺水裡逆著強勁的水流嬉戲,水流不時把他們的腿絆倒,大大增加了樂趣。

passages.original: And now and then they stooped in a group and splashed water in each other’s faces with their palms, gradually approaching each other, with averted faces to avoid the strangling sprays, and finally gripping and struggling till the best man ducked his neighbor, and then they all went under in a tangle of white legs and arms and came up blowing, sputtering, laughing, and gasping for breath at one and the same time.
passages.vernacular: 時不時佢哋成群彎下腰,用手掌互相潑水到臉上,逐漸互相靠近,別過臉去避免被嗆嘅水花,最後抓住扭打,直到最強嘅一個把鄰居按到水下,然後佢哋全都喺一團白腿白臂中沉下去,冒出嚟時同時吹氣、噴水、大笑、喘息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時不時他們成群彎下腰,用手掌互相潑水到臉上,逐漸互相靠近,別過臉去避免被嗆的水花,最後抓住扭打,直到最強的一個把鄰居按到水下,然後他們全都在一團白腿白臂中沉下去,冒出來時同時吹氣、噴水、大笑、喘息。

passages.original: When they were well exhausted, they would run out and sprawl on the dry, hot sand, and lie there and cover themselves up with it, and by and by break for the water again and go through the original performance once more.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋筋疲力盡時,會跑出嚟四仰八叉地躺喺乾熱嘅沙上,躺喺嗰度用沙子蓋住自己,不久又衝向水裡,再把原來嘅表演重嚟一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們筋疲力盡時,會跑出來四仰八叉地躺在乾熱的沙上,躺在那裡用沙子蓋住自己,不久又衝向水裡,再把原來的表演重來一遍。

passages.original: Finally it occurred to them that their naked skin represented flesh-colored “tights” very fairly; so they drew a ring in the sand and had a circus—with three clowns in it, for none would yield this proudest post to his neighbor.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢哋想到,佢哋赤裸嘅皮膚相當像肉色嘅「緊身衣」;於是佢哋喺沙地上畫咗個圈,辦咗個馬戲團——裡面有三個小丑,因為冇人肯把呢個最光榮嘅職位讓畀鄰居。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他們想到,他們赤裸的皮膚相當像肉色的「緊身衣」;於是他們在沙地上畫了個圈,辦了個馬戲團——裡面有三個小丑,因為沒有人肯把這個最光榮的職位讓給鄰居。

passages.original: Next they got their marbles and played “knucks” and “ringtaw” and “keeps” till that amusement grew stale.
passages.vernacular: 接住佢哋攞出彈珠,玩「彈指」、「環彈」同「贏彈」,直到呢種娛樂變得乏味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著他們拿出彈珠,玩「彈指」、「環彈」和「贏彈」,直到這種娛樂變得乏味。

passages.original: Then Joe and Huck had another swim, but Tom would not venture, because he found that in kicking off his trousers he had kicked his string of rattlesnake rattles off his ankle, and he wondered how he had escaped cramp so long without the protection of this mysterious charm.
passages.vernacular: 然後喬同哈克又游咗一次泳,但湯姆唔敢,因為佢發現踢掉褲子時,把佢腳踝上嘅一串響尾蛇響環踢掉喇,佢納悶冇呢個神祕護符嘅保護,佢點咁久冇抽筋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後喬和哈克又游了一次泳,但湯姆不敢,因為他發現踢掉褲子時,把他腳踝上的一串響尾蛇響環踢掉了,他納悶沒有這個神祕護符的保護,他怎麼這麼久沒有抽筋。

passages.original: He did not venture again until he had found it, and by that time the other boys were tired and ready to rest.
passages.vernacular: 直到找到佢佢才又敢下水,嗰時其他男孩已累喇,準備休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到找到它他才又敢下水,那時其他男孩已累了,準備休息。

passages.original: They gradually wandered apart, dropped into the “dumps,” and fell to gazing longingly across the wide river to where the village lay drowsing in the sun.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋漸漸地散開,陷入「消沉」,開始渴望地遠望寬闊嘅河嗰邊喺陽光下打盹嘅村子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們漸漸地散開,陷入「消沉」,開始渴望地遠望寬闊的河那邊在陽光下打盹的村子。

passages.original: Tom found himself writing “BECKY” in the sand with his big toe; he scratched it out, and was angry with himself for his weakness.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆發現自己用大腳趾喺沙上寫「貝琪」;佢把佢劃掉,為自己嘅軟弱生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆發現自己用大腳趾在沙上寫「貝琪」;他把它劃掉,為自己的軟弱生氣。

passages.original: But he wrote it again, nevertheless; he could not help it.
passages.vernacular: 但佢定係又寫咗一遍;佢忍不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他還是又寫了一遍;他忍不住。

passages.original: He erased it once more and then took himself out of temptation by driving the other boys together and joining them.
passages.vernacular: 佢又擦掉一次,然後把其他男孩趕到一起,加入佢哋,擺脫咗誘惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他又擦掉一次,然後把其他男孩趕到一起,加入他們,擺脫了誘惑。

passages.original: But Joe’s spirits had gone down almost beyond resurrection.
passages.vernacular: 但喬嘅情緒已經落到幾乎無法恢復嘅地步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但喬的情緒已經落到幾乎無法恢復的地步。

passages.original: He was so homesick that he could hardly endure the misery of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢咁想家,幾乎忍受不了嗰種痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他那麼想家,幾乎忍受不了那種痛苦。

passages.original: The tears lay very near the surface.
passages.vernacular: 眼淚離表面好近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 眼淚離表面很近。

passages.original: Huck was melancholy, too.
passages.vernacular: 哈克都憂鬱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克也憂鬱。

passages.original: Tom was downhearted, but tried hard not to show it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆情緒低落,但努力不表現出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆情緒低落,但努力不表現出來。

passages.original: He had a secret which he was not ready to tell, yet, but if this mutinous depression was not broken up soon, he would have to bring it out.
passages.vernacular: 佢有一個仲冇準備講嘅祕密,但如果呢種叛變嘅沮喪不即刻被打破,佢就得把佢攞出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有一個還沒準備說的祕密,但如果這種叛變的沮喪不馬上被打破,他就得把它拿出來。

passages.original: He said, with a great show of cheerfulness:
passages.vernacular: 佢故作好快活地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他故作十分快活地說:

passages.original: “I bet there’s been pirates on this island before, boys.
passages.vernacular: 「我打賭呢座島以前有過海盜,夥計哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我打賭這座島以前有過海盜,夥計們。

passages.original: We’ll explore it again.
passages.vernacular: 我哋再去探索一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們再去探索一次。

passages.original: They’ve hid treasures here somewhere.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺呢度某處藏咗寶藏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在這裡某處藏了寶藏。

passages.original: How’d you feel to light on a rotten chest full of gold and silver—hey?”
passages.vernacular: 你哋碰到一個腐爛嘅、裝滿金銀嘅箱子係乜嘢感覺——嗯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們碰到一個腐爛的、裝滿金銀的箱子是什麼感覺——嗯?」

passages.original: But it roused only faint enthusiasm, which faded out, with no reply.
passages.vernacular: 但呢只激起微弱嘅熱情,佢消退喇,冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這只激起微弱的熱情,它消退了,沒有回答。

passages.original: Tom tried one or two other seductions; but they failed, too.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆又試咗一兩種誘惑;但都失敗喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆又試了一兩種誘惑;但也失敗了。

passages.original: It was discouraging work.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係令人氣餒嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是令人氣餒的工作。

passages.original: Joe sat poking up the sand with a stick and looking very gloomy.
passages.vernacular: 喬坐住用棍子戳沙子,睇起嚟好陰鬱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬坐著用棍子戳沙子,看起來非常陰鬱。

passages.original: Finally he said:
passages.vernacular: 最後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他說:

passages.original: “Oh, boys, let’s give it up.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,夥計哋,我哋放棄吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,夥計們,我們放棄吧。

passages.original: I want to go home.
passages.vernacular: 我想回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想回家。

passages.original: It’s so lonesome.”
passages.vernacular: 咁孤單。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這麼孤單。」

passages.original: “Oh no, Joe, you’ll feel better by and by,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「哦不,喬,你過一會兒就會覺得好些,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦不,喬,你過一會兒就會覺得好些,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “Just think of the fishing that’s here.”
passages.vernacular: 「想想呢度嘅釣魚吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想想這裡的釣魚吧。」

passages.original: “I don’t care for fishing.
passages.vernacular: 「我不在乎釣魚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不在乎釣魚。

passages.original: I want to go home.”
passages.vernacular: 我想回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想回家。」

passages.original: “But, Joe, there ain’t such another swimming-place anywhere.”
passages.vernacular: 「但係,喬,別嘅地方冇咁樣嘅游泳地方喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,喬,別的地方沒有這樣的游泳地方了。」

passages.original: “Swimming’s no good.
passages.vernacular: 「游泳不好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「游泳不好。

passages.original: I don’t seem to care for it, somehow, when there ain’t anybody to say I sha’n’t go in.
passages.vernacular: 當冇人講我不許下水時,我唔知點就不在乎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當沒有人說我不許下水時,我不知怎麼就不在乎了。

passages.original: I mean to go home.”
passages.vernacular: 我決心回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我決心回家。」

passages.original: “Oh, shucks!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,算喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,算了!

passages.original: Baby!
passages.vernacular: 寶寶!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寶寶!

passages.original: You want to see your mother, I reckon.”
passages.vernacular: 你想見你媽媽,我想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想見你媽媽,我想。」

passages.original: “Yes, I do want to see my mother—and you would, too, if you had one.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我確實想見我媽媽——如果你有一個,你都會想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我確實想見我媽媽——如果你有一個,你也會想。

passages.original: I ain’t any more baby than you are.”
passages.vernacular: 我不比你更像寶寶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不比你更像寶寶。」

passages.original: And Joe snuffled a little.
passages.vernacular: 喬抽咗抽鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬抽了抽鼻子。

passages.original: “Well, we’ll let the crybaby go home to his mother, won’t we, Huck?
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我哋讓愛哭鬼回家找佢媽媽,對吧,哈克?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我們讓愛哭鬼回家找他媽媽,對吧,哈克?

passages.original: Poor thing—does it want to see its mother?
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅嘢——佢想見佢媽媽嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的東西——它想見它媽媽嗎?

passages.original: And so it shall.
passages.vernacular: 嗰佢就能見到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那它就能見到。

passages.original: You like it here, don’t you, Huck?
passages.vernacular: 你鍾意呢度,對吧,哈克?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你喜歡這裡,對吧,哈克?

passages.original: We’ll stay, won’t we?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋留下,對吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們留下,對吧?」

passages.original: Huck said, “Y-e-s”—without any heart in it.
passages.vernacular: 哈克講:「係——嘅」——冇啲心思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克說:「是——的」——沒有一點心思。

passages.original: “I’ll never speak to you again as long as I live,” said Joe, rising.
passages.vernacular: 「只要我活住,我再都不同你講話喇,」喬站起來講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只要我活著,我再也不同你說話了,」喬站起來說。

passages.original: “There now!”
passages.vernacular: 「好喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了!」

passages.original: And he moved moodily away and began to dress himself.
passages.vernacular: 佢陰沉地走開,開始穿衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他陰沉地走開,開始穿衣服。

passages.original: “Who cares!” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「邊個在乎!」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰在乎!」湯姆說。

passages.original: “Nobody wants you to.
passages.vernacular: 「冇人要你講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒人要你說。

passages.original: Go ’long home and get laughed at.
passages.vernacular: 回家去,被人笑吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回家去,被人笑吧。

passages.original: Oh, you’re a nice pirate.
passages.vernacular: 哦,你係個好海盜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,你是個好海盜。

passages.original: Huck and me ain’t crybabies.
passages.vernacular: 哈克同我唔係愛哭鬼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克和我不是愛哭鬼。

passages.original: We’ll stay, won’t we, Huck?
passages.vernacular: 我哋留下,對吧,哈克?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們留下,對吧,哈克?

passages.original: Let him go if he wants to.
passages.vernacular: 佢想走就讓佢走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想走就讓他走吧。

passages.original: I reckon we can get along without him, per’aps.”
passages.vernacular: 我想冇佢我哋或者能過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想沒有他我們也許能過。」

passages.original: But Tom was uneasy, nevertheless, and was alarmed to see Joe go sullenly on with his dressing.
passages.vernacular: 但湯姆定係不安,睇到喬繼續悶悶地穿衣服,佢好驚慌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但湯姆還是不安,看到喬繼續悶悶地穿衣服,他很驚慌。

passages.original: And then it was discomforting to see Huck eying Joe’s preparations so wistfully, and keeping up such an ominous silence.
passages.vernacular: 然後睇到哈克咁渴望地睇住喬嘅準備,並保持嗰種不祥嘅沉默,令人不舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後看到哈克那麼渴望地看著喬的準備,並保持那種不祥的沉默,令人不舒服。

passages.original: Presently, without a parting word, Joe began to wade off toward the Illinois shore.
passages.vernacular: 不久,喬冇告別嘅話,開始涉水朝伊利諾州岸走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久,喬沒有告別的話,開始涉水朝伊利諾州岸走去。

passages.original: Tom’s heart began to sink.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅心開始下沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的心開始下沉。

passages.original: He glanced at Huck.
passages.vernacular: 佢瞥咗一眼哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他瞥了一眼哈克。

passages.original: Huck could not bear the look, and dropped his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 哈克受不了嗰目光,垂下眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克受不了那目光,垂下眼睛。

passages.original: Then he said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他說:

passages.original: “I want to go, too, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「我都想去,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也想去,湯姆。

passages.original: It was getting so lonesome anyway, and now it’ll be worse.
passages.vernacular: 反正越嚟越孤單,而家會更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正越來越孤單,現在會更糟。

passages.original: Let’s us go, too, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋都走吧,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們也走吧,湯姆。」

passages.original: “I won’t!
passages.vernacular: 「我不!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不!

passages.original: You can all go, if you want to.
passages.vernacular: 你哋想嘅話都可以走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們想的話都可以走。

passages.original: I mean to stay.”
passages.vernacular: 我決心留下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我決心留下。」

passages.original: “Tom, I better go.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我最好走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我最好走。」

passages.original: “Well, go ’long—who’s hendering you.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,走吧——邊個攔你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,走吧——誰攔你。」

passages.original: Huck began to pick up his scattered clothes.
passages.vernacular: 哈克開始撿起佢散落嘅衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克開始撿起他散落的衣服。

passages.original: He said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “Tom, I wisht you’d come, too.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我希望你都嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我希望你也來。

passages.original: Now you think it over.
passages.vernacular: 而家你想想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你想想。

passages.original: We’ll wait for you when we get to shore.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋到岸上等你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們到岸上等你。」

passages.original: “Well, you’ll wait a blame long time, that’s all.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,你哋要等好久,就咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,你們要等很久,就這樣。」

passages.original: Huck started sorrowfully away, and Tom stood looking after him, with a strong desire tugging at his heart to yield his pride and go along too.
passages.vernacular: 哈克悲傷地開始走開,湯姆站住睇住佢嘅背影,一種強烈嘅願望牽引住佢嘅心,要放棄自尊都跟住去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克悲傷地開始走開,湯姆站著看著他的背影,一種強烈的願望牽引著他的心,要放棄自尊也跟著去。

passages.original: He hoped the boys would stop, but they still waded slowly on.
passages.vernacular: 佢希望男孩哋會停下,但佢哋仍緩緩涉水前行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他希望男孩們會停下,但他們仍緩緩涉水前行。

passages.original: It suddenly dawned on Tom that it was become very lonely and still.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆突然意識到,四周變得好孤單同寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆突然意識到,四周變得非常孤單和寂靜。

passages.original: He made one final struggle with his pride, and then darted after his comrades, yelling:
passages.vernacular: 佢同自己嘅自尊作咗最後嘅掙扎,然後衝向佢嘅夥伴,大喊:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他同自己的自尊作了最後的掙扎,然後衝向他的夥伴,大喊:

passages.original: “Wait!
passages.vernacular: 「等等!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等等!

passages.original: Wait!
passages.vernacular: 等等!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等等!

passages.original: I want to tell you something!”
passages.vernacular: 我有事告訴你哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有事告訴你們!」

passages.original: They presently stopped and turned around.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不久停下轉過身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不久停下轉過身來。

passages.original: When he got to where they were, he began unfolding his secret, and they listened moodily till at last they saw the “point” he was driving at, and then they set up a warwhoop of applause and said it was “splendid!” and said if he had told them at first, they wouldn’t have started away.
passages.vernacular: 佢到咗佢哋嗰度,開始展開佢嘅祕密,佢哋陰鬱地聽住,直到最後佢哋睇出佢要講嘅「重點」,然後佢哋發出歡呼嘅戰吼,講「太棒喇!」講如果佢一開始就告訴佢哋,佢哋就唔會走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他到了他們那裡,開始展開他的祕密,他們陰鬱地聽著,直到最後他們看出他要說的「重點」,然後他們發出歡呼的戰吼,說「太棒了!」說如果他一開始就告訴他們,他們就不會走了。

passages.original: He made a plausible excuse; but his real reason had been the fear that not even the secret would keep them with him any very great length of time, and so he had meant to hold it in reserve as a last seduction.
passages.vernacular: 佢編咗一個似係而非嘅藉口;但佢真正嘅原因係害怕連祕密都唔能夠把佢哋留喺身邊好長時間,所以佢打算把佢留作最後嘅誘惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他編了一個似是而非的藉口;但他真正的原因是害怕連祕密也不能把他們留在身邊很長時間,所以他打算把它留作最後的誘惑。

passages.original: The lads came gayly back and went at their sports again with a will, chattering all the time about Tom’s stupendous plan and admiring the genius of it.
passages.vernacular: 小伙子哋高興地回嚟,有勁地又投入佢哋嘅運動,一直喋喋不休地談論湯姆驚人嘅計畫,欽佩佢嘅天才。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小伙子們高興地回來,有勁地又投入他們的運動,一直喋喋不休地談論湯姆驚人的計畫,欽佩它的天才。

passages.original: After a dainty egg and fish dinner, Tom said he wanted to learn to smoke, now.
passages.vernacular: 喺一頓精緻嘅蛋同魚午餐後,湯姆講佢而家想學抽菸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一頓精緻的蛋和魚午餐後,湯姆說他現在想學抽菸。

passages.original: Joe caught at the idea and said he would like to try, too.
passages.vernacular: 喬抓住呢個主意,講佢都想試試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬抓住這個主意,說他也想試試。

passages.original: So Huck made pipes and filled them.
passages.vernacular: 於是哈克做咗菸斗,裝滿煙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是哈克做了菸斗,裝滿煙。

passages.original: These novices had never smoked anything before but cigars made of grapevine, and they “bit” the tongue, and were not considered manly anyway.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲新手以前除咗葡萄藤做嘅雪茄乜嘢都冇抽過,佢「咬」舌頭,而且無論如何不被認為有男子氣概。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些新手以前除了葡萄藤做的雪茄什麼也沒抽過,它「咬」舌頭,而且無論如何不被認為有男子氣概。

passages.original: Now they stretched themselves out on their elbows and began to puff, charily, and with slender confidence.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢哋用手肘撐住伸展身子,開始吸,謹慎地,信心微弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他們用手肘撐著伸展身子,開始吸,謹慎地,信心微弱。

passages.original: The smoke had an unpleasant taste, and they gagged a little, but Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 煙有一種令人不快嘅味道,佢哋有點作嘔,但湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 煙有一種令人不快的味道,他們有點作嘔,但湯姆說:

passages.original: “Why, it’s just as easy!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,咁容易!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,這麼容易!

passages.original: If I’d a knowed this was all, I’d a learnt long ago.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我知道只係咁樣,我早就學喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我知道只是這樣,我早就學了。」

passages.original: “So would I,” said Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「我都係,」喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是,」喬說。

passages.original: “It’s just nothing.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢乜嘢都唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這什麼也不是。」

passages.original: “Why, many a time I’ve looked at people smoking, and thought well I wish I could do that; but I never thought I could,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我多次睇住人哋抽菸,想,我希望我能嗰樣;但我從冇想到我能,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我多次看著人們抽菸,想,我希望我能那樣;但我從沒想到我能,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “That’s just the way with me, hain’t it, Huck?
passages.vernacular: 「我就係咁樣,唔係嗎,哈克?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就是這樣,不是嗎,哈克?

passages.original: You’ve heard me talk just that way—haven’t you, Huck?
passages.vernacular: 你聽過我就咁樣講——對吧,哈克?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聽過我就這樣說——對吧,哈克?

passages.original: I’ll leave it to Huck if I haven’t.”
passages.vernacular: 我讓哈克嚟評判我有冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讓哈克來評判我有沒有。」

passages.original: “Yes—heaps of times,” said Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——好多次,」哈克講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——好多次,」哈克說。

passages.original: “Well, I have too,” said Tom; “oh, hundreds of times.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我都係,」湯姆講;「哦,幾百次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我也是,」湯姆說;「哦,幾百次。

passages.original: Once down by the slaughter-house.
passages.vernacular: 有一次喺屠宰場嗰邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一次在屠宰場那邊。

passages.original: Don’t you remember, Huck?
passages.vernacular: 你不記得咗嗎,哈克?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不記得了嗎,哈克?

passages.original: Bob Tanner was there, and Johnny Miller, and Jeff Thatcher, when I said it.
passages.vernacular: 我講嘅時候,鮑勃·坦納喺嗰度,強尼·米勒都喺,傑夫·撒切爾都喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說的時候,鮑勃·坦納在那裡,強尼·米勒也在,傑夫·撒切爾也在。

passages.original: Don’t you remember, Huck, ’bout me saying that?”
passages.vernacular: 你不記得咗嗎,哈克,我講嗰話嘅事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不記得了嗎,哈克,我說那話的事?」

passages.original: “Yes, that’s so,” said Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係咁樣,」哈克講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是這樣,」哈克說。

passages.original: “That was the day after I lost a white alley.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係我丟咗一顆白大理石彈珠嘅第二天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是我丟了一顆白大理石彈珠的第二天。

passages.original: No, ’twas the day before.”
passages.vernacular: 不,係前一天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,是前一天。」

passages.original: “There—I told you so,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「睇——我告訴你吧,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看——我告訴你吧,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “Huck recollects it.”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克記得。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克記得。」

passages.original: “I bleeve I could smoke this pipe all day,” said Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「我相信我可以抽呢個菸斗抽一整天,」喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信我可以抽這個菸斗抽一整天,」喬說。

passages.original: “I don’t feel sick.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不覺得噁心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不覺得噁心。」

passages.original: “Neither do I,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「我都不覺得,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也不覺得,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “I could smoke it all day.
passages.vernacular: 「我可以抽一整天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以抽一整天。

passages.original: But I bet you Jeff Thatcher couldn’t.”
passages.vernacular: 但我打賭傑夫·撒切爾做唔到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我打賭傑夫·撒切爾做不到。」

passages.original: “Jeff Thatcher!
passages.vernacular: 「傑夫·撒切爾!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「傑夫·撒切爾!

passages.original: Why, he’d keel over just with two draws.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,佢兩口就會翻倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,他兩口就會翻倒。

passages.original: Just let him try it once.
passages.vernacular: 只要讓佢試一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要讓他試一次。

passages.original: He’d see!”
passages.vernacular: 佢會知道!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會知道!」

passages.original: “I bet he would.
passages.vernacular: 「我打賭佢會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我打賭他會。

passages.original: And Johnny Miller—I wish could see Johnny Miller tackle it once.”
passages.vernacular: 仲有強尼·米勒——我希望能睇到強尼·米勒試一次。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有強尼·米勒——我希望能看到強尼·米勒試一次。」

passages.original: “Oh, don’t I!” said Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我都係!」喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我也是!」喬說。

passages.original: “Why, I bet you Johnny Miller couldn’t any more do this than nothing.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我打賭強尼·米勒做呢個乜嘢都做唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我打賭強尼·米勒做這個什麼也做不到。

passages.original: Just one little snifter would fetch him.”
passages.vernacular: 只要一口小酒就能撂倒佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要一口小酒就能撂倒他。」

passages.original: “’Deed it would, Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅會,喬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的會,喬。

passages.original: Say—I wish the boys could see us now.”
passages.vernacular: 喂——我希望男孩哋而家能睇到我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂——我希望男孩們現在能看到我們。」

passages.original: “So do I.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是。」

passages.original: “Say—boys, don’t say anything about it, and some time when they’re around, I’ll come up to you and say, ‘Joe, got a pipe?
passages.vernacular: 「喂——夥計哋,唔好講呢件事,改天佢哋喺附近時,我走到你哋面前講:『喬,有菸斗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂——夥計們,別說這件事,改天他們在附近時,我走到你們面前說:『喬,有菸斗嗎?

passages.original: I want a smoke.’
passages.vernacular: 我想抽一口。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想抽一口。』

passages.original: And you’ll say, kind of careless like, as if it warn’t anything, you’ll say, ‘Yes, I got my old pipe, and another one, but my tobacker ain’t very good.’
passages.vernacular: 你就講,有點漫不經心嘅樣子,好像乜嘢都不算,你講:『有,我有我嘅舊菸斗,仲有另一支,但我嘅煙草不太好。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就說,有點漫不經心的樣子,好像什麼也不算,你說:『有,我有我的舊菸斗,還有另一支,但我的煙草不太好。』

passages.original: And I’ll say, ‘Oh, that’s all right, if it’s strong enough.’
passages.vernacular: 我講:『哦,冇關係,只要夠烈。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說:『哦,沒關係,只要夠烈。』

passages.original: And then you’ll out with the pipes, and we’ll light up just as ca’m, and then just see ’em look!”
passages.vernacular: 然後你攞出菸斗,我哋好鎮定地點燃,然後睇佢哋嘅樣子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後你拿出菸斗,我們很鎮定地點燃,然後看他們的樣子!」

passages.original: “By jings, that’ll be gay, Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,嗰會好棒,湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,那會很棒,湯姆!

passages.original: I wish it was now!”
passages.vernacular: 我希望而家就係!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望現在就是!」

passages.original: “So do I!
passages.vernacular: 「我都係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是!

passages.original: And when we tell ’em we learned when we was off pirating, won’t they wish they’d been along?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋告訴佢哋我哋出去當海盜時學會嘅,佢哋唔會希望自己都一起去嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們告訴他們我們出去當海盜時學會的,他們不會希望自己也一起去嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, I reckon not!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我想唔會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我想不會!

passages.original: I’ll just bet they will!”
passages.vernacular: 我打賭佢哋會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打賭他們會!」

passages.original: So the talk ran on.
passages.vernacular: 於是談話繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是談話繼續。

passages.original: But presently it began to flag a trifle, and grow disjointed.
passages.vernacular: 但不久佢開始有點減弱,變得支離破碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不久它開始有點減弱,變得支離破碎。

passages.original: The silences widened; the expectoration marvellously increased.
passages.vernacular: 沉默擴大;吐口水奇妙地增加。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉默擴大;吐口水奇妙地增加。

passages.original: Every pore inside the boys’ cheeks became a spouting fountain; they could scarcely bail out the cellars under their tongues fast enough to prevent an inundation; little overflowings down their throats occurred in spite of all they could do, and sudden retchings followed every time.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋頰內嘅每個毛孔都成咗噴泉;佢哋幾乎嚟不及把舌頭下嘅地窖舀乾,以防氾濫;不管佢哋點做,小小嘅溢流定係流進喉嚨,每次隨之而嚟嘅係突然嘅乾嘔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們頰內的每個毛孔都成了噴泉;他們幾乎來不及把舌頭下的地窖舀乾,以防氾濫;不管他們怎麼做,小小的溢流還是流進喉嚨,每次隨之而來的是突然的乾嘔。

passages.original: Both boys were looking very pale and miserable, now.
passages.vernacular: 兩個男孩而家睇起嚟都好蒼白同悲慘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個男孩現在看起來都非常蒼白和悲慘。

passages.original: Joe’s pipe dropped from his nerveless fingers.
passages.vernacular: 喬嘅菸斗從佢無力嘅手指間掉下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬的菸斗從他無力的手指間掉下。

passages.original: Tom’s followed.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅跟住掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的跟著掉。

passages.original: Both fountains were going furiously and both pumps bailing with might and main.
passages.vernacular: 兩個噴泉都喺猛烈噴湧,兩個水泵都喺拼命舀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個噴泉都在猛烈噴湧,兩個水泵都在拼命舀。

passages.original: Joe said feebly:
passages.vernacular: 喬虛弱地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬虛弱地說:

passages.original: “I’ve lost my knife.
passages.vernacular: 「我丟咗我嘅刀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我丟了我的刀。

passages.original: I reckon I better go and find it.”
passages.vernacular: 我想我最好去找找。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我最好去找找。」

passages.original: Tom said, with quivering lips and halting utterance:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘴唇顫抖,斷斷續續地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆嘴唇顫抖,斷斷續續地說:

passages.original: “I’ll help you.
passages.vernacular: 「我幫你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我幫你。

passages.original: You go over that way and I’ll hunt around by the spring.
passages.vernacular: 你往嗰邊走,我喺泉水附近找。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你往那邊走,我在泉水附近找。

passages.original: No, you needn’t come, Huck—we can find it.”
passages.vernacular: 不,你唔使嚟,哈克——我哋能找到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,你不用來,哈克——我們能找到。」

passages.original: So Huck sat down again, and waited an hour.
passages.vernacular: 於是哈克又坐下,等咗一個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是哈克又坐下,等了一個小時。

passages.original: Then he found it lonesome, and went to find his comrades.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢覺得孤單,去找佢嘅夥伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他覺得孤單,去找他的夥伴。

passages.original: They were wide apart in the woods, both very pale, both fast asleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺樹林裡分得好開,兩人都好蒼白,都瞓得好沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在樹林裡分得很開,兩人都很蒼白,都睡得很沉。

passages.original: But something informed him that if they had had any trouble they had got rid of it.
passages.vernacular: 但有乜嘢嘢告訴佢,如果佢哋曾有麻煩,而家已經擺脫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但有什麼東西告訴他,如果他們曾有麻煩,現在已經擺脫了。

passages.original: They were not talkative at supper that night.
passages.vernacular: 嗰晚食晚餐時佢哋不太愛講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那晚吃晚餐時他們不太愛說話。

passages.original: They had a humble look, and when Huck prepared his pipe after the meal and was going to prepare theirs, they said no, they were not feeling very well—something they ate at dinner had disagreed with them.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋有一副謙卑嘅樣子,哈克喺飯後準備佢嘅菸斗,打算準備佢哋嘅時,佢哋講不,佢哋感覺不太好——午飯食嘅嘢同佢哋不合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們有一副謙卑的樣子,哈克在飯後準備他的菸斗,打算準備他們的時,他們說不,他們感覺不太好——午飯吃的東西同他們不合。

passages.original: About midnight Joe awoke, and called the boys.
passages.vernacular: 大約午夜,喬醒喇,叫醒男孩哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約午夜,喬醒了,叫醒男孩們。

passages.original: There was a brooding oppressiveness in the air that seemed to bode something.
passages.vernacular: 空氣中有一種沉悶嘅壓抑,似乎預示住乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 空氣中有一種沉悶的壓抑,似乎預示著什麼。

passages.original: The boys huddled themselves together and sought the friendly companionship of the fire, though the dull dead heat of the breathless atmosphere was stifling.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋擠喺一起,尋求火嘅友善陪伴,雖然悶熱冇風嘅氣氛令人窒息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們擠在一起,尋求火的友善陪伴,雖然悶熱沒有風的氣氛令人窒息。

passages.original: They sat still, intent and waiting.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋靜靜坐住,專注而等待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們靜靜坐著,專注而等待。

passages.original: The solemn hush continued.
passages.vernacular: 莊嚴嘅寂靜持續住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 莊嚴的寂靜持續著。

passages.original: Beyond the light of the fire everything was swallowed up in the blackness of darkness.
passages.vernacular: 火光之外,一切都被黑暗嘅漆黑吞冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 火光之外,一切都被黑暗的漆黑吞沒了。

passages.original: Presently there came a quivering glow that vaguely revealed the foliage for a moment and then vanished.
passages.vernacular: 不久出現一道顫動嘅光,朦朧地照出樹葉片刻,然後消失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久出現一道顫動的光,朦朧地照出樹葉片刻,然後消失。

passages.original: By and by another came, a little stronger.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地又嚟一道,稍強啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地又來一道,稍強一點。

passages.original: Then another.
passages.vernacular: 然後又一道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後又一道。

passages.original: Then a faint moan came sighing through the branches of the forest and the boys felt a fleeting breath upon their cheeks, and shuddered with the fancy that the Spirit of the Night had gone by.
passages.vernacular: 然後一聲微弱嘅呻吟歎息住穿過森林嘅樹枝,男孩哋感到臉頰上一陣短暫嘅氣息,顫抖著想像夜晚嘅精靈經過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一聲微弱的呻吟歎息著穿過森林的樹枝,男孩們感到臉頰上一陣短暫的氣息,顫抖著想像夜晚的精靈經過了。

passages.original: There was a pause.
passages.vernacular: 有一陣停頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一陣停頓。

passages.original: Now a weird flash turned night into day and showed every little grassblade, separate and distinct, that grew about their feet.
passages.vernacular: 而家一道怪異嘅閃光把黑夜變成白晝,顯示出佢哋腳邊生長嘅每一片小草葉,單獨而清晰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在一道怪異的閃光把黑夜變成白晝,顯示出他們腳邊生長的每一片小草葉,單獨而清晰。

passages.original: And it showed three white, startled faces, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢都顯示出三張白色、受驚嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它也顯示出三張白色、受驚的臉。

passages.original: A deep peal of thunder went rolling and tumbling down the heavens and lost itself in sullen rumblings in the distance.
passages.vernacular: 一聲深沉嘅雷鳴滾過天空,翻滾而下,消失喺遠處陰鬱嘅隆隆聲中。
