passages.vernacularMandarin: 一聲深沉的雷鳴滾過天空,翻滾而下,消失在遠處陰鬱的隆隆聲中。

passages.original: A sweep of chilly air passed by, rustling all the leaves and snowing the flaky ashes broadcast about the fire.
passages.vernacular: 一陣寒冷嘅氣流經過,沙沙吹動所有嘅葉子,把片狀嘅灰燼像雪一樣大面積撒喺火堆周圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣寒冷的氣流經過,沙沙吹動所有的葉子,把片狀的灰燼像雪一樣大面積撒在火堆周圍。

passages.original: Another fierce glare lit up the forest and an instant crash followed that seemed to rend the treetops right over the boys’ heads.
passages.vernacular: 又一道猛烈嘅亮光照亮森林,隨後立即一聲巨響,似乎要撕裂男孩哋頭頂上嘅樹梢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一道猛烈的亮光照亮森林,隨後立即一聲巨響,似乎要撕裂男孩們頭頂上的樹梢。

passages.original: They clung together in terror, in the thick gloom that followed.
passages.vernacular: 喺隨後嘅濃重黑暗中,佢哋驚恐地緊抱喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在隨後的濃重黑暗中,他們驚恐地緊抱在一起。

passages.original: A few big raindrops fell pattering upon the leaves.
passages.vernacular: 幾滴大雨點劈啪落喺樹葉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾滴大雨點劈啪落在樹葉上。

passages.original: “Quick! boys, go for the tent!” exclaimed Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「快!夥計哋,去帳篷!」湯姆喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快!夥計們,去帳篷!」湯姆喊道。

passages.original: They sprang away, stumbling over roots and among vines in the dark, no two plunging in the same direction.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋跳起嚟,喺黑暗中絆住樹根、穿過藤蔓,冇兩個人衝向同一個方向。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們跳起來,在黑暗中絆著樹根、穿過藤蔓,沒有兩個人衝向同一個方向。

passages.original: A furious blast roared through the trees, making everything sing as it went.
passages.vernacular: 一陣猛烈嘅狂風怒吼住穿過樹林,所到之處萬物齊鳴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣猛烈的狂風怒吼著穿過樹林,所到之處萬物齊鳴。

passages.original: One blinding flash after another came, and peal on peal of deafening thunder.
passages.vernacular: 一道又一道令人眼盲嘅閃電,一聲接一聲震耳欲聾嘅雷鳴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一道又一道令人眼盲的閃電,一聲接一聲震耳欲聾的雷鳴。

passages.original: And now a drenching rain poured down and the rising hurricane drove it in sheets along the ground.
passages.vernacular: 而家傾盆大雨落下,不斷增強嘅颶風把佢成片地沿住地面驅趕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在傾盆大雨落下,不斷增強的颶風把它成片地沿著地面驅趕。

passages.original: The boys cried out to each other, but the roaring wind and the booming thunderblasts drowned their voices utterly.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋互相呼喊,但咆哮嘅風同隆隆嘅雷聲徹底淹沒咗佢哋嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們互相呼喊,但咆哮的風和隆隆的雷聲徹底淹沒了他們的聲音。

passages.original: However, one by one they straggled in at last and took shelter under the tent, cold, scared, and streaming with water; but to have company in misery seemed something to be grateful for.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢哋一個一個終於蹣跚地進嚟,躲喺帳篷下,冷、驚恐、渾身流水;但喺苦難中有伴似乎係值得感激嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,他們一個一個終於蹣跚地進來,躲在帳篷下,冷、驚恐、渾身流水;但在苦難中有伴似乎是值得感激的事。

passages.original: They could not talk, the old sail flapped so furiously, even if the other noises would have allowed them.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔能夠講話,舊帆瘋狂地拍打,即使其他噪音允許。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不能說話,舊帆瘋狂地拍打,即使其他噪音允許。

passages.original: The tempest rose higher and higher, and presently the sail tore loose from its fastenings and went winging away on the blast.
passages.vernacular: 暴風雨越嚟越高,不久帆從固定處撕脫,隨住狂風飛走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暴風雨越來越高,不久帆從固定處撕脫,隨著狂風飛走了。

passages.original: The boys seized each others’ hands and fled, with many tumblings and bruises, to the shelter of a great oak that stood upon the riverbank.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋抓住彼此嘅手,逃跑,跌跌撞撞、擦傷好多,逃到河岸上一棵大橡樹嘅庇護下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們抓住彼此的手,逃跑,跌跌撞撞、擦傷很多,逃到河岸上一棵大橡樹的庇護下。

passages.original: Now the battle was at its highest.
passages.vernacular: 而家戰鬥達到咗頂峰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在戰鬥達到了頂峰。

passages.original: Under the ceaseless conflagration of lightning that flamed in the skies, everything below stood out in cleancut and shadowless distinctness: the bending trees, the billowy river, white with foam, the driving spray of spumeflakes, the dim outlines of the high bluffs on the other side, glimpsed through the drifting cloudrack and the slanting veil of rain.
passages.vernacular: 喺天空中燃燒嘅閃電不停嘅光芒下,下面嘅一切都顯得輪廓分明、冇陰影:彎曲嘅樹、翻滾嘅河、白色嘅泡沫、飛濺嘅浪花、對岸高崖嘅朦朧輪廓,喺飄動嘅雲層同斜斜嘅雨簾中瞥見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在天空中燃燒的閃電不停的光芒下,下面的一切都顯得輪廓分明、沒有陰影:彎曲的樹、翻滾的河、白色的泡沫、飛濺的浪花、對岸高崖的朦朧輪廓,在飄動的雲層和斜斜的雨簾中瞥見。

passages.original: Every little while some giant tree yielded the fight and fell crashing through the younger growth; and the unflagging thunderpeals came now in ear-splitting explosive bursts, keen and sharp, and unspeakably appalling.
passages.vernacular: 每隔一小會兒,有巨大嘅樹放棄咗戰鬥,轟然倒下,穿過較年輕嘅樹叢;不倦嘅雷聲而家以震耳欲聾嘅爆炸性爆發而嚟,尖銳而銳利,令人無法形容地恐怖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每隔一小會兒,有巨大的樹放棄了戰鬥,轟然倒下,穿過較年輕的樹叢;不倦的雷聲現在以震耳欲聾的爆炸性爆發而來,尖銳而銳利,令人無法形容地恐怖。

passages.original: The storm culminated in one matchless effort that seemed likely to tear the island to pieces, burn it up, drown it to the treetops, blow it away, and deafen every creature in it, all at one and the same moment.
passages.vernacular: 暴風雨喺一次無同倫比嘅努力中達到頂點,似乎要把島撕成碎片,把佢燒毀,把佢淹到樹梢,把佢吹走,同時震聾島上每一個生物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暴風雨在一次無與倫比的努力中達到頂點,似乎要把島撕成碎片,把它燒毀,把它淹到樹梢,把它吹走,同時震聾島上每一個生物。

passages.original: It was a wild night for homeless young heads to be out in.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一個對無家可歸嘅年輕頭腦來講野蠻嘅夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一個對無家可歸的年輕頭腦來說野蠻的夜晚。

passages.original: But at last the battle was done, and the forces retired with weaker and weaker threatenings and grumblings, and peace resumed her sway.
passages.vernacular: 但最後戰鬥結束喇,力量以越嚟越弱嘅威脅同咆哮撤退,和平重新統治。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但最後戰鬥結束了,力量以越來越弱的威脅和咆哮撤退,和平重新統治。

passages.original: The boys went back to camp, a good deal awed; but they found there was still something to be thankful for, because the great sycamore, the shelter of their beds, was a ruin, now, blasted by the lightnings, and they were not under it when the catastrophe happened.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋回到營地,相當敬畏;但佢哋發現仍有可以感謝嘅事,因為嗰棵大梧桐,佢哋床嘅庇護所,而家成咗廢墟,被閃電劈毀,災難發生時佢哋不喺佢下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們回到營地,相當敬畏;但他們發現仍有可以感謝的事,因為那棵大梧桐,他們床的庇護所,現在成了廢墟,被閃電劈毀,災難發生時他們不在它下面。

passages.original: Everything in camp was drenched, the campfire as well; for they were but heedless lads, like their generation, and had made no provision against rain.
passages.vernacular: 營地裡嘅一切都濕透喇,營火都係;因為佢哋只係不留神嘅小伙子,像佢哋嗰一代人,冇為下雨作任何準備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 營地裡的一切都濕透了,營火也是;因為他們只是不留神的小伙子,像他們那一代人,沒有為下雨作任何準備。

passages.original: Here was matter for dismay, for they were soaked through and chilled.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係令人沮喪嘅事,因為佢哋被浸透、凍僵喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是令人沮喪的事,因為他們被浸透、凍僵了。

passages.original: They were eloquent in their distress; but they presently discovered that the fire had eaten so far up under the great log it had been built against (where it curved upward and separated itself from the ground), that a handbreadth or so of it had escaped wetting; so they patiently wrought until, with shreds and bark gathered from the under sides of sheltered logs, they coaxed the fire to burn again.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅苦惱講得好動聽;但佢哋不久發現,火已經燒進咗佢所靠嘅大原木底下咁深(嗰度佢向上彎曲,同地面分開),一手寬左右嘅地方冇被濕到;於是佢哋耐心地工作,用從有遮蔽嘅原木下面收集嘅碎片同樹皮,哄住火又燒起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們的苦惱說得很動聽;但他們不久發現,火已經燒進了它所靠的大原木底下那麼深(那裡它向上彎曲,與地面分開),一手寬左右的地方沒被濕到;於是他們耐心地工作,用從有遮蔽的原木下面收集的碎片和樹皮,哄著火又燒起來。

passages.original: Then they piled on great dead boughs till they had a roaring furnace, and were gladhearted once more.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋堆上大枯樹枝,直到有咗一座咆哮嘅熔爐,又開心起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們堆上大枯樹枝,直到有了一座咆哮的熔爐,又開心起來。

passages.original: They dried their boiled ham and had a feast, and after that they sat by the fire and expanded and glorified their midnight adventure until morning, for there was not a dry spot to sleep on, anywhere around.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋烘乾咗煮熟嘅火腿,美餐一頓,然後坐喺火邊,把佢哋午夜嘅冒險擴大、美化,直到早晨,因為周圍冇一處乾嘅地方可以瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們烘乾了煮熟的火腿,美餐一頓,然後坐在火邊,把他們午夜的冒險擴大、美化,直到早晨,因為周圍沒有一處乾的地方可以睡覺。

passages.original: As the sun began to steal in upon the boys, drowsiness came over them, and they went out on the sandbar and lay down to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 太陽開始悄悄照向男孩哋時,瞓意襲嚟,佢哋走到沙洲上躺下瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽開始悄悄照向男孩們時,睡意襲來,他們走到沙洲上躺下睡覺。

passages.original: They got scorched out by and by, and drearily set about getting breakfast.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋被曬得待不住,淒涼地開始準備早餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們被曬得待不住,淒涼地開始準備早餐。

passages.original: After the meal they felt rusty, and stiff-jointed, and a little homesick once more.
passages.vernacular: 飯後佢哋覺得生鏽、關節僵硬,又有點想家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 飯後他們覺得生鏽、關節僵硬,又有點想家。

passages.original: Tom saw the signs, and fell to cheering up the pirates as well as he could.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆睇出咗跡象,盡力讓海盜哋高興起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆看出了跡象,盡力讓海盜們高興起來。

passages.original: But they cared nothing for marbles, or circus, or swimming, or anything.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋對彈珠、馬戲團、游泳或任何嘢都不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們對彈珠、馬戲團、游泳或任何東西都不在乎。

passages.original: He reminded them of the imposing secret, and raised a ray of cheer.
passages.vernacular: 佢提醒佢哋嗰個令人印象深刻嘅祕密,升起咗一線歡樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他提醒他們那個令人印象深刻的祕密,升起了一線歡樂。

passages.original: While it lasted, he got them interested in a new device.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢持續期間,佢讓佢哋對一個新花招感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在它持續期間,他讓他們對一個新花招感興趣。

passages.original: This was to knock off being pirates, for a while, and be Indians for a change.
passages.vernacular: 就係暫時不當海盜,換成當印第安人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是暫時不當海盜,換成當印第安人。

passages.original: They were attracted by this idea; so it was not long before they were stripped, and striped from head to heel with black mud, like so many zebras—all of them chiefs, of course—and then they went tearing through the woods to attack an English settlement.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋被呢個主意吸引;所以不久佢哋就脫咗衣服,從頭到腳塗住黑泥條紋,像許多斑馬——當然都係酋長——然後佢哋撕扯住跑過樹林去襲擊一個英國殖民點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們被這個主意吸引;所以不久他們就脫了衣服,從頭到腳塗著黑泥條紋,像許多斑馬——當然都是酋長——然後他們撕扯著跑過樹林去襲擊一個英國殖民點。

passages.original: By and by they separated into three hostile tribes, and darted upon each other from ambush with dreadful warwhoops, and killed and scalped each other by thousands.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地佢哋分成三個敵對嘅部落,伴住可怕嘅戰吼從埋伏處撲向彼此,殺死彼此、剝彼此嘅頭皮數以千計。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地他們分成三個敵對的部落,伴著可怕的戰吼從埋伏處撲向彼此,殺死彼此、剝彼此的頭皮數以千計。

passages.original: It was a gory day.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係血腥嘅一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是血腥的一天。

passages.original: Consequently it was an extremely satisfactory one.
passages.vernacular: 因此係極其令人滿意嘅一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此是極其令人滿意的一天。

passages.original: They assembled in camp toward suppertime, hungry and happy; but now a difficulty arose—hostile Indians could not break the bread of hospitality together without first making peace, and this was a simple impossibility without smoking a pipe of peace.
passages.vernacular: 臨近晚餐時佢哋聚集喺營地,又餓又快樂;但而家出現咗一個困難——敵對嘅印第安人不先講同,就唔能夠一起分享好客嘅麵包,而不抽和平煙斗,呢個係簡單嘅唔可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 臨近晚餐時他們聚集在營地,又餓又快樂;但現在出現了一個困難——敵對的印第安人不先講和,就不能一起分享好客的麵包,而不抽和平煙斗,這是簡單的不可能。

passages.original: There was no other process that ever they had heard of.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋冇聽講過有別嘅程序。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沒聽說過有別的程序。

passages.original: Two of the savages almost wished they had remained pirates.
passages.vernacular: 兩個野人幾乎希望佢哋一直當海盜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個野人幾乎希望他們一直當海盜。

passages.original: However, there was no other way; so with such show of cheerfulness as they could muster they called for the pipe and took their whiff as it passed, in due form.
passages.vernacular: 不過,冇別嘅辦法;所以以佢哋能鼓起嘅盡可能快活嘅樣子,佢哋要咗菸斗,依次按正式禮儀吸咗一口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,沒有別的辦法;所以以他們能鼓起的盡可能快活的樣子,他們要了菸斗,依次按正式禮儀吸了一口。

passages.original: And behold, they were glad they had gone into savagery, for they had gained something; they found that they could now smoke a little without having to go and hunt for a lost knife; they did not get sick enough to be seriously uncomfortable.
passages.vernacular: 睇邊,佢哋好高興進入咗野蠻狀態,因為佢哋得到咗點嘢;佢哋發現佢哋而家可以抽啲而唔使去找丟失嘅刀;佢哋冇病到嚴重不適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看哪,他們很高興進入了野蠻狀態,因為他們得到了點東西;他們發現他們現在可以抽一點而不必去找丟失的刀;他們沒有病到嚴重不適。

passages.original: They were not likely to fool away this high promise for lack of effort.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔可能因為缺少努力而浪費呢個高度嘅前景。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不可能因為缺少努力而浪費這個高度的前景。

passages.original: No, they practised cautiously, after supper, with right fair success, and so they spent a jubilant evening.
passages.vernacular: 不,佢哋晚餐後謹慎地練習,頗為成功,於是佢哋度過咗一個歡欣嘅晚上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,他們晚餐後謹慎地練習,頗為成功,於是他們度過了一個歡欣的晚上。

passages.original: They were prouder and happier in their new acquirement than they would have been in the scalping and skinning of the Six Nations.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋對新獲得嘅本領比剝取同剝皮六個民族更驕傲同快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們對新獲得的本領比剝取和剝皮六個民族更驕傲和快樂。

passages.original: We will leave them to smoke and chatter and brag, since we have no further use for them at present.
passages.vernacular: 我哋就讓佢哋抽菸、閒聊、吹牛吧,因為我哋目前不需要佢哋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們就讓他們抽菸、閒聊、吹牛吧,因為我們目前不需要他們了。

chapters.title: Chapter XVII: Memories of the Lost Heroes 第十七章:失蹤英雄的追憶

passages.original: CH But there was no hilarity in the little town that same tranquil Saturday afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 但喺嗰個同樣寧靜嘅星期六下午,小鎮上冇歡樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在那個同樣寧靜的星期六下午,小鎮上沒有歡樂。

passages.original: The Harpers, and Aunt Polly’s family, were being put into mourning, with great grief and many tears.
passages.vernacular: 哈珀家同波莉姨媽一家正帶住巨大嘅悲痛同許多眼淚披上喪服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈珀家和波莉姨媽一家正帶著巨大的悲痛和許多眼淚披上喪服。

passages.original: An unusual quiet possessed the village, although it was ordinarily quiet enough, in all conscience.
passages.vernacular: 一種不尋常嘅安靜佔據咗村子,雖然佢平時講實話已經夠安靜喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種不尋常的安靜佔據了村子,雖然它平時說實話已經夠安靜了。

passages.original: The villagers conducted their concerns with an absent air, and talked little; but they sighed often.
passages.vernacular: 村民哋心不喺焉地處理自己嘅事務,好少講話;但常常歎息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 村民們心不在焉地處理自己的事務,很少說話;但常常歎息。

passages.original: The Saturday holiday seemed a burden to the children.
passages.vernacular: 星期六嘅假日對細路哋似乎成咗負擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期六的假日對孩子們似乎成了負擔。

passages.original: They had no heart in their sports, and gradually gave them up.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋對運動冇心情,漸漸放棄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們對運動沒有心情,漸漸放棄了。

passages.original: In the afternoon Becky Thatcher found herself moping about the deserted schoolhouse yard, and feeling very melancholy.
passages.vernacular: 下午,貝琪·撒切爾發現自己喺空蕩蕩嘅校舍院子裡悶悶不樂地閒逛,感到好憂鬱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午,貝琪·撒切爾發現自己在空蕩蕩的校舍院子裡悶悶不樂地閒逛,感到非常憂鬱。

passages.original: But she found nothing there to comfort her.
passages.vernacular: 但佢喺嗰度找唔到任何安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她在那裡找不到任何安慰。

passages.original: She soliloquized:
passages.vernacular: 佢自言自語:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她自言自語:

passages.original: “Oh, if I only had a brass andiron-knob again!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,要係我仲有嗰個黃銅柴架球就好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,要是我還有那個黃銅柴架球就好了!

passages.original: But I haven’t got anything now to remember him by.”
passages.vernacular: 但我而家冇任何嘢嚟紀念佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我現在沒有任何東西來紀念他。」

passages.original: And she choked back a little sob.
passages.vernacular: 佢哽住咗一小聲抽泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她哽住了一小聲抽泣。

passages.original: Presently she stopped, and said to herself:
passages.vernacular: 不久佢停下嚟,對自己講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久她停下來,對自己說:

passages.original: “It was right here.
passages.vernacular: 「就喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就在這裡。

passages.original: Oh, if it was to do over again, I wouldn’t say that—I wouldn’t say it for the whole world.
passages.vernacular: 哦,如果能重嚟一次,我唔會講嗰話——我為全世界都唔會講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,如果能重來一次,我不會說那話——我為全世界也不會說。

passages.original: But he’s gone now; I’ll never, never, never see him any more.”
passages.vernacular: 但佢而家走喇;我再都、再都、再都見唔到佢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他現在走了;我再也、再也、再也見不到他了。」

passages.original: This thought broke her down, and she wandered away, with tears rolling down her cheeks.
passages.vernacular: 呢個念頭使佢崩潰,佢走開喇,淚水順住臉頰滾落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個念頭使她崩潰,她走開了,淚水順著臉頰滾落。

passages.original: Then quite a group of boys and girls—playmates of Tom’s and Joe’s—came by, and stood looking over the paling fence and talking in reverent tones of how Tom did so-and-so the last time they saw him, and how Joe said this and that small trifle (pregnant with awful prophecy, as they could easily see now!)—and each speaker pointed out the exact spot where the lost lads stood at the time, and then added something like “and I was a-standing just so—just as I am now, and as if you was him—I was as close as that—and he smiled, just this way—and then something seemed to go all over me, like—awful, you know—and I never thought what it meant, of course, but I can see now!”
passages.vernacular: 然後一大群男孩女孩——湯姆同喬嘅玩伴——走過嚟,站住越過尖樁圍欄往裡睇,用恭敬嘅語氣談論湯姆最後一次見到佢時如何如何,喬講咗咁樣嗰樣嘅小事(而家可以輕易睇出蘊含住可怕嘅預言!)——每個發言者指出失蹤嘅小伙子哋當時站的確切地點,然後補充類似「我當時就站喺咁樣——就像我而家咁樣,好像你係佢——我離得咁近——佢笑喇,就咁樣笑——然後有嘢好像傳遍我全身,像——可怕嘅,你知道——我當然冇想到嗰個係乜嘢意思,但我而家睇出嚟喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一大群男孩女孩——湯姆和喬的玩伴——走過來,站著越過尖樁圍欄往裡看,用恭敬的語氣談論湯姆最後一次見到他時如何如何,喬說了這樣那樣的小事(現在可以輕易看出蘊含著可怕的預言!)——每個發言者指出失蹤的小伙子們當時站的確切地點,然後補充類似「我當時就站在這樣——就像我現在這樣,好像你是他——我離得這麼近——他笑了,就這樣笑——然後有東西好像傳遍我全身,像——可怕的,你知道——我當然沒想到那是什麼意思,但我現在看出來了!」

passages.original: Then there was a dispute about who saw the dead boys last in life, and many claimed that dismal distinction, and offered evidences, more or less tampered with by the witness; and when it was ultimately decided who did see the departed last, and exchanged the last words with them, the lucky parties took upon themselves a sort of sacred importance, and were gaped at and envied by all the rest.
passages.vernacular: 然後有爭論,邊個最後一次喺生前見到死去嘅男孩哋,許多人聲稱嗰個淒涼嘅殊榮,並提供證據,多少被證人篡改喇;最後決定邊個最後見到逝者,並同佢哋交換咗最後嘅話時,幸運嘅人畀自己加上咗一種神聖嘅重要性,被所有其他人張口結舌地羨慕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後有爭論,誰最後一次在生前見到死去的男孩們,許多人聲稱那個淒涼的殊榮,並提供證據,多少被證人篡改了;最後決定誰最後見到逝者,並同他們交換了最後的話時,幸運的人給自己加上了一種神聖的重要性,被所有其他人張口結舌地羨慕。

passages.original: One poor chap, who had no other grandeur to offer, said with tolerably manifest pride in the remembrance:
passages.vernacular: 一個冇其他光彩可炫耀嘅可憐傢伙,帶住明顯相當嘅對記憶嘅驕傲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個沒有其他光彩可炫耀的可憐傢伙,帶著明顯相當的對記憶的驕傲說:

passages.original: “Well, Tom Sawyer he licked me once.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,湯姆·索亞有一次揍過我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,湯姆·索亞有一次揍過我。」

passages.original: But that bid for glory was a failure.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰個爭榮耀嘅嘗試失敗喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那個爭榮耀的嘗試失敗了。

passages.original: Most of the boys could say that, and so that cheapened the distinction too much.
passages.vernacular: 大多數男孩都能講呢個,所以呢使殊榮大大貶值。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大多數男孩都能說這個,所以這使殊榮大大貶值。

passages.original: The group loitered away, still recalling memories of the lost heroes, in awed voices.
passages.vernacular: 呢群人漸漸閒蕩走開,仍然用敬畏嘅聲音回憶住失蹤英雄哋嘅記憶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這群人漸漸閒蕩走開,仍然用敬畏的聲音回憶著失蹤英雄們的記憶。

passages.original: When the Sunday-school hour was finished, the next morning, the bell began to toll, instead of ringing in the usual way.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨主日學校時間結束後,鐘開始鳴響,而唔係以平常嘅方式響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨主日學校時間結束後,鐘開始鳴響,而不是以平常的方式響。

passages.original: It was a very still Sabbath, and the mournful sound seemed in keeping with the musing hush that lay upon nature.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個好寂靜嘅安息日,哀傷嘅聲音似乎同籠罩大自然嘅沉思寂靜相稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個非常寂靜的安息日,哀傷的聲音似乎同籠罩大自然的沉思寂靜相稱。

passages.original: The villagers began to gather, loitering a moment in the vestibule to converse in whispers about the sad event.
passages.vernacular: 村民哋開始聚集,喺前廳逗留片刻,低聲談論呢件悲傷嘅事件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 村民們開始聚集,在前廳逗留片刻,低聲談論這件悲傷的事件。

passages.original: But there was no whispering in the house; only the funereal rustling of dresses as the women gathered to their seats disturbed the silence there.
passages.vernacular: 但屋子裡冇低語;只有女人哋聚到座位時衣服葬禮般嘅窸窣聲打擾嗰度嘅寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但屋子裡沒有低語;只有女人們聚到座位時衣服葬禮般的窸窣聲打擾那裡的寂靜。

passages.original: None could remember when the little church had been so full before.
passages.vernacular: 冇人能記得小教堂以前乜嘢時候咁樣滿過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人能記得小教堂以前什麼時候這樣滿過。

passages.original: There was finally a waiting pause, an expectant dumbness, and then Aunt Polly entered, followed by Sid and Mary, and they by the Harper family, all in deep black, and the whole congregation, the old minister as well, rose reverently and stood until the mourners were seated in the front pew.
passages.vernacular: 最後有一個等待嘅停頓,一種期待嘅沉默,然後波莉姨媽進嚟,希德同瑪麗跟喺後面,哈珀一家跟喺佢哋後面,全都穿深黑色,整個會眾,連老牧師都係,恭敬地站起嚟,直到哀悼者喺前排長椅坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後有一個等待的停頓,一種期待的沉默,然後波莉姨媽進來,希德和瑪麗跟在後面,哈珀一家跟在他們後面,全都穿深黑色,整個會眾,連老牧師也是,恭敬地站起來,直到哀悼者在前排長椅坐下。

passages.original: There was another communing silence, broken at intervals by muffled sobs, and then the minister spread his hands abroad and prayed.
passages.vernacular: 又一陣交融嘅沉默,不時被壓抑嘅抽泣聲打斷,然後牧師張開雙手禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一陣交融的沉默,不時被壓抑的抽泣聲打斷,然後牧師張開雙手禱告。

passages.original: A moving hymn was sung, and the text followed: “I am the Resurrection and the Life.”
passages.vernacular: 唱咗一首動人嘅讚美詩,隨後係經文:「復活喺我,生命都喺我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唱了一首動人的讚美詩,隨後是經文:「復活在我,生命也在我。」

passages.original: As the service proceeded, the clergyman drew such pictures of the graces, the winning ways, and the rare promise of the lost lads that every soul there, thinking he recognized these pictures, felt a pang in remembering that he had persistently blinded himself to them always before, and had as persistently seen only faults and flaws in the poor boys.
passages.vernacular: 隨住禮拜嘅進行,牧師描繪咗失蹤小伙子哋嘅美德、可愛嘅方式同罕見嘅前程嘅圖畫,在場每個靈魂,認為自己認出咗呢啲畫,想起以前總是固執地對佢哋視而唔見,而同樣固執地只睇到呢啲可憐男孩嘅缺點同瑕疵,感到一陣痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨著禮拜的進行,牧師描繪了失蹤小伙子們的美德、可愛的方式和罕見的前程的圖畫,在場每個靈魂,認為自己認出了這些畫,想起以前總是固執地對它們視而不見,而同樣固執地只看到這些可憐男孩的缺點和瑕疵,感到一陣痛苦。

passages.original: The minister related many a touching incident in the lives of the departed, too, which illustrated their sweet, generous natures, and the people could easily see, now, how noble and beautiful those episodes were, and remembered with grief that at the time they occurred they had seemed rank rascalities, well deserving of the cowhide.
passages.vernacular: 牧師仲講述咗逝者生活中許多動人嘅事件,講明佢哋甜美慷慨嘅天性,人哋而家輕易睇出呢啲插曲幾咁高貴美麗,悲傷地記起,喺佢哋發生時,似乎係肆意嘅惡行,應該挨牛皮鞭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師還講述了逝者生活中許多動人的事件,說明他們甜美慷慨的天性,人們現在輕易看出這些插曲多麼高貴美麗,悲傷地記起,在它們發生時,似乎是肆意的惡行,應該挨牛皮鞭。

passages.original: The congregation became more and more moved, as the pathetic tale went on, till at last the whole company broke down and joined the weeping mourners in a chorus of anguished sobs, the preacher himself giving way to his feelings, and crying in the pulpit.
passages.vernacular: 隨住動人嘅故事繼續,會眾越嚟越感動,最後全場崩潰,加入哭泣嘅哀悼者,發出痛苦抽泣嘅合唱,連傳道者自己都屈服於感情,喺講壇上哭泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨著動人的故事繼續,會眾越來越感動,最後全場崩潰,加入哭泣的哀悼者,發出痛苦抽泣的合唱,連傳道者自己也屈服於感情,在講壇上哭泣。

passages.original: There was a rustle in the gallery, which nobody noticed; a moment later the church door creaked; the minister raised his streaming eyes above his handkerchief, and stood transfixed!
passages.vernacular: 樓座裡有一陣窸窣聲,冇人注意;片刻後教堂門吱嘎響;牧師從手帕上方抬起淚眼,呆立不動!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樓座裡有一陣窸窣聲,沒有人注意;片刻後教堂門吱嘎響;牧師從手帕上方抬起淚眼,呆立不動!

passages.original: First one and then another pair of eyes followed the minister’s, and then almost with one impulse the congregation rose and stared while the three dead boys came marching up the aisle, Tom in the lead, Joe next, and Huck, a ruin of drooping rags, sneaking sheepishly in the rear!
passages.vernacular: 一對一對嘅眼睛跟隨牧師嘅目光,然後幾乎係一個衝動,會眾站起嚟,瞪住三個死去嘅男孩沿住過道行進,湯姆領頭,喬其次,哈克,一堆下垂嘅破布嘅廢墟,羞怯地溜喺後面!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一對一對的眼睛跟隨牧師的目光,然後幾乎是一個衝動,會眾站起來,瞪著三個死去的男孩沿著過道行進,湯姆領頭,喬其次,哈克,一堆下垂的破布的廢墟,羞怯地溜在後面!

passages.original: They had been hid in the unused gallery listening to their own funeral sermon!
passages.vernacular: 佢哋一直躲喺唔使嘅樓座裡聽佢哋自己嘅葬禮講道!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們一直躲在不用的樓座裡聽他們自己的葬禮講道!

passages.original: Aunt Polly, Mary, and the Harpers threw themselves upon their restored ones, smothered them with kisses and poured out thanksgivings, while poor Huck stood abashed and uncomfortable, not knowing exactly what to do or where to hide from so many unwelcoming eyes.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽、瑪麗同哈珀一家撲向失而復得嘅細路哋,用吻窒息佢哋,傾瀉感恩,而可憐嘅哈克站住,羞愧不安,唔知道該做乜嘢或喺咁多不歡迎嘅眼睛下躲到邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽、瑪麗和哈珀一家撲向失而復得的孩子們,用吻窒息他們,傾瀉感恩,而可憐的哈克站著,羞愧不安,不知道該做什麼或在那麼多不歡迎的眼睛下躲到哪裡。

passages.original: He wavered, and started to slink away, but Tom seized him and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢猶豫住,開始想溜走,但湯姆抓住佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他猶豫著,開始想溜走,但湯姆抓住他說:

passages.original: “Aunt Polly, it ain’t fair.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽,呢不公平。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽,這不公平。

passages.original: Somebody’s got to be glad to see Huck.”
passages.vernacular: 總得有人高興睇到哈克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總得有人高興看到哈克。」

passages.original: “And so they shall.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們會的。

passages.original: I’m glad to see him, poor motherless thing!”
passages.vernacular: 我好高興睇到佢,可憐冇母親嘅嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興看到他,可憐沒有母親的東西!」

passages.original: And the loving attentions Aunt Polly lavished upon him were the one thing capable of making him more uncomfortable than he was before.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽傾瀉喺佢身上嘅愛嘅關懷,係唯一能讓佢比以前更不舒服嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽傾瀉在他身上的愛的關懷,是唯一能讓他比以前更不舒服的事。

passages.original: Suddenly the minister shouted at the top of his voice: “Praise God from whom all blessings flow—sing!—and put your hearts in it!”
passages.vernacular: 突然牧師放聲大喊:「讚美上帝,萬福之源——唱!——把你哋嘅心放進去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然牧師放聲大喊:「讚美上帝,萬福之源——唱!——把你們的心放進去!」

passages.original: And they did.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唱喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們唱了。

passages.original: Old Hundred swelled up with a triumphant burst, and while it shook the rafters Tom Sawyer the Pirate looked around upon the envying juveniles about him and confessed in his heart that this was the proudest moment of his life.
passages.vernacular: 《老一百首》以勝利嘅爆發高漲,佢震動住屋樑時,海盜湯姆·索亞環顧佢周圍羨慕嘅少年哋,心裡承認呢個係佢一生中最驕傲嘅時刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 《老一百首》以勝利的爆發高漲,它震動著屋樑時,海盜湯姆·索亞環顧他周圍羨慕的少年們,心裡承認這是他一生中最驕傲的時刻。

passages.original: As the “sold” congregation trooped out they said they would almost be willing to be made ridiculous again to hear Old Hundred sung like that once more.
passages.vernacular: 「上當」嘅會眾魚貫而出時講,佢哋幾乎願意再被弄得可笑一次,只為再聽一次《老一百首》嗰樣唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「上當」的會眾魚貫而出時說,他們幾乎願意再被弄得可笑一次,只為再聽一次《老一百首》那樣唱。

passages.original: Tom got more cuffs and kisses that day—according to Aunt Polly’s varying moods—than he had earned before in a year; and he hardly knew which expressed the most gratefulness to God and affection for himself.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天湯姆得到嘅巴掌同吻——根據波莉姨媽變化嘅心情——比佢一年中掙嚟嘅仲多;佢幾乎唔知道邊一個表達咗對上帝最大嘅感謝同對佢自己最大嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天湯姆得到的巴掌和吻——根據波莉姨媽變化的心情——比他一年中掙來的還多;他幾乎不知道哪一個表達了對上帝最大的感謝和對他自己最大的愛。

chapters.title: Chapter XVIII: Tom's Feelings Investigated 第十八章:湯姆的感受

passages.original: CH That was Tom’s great secret—the scheme to return home with his brother pirates and attend their own funerals.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個就係湯姆嘅大祕密——同佢嘅海盜兄弟哋一起回家、參加自己嘅葬禮嘅計畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就是湯姆的大祕密——與他的海盜兄弟們一起回家、參加自己的葬禮的計畫。

passages.original: They had paddled over to the Missouri shore on a log, at dusk on Saturday, landing five or six miles below the village; they had slept in the woods at the edge of the town till nearly daylight, and had then crept through back lanes and alleys and finished their sleep in the gallery of the church among a chaos of invalided benches.
passages.vernacular: 星期六黃昏時,佢哋乘住一根原木划到密蘇里岸邊,喺村子下游五六英里處登陸;佢哋喺城鎮邊上嘅樹林裡瞓到天幾乎亮,然後悄悄穿過後巷同小路,喺教堂樓座裡一堆殘廢長椅之間補完咗瞓眠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期六黃昏時,他們乘著一根原木划到密蘇里岸邊,在村子下游五六英里處登陸;他們在城鎮邊上的樹林裡睡到天幾乎亮,然後悄悄穿過後巷和小路,在教堂樓座裡一堆殘廢長椅之間補完了睡眠。

passages.original: At breakfast, Monday morning, Aunt Polly and Mary were very loving to Tom, and very attentive to his wants.
passages.vernacular: 星期一早晨食早餐時,波莉姨媽同瑪麗對湯姆好親愛,好關注佢嘅需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期一早晨吃早餐時,波莉姨媽和瑪麗對湯姆非常親愛,非常關注他的需要。

passages.original: There was an unusual amount of talk.
passages.vernacular: 談話異乎尋常地多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 談話異乎尋常地多。

passages.original: In the course of it Aunt Polly said:
passages.vernacular: 喺談話中,波莉姨媽講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在談話中,波莉姨媽說:

passages.original: “Well, I don’t say it wasn’t a fine joke, Tom, to keep everybody suffering ’most a week so you boys had a good time, but it is a pity you could be so hard-hearted as to let me suffer so.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我不講呢唔係個好玩笑,湯姆,讓大家受咗差不多一個星期嘅苦,好讓你哋呢啲男孩玩得開心,但可惜你竟然能咁狠心,讓我咁受苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不說這不是個好玩笑,湯姆,讓大家受了差不多一個星期的苦,好讓你們這些男孩玩得開心,但可惜你竟然能那麼狠心,讓我這麼受苦。

passages.original: If you could come over on a log to go to your funeral, you could have come over and give me a hint some way that you warn’t dead, but only run off.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你能乘原木過嚟參加自己嘅葬禮,你本可以過嚟,以某種方式畀我個暗示,告訴我你冇死,只係跑掉喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你能乘原木過來參加自己的葬禮,你本可以過來,以某種方式給我個暗示,告訴我你沒死,只是跑掉了。」

passages.original: “Yes, you could have done that, Tom,” said Mary; “and I believe you would if you had thought of it.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,你本可以嗰樣做,湯姆,」瑪麗講;「我相信如果你想到喇,你會嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,你本可以那樣做,湯姆,」瑪麗說;「我相信如果你想到了,你會的。」

passages.original: “Would you, Tom?” said Aunt Polly, her face lighting wistfully.
passages.vernacular: 「你會嗎,湯姆?」波莉姨媽講,佢嘅臉渴望地亮起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會嗎,湯姆?」波莉姨媽說,她的臉渴望地亮起來。

passages.original: “Say, now, would you, if you’d thought of it?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,而家,如果你想到喇,你會嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,現在,如果你想到了,你會嗎?」

passages.original: “I—well, I don’t know. ’Twould ’a’ spoiled everything.”
passages.vernacular: 「我——嗯,我唔知道。嗰會毀掉一切。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——嗯,我不知道。那會毀掉一切。」

passages.original: “Tom, I hoped you loved me that much,” said Aunt Polly, with a grieved tone that discomforted the boy.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我本希望你咁愛我,」波莉姨媽用悲傷嘅語氣講,呢使男孩不自在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我本希望你那麼愛我,」波莉姨媽用悲傷的語氣說,這使男孩不自在。

passages.original: “It would have been something if you’d cared enough to think of it, even if you didn’t do it.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你在乎到想到佢,即使你冇做,嗰都算點乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你在乎到想到它,即使你沒有做,那也算點什麼。」

passages.original: “Now, auntie, that ain’t any harm,” pleaded Mary; “it’s only Tom’s giddy way—he is always in such a rush that he never thinks of anything.”
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,姨媽,嗰冇乜嘢壞處,」瑪麗懇求;「嗰只係湯姆嘅輕浮方式——佢總是咁匆忙,以致乜嘢都想唔到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,姨媽,那沒有什麼壞處,」瑪麗懇求;「那只是湯姆的輕浮方式——他總是那麼匆忙,以致什麼也想不到。」

passages.original: “More’s the pity.
passages.vernacular: 「更可惜喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「更可惜了。

passages.original: Sid would have thought.
passages.vernacular: 希德就會想到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德就會想到。

passages.original: And Sid would have come and done it, too.
passages.vernacular: 而且希德會嚟做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且希德會來做的。

passages.original: Tom, you’ll look back, some day, when it’s too late, and wish you’d cared a little more for me when it would have cost you so little.”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,有一天你會回頭睇,太遲喇,希望你喺嗰時對我多在乎啲,嗰時對你代價咁小。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,有一天你會回頭看,太遲了,希望你在那時對我多在乎一點,那時對你代價那麼小。」

passages.original: “Now, auntie, you know I do care for you,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,姨媽,你知道我在乎你,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,姨媽,你知道我在乎你,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “I’d know it better if you acted more like it.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你更像嗰樣行動,我會更清楚地知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你更像那樣行動,我會更清楚地知道。」

passages.original: “I wish now I’d thought,” said Tom, with a repentant tone; “but I dreamt about you, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 「我而家希望我想到喇,」湯姆用悔過嘅語氣講;「但我無論如何夢到咗你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在希望我想到了,」湯姆用悔過的語氣說;「但我無論如何夢到了你。

passages.original: That’s something, ain’t it?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰都算點乜嘢,唔係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那也算點什麼,不是嗎?」

passages.original: “It ain’t much—a cat does that much—but it’s better than nothing.
passages.vernacular: 「不算多——貓都能做到咁多——但比冇好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不算多——貓也能做到這麼多——但比沒有好。

passages.original: What did you dream?”
passages.vernacular: 你夢到咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你夢到了什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, Wednesday night I dreamt that you was sitting over there by the bed, and Sid was sitting by the woodbox, and Mary next to him.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,星期三晚上我夢到你坐喺嗰邊床邊,希德坐喺柴箱邊,瑪麗喺佢旁邊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,星期三晚上我夢到你坐在那邊床邊,希德坐在柴箱邊,瑪麗在他旁邊。」

passages.original: “Well, so we did.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我哋確實係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我們確實是這樣。

passages.original: So we always do.
passages.vernacular: 我哋總是咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們總是這樣。

passages.original: I’m glad your dreams could take even that much trouble about us.”
passages.vernacular: 我好高興你嘅夢甚至肯喺我哋身上費咁多力氣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興你的夢甚至肯在我們身上費那麼多力氣。」

passages.original: “And I dreamt that Joe Harper’s mother was here.”
passages.vernacular: 「我仲夢到喬·哈珀嘅母親喺呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還夢到喬·哈珀的母親在這裡。」

passages.original: “Why, she was here!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,佢確實在呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,她確實在這裡!

passages.original: Did you dream any more?”
passages.vernacular: 你仲夢到更多咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還夢到更多了嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, lots.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,很多。

passages.original: But it’s so dim, now.”
passages.vernacular: 但而家好模糊喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在很模糊了。」

passages.original: “Well, try to recollect—can’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,試住回憶——你唔能夠嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,試著回憶——你不能嗎?」

passages.original: “Somehow it seems to me that the wind—the wind blowed the—the—”
passages.vernacular: 「唔知點,我覺得風——風吹喇——嗰個——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不知怎麼,我覺得風——風吹了——那個——」

passages.original: “Try harder, Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「再努力點,湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再努力點,湯姆!

passages.original: The wind did blow something.
passages.vernacular: 風確實吹咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 風確實吹了什麼。

passages.original: Come!”
Tom pressed his fingers on his forehead an anxious minute, and then said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆把手指按喺額頭上焦急地想咗一分鐘,然後講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆把手指按在額頭上焦急地想了一分鐘,然後說:

passages.original: “I’ve got it now!
passages.vernacular: 「我而家想起嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在想起來了!

passages.original: I’ve got it now!
passages.vernacular: 我而家想起嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在想起來了!

passages.original: It blowed the candle!”
passages.vernacular: 佢吹咗蠟燭!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它吹了蠟燭!」

passages.original: “Mercy on us!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!

passages.original: Go on, Tom—go on!”
passages.vernacular: 繼續,湯姆——繼續!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繼續,湯姆——繼續!」

passages.original: “And it seems to me that you said, ‘Why, I believe that that door—’”
passages.vernacular: 「我覺得你講:『哎呀,我相信嗰扇門——』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我覺得你說:『哎呀,我相信那扇門——』」

passages.original: “Go on, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 「繼續,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「繼續,湯姆!」

passages.original: “Just let me study a moment—just a moment.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我想一會兒——就一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我想一會兒——就一會兒。

passages.original: Oh, yes—you said you believed the door was open.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,對喇——你講你相信門開住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,對了——你說你相信門開著。」

passages.original: “As I’m sitting here, I did!
passages.vernacular: 「我坐喺呢度發誓,我講過!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我坐在這裡發誓,我說過!

passages.original: Didn’t I, Mary!
passages.vernacular: 我講過嗎,瑪麗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說過嗎,瑪麗!

passages.original: Go on!”
passages.vernacular: 繼續!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繼續!」

passages.original: “And then—and then—well I won’t be certain, but it seems like as if you made Sid go and—and—”
passages.vernacular: 「然後——然後——嗯,我唔能夠肯定,但好像你讓希德去——去——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後——然後——嗯,我不能肯定,但好像你讓希德去——去——」

passages.original: “Well?
Well?
passages.vernacular: 嗯?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯?

passages.original: What did I make him do, Tom?
passages.vernacular: 我讓佢做乜嘢,湯姆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讓他做什麼,湯姆?

passages.original: What did I make him do?”
passages.vernacular: 我讓佢做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我讓他做什麼?」

passages.original: “You made him—you—Oh, you made him shut it.”
passages.vernacular: 「你讓佢——你——哦,你讓佢把佢關上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你讓他——你——哦,你讓他把它關上。」

passages.original: “Well, for the land’s sake!
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,睇喺老天份上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,看在老天份上!

passages.original: I never heard the beat of that in all my days!
passages.vernacular: 我呢輩子從冇聽過呢種事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這輩子從沒聽過這種事!

passages.original: Don’t tell me there ain’t anything in dreams, any more.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再對我講夢裡冇乜嘢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再對我說夢裡沒有什麼了。

passages.original: Sereny Harper shall know of this before I’m an hour older.
passages.vernacular: 喺我老一個小時之前,塞蕾妮·哈珀就會知道呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我老一個小時之前,塞蕾妮·哈珀就會知道這件事。

passages.original: I’d like to see her get around this with her rubbage ’bout superstition.
passages.vernacular: 我倒想睇佢點用佢嗰套關於迷信嘅廢話繞過呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我倒想看她怎麼用她那套關於迷信的廢話繞過這個。

passages.original: Go on, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 繼續,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繼續,湯姆!」

passages.original: “Oh, it’s all getting just as bright as day, now.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,而家一切都變得像白天一樣清楚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,現在一切都變得像白天一樣清楚了。

passages.original: Next you said I warn’t bad, only mischeevous and harum-scarum, and not any more responsible than—than—I think it was a colt, or something.”
passages.vernacular: 接住你講我不壞,只係淘氣同魯莽,不比——比——我想係一匹小馬,或乜嘢嘅,更負責任。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著你說我不壞,只是淘氣和魯莽,不比——比——我想是一匹小馬,或什麼的,更負責任。」

passages.original: “And so it was!
passages.vernacular: 「確實如此!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實如此!

passages.original: Well, goodness gracious!
passages.vernacular: 嗯,天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,天哪!

passages.original: Go on, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 繼續,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繼續,湯姆!」

passages.original: “And then you began to cry.”
passages.vernacular: 「然後你開始哭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後你開始哭。」

passages.original: “So I did.
passages.vernacular: 「我係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是這樣。

passages.original: So I did.
passages.vernacular: 我係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是這樣。

passages.original: Not the first time, neither.
passages.vernacular: 都唔係第一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不是第一次。

passages.original: And then—”
passages.vernacular: 然後——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後——」

passages.original: “Then Mrs. Harper she began to cry, and said Joe was just the same, and she wished she hadn’t whipped him for taking cream when she’d throwed it out her own self—”
passages.vernacular: 「然後哈珀太太佢開始哭,講喬都係一樣,佢希望佢冇為了佢攞奶油鞭打佢,而嗰個係佢自己倒掉嘅——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後哈珀太太她開始哭,說喬也是一樣,她希望她沒有為了他拿奶油鞭打他,而那是她自己倒掉的——」

passages.original: “Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆!

passages.original: The sperrit was upon you!
passages.vernacular: 精靈喺你身上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 精靈在你身上!

passages.original: You was a prophesying—that’s what you was doing!
passages.vernacular: 你喺預言——你喺做嘅就係呢個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在預言——你在做的就是這個!

passages.original: Land alive, go on, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 天呀,繼續,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,繼續,湯姆!」

passages.original: “Then Sid he said—he said—”
passages.vernacular: 「然後希德佢講——佢講——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後希德他說——他說——」

passages.original: “I don’t think I said anything,” said Sid.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我乜嘢都冇講,」希德講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我什麼也沒說,」希德說。

passages.original: “Yes you did, Sid,” said Mary.
passages.vernacular: 「你講喇,希德,」瑪麗講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說了,希德,」瑪麗說。

passages.original: “Shut your heads and let Tom go on!
passages.vernacular: 「閉上你嘅嘴,讓湯姆繼續!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「閉上你的嘴,讓湯姆繼續!

passages.original: What did he say, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 佢講咗乜嘢,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說了什麼,湯姆?」

passages.original: “He said—I think he said he hoped I was better off where I was gone to, but if I’d been better sometimes—”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講——我想佢講佢希望我去咗嘅地方過得更好,但如果我有時好啲——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說——我想他說他希望我去了的地方過得更好,但如果我有時好一點——」

passages.original: “There, d’you hear that!
passages.vernacular: 「睇,你聽到咗嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看,你聽到了嗎!

passages.original: It was his very words!”
passages.vernacular: 正是佢嘅話!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正是他的話!」

passages.original: “And you shut him up sharp.”
passages.vernacular: 「你狠狠地叫佢住嘴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你狠狠地叫他住嘴。」

passages.original: “I lay I did!
passages.vernacular: 「我發誓我係咁樣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我發誓我是這樣!

passages.original: There must ’a’ been an angel there.
passages.vernacular: 嗰度一定有個天使。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡一定有個天使。

passages.original: There was an angel there, somewheres!”
passages.vernacular: 嗰度某處有個天使!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡某處有個天使!」

passages.original: “And Mrs. Harper told about Joe scaring her with a firecracker, and you told about Peter and the Pain-killer—”
passages.vernacular: 「哈珀太太講喬用爆竹嚇佢,你講咗彼得同痛靈嘅事——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈珀太太說喬用爆竹嚇她,你說了彼得和痛靈的事——」

passages.original: “Just as true as I live!”
passages.vernacular: 「像我活住一樣千真萬確!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「像我活著一樣千真萬確!」

passages.original: “And then there was a whole lot of talk ’bout dragging the river for us, and ’bout having the funeral Sunday, and then you and old Miss Harper hugged and cried, and she went.”
passages.vernacular: 「然後有一大堆談話,關於喺河裡為我哋打撈,關於星期日舉行葬禮,然後你同老哈珀太太擁抱哭泣,佢走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後有一大堆談話,關於在河裡為我們打撈,關於星期日舉行葬禮,然後你和老哈珀太太擁抱哭泣,她走了。」

passages.original: “It happened just so!
passages.vernacular: 「就係咁樣發生嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是這樣發生的!

passages.original: It happened just so, as sure as I’m a-sitting in these very tracks.
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣發生嘅,就像我坐喺呢個地方一樣肯定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣發生的,就像我坐在這個地方一樣肯定。

passages.original: Tom, you couldn’t told it more like if you’d ’a’ seen it!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,即使你親眼睇到,你都唔可能講得更像喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,即使你親眼看到,你也不可能講得更像了!

passages.original: And then what?
passages.vernacular: 然後呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後呢?

passages.original: Go on, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 繼續,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 繼續,湯姆!」

passages.original: “Then I thought you prayed for me—and I could see you and hear every word you said.
passages.vernacular: 「然後我以為你為我禱告——我能睇到你,聽到你講嘅每一個字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後我以為你為我禱告——我能看到你,聽到你說的每一個字。

passages.original: And you went to bed, and I was so sorry that I took and wrote on a piece of sycamore bark, ‘We ain’t dead—we are only off being pirates,’ and put it on the table by the candle; and then you looked so good, laying there asleep, that I thought I went and leaned over and kissed you on the lips.”
passages.vernacular: 你上床喇,我好難過,我就攞咗一片梧桐樹皮寫上『我哋冇死——只係去當海盜喇』,放喺蠟燭旁嘅桌上;然後你躺喺嗰度瞓住嘅樣子咁好,我想我走過去,俯身吻咗你嘅嘴唇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你上床了,我很難過,我就拿了一片梧桐樹皮寫上『我們沒死——只是去當海盜了』,放在蠟燭旁的桌上;然後你躺在那裡睡著的樣子那麼好,我想我走過去,俯身吻了你的嘴唇。」

passages.original: “Did you, Tom, did you!
passages.vernacular: 「你做咗嗎,湯姆,你做咗嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做了嗎,湯姆,你做了嗎!

passages.original: I just forgive you everything for that!”
passages.vernacular: 為呢個我完全原諒你一切!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為這個我完全原諒你一切!」

passages.original: And she seized the boy in a crushing embrace that made him feel like the guiltiest of villains.
passages.vernacular: 佢抓住男孩,緊緊擁抱,使佢覺得像係罪人中最有罪嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她抓住男孩,緊緊擁抱,使他覺得像是罪人中最有罪的。

passages.original: “It was very kind, even though it was only a—dream,” Sid soliloquized just audibly.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個好好,雖然只係——夢,」希德自言自語,剛好聽得見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這很好,雖然只是——夢,」希德自言自語,剛好聽得見。

passages.original: “Shut up, Sid!
passages.vernacular: 「閉嘴,希德!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「閉嘴,希德!

passages.original: A body does just the same in a dream as he’d do if he was awake.
passages.vernacular: 一個人喺夢裡做嘅同佢醒住時做嘅一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人在夢裡做的和他醒著時做的一樣。

passages.original: Here’s a big Milum apple I’ve been saving for you, Tom, if you was ever found again—now go ’long to school.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我一直畀你留住嘅一個大米勒姆蘋果,湯姆,如果你仲能被找回嚟嘅話——而家去上學吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我一直給你留著的一個大米勒姆蘋果,湯姆,如果你還能被找回來的話——現在去上學吧。

passages.original: I’m thankful to the good God and Father of us all I’ve got you back, that’s long-suffering and merciful to them that believe on Him and keep His word, though goodness knows I’m unworthy of it, but if only the worthy ones got His blessings and had His hand to help them over the rough places, there’s few enough would smile here or ever enter into His rest when the long night comes.
passages.vernacular: 我感謝我哋大家良善嘅上帝同父,我把你找回嚟喇,祂對嗰啲信祂、遵守祂話語嘅人係長期忍耐同憐憫嘅,雖然天知道我不配,但如果只有配得嘅人才得到祂嘅祝福、有祂嘅手幫助佢哋度過艱難嘅地方,咁喺漫長嘅夜晚來臨時,喺呢度微笑或將來進入祂嘅安息嘅人就寥寥無幾喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感謝我們大家良善的上帝和父,我把你找回來了,祂對那些信祂、遵守祂話語的人是長期忍耐和憐憫的,雖然天知道我不配,但如果只有配得的人才得到祂的祝福、有祂的手幫助他們度過艱難的地方,那麼在漫長的夜晚來臨時,在這裡微笑或將來進入祂的安息的人就寥寥無幾了。

passages.original: Go ’long Sid, Mary, Tom—take yourselves off—you’ve hendered me long enough.”
passages.vernacular: 走吧,希德、瑪麗、湯姆——都走開——你哋已經妨礙我夠久喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走吧,希德、瑪麗、湯姆——都走開——你們已經妨礙我夠久了。」

passages.original: The children left for school, and the old lady to call on Mrs. Harper and vanquish her realism with Tom’s marvellous dream.
passages.vernacular: 細路哋去上學,老太太去拜訪哈珀太太,用湯姆神奇嘅夢嚟擊敗佢嘅現實主義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們去上學,老太太去拜訪哈珀太太,用湯姆神奇的夢來擊敗她的現實主義。

passages.original: Sid had better judgment than to utter the thought that was in his mind as he left the house.
passages.vernacular: 希德有比講出佢離開屋子時腦子裡嘅想法更好嘅判斷力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德有比說出他離開屋子時腦子裡的想法更好的判斷力。

passages.original: It was this: “Pretty thin—as long a dream as that, without any mistakes in it!”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係咁樣嘅:「太牽強喇——咁長嘅夢,啲錯誤都冇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是這樣的:「太牽強了——這麼長的夢,一點錯誤也沒有!」

passages.original: What a hero Tom was become, now!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆而家成咗幾咁嘅英雄!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆現在成了多麼的英雄!

passages.original: He did not go skipping and prancing, but moved with a dignified swagger as became a pirate who felt that the public eye was on him.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇蹦蹦跳跳,而係以威嚴嘅大搖大擺移動,像一個感到公眾目光喺佢身上嘅海盜應有嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有蹦蹦跳跳,而是以威嚴的大搖大擺移動,像一個感到公眾目光在他身上的海盜應有的樣子。

passages.original: And indeed it was; he tried not to seem to see the looks or hear the remarks as he passed along, but they were food and drink to him.
passages.vernacular: 確實如此;佢試圖顯得冇睇到嗰啲目光或冇聽到嗰啲議論,但佢哋對佢來講係食物同飲料。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實如此;他試圖顯得沒看到那些目光或沒聽到那些議論,但它們對他來說是食物和飲料。

passages.original: Smaller boys than himself flocked at his heels, as proud to be seen with him, and tolerated by him, as if he had been the drummer at the head of a procession or the elephant leading a menagerie into town.
passages.vernacular: 比佢小嘅男孩哋圍喺佢腳後,為同佢同行、被佢容忍而驕傲,好像佢係遊行隊伍領頭嘅鼓手,或帶領動物園進城嘅大象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比他小的男孩們圍在他腳後,為與他同行、被他容忍而驕傲,好像他是遊行隊伍領頭的鼓手,或帶領動物園進城的大象。

passages.original: Boys of his own size pretended not to know he had been away at all; but they were consuming with envy, nevertheless.
passages.vernacular: 同佢一樣大嘅男孩假裝唔知道佢離開過,但佢哋嫉妒得要命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 和他一樣大的男孩假裝不知道他離開過,但他們嫉妒得要命。

passages.original: They would have given anything to have that swarthy sun-tanned skin of his, and his glittering notoriety; and Tom would not have parted with either for a circus.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋願意付出任何嘢嚟擁有佢嗰黝黑曬黑嘅皮膚同佢閃光嘅名聲;湯姆為一個馬戲團都唔會放棄呢兩樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們願意付出任何東西來擁有他那黝黑曬黑的皮膚和他閃光的名聲;湯姆為一個馬戲團也不會放棄這兩樣。

passages.original: At school the children made so much of him and of Joe, and delivered such eloquent admiration from their eyes, that the two heroes were not long in becoming insufferably “stuck-up.”
passages.vernacular: 喺學校,細路哋咁睇重佢同喬,眼睛裡流露出咁雄辯嘅欽佩,以致兩位英雄不久就變得令人難以忍受地「傲慢」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在學校,孩子們那麼看重他和喬,眼睛裡流露出那麼雄辯的欽佩,以致兩位英雄不久就變得令人難以忍受地「傲慢」。

passages.original: They began to tell their adventures to hungry listeners—but they only began; it was not a thing likely to have an end, with imaginations like theirs to furnish material.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋開始向飢渴嘅聽眾講述佢哋嘅冒險——但只係開始;像佢哋嗰樣嘅想像力提供材料,呢唔可能有個結尾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們開始向飢渴的聽眾講述他們的冒險——但只是開始;像他們那樣的想像力提供材料,這不可能有個結尾。

passages.original: And finally, when they got out their pipes and went serenely puffing around, the very summit of glory was reached.
passages.vernacular: 最後,當佢哋攞出菸斗,安然地抽住煙到處走時,榮耀達到咗頂峰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,當他們拿出菸斗,安然地抽著煙到處走時,榮耀達到了頂峰。

passages.original: Tom decided that he could be independent of Becky Thatcher now.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆決定佢而家可以不依賴貝琪·撒切爾喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆決定他現在可以不依賴貝琪·撒切爾了。

passages.original: Glory was sufficient.
passages.vernacular: 榮耀就夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 榮耀就夠了。

passages.original: He would live for glory.
passages.vernacular: 佢要為榮耀而活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要為榮耀而活。

passages.original: Now that he was distinguished, maybe she would be wanting to “make up.”
passages.vernacular: 而家佢出名喇,或者佢會想「同好」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他出名了,也許她會想「和好」。

passages.original: Well, let her—she should see that he could be as indifferent as some other people.
passages.vernacular: 好吧,隨佢——佢將睇到佢可以像別人一樣無動於衷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,隨她——她將看到他可以像別人一樣無動於衷。

passages.original: Presently she arrived.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久她到了。

passages.original: Tom pretended not to see her.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆假裝冇睇到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆假裝沒看到她。

passages.original: He moved away and joined a group of boys and girls and began to talk.
passages.vernacular: 佢走開,加入一群男孩女孩,開始講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走開,加入一群男孩女孩,開始說話。

passages.original: Soon he observed that she was tripping gayly back and forth with flushed face and dancing eyes, pretending to be busy chasing schoolmates, and screaming with laughter when she made a capture; but he noticed that she always made her captures in his vicinity, and that she seemed to cast a conscious eye in his direction at such times, too.
passages.vernacular: 好快佢注意到佢輕快地嚟回走動,臉頰緋紅,眼睛閃動,假裝忙住追同學,捉到人時笑得尖叫;但佢注意到佢總是喺佢附近捉人,而且佢嗰時似乎都有意識地朝佢嘅方向瞥一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很快他注意到她輕快地來回走動,臉頰緋紅,眼睛閃動,假裝忙著追同學,捉到人時笑得尖叫;但他注意到她總是在他附近捉人,而且她那時似乎也有意識地朝他的方向瞥一眼。

passages.original: It gratified all the vicious vanity that was in him; and so, instead of winning him, it only “set him up” the more and made him the more diligent to avoid betraying that he knew she was about.
passages.vernacular: 呢滿足咗佢身上所有惡毒嘅虛榮;所以,不但冇贏得佢,反而只係更「抬高咗佢」,使佢更勤奮地避免洩露佢知道佢喺附近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這滿足了他身上所有惡毒的虛榮;所以,不但沒有贏得他,反而只是更「抬高了他」,使他更勤奮地避免洩露他知道她在附近。

passages.original: Presently she gave over skylarking, and moved irresolutely about, sighing once or twice and glancing furtively and wistfully toward Tom.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢唔再嬉鬧,猶豫地走嚟走去,歎一兩次氣,偷偷地、渴望地瞥向湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久她不再嬉鬧,猶豫地走來走去,歎一兩次氣,偷偷地、渴望地瞥向湯姆。

passages.original: Then she observed that now Tom was talking more particularly to Amy Lawrence than to any one else.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢注意到湯姆而家同艾米·勞倫斯談話比同其他任何人更專注。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她注意到湯姆現在同艾米·勞倫斯談話比同其他任何人更專注。

passages.original: She felt a sharp pang and grew disturbed and uneasy at once.
passages.vernacular: 佢感到一陣尖銳嘅刺痛,立即變得煩亂不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她感到一陣尖銳的刺痛,立即變得煩亂不安。

passages.original: She tried to go away, but her feet were treacherous, and carried her to the group instead.
passages.vernacular: 佢試圖走開,但佢嘅腳不聽話,反而把佢帶到嗰群人裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她試圖走開,但她的腳不聽話,反而把她帶到那群人裡。

passages.original: She said to a girl almost at Tom’s elbow—with sham vivacity:
passages.vernacular: 佢對一個幾乎喺湯姆手肘邊嘅女孩講——帶住假裝嘅活潑:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對一個幾乎在湯姆手肘邊的女孩說——帶著假裝的活潑:

passages.original: “Why, Mary Austin! you bad girl, why didn’t you come to Sunday-school?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,瑪麗·奧斯汀!你呢壞女孩,你點解冇去主日學校?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,瑪麗·奧斯汀!你這壞女孩,你為什麼沒去主日學校?」

passages.original: “I did come—didn’t you see me?”
passages.vernacular: 「我去喇——你冇睇到我嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我去了——你沒看到我嗎?」

passages.original: “Why, no!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,沒有!

passages.original: Did you?
passages.vernacular: 你去咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去了嗎?

passages.original: Where did you sit?”
passages.vernacular: 你坐喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你坐在哪裡?」

passages.original: “I was in Miss Peters’ class, where I always go.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺彼得斯小姐嘅班,我總是去嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在彼得斯小姐的班,我總是去那裡。

passages.original: I saw you.”
passages.vernacular: 我睇到你喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看到你了。」

passages.original: “Did you?
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?

passages.original: Why, it’s funny I didn’t see you.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,奇怪我冇睇到你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,奇怪我沒看到你。

passages.original: I wanted to tell you about the picnic.”
passages.vernacular: 我想告訴你關於野餐嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想告訴你關於野餐的事。」

passages.original: “Oh, that’s jolly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰太好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那太好了。

passages.original: Who’s going to give it?”
passages.vernacular: 邊個要辦?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰要辦?」

passages.original: “My ma’s going to let me have one.”
passages.vernacular: 「我媽媽要讓我辦一個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我媽媽要讓我辦一個。」

passages.original: “Oh, goody; I hope she’ll let me come.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,太好喇;我希望佢讓我去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,太好了;我希望她讓我去。」

passages.original: “Well, she will.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,她會的。

passages.original: The picnic’s for me.
passages.vernacular: 野餐係為我辦嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 野餐是為我辦的。

passages.original: She’ll let anybody come that I want, and I want you.”
passages.vernacular: 佢會讓我想要嘅任何人嚟,我要你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會讓我想要的任何人來,我要你。」

passages.original: “That’s ever so nice.
passages.vernacular: 「太好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太好了。

passages.original: When is it going to be?”
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢時候辦?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼時候辦?」

passages.original: “By and by.
passages.vernacular: 「過一陣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「過一陣子。

passages.original: Maybe about vacation.”
passages.vernacular: 或者喺放假嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許在放假的時候。」

passages.original: “Oh, won’t it be fun!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,多有趣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,多有趣!

passages.original: You going to have all the girls and boys?”
passages.vernacular: 你要請所有嘅女孩男孩嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要請所有的女孩男孩嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, every one that’s friends to me—or wants to be”; and she glanced ever so furtively at Tom, but he talked right along to Amy Lawrence about the terrible storm on the island, and how the lightning tore the great sycamore tree “all to flinders” while he was “standing within three feet of it.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,每個係我朋友嘅人——或想成為嘅」;佢極其偷偷地瞥咗湯姆一眼,但佢繼續對艾米·勞倫斯講島上嘅可怕暴風雨,講閃電點樣把嗰棵大梧桐樹「劈成碎片」,而佢當時「就站喺離佢三呎以內」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,每個是我朋友的人——或想成為的」;她極其偷偷地瞥了湯姆一眼,但他繼續對艾米·勞倫斯講島上的可怕暴風雨,說閃電怎樣把那棵大梧桐樹「劈成碎片」,而他當時「就站在離它三呎以內」。

passages.original: “Oh, may I come?” said Grace Miller.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我可以來嗎?」格雷絲·米勒講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我可以來嗎?」格雷絲·米勒說。

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「可以。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可以。」

passages.original: “And me?” said Sally Rogers.
passages.vernacular: 「仲有我?」薩莉·羅傑斯講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有我?」薩莉·羅傑斯說。

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「可以。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可以。」

passages.original: “And me, too?” said Susy Harper.
passages.vernacular: 「仲有我呢?」蘇西·哈珀講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有我呢?」蘇西·哈珀說。

passages.original: “And Joe?”
passages.vernacular: 「仲有喬?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有喬?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「可以。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可以。」

passages.original: And so on, with clapping of joyful hands till all the group had begged for invitations but Tom and Amy.
passages.vernacular: 如此等等,伴住高興嘅拍手,直到嗰群人中除湯姆同艾米外都央求咗邀請。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如此等等,伴著高興的拍手,直到那群人中除湯姆和艾米外都央求了邀請。

passages.original: Then Tom turned coolly away, still talking, and took Amy with him.
passages.vernacular: 然後湯姆冷淡地轉身走開,仍喺講話,把艾米帶走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後湯姆冷淡地轉身走開,仍在說話,把艾米帶走。

passages.original: Becky’s lips trembled and the tears came to her eyes; she hid these signs with a forced gayety and went on chattering, but the life had gone out of the picnic, now, and out of everything else; she got away as soon as she could and hid herself and had what her sex call “a good cry.”
passages.vernacular: 貝琪嘅嘴唇顫抖,眼淚湧上眼眶;佢用強裝嘅快活掩藏呢啲跡象,繼續閒談,但而家野餐嘅生氣已經冇喇,一切嘅生氣都冇喇;佢盡快走開,躲起嚟,痛痛快快地哭咗佢嗰個性別所稱嘅「一場好哭」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪的嘴唇顫抖,眼淚湧上眼眶;她用強裝的快活掩藏這些跡象,繼續閒談,但現在野餐的生氣已經沒了,一切的生氣都沒了;她盡快走開,躲起來,痛痛快快地哭了她那個性別所稱的「一場好哭」。

passages.original: Then she sat moody, with wounded pride, till the bell rang.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢陰鬱地坐住,自尊受傷,直到鐘響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她陰鬱地坐著,自尊受傷,直到鐘響。

passages.original: She roused up, now, with a vindictive cast in her eye, and gave her plaited tails a shake and said she knew what she’d do.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家振作起嚟,眼睛裡帶住報復嘅神色,甩咗甩佢嘅辮子,講佢知道佢要點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在振作起來,眼睛裡帶著報復的神色,甩了甩她的辮子,說她知道她要怎麼辦。

passages.original: At recess Tom continued his flirtation with Amy with jubilant self-satisfaction.
passages.vernacular: 休息時湯姆以歡欣嘅自滿繼續同艾米調情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 休息時湯姆以歡欣的自滿繼續同艾米調情。

passages.original: And he kept drifting about to find Becky and lacerate her with the performance.
passages.vernacular: 佢不斷四處游蕩尋找貝琪,用呢表演撕裂佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不斷四處游蕩尋找貝琪,用這表演撕裂她。

passages.original: At last he spied her, but there was a sudden falling of his mercury.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢發現咗佢,但佢嘅水銀柱突然下降。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他發現了她,但他的水銀柱突然下降。

passages.original: She was sitting cosily on a little bench behind the schoolhouse looking at a picture-book with Alfred Temple—and so absorbed were they, and their heads so close together over the book, that they did not seem to be conscious of anything in the world besides.
passages.vernacular: 佢正舒適地坐喺校舍後面一張小長凳上,同阿爾弗雷德·坦普爾睇一本圖畫書——佢哋咁專注,頭靠得咁近,喺書上,似乎意識唔到世界上其他任何嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她正舒適地坐在校舍後面一張小長凳上,同阿爾弗雷德·坦普爾看一本圖畫書——他們那麼專注,頭靠得那麼近,在書上,似乎意識不到世界上其他任何東西。

passages.original: Jealousy ran red-hot through Tom’s veins.
passages.vernacular: 嫉妒灼熱地流過湯姆嘅血管。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嫉妒灼熱地流過湯姆的血管。

passages.original: He began to hate himself for throwing away the chance Becky had offered for a reconciliation.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始恨自己,因為扔掉咗貝琪提供嘅和解機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他開始恨自己,因為扔掉了貝琪提供的和解機會。

passages.original: He called himself a fool, and all the hard names he could think of.
passages.vernacular: 佢叫自己傻瓜,用佢能想到嘅所有難聽嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他叫自己傻瓜,用他能想到的所有難聽的名字。

passages.original: He wanted to cry with vexation.
passages.vernacular: 佢氣得想哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他氣得想哭。

passages.original: Amy chatted happily along, as they walked, for her heart was singing, but Tom’s tongue had lost its function.
passages.vernacular: 艾米一路愉快地閒談,因為佢嘅心喺歌唱,但湯姆嘅舌頭失去咗功能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾米一路愉快地閒談,因為她的心在歌唱,但湯姆的舌頭失去了功能。

passages.original: He did not hear what Amy was saying, and whenever she paused expectantly he could only stammer an awkward assent, which was as often misplaced as otherwise.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇聽到艾米喺講乜嘢,每當佢期待地停頓時,佢只能結結巴巴地笨拙同意,常常係錯位嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒聽到艾米在說什麼,每當她期待地停頓時,他只能結結巴巴地笨拙同意,常常是錯位的。

passages.original: He kept drifting to the rear of the schoolhouse, again and again, to sear his eyeballs with the hateful spectacle there.
passages.vernacular: 佢一再漂移到校舍後面,用嗰度可恨嘅景象灼傷佢嘅眼球。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一再漂移到校舍後面,用那裡可恨的景象灼傷他的眼球。

passages.original: He could not help it.
passages.vernacular: 佢忍不住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他忍不住。

passages.original: And it maddened him to see, as he thought he saw, that Becky Thatcher never once suspected that he was even in the land of the living.
passages.vernacular: 而佢睇到,或自以為睇到,貝琪·撒切爾一次都不曾懷疑佢仲活在世上,呢讓佢發瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而他看到,或自以為看到,貝琪·撒切爾一次也不曾懷疑他還活在世上,這讓他發瘋。

passages.original: But she did see, nevertheless; and she knew she was winning her fight, too, and was glad to see him suffer as she had suffered.
passages.vernacular: 但佢確實睇到喇;佢知道佢都喺贏得佢嘅戰鬥,好高興睇到佢像佢一樣受苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她確實看到了;她知道她也在贏得她的戰鬥,很高興看到他像她一樣受苦。

passages.original: Amy’s happy prattle became intolerable.
passages.vernacular: 艾米快樂嘅閒談變得難以忍受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾米快樂的閒談變得難以忍受。

passages.original: Tom hinted at things he had to attend to; things that must be done; and time was fleeting.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆暗示有些事要處理;必須做嘅事;時間喺流逝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆暗示有些事要處理;必須做的事;時間在流逝。

passages.original: But in vain—the girl chirped on.
passages.vernacular: 但徒勞——女孩繼續嘰嘰喳喳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但徒勞——女孩繼續嘰嘰喳喳。

passages.original: Tom thought, “Oh, hang her, ain’t I ever going to get rid of her?”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆想:「哦,該死,我永遠擺脫不咗佢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆想:「哦,該死,我永遠擺脫不了她嗎?」

passages.original: At last he must be attending to those things—and she said artlessly that she would be “around” when school let out.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢必須去處理嗰啲事——佢天真地講佢放學時會「喺附近」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他必須去處理那些事——她天真地說她放學時會「在附近」。

passages.original: And he hastened away, hating her for it.
passages.vernacular: 佢匆忙走開,因此恨佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他匆忙走開,因此恨她。

passages.original: “Any other boy!”
passages.vernacular: 「換任何其他男孩都行!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「換任何其他男孩都行!」

passages.original: Tom thought, grating his teeth.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆咬牙切齒地想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆咬牙切齒地想。

passages.original: “Any boy in the whole town but that Saint Louis smarty that thinks he dresses so fine and is aristocracy!
passages.vernacular: 「全鎮任何男孩,除咗嗰個以為自己穿得咁好、係貴族嘅聖路易斯自作聰明嘅傢伙!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「全鎮任何男孩,除了那個以為自己穿得這麼好、是貴族的聖路易斯自作聰明的傢伙!

passages.original: Oh, all right, I licked you the first day you ever saw this town, mister, and I’ll lick you again!
passages.vernacular: 哦,好吧,你第一天嚟呢個鎮上我就揍咗你,先生,我會再揍你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,好吧,你第一天來這個鎮上我就揍了你,先生,我會再揍你!

passages.original: You just wait till I catch you out!
passages.vernacular: 你等住,等我抓到你喺外面!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你等著,等我抓到你在外面!

passages.original: I’ll just take and—”
passages.vernacular: 我就要——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就要——」

passages.original: And he went through the motions of thrashing an imaginary boy—pummelling the air, and kicking and gouging.
passages.vernacular: 佢做咗鞭打一個想像中嘅男孩嘅動作——捶打空氣,踢同挖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他做了鞭打一個想像中的男孩的動作——捶打空氣,踢和挖。

passages.original: “Oh, you do, do you?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你係嗎,係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你是嗎,是嗎?

passages.original: You holler ’nough, do you?
passages.vernacular: 你喊夠喇,係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你喊夠了,是嗎?

passages.original: Now, then, let that learn you!”
passages.vernacular: 好喇,讓呢個教訓你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,讓這個教訓你!」

passages.original: And so the imaginary flogging was finished to his satisfaction.
passages.vernacular: 於是想像中嘅鞭打令佢滿意地結束喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是想像中的鞭打令他滿意地結束了。

passages.original: Tom fled home at noon.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆中午逃回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆中午逃回家。

passages.original: His conscience could not endure any more of Amy’s grateful happiness, and his jealousy could bear no more of the other distress.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅良心再都唔能夠忍受艾米感激嘅幸福,佢嘅嫉妒再都唔能夠忍受另一種痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的良心再也不能忍受艾米感激的幸福,他的嫉妒再也不能忍受另一種痛苦。

passages.original: Becky resumed her picture inspections with Alfred, but as the minutes dragged along and no Tom came to suffer, her triumph began to cloud and she lost interest; gravity and absentmindedness followed, and then melancholy; two or three times she pricked up her ear at a footstep, but it was a false hope; no Tom came.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪繼續同阿爾弗雷德睇圖畫,但隨住幾分鐘拖過去,湯姆冇嚟受苦,佢嘅勝利開始蒙上陰影,佢失去咗興趣;嚴肅同心不喺焉隨之而嚟,然後係憂鬱;兩三次佢聽到腳步聲豎起耳朵,但係假希望;湯姆冇嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪繼續同阿爾弗雷德看圖畫,但隨著幾分鐘拖過去,湯姆沒來受苦,她的勝利開始蒙上陰影,她失去了興趣;嚴肅和心不在焉隨之而來,然後是憂鬱;兩三次她聽到腳步聲豎起耳朵,但是假希望;湯姆沒來。

passages.original: At last she grew entirely miserable and wished she hadn’t carried it so far.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢變得完全悲慘,希望佢冇做得咁過分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後她變得完全悲慘,希望她沒有做得那麼過分。

passages.original: When poor Alfred, seeing that he was losing her, he did not know how, kept exclaiming: “Oh, here’s a jolly one! look at this!” she lost patience at last, and said, “Oh, don’t bother me!
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅阿爾弗雷德見自己正在失去佢,唔知道點回事,不斷喊:「哦,呢度有個好玩嘅!睇呢個!」佢終於失去耐心,講:「哦,別煩我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的阿爾弗雷德見自己正在失去她,不知道怎麼回事,不斷喊:「哦,這裡有個好玩的!看這個!」她終於失去耐心,說:「哦,別煩我!

passages.original: I don’t care for them!” and burst into tears, and got up and walked away.
passages.vernacular: 我不在乎佢哋!」哭咗起嚟,站起嚟走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不在乎它們!」哭了起來,站起來走開。

passages.original: Alfred dropped alongside and was going to try to comfort her, but she said:
passages.vernacular: 阿爾弗雷德跟喺旁邊,想試住安慰佢,但佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿爾弗雷德跟在旁邊,想試著安慰她,但她說:

passages.original: “Go away and leave me alone, can’t you!
passages.vernacular: 「走開,別管我,好嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「走開,別管我,好嗎!

passages.original: I hate you!”
passages.vernacular: 我恨你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我恨你!」

passages.original: So the boy halted, wondering what he could have done—for she had said she would look at pictures all through the nooning—and she walked on, crying.
passages.vernacular: 於是男孩停下,納悶佢做咗乜嘢——因為佢講過佢要整個午休都睇圖畫——佢哭住走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是男孩停下,納悶他做了什麼——因為她說過她要整個午休都看圖畫——她哭著走了。

passages.original: Then Alfred went musing into the deserted schoolhouse.
passages.vernacular: 然後阿爾弗雷德沉思住走進空蕩蕩嘅校舍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後阿爾弗雷德沉思著走進空蕩蕩的校舍。

passages.original: He was humiliated and angry.
passages.vernacular: 佢感到屈辱同憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他感到屈辱和憤怒。

passages.original: He easily guessed his way to the truth—the girl had simply made a convenience of him to vent her spite upon Tom Sawyer.
passages.vernacular: 佢好容易猜出真相——女孩不過係把佢當作工具,對湯姆·索亞發洩佢嘅怨恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他很容易猜出真相——女孩不過是把他當作工具,對湯姆·索亞發洩她的怨恨。

passages.original: He was far from hating Tom the less when this thought occurred to him.
passages.vernacular: 想到呢個時,佢遠冇因此少恨湯姆啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到這個時,他遠沒有因此少恨湯姆一點。

passages.original: He wished there was some way to get that boy into trouble without much risk to himself.
passages.vernacular: 佢希望有辦法讓嗰個男孩惹麻煩而自己不冒太大風險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他希望有辦法讓那個男孩惹麻煩而自己不冒太大風險。

passages.original: Tom’s spelling-book fell under his eye.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅拼字課本落入佢嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的拼字課本落入他的眼睛。

passages.original: Here was his opportunity.
passages.vernacular: 機會嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 機會來了。

passages.original: He gratefully opened to the lesson for the afternoon and poured ink upon the page.
passages.vernacular: 佢感激地翻開下午嘅課,把墨水倒喺嗰頁上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他感激地翻開下午的課,把墨水倒在那頁上。

passages.original: Becky, glancing in at a window behind him at the moment, saw the act, and moved on, without discovering herself.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪此刻正好從佢身後嘅窗口瞥進嚟,睇到咗呢個動作,走開喇,冇暴露自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪此刻正好從他身後的窗口瞥進來,看到了這個動作,走開了,沒有暴露自己。

passages.original: She started homeward, now, intending to find Tom and tell him; Tom would be thankful and their troubles would be healed.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家開始往家走,打算找到湯姆告訴佢;湯姆會感激,佢哋嘅煩惱就會癒合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在開始往家走,打算找到湯姆告訴他;湯姆會感激,他們的煩惱就會癒合。

passages.original: Before she was half way home, however, she had changed her mind.
passages.vernacular: 然而佢仲冇走到一半就改變咗主意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而她還沒走到一半就改變了主意。

passages.original: The thought of Tom’s treatment of her when she was talking about her picnic came scorching back and filled her with shame.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喺佢談論佢嘅野餐時對待佢嘅方式嘅念頭灼熱地回嚟,使佢充滿羞恥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆在她談論她的野餐時對待她的方式的念頭灼熱地回來,使她充滿羞恥。

passages.original: She resolved to let him get whipped on the damaged spelling-book’s account, and to hate him forever, into the bargain.
passages.vernacular: 佢決心讓佢因損壞嘅拼字課本挨鞭打,並且永遠恨佢,作為附帶嘅獎賞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她決心讓他因損壞的拼字課本挨鞭打,並且永遠恨他,作為附帶的獎賞。

chapters.title: Chapter XIX: Tom Tells the Truth 第十九章:湯姆說出真相

passages.original: CH Tom arrived at home in a dreary mood, and the first thing his aunt said to him showed him that he had brought his sorrows to an unpromising market:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆心情沉悶地到家,佢姨媽對佢講嘅第一句話表明,佢把佢嘅悲傷帶到咗一個冇前途嘅市場:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆心情沉悶地到家,他姨媽對他說的第一句話表明,他把他的悲傷帶到了一個沒有前途的市場:

passages.original: “Tom, I’ve a notion to skin you alive!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我真想把你活剝喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我真想把你活剝了!」

passages.original: “Auntie, what have I done?”
passages.vernacular: 「姨媽,我做咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「姨媽,我做了什麼?」

passages.original: “Well, you’ve done enough.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你做得夠多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你做得夠多了。

passages.original: Here I go over to Sereny Harper, like an old softy, expecting I’m going to make her believe all that rubbage about that dream, when lo and behold you she’d found out from Joe that you was over here and heard all the talk we had that night.
passages.vernacular: 我像個老糊塗一樣跑到塞蕾妮·哈珀嗰度,以為我會讓佢相信關於嗰個夢嘅所有廢話,邊個知你猜點住,佢從喬嗰度發現你當時喺呢度,聽到咗我哋嗰天晚上嘅所有談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我像個老糊塗一樣跑到塞蕾妮·哈珀那裡,以為我會讓她相信關於那個夢的所有廢話,誰知你猜怎麼著,她從喬那裡發現你當時在這裡,聽到了我們那天晚上的所有談話。

passages.original: Tom, I don’t know what is to become of a boy that will act like that.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,我唔知道一個會咁樣做嘅男孩將來會點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,我不知道一個會這樣做的男孩將來會怎樣。

passages.original: It makes me feel so bad to think you could let me go to Sereny Harper and make such a fool of myself and never say a word.”
passages.vernacular: 想到你竟然讓我去塞蕾妮·哈珀嗰度出咁樣嘅洋相,一句話都不講,我就覺得好難受。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到你竟然讓我去塞蕾妮·哈珀那裡出這樣的洋相,一句話也不說,我就覺得很難受。」

passages.original: This was a new aspect of the thing.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係呢件事嘅一個新面貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是這件事的一個新面貌。

passages.original: His smartness of the morning had seemed to Tom a good joke before, and very ingenious.
passages.vernacular: 佢早晨嘅聰明以前喺湯姆睇來係個好玩笑,而且好巧妙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他早晨的聰明以前在湯姆看來是個好玩笑,而且很巧妙。

passages.original: It merely looked mean and shabby now.
passages.vernacular: 而家只顯得卑鄙同寒酸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在只顯得卑鄙和寒酸。

passages.original: He hung his head and could not think of anything to say for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 佢垂住頭,一時想不出任何話講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他垂著頭,一時想不出任何話說。

passages.original: Then he said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他說:

passages.original: “Auntie, I wish I hadn’t done it—but I didn’t think.”
passages.vernacular: 「姨媽,我希望我冇做——但我冇想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「姨媽,我希望我沒做——但我沒想。」

passages.original: “Oh, child, you never think.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,細路,你從唔想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,孩子,你從不想。

passages.original: You never think of anything but your own selfishness.
passages.vernacular: 你除咗你自己嘅自私,乜嘢都唔想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你除了你自己的自私,什麼也不想。

passages.original: You could think to come all the way over here from Jackson’s Island in the night to laugh at our troubles, and you could think to fool me with a lie about a dream; but you couldn’t ever think to pity us and save us from sorrow.”
passages.vernacular: 你能想到半夜從傑克森島一路過嚟嘲笑我哋嘅煩惱,你能想到用一個關於夢嘅謊言愚弄我;但你從唔能夠想到可憐我哋、使我哋免於悲傷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能想到半夜從傑克森島一路過來嘲笑我們的煩惱,你能想到用一個關於夢的謊言愚弄我;但你從不能想到可憐我們、使我們免於悲傷。」

passages.original: “Auntie, I know now it was mean, but I didn’t mean to be mean.
passages.vernacular: 「姨媽,我而家知道嗰個係卑鄙嘅,但我唔係有意卑鄙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「姨媽,我現在知道那是卑鄙的,但我不是有意卑鄙。

passages.original: I didn’t, honest.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係,講實話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是,說實話。

passages.original: And besides, I didn’t come over here to laugh at you that night.”
passages.vernacular: 而且,嗰天晚上我過嚟唔係為了嘲笑你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,那天晚上我過來不是為了嘲笑你。」

passages.original: “What did you come for, then?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你係點解嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你是為什麼來的?」

passages.original: “It was to tell you not to be uneasy about us, because we hadn’t got drownded.”
passages.vernacular: 「係告訴你唔好為我哋擔心,因為我哋冇淹死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是告訴你不要為我們擔心,因為我們沒有淹死。」

passages.original: “Tom, Tom, I would be the thankfullest soul in this world if I could believe you ever had as good a thought as that, but you know you never did—and I know it, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,湯姆,如果我能相信你曾經有過咁好嘅想法,我會係世界上最感激嘅人,但你知道你從冇——我都知道,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,湯姆,如果我能相信你曾經有過這麼好的想法,我會是世界上最感激的人,但你知道你從沒有——我也知道,湯姆。」

passages.original: “Indeed and ’deed I did, auntie—I wish I may never stir if I didn’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅,真嘅我有,姨媽——如果我冇,我願永遠不動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的,真的我有,姨媽——如果我沒有,我願永遠不動。」

passages.original: “Oh, Tom, don’t lie—don’t do it.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆,別撒謊——別咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆,別撒謊——別這樣。

passages.original: It only makes things a hundred times worse.”
passages.vernacular: 佢只會使事情壞一百倍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它只會使事情壞一百倍。」

passages.original: “It ain’t a lie, auntie; it’s the truth.
passages.vernacular: 「呢唔係謊話,姨媽;係真話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不是謊話,姨媽;是真話。

passages.original: I wanted to keep you from grieving—that was all that made me come.”
passages.vernacular: 我想不讓你悲傷——嗰個係使我過嚟嘅全部原因。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想不讓你悲傷——那是使我過來的全部原因。」

passages.original: “I’d give the whole world to believe that—it would cover up a power of sins, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「我願意付出整個世界嚟相信嗰個——佢會掩蓋好多罪,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我願意付出整個世界來相信那個——它會掩蓋很多罪,湯姆。

passages.original: I’d ’most be glad you’d run off and acted so bad.
passages.vernacular: 我幾乎會為你跑掉、表現得咁壞而高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幾乎會為你跑掉、表現得那麼壞而高興。

passages.original: But it ain’t reasonable; because, why didn’t you tell me, child?”
passages.vernacular: 但呢不合理;因為,你點解不告訴我,細路?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這不合理;因為,你為什麼不告訴我,孩子?」

passages.original: “Why, you see, when you got to talking about the funeral, I just got all full of the idea of our coming and hiding in the church, and I couldn’t somehow bear to spoil it.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,你睇,你講到葬禮時,我滿腦子都係我哋嚟躲喺教堂裡嘅主意,我唔知點不忍心破壞佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,你看,你說到葬禮時,我滿腦子都是我們來躲在教堂裡的主意,我不知怎麼不忍心破壞它。

passages.original: So I just put the bark back in my pocket and kept mum.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我就把樹皮放回口袋,冇作聲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我就把樹皮放回口袋,沒作聲。」

passages.original: “What bark?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢樹皮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼樹皮?」

passages.original: “The bark I had wrote on to tell you we’d gone pirating.
passages.vernacular: 「我寫咗字告訴你我哋去當海盜咗嘅嗰塊樹皮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我寫了字告訴你我們去當海盜了的那塊樹皮。

passages.original: I wish, now, you’d waked up when I kissed you—I do, honest.”
passages.vernacular: 我而家希望你喺我吻你時醒嚟——我真嘅希望,講實話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在希望你在我吻你時醒來——我真的希望,說實話。」

passages.original: The hard lines in his aunt’s face relaxed and a sudden tenderness dawned in her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢姨媽臉上嘅硬線條放鬆喇,眼睛裡突然露出溫柔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他姨媽臉上的硬線條放鬆了,眼睛裡突然露出溫柔。

passages.original: “Did you kiss me, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 「你吻我咗嗎,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你吻我了嗎,湯姆?」

passages.original: “Why, yes, I did.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,係嘅,我吻喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,是的,我吻了。」

passages.original: “Are you sure you did, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 「你確定你吻喇,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你確定你吻了,湯姆?」

passages.original: “Why, yes, I did, auntie—certain sure.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,係嘅,我吻喇,姨媽——肯定。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,是的,我吻了,姨媽——肯定。」

passages.original: “What did you kiss me for, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點解吻我,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼吻我,湯姆?」

passages.original: “Because I loved you so, and you laid there moaning and I was so sorry.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為我咁愛你,你躺喺嗰度呻吟,我好難過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為我那麼愛你,你躺在那裡呻吟,我很難過。」

passages.original: The words sounded like truth.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲話聽起嚟像真話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些話聽起來像真話。

passages.original: The old lady could not hide a tremor in her voice when she said:
passages.vernacular: 老太太講話時,聲音裡無法掩飾顫抖:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老太太說話時,聲音裡無法掩飾顫抖:

passages.original: “Kiss me again, Tom!—and be off with you to school, now, and don’t bother me any more.”
passages.vernacular: 「再吻我一次,湯姆!——而家去學校吧,唔好再煩我喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再吻我一次,湯姆!——現在去學校吧,別再煩我了。」

passages.original: The moment he was gone, she ran to a closet and got out the ruin of a jacket which Tom had gone pirating in.
passages.vernacular: 佢一走,佢就跑到一個櫃子旁,攞出湯姆去當海盜時穿嘅嗰件破外套嘅殘骸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一走,她就跑到一個櫃子旁,拿出湯姆去當海盜時穿的那件破外套的殘骸。

passages.original: Then she stopped, with it in her hand, and said to herself:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢停下,手裡攞住佢,對自己講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她停下,手裡拿著它,對自己說:

passages.original: “No, I don’t dare.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我唔敢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我不敢。

passages.original: Poor boy, I reckon he’s lied about it—but it’s a blessed, blessed lie, there’s such a comfort come from it.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅細路,我想佢撒咗謊——但呢個係個有福嘅、有福嘅謊言,從中得到咁大嘅安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的孩子,我想他撒了謊——但這是個有福的、有福的謊言,從中得到那麼大的安慰。

passages.original: I hope the Lord—I know the Lord will forgive him, because it was such good-heartedness in him to tell it.
passages.vernacular: 我希望主——我知道主會原諒佢,因為佢講呢話係咁好嘅心腸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望主——我知道主會原諒他,因為他說這話是那麼好的心腸。

passages.original: But I don’t want to find out it’s a lie.
passages.vernacular: 但我唔想發現呢個係個謊言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不想發現這是個謊言。

passages.original: I won’t look.”
passages.vernacular: 我不睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不看。」

passages.original: She put the jacket away, and stood by musing a minute.
passages.vernacular: 佢把外套放好,站住沉思咗一分鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把外套放好,站著沉思了一分鐘。

passages.original: Twice she put out her hand to take the garment again, and twice she refrained.
passages.vernacular: 兩次佢伸出手想再攞嗰件衣服,兩次佢克制住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩次她伸出手想再拿那件衣服,兩次她克制住了。

passages.original: Once more she ventured, and this time she fortified herself with the thought: “It’s a good lie—it’s a good lie—I won’t let it grieve me.”
passages.vernacular: 又一次佢冒險,呢次佢用呢個念頭加強自己:「呢個係個好謊言——呢個係個好謊言——我不讓佢使我悲傷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一次她冒險,這次她用這個念頭加強自己:「這是個好謊言——這是個好謊言——我不讓它使我悲傷。」

passages.original: So she sought the jacket pocket.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢去摸外套口袋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是她去摸外套口袋。

passages.original: A moment later she was reading Tom’s piece of bark through flowing tears and saying: “I could forgive the boy, now, if he’d committed a million sins!”
passages.vernacular: 片刻後佢透過流淌嘅淚水讀住湯姆嗰塊樹皮,講住:「我而家可以原諒呢細路,即使佢犯咗一百萬樁罪!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 片刻後她透過流淌的淚水讀著湯姆那塊樹皮,說著:「我現在可以原諒這孩子,即使他犯了一百萬樁罪!」

chapters.title: Chapter XX: Becky in a Dilemma 第二十章:貝琪的困境

passages.original: CH There was something about Aunt Polly’s manner, when she kissed Tom, that swept away his low spirits and made him lighthearted and happy again.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽吻湯姆時嘅神態,有一種嘢掃除咗佢嘅低落情緒,使佢又變得輕鬆快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽吻湯姆時的神態,有一種東西掃除了他的低落情緒,使他又變得輕鬆快樂。

passages.original: He started to school and had the luck of coming upon Becky Thatcher at the head of Meadow Lane.
passages.vernacular: 佢出發去學校,運氣好,喺草地巷口遇到咗貝琪·撒切爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他出發去學校,運氣好,在草地巷口遇到了貝琪·撒切爾。

passages.original: His mood always determined his manner.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅心情總是決定佢嘅態度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的心情總是決定他的態度。

passages.original: Without a moment’s hesitation he ran to her and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢毫不猶豫地跑到佢面前講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他毫不猶豫地跑到她面前說:

passages.original: “I acted mighty mean today, Becky, and I’m so sorry.
passages.vernacular: 「我今日表現得好卑鄙,貝琪,我好抱歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我今天表現得非常卑鄙,貝琪,我很抱歉。

passages.original: I won’t ever, ever do that way again, as long as ever I live—please make up, won’t you?”
passages.vernacular: 只要我活住,我永遠、永遠唔會再嗰樣做——求你同好吧,好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要我活著,我永遠、永遠不會再那樣做——求你和好吧,好嗎?」

passages.original: The girl stopped and looked him scornfully in the face:
passages.vernacular: 女孩停下嚟,輕蔑地睇住佢嘅臉:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩停下來,輕蔑地看著他的臉:

passages.original: “I’ll thank you to keep yourself to yourself, Mr. Thomas Sawyer.
passages.vernacular: 「請你管好你自己,湯瑪斯·索亞先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請你管好你自己,湯瑪斯·索亞先生。

passages.original: I’ll never speak to you again.”
passages.vernacular: 我再都不同你講話喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我再也不同你說話了。」

passages.original: She tossed her head and passed on.
passages.vernacular: 佢昂起頭,走過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她昂起頭,走過去了。
