passages.original: Tom was so stunned that he had not even presence of mind enough to say “Who cares, Miss Smarty?” until the right time to say it had gone by.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆被震住喇,甚至冇足夠嘅機智講「邊個在乎,自作聰明小姐?」,直到講呢句話嘅恰當時機已經過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆被震住了,甚至沒有足夠的機智說「誰在乎,自作聰明小姐?」,直到說這句話的恰當時機已經過去。

passages.original: So he said nothing.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他什麼也沒說。

passages.original: But he was in a fine rage, nevertheless.
passages.vernacular: 但佢仍然好憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他仍然非常憤怒。

passages.original: He moped into the schoolyard wishing she were a boy, and imagining how he would trounce her if she were.
passages.vernacular: 佢悶悶不樂地走進校園,希望佢係個男孩,想像如果佢係,佢會點樣痛打佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他悶悶不樂地走進校園,希望她是個男孩,想像如果她是,他會怎樣痛打她。

passages.original: He presently encountered her and delivered a stinging remark as he passed.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢遇到佢,經過時講咗一句刺人嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他遇到她,經過時說了一句刺人的話。

passages.original: She hurled one in return, and the angry breach was complete.
passages.vernacular: 佢回敬一句,憤怒嘅決裂就完成喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她回敬一句,憤怒的決裂就完成了。

passages.original: It seemed to Becky, in her hot resentment, that she could hardly wait for school to “take in,” she was so impatient to see Tom flogged for the injured spelling-book.
passages.vernacular: 喺貝琪熱烈嘅怨恨中,佢似乎幾乎等不及學校「開課」,佢咁急著想睇湯姆因受損嘅拼字課本挨鞭打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在貝琪熱烈的怨恨中,她似乎幾乎等不及學校「開課」,她那麼急著想看湯姆因受損的拼字課本挨鞭打。

passages.original: If she had had any lingering notion of exposing Alfred Temple, Tom’s offensive fling had driven it entirely away.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢仲有任何揭露阿爾弗雷德·坦普爾嘅殘留念頭,湯姆嗰句冒犯嘅話把佢完全趕走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她還有任何揭露阿爾弗雷德·坦普爾的殘留念頭,湯姆那句冒犯的話把它完全趕走了。

passages.original: Poor girl, she did not know how fast she was nearing trouble herself.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅女孩,佢唔知道佢自己正多快地接近麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的女孩,她不知道她自己正多快地接近麻煩。

passages.original: The master, Mr. Dobbins, had reached middle age with an unsatisfied ambition.
passages.vernacular: 老師道賓斯先生到咗中年,仍有一個未實現嘅野心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師道賓斯先生到了中年,仍有一個未實現的野心。

passages.original: The darling of his desires was, to be a doctor, but poverty had decreed that he should be nothing higher than a village schoolmaster.
passages.vernacular: 佢心愛嘅願望係當醫生,但貧窮規定佢只能做個鄉村校長,唔能夠更高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他心愛的願望是當醫生,但貧窮規定他只能做個鄉村校長,不能更高。

passages.original: Every day he took a mysterious book out of his desk and absorbed himself in it at times when no classes were reciting.
passages.vernacular: 每天佢從桌子裡攞出一本神祕嘅書,喺冇班級背誦嘅時候全神貫注地睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每天他從桌子裡拿出一本神祕的書,在沒有班級背誦的時候全神貫注地看。

passages.original: He kept that book under lock and key.
passages.vernacular: 佢把嗰本書鎖得好好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把那本書鎖得好好的。

passages.original: There was not an urchin in school but was perishing to have a glimpse of it, but the chance never came.
passages.vernacular: 學校裡冇一個頑童不渴望瞥一眼佢,但機會從冇嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學校裡沒有一個頑童不渴望瞥一眼它,但機會從沒有來。

passages.original: Every boy and girl had a theory about the nature of that book; but no two theories were alike, and there was no way of getting at the facts in the case.
passages.vernacular: 每個男孩女孩對嗰本書嘅性質都有一個理論;但冇兩個理論相同,冇辦法弄清呢件事嘅事實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個男孩女孩對那本書的性質都有一個理論;但沒有兩個理論相同,沒有辦法弄清這件事的事實。

passages.original: Now, as Becky was passing by the desk, which stood near the door, she noticed that the key was in the lock!
passages.vernacular: 而家,貝琪經過靠近門嘅桌子時,佢注意到鑰匙插喺鎖裡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,貝琪經過靠近門的桌子時,她注意到鑰匙插在鎖裡!

passages.original: It was a precious moment.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個珍貴嘅時刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個珍貴的時刻。

passages.original: She glanced around; found herself alone, and the next instant she had the book in her hands.
passages.vernacular: 佢環顧四周;發現自己一個人,下一刻書已喺佢手裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她環顧四周;發現自己一個人,下一刻書已在她手裡。

passages.original: The titlepage—Professor Somebody’s Anatomy—carried no information to her mind; so she began to turn the leaves.
passages.vernacular: 書名頁——某某教授嘅《解剖學》——冇畀佢嘅頭腦帶嚟任何信息;於是佢開始翻頁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 書名頁——某某教授的《解剖學》——沒給她的頭腦帶來任何信息;於是她開始翻頁。

passages.original: She came at once upon a handsomely engraved and colored frontispiece—a human figure, stark naked.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻睇到一幅精美雕刻、上色嘅卷首插圖——一個人體,全身赤裸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她馬上看到一幅精美雕刻、上色的卷首插圖——一個人體,全身赤裸。

passages.original: At that moment a shadow fell on the page and Tom Sawyer stepped in at the door and caught a glimpse of the picture.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢一刻,一道影子落喺書頁上,湯姆·索亞走進門,瞥見咗嗰幅畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這一刻,一道影子落在書頁上,湯姆·索亞走進門,瞥見了那幅畫。

passages.original: Becky snatched at the book to close it, and had the hard luck to tear the pictured page half down the middle.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪猛地抓起書想合上,不幸把嗰張有畫嘅書頁從中間撕下咗一半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪猛地抓起書想合上,不幸把那張有畫的書頁從中間撕下了一半。

passages.original: She thrust the volume into the desk, turned the key, and burst out crying with shame and vexation.
passages.vernacular: 佢把書塞進桌子,轉動鑰匙,羞愧同惱怒地哭咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把書塞進桌子,轉動鑰匙,羞愧和惱怒地哭了起來。

passages.original: “Tom Sawyer, you are just as mean as you can be, to sneak up on a person and look at what they’re looking at.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆·索亞,你卑鄙到極點,偷偷靠近一個人睇佢喺睇乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆·索亞,你卑鄙到極點,偷偷靠近一個人看她在看什麼。」

passages.original: “How could I know you was looking at anything?”
passages.vernacular: 「我點知道你喺睇乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怎麼知道你在看什麼?」

passages.original: “You ought to be ashamed of yourself, Tom Sawyer; you know you’re going to tell on me, and oh, what shall I do, what shall I do!
passages.vernacular: 「你應該為自己感到羞恥,湯姆·索亞;你知道你要告發我,哦,我點算,我點算!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你應該為自己感到羞恥,湯姆·索亞;你知道你要告發我,哦,我怎麼辦,我怎麼辦!

passages.original: I’ll be whipped, and I never was whipped in school.”
passages.vernacular: 我會被鞭打,我喺學校從冇被鞭打過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會被鞭打,我在學校從沒被鞭打過。」

passages.original: Then she stamped her little foot and said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢跺住小腳講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她跺著小腳說:

passages.original: “Be so mean if you want to!
passages.vernacular: 「你想卑鄙就卑鄙吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想卑鄙就卑鄙吧!

passages.original: I know something that’s going to happen.
passages.vernacular: 我知道將要發生乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道將要發生什麼。

passages.original: You just wait and you’ll see!
passages.vernacular: 你等住瞧吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你等著瞧吧!

passages.original: Hateful, hateful, hateful!”—and she flung out of the house with a new explosion of crying.
passages.vernacular: 可恨,可恨,可恨!」——佢哭住再次爆發,衝出咗屋子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可恨,可恨,可恨!」——她哭著再次爆發,衝出了屋子。

passages.original: Tom stood still, rather flustered by this onslaught.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆站住不動,被呢番攻擊弄得有些慌亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆站著不動,被這番攻擊弄得有些慌亂。

passages.original: Presently he said to himself:
passages.vernacular: 不久佢對自己講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他對自己說:

passages.original: “What a curious kind of a fool a girl is!
passages.vernacular: 「女孩係幾咁古怪嘅傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「女孩是多麼古怪的傻瓜!

passages.original: Never been licked in school!
passages.vernacular: 喺學校從冇挨過揍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在學校從沒挨過揍!

passages.original: Shucks!
passages.vernacular: 算喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 算了!

passages.original: What’s a licking!
passages.vernacular: 挨揍算乜嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 挨揍算什麼!

passages.original: That’s just like a girl—they’re so thin-skinned and chicken-hearted.
passages.vernacular: 呢正是女孩嘅樣子——佢哋咁薄皮、咁膽小。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這正是女孩的樣子——她們那麼薄皮、那麼膽小。

passages.original: Well, of course I ain’t going to tell old Dobbins on this little fool, because there’s other ways of getting even on her, that ain’t so mean; but what of it?
passages.vernacular: 好吧,當然我唔會向老道賓斯告發呢個小傻瓜,因為有其他不咁卑鄙嘅辦法同佢算帳;但嗰又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,當然我不會向老道賓斯告發這個小傻瓜,因為有其他不那麼卑鄙的辦法同她算帳;但那又怎麼樣?

passages.original: Old Dobbins will ask who it was tore his book.
passages.vernacular: 老道賓斯會問係邊個撕咗佢嘅書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老道賓斯會問是誰撕了他的書。

passages.original: Nobody’ll answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇人回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人回答。

passages.original: Then he’ll do just the way he always does—ask first one and then t’other, and when he comes to the right girl he’ll know it, without any telling.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢會像佢一貫嗰樣——先問一個然後問另一個,問到嗰個女孩時,佢唔使任何人講就會知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他會像他一貫那樣——先問一個然後問另一個,問到那個女孩時,他不用任何人說就會知道。

passages.original: Girls’ faces always tell on them.
passages.vernacular: 女孩嘅臉總是出賣佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩的臉總是出賣她們。

passages.original: They ain’t got any backbone.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋冇骨氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們沒有骨氣。

passages.original: She’ll get licked.
passages.vernacular: 佢會挨打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會挨打。

passages.original: Well, it’s a kind of a tight place for Becky Thatcher, because there ain’t any way out of it.”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,呢對貝琪·撒切爾係個困境,因為冇出路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,這對貝琪·撒切爾是個困境,因為沒有出路。」

passages.original: Tom conned the thing a moment longer, and then added: “All right, though; she’d like to see me in just such a fix—let her sweat it out!”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆又琢磨咗一會兒,然後補充:「不過,好吧;佢好樂意睇到我處喺咁樣嘅困境——讓佢煎熬吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆又琢磨了一會兒,然後補充:「不過,好吧;她很樂意看到我處在這樣的困境——讓她煎熬吧!」

passages.original: Tom joined the mob of skylarking scholars outside.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆加入咗外面嬉鬧嘅學生群。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆加入了外面嬉鬧的學生群。

passages.original: In a few moments the master arrived and school “took in.”
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒老師到喇,學校「開課」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒老師到了,學校「開課」。

passages.original: Tom did not feel a strong interest in his studies.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆對佢嘅學業冇強烈嘅興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆對他的學業沒有強烈的興趣。

passages.original: Every time he stole a glance at the girls’ side of the room Becky’s face troubled him.
passages.vernacular: 每次佢偷偷瞥向教室女生嗰邊,貝琪嘅臉都讓佢不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每次他偷偷瞥向教室女生那邊,貝琪的臉都讓他不安。

passages.original: Considering all things, he did not want to pity her, and yet it was all he could do to help it.
passages.vernacular: 考慮到一切,佢唔想可憐佢,但佢幾乎無法不咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 考慮到一切,他不想可憐她,但他幾乎無法不這樣。

passages.original: He could get up no exultation that was really worthy the name.
passages.vernacular: 佢無法升起任何真正配得上呢個名字嘅得意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他無法升起任何真正配得上這個名字的得意。

passages.original: Presently the spelling-book discovery was made, and Tom’s mind was entirely full of his own matters for a while after that.
passages.vernacular: 不久發現咗拼字課本,湯姆之後有一陣子心思完全被自己嘅事佔滿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久發現了拼字課本,湯姆之後有一陣子心思完全被自己的事佔滿。

passages.original: Becky roused up from her lethargy of distress and showed good interest in the proceedings.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪從痛苦嘅昏沉中振作起嚟,對審訊顯示出好好嘅興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪從痛苦的昏沉中振作起來,對審訊顯示出很好的興趣。

passages.original: She did not expect that Tom could get out of his trouble by denying that he spilt the ink on the book himself; and she was right.
passages.vernacular: 佢不指望湯姆能否認係自己把墨水灑喺書上而擺脫麻煩;佢係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不指望湯姆能否認是自己把墨水灑在書上而擺脫麻煩;她是對的。

passages.original: The denial only seemed to make the thing worse for Tom.
passages.vernacular: 否認似乎只使事情對湯姆更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 否認似乎只使事情對湯姆更糟。

passages.original: Becky supposed she would be glad of that, and she tried to believe she was glad of it, but she found she was not certain.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪以為佢會為此高興,佢試圖相信佢係高興嘅,但佢發現佢並不確定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪以為她會為此高興,她試圖相信她是高興的,但她發現她並不確定。

passages.original: When the worst came to the worst, she had an impulse to get up and tell on Alfred Temple, but she made an effort and forced herself to keep still—because, said she to herself, “he’ll tell about me tearing the picture sure.
passages.vernacular: 事態最壞時,佢有衝動站起嚟告發阿爾弗雷德·坦普爾,但佢努力強迫自己保持安靜——因為,佢對自己講,「佢肯定會講我撕畫嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事態最壞時,她有衝動站起來告發阿爾弗雷德·坦普爾,但她努力強迫自己保持安靜——因為,她對自己說,「他肯定會說我撕畫的事。

passages.original: I wouldn’t say a word, not to save his life!”
passages.vernacular: 我一個字都不講,即使為了救佢嘅命!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一個字也不說,即使為了救他的命!」

passages.original: Tom took his whipping and went back to his seat not at all broken-hearted, for he thought it was possible that he had unknowingly upset the ink on the spelling-book himself, in some skylarking bout—he had denied it for form’s sake and because it was custom, and had stuck to the denial from principle.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆挨咗鞭打,回到座位上,啲都不傷心,因為佢覺得有可能係佢喺某次嬉鬧中無意間把墨水灑喺咗拼字課本上——佢為了形式同因為呢個係慣例而否認,並出於原則堅持咗否認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆挨了鞭打,回到座位上,一點也不傷心,因為他覺得有可能是他在某次嬉鬧中無意間把墨水灑在了拼字課本上——他為了形式和因為這是慣例而否認,並出於原則堅持了否認。

passages.original: A whole hour drifted by, the master sat nodding in his throne, the air was drowsy with the hum of study.
passages.vernacular: 整整一個小時漂過去,老師坐喺寶座上打盹,空氣因學習嘅嗡嗡聲而昏昏欲瞓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整整一個小時漂過去,老師坐在寶座上打盹,空氣因學習的嗡嗡聲而昏昏欲睡。

passages.original: By and by, Mr. Dobbins straightened himself up, yawned, then unlocked his desk, and reached for his book, but seemed undecided whether to take it out or leave it.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地,道賓斯先生挺直身子,打咗個呵欠,然後打開桌子,伸手去攞佢嘅書,但似乎猶豫係攞出嚟定係留下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地,道賓斯先生挺直身子,打了個呵欠,然後打開桌子,伸手去拿他的書,但似乎猶豫是拿出來還是留下。

passages.original: Most of the pupils glanced up languidly, but there were two among them that watched his movements with intent eyes.
passages.vernacular: 大多數學生懶洋洋地抬頭睇咗一眼,但其中兩個用專注嘅眼睛睇住佢嘅動作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大多數學生懶洋洋地抬頭看了一眼,但其中兩個用專注的眼睛看著他的動作。

passages.original: Mr. Dobbins fingered his book absently for a while, then took it out and settled himself in his chair to read!
passages.vernacular: 道賓斯先生心不喺焉地撫弄咗一會兒佢嘅書,然後攞出嚟,安頓喺椅子上睇起嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 道賓斯先生心不在焉地撫弄了一會兒他的書,然後拿出來,安頓在椅子上看起來!

passages.original: Tom shot a glance at Becky.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆向貝琪瞥咗一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆向貝琪瞥了一眼。

passages.original: He had seen a hunted and helpless rabbit look as she did, with a gun levelled at its head.
passages.vernacular: 佢曾見過一隻被追獵嘅無助嘅兔子,頭上被槍指住時,就係佢嗰個樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他曾見過一隻被追獵的無助的兔子,頭上被槍指著時,就是她那個樣子。

passages.original: Instantly he forgot his quarrel with her.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻忘咗同佢嘅爭吵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他立刻忘了與她的爭吵。

passages.original: Quick—something must be done! done in a flash, too!
passages.vernacular: 快——必須做點乜嘢!都得喺一瞬間做!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快——必須做點什麼!也得在一瞬間做!

passages.original: But the very imminence of the emergency paralyzed his invention.
passages.vernacular: 但緊急情況嘅迫近恰恰使佢嘅急智癱瘓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但緊急情況的迫近恰恰使他的急智癱瘓。

passages.original: Good!—he had an inspiration!
passages.vernacular: 好!——佢有咗靈感!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好!——他有了靈感!

passages.original: He would run and snatch the book, spring through the door and fly.
passages.vernacular: 佢要跑過去搶書,跳出門飛奔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要跑過去搶書,跳出門飛奔。

passages.original: But his resolution shook for one little instant, and the chance was lost—the master opened the volume.
passages.vernacular: 但佢嘅決心動搖咗一小會兒,機會失去喇——老師打開咗書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他的決心動搖了一小會兒,機會失去了——老師打開了書。

passages.original: If Tom only had the wasted opportunity back again!
passages.vernacular: 如果湯姆能把浪費嘅機會攞回嚟就好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果湯姆能把浪費的機會拿回來就好了!

passages.original: Too late.
passages.vernacular: 太遲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太遲了。

passages.original: There was no help for Becky now, he said.
passages.vernacular: 而家貝琪冇救喇,佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在貝琪沒救了,他說。

passages.original: The next moment the master faced the school.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻老師面向學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻老師面向學校。

passages.original: Every eye sank under his gaze.
passages.vernacular: 每雙眼睛都喺佢嘅凝視下沉下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每雙眼睛都在他的凝視下沉下去。

passages.original: There was that in it which smote even the innocent with fear.
passages.vernacular: 嗰凝視裡有一種嘢,連無辜嘅人都嚇得發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那凝視裡有一種東西,連無辜的人也嚇得發抖。

passages.original: There was silence while one might count ten—the master was gathering his wrath.
passages.vernacular: 沉默咗大約數十個數嘅時間——老師喺積聚佢嘅憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉默了大約數十個數的時間——老師在積聚他的憤怒。

passages.original: Then he spoke: “Who tore this book?”
passages.vernacular: 然後佢講:「邊個撕咗呢本書?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他說:「誰撕了這本書?」

passages.original: There was not a sound.
passages.vernacular: 冇啲聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一點聲音。

passages.original: One could have heard a pin drop.
passages.vernacular: 落下一根針都能聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 落下一根針都能聽見。

passages.original: The stillness continued; the master searched face after face for signs of guilt.
passages.vernacular: 寂靜持續住;老師一張臉一張臉地搜尋罪過嘅跡象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寂靜持續著;老師一張臉一張臉地搜尋罪過的跡象。

passages.original: “Benjamin Rogers, did you tear this book?”
passages.vernacular: 「本傑明·羅傑斯,係你撕咗呢本書嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「本傑明·羅傑斯,是你撕了這本書嗎?」

passages.original: A denial.
passages.vernacular: 否認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 否認。

passages.original: Another pause.
passages.vernacular: 又一個停頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一個停頓。

passages.original: “Joseph Harper, did you?”
passages.vernacular: 「約瑟夫·哈珀,係你嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約瑟夫·哈珀,是你嗎?」

passages.original: Another denial.
passages.vernacular: 又一個否認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一個否認。

passages.original: Tom’s uneasiness grew more and more intense under the slow torture of these proceedings.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢啲程序緩慢嘅折磨下,湯姆嘅不安越嚟越強烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這些程序緩慢的折磨下,湯姆的不安越來越強烈。

passages.original: The master scanned the ranks of boys—considered a while, then turned to the girls:
passages.vernacular: 老師掃視男孩嘅隊列——考慮咗一會兒,然後轉向女孩:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師掃視男孩的隊列——考慮了一會兒,然後轉向女孩:

passages.original: “Amy Lawrence?”
passages.vernacular: 「艾米·勞倫斯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「艾米·勞倫斯?」

passages.original: A shake of the head.
passages.vernacular: 搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 搖頭。

passages.original: “Gracie Miller?”
passages.vernacular: 「格雷西·米勒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「格雷西·米勒?」

passages.original: The same sign.
passages.vernacular: 同樣嘅表示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同樣的表示。

passages.original: “Susan Harper, did you do this?”
passages.vernacular: 「蘇珊·哈珀,係你做嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蘇珊·哈珀,是你做的嗎?」

passages.original: Another negative.
passages.vernacular: 又一個否定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一個否定。

passages.original: The next girl was Becky Thatcher.
passages.vernacular: 下一個女孩係貝琪·撒切爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一個女孩是貝琪·撒切爾。

passages.original: Tom was trembling from head to foot with excitement and a sense of the hopelessness of the situation.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆因興奮同對局勢無望嘅感覺而從頭到腳顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆因興奮和對局勢無望的感覺而從頭到腳顫抖。

passages.original: “Rebecca Thatcher” [Tom glanced at her face—it was white with terror]—“did you tear—no, look me in the face” [her hands rose in appeal]—“did you tear this book?”
passages.vernacular: 「麗貝卡·撒切爾」[湯姆瞥咗一眼佢嘅臉——因恐懼而發白]——「係你撕嘅嗎——不,睇住我嘅臉」[佢嘅手舉起嚟求情]——「係你撕咗呢本書嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「麗貝卡·撒切爾」[湯姆瞥了一眼她的臉——因恐懼而發白]——「是你撕的嗎——不,看著我的臉」[她的手舉起來求情]——「是你撕了這本書嗎?」

passages.original: A thought shot like lightning through Tom’s brain.
passages.vernacular: 一個念頭像閃電般射過湯姆嘅腦子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個念頭像閃電般射過湯姆的腦子。

passages.original: He sprang to his feet and shouted—“I done it!”
passages.vernacular: 佢跳起嚟喊道——「係我幹嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他跳起來喊道——「是我幹的!」

passages.original: The school stared in perplexity at this incredible folly.
passages.vernacular: 全校困惑地瞪住呢難以置信嘅愚蠢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全校困惑地瞪著這難以置信的愚蠢。

passages.original: Tom stood a moment, to gather his dismembered faculties; and when he stepped forward to go to his punishment the surprise, the gratitude, the adoration that shone upon him out of poor Becky’s eyes seemed pay enough for a hundred floggings.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆站咗一會兒,收攏佢零散嘅神志;當佢走上前去接受懲罰時,可憐嘅貝琪眼睛裡閃耀住嘅驚訝、感激、崇拜,似乎足以抵一百次鞭打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆站了一會兒,收攏他零散的神志;當他走上前去接受懲罰時,可憐的貝琪眼睛裡閃耀著的驚訝、感激、崇拜,似乎足以抵一百次鞭打。

passages.original: Inspired by the splendor of his own act, he took without an outcry the most merciless flaying that even Mr. Dobbins had ever administered; and also received with indifference the added cruelty of a command to remain two hours after school should be dismissed—for he knew who would wait for him outside till his captivity was done, and not count the tedious time as loss, either.
passages.vernacular: 受到自己行為輝煌嘅鼓舞,佢冇叫一聲就承受咗連道賓斯先生都從未施予過嘅最無情嘅鞭打;仲漠然接受咗喺放學後多留兩個小時嘅命令嘅額外殘酷——因為佢知道邊個會喺外面等佢,直到佢嘅囚禁結束,都唔會把乏味嘅時間算作損失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 受到自己行為輝煌的鼓舞,他沒有叫一聲就承受了連道賓斯先生也從未施予過的最無情的鞭打;還漠然接受了在放學後多留兩個小時的命令的額外殘酷——因為他知道誰會在外面等他,直到他的囚禁結束,也不會把乏味的時間算作損失。

passages.original: Tom went to bed that night planning vengeance against Alfred Temple; for with shame and repentance Becky had told him all, not forgetting her own treachery; but even the longing for vengeance had to give way, soon, to pleasanter musings, and he fell asleep at last with Becky’s latest words lingering dreamily in his ear—
passages.vernacular: 嗰晚湯姆上床時計劃對阿爾弗雷德·坦普爾報復;因為貝琪懷住羞愧同悔過告訴咗佢一切,冇忘記佢自己嘅背叛;但連復仇嘅渴望都好快讓位畀更愉快嘅沉思,最後佢瞓住喇,貝琪最近嘅話語仍夢幻般縈繞喺佢耳邊——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那晚湯姆上床時計劃對阿爾弗雷德·坦普爾報復;因為貝琪懷著羞愧和悔過告訴了他一切,沒有忘記她自己的背叛;但連復仇的渴望也很快讓位給更愉快的沉思,最後他睡著了,貝琪最近的話語仍夢幻般縈繞在他耳邊——

passages.original: “Tom, how could you be so noble!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,你點能咁高尚!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,你怎麼能這麼高尚!」

chapters.title: Chapter XXI: Youthful Eloquence 第二十一章:少年雄辯

passages.original: CH Vacation was approaching.
passages.vernacular: 假期臨近喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假期臨近了。

passages.original: The schoolmaster, always severe, grew severer and more exacting than ever, for he wanted the school to make a good showing on “Examination” day.
passages.vernacular: 校長,一向嚴厲,變得比以往更嚴厲更苛求,因為佢想讓學校喺「考試」日有良好嘅表現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 校長,一向嚴厲,變得比以往更嚴厲更苛求,因為他想讓學校在「考試」日有良好的表現。

passages.original: His rod and his ferule were seldom idle now—at least among the smaller pupils.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅鞭子同戒尺而家好少閒住——至少對較小嘅學生係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的鞭子和戒尺現在很少閒著——至少對較小的學生是這樣。

passages.original: Only the biggest boys, and young ladies of eighteen and twenty, escaped lashing.
passages.vernacular: 只有最大嘅男孩同十八二十歲嘅年輕小姐逃過咗鞭打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有最大的男孩和十八二十歲的年輕小姐逃過了鞭打。

passages.original: Mr. Dobbins’ lashings were very vigorous ones, too; for although he carried, under his wig, a perfectly bald and shiny head, he had only reached middle age, and there was no sign of feebleness in his muscle.
passages.vernacular: 道賓斯先生嘅鞭打都好有力;因為雖然佢喺假髮下戴住一個完全禿而發亮嘅頭,佢只到中年,佢嘅肌肉冇任何衰弱嘅跡象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 道賓斯先生的鞭打也非常有力;因為雖然他在假髮下戴著一個完全禿而發亮的頭,他只到中年,他的肌肉沒有任何衰弱的跡象。

passages.original: As the great day approached, all the tyranny that was in him came to the surface; he seemed to take a vindictive pleasure in punishing the least shortcomings.
passages.vernacular: 隨住大日子臨近,佢身上所有嘅暴虐都浮出水面;佢似乎喺懲罰最小嘅缺點中得到一種報復性嘅快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨著大日子臨近,他身上所有的暴虐都浮出水面;他似乎在懲罰最小的缺點中得到一種報復性的快樂。

passages.original: The consequence was, that the smaller boys spent their days in terror and suffering and their nights in plotting revenge.
passages.vernacular: 結果係,較小嘅男孩哋白天喺恐懼同痛苦中度過,夜裡策劃報復。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果是,較小的男孩們白天在恐懼和痛苦中度過,夜裡策劃報復。

passages.original: They threw away no opportunity to do the master a mischief.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不放過任何對老師惡作劇嘅機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不放過任何對老師惡作劇的機會。

passages.original: But he kept ahead all the time.
passages.vernacular: 但佢一直領先。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他一直領先。

passages.original: The retribution that followed every vengeful success was so sweeping and majestic that the boys always retired from the field badly worsted.
passages.vernacular: 每次報復成功後隨之而嚟嘅報應係咁徹底而威嚴,男孩哋總是慘敗地從戰場撤退。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每次報復成功後隨之而來的報應是那麼徹底而威嚴,男孩們總是慘敗地從戰場撤退。

passages.original: At last they conspired together and hit upon a plan that promised a dazzling victory.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢哋合謀,想出一個承諾輝煌勝利嘅計畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他們合謀,想出一個承諾輝煌勝利的計畫。

passages.original: They swore in the signpainter’s boy, told him the scheme, and asked his help.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋宣誓拉進咗招牌畫匠嘅兒子,告訴佢計畫,請佢幫忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們宣誓拉進了招牌畫匠的兒子,告訴他計畫,請他幫忙。

passages.original: He had his own reasons for being delighted, for the master boarded in his father’s family and had given the boy ample cause to hate him.
passages.vernacular: 佢有佢自己高興嘅理由,因為老師喺佢父親家寄宿,畀咗呢男孩充分嘅理由恨佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有他自己高興的理由,因為老師在他父親家寄宿,給了這男孩充分的理由恨他。

passages.original: The master’s wife would go on a visit to the country in a few days, and there would be nothing to interfere with the plan; the master always prepared himself for great occasions by getting pretty well fuddled, and the signpainter’s boy said that when the dominie had reached the proper condition on Examination Evening he would “manage the thing” while he napped in his chair; then he would have him awakened at the right time and hurried away to school.
passages.vernacular: 老師嘅妻子幾天後要去鄉下探訪,就冇乜嘢會妨礙呢個計畫;老師總是通過飲得相當糊塗嚟為大場合做準備,招牌畫匠嘅兒子講,當老師喺考試晚上達到適當嘅狀態時,佢會喺老師喺椅子上打盹時「安排呢件事」;然後佢會喺適當嘅時候叫醒佢,匆忙送佢到學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師的妻子幾天後要去鄉下探訪,就沒有什麼會妨礙這個計畫;老師總是通過喝得相當糊塗來為大場合做準備,招牌畫匠的兒子說,當老師在考試晚上達到適當的狀態時,他會在老師在椅子上打盹時「安排這件事」;然後他會在適當的時候叫醒他,匆忙送他到學校。

passages.original: In the fulness of time the interesting occasion arrived.
passages.vernacular: 時機成熟,呢個有趣嘅場合到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時機成熟,這個有趣的場合到了。

passages.original: At eight in the evening the schoolhouse was brilliantly lighted, and adorned with wreaths and festoons of foliage and flowers.
passages.vernacular: 晚上八點,校舍燈火輝煌,用花環同樹葉花卉嘅垂飾裝飾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚上八點,校舍燈火輝煌,用花環和樹葉花卉的垂飾裝飾。

passages.original: The master sat throned in his great chair upon a raised platform, with his blackboard behind him.
passages.vernacular: 老師高坐喺高台上佢嘅大椅子上,身後係黑板。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師高坐在高台上他的大椅子上,身後是黑板。

passages.original: He was looking tolerably mellow.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟相當醺醺然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看起來相當醺醺然。

passages.original: Three rows of benches on each side and six rows in front of him were occupied by the dignitaries of the town and by the parents of the pupils.
passages.vernacular: 佢兩邊各三排長椅同面前六排長椅上,坐住鎮上嘅顯要同學生嘅家長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他兩邊各三排長椅和面前六排長椅上,坐著鎮上的顯要和學生的家長。

passages.original: To his left, back of the rows of citizens, was a spacious temporary platform upon which were seated the scholars who were to take part in the exercises of the evening; rows of small boys, washed and dressed to an intolerable state of discomfort; rows of gawky big boys; snowbanks of girls and young ladies clad in lawn and muslin and conspicuously conscious of their bare arms, their grandmothers’ ancient trinkets, their bits of pink and blue ribbon and the flowers in their hair.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢左邊,公民嘅排後面,係一個寬敞嘅臨時平台,上面坐住要參加當晚節目的學生:一排排洗過、打扮得到咗難以忍受嘅不舒服程度嘅小男孩;一排排笨拙嘅大男孩;一堆堆雪堆似嘅女孩同年輕小姐,穿住細麻布同薄紗,明顯地意識到佢哋裸露嘅手臂、佢哋祖母嘅古老小飾物、佢哋嘅粉紅色同藍色絲帶碎片同頭髮上嘅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他左邊,公民的排後面,是一個寬敞的臨時平台,上面坐著要參加當晚節目的學生:一排排洗過、打扮得到了難以忍受的不舒服程度的小男孩;一排排笨拙的大男孩;一堆堆雪堆似的女孩和年輕小姐,穿著細麻布和薄紗,明顯地意識到她們裸露的手臂、她們祖母的古老小飾物、她們的粉紅色和藍色絲帶碎片和頭髮上的花。

passages.original: All the rest of the house was filled with non-participating scholars.
passages.vernacular: 屋子其餘部分擠滿咗不參加節目的學生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 屋子其餘部分擠滿了不參加節目的學生。

passages.original: The exercises began.
passages.vernacular: 節目開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 節目開始了。

passages.original: A very little boy stood up and sheepishly recited, “You’d scarce expect one of my age to speak in public on the stage,” etc.—accompanying himself with the painfully exact and spasmodic gestures which a machine might have used—supposing the machine to be a trifle out of order.
passages.vernacular: 一個好小嘅男孩站起嚟,羞怯地背誦:「你好難期望我咁樣嘅年紀喺舞台上公開講話」等等——伴隨住一台機器可能用嘅痛苦準確而痙攣嘅手勢——假設呢台機器有點故障。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個很小的男孩站起來,羞怯地背誦:「你很難期望我這樣的年紀在舞台上公開講話」等等——伴隨著一台機器可能用的痛苦準確而痙攣的手勢——假設這台機器有點故障。

passages.original: But he got through safely, though cruelly scared, and got a fine round of applause when he made his manufactured bow and retired.
passages.vernacular: 但佢安全地通過喇,雖然嚇得厲害,佢做咗個機械嘅鞠躬退下時得到咗一輪不錯嘅掌聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他安全地通過了,雖然嚇得厲害,他做了個機械的鞠躬退下時得到了一輪不錯的掌聲。

passages.original: A little shamefaced girl lisped, “Mary had a little lamb,” etc., performed a compassion-inspiring curtsy, got her meed of applause, and sat down flushed and happy.
passages.vernacular: 一個害羞嘅小女孩口齒不清地講:「瑪麗有一隻小羊羔」等等,行咗個令人憐憫嘅屈膝禮,得到佢應得嘅掌聲,臉紅而高興地坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個害羞的小女孩口齒不清地說:「瑪麗有一隻小羊羔」等等,行了個令人憐憫的屈膝禮,得到她應得的掌聲,臉紅而高興地坐下。

passages.original: Tom Sawyer stepped forward with conceited confidence and soared into the unquenchable and indestructible “Give me liberty or give me death” speech, with fine fury and frantic gesticulation, and broke down in the middle of it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆·索亞帶住自負嘅信心走上前,以精彩嘅憤怒同瘋狂嘅手勢,飛入嗰不可熄滅、不可摧毀嘅「不自由,毋寧死」演講,喺中間崩潰喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆·索亞帶著自負的信心走上前,以精彩的憤怒和瘋狂的手勢,飛入那不可熄滅、不可摧毀的「不自由,毋寧死」演講,在中間崩潰了。

passages.original: A ghastly stage-fright seized him, his legs quaked under him and he was like to choke.
passages.vernacular: 一種可怕嘅怯場抓住咗佢,佢嘅腿喺身下顫抖,佢幾乎要窒息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種可怕的怯場抓住了他,他的腿在身下顫抖,他幾乎要窒息。

passages.original: True, he had the manifest sympathy of the house but he had the house’s silence, too, which was even worse than its sympathy.
passages.vernacular: 誠然,佢有全場明顯嘅同情,但佢都有全場嘅沉默,嗰比佢嘅同情更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠然,他有全場明顯的同情,但他也有全場的沉默,那比它的同情更糟。

passages.original: The master frowned, and this completed the disaster.
passages.vernacular: 老師皺眉,呢完成咗災難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師皺眉,這完成了災難。

passages.original: Tom struggled awhile and then retired, utterly defeated.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆掙扎咗一會兒,然後退下,徹底失敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆掙扎了一會兒,然後退下,徹底失敗。

passages.original: There was a weak attempt at applause, but it died early.
passages.vernacular: 有一次微弱嘅鼓掌嘗試,但好早就死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一次微弱的鼓掌嘗試,但很早就死了。

passages.original: “The Boy Stood on the Burning Deck” followed; also “The Assyrian Came Down,” and other declamatory gems.
passages.vernacular: 隨後係《男孩站喺燃燒嘅甲板上》;仲有《亞述人下嚟咗》,同其他朗誦嘅瑰寶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨後是《男孩站在燃燒的甲板上》;還有《亞述人下來了》,和其他朗誦的瑰寶。

passages.original: Then there were reading exercises, and a spelling fight.
passages.vernacular: 然後有朗讀練習,同一場拼字比賽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後有朗讀練習,和一場拼字比賽。

passages.original: The meagre Latin class recited with honor.
passages.vernacular: 貧乏嘅拉丁班光榮地背誦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貧乏的拉丁班光榮地背誦。

passages.original: The prime feature of the evening was in order, now—original “compositions” by the young ladies.
passages.vernacular: 當晚嘅主要節目而家輪到喇——年輕小姐哋嘅原創「作文」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當晚的主要節目現在輪到了——年輕小姐們的原創「作文」。

passages.original: Each in her turn stepped forward to the edge of the platform, cleared her throat, held up her manuscript (tied with dainty ribbon), and proceeded to read, with labored attention to “expression” and punctuation.
passages.vernacular: 每個人依次走到平台邊緣,清清嗓子,舉起佢嘅手稿(用精緻嘅絲帶捆住),開始朗讀,辛苦地注意「表情」同標點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個人依次走到平台邊緣,清清嗓子,舉起她的手稿(用精緻的絲帶捆著),開始朗讀,辛苦地注意「表情」和標點。

passages.original: The themes were the same that had been illuminated upon similar occasions by their mothers before them, their grandmothers, and doubtless all their ancestors in the female line clear back to the Crusades.
passages.vernacular: 主題同佢哋嘅母親、祖母、無疑仲有佢哋所有女系祖先一路回溯到十字軍東征喺類似場合闡述過嘅相同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主題與她們的母親、祖母、無疑還有她們所有女系祖先一路回溯到十字軍東征在類似場合闡述過的相同。

passages.original: “Friendship” was one; “Memories of Other Days”; “Religion in History”; “Dream Land”; “The Advantages of Culture”; “Forms of Political Government Compared and Contrasted”; “Melancholy”; “Filial Love”; “Heart Longings,” etc., etc.
passages.vernacular: 「友誼」係一個;「往日嘅回憶」;「歷史中嘅宗教」;「夢境」;「文化嘅好處」;「政治政府形式嘅比較同對比」;「憂鬱」;「孝愛」;「心嘅渴望」等等,等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「友誼」是一個;「往日的回憶」;「歷史中的宗教」;「夢境」;「文化的好處」;「政治政府形式的比較與對比」;「憂鬱」;「孝愛」;「心的渴望」等等,等等。

passages.original: A prevalent feature in these compositions was a nursed and petted melancholy; another was a wasteful and opulent gush of “fine language”; another was a tendency to lug in by the ears particularly prized words and phrases until they were worn entirely out; and a peculiarity that conspicuously marked and marred them was the inveterate and intolerable sermon that wagged its crippled tail at the end of each and every one of them.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲作文嘅一個普遍特點係被培養同寵愛嘅憂鬱;另一個係揮霍而豐盈嘅「優美語言」嘅湧流;另一個係傾向於硬把特別珍愛嘅詞同短語拽進去,直到被磨損殆盡;一個明顯標記並損害佢哋嘅特點係,每一篇結尾都有一條根深蒂固、難以忍受嘅講教,搖住佢殘廢嘅尾巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些作文的一個普遍特點是被培養和寵愛的憂鬱;另一個是揮霍而豐盈的「優美語言」的湧流;另一個是傾向於硬把特別珍愛的詞和短語拽進去,直到被磨損殆盡;一個明顯標記並損害它們的特點是,每一篇結尾都有一條根深蒂固、難以忍受的說教,搖著它殘廢的尾巴。

passages.original: No matter what the subject might be, a brainracking effort was made to squirm it into some aspect or other that the moral and religious mind could contemplate with edification.
passages.vernacular: 無論主題係乜嘢,都要絞盡腦汁地把佢扭曲成道德同宗教頭腦可以教益地思考嘅某個方面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論主題是什麼,都要絞盡腦汁地把它扭曲成道德與宗教頭腦可以教益地思考的某個方面。

passages.original: The glaring insincerity of these sermons was not sufficient to compass the banishment of the fashion from the schools, and it is not sufficient today; it never will be sufficient while the world stands, perhaps.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲講教嘅明顯不真誠不足以讓呢種風尚從學校中消失,今日都不足以;只要世界存在,或者永遠不足以。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些說教的明顯不真誠不足以讓這種風尚從學校中消失,今天也不足以;只要世界存在,也許永遠不足以。

passages.original: There is no school in all our land where the young ladies do not feel obliged to close their compositions with a sermon; and you will find that the sermon of the most frivolous and the least religious girl in the school is always the longest and the most relentlessly pious.
passages.vernacular: 我國冇一所學校,年輕小姐哋不覺得有義務以講教結束作文;你會發現,學校裡最輕浮、最不虔誠嘅女孩嘅講教,總是最長最無情地虔誠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我國沒有一所學校,年輕小姐們不覺得有義務以說教結束作文;你會發現,學校裡最輕浮、最不虔誠的女孩的說教,總是最長最無情地虔誠。

passages.original: But enough of this.
passages.vernacular: 但夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但夠了。

passages.original: Homely truth is unpalatable.
passages.vernacular: 質樸嘅真理係不討人鍾意嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 質樸的真理是不討人喜歡的。

passages.original: Let us return to the “Examination.”
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋回到「考試」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們回到「考試」。

passages.original: The first composition that was read was one entitled “Is this, then, Life?”
passages.vernacular: 讀嘅第一篇作文,題為《呢,就係生命嗎?》
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讀的第一篇作文,題為《這,就是生命嗎?》

passages.original: Perhaps the reader can endure an extract from it:
passages.vernacular: 或者讀者能忍受從中摘錄一段:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許讀者能忍受從中摘錄一段:

passages.original: “In the common walks of life, with what delightful emotions does the youthful mind look forward to some anticipated scene of festivity!
passages.vernacular: 「喺平凡嘅生活中,青春嘅頭腦以幾咁愉快嘅情感期待住某個預期嘅慶典場面!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在平凡的生活中,青春的頭腦以多麼愉快的情感期待著某個預期的慶典場面!

passages.original: Imagination is busy sketching rose-tinted pictures of joy.
passages.vernacular: 想像力忙住勾畫玫瑰色嘅歡樂圖畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想像力忙著勾畫玫瑰色的歡樂圖畫。

passages.original: In fancy, the voluptuous votary of fashion sees herself amid the festive throng, ‘the observed of all observers.’
passages.vernacular: 喺幻想中,時尚嘅肉慾信徒睇見自己喺歡慶嘅人群之中,『眾目所矚』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在幻想中,時尚的肉慾信徒看見自己在歡慶的人群之中,『眾目所矚』。

passages.original: Her graceful form, arrayed in snowy robes, is whirling through the mazes of the joyous dance; her eye is brightest, her step is lightest in the gay assembly.
passages.vernacular: 佢優雅嘅身姿,身住雪白嘅長袍,喺歡樂舞蹈嘅迷宮裡旋轉;喺歡快嘅聚會中,佢嘅眼睛最亮,佢嘅腳步最輕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她優雅的身姿,身著雪白的長袍,在歡樂舞蹈的迷宮裡旋轉;在歡快的聚會中,她的眼睛最亮,她的腳步最輕。

passages.original: “In such delicious fancies time quickly glides by, and the welcome hour arrives for her entrance into the Elysian world, of which she has had such bright dreams.
passages.vernacular: 「喺呢啲甜美嘅幻想中,時間迅速滑過,佢進入佢曾做過咁光明嘅夢嘅極樂世界嘅受歡迎時刻到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在這些甜美的幻想中,時間迅速滑過,她進入她曾做過那麼光明的夢的極樂世界的受歡迎時刻到了。

passages.original: How fairy-like does everything appear to her enchanted vision!
passages.vernacular: 喺佢著迷嘅眼中,一切幾咁像仙境!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她著迷的眼中,一切多麼像仙境!

passages.original: Each new scene is more charming than the last.
passages.vernacular: 每一個新場面都比上一個更迷人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每一個新場面都比上一個更迷人。

passages.original: But after a while she finds that beneath this goodly exterior, all is vanity, the flattery which once charmed her soul, now grates harshly upon her ear; the ballroom has lost its charms; and with wasted health and imbittered heart, she turns away with the conviction that earthly pleasures cannot satisfy the longings of the soul!”
passages.vernacular: 但過咗一會兒,佢發而家呢美好嘅外表之下,一切都係虛空,曾經迷住佢靈魂嘅奉承,而家刺耳地磨擦住佢嘅耳朵;舞廳失去咗魅力;帶住耗損嘅健康同苦澀嘅心,佢轉身離開,確信塵世嘅快樂唔能夠滿足靈魂嘅渴望!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但過了一會兒,她發現在這美好的外表之下,一切都是虛空,曾經迷住她靈魂的奉承,現在刺耳地磨擦著她的耳朵;舞廳失去了魅力;帶著耗損的健康和苦澀的心,她轉身離開,確信塵世的快樂不能滿足靈魂的渴望!」

passages.original: And so forth and so on.
passages.vernacular: 如此等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如此等等。

passages.original: There was a buzz of gratification from time to time during the reading, accompanied by whispered ejaculations of “How sweet!”
passages.vernacular: 朗讀期間不時有滿足嘅嗡嗡聲,伴隨住低聲嘅驚歎:「幾咁甜美!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 朗讀期間不時有滿足的嗡嗡聲,伴隨著低聲的驚歎:「多麼甜美!」

passages.original: “How eloquent!”
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁雄辯!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼雄辯!」

passages.original: “So true!” etc., and after the thing had closed with a peculiarly afflicting sermon the applause was enthusiastic.
passages.vernacular: 「太真實喇!」等等,作文以一篇特別令人悲痛嘅講教結束後,掌聲熱烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太真實了!」等等,作文以一篇特別令人悲痛的說教結束後,掌聲熱烈。

passages.original: Then arose a slim, melancholy girl, whose face had the “interesting” paleness that comes of pills and indigestion, and read a “poem.”
passages.vernacular: 然後站起一位瘦削憂鬱嘅女孩,臉上有因藥丸同消化不良而嚟嘅「有趣嘅」蒼白,朗讀咗一首「詩」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後站起一位瘦削憂鬱的女孩,臉上有因藥丸和消化不良而來的「有趣的」蒼白,朗讀了一首「詩」。

passages.original: Two stanzas of it will do:
passages.vernacular: 其中兩節就夠喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中兩節就夠了:

passages.original: “A MISSOURI MAIDEN’S FAREWELL TO ALABAMA
passages.vernacular: 「密蘇里少女告別阿拉巴馬」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「密蘇里少女告別阿拉巴馬」

passages.original: “Alabama, goodbye!
passages.vernacular: 「阿拉巴馬,再見!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「阿拉巴馬,再見!

passages.original: I love thee well!
passages.vernacular: 我深愛你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我深愛你!

passages.original: But yet for a while do I leave thee now!
passages.vernacular: 但我而家暫時離開你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我現在暫時離開你!

passages.original: Sad, yes, sad thoughts of thee my heart doth swell, And burning recollections throng my brow!
passages.vernacular: 悲傷,係嘅,悲傷關於你嘅思緒脹滿我嘅心,灼熱嘅回憶擁擠喺我嘅額頭!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 悲傷,是的,悲傷關於你的思緒脹滿我的心,灼熱的回憶擁擠在我的額頭!

passages.original: For I have wandered through thy flowery woods; Have roamed and read near Tallapoosa’s stream; Have listened to Tallassee’s warring floods, And wooed on Coosa’s side Aurora’s beam.
passages.vernacular: 因為我曾漫遊你開滿花嘅樹林;曾喺塔拉普薩河邊漫步閱讀;曾聽塔拉西嘅好戰洪流,曾喺庫薩河邊追求曙光女神嘅光芒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我曾漫遊你開滿花的樹林;曾在塔拉普薩河邊漫步閱讀;曾聽塔拉西的好戰洪流,曾在庫薩河邊追求曙光女神的光芒。

passages.original: “Yet shame I not to bear an o’erfull heart, Nor blush to turn behind my tearful eyes; ’Tis from no stranger land I now must part, ’Tis to no strangers left I yield these sighs.
passages.vernacular: 「然而我不羞於承受滿溢嘅心,都不臉紅地轉過我含淚嘅眼睛;我而家要離開嘅唔係異鄉,我歎息嘅對象並非陌生人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然而我不羞於承受滿溢的心,也不臉紅地轉過我含淚的眼睛;我現在要離開的不是異鄉,我歎息的對象並非陌生人。

passages.original: Welcome and home were mine within this State, Whose vales I leave—whose spires fade fast from me And cold must be mine eyes, and heart, and tête, When, dear Alabama! they turn cold on thee!”
passages.vernacular: 歡迎同家都係我喺呢州內嘅,我離開佢嘅山谷——佢嘅尖塔迅速從我眼前淡去,當我嘅眼睛、心同頭,親愛嘅阿拉巴馬!對你變冷時,必定係冷嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎和家都是我在這州內的,我離開它的山谷——它的尖塔迅速從我眼前淡去,當我的眼睛、心和頭,親愛的阿拉巴馬!對你變冷時,必定是冷的!」

passages.original: There were very few there who knew what “tête” meant, but the poem was very satisfactory, nevertheless.
passages.vernacular: 在場懂「tête(法語:頭)」係乜嘢意思嘅人好少,但無論如何呢首詩好令人滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在場懂「tête(法語:頭)」是什麼意思的人很少,但無論如何這首詩非常令人滿意。

passages.original: Next appeared a dark-complexioned, black-eyed, black-haired young lady, who paused an impressive moment, assumed a tragic expression, and began to read in a measured, solemn tone:
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟出現一位膚色黝黑、黑眼睛、黑頭髮嘅年輕小姐,佢停頓咗一個令人印象深刻嘅片刻,擺出悲劇嘅表情,開始以有節奏嘅莊嚴語調朗讀:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來出現一位膚色黝黑、黑眼睛、黑頭髮的年輕小姐,她停頓了一個令人印象深刻的片刻,擺出悲劇的表情,開始以有節奏的莊嚴語調朗讀:

passages.original: A VISION
passages.vernacular: 《一個幻象》
passages.vernacularMandarin: 《一個幻象》

passages.original: Dark and tempestuous was night.
passages.vernacular: 黑暗而暴風雨嘅夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑暗而暴風雨的夜晚。

passages.original: Around the throne on high not a single star quivered; but the deep intonations of the heavy thunder constantly vibrated upon the ear; whilst the terrific lightning revelled in angry mood through the cloudy chambers of heaven, seeming to scorn the power exerted over its terror by the illustrious Franklin!
passages.vernacular: 喺高處嘅寶座周圍,冇一顆星星顫動;但沉重雷聲深沉嘅語調不斷喺耳中震盪;而可怕嘅閃電以憤怒嘅心情喺天空雲霧嘅房間裡狂歡,似乎蔑視住著名嘅富蘭克林對其恐怖所施嘅力量!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在高處的寶座周圍,沒有一顆星星顫動;但沉重雷聲深沉的語調不斷在耳中震盪;而可怕的閃電以憤怒的心情在天空雲霧的房間裡狂歡,似乎蔑視著著名的富蘭克林對其恐怖所施的力量!

passages.original: Even the boisterous winds unanimously came forth from their mystic homes, and blustered about as if to enhance by their aid the wildness of the scene.
passages.vernacular: 連狂暴嘅風都一致地從佢哋神祕嘅家出嚟,大聲吼叫,好像要借其幫助增加場景嘅狂野。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連狂暴的風也一致地從它們神祕的家出來,大聲吼叫,好像要借其幫助增加場景的狂野。

passages.original: At such a time, so dark, so dreary, for human sympathy my very spirit sighed; but instead thereof,
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣一個時刻,咁黑暗,咁淒涼,我嘅靈魂渴望人類嘅同情;但嚟到我身邊嘅卻係,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣一個時刻,這麼黑暗,這麼淒涼,我的靈魂渴望人類的同情;但來到我身邊的卻是,

passages.original: ‘My dearest friend, my counsellor, my comforter and guide— My joy in grief, my second bliss in joy,’ came to my side.
passages.vernacular: 『我最親愛嘅朋友,我嘅顧問,我嘅安慰者同嚮導——我悲哀中嘅快樂,我快樂中嘅第二種幸福』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『我最親愛的朋友,我的顧問,我的安慰者和嚮導——我悲哀中的快樂,我快樂中的第二種幸福』。

passages.original: She moved like one of those bright beings pictured in the sunny walks of fancy’s Eden by the romantic and young, a queen of beauty unadorned save by her own transcendent loveliness.
passages.vernacular: 佢移動像嗰啲由浪漫嘅年輕人喺幻想伊甸園嘅陽光步道上描繪嘅光明生命之一,一個美麗嘅女王,除咗佢自己超凡嘅可愛外冇任何裝飾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她移動像那些由浪漫的年輕人在幻想伊甸園的陽光步道上描繪的光明生命之一,一個美麗的女王,除了她自己超凡的可愛外沒有任何裝飾。

passages.original: So soft was her step, it failed to make even a sound, and but for the magical thrill imparted by her genial touch, as other unobtrusive beauties, she would have glided away unperceived—unsought.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅腳步係咁輕柔,連啲聲音都冇發出,若唔係佢友善嘅觸碰傳嚟嘅神奇震顫,像其他不顯眼嘅美人一樣,佢會不被察覺地、不被尋找地滑走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的腳步是那麼輕柔,連一點聲音都沒有發出,若不是她友善的觸碰傳來的神奇震顫,像其他不顯眼的美人一樣,她會不被察覺地、不被尋找地滑走。

passages.original: A strange sadness rested upon her features, like icy tears upon the robe of December, as she pointed to the contending elements without, and bade me contemplate the two beings presented.
passages.vernacular: 一種奇異嘅悲傷落喺佢嘅容顏上,像十二月長袍上嘅冰淚,佢指住外面競爭嘅元素,叫我思考呈現出嘅兩個存在。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種奇異的悲傷落在她的容顏上,像十二月長袍上的冰淚,她指著外面競爭的元素,叫我思考呈現出的兩個存在。

passages.original: This nightmare occupied some ten pages of manuscript and wound up with a sermon so destructive of all hope to non-Presbyterians that it took the first prize.
passages.vernacular: 呢場噩夢佔據咗大約十頁手稿,結束以一篇如此摧毀所有非長老會教徒希望嘅講教,所以得咗頭獎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這場噩夢佔據了大約十頁手稿,結束以一篇如此摧毀所有非長老會教徒希望的說教,所以得了頭獎。

passages.original: This composition was considered to be the very finest effort of the evening.
passages.vernacular: 呢篇作文被認為係當晚最出色嘅努力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這篇作文被認為是當晚最出色的努力。

passages.original: The mayor of the village, in delivering the prize to the author of it, made a warm speech in which he said that it was by far the most “eloquent” thing he had ever listened to, and that Daniel Webster himself might well be proud of it.
passages.vernacular: 村長向作者頒獎時,做咗熱情嘅演講,講呢個係迄今佢聽過嘅最「雄辯」嘅嘢,連丹尼爾·韋伯斯特本人都應為之驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 村長向作者頒獎時,做了熱情的演講,說這是迄今他聽過的最「雄辯」的東西,連丹尼爾·韋伯斯特本人也應為之驕傲。

passages.original: It may be remarked, in passing, that the number of compositions in which the word “beauteous” was over-fondled, and human experience referred to as “life’s page,” was up to the usual average.
passages.vernacular: 順便講一下,「美麗嘅」呢個詞被過度寵愛、人類經驗被稱為「生命之頁」嘅作文數量,達到咗通常嘅平均水平。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 順便說一下,「美麗的」這個詞被過度寵愛、人類經驗被稱為「生命之頁」的作文數量,達到了通常的平均水平。

passages.original: Now the master, mellow almost to the verge of geniality, put his chair aside, turned his back to the audience, and began to draw a map of America on the blackboard, to exercise the geography class upon.
passages.vernacular: 而家老師,醺然到幾乎親切嘅邊緣,把椅子推到一邊,背對聽眾,開始喺黑板上畫美洲地圖,讓地理班練習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在老師,醺然到幾乎親切的邊緣,把椅子推到一邊,背對聽眾,開始在黑板上畫美洲地圖,讓地理班練習。

passages.original: But he made a sad business of it with his unsteady hand, and a smothered titter rippled over the house.
passages.vernacular: 但佢用不穩嘅手把事情搞得好糟,一陣被悶住嘅竊笑喺全場蕩漾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他用不穩的手把事情搞得很糟,一陣被悶住的竊笑在全場蕩漾。

passages.original: He knew what the matter was, and set himself to right it.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道係點回事,著手糾正佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他知道是怎麼回事,著手糾正它。

passages.original: He sponged out lines and remade them; but he only distorted them more than ever, and the tittering was more pronounced.
passages.vernacular: 佢用海綿擦掉線條,重畫;但佢只係比以前更扭曲咗佢哋,竊笑更明顯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他用海綿擦掉線條,重畫;但他只是比以前更扭曲了它們,竊笑更明顯了。

passages.original: He threw his entire attention upon his work, now, as if determined not to be put down by the mirth.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家把全部注意力投入佢嘅工作,好像決心不被歡笑壓倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在把全部注意力投入他的工作,好像決心不被歡笑壓倒。

passages.original: He felt that all eyes were fastened upon him; he imagined he was succeeding, and yet the tittering continued; it even manifestly increased.
passages.vernacular: 佢覺得所有眼睛都盯住佢;佢想像自己喺成功,但竊笑仍然繼續;甚至明顯增加。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他覺得所有眼睛都盯著他;他想像自己在成功,但竊笑仍然繼續;甚至明顯增加。

passages.original: And well it might.
passages.vernacular: 都理應如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也理應如此。

passages.original: There was a garret above, pierced with a scuttle over his head; and down through this scuttle came a cat, suspended around the haunches by a string; she had a rag tied about her head and jaws to keep her from mewing; as she slowly descended she curved upward and clawed at the string, she swung downward and clawed at the intangible air.
passages.vernacular: 上面有一個閣樓,喺佢頭上有個天窗;一隻貓從呢個天窗垂下嚟,腰部被一根繩子吊住;佢頭同下巴上綁住一塊破布,防止佢喵叫;佢慢慢下降時,向上彎起,抓繩子,向下擺動,抓無形嘅空氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面有一個閣樓,在他頭上有個天窗;一隻貓從這個天窗垂下來,腰部被一根繩子吊著;她頭和下巴上綁著一塊破布,防止她喵叫;她慢慢下降時,向上彎起,抓繩子,向下擺動,抓無形的空氣。

passages.original: The tittering rose higher and higher—the cat was within six inches of the absorbed teacher’s head—down, down, a little lower, and she grabbed his wig with her desperate claws, clung to it, and was snatched up into the garret in an instant with her trophy still in her possession!
passages.vernacular: 竊笑聲越嚟越高——貓離專心嘅老師嘅頭只有六英寸——下去,下去,再低啲,佢用絕望嘅爪子抓住佢嘅假髮,緊抓不放,瞬間被拉回閣樓,戰利品仍喺佢手裡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 竊笑聲越來越高——貓離專心的老師的頭只有六英寸——下去,下去,再低一點,她用絕望的爪子抓住他的假髮,緊抓不放,瞬間被拉回閣樓,戰利品仍在她手裡!

passages.original: And how the light did blaze abroad from the master’s bald pate—for the signpainter’s boy had gilded it!
passages.vernacular: 老師嘅禿頭上光芒四射——因為招牌畫匠嘅兒子畀佢鍍咗金!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老師的禿頭上光芒四射——因為招牌畫匠的兒子給它鍍了金!

passages.original: That broke up the meeting.
passages.vernacular: 呢結束咗會議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這結束了會議。

passages.original: The boys were avenged.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋報咗仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們報了仇。

passages.original: Vacation had come.
passages.vernacular: 假期到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假期到了。

passages.original: [*] NOTE:—The pretended “compositions” quoted in this chapter are taken without alteration from a volume entitled “Prose and Poetry, by a Western Lady”—but they are exactly and precisely after the schoolgirl pattern, and hence are much happier than any mere imitations could be.
passages.vernacular: [*]注:本章所引嘅偽「作文」,未加修改地取自一本題為《西部女士嘅散文同詩》嘅書——但佢哋完全精確地符合女學生嘅模式,因此比任何單純嘅模仿都更精彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [*]注:本章所引的偽「作文」,未加修改地取自一本題為《西部女士的散文與詩》的書——但它們完全精確地符合女學生的模式,因此比任何單純的模仿都更精彩。

chapters.title: Chapter XXII: Tom's Confidence Betrayed 第二十二章:湯姆的信任被出賣

passages.original: CH Tom joined the new order of Cadets of Temperance, being attracted by the showy character of their “regalia.”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆加入咗新成立嘅節制少年團,被佢哋「制服」嘅華麗吸引。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆加入了新成立的節制少年團,被他們「制服」的華麗吸引。

passages.original: He promised to abstain from smoking, chewing, and profanity as long as he remained a member.
passages.vernacular: 佢答應只要定係會員,就戒除吸菸、嚼菸同講髒話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他答應只要還是會員,就戒除吸菸、嚼菸和說髒話。

passages.original: Now he found out a new thing—namely, that to promise not to do a thing is the surest way in the world to make a body want to go and do that very thing.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢發現咗一件新事——就係,答應不做一件事,係世界上最確定能讓人想去做嗰件事嘅辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他發現了一件新事——就是,答應不做一件事,是世界上最確定能讓人想去做那件事的辦法。

passages.original: Tom soon found himself tormented with a desire to drink and swear; the desire grew to be so intense that nothing but the hope of a chance to display himself in his red sash kept him from withdrawing from the order.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆好快發現自己被想飲酒同罵人嘅慾望折磨;呢慾望變得咁強烈,除咗有機會戴住紅腰帶炫耀嘅希望,冇別嘅嘢讓佢冇退出呢個團體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆很快發現自己被想喝酒和罵人的慾望折磨;這慾望變得那麼強烈,除了有機會戴著紅腰帶炫耀的希望,沒有別的東西讓他沒有退出這個團體。

passages.original: Fourth of July was coming; but he soon gave that up—gave it up before he had worn his shackles over forty-eight hours—and fixed his hopes upon old Judge Frazer, justice of the peace, who was apparently on his deathbed and would have a big public funeral, since he was so high an official.
passages.vernacular: 七月四日快到喇;但佢好快放棄喇——喺戴上枷鎖唔到四十八小時就放棄喇——把希望寄託喺老弗雷澤法官身上,佢係治安法官,顯然奄奄一息,既然係咁高級嘅官員,會有盛大嘅公共葬禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 七月四日快到了;但他很快放棄了——在戴上枷鎖不到四十八小時就放棄了——把希望寄託在老弗雷澤法官身上,他是治安法官,顯然奄奄一息,既然是那麼高級的官員,會有盛大的公共葬禮。

passages.original: During three days Tom was deeply concerned about the Judge’s condition and hungry for news of it.
passages.vernacular: 三天內湯姆深深關心法官嘅情況,渴望佢嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三天內湯姆深深關心法官的情況,渴望他的消息。

passages.original: Sometimes his hopes ran high—so high that he would venture to get out his regalia and practise before the looking-glass.
passages.vernacular: 有時佢嘅希望好高——高到佢敢攞出佢嘅制服,喺鏡子前練習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時他的希望很高——高到他敢拿出他的制服,在鏡子前練習。

passages.original: But the Judge had a most discouraging way of fluctuating.
passages.vernacular: 但法官有一種最令人氣餒嘅波動方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但法官有一種最令人氣餒的波動方式。

passages.original: At last he was pronounced upon the mend—and then convalescent.
passages.vernacular: 最後佢被宣布喺好轉——然後係康復中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他被宣布在好轉——然後是康復中。

passages.original: Tom was disgusted; and felt a sense of injury, too.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆感到噁心,都有一種受傷害嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆感到噁心,也有一種受傷害的感覺。

passages.original: He handed in his resignation at once—and that night the Judge suffered a relapse and died.
passages.vernacular: 佢立即遞交咗辭呈——嗰晚法官病情復發,死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他立即遞交了辭呈——那晚法官病情復發,死了。

passages.original: Tom resolved that he would never trust a man like that again.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆決心再都不信任咁樣嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆決心再也不信任這樣的人。

passages.original: The funeral was a fine thing.
passages.vernacular: 葬禮好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葬禮很好。

passages.original: The Cadets paraded in a style calculated to kill the late member with envy.
passages.vernacular: 少年團以足以嫉妒死去會員嘅風格遊行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 少年團以足以嫉妒死去會員的風格遊行。

passages.original: Tom was a free boy again, however—there was something in that.
passages.vernacular: 不過湯姆又自由喇——呢都算點乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過湯姆又自由了——這也算點什麼。

passages.original: He could drink and swear, now—but found to his surprise that he did not want to.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家可以飲酒、罵人喇——卻驚訝地發現佢唔想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在可以喝酒、罵人了——卻驚訝地發現他不想。

passages.original: The simple fact that he could, took the desire away, and the charm of it.
passages.vernacular: 佢能呢個簡單嘅事實,攞走咗慾望同佢嘅魅力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他能這個簡單的事實,拿走了慾望和它的魅力。

passages.original: Tom presently wondered to find that his coveted vacation was beginning to hang a little heavily on his hands.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆不久驚奇地發現,佢渴望嘅假期開始喺佢手上有點沉重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆不久驚奇地發現,他渴望的假期開始在他手上有點沉重。

passages.original: He attempted a diary—but nothing happened during three days, and so he abandoned it.
passages.vernacular: 佢試住寫日記——但三天內乜嘢都冇發生,於是佢放棄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他試著寫日記——但三天內什麼也沒發生,於是他放棄了。

passages.original: The first of all the negro minstrel shows came to town, and made a sensation.
passages.vernacular: 所有黑人滑稽秀中嘅第一個嚟到鎮上,引起轟動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有黑人滑稽秀中的第一個來到鎮上,引起轟動。

passages.original: Tom and Joe Harper got up a band of performers and were happy for two days.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆同喬·哈珀組織咗一個表演團,快樂咗兩天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆和喬·哈珀組織了一個表演團,快樂了兩天。

passages.original: Even the Glorious Fourth was in some sense a failure, for it rained hard, there was no procession in consequence, and the greatest man in the world (as Tom supposed), Mr. Benton, an actual United States Senator, proved an overwhelming disappointment—for he was not twenty-five feet high, nor even anywhere in the neighborhood of it.
passages.vernacular: 連光榮嘅七月四日喺某種意義上都係失敗,因為下大雨,結果冇遊行,而世界上最偉大嘅人(如湯姆所想),真正嘅美國參議員本頓先生,結果令人極度失望——因為佢唔係二十五呎高,甚至喺附近都唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連光榮的七月四日在某種意義上也是失敗,因為下大雨,結果沒有遊行,而世界上最偉大的人(如湯姆所想),真正的美國參議員本頓先生,結果令人極度失望——因為他不是二十五呎高,甚至在附近也不是。

passages.original: A circus came.
passages.vernacular: 馬戲團嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬戲團來了。

passages.original: The boys played circus for three days afterward in tents made of rag carpeting—admission, three pins for boys, two for girls—and then circusing was abandoned.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋此後三天用破地毯做嘅帳篷玩馬戲——入場費,男孩三根針,女孩兩根——然後放棄咗玩馬戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們此後三天用破地毯做的帳篷玩馬戲——入場費,男孩三根針,女孩兩根——然後放棄了玩馬戲。

passages.original: A phrenologist and a mesmerizer came—and went again and left the village duller and drearier than ever.
passages.vernacular: 一位骨相學家同一位催眠師嚟喇——又走喇,留下村子比以往更沉悶淒涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位骨相學家和一位催眠師來了——又走了,留下村子比以往更沉悶淒涼。

passages.original: There were some boys-and-girls’ parties, but they were so few and so delightful that they only made the aching voids between ache the harder.
passages.vernacular: 有啲男孩女孩嘅聚會,但佢哋咁少又咁愉快,只係使其間疼痛嘅空虛更痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一些男孩女孩的聚會,但它們那麼少又那麼愉快,只是使其間疼痛的空虛更痛。

passages.original: Becky Thatcher was gone to her Constantinople home to stay with her parents during vacation—so there was no bright side to life anywhere.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪·撒切爾回佢君士坦丁堡嘅家同父母度假去喇——所以生活喺任何地方都冇光明嘅一面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪·撒切爾回她君士坦丁堡的家同父母度假去了——所以生活在任何地方都沒有光明的一面。

passages.original: The dreadful secret of the murder was a chronic misery.
passages.vernacular: 謀殺案嘅可怕祕密係慢性嘅痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謀殺案的可怕祕密是慢性的痛苦。

passages.original: It was a very cancer for permanency and pain.
passages.vernacular: 喺持久同痛苦方面佢簡直係一個癌症。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在持久和痛苦方面它簡直是一個癌症。

passages.original: Then came the measles.
passages.vernacular: 然後麻疹嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後麻疹來了。

passages.original: During two long weeks Tom lay a prisoner, dead to the world and its happenings.
passages.vernacular: 整整兩個漫長嘅星期湯姆躺住做囚犯,對世界同佢嘅事情都死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整整兩個漫長的星期湯姆躺著做囚犯,對世界和它的事情都死了。

passages.original: He was very ill, he was interested in nothing.
passages.vernacular: 佢病得好重,對乜嘢都不感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他病得很重,對什麼都不感興趣。

passages.original: When he got upon his feet at last and moved feebly downtown, a melancholy change had come over everything and every creature.
passages.vernacular: 佢終於站起嚟,虛弱地走到鎮上時,憂鬱嘅變化已經降臨喺一切事物同每個生物身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他終於站起來,虛弱地走到鎮上時,憂鬱的變化已經降臨在一切事物和每個生物身上。

passages.original: There had been a “revival,” and everybody had “got religion,” not only the adults, but even the boys and girls.
passages.vernacular: 有過一次「復興」,每個人都「得到咗宗教」,不僅係成年人,甚至男孩女孩都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有過一次「復興」,每個人都「得到了宗教」,不僅是成年人,甚至男孩女孩也是。

passages.original: Tom went about, hoping against hope for the sight of one blessed sinful face, but disappointment crossed him everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆四處走,絕望中抱住希望睇到一張有福嘅有罪嘅臉,但失望到處阻攔佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆四處走,絕望中抱著希望看到一張有福的有罪的臉,但失望到處阻攔他。

passages.original: He found Joe Harper studying a Testament, and turned sadly away from the depressing spectacle.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現喬·哈珀喺學習新約,悲傷地從呢令人沮喪嘅景象轉開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他發現喬·哈珀在學習新約,悲傷地從這令人沮喪的景象轉開。

passages.original: He sought Ben Rogers, and found him visiting the poor with a basket of tracts.
passages.vernacular: 佢找本·羅傑斯,發現佢提住一籃子宣傳小冊子去探訪窮人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他找本·羅傑斯,發現他提著一籃子宣傳小冊子去探訪窮人。

passages.original: He hunted up Jim Hollis, who called his attention to the precious blessing of his late measles as a warning.
passages.vernacular: 佢找到吉姆·霍利斯,吉姆讓佢注意佢最近麻疹嘅珍貴祝福,作為警告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他找到吉姆·霍利斯,吉姆讓他注意他最近麻疹的珍貴祝福,作為警告。

passages.original: Every boy he encountered added another ton to his depression; and when, in desperation, he flew for refuge at last to the bosom of Huckleberry Finn and was received with a Scriptural quotation, his heart broke and he crept home and to bed realizing that he alone of all the town was lost, forever and forever.
passages.vernacular: 佢遇到嘅每個男孩都畀佢嘅沮喪增加一噸;當佢絕望中最後飛到哈克貝利·費恩懷裡尋求庇護,卻被用一句聖經引文接待時,佢嘅心碎喇,爬回家上床,意識到全鎮只有佢一個人失落喇,永遠永遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他遇到的每個男孩都給他的沮喪增加一噸;當他絕望中最後飛到哈克貝利·費恩懷裡尋求庇護,卻被用一句聖經引文接待時,他的心碎了,爬回家上床,意識到全鎮只有他一個人失落了,永遠永遠。

passages.original: And that night there came on a terrific storm, with driving rain, awful claps of thunder and blinding sheets of lightning.
passages.vernacular: 嗰晚嚟咗一場可怕嘅暴風雨,大雨傾盆,可怕嘅雷鳴同令人眼盲嘅片狀閃電。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那晚來了一場可怕的暴風雨,大雨傾盆,可怕的雷鳴和令人眼盲的片狀閃電。

passages.original: He covered his head with the bedclothes and waited in a horror of suspense for his doom; for he had not the shadow of a doubt that all this hubbub was about him.
passages.vernacular: 佢用被子蒙住頭,恐懼而懸念地等待佢嘅厄運;因為佢毫不懷疑所有呢啲喧鬧都係為佢而嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他用被子蒙住頭,恐懼而懸念地等待他的厄運;因為他毫不懷疑所有這些喧鬧都是為他而來的。

passages.original: He believed he had taxed the forbearance of the powers above to the extremity of endurance and that this was the result.
passages.vernacular: 佢相信佢已經把上面權柄嘅忍耐耗到咗忍耐嘅極限,呢個就係結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他相信他已經把上面權柄的忍耐耗到了忍耐的極限,這就是結果。

passages.original: It might have seemed to him a waste of pomp and ammunition to kill a bug with a battery of artillery, but there seemed nothing incongruous about the getting up such an expensive thunderstorm as this to knock the turf from under an insect like himself.
passages.vernacular: 對佢來講,用一個炮兵連擊斃一隻蟲子,或者係浪費排場同彈藥,但係要製造咁樣昂貴嘅雷暴把像佢咁樣嘅昆蟲腳下嘅草皮打掉,似乎冇乜嘢不協調。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對他來說,用一個炮兵連擊斃一隻蟲子,也許是浪費排場和彈藥,但是要製造這樣昂貴的雷暴把像他這樣的昆蟲腳下的草皮打掉,似乎沒有什麼不協調。

passages.original: By and by the tempest spent itself and died without accomplishing its object.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地暴風雨自己耗盡,冇完成目標就死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地暴風雨自己耗盡,沒有完成目標就死了。

passages.original: The boy’s first impulse was to be grateful, and reform.
passages.vernacular: 男孩嘅第一個衝動係感激並改過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩的第一個衝動是感激並改過。

passages.original: His second was to wait—for there might not be any more storms.
passages.vernacular: 第二個係等待——因為或者唔會再有暴風雨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二個是等待——因為也許不會再有暴風雨。

passages.original: The next day the doctors were back; Tom had relapsed.
passages.vernacular: 第二天醫生哋又回嚟喇;湯姆復發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天醫生們又回來了;湯姆復發了。

passages.original: The three weeks he spent on his back this time seemed an entire age.
passages.vernacular: 呢次佢躺喺床上度過嘅三個星期似乎係整個時代。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次他躺在床上度過的三個星期似乎是整個時代。

passages.original: When he got abroad at last he was hardly grateful that he had been spared, remembering how lonely was his estate, how companionless and forlorn he was.
passages.vernacular: 佢終於出去時,幾乎不感激自己被饒過,記起佢嘅處境幾咁孤獨,佢幾咁冇伴侶、幾咁淒涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他終於出去時,幾乎不感激自己被饒過,記起他的處境多麼孤獨,他多麼沒有伴侶、多麼淒涼。

passages.original: He drifted listlessly down the street and found Jim Hollis acting as judge in a juvenile court that was trying a cat for murder, in the presence of her victim, a bird.
passages.vernacular: 佢無精打采地沿街漂流,發現吉姆·霍利斯正擔任少年法庭嘅法官,審判一隻貓謀殺,當住佢嘅受害者一隻鳥嘅面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他無精打采地沿街漂流,發現吉姆·霍利斯正擔任少年法庭的法官,審判一隻貓謀殺,當著它的受害者一隻鳥的面。

passages.original: He found Joe Harper and Huck Finn up an alley eating a stolen melon.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺一條小巷裡發現喬·哈珀同哈克·費恩喺食偷嚟嘅瓜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在一條小巷裡發現喬·哈珀和哈克·費恩在吃偷來的瓜。

passages.original: Poor lads! they—like Tom—had suffered a relapse.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅小伙子!佢哋像湯姆一樣,都復發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的小伙子!他們像湯姆一樣,也復發了。

chapters.title: Chapter XXIII: Old Muff's Friends 第二十三章:馬夫的朋友

passages.original: CH At last the sleepy atmosphere was stirred—and vigorously: the murder trial came on in the court.
passages.vernacular: 終於昏昏欲瞓嘅氣氛被攪動喇——而且好猛烈:謀殺案嘅審判喺法院開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於昏昏欲睡的氣氛被攪動了——而且很猛烈:謀殺案的審判在法院開始了。

passages.original: It became the absorbing topic of village talk immediately.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻成咗村裡談話嘅吸引人嘅話題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它立刻成了村裡談話的吸引人的話題。

passages.original: Tom could not get away from it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆擺脫不咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆擺脫不了它。

passages.original: Every reference to the murder sent a shudder to his heart, for his troubled conscience and fears almost persuaded him that these remarks were put forth in his hearing as “feelers”; he did not see how he could be suspected of knowing anything about the murder, but still he could not be comfortable in the midst of this gossip.
passages.vernacular: 每次提到謀殺案都使佢嘅心戰慄,因為佢不安嘅良心同恐懼幾乎使佢相信呢啲話係當住佢嘅面「試探」講出嘅;佢睇不出點會有人懷疑佢知道謀殺案嘅任何事,但佢喺呢啲閒話中仍唔能夠感到舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每次提到謀殺案都使他的心戰慄,因為他不安的良心和恐懼幾乎使他相信這些話是當著他的面「試探」說出的;他看不出怎麼會有人懷疑他知道謀殺案的任何事,但他在這些閒話中仍不能感到舒服。

passages.original: It kept him in a cold shiver all the time.
passages.vernacular: 呢使佢一直冷得發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使他一直冷得發抖。

passages.original: He took Huck to a lonely place to have a talk with him.
passages.vernacular: 佢把哈克帶到一個荒涼嘅地方同佢談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他把哈克帶到一個荒涼的地方同他談話。

passages.original: It would be some relief to unseal his tongue for a little while; to divide his burden of distress with another sufferer.
passages.vernacular: 解開舌頭一會兒會係一種解脫;同另一個受難者分擔佢嘅苦惱負擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 解開舌頭一會兒會是一種解脫;同另一個受難者分擔他的苦惱負擔。

passages.original: Moreover, he wanted to assure himself that Huck had remained discreet.
passages.vernacular: 而且,佢想讓自己確定哈克一直保持謹慎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,他想讓自己確定哈克一直保持謹慎。

passages.original: “Huck, have you ever told anybody about—that?”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,你曾對任何人講過——嗰件事嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,你曾對任何人說過——那件事嗎?」

passages.original: “’Bout what?”
passages.vernacular: 「講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說什麼?」

passages.original: “You know what.”
passages.vernacular: 「你知道乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道什麼。」

passages.original: “Oh—’course I haven’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦——當然冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦——當然沒有。」

passages.original: “Never a word?”
passages.vernacular: 「一個字都冇講?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個字都沒說?」

passages.original: “Never a solitary word, so help me.
passages.vernacular: 「一個字都冇,天作證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個字也沒有,天作證。

passages.original: What makes you ask?”
passages.vernacular: 你點解問?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼問?」

passages.original: “Well, I was afeard.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我怕。」

passages.original: “Why, Tom Sawyer, we wouldn’t be alive two days if that got found out.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,湯姆·索亞,如果嗰件事被發現,我哋活不過兩天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,湯姆·索亞,如果那件事被發現,我們活不過兩天。

passages.original: You know that.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道的。」

passages.original: Tom felt more comfortable.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆感到舒服咗些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆感到舒服了些。

passages.original: After a pause:
passages.vernacular: 停頓後:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 停頓後:

passages.original: “Huck, they couldn’t anybody get you to tell, could they?”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,冇人能讓你講出去,對吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,沒有人能讓你說出去,對吧?」

passages.original: “Get me to tell?
passages.vernacular: 「讓我講出去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我說出去?

passages.original: Why, if I wanted that halfbreed devil to drownd me they could get me to tell.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,如果我想讓嗰個混血魔鬼淹死我,佢哋能讓我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,如果我想讓那個混血魔鬼淹死我,他們能讓我說。

passages.original: They ain’t no different way.”
passages.vernacular: 冇別嘅辦法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有別的辦法。」

passages.original: “Well, that’s all right, then.
passages.vernacular: 「咁好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼好了。

passages.original: I reckon we’re safe as long as we keep mum.
passages.vernacular: 我想只要我哋保持沉默,我哋就係安全嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想只要我們保持沉默,我們就是安全的。

passages.original: But let’s swear again, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 不過讓我哋再發誓一次,無論如何。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過讓我們再發誓一次,無論如何。

passages.original: It’s more surer.”
passages.vernacular: 更保險。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 更保險。」

passages.original: “I’m agreed.”
passages.vernacular: 「我同意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我同意。」

passages.original: So they swore again with dread solemnities.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋帶住可怕嘅莊嚴又發咗一次誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們帶著可怕的莊嚴又發了一次誓。

passages.original: “What is the talk around, Huck?
passages.vernacular: 「周圍喺談乜嘢,哈克?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「周圍在談什麼,哈克?

passages.original: I’ve heard a power of it.”
passages.vernacular: 我聽到好多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽到很多。」

passages.original: “Talk?
Well, it’s just Muff Potter, Muff Potter, Muff Potter all the time.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,總是只有馬夫·波特,馬夫·波特,馬夫·波特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,總是只有馬夫·波特,馬夫·波特,馬夫·波特。

passages.original: It keeps me in a sweat, constant, so’s I want to hide som’ers.”
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我不停地出汗,我想躲到某處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它讓我不停地出汗,我想躲到某處。」

passages.original: “That’s just the same way they go on round me.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋喺我周圍都係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們在我周圍也是這樣。

passages.original: I reckon he’s a goner.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他完了。

passages.original: Don’t you feel sorry for him, sometimes?”
passages.vernacular: 你有時不為佢難過嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有時不為他難過嗎?」

passages.original: “Most always—most always.
passages.vernacular: 「幾乎總是——幾乎總是。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「幾乎總是——幾乎總是。

passages.original: He ain’t no account; but then he hain’t ever done anything to hurt anybody.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇乜嘢出息;但佢從冇做過傷害任何人嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒什麼出息;但他從沒做過傷害任何人的事。

passages.original: Just fishes a little, to get money to get drunk on—and loafs around considerable; but lord, we all do that—leastways most of us—preachers and such like.
passages.vernacular: 只係釣點魚,賺錢去飲醉——仲相當遊手好閒;但天呀,我哋都咁樣——至少大多數人——牧師之類嘅人都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是釣點魚,賺錢去喝醉——還相當遊手好閒;但天哪,我們都這樣——至少大多數人——牧師之類的人也是。

passages.original: But he’s kind of good—he give me half a fish, once, when there warn’t enough for two; and lots of times he’s kind of stood by me when I was out of luck.”
passages.vernacular: 但佢有點好——佢有一次分畀我半條魚,當唔夠兩個人食嘅時候;好多次當我倒霉時,佢有點站喺我呢邊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他有點好——他有一次分給我半條魚,當不夠兩個人吃的時候;很多次當我倒霉時,他有點站在我這邊。」

passages.original: “Well, he’s mended kites for me, Huck, and knitted hooks on to my line.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢替我補過風箏,把鉤子結喺我嘅線上,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,他替我補過風箏,把鉤子結在我的線上,哈克。

passages.original: I wish we could get him out of there.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望我哋能把佢從嗰度弄出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我們能把他從那裡弄出來。」

passages.original: “My! we couldn’t get him out, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!我哋唔能夠把佢弄出嚟,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!我們不能把他弄出來,湯姆。

passages.original: And besides, ’twouldn’t do any good; they’d ketch him again.”
passages.vernacular: 而且,都冇好處;佢哋會再抓住佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,也沒好處;他們會再抓住他。」

passages.original: “Yes—so they would.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——佢哋會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——他們會。

passages.original: But I hate to hear ’em abuse him so like the dickens when he never done—that.”
passages.vernacular: 但我討厭聽佢哋咁樣該死地辱罵佢,而佢從冇做——嗰件事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我討厭聽他們這樣該死地辱罵他,而他從沒做——那件事。」

passages.original: “I do too, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「我都係,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是,湯姆。

passages.original: Lord, I hear ’em say he’s the bloodiest looking villain in this country, and they wonder he wasn’t ever hung before.”
passages.vernacular: 天呀,我聽佢哋講佢係呢個國家最血腥相貌嘅惡棍,佢哋納悶佢以前點解冇被絞死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,我聽他們說他是這個國家最血腥相貌的惡棍,他們納悶他以前為什麼沒被絞死。」

passages.original: “Yes, they talk like that, all the time.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢哋一直咁樣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,他們一直這樣說。

passages.original: I’ve heard ’em say that if he was to get free they’d lynch him.”
passages.vernacular: 我聽佢哋講如果佢逃出嚟,佢哋會私刑處死佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽他們說如果他逃出來,他們會私刑處死他。」

passages.original: “And they’d do it, too.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋都會咁樣做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們也會這樣做。」

passages.original: The boys had a long talk, but it brought them little comfort.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋談咗好久,但呢帶畀佢哋嘅安慰好少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們談了很久,但這帶給他們的安慰很少。

passages.original: As the twilight drew on, they found themselves hanging about the neighborhood of the little isolated jail, perhaps with an undefined hope that something would happen that might clear away their difficulties.
passages.vernacular: 暮色降臨時,佢哋發現自己喺嗰間孤立嘅小監獄附近徘徊,或者帶住一種不明確嘅希望,希望發生點乜嘢可能掃除佢哋困難嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暮色降臨時,他們發現自己在那間孤立的小監獄附近徘徊,也許帶著一種不明確的希望,希望發生點什麼可能掃除他們困難的事。

passages.original: But nothing happened; there seemed to be no angels or fairies interested in this luckless captive.
passages.vernacular: 但乜嘢都冇發生;似乎冇天使或仙子對呢個倒霉嘅囚犯感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但什麼也沒發生;似乎沒有天使或仙子對這個倒霉的囚犯感興趣。

passages.original: The boys did as they had often done before—went to the cell grating and gave Potter some tobacco and matches.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋像以前常做嘅嗰樣,走到牢房嘅鐵窗前,畀咗波特啲煙草同火柴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們像以前常做的那樣,走到牢房的鐵窗前,給了波特一些煙草和火柴。

passages.original: He was on the ground floor and there were no guards.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺底層,冇守衛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在底層,沒有守衛。

passages.original: His gratitude for their gifts had always smote their consciences before—it cut deeper than ever, this time.
passages.vernacular: 佢對佢哋禮物嘅感激以前總是刺痛佢哋嘅良心——呢次割得比以往更深。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對他們禮物的感激以前總是刺痛他們的良心——這次割得比以往更深。

passages.original: They felt cowardly and treacherous to the last degree when Potter said:
passages.vernacular: 波特講話時,佢哋覺得自己膽小同背信到咗極點:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特說話時,他們覺得自己膽小和背信到了極點:

passages.original: “You’ve been mighty good to me, boys—better’n anybody else in this town.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋對我好好,細路哋——比呢鎮上任何人都好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們對我非常好,孩子們——比這鎮上任何人都好。

passages.original: And I don’t forget it, I don’t.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會忘記,我唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會忘記,我不會。

passages.original: Often I says to myself, says I, ‘I used to mend all the boys’ kites and things, and show ’em where the good fishin’ places was, and befriend ’em what I could, and now they’ve all forgot old Muff when he’s in trouble; but Tom don’t, and Huck don’t—they don’t forget him,’ says I, ‘and I don’t forget them.’
passages.vernacular: 我常對自己講,我講:『我以前替所有男孩補風箏同嘢,告訴佢哋好釣魚嘅地方,盡我所能同佢哋交朋友,而家佢哋都忘咗老馬夫,當佢有麻煩嘅時候;但湯姆冇,哈克冇——佢哋冇忘記佢,』我講,『我都不忘記佢哋。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我常對自己說,我說:『我以前替所有男孩補風箏和東西,告訴他們好釣魚的地方,盡我所能與他們交朋友,現在他們都忘了老馬夫,當他有麻煩的時候;但湯姆沒有,哈克沒有——他們沒有忘記他,』我說,『我也不忘記他們。』

passages.original: Well, boys, I done an awful thing—drunk and crazy at the time—that’s the only way I account for it—and now I got to swing for it, and it’s right.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,細路哋,我做咗一件可怕嘅事——當時飲醉咗、瘋喇——呢個係我解釋佢嘅唯一方式——而家我得為此被吊死,呢個係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,孩子們,我做了一件可怕的事——當時喝醉了、瘋了——這是我解釋它的唯一方式——現在我得為此被吊死,這是對的。

passages.original: Right, and best, too, I reckon—hope so, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 對嘅,都最好,我想——至少希望如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對的,也最好,我想——至少希望如此。

passages.original: Well, we won’t talk about that.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,我哋不談呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,我們不談這個。

passages.original: I don’t want to make you feel bad; you’ve befriended me.
passages.vernacular: 我唔想讓你哋難受;你哋對我友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想讓你們難受;你們對我友好。

passages.original: But what I want to say, is, don’t you ever get drunk—then you won’t ever get here.
passages.vernacular: 但我想講嘅係,你哋千萬別飲醉——嗰樣你哋就永遠唔會嚟呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我想說的是,你們千萬別喝醉——那樣你們就永遠不會來這裡。

passages.original: Stand a litter furder west—so—that’s it; it’s a prime comfort to see faces that’s friendly when a body’s in such a muck of trouble, and there don’t none come here but yourn.
passages.vernacular: 再往西站啲——就係咁樣;一個人處於咁樣一團麻煩中時,睇到友好嘅臉係主要嘅安慰,除咗你哋嘅,冇別人嚟呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再往西站一點——就是這樣;一個人處於這樣一團麻煩中時,看到友好的臉是主要的安慰,除了你們的,沒有別人來這裡。

passages.original: Good friendly faces—good friendly faces.
passages.vernacular: 友好嘅好臉——友好嘅好臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 友好的好臉——友好的好臉。

passages.original: Git up on one another’s backs and let me touch ’em.
passages.vernacular: 爬到彼此嘅背上讓我摸摸佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爬到彼此的背上讓我摸摸它們。

passages.original: That’s it.
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣。

passages.original: Shake hands—yourn’ll come through the bars, but mine’s too big.
passages.vernacular: 握手——你哋嘅會穿過欄杆,但我嘅太大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 握手——你們的會穿過欄杆,但我的太大。

passages.original: Little hands, and weak—but they’ve helped Muff Potter a power, and they’d help him more if they could.”
passages.vernacular: 小手,又弱——但佢哋對馬夫·波特幫助好大,如果能,佢哋會幫助佢更多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小手,又弱——但它們對馬夫·波特幫助很大,如果能,它們會幫助他更多。」

passages.original: Tom went home miserable, and his dreams that night were full of horrors.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆悲慘地回家,佢嗰晚嘅夢充滿恐怖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆悲慘地回家,他那晚的夢充滿恐怖。

passages.original: The next day and the day after, he hung about the courtroom, drawn by an almost irresistible impulse to go in, but forcing himself to stay out.
passages.vernacular: 第二天同後天,佢喺法庭周圍徘徊,被一種幾乎不可抗拒嘅衝動吸引著想進去,但強迫自己待喺外面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天和後天,他在法庭周圍徘徊,被一種幾乎不可抗拒的衝動吸引著想進去,但強迫自己待在外面。

passages.original: Huck was having the same experience.
passages.vernacular: 哈克都有同樣嘅經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克也有同樣的經歷。

passages.original: They studiously avoided each other.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋刻意避開彼此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們刻意避開彼此。

passages.original: Each wandered away, from time to time, but the same dismal fascination always brought them back presently.
passages.vernacular: 每個人不時走開,但同樣淒涼嘅魔力總是不久又把佢哋帶回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個人不時走開,但同樣淒涼的魔力總是不久又把他們帶回來。

passages.original: Tom kept his ears open when idlers sauntered out of the courtroom, but invariably heard distressing news—the toils were closing more and more relentlessly around poor Potter.
passages.vernacular: 閒人從法庭踱出嚟時,湯姆豎起耳朵,卻總是聽到令人痛苦嘅消息——網正越嚟越無情地收緊可憐嘅波特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 閒人從法庭踱出來時,湯姆豎起耳朵,卻總是聽到令人痛苦的消息——網正越來越無情地收緊可憐的波特。

passages.original: At the end of the second day the village talk was to the effect that Injun Joe’s evidence stood firm and unshaken, and that there was not the slightest question as to what the jury’s verdict would be.
passages.vernacular: 第二天結束時,村裡嘅談話係,印第安喬嘅證據穩固不動搖,陪審團嘅裁決冇絲毫疑問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天結束時,村裡的談話是,印第安喬的證據穩固不動搖,陪審團的裁決沒有絲毫疑問。

passages.original: Tom was out late, that night, and came to bed through the window.
passages.vernacular: 嗰晚湯姆好晚才出嚟,從窗子上床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那晚湯姆很晚才出來,從窗子上床。

passages.original: He was in a tremendous state of excitement.
passages.vernacular: 佢處於極度興奮嘅狀態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他處於極度興奮的狀態。

passages.original: It was hours before he got to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 過咗幾個小時佢才入瞓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了幾個小時他才入睡。

passages.original: All the village flocked to the courthouse the next morning, for this was to be the great day.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨全村嘅人湧向法院,因為呢個係大日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨全村的人湧向法院,因為這是大日子。

passages.original: Both sexes were about equally represented in the packed audience.
passages.vernacular: 擠滿嘅聽眾中兩性嘅代表人數幾乎相等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 擠滿的聽眾中兩性的代表人數幾乎相等。

passages.original: After a long wait the jury filed in and took their places; shortly afterward, Potter, pale and haggard, timid and hopeless, was brought in, with chains upon him, and seated where all the curious eyes could stare at him; no less conspicuous was Injun Joe, stolid as ever.
passages.vernacular: 等咗好久之後,陪審團魚貫進嚟就座;不久後,波特,蒼白憔悴,膽怯而絕望,戴住鐐銬被帶進嚟,坐喺所有好奇嘅眼睛能盯住佢嘅地方;同樣顯眼嘅係印第安喬,一如既往地冷漠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等了很久之後,陪審團魚貫進來就座;不久後,波特,蒼白憔悴,膽怯而絕望,戴著鐐銬被帶進來,坐在所有好奇的眼睛能盯著他的地方;同樣顯眼的是印第安喬,一如既往地冷漠。

passages.original: There was another pause, and then the judge arrived and the sheriff proclaimed the opening of the court.
passages.vernacular: 又一次停頓,然後法官到喇,郡長宣布法庭開庭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一次停頓,然後法官到了,郡長宣布法庭開庭。

passages.original: The usual whisperings among the lawyers and gathering together of papers followed.
passages.vernacular: 通常律師之間嘅耳語同文件嘅整理隨之而嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通常律師之間的耳語和文件的整理隨之而來。

passages.original: These details and accompanying delays worked up an atmosphere of preparation that was as impressive as it was fascinating.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲細節同隨之而嚟嘅延誤營造出一種準備嘅氣氛,既令人印象深刻又迷人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些細節和隨之而來的延誤營造出一種準備的氣氛,既令人印象深刻又迷人。

passages.original: Now a witness was called who testified that he found Muff Potter washing in the brook, at an early hour of the morning that the murder was discovered, and that he immediately sneaked away.
passages.vernacular: 而家傳喚咗一個證人,佢作證講,喺發現謀殺案嘅嗰天清晨,佢發現馬夫·波特喺小溪裡洗澡,並立即溜走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在傳喚了一個證人,他作證說,在發現謀殺案的那天清晨,他發現馬夫·波特在小溪裡洗澡,並立即溜走了。

passages.original: After some further questioning, counsel for the prosecution said:
passages.vernacular: 經過啲進一步嘅詢問,控方律師講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過一些進一步的詢問,控方律師說:

passages.original: “Take the witness.”
passages.vernacular: 「請辯方詰問證人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請辯方詰問證人。」

passages.original: The prisoner raised his eyes for a moment, but dropped them again when his own counsel said:
passages.vernacular: 犯人抬眼片刻,但佢自己嘅律師講話時又垂下:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 犯人抬眼片刻,但他自己的律師說話時又垂下:

passages.original: “I have no questions to ask him.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇問題要問佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有問題要問他。」

passages.original: The next witness proved the finding of the knife near the corpse.
passages.vernacular: 下一個證人證明了喺屍體附近發現刀子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一個證人證明了在屍體附近發現刀子。

passages.original: Counsel for the prosecution said:
passages.vernacular: 控方律師講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 控方律師說:

passages.original: “Take the witness.”
passages.vernacular: 「請辯方詰問證人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請辯方詰問證人。」

passages.original: “I have no questions to ask him,” Potter’s lawyer replied.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇問題要問佢,」波特嘅律師回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有問題要問他,」波特的律師回答。

passages.original: A third witness swore he had often seen the knife in Potter’s possession.
passages.vernacular: 第三個證人發誓佢常睇到刀子喺波特手裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第三個證人發誓他常看到刀子在波特手裡。

passages.original: “Take the witness.”
passages.vernacular: 「請辯方詰問證人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請辯方詰問證人。」

passages.original: Counsel for Potter declined to question him.
passages.vernacular: 波特嘅律師拒絕詰問佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波特的律師拒絕詰問他。

passages.original: The faces of the audience began to betray annoyance.
passages.vernacular: 聽眾嘅臉開始流露出惱怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽眾的臉開始流露出惱怒。

passages.original: Did this attorney mean to throw away his client’s life without an effort?
passages.vernacular: 呢位律師係想不作任何努力就放棄佢當事人嘅命嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位律師是想不作任何努力就放棄他當事人的命嗎?

passages.original: Several witnesses deposed concerning Potter’s guilty behavior when brought to the scene of the murder.
passages.vernacular: 幾位證人就波特被帶到謀殺現場時嘅有罪舉止作證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾位證人就波特被帶到謀殺現場時的有罪舉止作證。

passages.original: They were allowed to leave the stand without being cross-questioned.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋被允許離開證人席,冇被交叉詰問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們被允許離開證人席,沒有被交叉詰問。
