passages.original: Every detail of the damaging circumstances that occurred in the graveyard upon that morning which all present remembered so well was brought out by credible witnesses, but none of them were cross-examined by Potter’s lawyer.
passages.vernacular: 喺每個在場者都記得咁清楚嘅嗰天早晨墳場發生嘅不利情況嘅每個細節,由可信嘅證人講咗出嚟,但波特嘅律師冇詰問其中任何一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在每個在場者都記得那麼清楚的那天早晨墳場發生的不利情況的每個細節,由可信的證人說了出來,但波特的律師沒有詰問其中任何一個。

passages.original: The perplexity and dissatisfaction of the house expressed itself in murmurs and provoked a reproof from the bench.
passages.vernacular: 全場嘅困惑同不滿以低語表達,並引起法官席嘅斥責。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全場的困惑和不滿以低語表達,並引起法官席的斥責。

passages.original: Counsel for the prosecution now said:
passages.vernacular: 控方律師而家講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 控方律師現在說:

passages.original: “By the oaths of citizens whose simple word is above suspicion, we have fastened this awful crime, beyond all possibility of question, upon the unhappy prisoner at the bar.
passages.vernacular: 「憑公民哋嘅誓言,佢哋嘅簡單話語超越懷疑,我哋已將呢個可怕嘅罪行,毫無疑問地,釘喺咗被告席上呢位不幸嘅犯人身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「憑公民們的誓言,他們的簡單話語超越懷疑,我們已將這可怕的罪行,毫無疑問地,釘在了被告席上這位不幸的犯人身上。

passages.original: We rest our case here.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅案子到此結束。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的案子到此結束。」

passages.original: A groan escaped from poor Potter, and he put his face in his hands and rocked his body softly to and fro, while a painful silence reigned in the courtroom.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅波特發出一聲呻吟,把臉埋喺手裡,輕輕前後搖晃身體,痛苦嘅沉默籠罩法庭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的波特發出一聲呻吟,把臉埋在手裡,輕輕前後搖晃身體,痛苦的沉默籠罩法庭。

passages.original: Many men were moved, and many women’s compassion testified itself in tears.
passages.vernacular: 許多男人被感動,許多女人嘅同情以眼淚表現出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多男人被感動,許多女人的同情以眼淚表現出來。

passages.original: Counsel for the defence rose and said:
passages.vernacular: 辯護律師站起來講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 辯護律師站起來說:

passages.original: “Your honor, in our remarks at the opening of this trial, we foreshadowed our purpose to prove that our client did this fearful deed while under the influence of a blind and irresponsible delirium produced by drink.
passages.vernacular: 「法官大人,喺審判開始時嘅陳述中,我哋預示我哋嘅目的係證明我哋嘅當事人係喺飲酒產生嘅盲目、不負責任嘅譫妄影響下做呢件可怕嘅事嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「法官大人,在審判開始時的陳述中,我們預示我們的目的是證明我們的當事人是在飲酒產生的盲目、不負責任的譫妄影響下做這件可怕的事的。

passages.original: We have changed our mind.
passages.vernacular: 我哋改變咗主意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們改變了主意。

passages.original: We shall not offer that plea.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔會提出嗰個辯護。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不會提出那個辯護。」

passages.original: [Then to the clerk:] “Call Thomas Sawyer!”
passages.vernacular: [然後對書記員:]「傳喚湯瑪斯·索亞!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: [然後對書記員:]「傳喚湯瑪斯·索亞!」

passages.original: A puzzled amazement awoke in every face in the house, not even excepting Potter’s.
passages.vernacular: 困惑嘅驚愕在場內每張臉上甦醒,連波特都不例外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 困惑的驚愕在場內每張臉上甦醒,連波特也不例外。

passages.original: Every eye fastened itself with wondering interest upon Tom as he rose and took his place upon the stand.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆站起嚟走到證人席上時,每雙眼睛都帶住好奇嘅興趣盯住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆站起來走到證人席上時,每雙眼睛都帶著好奇的興趣盯著他。

passages.original: The boy looked wild enough, for he was badly scared.
passages.vernacular: 男孩睇起嚟夠狂野嘅,因為佢嚇得厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩看起來夠狂野的,因為他嚇得厲害。

passages.original: The oath was administered.
passages.vernacular: 宣咗誓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 宣了誓。

passages.original: “Thomas Sawyer, where were you on the seventeenth of June, about the hour of midnight?”
passages.vernacular: 「湯瑪斯·索亞,六月十七日午夜時分你喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯瑪斯·索亞,六月十七日午夜時分你在哪裡?」

passages.original: Tom glanced at Injun Joe’s iron face and his tongue failed him.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆瞥咗一眼印第安喬鐵一般嘅臉,舌頭不聽使喚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆瞥了一眼印第安喬鐵一般的臉,舌頭不聽使喚。

passages.original: The audience listened breathless, but the words refused to come.
passages.vernacular: 聽眾屏息聽住,但話語唔肯出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽眾屏息聽著,但話語不肯出來。

passages.original: After a few moments, however, the boy got a little of his strength back, and managed to put enough of it into his voice to make part of the house hear:
passages.vernacular: 然而幾分鐘後,男孩恢復咗啲力氣,設法喺聲音裡放入足夠嘅力氣,讓場內一部分人聽到:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而幾分鐘後,男孩恢復了一點力氣,設法在聲音裡放入足夠的力氣,讓場內一部分人聽到:

passages.original: “In the graveyard!”
passages.vernacular: 「喺墳場!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在墳場!」

passages.original: “A little bit louder, please.
passages.vernacular: 「請稍微大聲啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請稍微大聲一點。

passages.original: Don’t be afraid.
passages.vernacular: 別怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別怕。

passages.original: You were—”
passages.vernacular: 你喺——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在——」

passages.original: “In the graveyard.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺墳場。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在墳場。」

passages.original: A contemptuous smile flitted across Injun Joe’s face.
passages.vernacular: 一絲輕蔑嘅微笑掠過印第安喬嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一絲輕蔑的微笑掠過印第安喬的臉。

passages.original: “Were you anywhere near Horse Williams’ grave?”
passages.vernacular: 「你有冇靠近霍斯·威廉斯嘅墳?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有沒有靠近霍斯·威廉斯的墳?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「有,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,先生。」

passages.original: “Speak up—just a trifle louder.
passages.vernacular: 「大聲講——稍微大聲啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大聲說——稍微大聲一點。

passages.original: How near were you?”
passages.vernacular: 你離得多近?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你離得多近?」

passages.original: “Near as I am to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「像我離你咁近。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「像我離你這麼近。」

passages.original: “Were you hidden, or not?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係藏住嘅,定係冇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是藏著的,還是沒有?」

passages.original: “I was hid.”
passages.vernacular: 「我藏住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我藏著。」

passages.original: “Where?”
passages.vernacular: 「喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在哪裡?」

passages.original: “Behind the elms that’s on the edge of the grave.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺墳邊嘅嗰幾棵榆樹後面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在墳邊的那幾棵榆樹後面。」

passages.original: Injun Joe gave a barely perceptible start.
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬幾乎察覺不出地動咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬幾乎察覺不出地動了一下。

passages.original: “Any one with you?”
passages.vernacular: 「有人同你喺一起嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有人同你在一起嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「有,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,先生。

passages.original: I went there with—”
passages.vernacular: 我同——一起去嗰度——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我同——一起去那裡——」

passages.original: “Wait—wait a moment.
passages.vernacular: 「等等——等一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等等——等一會兒。

passages.original: Never mind mentioning your companion’s name.
passages.vernacular: 唔使提你同伴嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不用提你同伴的名字。

passages.original: We will produce him at the proper time.
passages.vernacular: 我哋會喺適當嘅時候把佢帶嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會在適當的時候把他帶來。

passages.original: Did you carry anything there with you.”
passages.vernacular: 你帶咗乜嘢嘢去嗰度嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你帶了什麼東西去那裡嗎?」

passages.original: Tom hesitated and looked confused.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆猶豫住,顯得困惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆猶豫著,顯得困惑。

passages.original: “Speak out, my boy—don’t be diffident.
passages.vernacular: 「講出嚟,我嘅細路——別羞怯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說出來,我的孩子——別羞怯。

passages.original: The truth is always respectable.
passages.vernacular: 真相總是體面嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真相總是體面的。

passages.original: What did you take there?”
passages.vernacular: 你帶咗乜嘢去嗰度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你帶了什麼去那裡?」

passages.original: “Only a—a—dead cat.”
passages.vernacular: 「只係一隻——一隻——死貓。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是一隻——一隻——死貓。」

passages.original: There was a ripple of mirth, which the court checked.
passages.vernacular: 有一陣歡笑嘅漣漪,被法庭制止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一陣歡笑的漣漪,被法庭制止。

passages.original: “We will produce the skeleton of that cat.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋會出示嗰隻貓嘅骨骼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們會出示那隻貓的骨骼。

passages.original: Now, my boy, tell us everything that occurred—tell it in your own way—don’t skip anything, and don’t be afraid.”
passages.vernacular: 而家,我嘅細路,告訴我哋發生嘅一切——用你自己嘅方式講——別漏掉任何嘢,都別害怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,我的孩子,告訴我們發生的一切——用你自己的方式講——別漏掉任何東西,也別害怕。」

passages.original: Tom began—hesitatingly at first, but as he warmed to his subject his words flowed more and more easily; in a little while every sound ceased but his own voice; every eye fixed itself upon him; with parted lips and bated breath the audience hung upon his words, taking no note of time, rapt in the ghastly fascinations of the tale.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆開始喇——起初猶豫,但隨住佢對題目的熱情升溫,佢嘅話語越嚟越流暢;不久除咗佢自己嘅聲音,所有聲音都停止喇;每雙眼睛都盯住佢;聽眾張住嘴唇、屏住呼吸,抓住佢嘅話,不注意時間,沉浸喺故事可怕嘅魅力中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆開始了——起初猶豫,但隨著他對題目的熱情升溫,他的話語越來越流暢;不久除了他自己的聲音,所有聲音都停止了;每雙眼睛都盯著他;聽眾張著嘴唇、屏住呼吸,抓住他的話,不注意時間,沉浸在故事可怕的魅力中。

passages.original: The strain upon pent emotion reached its climax when the boy said:
passages.vernacular: 當男孩講到下面呢句時,對壓抑情緒嘅緊張達到頂點:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當男孩說到下面這句時,對壓抑情緒的緊張達到頂點:

passages.original: “—and as the doctor fetched the board around and Muff Potter fell, Injun Joe jumped with the knife and—”
passages.vernacular: 「——醫生把木板揮過嚟,馬夫·波特倒下時,印第安喬攞住刀跳起嚟,然後——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「——醫生把木板揮過來,馬夫·波特倒下時,印第安喬拿著刀跳起來,然後——」

passages.original: Crash!
passages.vernacular: 砰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 砰!

passages.original: Quick as lightning the halfbreed sprang for a window, tore his way through all opposers, and was gone!
passages.vernacular: 混血兒快如閃電地撲向一扇窗子,衝破所有阻攔者,逃走喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 混血兒快如閃電地撲向一扇窗子,衝破所有阻攔者,逃走了!

chapters.title: Chapter XXIV: Tom as the Village Hero 第二十四章:村裡的英雄

passages.original: CH Tom was a glittering hero once more—the pet of the old, the envy of the young.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆又成咗閃光嘅英雄——老人嘅寵兒,年輕人嘅羨慕對象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆又成了閃光的英雄——老人的寵兒,年輕人的羨慕對象。

passages.original: His name even went into immortal print, for the village paper magnified him.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅名字甚至登上咗不朽嘅印刷品,因為村報誇大咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的名字甚至登上了不朽的印刷品,因為村報誇大了他。

passages.original: There were some that believed he would be President, yet, if he escaped hanging.
passages.vernacular: 有些人相信,如果佢逃過絞刑,佢仲會當總統。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人相信,如果他逃過絞刑,他還會當總統。

passages.original: As usual, the fickle, unreasoning world took Muff Potter to its bosom and fondled him as lavishly as it had abused him before.
passages.vernacular: 一如既往,善變、不講道理嘅世界把馬夫·波特抱喺懷裡,像以前辱罵佢一樣慷慨地愛撫佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一如既往,善變、不講道理的世界把馬夫·波特抱在懷裡,像以前辱罵他一樣慷慨地愛撫他。

passages.original: But that sort of conduct is to the world’s credit; therefore it is not well to find fault with it.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰種行為係世界嘅功勞;因此不宜挑剔佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那種行為是世界的功勞;因此不宜挑剔它。

passages.original: Tom’s days were days of splendor and exultation to him, but his nights were seasons of horror.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅白天對佢來講係輝煌同歡欣嘅日子,但佢嘅夜晚係恐怖嘅季節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的白天對他來說是輝煌和歡欣的日子,但他的夜晚是恐怖的季節。

passages.original: Injun Joe infested all his dreams, and always with doom in his eye.
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬纏擾佢所有嘅夢,眼睛裡總是帶住厄運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬纏擾他所有的夢,眼睛裡總是帶著厄運。

passages.original: Hardly any temptation could persuade the boy to stir abroad after nightfall.
passages.vernacular: 幾乎冇乜嘢誘惑能講服男孩喺天黑後出門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾乎沒有什麼誘惑能說服男孩在天黑後出門。

passages.original: Poor Huck was in the same state of wretchedness and terror, for Tom had told the whole story to the lawyer the night before the great day of the trial, and Huck was sore afraid that his share in the business might leak out, yet, notwithstanding Injun Joe’s flight had saved him the suffering of testifying in court.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅哈克都處喺同樣嘅悲慘同恐懼之中,因為湯姆喺審判大日子嘅前一晚把整個故事告訴咗律師,哈克好害怕佢喺呢件事中嘅角色可能洩露出去,雖然印第安喬嘅逃走讓佢免除咗喺法庭作證嘅痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的哈克也處在同樣的悲慘和恐懼之中,因為湯姆在審判大日子的前一晚把整個故事告訴了律師,哈克非常害怕他在這件事中的角色可能洩露出去,雖然印第安喬的逃走讓他免除了在法庭作證的痛苦。

passages.original: The poor fellow had got the attorney to promise secrecy, but what of that?
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅傢伙曾讓律師答應保密,但嗰有乜嘢用?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的傢伙曾讓律師答應保密,但那有什麼用?

passages.original: Since Tom’s harassed conscience had managed to drive him to the lawyer’s house by night and wring a dread tale from lips that had been sealed with the dismalest and most formidable of oaths, Huck’s confidence in the human race was wellnigh obliterated.
passages.vernacular: 既然湯姆被折磨嘅良心居然能夠驅使佢夜裡去律師家,從被最陰鬱可怕嘅誓言封住嘅嘴唇裡擰出一個可怕嘅故事,哈克對人類嘅信心幾乎被消滅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然湯姆被折磨的良心居然能夠驅使他夜裡去律師家,從被最陰鬱可怕的誓言封住的嘴唇裡擰出一個可怕的故事,哈克對人類的信心幾乎被消滅了。

passages.original: Daily Muff Potter’s gratitude made Tom glad he had spoken; but nightly he wished he had sealed up his tongue.
passages.vernacular: 每天馬夫·波特嘅感激讓湯姆高興佢講咗出嚟;但每晚佢希望封住自己嘅舌頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每天馬夫·波特的感激讓湯姆高興他說了出來;但每晚他希望封住自己的舌頭。

passages.original: Half the time Tom was afraid Injun Joe would never be captured; the other half he was afraid he would be.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆有一半時間害怕印第安喬永遠唔會被抓到;另一半時間佢害怕佢會被抓到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆有一半時間害怕印第安喬永遠不會被抓到;另一半時間他害怕他會被抓到。

passages.original: He felt sure he never could draw a safe breath again until that man was dead and he had seen the corpse.
passages.vernacular: 佢肯定,喺嗰個人死咗並且佢睇到屍體之前,佢永遠唔能夠安全地呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他肯定,在那個人死了並且他看到屍體之前,他永遠不能安全地呼吸。

passages.original: Rewards had been offered, the country had been scoured, but no Injun Joe was found.
passages.vernacular: 懸賞已提出,全國已被搜遍,但冇找到印第安喬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懸賞已提出,全國已被搜遍,但沒有找到印第安喬。

passages.original: One of those omniscient and awe-inspiring marvels, a detective, came up from St. Louis, moused around, shook his head, looked wise, and made that sort of astounding success which members of that craft usually achieve.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲無所唔知、令人敬畏嘅奇蹟之一,一名偵探,從聖路易斯嚟,到處嗅探,搖頭,顯得聰明,取得咗嗰種嗰個行業嘅人通常取得嘅令人驚異嘅成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些無所不知、令人敬畏的奇蹟之一,一名偵探,從聖路易斯來,到處嗅探,搖頭,顯得聰明,取得了那種那個行業的人通常取得的令人驚異的成功。

passages.original: That is to say, he “found a clew.”
passages.vernacular: 都就係講,佢「發現咗一條線索」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也就是說,他「發現了一條線索」。

passages.original: But you can’t hang a “clew” for murder, and so after that detective had got through and gone home, Tom felt just as insecure as he was before.
passages.vernacular: 但你唔能夠因為謀殺而絞死一條「線索」,所以嗰個偵探辦完事回家後,湯姆覺得同以前一樣不安全。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你不能因為謀殺而絞死一條「線索」,所以那個偵探辦完事回家後,湯姆覺得和以前一樣不安全。

passages.original: The slow days drifted on, and each left behind it a slightly lightened weight of apprehension.
passages.vernacular: 緩慢嘅日子漂過去,每一天都留下稍微減輕嘅憂慮重量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 緩慢的日子漂過去,每一天都留下稍微減輕的憂慮重量。

chapters.title: Chapter XXV: About Kings and Diamonds 第二十五章:尋寶

passages.original: CH There comes a time in every rightly-constructed boy’s life when he has a raging desire to go somewhere and dig for hidden treasure.
passages.vernacular: 喺每個構造正確嘅男孩生命中都會有一個時期,佢狂熱地想去某個地方挖掘隱藏嘅寶藏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在每個構造正確的男孩生命中都會有一個時期,他狂熱地想去某個地方挖掘隱藏的寶藏。

passages.original: This desire suddenly came upon Tom one day.
passages.vernacular: 有一天呢個慾望突然襲上湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天這個慾望突然襲上湯姆。

passages.original: He sallied out to find Joe Harper, but failed of success.
passages.vernacular: 佢出去找喬·哈珀,冇成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他出去找喬·哈珀,沒有成功。

passages.original: Next he sought Ben Rogers; he had gone fishing.
passages.vernacular: 接住佢找本·羅傑斯;佢去釣魚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著他找本·羅傑斯;他去釣魚了。

passages.original: Presently he stumbled upon Huck Finn the Red-Handed.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢偶然碰到紅手哈克·費恩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他偶然碰到紅手哈克·費恩。

passages.original: Huck would answer.
passages.vernacular: 哈克會答應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克會答應。

passages.original: Tom took him to a private place and opened the matter to him confidentially.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆把佢帶到一個私密嘅地方,祕密地向佢講明呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆把他帶到一個私密的地方,祕密地向他說明這件事。

passages.original: Huck was willing.
passages.vernacular: 哈克願意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克願意。

passages.original: Huck was always willing to take a hand in any enterprise that offered entertainment and required no capital, for he had a troublesome superabundance of that sort of time which is not money.
passages.vernacular: 哈克總是願意參與任何提供娛樂又不需要資本嘅事業,因為佢有討厭嘅過剩嘅嗰種唔係金錢嘅時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克總是願意參與任何提供娛樂又不需要資本的事業,因為他有討厭的過剩的那種不是金錢的時間。

passages.original: “Where’ll we dig?” said Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋喺邊度挖?」哈克講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們在哪裡挖?」哈克說。

passages.original: “Oh, most anywhere.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,幾乎邊度都行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,幾乎哪裡都行。」

passages.original: “Why, is it hid all around?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,到處都藏住嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,到處都藏著嗎?」

passages.original: “No, indeed it ain’t.
passages.vernacular: 「不,真嘅唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,真的不是。

passages.original: It’s hid in mighty particular places, Huck—sometimes on islands, sometimes in rotten chests under the end of a limb of an old dead tree, just where the shadow falls at midnight; but mostly under the floor in ha’nted houses.”
passages.vernacular: 佢藏喺好特定嘅地方,哈克——有時喺島上,有時喺老死樹一根樹枝末端下嘅腐爛箱子裡,就喺午夜影子落下嘅地方;但大多喺鬧鬼房子嘅地板下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它藏在非常特定的地方,哈克——有時在島上,有時在老死樹一根樹枝末端下的腐爛箱子裡,就在午夜影子落下的地方;但大多在鬧鬼房子的地板下。」

passages.original: “Who hides it?”
passages.vernacular: 「邊個藏嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰藏的?」

passages.original: “Why, robbers, of course—who’d you reckon?
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,當然係強盜——你以為係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,當然是強盜——你以為是誰?

passages.original: Sunday-school sup’rintendents?”
passages.vernacular: 主日學校嘅監督?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主日學校的監督?」

passages.original: “I don’t know.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: If ’twas mine I wouldn’t hide it; I’d spend it and have a good time.”
passages.vernacular: 如果係我嘅,我唔會藏;我會花掉佢,好好享受。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是我的,我不會藏;我會花掉它,好好享受。」

passages.original: “So would I. But robbers don’t do that way.
passages.vernacular: 「我都係。但強盜唔係嗰樣做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是。但強盜不是那樣做的。

passages.original: They always hide it and leave it there.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋總是把佢藏起嚟,留喺嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們總是把它藏起來,留在那裡。」

passages.original: “Don’t they come after it any more?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋唔再回嚟取嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們不再回來取嗎?」

passages.original: “No, they think they will, but they generally forget the marks, or else they die.
passages.vernacular: 「不,佢哋想會,但佢哋通常忘咗標記,否則就死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,他們想會,但他們通常忘了標記,否則就死了。

passages.original: Anyway, it lays there a long time and gets rusty; and by and by somebody finds an old yellow paper that tells how to find the marks—a paper that’s got to be ciphered over about a week because it’s mostly signs and hy’roglyphics.”
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,佢躺喺嗰度好長時間,生鏽;不久有人發現一張老黃紙,告訴點樣找到標記——一張得破譯大約一個星期嘅紙,因為大多係記號同象形文字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,它躺在那裡很長時間,生鏽;不久有人發現一張老黃紙,告訴怎樣找到標記——一張得破譯大約一個星期的紙,因為大多是記號和象形文字。」

passages.original: “Hyro—which?”
“Hy’roglyphics—pictures and things, you know, that don’t seem to mean anything.”
passages.vernacular: 「象形文字——圖畫之類嘅,你知道,似乎冇意義。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「象形文字——圖畫之類的,你知道,似乎沒有意義。」

passages.original: “Have you got one of them papers, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 「你有嗰種紙嗎,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有那種紙嗎,湯姆?」

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。」

passages.original: “Well then, how you going to find the marks?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁你點找標記?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼你怎麼找標記?」

passages.original: “I don’t want any marks.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔好任何標記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不要任何標記。

passages.original: They always bury it under a ha’nted house or on an island, or under a dead tree that’s got one limb sticking out.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋總是把佢埋喺鬧鬼房子下,或島上,或有一根樹枝伸出嘅死樹下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們總是把它埋在鬧鬼房子下,或島上,或有一根樹枝伸出的死樹下。

passages.original: Well, we’ve tried Jackson’s Island a little, and we can try it again some time; and there’s the old ha’nted house up the Still-House branch, and there’s lots of dead-limb trees—dead loads of ’em.”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我哋稍微試過傑克森島,我哋有時可以再試;仲有蒸餾坊支流上嗰座老鬧鬼房子,有好多死枝樹——一大堆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我們稍微試過傑克森島,我們有時可以再試;還有蒸餾坊支流上那座老鬧鬼房子,有很多死枝樹——一大堆。」

passages.original: “Is it under all of them?”
passages.vernacular: 「喺所有嗰啲下面都有嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在所有那些下面都有嗎?」

passages.original: “How you talk!
passages.vernacular: 「你點講話!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼說話!

passages.original: No!”
“Then how you going to know which one to go for?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁你點知道去邊一個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼你怎麼知道去哪一個?」

passages.original: “Go for all of ’em!”
passages.vernacular: 「全都去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「全都去!」

passages.original: “Why, Tom, it’ll take all summer.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,湯姆,嗰要花整個夏天。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,湯姆,那要花整個夏天。」

passages.original: “Well, what of that?
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那又怎樣?

passages.original: Suppose you find a brass pot with a hundred dollars in it, all rusty and gray, or rotten chest full of di’monds.
passages.vernacular: 假設你找到一個黃銅罐,裡面有一百塊錢,全係鏽,灰色嘅,或者一個腐爛嘅箱子,裝滿鑽石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假設你找到一個黃銅罐,裡面有一百塊錢,全是鏽,灰色的,或者一個腐爛的箱子,裝滿鑽石。

passages.original: How’s that?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那怎麼樣?」

passages.original: Huck’s eyes glowed.
passages.vernacular: 哈克嘅眼睛發光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克的眼睛發光。

passages.original: “That’s bully.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰太棒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那太棒了。

passages.original: Plenty bully enough for me.
passages.vernacular: 對我來講足夠棒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我來說足夠棒了。

passages.original: Just you gimme the hundred dollars and I don’t want no di’monds.”
passages.vernacular: 只要你畀我一百塊錢,我唔好鑽石。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要你給我一百塊錢,我不要鑽石。」

passages.original: “All right.
But I bet you I ain’t going to throw off on di’monds.
passages.vernacular: 但我打賭我唔會拋棄鑽石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我打賭我不會拋棄鑽石。

passages.original: Some of ’em’s worth twenty dollars apiece—there ain’t any, hardly, but’s worth six bits or a dollar.”
passages.vernacular: 有些鑽石每顆值二十塊——幾乎冇一顆不值六毛或一塊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些鑽石每顆值二十塊——幾乎沒有一顆不值六毛或一塊。」

passages.original: “No!
passages.vernacular: 「唔會吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會吧!

passages.original: Is that so?”
passages.vernacular: 係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是嗎?」

passages.original: “Cert’nly—anybody’ll tell you so.
passages.vernacular: 「當然——任何人都會告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然——任何人都會告訴你。

passages.original: Hain’t you ever seen one, Huck?”
passages.vernacular: 你冇見過嗎,哈克?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你沒見過嗎,哈克?」

passages.original: “Not as I remember.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不記得見過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不記得見過。」

passages.original: “Oh, kings have slathers of them.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,國王哋有一大堆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,國王們有一大堆。」

passages.original: “Well, I don’ know no kings, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我不認識國王,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不認識國王,湯姆。」

passages.original: “I reckon you don’t.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你不認識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你不認識。

passages.original: But if you was to go to Europe you’d see a raft of ’em hopping around.”
passages.vernacular: 但如果你去歐洲,你會睇到一大堆喺蹦跳。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果你去歐洲,你會看到一大堆在蹦跳。」

passages.original: “Do they hop?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋蹦跳嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們蹦跳嗎?」

passages.original: “Hop?—your granny!
passages.vernacular: 「蹦跳?——你奶奶!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蹦跳?——你奶奶!

passages.original: No!”
“Well, what did you say they did, for?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你講佢哋蹦跳係點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你說他們蹦跳是為什麼?」

passages.original: “Shucks, I only meant you’d see ’em—not hopping, of course—what do they want to hop for?—but I mean you’d just see ’em—scattered around, you know, in a kind of a general way.
passages.vernacular: 「算喇,我只係講你會睇到佢哋——當然唔係蹦跳——佢哋點解要蹦跳?——我係講你只係會睇到佢哋——散布喺周圍,你知道,以一種一般嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「算了,我只是說你會看到他們——當然不是蹦跳——他們為什麼要蹦跳?——我是說你只是會看到他們——散布在周圍,你知道,以一種一般的方式。

passages.original: Like that old humpbacked Richard.”
passages.vernacular: 像嗰個駝背老理查。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像那個駝背老理查。」

passages.original: “Richard?
passages.vernacular: 「理查?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「理查?

passages.original: What’s his other name?”
passages.vernacular: 佢另一個名字係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他另一個名字是什麼?」

passages.original: “He didn’t have any other name.
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇另一個名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他沒有另一個名字。

passages.original: Kings don’t have any but a given name.”
passages.vernacular: 國王除咗名字冇別嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 國王除了名字沒有別的。」

passages.original: “No?”
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有?」

passages.original: “But they don’t.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋確實冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們確實沒有。」

passages.original: “Well, if they like it, Tom, all right; but I don’t want to be a king and have only just a given name, like a nigger.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,如果佢哋鍾意,湯姆,好吧;但我唔想當國王只有一個名字,像個黑人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,如果他們喜歡,湯姆,好吧;但我不想當國王只有一個名字,像個黑人。

passages.original: But say—where you going to dig first?”
passages.vernacular: 但係,喂——你要先喺邊度挖?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,喂——你要先在哪裡挖?」

passages.original: “Well, I don’t know.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道。

passages.original: S’pose we tackle that old dead-limb tree on the hill t’other side of Still-House branch?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋試試嗰棵喺蒸餾坊支流對面山上嘅老死枝樹點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們試試那棵在蒸餾坊支流對面山上的老死枝樹怎麼樣?」

passages.original: “I’m agreed.”
passages.vernacular: 「我同意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我同意。」

passages.original: So they got a crippled pick and a shovel, and set out on their three-mile tramp.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋攞咗一把破鎬同一把鏟子,出發走三英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們拿了一把破鎬和一把鏟子,出發走三英里。

passages.original: They arrived hot and panting, and threw themselves down in the shade of a neighboring elm to rest and have a smoke.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋又熱又喘地到達,倒喺附近一棵榆樹嘅陰涼下休息抽菸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們又熱又喘地到達,倒在附近一棵榆樹的陰涼下休息抽菸。

passages.original: “I like this,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「我鍾意呢個,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我喜歡這個,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “So do I.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是。」

passages.original: “Say, Huck, if we find a treasure here, what you going to do with your share?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,哈克,如果我哋喺呢度找到寶藏,你會點用你嗰一份?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,哈克,如果我們在這裡找到寶藏,你會怎麼用你那一份?」

passages.original: “Well, I’ll have pie and a glass of soda every day, and I’ll go to every circus that comes along.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我每天要食餡餅同一杯蘇打水,每個嚟嘅馬戲團我都去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我每天要吃餡餅和一杯蘇打水,每個來的馬戲團我都去。

passages.original: I bet I’ll have a gay time.”
passages.vernacular: 我打賭我會玩得好開心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打賭我會玩得很開心。」

passages.original: “Well, ain’t you going to save any of it?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你不打算存啲嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你不打算存一些嗎?」

passages.original: “Save it?
What for?”
passages.vernacular: 點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, so as to have something to live on, by and by.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,為了將來有嘢靠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,為了將來有東西靠。」

passages.original: “Oh, that ain’t any use.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,沒有用。

passages.original: Pap would come back to thish-yer town some day and get his claws on it if I didn’t hurry up, and I tell you he’d clean it out pretty quick.
passages.vernacular: 爸爸有一天會回呢個鎮上,如果我不趕快,佢會抓走佢,我告訴你佢會好快把佢搞光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸有一天會回這個鎮上,如果我不趕快,他會抓走它,我告訴你他會很快把它搞光。

passages.original: What you going to do with yourn, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 你嘅你點用,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的你怎麼用,湯姆?」

passages.original: “I’m going to buy a new drum, and a sure’nough sword, and a red necktie and a bull pup, and get married.”
passages.vernacular: 「我要買一面新鼓、一把真劍、一條紅領帶同一隻鬥牛犬崽,然後結婚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要買一面新鼓、一把真劍、一條紅領帶和一隻鬥牛犬崽,然後結婚。」

passages.original: “Married!”
passages.vernacular: 「結婚!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「結婚!」

passages.original: “That’s it.”
passages.vernacular: 「就係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是。」

passages.original: “Tom, you—why, you ain’t in your right mind.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,你——哎呀,你神志不清喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,你——哎呀,你神志不清了。」

passages.original: “Wait—you’ll see.”
passages.vernacular: 「等住——你會睇到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等著——你會看到。」

passages.original: “Well, that’s the foolishest thing you could do.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰個係你能做嘅最傻嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那是你能做的最傻的事。

passages.original: Look at pap and my mother.
passages.vernacular: 睇睇爸爸同我媽媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看看爸爸和我媽媽。

passages.original: Fight!
passages.vernacular: 打架!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打架!

passages.original: Why, they used to fight all the time.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,佢哋過去總是打架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,他們過去總是打架。

passages.original: I remember, mighty well.”
passages.vernacular: 我記得好清楚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記得很清楚。」

passages.original: “That ain’t anything.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰不算乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那不算什麼。

passages.original: The girl I’m going to marry won’t fight.”
passages.vernacular: 我要娶嘅女孩唔會打架。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要娶的女孩不會打架。」

passages.original: “Tom, I reckon they’re all alike.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我想佢哋都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我想她們都一樣。

passages.original: They’ll all comb a body.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都會抓人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們都會抓人。

passages.original: Now you better think ’bout this awhile.
passages.vernacular: 而家你最好再想想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你最好再想想。

passages.original: I tell you you better.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你你最好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你你最好。

passages.original: What’s the name of the gal?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個『女子』叫乜嘢名字?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個『女子』叫什麼名字?」

passages.original: “It ain’t a gal at all—it’s a girl.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔係『女子』,係女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是『女子』,是女孩。」

passages.original: “It’s all the same, I reckon; some says gal, some says girl—both’s right, like enough.
passages.vernacular: 「我想都一樣;有人講女子,有人講女孩——大概都對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想都一樣;有人說女子,有人說女孩——大概都對。

passages.original: Anyway, what’s her name, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,佢叫乜嘢,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,她叫什麼,湯姆?」

passages.original: “I’ll tell you some time—not now.”
passages.vernacular: 「我改天告訴你——唔係而家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我改天告訴你——不是現在。」

passages.original: “All right—that’ll do.
passages.vernacular: 「好——可以。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好——可以。

passages.original: Only if you get married I’ll be more lonesomer than ever.”
passages.vernacular: 只係如果你結婚,我會比以前更孤單。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是如果你結婚,我會比以前更孤單。」

passages.original: “No you won’t.
passages.vernacular: 「不,你唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,你不會。

passages.original: You’ll come and live with me.
passages.vernacular: 你會嚟同我住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會來同我住。

passages.original: Now stir out of this and we’ll go to digging.”
passages.vernacular: 而家離開呢度,我哋去挖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在離開這裡,我們去挖。」

passages.original: They worked and sweated for half an hour.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋工作流汗半個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們工作流汗半個小時。

passages.original: No result.
passages.vernacular: 冇結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有結果。

passages.original: They toiled another halfhour.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋又辛苦咗半個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們又辛苦了半個小時。

passages.original: Still no result.
passages.vernacular: 仍然冇結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仍然沒有結果。

passages.original: Huck said:
passages.vernacular: 哈克講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克說:

passages.original: “Do they always bury it as deep as this?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋總是埋得咁深嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們總是埋得這麼深嗎?」

passages.original: “Sometimes—not always.
passages.vernacular: 「有時——不總是。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有時——不總是。

passages.original: Not generally.
passages.vernacular: 通常不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通常不。

passages.original: I reckon we haven’t got the right place.”
passages.vernacular: 我想我哋冇找到對嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我們沒找到對的地方。」

passages.original: So they chose a new spot and began again.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋選咗一個新地點,重新開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們選了一個新地點,重新開始。

passages.original: The labor dragged a little, but still they made progress.
passages.vernacular: 工作有點拖沓,但佢哋仍然有進展。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 工作有點拖沓,但他們仍然有進展。

passages.original: They pegged away in silence for some time.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋默默地苦幹咗一段時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們默默地苦幹了一段時間。

passages.original: Finally Huck leaned on his shovel, swabbed the beaded drops from his brow with his sleeve, and said:
passages.vernacular: 最後哈克靠喺鏟子上,用袖子擦掉額頭上嘅汗珠,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後哈克靠在鏟子上,用袖子擦掉額頭上的汗珠,說:

passages.original: “Where you going to dig next, after we get this one?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋弄完呢個之後,你要喺邊度挖下一個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們弄完這個之後,你要在哪裡挖下一個?」

passages.original: “I reckon maybe we’ll tackle the old tree that’s over yonder on Cardiff Hill back of the widow’s.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想或者我哋試試寡婦家後面卡迪夫山上嗰邊嘅嗰棵老樹。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想也許我們試試寡婦家後面卡迪夫山上那邊的那棵老樹。」

passages.original: “I reckon that’ll be a good one.
passages.vernacular: 「我想嗰會係個好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想那會是個好的。

passages.original: But won’t the widow take it away from us, Tom?
passages.vernacular: 但寡婦唔會從我哋呢度攞走嗎,湯姆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但寡婦不會從我們這裡拿走嗎,湯姆?

passages.original: It’s on her land.”
passages.vernacular: 佢喺佢嘅地上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它在她的地上。」

passages.original: “She take it away!
passages.vernacular: 「佢攞走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她拿走!

passages.original: Maybe she’d like to try it once.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢想試一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許她想試一次。

passages.original: Whoever finds one of these hid treasures, it belongs to him.
passages.vernacular: 不管邊個找到呢啲藏起嚟嘅寶藏,都屬於佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管誰找到這些藏起來的寶藏,都屬於他。

passages.original: It don’t make any difference whose land it’s on.”
passages.vernacular: 不管佢喺邊個嘅地上都冇關係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管它在誰的地上都沒關係。」

passages.original: That was satisfactory.
passages.vernacular: 呢令人滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這令人滿意。

passages.original: The work went on.
passages.vernacular: 工作繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 工作繼續。

passages.original: By and by Huck said:
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒哈克講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒哈克說:

passages.original: “Blame it, we must be in the wrong place again.
passages.vernacular: 「真該死,我哋一定又喺錯嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真該死,我們一定又在錯的地方。

passages.original: What do you think?”
passages.vernacular: 你點想?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼想?」

passages.original: “It is mighty curious, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「真係奇怪,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真是奇怪,哈克。

passages.original: I don’t understand it.
passages.vernacular: 我不明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不明白。

passages.original: Sometimes witches interfere.
passages.vernacular: 有時女巫干擾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時女巫干擾。

passages.original: I reckon maybe that’s what’s the trouble now.”
passages.vernacular: 我想或者嗰個就係而家嘅麻煩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想也許那就是現在的麻煩。」

passages.original: “Shucks!
passages.vernacular: 「算喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「算了!

passages.original: Witches ain’t got no power in the daytime.”
passages.vernacular: 女巫白天冇力量。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女巫白天沒有力量。」

passages.original: “Well, that’s so.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,是這樣。

passages.original: I didn’t think of that.
passages.vernacular: 我冇想到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒想到。

passages.original: Oh, I know what the matter is!
passages.vernacular: 哦,我知道係點回事喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我知道是怎麼回事了!

passages.original: What a blamed lot of fools we are!
passages.vernacular: 我哋係幾咁該死嘅一群傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們是多麼該死的一群傻瓜!

passages.original: You got to find out where the shadow of the limb falls at midnight, and that’s where you dig!”
passages.vernacular: 你得找出樹枝嘅影子喺午夜落喺邊度,嗰個就係你挖嘅地方!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得找出樹枝的影子在午夜落在哪裡,那就是你挖的地方!」

passages.original: “Then consound it, we’ve fooled away all this work for nothing.
passages.vernacular: 「咁真該死,我哋白白浪費咗所有呢啲工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼真該死,我們白白浪費了所有這些工作。

passages.original: Now hang it all, we got to come back in the night.
passages.vernacular: 而家真該死,我哋得夜裡回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在真該死,我們得夜裡回來。

passages.original: It’s an awful long way.
passages.vernacular: 路好長好長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路好長好長。

passages.original: Can you get out?”
passages.vernacular: 你能出嚟嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能出來嗎?」

passages.original: “I bet I will.
passages.vernacular: 「我打賭我能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我打賭我能。

passages.original: We’ve got to do it tonight, too, because if somebody sees these holes they’ll know in a minute what’s here and they’ll go for it.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋今晚都得做,因為如果有人睇到呢啲洞,佢哋即刻就會知道呢度有乜嘢,佢哋會去找。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們今晚也得做,因為如果有人看到這些洞,他們馬上就會知道這裡有什麼,他們會去找。」

passages.original: “Well, I’ll come around and maow tonight.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我今晚嚟喵喵叫。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我今晚來喵喵叫。」

passages.original: “All right.
Let’s hide the tools in the bushes.”
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋把工具藏喺灌木叢裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們把工具藏在灌木叢裡。」

passages.original: The boys were there that night, about the appointed time.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋嗰晚喺約定嘅時間左右到咗嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們那晚在約定的時間左右到了那裡。

passages.original: They sat in the shadow waiting.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋坐喺陰影中等待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們坐在陰影中等待。

passages.original: It was a lonely place, and an hour made solemn by old traditions.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個荒涼嘅地方,係一個被古老傳講弄得莊嚴嘅時辰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個荒涼的地方,是一個被古老傳說弄得莊嚴的時辰。

passages.original: Spirits whispered in the rustling leaves, ghosts lurked in the murky nooks, the deep baying of a hound floated up out of the distance, an owl answered with his sepulchral note.
passages.vernacular: 精靈喺沙沙作響嘅樹葉中低語,鬼魂潛伏喺陰暗嘅角落,一隻獵犬深沉嘅吠聲從遠處飄嚟,貓頭鷹用佢墓穴般嘅聲音回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 精靈在沙沙作響的樹葉中低語,鬼魂潛伏在陰暗的角落,一隻獵犬深沉的吠聲從遠處飄來,貓頭鷹用他墓穴般的聲音回答。

passages.original: The boys were subdued by these solemnities, and talked little.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋被呢啲莊嚴壓制,好少講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們被這些莊嚴壓制,很少說話。

passages.original: By and by they judged that twelve had come; they marked where the shadow fell, and began to dig.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋判斷十二點到喇;佢哋標出影子落下嘅地方,開始挖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們判斷十二點到了;他們標出影子落下的地方,開始挖。

passages.original: Their hopes commenced to rise.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅希望開始升起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們的希望開始升起。

passages.original: Their interest grew stronger, and their industry kept pace with it.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅興趣更強烈,佢哋嘅勤奮同之同步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們的興趣更強烈,他們的勤奮與之同步。

passages.original: The hole deepened and still deepened, but every time their hearts jumped to hear the pick strike upon something, they only suffered a new disappointment.
passages.vernacular: 洞越挖越深,但每次聽到鎬碰到乜嘢嘢,佢哋嘅心就跳起嚟,結果只係遭受新嘅失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 洞越挖越深,但每次聽到鎬碰到什麼東西,他們的心就跳起來,結果只是遭受新的失望。

passages.original: It was only a stone or a chunk.
passages.vernacular: 只係一塊石頭或一塊泥塊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是一塊石頭或一塊泥塊。

passages.original: At last Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 最後湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後湯姆說:

passages.original: “It ain’t any use, Huck, we’re wrong again.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇用,哈克,我哋又錯喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒用,哈克,我們又錯了。」

passages.original: “Well, but we can’t be wrong.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,但我哋唔可能錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,但我們不可能錯。

passages.original: We spotted the shadder to a dot.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋把影子定位得啲不差。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們把影子定位得一點不差。」

passages.original: “I know it, but then there’s another thing.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,但仲有另一件事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,但還有另一件事。」

passages.original: “What’s that?”
passages.vernacular: 「係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, we only guessed at the time.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我哋只係猜時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我們只是猜時間。

passages.original: Like enough it was too late or too early.”
passages.vernacular: 好可能太晚或太早喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很可能太晚或太早了。」

passages.original: Huck dropped his shovel.
passages.vernacular: 哈克扔下鏟子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克扔下鏟子。

passages.original: “That’s it,” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「就係,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是,」他說。

passages.original: “That’s the very trouble.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是麻煩。

passages.original: We got to give this one up.
passages.vernacular: 我哋得放棄呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們得放棄這個。

passages.original: We can’t ever tell the right time, and besides this kind of thing’s too awful, here this time of night with witches and ghosts a-fluttering around so.
passages.vernacular: 我哋永遠講不準正確嘅時間,而且呢種事太可怕,喺呢個時辰喺呢度,女巫同鬼魂咁到處撲騰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們永遠說不準正確的時間,而且這種事太可怕,在這個時辰在這裡,女巫和鬼魂這麼到處撲騰。

passages.original: I feel as if something’s behind me all the time; and I’m afeard to turn around, becuz maybe there’s others in front a-waiting for a chance.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得好像一直有嘢喺我後面;我怕轉身,因為或者前面仲有其他嘅喺等機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得好像一直有東西在我後面;我怕轉身,因為也許前面還有其他的在等機會。

passages.original: I been creeping all over, ever since I got here.”
passages.vernacular: 自從我到呢度,我一直渾身爬雞皮疙瘩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從我到這裡,我一直渾身爬雞皮疙瘩。」

passages.original: “Well, I’ve been pretty much so, too, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我都差不多,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我也差不多,哈克。

passages.original: They most always put in a dead man when they bury a treasure under a tree, to look out for it.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把寶藏埋喺樹下時,幾乎總是放一個死人,睇守佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把寶藏埋在樹下時,幾乎總是放一個死人,看守它。」

passages.original: “Lordy!”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」

passages.original: “Yes, they do.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢哋咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,他們這樣做。

passages.original: I’ve always heard that.”
passages.vernacular: 我一直聽講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直聽說。」

passages.original: “Tom, I don’t like to fool around much where there’s dead people.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我不鍾意喺有死人嘅地方瞎混。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我不喜歡在有死人的地方瞎混。

passages.original: A body’s bound to get into trouble with ’em, sure.”
passages.vernacular: 一個人肯定會同佢哋惹上麻煩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個人肯定會和他們惹上麻煩。」

passages.original: “I don’t like to stir ’em up, either.
passages.vernacular: 「我都不鍾意驚動佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也不喜歡驚動他們。

passages.original: S’pose this one here was to stick his skull out and say something!”
passages.vernacular: 假設呢度呢個把頭骨伸出來講點乜嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假設這裡這個把頭骨伸出來說點什麼!」

passages.original: “Don’t Tom!
passages.vernacular: 「別,湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別,湯姆!

passages.original: It’s awful.”
passages.vernacular: 太可怕喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太可怕了。」

passages.original: “Well, it just is.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,就係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,就是。

passages.original: Huck, I don’t feel comfortable a bit.”
passages.vernacular: 哈克,我啲都不覺得舒服。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克,我一點也不覺得舒服。」

passages.original: “Say, Tom, let’s give this place up, and try somewheres else.”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,湯姆,我哋放棄呢個地方,試別處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,湯姆,我們放棄這個地方,試別處。」

passages.original: “All right, I reckon we better.”
passages.vernacular: 「好,我想我哋最好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,我想我們最好。」

passages.original: “What’ll it be?”
passages.vernacular: 「去邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去哪裡?」

passages.original: Tom considered awhile; and then said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆考慮咗一會兒;然後講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆考慮了一會兒;然後說:

passages.original: “The ha’nted house.
passages.vernacular: 「鬧鬼嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鬧鬼的房子。

passages.original: That’s it!”
passages.vernacular: 就係佢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是它!」

passages.original: “Blame it, I don’t like ha’nted houses, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「真該死,我不鍾意鬧鬼嘅房子,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真該死,我不喜歡鬧鬼的房子,湯姆。

passages.original: Why, they’re a dern sight worse’n dead people.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,佢哋比死人糟得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,它們比死人糟得多。

passages.original: Dead people might talk, maybe, but they don’t come sliding around in a shroud, when you ain’t noticing, and peep over your shoulder all of a sudden and grit their teeth, the way a ghost does.
passages.vernacular: 死人或者會講話,但佢哋唔會喺你冇注意時裹住壽衣滑過嚟,突然從你肩上偷睇並咬牙,像鬼嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 死人也許會說話,但他們不會在你沒注意時裹著壽衣滑過來,突然從你肩上偷看並咬牙,像鬼那樣。

passages.original: I couldn’t stand such a thing as that, Tom—nobody could.”
passages.vernacular: 我受不了嗰樣嘅事,湯姆——冇人受得喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我受不了那樣的事,湯姆——沒有人受得了。」

passages.original: “Yes, but, Huck, ghosts don’t travel around only at night.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,但,哈克,鬼不只喺夜裡出動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,但,哈克,鬼不只在夜裡出動。

passages.original: They won’t hender us from digging there in the daytime.”
passages.vernacular: 白天佢哋唔會妨礙我哋喺嗰度挖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白天他們不會妨礙我們在那裡挖。」

passages.original: “Well, that’s so.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,是這樣。

passages.original: But you know mighty well people don’t go about that ha’nted house in the day nor the night.”
passages.vernacular: 但你好清楚,白天同夜裡人哋都不去嗰座鬧鬼嘅房子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你很清楚,白天和夜裡人們都不去那座鬧鬼的房子。」

passages.original: “Well, that’s mostly because they don’t like to go where a man’s been murdered, anyway—but nothing’s ever been seen around that house except in the night—just some blue lights slipping by the windows—no regular ghosts.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰主要係因為佢哋不鍾意去有人被謀殺嘅地方,無論如何——但嗰所房子周圍除咗夜裡從冇見過乜嘢——只係啲藍燈從窗子旁滑過——冇真正嘅鬼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那主要是因為他們不喜歡去有人被謀殺的地方,無論如何——但那所房子周圍除了夜裡從沒見過什麼——只是一些藍燈從窗子旁滑過——沒有真正的鬼。」

passages.original: “Well, where you see one of them blue lights flickering around, Tom, you can bet there’s a ghost mighty close behind it.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你睇到嗰啲藍燈喺周圍閃爍嘅地方,湯姆,你可以打賭有鬼就緊跟喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你看到那些藍燈在周圍閃爍的地方,湯姆,你可以打賭有鬼就緊跟在後面。

passages.original: It stands to reason.
passages.vernacular: 呢合情合理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這合情合理。

passages.original: Becuz you know that they don’t anybody but ghosts use ’em.”
passages.vernacular: 因為你知道,除咗鬼,冇人用佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你知道,除了鬼,沒有人用它們。」

passages.original: “Yes, that’s so.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是這樣。

passages.original: But anyway they don’t come around in the daytime, so what’s the use of our being afeard?”
passages.vernacular: 但無論如何佢哋白天不嚟,所以我哋害怕有乜嘢用?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但無論如何他們白天不來,所以我們害怕有什麼用?」

passages.original: “Well, all right.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,好吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,好吧。

passages.original: We’ll tackle the ha’nted house if you say so—but I reckon it’s taking chances.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你講,我哋就試鬧鬼嘅房子——但我想係喺冒險。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你說,我們就試鬧鬼的房子——但我想是在冒險。」

passages.original: They had started down the hill by this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣佢哋已經開始下山。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時他們已經開始下山。

passages.original: There in the middle of the moonlit valley below them stood the “ha’nted” house, utterly isolated, its fences gone long ago, rank weeds smothering the very doorsteps, the chimney crumbled to ruin, the window-sashes vacant, a corner of the roof caved in.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢哋下面月光照耀嘅山谷中間,站住嗰所「鬧鬼」嘅房子,完全孤立,佢嘅籬笆早已唔見,茂盛嘅野草淹沒咗門階,煙囪倒塌成廢墟,窗框空住,屋頂一角塌陷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他們下面月光照耀的山谷中間,站著那所「鬧鬼」的房子,完全孤立,它的籬笆早已不見,茂盛的野草淹沒了門階,煙囪倒塌成廢墟,窗框空著,屋頂一角塌陷。

passages.original: The boys gazed awhile, half expecting to see a blue light flit past a window; then talking in a low tone, as befitted the time and the circumstances, they struck far off to the right, to give the haunted house a wide berth, and took their way homeward through the woods that adorned the rearward side of Cardiff Hill.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋凝視咗一會兒,半期待睇到一盞藍燈從窗邊閃過;然後用低聲講話,同時間同情況相稱,佢哋向右遠遠走開,繞過鬧鬼嘅房子,經過卡迪夫山後面嘅樹林走回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們凝視了一會兒,半期待看到一盞藍燈從窗邊閃過;然後用低聲說話,與時間和情況相稱,他們向右遠遠走開,繞過鬧鬼的房子,經過卡迪夫山後面的樹林走回家。

chapters.title: Chapter XXVI: The Haunted House 第二十六章:鬧鬼的房子

passages.original: CH About noon the next day the boys arrived at the dead tree; they had come for their tools.
passages.vernacular: 第二天大約中午,男孩哋到咗死樹嗰度;佢哋係嚟取工具嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天大約中午,男孩們到了死樹那裡;他們是來取工具的。

passages.original: Tom was impatient to go to the haunted house; Huck was measurably so, also—but suddenly said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆急住去鬧鬼嘅房子;哈克都喺相當程度上如此——但突然講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆急著去鬧鬼的房子;哈克也在相當程度上如此——但突然說:

passages.original: “Lookyhere, Tom, do you know what day it is?”
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,湯姆,你知道今日係星期幾嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,湯姆,你知道今天是星期幾嗎?」

passages.original: Tom mentally ran over the days of the week, and then quickly lifted his eyes with a startled look in them—
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喺心裡數咗一遍一週嘅日子,然後迅速抬起眼睛,眼裡帶住驚嚇——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆在心裡數了一遍一週的日子,然後迅速抬起眼睛,眼裡帶著驚嚇——

passages.original: “My!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!

passages.original: I never once thought of it, Huck!”
passages.vernacular: 我一次都冇想到,哈克!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一次也沒想到,哈克!」

passages.original: “Well, I didn’t neither, but all at once it popped onto me that it was Friday.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我都冇,但我突然想起係星期五。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我也沒有,但我突然想起是星期五。」

passages.original: “Blame it, a body can’t be too careful, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「真該死,一個人點小心都不為過,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真該死,一個人怎麼小心都不為過,哈克。

passages.original: We might ’a’ got into an awful scrape, tackling such a thing on a Friday.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺星期五動手做呢種事,可能惹上可怕嘅麻煩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在星期五動手做這種事,可能惹上可怕的麻煩。」

passages.original: “Might!
passages.vernacular: 「可能!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可能!

passages.original: Better say we would!
passages.vernacular: 最好講我哋會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最好說我們會!

passages.original: There’s some lucky days, maybe, but Friday ain’t.”
passages.vernacular: 或者有些日子係吉日,但星期五唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許有些日子是吉日,但星期五不是。」

passages.original: “Any fool knows that.
passages.vernacular: 「任何傻瓜都知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「任何傻瓜都知道。

passages.original: I don’t reckon you was the first that found it out, Huck.”
passages.vernacular: 我不認為你係第一個發現嘅,哈克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不認為你是第一個發現的,哈克。」

passages.original: “Well, I never said I was, did I?
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我從冇講我係,對嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我從沒說我是,對嗎?

passages.original: And Friday ain’t all, neither.
passages.vernacular: 而且不只係星期五。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且不只是星期五。

passages.original: I had a rotten bad dream last night—dreampt about rats.”
passages.vernacular: 我琴晚做咗一個好壞嘅夢——夢到老鼠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我昨晚做了一個非常壞的夢——夢到老鼠。」

passages.original: “No!
passages.vernacular: 「唔會吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會吧!

passages.original: Sure sign of trouble.
passages.vernacular: 麻煩的確定徵兆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麻煩的確定徵兆。

passages.original: Did they fight?”
passages.vernacular: 牠哋打架咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牠們打架了嗎?」

passages.original: “No.”
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有。」

passages.original: “Well, that’s good, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰好,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那好,哈克。

passages.original: When they don’t fight it’s only a sign that there’s trouble around, you know.
passages.vernacular: 牠哋不打架,只係講明附近有麻煩,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牠們不打架,只是說明附近有麻煩,你知道。

passages.original: All we got to do is to look mighty sharp and keep out of it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要做嘅就係好警覺並且避開佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要做的就是非常警覺並且避開它。

passages.original: We’ll drop this thing for today, and play.
passages.vernacular: 我哋今日放棄呢件事,去玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們今天放棄這件事,去玩。

passages.original: Do you know Robin Hood, Huck?”
passages.vernacular: 你知道羅賓漢嗎,哈克?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道羅賓漢嗎,哈克?」

passages.original: “No. Who’s Robin Hood?”
passages.vernacular: 「不。羅賓漢係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不。羅賓漢是誰?」

passages.original: “Why, he was one of the greatest men that was ever in England—and the best.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,佢係英格蘭曾有過嘅最偉大嘅人之一——都係最好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,他是英格蘭曾有過的最偉大的人之一——也是最好的。

passages.original: He was a robber.”
passages.vernacular: 佢係強盜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是強盜。」

passages.original: “Cracky, I wisht I was.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,我真希望我係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,我真希望我是。

passages.original: Who did he rob?”
passages.vernacular: 佢搶邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他搶誰?」

passages.original: “Only sheriffs and bishops and rich people and kings, and such like.
passages.vernacular: 「只搶郡長、主教、有錢人同國王之類。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只搶郡長、主教、有錢人和國王之類。

passages.original: But he never bothered the poor.
passages.vernacular: 但佢從不打擾窮人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他從不打擾窮人。

passages.original: He loved ’em.
passages.vernacular: 佢愛佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他愛他們。

passages.original: He always divided up with ’em perfectly square.”
passages.vernacular: 佢總是同佢哋完全公平地平分。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他總是同他們完全公平地平分。」

passages.original: “Well, he must ’a’ been a brick.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢一定係個好漢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,他一定是個好漢。」

passages.original: “I bet you he was, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「我打賭佢係,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我打賭他是,哈克。

passages.original: Oh, he was the noblest man that ever was.
passages.vernacular: 哦,佢係有史以來最高貴嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,他是有史以來最高貴的人。

passages.original: They ain’t any such men now, I can tell you.
passages.vernacular: 而家冇咁樣嘅人喇,我告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在沒有這樣的人了,我告訴你。

passages.original: He could lick any man in England, with one hand tied behind him; and he could take his yew bow and plug a ten-cent piece every time, a mile and a half.”
passages.vernacular: 佢能把一隻手綁喺背後,打敗英格蘭任何人;佢能攞佢嘅紫杉弓,每次射中一英里半外嘅一枚好硬幣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他能把一隻手綁在背後,打敗英格蘭任何人;他能拿他的紫杉弓,每次射中一英里半外的一枚十分硬幣。」

passages.original: “What’s a yew bow?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢係紫杉弓?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼是紫杉弓?」

passages.original: “I don’t know.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: It’s some kind of a bow, of course.
passages.vernacular: 當然係某種弓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然是某種弓。

passages.original: And if he hit that dime only on the edge he would set down and cry—and curse.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢只射中嗰枚硬幣嘅邊緣,佢會坐下嚟哭——同咒罵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他只射中那枚硬幣的邊緣,他會坐下來哭——和咒罵。

passages.original: But we’ll play Robin Hood—it’s nobby fun.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋嚟玩羅賓漢——呢個係好棒嘅樂趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們來玩羅賓漢——這是很棒的樂趣。

passages.original: I’ll learn you.”
passages.vernacular: 我教你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我教你。」

passages.original: “I’m agreed.”
passages.vernacular: 「我同意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我同意。」

passages.original: So they played Robin Hood all the afternoon, now and then casting a yearning eye down upon the haunted house and passing a remark about the morrow’s prospects and possibilities there.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋整個下午玩羅賓漢,時不時向下投去渴望嘅目光,望向鬧鬼嘅房子,議論聽日喺嗰度嘅前景同可能性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們整個下午玩羅賓漢,時不時向下投去渴望的目光,望向鬧鬼的房子,議論明天在那裡的前景和可能性。

passages.original: As the sun began to sink into the west they took their way homeward athwart the long shadows of the trees and soon were buried from sight in the forests of Cardiff Hill.
passages.vernacular: 太陽開始向西下沉時,佢哋穿過樹嘅長長影子向家走去,不久就消失喺卡迪夫山嘅森林中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽開始向西下沉時,他們穿過樹的長長影子向家走去,不久就消失在卡迪夫山的森林中。

passages.original: On Saturday, shortly after noon, the boys were at the dead tree again.
passages.vernacular: 星期六,中午剛過,男孩哋又到咗死樹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期六,中午剛過,男孩們又到了死樹。

passages.original: They had a smoke and a chat in the shade, and then dug a little in their last hole, not with great hope, but merely because Tom said there were so many cases where people had given up a treasure after getting down within six inches of it, and then somebody else had come along and turned it up with a single thrust of a shovel.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺陰涼處抽咗菸、聊咗天,然後喺佢哋最後嘅洞裡挖咗啲,唔係帶住好大嘅希望,而僅僅因為湯姆講有咁多案例,人哋喺挖到離寶藏只有六英寸時放棄喇,然後有人嚟,一鏟子就把佢翻咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在陰涼處抽了菸、聊了天,然後在他們最後的洞裡挖了一點,不是帶著很大的希望,而僅僅因為湯姆說有那麼多案例,人們在挖到離寶藏只有六英寸時放棄了,然後有人來,一鏟子就把它翻了出來。

passages.original: The thing failed this time, however, so the boys shouldered their tools and went away feeling that they had not trifled with fortune, but had fulfilled all the requirements that belong to the business of treasure-hunting.
passages.vernacular: 不過呢次冇成功,於是男孩哋扛起工具走喇,覺得佢哋冇玩弄命運,而係完成咗尋寶呢一行嘅所有要求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過這次沒有成功,於是男孩們扛起工具走了,覺得他們沒有玩弄命運,而是完成了尋寶這一行的所有要求。

passages.original: When they reached the haunted house there was something so weird and grisly about the dead silence that reigned there under the baking sun, and something so depressing about the loneliness and desolation of the place, that they were afraid, for a moment, to venture in.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋到咗鬧鬼嘅房子時,嗰度喺烈日烘烤下統治住嘅死寂有種如此怪異可怕嘅嘢,嗰個地方嘅孤獨同荒涼有種如此令人沮喪嘅嘢,佢哋一時害怕唔敢進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們到了鬧鬼的房子時,那裡在烈日烘烤下統治著的死寂有種如此怪異可怕的東西,那個地方的孤獨和荒涼有種如此令人沮喪的東西,他們一時害怕不敢進去。

passages.original: Then they crept to the door and took a trembling peep.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋爬到門口,顫抖住偷睇咗一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們爬到門口,顫抖著偷看了一眼。

passages.original: They saw a weedgrown, floorless room, unplastered, an ancient fireplace, vacant windows, a ruinous staircase; and here, there, and everywhere hung ragged and abandoned cobwebs.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋睇到一個長滿野草、冇地板、冇抹灰嘅房間,一個古老嘅壁爐,空蕩蕩嘅窗子,一座破敗嘅樓梯;破爛被遺棄嘅蜘蛛網到處懸掛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們看到一個長滿野草、沒有地板、沒有抹灰的房間,一個古老的壁爐,空蕩蕩的窗子,一座破敗的樓梯;破爛被遺棄的蜘蛛網到處懸掛。

passages.original: They presently entered, softly, with quickened pulses, talking in whispers, ears alert to catch the slightest sound, and muscles tense and ready for instant retreat.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋輕輕走進去,脈搏加快,低聲講話,耳朵警覺地捕捉最輕微嘅聲音,肌肉緊張,隨時準備立即後退。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們輕輕走進去,脈搏加快,低聲說話,耳朵警覺地捕捉最輕微的聲音,肌肉緊張,隨時準備立即後退。

passages.original: In a little while familiarity modified their fears and they gave the place a critical and interested examination, rather admiring their own boldness, and wondering at it, too.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,熟悉感減輕咗佢哋嘅恐懼,佢哋對呢個地方進行批判性嘅有興趣嘅檢查,頗為欽佩自己嘅大膽,都對此感到驚奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,熟悉感減輕了他們的恐懼,他們對這個地方進行批判性的有興趣的檢查,頗為欽佩自己的大膽,也對此感到驚奇。

passages.original: Next they wanted to look upstairs.
passages.vernacular: 接住佢哋想睇樓上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著他們想看樓上。

passages.original: This was something like cutting off retreat, but they got to daring each other, and of course there could be but one result—they threw their tools into a corner and made the ascent.
passages.vernacular: 呢有點像切斷退路,但佢哋開始互相挑戰,當然結果只有一個——佢哋把工具扔喺角落,上咗樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這有點像切斷退路,但他們開始互相挑戰,當然結果只有一個——他們把工具扔在角落,上了樓。

passages.original: Up there were the same signs of decay.
passages.vernacular: 上面有同樣嘅腐朽跡象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面有同樣的腐朽跡象。

passages.original: In one corner they found a closet that promised mystery, but the promise was a fraud—there was nothing in it.
passages.vernacular: 喺一個角落佢哋發現一個承諾神祕嘅櫃子,但呢個承諾係騙人嘅——裡面乜嘢都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一個角落他們發現一個承諾神祕的櫃子,但這個承諾是騙人的——裡面什麼也沒有。

passages.original: Their courage was up now and well in hand.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅勇氣而家升起,並且掌握得好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們的勇氣現在升起,並且掌握得很好。

passages.original: They were about to go down and begin work when—
passages.vernacular: 佢哋正要下去開始工作時——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們正要下去開始工作時——

passages.original: “Sh!” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「噓!」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「噓!」湯姆說。

passages.original: “What is it?” whispered Huck, blanching with fright.
passages.vernacular: 「點喇?」哈克低聲講,嚇得臉色發白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了?」哈克低聲說,嚇得臉色發白。

passages.original: There!...
passages.vernacular: 嗰度!……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡!……

passages.original: Hear it?”
passages.vernacular: 聽到咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到了嗎?」

passages.vernacular: 「聽到喇!……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽到了!……

passages.original: Oh, my!
passages.vernacular: 天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!

passages.original: Let’s run!”
passages.vernacular: 我哋跑吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們跑吧!」

passages.original: “Keep still!
passages.vernacular: 「別出聲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別出聲!

passages.original: Don’t you budge!
passages.vernacular: 別動!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別動!

passages.original: They’re coming right toward the door.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋正朝門走嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們正朝門走來。」

passages.original: The boys stretched themselves upon the floor with their eyes to knotholes in the planking, and lay waiting, in a misery of fear.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋喺地板上伸展身體,眼睛貼喺木板嘅節孔上,躺住等待,喺恐懼嘅痛苦中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們在地板上伸展身體,眼睛貼在木板的節孔上,躺著等待,在恐懼的痛苦中。

passages.original: “They’ve stopped....
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋停喇……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們停了……

passages.original: No—coming....
passages.vernacular: 不——嚟喇……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不——來了……

passages.original: Here they are.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們來了。

passages.original: Don’t whisper another word, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再低聲講一個字,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再低聲說一個字,哈克。

passages.original: My goodness, I wish I was out of this!”
passages.vernacular: 天呀,我希望我不喺呢度!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,我希望我不在這裡!」

passages.original: Two men entered.
passages.vernacular: 兩個男人走咗進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個男人走了進來。

passages.original: Each boy said to himself: “There’s the old deaf and dumb Spaniard that’s been about town once or twice lately—never saw t’other man before.”
passages.vernacular: 每個男孩對自己講:「嗰個係最近喺鎮上出現過一兩次嘅老聾啞西班牙人——另一個人以前從冇見過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個男孩對自己說:「那是最近在鎮上出現過一兩次的老聾啞西班牙人——另一個人以前從沒見過。」

passages.original: “T’other” was a ragged, unkempt creature, with nothing very pleasant in his face.
passages.vernacular: 「另一個」係一個衣衫襤褸、頭髮蓬亂嘅傢伙,臉上冇任何令人愉快嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「另一個」是一個衣衫襤褸、頭髮蓬亂的傢伙,臉上沒有任何令人愉快的東西。

passages.original: The Spaniard was wrapped in a serape; he had bushy white whiskers; long white hair flowed from under his sombrero, and he wore green goggles.
passages.vernacular: 西班牙人裹住一件披肩;佢有濃密嘅白鬍鬚;長長嘅白頭髮從佢嘅寬邊帽下流出嚟,佢戴住綠色嘅護目鏡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 西班牙人裹著一件披肩;他有濃密的白鬍鬚;長長的白頭髮從他的寬邊帽下流出來,他戴著綠色的護目鏡。

passages.original: When they came in, “t’other” was talking in a low voice; they sat down on the ground, facing the door, with their backs to the wall, and the speaker continued his remarks.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋進嚟時,「另一個」正在低聲講話;佢哋面對住門,背靠住牆,坐喺地上,講話嘅人繼續佢嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們進來時,「另一個」正在低聲說話;他們面對著門,背靠著牆,坐在地上,說話的人繼續他的話。

passages.original: His manner became less guarded and his words more distinct as he proceeded:
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅態度變得不咁謹慎,講話越講越清楚:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的態度變得不那麼謹慎,說話越說越清楚:

passages.original: “No,” said he, “I’ve thought it all over, and I don’t like it.
passages.vernacular: 「不,」佢講,「我全想過喇,我不鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」他說,「我全想過了,我不喜歡。

passages.original: It’s dangerous.”
passages.vernacular: 好危險。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很危險。」

passages.original: “Dangerous!” grunted the “deaf and dumb” Spaniard—to the vast surprise of the boys.
passages.vernacular: 「危險!」「聾啞」西班牙人咕噥住——令男孩哋大為食驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「危險!」「聾啞」西班牙人咕噥著——令男孩們大為吃驚。

passages.original: “Milksop!”
passages.vernacular: 「膽小鬼!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「膽小鬼!」

passages.original: This voice made the boys gasp and quake.
passages.vernacular: 呢個聲音使男孩哋倒抽一口氣,發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個聲音使男孩們倒抽一口氣,發抖。

passages.original: It was Injun Joe’s!
passages.vernacular: 係印第安喬嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是印第安喬的!

passages.original: There was silence for some time.
passages.vernacular: 有一陣子冇聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一陣子沒有聲音。

passages.original: Then Joe said:
passages.vernacular: 然後喬講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後喬說:

passages.original: “What’s any more dangerous than that job up yonder—but nothing’s come of it.”
passages.vernacular: 「仲有乜嘢比上面嗰件工作更危險——但乜嘢都冇發生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還有什麼比上面那件工作更危險——但什麼也沒有發生。」

passages.original: “That’s different.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰不同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那不同。

passages.original: Away up the river so, and not another house about. ’Twon’t ever be known that we tried, anyway, long as we didn’t succeed.”
passages.vernacular: 遠喺河上游,附近冇別嘅房子。至少只要我哋冇成功,就永遠唔會有人知道我哋試過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠在河上游,附近沒有別的房子。至少只要我們沒成功,就永遠不會有人知道我們試過。」

passages.original: “Well, what’s more dangerous than coming here in the daytime!—anybody would suspicion us that saw us.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,有乜嘢比白天嚟呢度更危險!——任何睇到我哋嘅人都會懷疑我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,有什麼比白天來這裡更危險!——任何看到我們的人都會懷疑我們。」

passages.original: “I know that.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。

passages.original: But there warn’t any other place as handy after that fool of a job.
passages.vernacular: 但喺嗰件蠢事之後,冇其他地方咁方便。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在那件蠢事之後,沒有其他地方這麼方便。

passages.original: I want to quit this shanty.
passages.vernacular: 我想離開呢間破屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想離開這間破屋。

passages.original: I wanted to yesterday, only it warn’t any use trying to stir out of here, with those infernal boys playing over there on the hill right in full view.”
passages.vernacular: 我尋日就想,只係試圖離開呢度冇用,嗰啲該死嘅男孩喺嗰邊山上玩,一覽無遺。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我昨天就想,只是試圖離開這裡沒有用,那些該死的男孩在那邊山上玩,一覽無遺。」

passages.original: “Those infernal boys” quaked again under the inspiration of this remark, and thought how lucky it was that they had remembered it was Friday and concluded to wait a day.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰啲該死嘅男孩」喺呢句話嘅啟發下又發抖,想到佢哋記起嗰個係星期五,決定等一天,係幾咁幸運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那些該死的男孩」在這句話的啟發下又發抖,想到他們記起那是星期五,決定等一天,是多麼幸運。

passages.original: They wished in their hearts they had waited a year.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋心裡希望佢哋等一年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們心裡希望他們等一年。

passages.original: The two men got out some food and made a luncheon.
passages.vernacular: 兩個男人攞出啲食物,食咗午飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個男人拿出一些食物,吃了午飯。

passages.original: After a long and thoughtful silence, Injun Joe said:
passages.vernacular: 經過長時間嘅深思嘅沉默,印第安喬講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過長時間的深思的沉默,印第安喬說:

passages.original: “Look here, lad—you go back up the river where you belong.
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,小子——你回河上游你屬於嘅地方去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,小子——你回河上游你屬於的地方去。

passages.original: Wait there till you hear from me.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰度等我嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那裡等我的消息。

passages.original: I’ll take the chances on dropping into this town just once more, for a look.
passages.vernacular: 我再冒一次險嚟呢個鎮上,睇睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我再冒一次險來這個鎮上,看看。

passages.original: We’ll do that ‘dangerous’ job after I’ve spied around a little and think things look well for it.
passages.vernacular: 等我四處偵察咗一下,認為情況對嗰個『危險』工作有利後,我哋就做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我四處偵察了一下,認為情況對那個『危險』工作有利後,我們就做。

passages.original: Then for Texas!
passages.vernacular: 然後去德克薩斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後去德克薩斯!

passages.original: We’ll leg it together!”
passages.vernacular: 我哋一起走!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一起走!」

passages.original: This was satisfactory.
passages.vernacular: 呢令人滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這令人滿意。

passages.original: Both men presently fell to yawning, and Injun Joe said:
passages.vernacular: 兩個人不久都開始打呵欠,印第安喬講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個人不久都開始打呵欠,印第安喬說:

passages.original: “I’m dead for sleep!
passages.vernacular: 「我睏死喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我睏死了!

passages.original: It’s your turn to watch.”
passages.vernacular: 輪到你守望。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輪到你守望。」

passages.original: He curled down in the weeds and soon began to snore.
passages.vernacular: 佢蜷縮喺雜草中,好快開始打鼾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他蜷縮在雜草中,很快開始打鼾。

passages.original: His comrade stirred him once or twice and he became quiet.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅同伴推咗佢一兩次,佢安靜喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的同伴推了他一兩次,他安靜了。

passages.original: Presently the watcher began to nod; his head drooped lower and lower, both men began to snore now.
passages.vernacular: 不久守望者開始點頭;佢嘅頭越垂越低,兩個人而家都開始打鼾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久守望者開始點頭;他的頭越垂越低,兩個人現在都開始打鼾。

passages.original: The boys drew a long, grateful breath.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋感激地吸咗一口長氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們感激地吸了一口長氣。

passages.original: Tom whispered:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆低聲說:

passages.original: “Now’s our chance—come!”
passages.vernacular: 「而家係我哋嘅機會——嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在是我們的機會——來!」

passages.original: Huck said:
passages.vernacular: 哈克講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克說:

passages.original: “I can’t—I’d die if they was to wake.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠——如果佢哋醒嚟我會死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能——如果他們醒來我會死。」

passages.original: Tom urged—Huck held back.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆催促——哈克退縮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆催促——哈克退縮。

passages.original: At last Tom rose slowly and softly, and started alone.
passages.vernacular: 最後湯姆慢慢輕輕地站起嚟,獨自出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後湯姆慢慢輕輕地站起來,獨自出發。

passages.original: But the first step he made wrung such a hideous creak from the crazy floor that he sank down almost dead with fright.
passages.vernacular: 但佢邁出第一步,瘋狂嘅地板就發出咁可怕嘅吱嘎聲,佢嚇得幾乎半死地癱倒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他邁出第一步,瘋狂的地板就發出那麼可怕的吱嘎聲,他嚇得幾乎半死地癱倒。

passages.original: He never made a second attempt.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇再做第二次嘗試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有再做第二次嘗試。

passages.original: The boys lay there counting the dragging moments till it seemed to them that time must be done and eternity growing gray; and then they were grateful to note that at last the sun was setting.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋躺喺嗰度數住拖長嘅時刻,直到佢哋覺得時間一定完喇,永恆正變灰;然後佢哋感激地注意到太陽終於喺下沉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們躺在那裡數著拖長的時刻,直到他們覺得時間一定完了,永恆正變灰;然後他們感激地注意到太陽終於在下沉。

passages.original: Now one snore ceased.
passages.vernacular: 而家一個鼾聲停喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在一個鼾聲停了。

passages.original: Injun Joe sat up, stared around—smiled grimly upon his comrade, whose head was drooping upon his knees—stirred him up with his foot and said:
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬坐起嚟,環顧四周——冷酷地對佢嘅同伴微笑,同伴嘅頭垂喺膝蓋上——用腳踢醒佢,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬坐起來,環顧四周——冷酷地對他的同伴微笑,同伴的頭垂在膝蓋上——用腳踢醒他,說:

passages.original: “Here!
You’re a watchman, ain’t you!
passages.vernacular: 你係個守望嘅,對吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是個守望的,對吧!

passages.original: All right, though—nothing’s happened.”
passages.vernacular: 不過,好吧——乜嘢都冇發生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,好吧——什麼也沒發生。」

passages.original: “My! have I been asleep?”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!我瞓住咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!我睡著了嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, partly, partly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,有點,有點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,有點,有點。

passages.original: Nearly time for us to be moving, pard.
passages.vernacular: 我哋差不多該動身喇,夥計。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們差不多該動身了,夥計。

passages.original: What’ll we do with what little swag we’ve got left?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋剩下嘅呢點贓物點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們剩下的這點贓物怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “I don’t know—leave it here as we’ve always done, I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道——我想像我哋一直做嘅嗰樣留喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道——我想像我們一直做的那樣留在這裡。

passages.original: No use to take it away till we start south.
passages.vernacular: 喺我哋往南出發之前,攞走佢冇好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我們往南出發之前,拿走它沒好處。

passages.original: Six hundred and fifty in silver’s something to carry.”
passages.vernacular: 六百五十塊銀幣係要帶嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六百五十塊銀幣是要帶的東西。」

passages.original: “Well—all right—it won’t matter to come here once more.”
passages.vernacular: 「好——好吧——再嚟呢度一次冇關係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好——好吧——再來這裡一次沒關係。」

passages.original: “No—but I’d say come in the night as we used to do—it’s better.”
passages.vernacular: 「不——但我講夜裡嚟,像我哋以前嗰樣——更好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——但我說夜裡來,像我們以前那樣——更好。」

passages.original: “Yes: but look here; it may be a good while before I get the right chance at that job; accidents might happen; ’tain’t in such a very good place; we’ll just regularly bury it—and bury it deep.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅:但聽住;我可能要過好久才能對嗰工作有適當嘅機會;可能發生意外;呢個地方不太好;我哋就正式埋起嚟——埋深啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的:但聽著;我可能要過很久才能對那工作有適當的機會;可能發生意外;這個地方不太好;我們就正式埋起來——埋深一點。」

passages.original: “Good idea,” said the comrade, who walked across the room, knelt down, raised one of the rearward hearth-stones and took out a bag that jingled pleasantly.
passages.vernacular: 「好主意,」同伴講,佢走過房間,跪下,抬起後面嘅一塊壁爐石,取出一個叮噹作響好悅耳嘅袋子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好主意,」同伴說,他走過房間,跪下,抬起後面的一塊壁爐石,取出一個叮噹作響很悅耳的袋子。

passages.original: He subtracted from it twenty or thirty dollars for himself and as much for Injun Joe, and passed the bag to the latter, who was on his knees in the corner, now, digging with his bowie-knife.
passages.vernacular: 佢從中畀自己攞咗二三十塊,畀印第安喬都同樣多,把袋子遞畀後者,佢而家跪喺角落裡,正用佢嘅鮑伊刀喺挖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從中給自己拿了二三十塊,給印第安喬也同樣多,把袋子遞給後者,他現在跪在角落裡,正用他的鮑伊刀在挖。

passages.original: The boys forgot all their fears, all their miseries in an instant.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋一瞬間忘咗佢哋所有嘅恐懼、所有嘅痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們一瞬間忘了他們所有的恐懼、所有的痛苦。

passages.original: With gloating eyes they watched every movement.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋用貪婪嘅眼睛睇住每個動作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們用貪婪的眼睛看著每個動作。

passages.original: Luck!—the splendor of it was beyond all imagination!
passages.vernacular: 運氣!——佢嘅輝煌超出一切想像!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 運氣!——它的輝煌超出一切想像!

passages.original: Six hundred dollars was money enough to make half a dozen boys rich!
passages.vernacular: 六百塊錢足夠使半打男孩富有!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六百塊錢足夠使半打男孩富有!

passages.original: Here was treasure-hunting under the happiest auspices—there would not be any bothersome uncertainty as to where to dig.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係喺最幸運嘅徵兆下嘅尋寶——冇關於喺邊度挖嘅討厭嘅不確定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是在最幸運的徵兆下的尋寶——沒有關於在哪裡挖的討厭的不確定。

passages.original: They nudged each other every moment—eloquent nudges and easily understood, for they simply meant—“Oh, but ain’t you glad now we’re here!”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋每一刻都互相推撞——雄辯而容易理解嘅推撞,因為佢哋簡單嘅意思係——「哦,我哋喺呢度你不高興嗎!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們每一刻都互相推撞——雄辯而容易理解的推撞,因為它們簡單的意思是——「哦,我們在這裡你不高興嗎!」

passages.original: Joe’s knife struck upon something.
passages.vernacular: 喬嘅刀碰到咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬的刀碰到了什麼。

passages.original: “Hello!” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「喂!」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂!」他說。

passages.original: “What is it?” said his comrade.
passages.vernacular: 「係乜嘢?」佢嘅同伴講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是什麼?」他的同伴說。

passages.original: “Half-rotten plank—no, it’s a box, I believe.
passages.vernacular: 「半腐爛嘅木板——不,我相信係個箱子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「半腐爛的木板——不,我相信是個箱子。

passages.original: Here—bear a hand and we’ll see what it’s here for.
passages.vernacular: 嚟——搭把手,我哋睇睇佢喺呢度係幹乜嘢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來——搭把手,我們看看它在這裡是幹什麼的。

passages.original: Never mind, I’ve broke a hole.”
passages.vernacular: 算喇,我弄出一個洞喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 算了,我弄出一個洞了。」

passages.original: He reached his hand in and drew it out—
passages.vernacular: 佢伸手進去,拉出嚟——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他伸手進去,拉出來——

passages.original: “Man, it’s money!”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,係錢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,是錢!」

passages.original: The two men examined the handful of coins.
passages.vernacular: 兩個人檢查嗰一把硬幣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個人檢查那一把硬幣。

passages.original: They were gold.
passages.vernacular: 係金幣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是金幣。

passages.original: The boys above were as excited as themselves, and as delighted.
passages.vernacular: 上面嘅男孩哋同佢哋一樣興奮,一樣高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面的男孩們和他們一樣興奮,一樣高興。

passages.original: Joe’s comrade said:
passages.vernacular: 喬嘅同伴講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬的同伴說:

passages.original: “We’ll make quick work of this.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋好快就能搞定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們很快就能搞定。

passages.original: There’s an old rusty pick over amongst the weeds in the corner the other side of the fireplace—I saw it a minute ago.”
passages.vernacular: 壁爐另一邊角落雜草中有一把舊鏽鎬——我頭先睇見。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 壁爐另一邊角落雜草中有一把舊鏽鎬——我剛才看見。」

passages.original: He ran and brought the boys’ pick and shovel.
passages.vernacular: 佢跑去把男孩哋嘅鎬同鏟子攞嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他跑去把男孩們的鎬和鏟子拿來。

passages.original: Injun Joe took the pick, looked it over critically, shook his head, muttered something to himself, and then began to use it.
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬攞起鎬,批判性地查睇,搖搖頭,對自己嘀咕咗點乜嘢,然後開始使用佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬拿起鎬,批判性地查看,搖搖頭,對自己嘀咕了點什麼,然後開始使用它。

passages.original: The box was soon unearthed.
passages.vernacular: 箱子好快被挖咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 箱子很快被挖了出來。

passages.original: It was not very large; it was iron bound and had been very strong before the slow years had injured it.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係好大;包住鐵,喺緩慢嘅歲月損壞佢之前一定好堅固。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它不是很大;包著鐵,在緩慢的歲月損壞它之前一定非常堅固。

passages.original: The men contemplated the treasure awhile in blissful silence.
passages.vernacular: 兩個人喺幸福嘅沉默中凝視咗寶藏一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個人在幸福的沉默中凝視了寶藏一會兒。

passages.original: “Pard, there’s thousands of dollars here,” said Injun Joe.
passages.vernacular: 「夥計,呢度有幾千塊錢,」印第安喬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夥計,這裡有幾千塊錢,」印第安喬說。

passages.original: “’Twas always said that Murrel’s gang used to be around here one summer,” the stranger observed.
passages.vernacular: 「一直有人講默雷爾嘅幫派曾經有一個夏天喺呢附近,」陌生人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一直有人說默雷爾的幫派曾經有一個夏天在這附近,」陌生人說。

passages.original: “I know it,” said Injun Joe; “and this looks like it, I should say.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,」印第安喬講;「我應該講呢個睇起嚟像係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,」印第安喬說;「我應該說這看起來像是。」

passages.original: “Now you won’t need to do that job.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家你不需要做嗰件工作喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你不需要做那件工作了。」

passages.original: The halfbreed frowned.
passages.vernacular: 混血兒皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 混血兒皺眉。

passages.original: Said he:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “You don’t know me.
passages.vernacular: 「你不了解我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不了解我。

passages.original: Least you don’t know all about that thing. ’Tain’t robbery altogether—it’s revenge!” and a wicked light flamed in his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 至少你不了解嗰件事嘅全部。呢不完全係搶劫——呢個係復仇!」佢眼裡燃起一道邪惡嘅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少你不了解那件事的全部。這不完全是搶劫——這是復仇!」他眼裡燃起一道邪惡的光。

passages.original: “I’ll need your help in it.
passages.vernacular: 「我需要你幫忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我需要你幫忙。

passages.original: When it’s finished—then Texas.
passages.vernacular: 完成後——就去德克薩斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 完成後——就去德克薩斯。

passages.original: Go home to your Nance and your kids, and stand by till you hear from me.”
passages.vernacular: 回家去找你嘅南斯同細路哋,等我嘅消息。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回家去找你的南斯和孩子們,等我的消息。」

passages.original: “Well—if you say so; what’ll we do with this—bury it again?”
passages.vernacular: 「好——如果你咁講;我哋點處理呢個——再埋嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好——如果你這麼說;我們怎麼處理這個——再埋嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.
[Ravishing delight overhead.]
passages.vernacular: [頭上欣喜若狂。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [頭上欣喜若狂。]

passages.original: No! by the great Sachem, no!
passages.vernacular: 不!憑偉大嘅酋長,不!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不!憑偉大的酋長,不!

passages.original: [Profound distress overhead.]
passages.vernacular: [頭上深深嘅苦惱。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [頭上深深的苦惱。]

passages.original: I’d nearly forgot.
passages.vernacular: 我差點忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我差點忘了。

passages.original: That pick had fresh earth on it!
passages.vernacular: 嗰把鎬上有新土!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那把鎬上有新土!

passages.original: [The boys were sick with terror in a moment.]
passages.vernacular: [男孩哋轉眼嚇得難受。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [男孩們轉眼嚇得難受。]

passages.original: What business has a pick and a shovel here?
passages.vernacular: 鎬同鏟子喺呢度幹乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鎬和鏟子在這裡幹什麼?

passages.original: What business with fresh earth on them?
passages.vernacular: 上面帶新土幹乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面帶新土幹什麼?
