passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我們有那些壞蛋的某種描述——會有很大幫助。

passages.original: But you couldn’t see what they were like, in the dark, lad, I suppose?”
passages.vernacular: 但你喺黑暗中睇唔到佢哋乜嘢樣,我想,細路?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你在黑暗中看不到他們什麼樣,我想,孩子?」

passages.original: “Oh yes; I saw them downtown and follered them.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,睇得到;我喺鎮上睇到佢哋,並跟住佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,看得到;我在鎮上看到他們,並跟著他們。」

passages.original: “Splendid!
passages.vernacular: 「太好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太好了!

passages.original: Describe them—describe them, my boy!”
passages.vernacular: 描述佢哋——描述佢哋,我嘅細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 描述他們——描述他們,我的孩子!」

passages.original: “One’s the old deaf and dumb Spaniard that’s ben around here once or twice, and t’other’s a mean-looking, ragged—”
passages.vernacular: 「一個係最近喺呢度出現過一兩次嘅老聾啞西班牙人,另一個係個睇起嚟卑鄙、破爛嘅——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個是最近在這裡出現過一兩次的老聾啞西班牙人,另一個是個看起來卑鄙、破爛的——」

passages.original: “That’s enough, lad, we know the men!
passages.vernacular: 「夠喇,細路,我哋認識呢兩個人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夠了,孩子,我們認識這兩個人!

passages.original: Happened on them in the woods back of the widow’s one day, and they slunk away.
passages.vernacular: 有一天喺寡婦後面嘅樹林裡碰到佢哋,佢哋溜走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天在寡婦後面的樹林裡碰到他們,他們溜走了。

passages.original: Off with you, boys, and tell the sheriff—get your breakfast tomorrow morning!”
passages.vernacular: 你哋走吧,細路哋,告訴郡長——聽日早晨再食早餐!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們走吧,孩子們,告訴郡長——明天早晨再吃早餐!」

passages.original: The Welshman’s sons departed at once.
passages.vernacular: 威爾斯人嘅兒子哋即刻離開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威爾斯人的兒子們馬上離開。

passages.original: As they were leaving the room Huck sprang up and exclaimed:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋離開房間時,哈克跳起嚟喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們離開房間時,哈克跳起來喊道:

passages.original: “Oh, please don’t tell anybody it was me that blowed on them!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,求你哋別告訴任何人係我告發咗佢哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,求你們別告訴任何人是我告發了他們!

passages.original: Oh, please!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,求你哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,求你們!」

passages.original: “All right if you say it, Huck, but you ought to have the credit of what you did.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你咁講就好,哈克,但你應該為你所做嘅得到榮譽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你這麼說就好,哈克,但你應該為你所做的得到榮譽。」

passages.original: “Oh no, no!
passages.vernacular: 「哦不,不!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦不,不!

passages.original: Please don’t tell!”
passages.vernacular: 求你唔好講!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 求你別說!」

passages.original: When the young men were gone, the old Welshman said:
passages.vernacular: 年輕人走後,老威爾斯人講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕人走後,老威爾斯人說:

passages.original: “They won’t tell—and I won’t.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋唔會講——我都唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們不會說——我也不會。

passages.original: But why don’t you want it known?”
passages.vernacular: 但你點解唔想讓人知道?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你為什麼不想讓人知道?」

passages.original: Huck would not explain, further than to say that he already knew too much about one of those men and would not have the man know that he knew anything against him for the whole world—he would be killed for knowing it, sure.
passages.vernacular: 哈克唔願解釋,只講佢已經太了解其中一個人,為了全世界都唔想讓嗰人知道佢知道任何對佢不利嘅事——佢肯定會因知道而被殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克不願解釋,只說他已經太了解其中一個人,為了全世界也不想讓那人知道他知道任何對他不利的事——他肯定會因知道而被殺。

passages.original: The old man promised secrecy once more, and said:
passages.vernacular: 老人又一次答應保密,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人又一次答應保密,說:

passages.original: “How did you come to follow these fellows, lad?
passages.vernacular: 「你點會跟蹤呢啲傢伙嘅,細路?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼會跟蹤這些傢伙的,孩子?

passages.original: Were they looking suspicious?”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋睇起嚟可疑嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們看起來可疑嗎?」

passages.original: Huck was silent while he framed a duly cautious reply.
passages.vernacular: 哈克沉默,同時組織一個適當謹慎嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克沉默,同時組織一個適當謹慎的回答。

passages.original: Then he said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他說:

passages.original: “Well, you see, I’m a kind of a hard lot,—least everybody says so, and I don’t see nothing agin it—and sometimes I can’t sleep much, on account of thinking about it and sort of trying to strike out a new way of doing.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你睇,我算係個難纏嘅人——至少人人都咁講,我都睇不出乜嘢不對——有時我瞓不太好,因為想呢個,試圖想出一個新嘅做事方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你看,我算是個難纏的人——至少人人都這麼說,我也看不出什麼不對——有時我睡不太好,因為想這個,試圖想出一個新的做事方式。

passages.original: That was the way of it last night.
passages.vernacular: 琴晚就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨晚就是這樣。

passages.original: I couldn’t sleep, and so I come along upstreet ’bout midnight, a-turning it all over, and when I got to that old shackly brick store by the Temperance Tavern, I backed up agin the wall to have another think.
passages.vernacular: 我瞓不住,所以我大約午夜時走上街,翻嚟覆去地想,走到節制旅店旁嗰間搖搖晃晃嘅舊磚店時,我靠喺牆上再想一想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我睡不著,所以我大約午夜時走上街,翻來覆去地想,走到節制旅店旁那間搖搖晃晃的舊磚店時,我靠在牆上再想一想。

passages.original: Well, just then along comes these two chaps slipping along close by me, with something under their arm, and I reckoned they’d stole it.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,就喺嗰時,呢兩個傢伙貼近我悄悄走過,胳膊下夾住嘢,我想佢哋係偷嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,就在那時,這兩個傢伙貼近我悄悄走過,胳膊下夾著東西,我想他們是偷的。

passages.original: One was a-smoking, and t’other one wanted a light; so they stopped right before me and the cigars lit up their faces and I see that the big one was the deaf and dumb Spaniard, by his white whiskers and the patch on his eye, and t’other one was a rusty, ragged-looking devil.”
passages.vernacular: 一個喺抽菸,另一個要火;所以佢哋就停喺我面前,雪茄照亮咗佢哋嘅臉,我睇到嗰個大個子係聾啞西班牙人,憑佢嘅白鬍鬚同眼上嘅眼罩,另一個係個鏽跡斑斑、衣衫襤褸嘅魔鬼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個在抽菸,另一個要火;所以他們就停在我面前,雪茄照亮了他們的臉,我看到那個大個子是聾啞西班牙人,憑他的白鬍鬚和眼上的眼罩,另一個是個鏽跡斑斑、衣衫襤褸的魔鬼。」

passages.original: “Could you see the rags by the light of the cigars?”
passages.vernacular: 「你能借住雪茄嘅光睇到破爛衣服嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你能借著雪茄的光看到破爛衣服嗎?」

passages.original: This staggered Huck for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 呢使哈克一時語塞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使哈克一時語塞。

passages.original: Then he said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他說:

passages.original: “Well, I don’t know—but somehow it seems as if I did.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道——但唔知點好像我睇到喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道——但不知怎麼好像我看到了。」

passages.original: “Then they went on, and you—”
passages.vernacular: 「然後佢哋繼續走,你——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後他們繼續走,你——」

passages.original: “Follered ’em—yes.
passages.vernacular: 「跟住佢哋——係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「跟著他們——是的。

passages.original: That was it.
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣。

passages.original: I wanted to see what was up—they sneaked along so.
passages.vernacular: 我想睇睇出咗乜嘢事——佢哋鬼鬼祟祟地走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想看看出了什麼事——他們鬼鬼祟祟地走。

passages.original: I dogged ’em to the widder’s stile, and stood in the dark and heard the ragged one beg for the widder, and the Spaniard swear he’d spile her looks just as I told you and your two—”
passages.vernacular: 我跟佢哋到寡婦嘅踏階,站喺黑暗中聽到嗰個破爛嘅求寡婦,而西班牙人發誓佢要毀佢嘅容貌,就像我告訴你同你兩個——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟他們到寡婦的踏階,站在黑暗中聽到那個破爛的求寡婦,而西班牙人發誓他要毀她的容貌,就像我告訴你和你兩個——」

passages.original: “What!
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼!

passages.original: The deaf and dumb man said all that!”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個聾啞人講咗所有呢啲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個聾啞人說了所有這些!」

passages.original: Huck had made another terrible mistake!
passages.vernacular: 哈克又犯咗一個可怕嘅錯誤!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克又犯了一個可怕的錯誤!

passages.original: He was trying his best to keep the old man from getting the faintest hint of who the Spaniard might be, and yet his tongue seemed determined to get him into trouble in spite of all he could do.
passages.vernacular: 佢拼命努力不讓老人得到關於西班牙人可能係邊個嘅絲毫暗示,然而佢嘅舌頭似乎決心不管佢點做都要讓佢惹麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他拼命努力不讓老人得到關於西班牙人可能是誰的絲毫暗示,然而他的舌頭似乎決心不管他怎麼做都要讓他惹麻煩。

passages.original: He made several efforts to creep out of his scrape, but the old man’s eye was upon him and he made blunder after blunder.
passages.vernacular: 佢幾次努力從窘境中爬出嚟,但老人嘅眼睛盯住佢,佢犯咗一個又一個錯誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他幾次努力從窘境中爬出來,但老人的眼睛盯著他,他犯了一個又一個錯誤。

passages.original: Presently the Welshman said:
passages.vernacular: 不久威爾斯人講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久威爾斯人說:

passages.original: “My boy, don’t be afraid of me.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅細路,唔好怕我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的孩子,不要怕我。

passages.original: I wouldn’t hurt a hair of your head for all the world.
passages.vernacular: 我為了全世界都唔會傷你一根頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為了全世界也不會傷你一根頭髮。

passages.original: No—I’d protect you—I’d protect you.
passages.vernacular: 不——我會保護你——我會保護你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不——我會保護你——我會保護你。

passages.original: This Spaniard is not deaf and dumb; you’ve let that slip without intending it; you can’t cover that up now.
passages.vernacular: 呢個西班牙人唔係聾啞人;你無意中講漏喇;你而家遮不住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個西班牙人不是聾啞人;你無意中說漏了;你現在遮不住了。

passages.original: You know something about that Spaniard that you want to keep dark.
passages.vernacular: 你知道關於嗰個西班牙人嘅啲事,你想保密。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道關於那個西班牙人的一些事,你想保密。

passages.original: Now trust me—tell me what it is, and trust me—I won’t betray you.”
passages.vernacular: 而家信任我——告訴我係乜嘢,信任我——我唔會出賣你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在信任我——告訴我是什麼,信任我——我不會出賣你。」

passages.original: Huck looked into the old man’s honest eyes a moment, then bent over and whispered in his ear:
passages.vernacular: 哈克睇進老人誠實嘅眼睛一會兒,然後俯身喺佢耳邊低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克看進老人誠實的眼睛一會兒,然後俯身在他耳邊低聲說:

passages.original: “’Tain’t a Spaniard—it’s Injun Joe!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢唔係西班牙人——係印第安喬!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他不是西班牙人——是印第安喬!」

passages.original: The Welshman almost jumped out of his chair.
passages.vernacular: 威爾斯人幾乎從椅子上跳起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威爾斯人幾乎從椅子上跳起來。

passages.original: In a moment he said:
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒他說:

passages.original: “It’s all plain enough, now.
passages.vernacular: 「而家一切都好清楚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在一切都很清楚了。

passages.original: When you talked about notching ears and slitting noses I judged that that was your own embellishment, because white men don’t take that sort of revenge.
passages.vernacular: 你講到割耳朵同劃開鼻子時,我以為嗰個係你自己嘅潤色,因為白人唔會採取嗰種報復。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說到割耳朵和劃開鼻子時,我以為那是你自己的潤色,因為白人不會採取那種報復。

passages.original: But an Injun!
passages.vernacular: 但係印第安人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是印第安人!

passages.original: That’s a different matter altogether.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰完全係另一回事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那完全是另一回事。」

passages.original: During breakfast the talk went on, and in the course of it the old man said that the last thing which he and his sons had done, before going to bed, was to get a lantern and examine the stile and its vicinity for marks of blood.
passages.vernacular: 早餐時談話繼續,談話中老人講,佢同佢兒子哋瞓覺前做嘅最後一件事,係攞燈籠檢查踏階及其附近有冇血跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐時談話繼續,談話中老人說,他和他兒子們睡覺前做的最後一件事,是拿燈籠檢查踏階及其附近有沒有血跡。

passages.original: They found none, but captured a bulky bundle of—
passages.vernacular: 佢哋冇找到,但繳獲咗一個沉重嘅包裹,裡面有——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沒有找到,但繳獲了一個沉重的包裹,裡面有——

passages.original: “Of what?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼?」

passages.original: If the words had been lightning they could not have leaped with a more stunning suddenness from Huck’s blanched lips.
passages.vernacular: 如果呢啲話係閃電,佢哋唔可能以更令人震驚嘅突然性從哈克發白嘅嘴唇跳出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果這些話是閃電,它們不可能以更令人震驚的突然性從哈克發白的嘴唇跳出來。

passages.original: His eyes were staring wide, now, and his breath suspended—waiting for the answer.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛而家睜得好大,呼吸停止——等待答案。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的眼睛現在睜得很大,呼吸停止——等待答案。

passages.original: The Welshman started—stared in return—three seconds—five seconds—ten—then replied:
passages.vernacular: 威爾斯人一怔——瞪住回睇——三秒——五秒——十秒——然後回答:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威爾斯人一怔——瞪著回看——三秒——五秒——十秒——然後回答:

passages.original: “Of burglar’s tools.
passages.vernacular: 「竊賊嘅工具。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「竊賊的工具。

passages.original: Why, what’s the matter with you?”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,你點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,你怎麼了?」

passages.original: Huck sank back, panting gently, but deeply, unutterably grateful.
passages.vernacular: 哈克向後倒下,輕輕而深深地喘息,講不出嘅感激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克向後倒下,輕輕而深深地喘息,說不出的感激。

passages.original: The Welshman eyed him gravely, curiously—and presently said:
passages.vernacular: 威爾斯人嚴肅好奇地睇住佢——不久講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威爾斯人嚴肅好奇地看著他——不久說:

passages.original: “Yes, burglar’s tools.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,竊賊嘅工具。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,竊賊的工具。

passages.original: That appears to relieve you a good deal.
passages.vernacular: 呢似乎使你大大放心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這似乎使你大大放心。

passages.original: But what did give you that turn?
passages.vernacular: 但係乜嘢使你有嗰一驚?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是什麼使你有那一驚?

passages.original: What were you expecting we’d found?”
passages.vernacular: 你期望我哋發現咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你期望我們發現了什麼?」

passages.original: Huck was in a close place—the inquiring eye was upon him—he would have given anything for material for a plausible answer—nothing suggested itself—the inquiring eye was boring deeper and deeper—a senseless reply offered—there was no time to weigh it, so at a venture he uttered it—feebly:
passages.vernacular: 哈克處喺窘境——詢問嘅眼睛盯住佢——佢願意付出任何嘢得到一個似係而非嘅答案嘅材料——乜嘢都冇想到——詢問嘅眼睛越鑽越深——提出咗一個無意義嘅回答——冇時間權衡,所以佢冒險講咗出嚟——虛弱地:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克處在窘境——詢問的眼睛盯著他——他願意付出任何東西得到一個似是而非的答案的材料——什麼也沒想到——詢問的眼睛越鑽越深——提出了一個無意義的回答——沒時間權衡,所以他冒險說了出來——虛弱地:

passages.original: “Sunday-school books, maybe.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者係主日學校嘅書。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許是主日學校的書。」

passages.original: Poor Huck was too distressed to smile, but the old man laughed loud and joyously, shook up the details of his anatomy from head to foot, and ended by saying that such a laugh was money in a man’s pocket, because it cut down the doctor’s bill like everything.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅哈克太苦惱而笑不出嚟,但老人大聲而快樂地笑喇,從頭到腳抖動咗佢身體嘅各個部分,最後講咁樣嘅笑係口袋裡嘅錢,因為佢像乜嘢一樣減少醫生嘅帳單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的哈克太苦惱而笑不出來,但老人大聲而快樂地笑了,從頭到腳抖動了他身體的各個部分,最後說這樣的笑是口袋裡的錢,因為它像什麼一樣減少醫生的帳單。

passages.original: Then he added:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢補充:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他補充:

passages.original: “Poor old chap, you’re white and jaded—you ain’t well a bit—no wonder you’re a little flighty and off your balance.
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅老傢伙,你臉色蒼白、疲憊——你啲都不舒服——難怪你有點頭腦發昏、失去平衡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的老傢伙,你臉色蒼白、疲憊——你一點也不舒服——難怪你有點頭腦發昏、失去平衡。

passages.original: But you’ll come out of it.
passages.vernacular: 但你會好起嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你會好起來的。

passages.original: Rest and sleep will fetch you out all right, I hope.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望休息同瞓眠會讓你完全好起嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望休息和睡眠會讓你完全好起來。」

passages.original: Huck was irritated to think he had been such a goose and betrayed such a suspicious excitement, for he had dropped the idea that the parcel brought from the tavern was the treasure, as soon as he had heard the talk at the widow’s stile.
passages.vernacular: 哈克想到自己咁傻、表現出咁可疑嘅興奮而惱火,因為佢一聽到寡婦踏階嗰邊嘅談話,就已經放棄咗嗰包從旅店攞嚟嘅嘢係寶藏嘅想法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克想到自己這麼傻、表現出這麼可疑的興奮而惱火,因為他一聽到寡婦踏階那邊的談話,就已經放棄了那包從旅店拿來的東西是寶藏的想法。

passages.original: He had only thought it was not the treasure, however—he had not known that it wasn’t—and so the suggestion of a captured bundle was too much for his self-possession.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢只係想佢唔係寶藏——佢唔知道佢唔係——所以聽到繳獲一個包裹嘅暗示,佢嘅鎮定受不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過他只是想它不是寶藏——他不知道它不是——所以聽到繳獲一個包裹的暗示,他的鎮定受不了。

passages.original: But on the whole he felt glad the little episode had happened, for now he knew beyond all question that that bundle was not the bundle, and so his mind was at rest and exceedingly comfortable.
passages.vernacular: 但總嘅來講,佢好高興呢個小插曲發生喇,因為而家佢毫無疑問地知道嗰個包裹唔係嗰個包裹,所以佢嘅心平靜喇,好舒服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但總的來說,他很高興這個小插曲發生了,因為現在他毫無疑問地知道那個包裹不是那個包裹,所以他的心平靜了,非常舒服。

passages.original: In fact, everything seemed to be drifting just in the right direction, now; the treasure must be still in No. 2, the men would be captured and jailed that day, and he and Tom could seize the gold that night without any trouble or any fear of interruption.
passages.vernacular: 事實上,而家一切似乎都漂向正確嘅方向;寶藏一定仲喺二號房,嗰啲人當天會被捕入獄,佢同湯姆當晚可以毫不費力、毫不擔心打擾地奪取金子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實上,現在一切似乎都漂向正確的方向;寶藏一定還在二號房,那些人當天會被捕入獄,他和湯姆當晚可以毫不費力、毫不擔心打擾地奪取金子。

passages.original: Just as breakfast was completed there was a knock at the door.
passages.vernacular: 早餐剛食完,有人敲門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早餐剛吃完,有人敲門。

passages.original: Huck jumped for a hiding-place, for he had no mind to be connected even remotely with the late event.
passages.vernacular: 哈克跳去找藏身處,因為佢無意同近來嘅事件有任何邊怕係遙遠嘅關聯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克跳去找藏身處,因為他無意與近來的事件有任何哪怕是遙遠的關聯。

passages.original: The Welshman admitted several ladies and gentlemen, among them the Widow Douglas, and noticed that groups of citizens were climbing up the hill—to stare at the stile.
passages.vernacular: 威爾斯人接納咗幾位女士同先生,其中有道格拉斯寡婦,並注意到一群群市民正爬上山——去睇踏階。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威爾斯人接納了幾位女士和先生,其中有道格拉斯寡婦,並注意到一群群市民正爬上山——去看踏階。

passages.original: So the news had spread.
passages.vernacular: 所以消息已經傳開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以消息已經傳開了。

passages.original: The Welshman had to tell the story of the night to the visitors.
passages.vernacular: 威爾斯人唔得不向訪客講述夜裡嘅故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威爾斯人不得不向訪客講述夜裡的故事。

passages.original: The widow’s gratitude for her preservation was outspoken.
passages.vernacular: 寡婦對自己得救嘅感激毫不隱瞞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦對自己得救的感激毫不隱瞞。

passages.original: “Don’t say a word about it, madam.
passages.vernacular: 「唔好講一個字,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別說一個字,夫人。

passages.original: There’s another that you’re more beholden to than you are to me and my boys, maybe, but he don’t allow me to tell his name.
passages.vernacular: 仲有另一個人,你欠佢嘅或者比欠我同我嘅細路哋嘅更多,但佢不許我講出佢嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有另一個人,你欠他的也許比欠我和我的孩子們的更多,但他不許我說出他的名字。

passages.original: We wouldn’t have been there but for him.”
passages.vernacular: 冇佢我哋唔會喺嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有他我們不會在那裡。」

passages.original: Of course this excited a curiosity so vast that it almost belittled the main matter—but the Welshman allowed it to eat into the vitals of his visitors, and through them be transmitted to the whole town, for he refused to part with his secret.
passages.vernacular: 當然呢激起咗咁大嘅好奇心,幾乎使主要事件顯得微不足道——但威爾斯人讓佢啃噬佢嘅訪客嘅五臟六腑,並通過佢哋傳畀全鎮,因為佢拒絕交出佢嘅祕密。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然這激起了那麼大的好奇心,幾乎使主要事件顯得微不足道——但威爾斯人讓它啃噬他的訪客的五臟六腑,並通過他們傳給全鎮,因為他拒絕交出他的祕密。

passages.original: When all else had been learned, the widow said:
passages.vernacular: 知道咗其他一切後,寡婦講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 知道了其他一切後,寡婦說:

passages.original: “I went to sleep reading in bed and slept straight through all that noise.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺床上睇書瞓住喇,瞓過咗所有嗰啲噪音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在床上看書睡著了,睡過了所有那些噪音。

passages.original: Why didn’t you come and wake me?”
passages.vernacular: 你哋點解冇嚟叫醒我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們為什麼沒來叫醒我?」

passages.original: “We judged it warn’t worth while.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋判斷不值得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們判斷不值得。

passages.original: Those fellows warn’t likely to come again—they hadn’t any tools left to work with, and what was the use of waking you up and scaring you to death?
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲傢伙不太可能再嚟——佢哋冇工具可用喇,叫醒你、把你嚇死有乜嘢用?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些傢伙不太可能再來——他們沒有工具可用了,叫醒你、把你嚇死有什麼用?

passages.original: My three negro men stood guard at your house all the rest of the night.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅三個黑人傭工喺你家站崗站咗其餘整夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的三個黑人傭工在你家站崗站了其餘整夜。

passages.original: They’ve just come back.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們剛回來。」

passages.original: More visitors came, and the story had to be told and retold for a couple of hours more.
passages.vernacular: 更多訪客嚟喇,故事唔得唔再講再講咗兩個小時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 更多訪客來了,故事不得不再講再講了兩個小時。

passages.original: There was no Sabbath-school during day-school vacation, but everybody was early at church.
passages.vernacular: 日校假期期間冇安息日學校,但每個人都早早到教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 日校假期期間沒有安息日學校,但每個人都早早到教堂。

passages.original: The stirring event was well canvassed.
passages.vernacular: 呢個激動人心嘅事件得到充分討論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個激動人心的事件得到充分討論。

passages.original: News came that not a sign of the two villains had been yet discovered.
passages.vernacular: 消息傳來講,嗰兩個惡棍仲冇發現任何蹤跡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 消息傳來說,那兩個惡棍還沒發現任何蹤跡。

passages.original: When the sermon was finished, Judge Thatcher’s wife dropped alongside of Mrs. Harper as she moved down the aisle with the crowd and said:
passages.vernacular: 講道結束時,撒切爾法官嘅妻子喺哈珀太太隨人群走下過道時走到佢旁邊講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講道結束時,撒切爾法官的妻子在哈珀太太隨人群走下過道時走到她旁邊說:

passages.original: “Is my Becky going to sleep all day?
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅貝琪要瞓一整天嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的貝琪要睡一整天嗎?

passages.original: I just expected she would be tired to death.”
passages.vernacular: 我正預料佢會累得要死。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我正預料她會累得要死。」

passages.original: “Your Becky?”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅貝琪?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的貝琪?」

passages.original: “Yes,” with a startled look—“didn’t she stay with you last night?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」帶住驚嚇嘅神情——「佢琴晚冇同你哋喺一起嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」帶著驚嚇的神情——「她昨晚沒和你們在一起嗎?」

passages.original: “Why, no.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,沒有。」

passages.original: Mrs. Thatcher turned pale, and sank into a pew, just as Aunt Polly, talking briskly with a friend, passed by.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾太太臉色發白,倒喺一張長椅上,呢陣波莉姨媽正同朋友活潑地講話走過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾太太臉色發白,倒在一張長椅上,這時波莉姨媽正與朋友活潑地說話走過。

passages.original: Aunt Polly said:
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽說:

passages.original: “Goodmorning, Mrs. Thatcher.
passages.vernacular: 「早安,撒切爾太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「早安,撒切爾太太。

passages.original: Goodmorning, Mrs. Harper.
passages.vernacular: 早安,哈珀太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早安,哈珀太太。

passages.original: I’ve got a boy that’s turned up missing.
passages.vernacular: 我有個細路失蹤喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有個孩子失蹤了。

passages.original: I reckon my Tom stayed at your house last night—one of you.
passages.vernacular: 我想我嘅湯姆琴晚喺你哋家過夜——你哋中嘅一家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我的湯姆昨晚在你們家過夜——你們中的一家。

passages.original: And now he’s afraid to come to church.
passages.vernacular: 而家佢怕嚟教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他怕來教堂。

passages.original: I’ve got to settle with him.”
passages.vernacular: 我得跟佢算帳。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得跟他算帳。」

passages.original: Mrs. Thatcher shook her head feebly and turned paler than ever.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾太太虛弱地搖頭,臉色比以往更蒼白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾太太虛弱地搖頭,臉色比以往更蒼白。

passages.original: “He didn’t stay with us,” said Mrs. Harper, beginning to look uneasy.
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇喺我哋家,」哈珀太太講,開始顯得不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他沒在我們家,」哈珀太太說,開始顯得不安。

passages.original: A marked anxiety came into Aunt Polly’s face.
passages.vernacular: 一種明顯嘅焦慮進入咗波莉姨媽嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種明顯的焦慮進入了波莉姨媽的臉。

passages.original: “Joe Harper, have you seen my Tom this morning?”
passages.vernacular: 「喬·哈珀,你今日早晨見到我嘅湯姆咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喬·哈珀,你今天早晨見到我的湯姆了嗎?」

passages.original: “No’m.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,姨媽。」

passages.original: “When did you see him last?”
passages.vernacular: 「你最後一次見佢係乜嘢時候?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你最後一次見他是什麼時候?」

passages.original: Joe tried to remember, but was not sure he could say.
passages.vernacular: 喬試圖回憶,但不確定能講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喬試圖回憶,但不確定能說出來。

passages.original: The people had stopped moving out of church.
passages.vernacular: 人哋已經停止走出教堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們已經停止走出教堂。

passages.original: Whispers passed along, and a boding uneasiness took possession of every countenance.
passages.vernacular: 耳語傳遍,一種不祥嘅不安佔據咗每張臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 耳語傳遍,一種不祥的不安佔據了每張臉。

passages.original: Children were anxiously questioned, and young teachers.
passages.vernacular: 細路哋同年輕教師被焦急地詢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們和年輕教師被焦急地詢問。

passages.original: They all said they had not noticed whether Tom and Becky were on board the ferryboat on the homeward trip; it was dark; no one thought of inquiring if any one was missing.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都講冇注意湯姆同貝琪係咪喺回程嘅渡船上;天黑喇;冇人想到查問有冇人唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們都說沒有注意湯姆和貝琪是否在回程的渡船上;天黑了;沒有人想到查問有沒有人不見了。

passages.original: One young man finally blurted out his fear that they were still in the cave!
passages.vernacular: 一個年輕人終於脫口講出佢嘅恐懼,講佢哋仲喺山洞裡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個年輕人終於脫口說出他的恐懼,說他們還在山洞裡!

passages.original: Mrs. Thatcher swooned away.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾太太昏咗過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾太太昏了過去。

passages.original: Aunt Polly fell to crying and wringing her hands.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽開始哭並絞著手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽開始哭並絞著手。

passages.original: The alarm swept from lip to lip, from group to group, from street to street, and within five minutes the bells were wildly clanging and the whole town was up!
passages.vernacular: 警報從嘴唇傳到嘴唇,從一群傳到另一群,從一條街傳到另一條街,五分鐘內鐘聲狂亂地響起,全鎮都起嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 警報從嘴唇傳到嘴唇,從一群傳到另一群,從一條街傳到另一條街,五分鐘內鐘聲狂亂地響起,全鎮都起來了!

passages.original: The Cardiff Hill episode sank into instant insignificance, the burglars were forgotten, horses were saddled, skiffs were manned, the ferryboat ordered out, and before the horror was half an hour old, two hundred men were pouring down highroad and river toward the cave.
passages.vernacular: 卡迪夫山嘅事件轉眼變得無足輕重,竊賊被遺忘,馬被備鞍,小艇有人上船,渡船被下令出動,喺呢恐怖發生唔到半小時,兩百人正沿住公路同河流湧向山洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卡迪夫山的事件轉眼變得無足輕重,竊賊被遺忘,馬被備鞍,小艇有人上船,渡船被下令出動,在這恐怖發生不到半小時,兩百人正沿著公路和河流湧向山洞。

passages.original: All the long afternoon the village seemed empty and dead.
passages.vernacular: 整個漫長嘅下午,村子似乎空蕩蕩嘅、死寂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個漫長的下午,村子似乎空蕩蕩的、死寂。

passages.original: Many women visited Aunt Polly and Mrs. Thatcher and tried to comfort them.
passages.vernacular: 許多婦女探訪波莉姨媽同撒切爾太太,試圖安慰佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 許多婦女探訪波莉姨媽和撒切爾太太,試圖安慰她們。

passages.original: They cried with them, too, and that was still better than words.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋都同佢哋一起哭,嗰比言語更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們也同她們一起哭,那比言語更好。

passages.original: All the tedious night the town waited for news; but when the morning dawned at last, all the word that came was, “Send more candles—and send food.”
passages.vernacular: 整個乏味嘅夜晚鎮子等待消息;但黎明終於來臨時,傳嚟嘅全部話係:「多送蠟燭——送食物嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個乏味的夜晚鎮子等待消息;但黎明終於來臨時,傳來的全部話是:「多送蠟燭——送食物來。」

passages.original: Mrs. Thatcher was almost crazed; and Aunt Polly, also.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾太太幾乎瘋喇;波莉姨媽都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾太太幾乎瘋了;波莉姨媽也是。

passages.original: Judge Thatcher sent messages of hope and encouragement from the cave, but they conveyed no real cheer.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾法官從山洞送出希望同鼓勵嘅訊息,但佢哋冇傳達真正嘅歡樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾法官從山洞送出希望和鼓勵的訊息,但它們沒有傳達真正的歡樂。

passages.original: The old Welshman came home toward daylight, spattered with candle-grease, smeared with clay, and almost worn out.
passages.vernacular: 老威爾斯人黎明時回到家,濺滿蠟燭油,沾滿泥土,幾乎累垮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老威爾斯人黎明時回到家,濺滿蠟燭油,沾滿泥土,幾乎累垮。

passages.original: He found Huck still in the bed that had been provided for him, and delirious with fever.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現哈克仲喺為佢準備嘅床上,發高燒講胡話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他發現哈克還在為他準備的床上,發高燒說胡話。

passages.original: The physicians were all at the cave, so the Widow Douglas came and took charge of the patient.
passages.vernacular: 醫生哋都喺山洞,所以道格拉斯寡婦嚟接管咗病人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生們都在山洞,所以道格拉斯寡婦來接管了病人。

passages.original: She said she would do her best by him, because, whether he was good, bad, or indifferent, he was the Lord’s, and nothing that was the Lord’s was a thing to be neglected.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢會盡力照顧佢,因為不管佢係好、壞定係不好不壞,佢係主嘅,凡是主嘅,都唔能夠被忽視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她會盡力照顧他,因為不管他是好、壞還是不好不壞,他是主的,凡是主的,都不能被忽視。

passages.original: The Welshman said Huck had good spots in him, and the widow said:
passages.vernacular: 威爾斯人講哈克身上有好嘅地方,寡婦講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威爾斯人說哈克身上有好的地方,寡婦說:

passages.original: “You can depend on it.
passages.vernacular: 「你可以放心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你可以放心。

passages.original: That’s the Lord’s mark.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係主嘅標記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是主的標記。

passages.original: He don’t leave it off.
passages.vernacular: 祂唔會漏掉佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 祂不會漏掉它。

passages.original: He never does.
passages.vernacular: 祂從不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 祂從不。

passages.original: Puts it somewhere on every creature that comes from his hands.”
passages.vernacular: 喺每個出自祂手嘅生物身上都放喺某處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在每個出自祂手的生物身上都放在某處。」

passages.original: Early in the forenoon parties of jaded men began to straggle into the village, but the strongest of the citizens continued searching.
passages.vernacular: 上午早些時候,成批疲憊嘅人開始蹣跚進村,但最強壯嘅市民繼續搜索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上午早些時候,成批疲憊的人開始蹣跚進村,但最強壯的市民繼續搜索。

passages.original: All the news that could be gained was that remotenesses of the cavern were being ransacked that had never been visited before; that every corner and crevice was going to be thoroughly searched; that wherever one wandered through the maze of passages, lights were to be seen flitting hither and thither in the distance, and shoutings and pistol-shots sent their hollow reverberations to the ear down the sombre aisles.
passages.vernacular: 能得到嘅全部消息係:洞穴從未被探訪過嘅遙遠之處正被搜查;每個角落同裂縫都要被徹底搜尋;無論人喺迷宮般嘅通道中漫遊到邊度,都能睇到遠處閃爍嚟去嘅燈光,喊聲同手槍聲把佢哋空洞嘅回響通過陰沉嘅走廊送到耳中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 能得到的全部消息是:洞穴從未被探訪過的遙遠之處正被搜查;每個角落和裂縫都要被徹底搜尋;無論人在迷宮般的通道中漫遊到哪裡,都能看到遠處閃爍來去的燈光,喊聲和手槍聲把它們空洞的回響通過陰沉的走廊送到耳中。

passages.original: In one place, far from the section usually traversed by tourists, the names “BECKY & TOM” had been found traced upon the rocky wall with candle-smoke, and near at hand a grease-soiled bit of ribbon.
passages.vernacular: 喺一個遠離遊客通常經過嘅地段嘅地方,發現咗用蠟燭煙喺石壁上描出嘅名字「貝琪同湯姆」,附近仲有一小片沾咗油脂嘅絲帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一個遠離遊客通常經過的地段的地方,發現了用蠟燭煙在石壁上描出的名字「貝琪和湯姆」,附近還有一小片沾了油脂的絲帶。

passages.original: Mrs. Thatcher recognized the ribbon and cried over it.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾太太認出咗嗰條絲帶,對住佢哭泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾太太認出了那條絲帶,對著它哭泣。

passages.original: She said it was the last relic she should ever have of her child; and that no other memorial of her could ever be so precious, because this one parted latest from the living body before the awful death came.
passages.vernacular: 佢講呢個係佢將擁有嘅細路嘅最後遺物;冇別嘅紀念物能咁珍貴,因為呢件喺可怕嘅死亡來臨前最後離開活嘅身體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說這是她將擁有的孩子的最後遺物;沒有別的紀念物能這麼珍貴,因為這件在可怕的死亡來臨前最後離開活的身體。

passages.original: Some said that now and then, in the cave, a far-away speck of light would glimmer, and then a glorious shout would burst forth and a score of men go trooping down the echoing aisle—and then a sickening disappointment always followed; the children were not there; it was only a searcher’s light.
passages.vernacular: 有人講洞裡不時有一個遠處嘅光點閃爍,然後爆發出一陣輝煌嘅歡呼,幾十個人湧向回聲嘅走廊——然後總是跟住令人噁心嘅失望;細路哋不喺嗰度;嗰只係搜尋者嘅燈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人說洞裡不時有一個遠處的光點閃爍,然後爆發出一陣輝煌的歡呼,幾十個人湧向回聲的走廊——然後總是跟著令人噁心的失望;孩子們不在那裡;那只是搜尋者的燈。

passages.original: Three dreadful days and nights dragged their tedious hours along, and the village sank into a hopeless stupor.
passages.vernacular: 三個可怕嘅白天黑夜拖住佢哋乏味嘅時辰過去,村子陷入絕望嘅麻木。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三個可怕的白天黑夜拖著它們乏味的時辰過去,村子陷入絕望的麻木。

passages.original: No one had heart for anything.
passages.vernacular: 冇人對任何事有心思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人對任何事有心思。

passages.original: The accidental discovery, just made, that the proprietor of the Temperance Tavern kept liquor on his premises, scarcely fluttered the public pulse, tremendous as the fact was.
passages.vernacular: 啱啱偶然嘅發現,節制旅店嘅老闆喺佢嘅場所存有烈酒,雖然呢事實驚人,卻幾乎冇激起公眾嘅脈搏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛剛偶然的發現,節制旅店的老闆在他的場所存有烈酒,雖然這事實驚人,卻幾乎沒激起公眾的脈搏。

passages.original: In a lucid interval, Huck feebly led up to the subject of taverns, and finally asked—dimly dreading the worst—if anything had been discovered at the Temperance Tavern since he had been ill.
passages.vernacular: 喺一個清醒嘅間隙,哈克虛弱地把話題引到旅店,最後問——隱隱害怕最壞嘅——自從佢生病以來,節制旅店有冇發現乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一個清醒的間隙,哈克虛弱地把話題引到旅店,最後問——隱隱害怕最壞的——自從他生病以來,節制旅店有沒有發現什麼。

passages.original: “Yes,” said the widow.
passages.vernacular: 「有,」寡婦講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有,」寡婦說。

passages.original: Huck started up in bed, wild-eyed:
passages.vernacular: 哈克喺床上猛地坐起嚟,眼睛狂野:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克在床上猛地坐起來,眼睛狂野:

passages.original: “What?
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼?

passages.original: What was it?”
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼?」

passages.original: “Liquor!—and the place has been shut up.
passages.vernacular: 「烈酒!——地方已經被關閉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「烈酒!——地方已經被關閉了。

passages.original: Lie down, child—what a turn you did give me!”
passages.vernacular: 躺下,細路——你真嚇咗我一跳!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 躺下,孩子——你真嚇了我一跳!」

passages.original: “Only tell me just one thing—only just one—please!
passages.vernacular: 「只告訴我一件事——就一件——求你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只告訴我一件事——就一件——求你!

passages.original: Was it Tom Sawyer that found it?”
passages.vernacular: 係湯姆·索亞發現嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是湯姆·索亞發現的嗎?」

passages.original: The widow burst into tears.
passages.vernacular: 寡婦淚如泉湧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦淚如泉湧。

passages.original: “Hush, hush, child, hush!
passages.vernacular: 「噓,噓,細路,噓!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「噓,噓,孩子,噓!

passages.original: I’ve told you before, you must not talk.
passages.vernacular: 我以前告訴過你,你唔能夠講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前告訴過你,你不能說話。

passages.original: You are very, very sick!”
passages.vernacular: 你病得好,好重!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你病得很,很重!」

passages.original: Then nothing but liquor had been found; there would have been a great powwow if it had been the gold.
passages.vernacular: 咁只發現咗烈酒;如果係金子,會有一場大騷動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼只發現了烈酒;如果是金子,會有一場大騷動。

passages.original: So the treasure was gone forever—gone forever!
passages.vernacular: 所以寶藏永遠消失喇——永遠消失喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以寶藏永遠消失了——永遠消失了!

passages.original: But what could she be crying about?
passages.vernacular: 但佢點解哭?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她為什麼哭?

passages.original: Curious that she should cry.
passages.vernacular: 奇怪佢竟然哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇怪她竟然哭。

passages.original: These thoughts worked their dim way through Huck’s mind, and under the weariness they gave him he fell asleep.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲念頭喺哈克嘅頭腦中艱難地通過,喺佢哋帶嚟嘅疲倦下,佢瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些念頭在哈克的頭腦中艱難地通過,在它們帶來的疲倦下,他睡著了。

passages.original: The widow said to herself:
passages.vernacular: 寡婦對自己講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦對自己說:

passages.original: “There—he’s asleep, poor wreck.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇——佢瞓住喇,可憐嘅殘骸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了——他睡著了,可憐的殘骸。

passages.original: Tom Sawyer find it!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆·索亞發現嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆·索亞發現的!

passages.original: Pity but somebody could find Tom Sawyer!
passages.vernacular: 可惜唔能夠有人找到湯姆·索亞!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可惜不能有人找到湯姆·索亞!

passages.original: Ah, there ain’t many left, now, that’s got hope enough, or strength enough, either, to go on searching.”
passages.vernacular: 啊,而家剩下嘅冇多少人有足夠嘅希望,或足夠嘅力氣繼續搜尋喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,現在剩下的沒有多少人有足夠的希望,或足夠的力氣繼續搜尋了。」

chapters.title: Chapter XXXI: An Exploring Expedition 第三十一章:探險

passages.original: CH Now to return to Tom and Becky’s share in the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 而家回頭講湯姆同貝琪喺野餐中嘅經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在回頭說湯姆和貝琪在野餐中的經歷。

passages.original: They tripped along the murky aisles with the rest of the company, visiting the familiar wonders of the cave—wonders dubbed with rather over-descriptive names, such as “The Drawing-Room,” “The Cathedral,” “Aladdin’s Palace,” and so on.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋同其餘嘅人一起輕快地走過昏暗嘅通道,參觀山洞熟悉嘅奇觀——呢啲奇觀被取咗相當過度描述性嘅名字,如「客廳」、「大教堂」、「阿拉丁宮」等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們同其餘的人一起輕快地走過昏暗的通道,參觀山洞熟悉的奇觀——這些奇觀被取了相當過度描述性的名字,如「客廳」、「大教堂」、「阿拉丁宮」等等。

passages.original: Presently the hide-and-seek frolicking began, and Tom and Becky engaged in it with zeal until the exertion began to grow a trifle wearisome; then they wandered down a sinuous avenue holding their candles aloft and reading the tangled webwork of names, dates, postoffice addresses, and mottoes with which the rocky walls had been frescoed (in candle-smoke).
passages.vernacular: 不久捉迷藏嘅嬉鬧開始喇,湯姆同貝琪熱情地參加,直到努力開始有點令人疲倦;然後佢哋沿住一條蜿蜒嘅通道漫遊,高舉蠟燭,讀石壁上(用蠟燭煙)畫成壁畫嘅名字、日期、郵局地址同格言嘅糾纏嘅網。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久捉迷藏的嬉鬧開始了,湯姆和貝琪熱情地參加,直到努力開始有點令人疲倦;然後他們沿著一條蜿蜒的通道漫遊,高舉蠟燭,讀石壁上(用蠟燭煙)畫成壁畫的名字、日期、郵局地址和格言的糾纏的網。

passages.original: Still drifting along and talking, they scarcely noticed that they were now in a part of the cave whose walls were not frescoed.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋仍然邊漂邊談,幾乎冇注意到佢哋而家處喺山洞嘅一部分,嗰度嘅牆壁冇壁畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們仍然邊漂邊談,幾乎沒注意到他們現在處在山洞的一部分,那裡的牆壁沒有壁畫。

passages.original: They smoked their own names under an overhanging shelf and moved on.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺一個懸垂嘅岩架下用煙畫咗自己嘅名字,繼續前進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在一個懸垂的岩架下用煙畫了自己的名字,繼續前進。

passages.original: Presently they came to a place where a little stream of water, trickling over a ledge and carrying a limestone sediment with it, had, in the slow-dragging ages, formed a laced and ruffled Niagara in gleaming and imperishable stone.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋嚟到一個地方,嗰度一小股水流過一塊岩架,攜帶住石灰質沉積物,喺緩慢拖延嘅歲月中,形成咗一座閃光不朽嘅石頭嘅、花邊皺褶嘅尼亞加拉瀑布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們來到一個地方,那裡一小股水流過一塊岩架,攜帶著石灰質沉積物,在緩慢拖延的歲月中,形成了一座閃光不朽的石頭的、花邊皺褶的尼亞加拉瀑布。

passages.original: Tom squeezed his small body behind it in order to illuminate it for Becky’s gratification.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆把佢小小嘅身體擠到佢後面,好為貝琪嘅滿足而照亮佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆把他小小的身體擠到它後面,好為貝琪的滿足而照亮它。

passages.original: He found that it curtained a sort of steep natural stairway which was enclosed between narrow walls, and at once the ambition to be a discoverer seized him.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現佢遮住咗一種陡峭嘅天然階梯,封閉喺狹窄嘅牆壁之間,頓時當發現者嘅野心抓住咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他發現它遮住了一種陡峭的天然階梯,封閉在狹窄的牆壁之間,頓時當發現者的野心抓住了他。

passages.original: Becky responded to his call, and they made a smoke-mark for future guidance, and started upon their quest.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪回應佢嘅呼喚,佢哋畫咗一個煙痕作為將來嘅指引,出發開始佢哋嘅探索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪回應他的呼喚,他們畫了一個煙痕作為將來的指引,出發開始他們的探索。

passages.original: They wound this way and that, far down into the secret depths of the cave, made another mark, and branched off in search of novelties to tell the upper world about.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋左彎右拐,深入山洞嘅祕密深處,又畫咗一個標記,分岔出去尋找新奇事物,好告訴上面嘅世界。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們左彎右拐,深入山洞的祕密深處,又畫了一個標記,分岔出去尋找新奇事物,好告訴上面的世界。

passages.original: In one place they found a spacious cavern, from whose ceiling depended a multitude of shining stalactites of the length and circumference of a man’s leg; they walked all about it, wondering and admiring, and presently left it by one of the numerous passages that opened into it.
passages.vernacular: 喺一處佢哋發現一個寬敞嘅洞穴,從佢嘅天花板上垂下許多閃亮嘅鐘乳石,長度同圍度像一個人嘅腿;佢哋喺佢周圍走遍,驚奇欣賞,不久通過通向佢嘅許多通道之一離開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在一處他們發現一個寬敞的洞穴,從它的天花板上垂下許多閃亮的鐘乳石,長度和圍度像一個人的腿;他們在它周圍走遍,驚奇欣賞,不久通過通向它的許多通道之一離開。

passages.original: This shortly brought them to a bewitching spring, whose basin was incrusted with a frostwork of glittering crystals; it was in the midst of a cavern whose walls were supported by many fantastic pillars which had been formed by the joining of great stalactites and stalagmites together, the result of the ceaseless water-drip of centuries.
passages.vernacular: 呢不久把佢哋帶到一個迷人嘅泉水,佢嘅水池被閃光嘅水晶霜花覆蓋;佢喺一個洞穴嘅中間,洞穴嘅牆壁由許多奇異嘅柱子支撐,呢啲柱子係由大鐘乳石同石筍連喺一起形成嘅,係幾個世紀不停嘅水滴嘅結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不久把他們帶到一個迷人的泉水,它的水池被閃光的水晶霜花覆蓋;它在一個洞穴的中間,洞穴的牆壁由許多奇異的柱子支撐,這些柱子是由大鐘乳石和石筍連在一起形成的,是幾個世紀不停的水滴的結果。

passages.original: Under the roof vast knots of bats had packed themselves together, thousands in a bunch; the lights disturbed the creatures and they came flocking down by hundreds, squeaking and darting furiously at the candles.
passages.vernacular: 屋頂下,成大團嘅蝙蝠擠喺一起,一團有幾千隻;燈光驚擾咗呢啲生物,牠哋成百地湧下嚟,尖叫住猛撲蠟燭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 屋頂下,成大團的蝙蝠擠在一起,一團有幾千隻;燈光驚擾了這些生物,牠們成百地湧下來,尖叫著猛撲蠟燭。

passages.original: Tom knew their ways and the danger of this sort of conduct.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆知道牠哋嘅習性同呢種行為嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆知道牠們的習性和這種行為的危險。

passages.original: He seized Becky’s hand and hurried her into the first corridor that offered; and none too soon, for a bat struck Becky’s light out with its wing while she was passing out of the cavern.
passages.vernacular: 佢抓住貝琪嘅手,匆忙帶佢進入第一條出現嘅走廊;啲都不算早,因為貝琪走出洞穴時,一隻蝙蝠用翅膀打滅咗佢嘅燈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他抓住貝琪的手,匆忙帶她進入第一條出現的走廊;一點也不算早,因為貝琪走出洞穴時,一隻蝙蝠用翅膀打滅了她的燈。

passages.original: The bats chased the children a good distance; but the fugitives plunged into every new passage that offered, and at last got rid of the perilous things.
passages.vernacular: 蝙蝠追趕細路哋好遠一段距離;但逃亡者鑽進每一條出現嘅新通道,終於擺脫咗呢啲危險嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蝙蝠追趕孩子們很遠一段距離;但逃亡者鑽進每一條出現的新通道,終於擺脫了這些危險的東西。

passages.original: Tom found a subterranean lake, shortly, which stretched its dim length away until its shape was lost in the shadows.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆不久發現一個地下湖,佢昏暗嘅長度延伸出去,直到形狀消失喺陰影中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆不久發現一個地下湖,它昏暗的長度延伸出去,直到形狀消失在陰影中。

passages.original: He wanted to explore its borders, but concluded that it would be best to sit down and rest awhile, first.
passages.vernacular: 佢想探索佢嘅邊緣,但斷定最好先坐下休息一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想探索它的邊緣,但斷定最好先坐下休息一會兒。

passages.original: Now, for the first time, the deep stillness of the place laid a clammy hand upon the spirits of the children.
passages.vernacular: 而家,第一次,呢個地方深深嘅寂靜把冰冷嘅手放喺細路哋嘅心上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,第一次,這個地方深深的寂靜把冰冷的手放在孩子們的心上。

passages.original: Becky said:
passages.vernacular: 貝琪講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪說:

passages.original: “Why, I didn’t notice, but it seems ever so long since I heard any of the others.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我冇注意,但似乎好久冇聽到其他人喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我沒注意,但似乎很久沒聽到其他人了。」

passages.original: “Come to think, Becky, we are away down below them—and I don’t know how far away north, or south, or east, or whichever it is.
passages.vernacular: 「想起嚟,貝琪,我哋遠遠喺佢哋下面——我唔知道向北、向南、向東,定係邊個方向,有多遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想起來,貝琪,我們遠遠在他們下面——我不知道向北、向南、向東,還是哪個方向,有多遠。

passages.original: We couldn’t hear them here.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺呢度聽唔到佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在這裡聽不到他們。」

passages.original: Becky grew apprehensive.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪變得不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪變得不安。

passages.original: “I wonder how long we’ve been down here, Tom?
passages.vernacular: 「我想知道我哋喺下面多久喇,湯姆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想知道我們在下面多久了,湯姆?

passages.original: We better start back.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋最好開始回去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們最好開始回去。」

passages.original: “Yes, I reckon we better.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我想我哋最好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我想我們最好。

passages.original: P’raps we better.”
passages.vernacular: 或者我哋最好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許我們最好。」

passages.original: “Can you find the way, Tom?
passages.vernacular: 「你能找到路嗎,湯姆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你能找到路嗎,湯姆?

passages.original: It’s all a mixed-up crookedness to me.”
passages.vernacular: 對我來講一切都係混亂嘅彎曲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我來說一切都是混亂的彎曲。」

passages.original: “I reckon I could find it—but then the bats.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我能找到——但係蝙蝠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我能找到——但是蝙蝠。

passages.original: If they put our candles out it will be an awful fix.
passages.vernacular: 如果牠哋把我哋嘅蠟燭打滅,嗰會係個可怕嘅困境。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果牠們把我們的蠟燭打滅,那會是個可怕的困境。

passages.original: Let’s try some other way, so as not to go through there.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋試試別嘅路,咁樣不經過嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們試試別的路,這樣不經過那裡。」

passages.original: “Well.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧。

passages.original: But I hope we won’t get lost.
passages.vernacular: 但我希望我哋唔會迷路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我希望我們不會迷路。

passages.original: It would be so awful!” and the girl shuddered at the thought of the dreadful possibilities.
passages.vernacular: 嗰太可怕喇!」女孩對可怕嘅可能性嘅想法而顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那太可怕了!」女孩對可怕的可能性的想法而顫抖。

passages.original: They started through a corridor, and traversed it in silence a long way, glancing at each new opening, to see if there was anything familiar about the look of it; but they were all strange.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋出發穿過一條走廊,沉默地穿過好長一段,每次睇到新嘅開口都瞥一眼,睇佢嘅樣子係咪有任何熟悉嘅地方;但都係陌生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們出發穿過一條走廊,沉默地穿過很長一段,每次看到新的開口都瞥一眼,看它的樣子是否有任何熟悉的地方;但都是陌生的。

passages.original: Every time Tom made an examination, Becky would watch his face for an encouraging sign, and he would say cheerily:
passages.vernacular: 每次湯姆檢查時,貝琪都睇住佢嘅臉找鼓勵嘅跡象,佢會愉快地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每次湯姆檢查時,貝琪都看著他的臉找鼓勵的跡象,他會愉快地說:

passages.original: “Oh, it’s all right.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,冇事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,沒事。

passages.original: This ain’t the one, but we’ll come to it right away!”
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係,但我哋即刻就會到!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是,但我們馬上就會到!」

passages.original: But he felt less and less hopeful with each failure, and presently began to turn off into diverging avenues at sheer random, in desperate hope of finding the one that was wanted.
passages.vernacular: 但每次失敗佢都越嚟越冇希望,不久開始完全隨機地轉進分岔嘅通道,絕望地希望找到要找嘅嗰條。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但每次失敗他都越來越沒有希望,不久開始完全隨機地轉進分岔的通道,絕望地希望找到要找的那條。

passages.original: He still said it was “all right,” but there was such a leaden dread at his heart that the words had lost their ring and sounded just as if he had said, “All is lost!”
passages.vernacular: 佢仍然講「冇事」,但佢心裡有種鉛一般嘅恐懼,嗰啲話失去咗響亮,聽起嚟就像佢講咗「一切都完喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他仍然說「沒事」,但他心裡有種鉛一般的恐懼,那些話失去了響亮,聽起來就像他說了「一切都完了!」

passages.original: Becky clung to his side in an anguish of fear, and tried hard to keep back the tears, but they would come.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪喺恐懼嘅痛苦中緊貼喺佢身邊,努力忍住眼淚,但佢哋定係嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪在恐懼的痛苦中緊貼在他身邊,努力忍住眼淚,但它們還是來了。

passages.original: At last she said:
passages.vernacular: 最後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後她說:

passages.original: “Oh, Tom, never mind the bats, let’s go back that way!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆,別管蝙蝠喇,我哋從嗰邊回去吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆,別管蝙蝠了,我們從那邊回去吧!

passages.original: We seem to get worse and worse off all the time.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋似乎一直越嚟越糟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們似乎一直越來越糟。」

passages.original: “Listen!” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「聽!」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽!」他說。

passages.original: Profound silence; silence so deep that even their breathings were conspicuous in the hush.
passages.vernacular: 深沉嘅寂靜;如此深嘅寂靜,連佢哋嘅呼吸喺靜謐中都顯得突出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 深沉的寂靜;如此深的寂靜,連他們的呼吸在靜謐中都顯得突出。

passages.original: Tom shouted.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喊咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆喊了一聲。

passages.original: The call went echoing down the empty aisles and died out in the distance in a faint sound that resembled a ripple of mocking laughter.
passages.vernacular: 呼喊聲喺空蕩蕩嘅走廊回響,消失喺遠處,變成一種類似嘲笑嘅漣漪嘅微弱聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呼喊聲在空蕩蕩的走廊回響,消失在遠處,變成一種類似嘲笑的漣漪的微弱聲音。

passages.original: “Oh, don’t do it again, Tom, it is too horrid,” said Becky.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,唔好再喊喇,湯姆,太可怕喇,」貝琪講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不要再喊了,湯姆,太可怕了,」貝琪說。

passages.original: “It is horrid, but I better, Becky; they might hear us, you know,” and he shouted again.
passages.vernacular: 「係可怕,但我最好喊,貝琪;佢哋可能聽到我哋,你知道,」佢又喊咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是可怕,但我最好喊,貝琪;他們可能聽到我們,你知道,」他又喊了一聲。

passages.original: The “might” was even a chillier horror than the ghostly laughter, it so confessed a perishing hope.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個「可能」比鬼一般嘅笑聲更令人發冷,佢咁承認咗一個正在消亡嘅希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個「可能」比鬼一般的笑聲更令人發冷,它那麼承認了一個正在消亡的希望。

passages.original: The children stood still and listened; but there was no result.
passages.vernacular: 細路哋站住傾聽;但冇結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們站著傾聽;但沒有結果。

passages.original: Tom turned upon the back track at once, and hurried his steps.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆即刻轉身走回頭路,加快腳步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆馬上轉身走回頭路,加快腳步。

passages.original: It was but a little while before a certain indecision in his manner revealed another fearful fact to Becky—he could not find his way back!
passages.vernacular: 冇多久,佢態度中某種猶豫向貝琪顯示咗另一個可怕嘅事實——佢找唔到回去嘅路喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒多久,他態度中某種猶豫向貝琪顯示了另一個可怕的事實——他找不到回去的路了!

passages.original: “Oh, Tom, you didn’t make any marks!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆,你冇做任何標記!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆,你沒做任何標記!」

passages.original: “Becky, I was such a fool!
passages.vernacular: 「貝琪,我真係傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貝琪,我真是傻瓜!

passages.original: Such a fool!
passages.vernacular: 真係傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真是傻瓜!

passages.original: I never thought we might want to come back!
passages.vernacular: 我從冇想到我哋可能要回嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒想到我們可能要回來!

passages.original: No—I can’t find the way.
passages.vernacular: 不——我找唔到路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不——我找不到路。

passages.original: It’s all mixed up.”
passages.vernacular: 全搞混喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 全搞混了。」

passages.original: “Tom, Tom, we’re lost! we’re lost!
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,湯姆,我哋迷路喇!我哋迷路喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,湯姆,我們迷路了!我們迷路了!

passages.original: We never can get out of this awful place!
passages.vernacular: 我哋永遠出不咗呢個可怕嘅地方!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們永遠出不了這個可怕的地方!

passages.original: Oh, why did we ever leave the others!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我哋點解要離開其他人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我們為什麼要離開其他人!」

passages.original: She sank to the ground and burst into such a frenzy of crying that Tom was appalled with the idea that she might die, or lose her reason.
passages.vernacular: 佢倒喺地上,爆發出咁瘋狂嘅哭泣,湯姆被佢可能死去或失去理智嘅念頭嚇壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她倒在地上,爆發出那麼瘋狂的哭泣,湯姆被她可能死去或失去理智的念頭嚇壞了。

passages.original: He sat down by her and put his arms around her; she buried her face in his bosom, she clung to him, she poured out her terrors, her unavailing regrets, and the far echoes turned them all to jeering laughter.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐喺佢旁邊,用手臂摟住佢;佢把臉埋喺佢胸前,緊緊抱住佢,傾瀉佢嘅恐懼、佢無濟於事嘅後悔,遠處嘅回聲把佢哋全變成嘲弄嘅笑聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐在她旁邊,用手臂摟住她;她把臉埋在他胸前,緊緊抱住他,傾瀉她的恐懼、她無濟於事的後悔,遠處的回聲把它們全變成嘲弄的笑聲。

passages.original: Tom begged her to pluck up hope again, and she said she could not.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆懇求佢重新振作希望,佢講佢唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆懇求她重新振作希望,她說她不能。

passages.original: He fell to blaming and abusing himself for getting her into this miserable situation; this had a better effect.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始責備同辱罵自己把佢帶入呢悲慘嘅處境;呢有較好嘅效果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他開始責備和辱罵自己把她帶入這悲慘的處境;這有較好的效果。

passages.original: She said she would try to hope again, she would get up and follow wherever he might lead if only he would not talk like that any more.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢會試住再有希望,佢會站起嚟跟隨佢帶領嘅任何地方,只要佢唔再嗰樣講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她會試著再有希望,她會站起來跟隨他帶領的任何地方,只要他不再那樣說話。

passages.original: For he was no more to blame than she, she said.
passages.vernacular: 因為佢並不比佢更該受責備,佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為他並不比她更該受責備,她說。

passages.original: So they moved on again—aimlessly—simply at random—all they could do was to move, keep moving.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋又繼續前進——漫無目的——完全隨機——佢哋能做嘅只係移動,不斷移動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們又繼續前進——漫無目的——完全隨機——他們能做的只是移動,不斷移動。

passages.original: For a little while, hope made a show of reviving—not with any reason to back it, but only because it is its nature to revive when the spring has not been taken out of it by age and familiarity with failure.
passages.vernacular: 有一小會兒,希望裝模作樣地復甦——冇任何理由支持,只係因為當春天冇被年齡同對失敗嘅熟悉取走時,復甦係佢嘅天性。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一小會兒,希望裝模作樣地復甦——沒有任何理由支持,只是因為當春天沒有被年齡和對失敗的熟悉取走時,復甦是它的天性。

passages.original: By-and-by Tom took Becky’s candle and blew it out.
passages.vernacular: 不久湯姆攞過貝琪嘅蠟燭吹滅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久湯姆拿過貝琪的蠟燭吹滅了。

passages.original: This economy meant so much!
passages.vernacular: 呢種節約意味住咁多!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種節約意味著那麼多!

passages.original: Words were not needed.
passages.vernacular: 不需要言語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不需要言語。

passages.original: Becky understood, and her hope died again.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪明白喇,佢嘅希望又死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪明白了,她的希望又死了。

passages.original: She knew that Tom had a whole candle and three or four pieces in his pockets—yet he must economize.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道湯姆有一整支蠟燭同三四截喺口袋裡——然而佢必須節約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她知道湯姆有一整支蠟燭和三四截在口袋裡——然而他必須節約。

passages.original: By-and-by, fatigue began to assert its claims; the children tried to pay attention, for it was dreadful to think of sitting down when time was grown to be so precious, moving, in some direction, in any direction, was at least progress and might bear fruit; but to sit down was to invite death and shorten its pursuit.
passages.vernacular: 不久疲勞開始提出要求;細路哋試圖注意,因為喺時間變得咁寶貴時想到坐下係可怕嘅,向某個方向、任何方向移動,至少係進步,可能結果;但坐下就係邀請死亡,縮短佢嘅追趕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久疲勞開始提出要求;孩子們試圖注意,因為在時間變得這麼寶貴時想到坐下是可怕的,向某個方向、任何方向移動,至少是進步,可能結果;但坐下就是邀請死亡,縮短它的追趕。

passages.original: At last Becky’s frail limbs refused to carry her farther.
passages.vernacular: 最後貝琪虛弱嘅四肢拒絕再帶佢走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後貝琪虛弱的四肢拒絕再帶她走了。

passages.original: She sat down.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她坐下。

passages.original: Tom rested with her, and they talked of home, and the friends there, and the comfortable beds and, above all, the light!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆同佢一起休息,佢哋談論家、嗰度嘅朋友、舒適嘅床,最重要嘅係光!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆同她一起休息,他們談論家、那裡的朋友、舒適的床,最重要的是光!

passages.original: Becky cried, and Tom tried to think of some way of comforting her, but all his encouragements were grown thread-bare with use, and sounded like sarcasms.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪哭喇,湯姆試圖想出安慰佢嘅方法,但佢所有嘅鼓勵都因使用而變得破舊,聽起嚟像諷刺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪哭了,湯姆試圖想出安慰她的方法,但他所有的鼓勵都因使用而變得破舊,聽起來像諷刺。

passages.original: Fatigue bore so heavily upon Becky that she drowsed off to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 疲勞咁沉重地壓喺貝琪身上,佢打盹瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 疲勞那麼沉重地壓在貝琪身上,她打盹睡著了。

passages.original: Tom was grateful.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆好感激。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆很感激。

passages.original: He sat looking into her drawn face and saw it grow smooth and natural under the influence of pleasant dreams; and by-and-by a smile dawned and rested there.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐住睇佢憔悴嘅臉,睇到佢喺愉快嘅夢嘅影響下變得平滑自然;不久一個微笑出現並停喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐著看她憔悴的臉,看到它在愉快的夢的影響下變得平滑自然;不久一個微笑出現並停在那裡。

passages.original: The peaceful face reflected somewhat of peace and healing into his own spirit, and his thoughts wandered away to bygone times and dreamy memories.
passages.vernacular: 平靜嘅臉畀佢嘅精神反射咗啲平靜同癒合,佢嘅思緒飄向過去嘅時光同夢幻般嘅記憶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 平靜的臉給他的精神反射了一些平靜和癒合,他的思緒飄向過去的時光和夢幻般的記憶。

passages.original: While he was deep in his musings, Becky woke up with a breezy little laugh—but it was stricken dead upon her lips, and a groan followed it.
passages.vernacular: 佢深陷沉思時,貝琪帶住一聲輕快嘅小笑醒嚟——但佢死喺佢嘅嘴唇上,隨後係一聲呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他深陷沉思時,貝琪帶著一聲輕快的小笑醒來——但它死在她的嘴唇上,隨後是一聲呻吟。

passages.original: “Oh, how could I sleep!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我點能瞓住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我怎麼能睡著!

passages.original: I wish I never, never had waked!
passages.vernacular: 我真希望我從冇、從冇醒嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望我從沒、從沒醒來!

passages.original: No!
passages.vernacular: 不!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不!

passages.original: No, I don’t, Tom!
passages.vernacular: 不,我不,湯姆!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我不,湯姆!

passages.original: Don’t look so!
passages.vernacular: 別嗰樣睇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別那樣看!

passages.original: I won’t say it again.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔再講喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不再說了。」

passages.original: “I’m glad you’ve slept, Becky; you’ll feel rested, now, and we’ll find the way out.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興你瞓喇,貝琪;你而家會覺得休息好喇,我哋會找到出路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興你睡了,貝琪;你現在會覺得休息好了,我們會找到出路。」

passages.original: “We can try, Tom; but I’ve seen such a beautiful country in my dream.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋可以試,湯姆;但我喺夢裡睇到咗一個咁美麗嘅國家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們可以試,湯姆;但我在夢裡看到了一個那麼美麗的國家。

passages.original: I reckon we are going there.”
passages.vernacular: 我想我哋正要去嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我們正要去那裡。」

passages.original: “Maybe not, maybe not.
passages.vernacular: 「或者不,或者不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許不,也許不。

passages.original: Cheer up, Becky, and let’s go on trying.”
passages.vernacular: 振作,貝琪,讓我哋繼續試。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 振作,貝琪,讓我們繼續試。」

passages.original: They rose up and wandered along, hand in hand and hopeless.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋站起嚟,手拉著手,漫無希望地遊蕩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們站起來,手拉著手,漫無希望地遊蕩。

passages.original: They tried to estimate how long they had been in the cave, but all they knew was that it seemed days and weeks, and yet it was plain that this could not be, for their candles were not gone yet.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋試圖估計喺洞裡多久喇,但佢哋只知道似乎有幾天幾個星期,然而好明顯呢唔可能,因為佢哋嘅蠟燭仲冇用完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們試圖估計在洞裡多久了,但他們只知道似乎有幾天幾個星期,然而很明顯這不可能,因為他們的蠟燭還沒用完。

passages.original: A long time after this—they could not tell how long—Tom said they must go softly and listen for dripping water—they must find a spring.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢之後好長時間——佢哋講不出多久——湯姆講佢哋必須輕輕地走,聽有冇滴水聲——佢哋必須找到泉水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這之後很長時間——他們說不出多久——湯姆說他們必須輕輕地走,聽有沒有滴水聲——他們必須找到泉水。

passages.original: They found one presently, and Tom said it was time to rest again.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋找到咗一個,湯姆講又該休息喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他們找到了一個,湯姆說又該休息了。

passages.original: Both were cruelly tired, yet Becky said she thought she could go a little farther.
passages.vernacular: 兩人都累得殘酷,但貝琪講佢想佢可以再走啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩人都累得殘酷,但貝琪說她想她可以再走一點。

passages.original: She was surprised to hear Tom dissent.
passages.vernacular: 佢驚訝地聽到湯姆不同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她驚訝地聽到湯姆不同意。

passages.original: She could not understand it.
passages.vernacular: 佢不明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不明白。

passages.original: They sat down, and Tom fastened his candle to the wall in front of them with some clay.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋坐下,湯姆用啲黏土把佢嘅蠟燭固定喺佢哋面前嘅牆上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們坐下,湯姆用一些黏土把他的蠟燭固定在他們面前的牆上。

passages.original: Thought was soon busy; nothing was said for some time.
passages.vernacular: 思緒好快忙碌起嚟;有一陣子冇人講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 思緒很快忙碌起來;有一陣子沒人說話。

passages.original: Then Becky broke the silence:
passages.vernacular: 然後貝琪打破沉默:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後貝琪打破沉默:

passages.original: “Tom, I am so hungry!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我好餓!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我好餓!」

passages.original: Tom took something out of his pocket.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆從口袋裡攞出乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆從口袋裡拿出什麼。

passages.original: “Do you remember this?” said he.
passages.vernacular: 「你仲記得呢個嗎?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你還記得這個嗎?」他說。

passages.original: Becky almost smiled.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪幾乎笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪幾乎笑了。

passages.original: “It’s our wedding-cake, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「係我哋嘅結婚蛋糕,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是我們的結婚蛋糕,湯姆。」

passages.original: “Yes—I wish it was as big as a barrel, for it’s all we’ve got.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——我希望佢有一個桶咁大,因為呢個係我哋全部嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——我希望它有一個桶那麼大,因為這是我們全部的東西。」

passages.original: “I saved it from the picnic for us to dream on, Tom, the way grownup people do with wedding-cake—but it’ll be our—”
passages.vernacular: 「我從野餐中留下佢畀我哋做夢用,湯姆,像大人用結婚蛋糕嗰樣——但佢將係我哋嘅——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從野餐中留下它給我們做夢用,湯姆,像大人用結婚蛋糕那樣——但它將是我們的——」

passages.original: She dropped the sentence where it was.
passages.vernacular: 佢把呢句話停喺咗嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把這句話停在了那裡。

passages.original: Tom divided the cake and Becky ate with good appetite, while Tom nibbled at his moiety.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆把蛋糕分開,貝琪食得有好胃口,而湯姆啃佢嘅嗰一半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆把蛋糕分開,貝琪吃得有好胃口,而湯姆啃他的那一半。

passages.original: There was abundance of cold water to finish the feast with.
passages.vernacular: 有大量冷水嚟結束盛宴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有大量冷水來結束盛宴。

passages.original: By-and-by Becky suggested that they move on again.
passages.vernacular: 漸漸地貝琪建議佢哋再往前走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漸漸地貝琪建議他們再往前走。

passages.original: Tom was silent a moment.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆沉默咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆沉默了一會兒。

passages.original: Then he said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他說:

passages.original: “Becky, can you bear it if I tell you something?”
passages.vernacular: 「貝琪,如果我告訴你一件事,你能承受嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「貝琪,如果我告訴你一件事,你能承受嗎?」

passages.original: Becky’s face paled, but she thought she could.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪嘅臉變白,但佢想佢能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪的臉變白,但她想她能。

passages.original: “Well, then, Becky, we must stay here, where there’s water to drink.
passages.vernacular: 「咁,貝琪,我哋必須留喺呢度,呢度有水飲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,貝琪,我們必須留在這裡,這裡有水喝。

passages.original: That little piece is our last candle!”
passages.vernacular: 嗰一小截係我哋嘅最後一支蠟燭!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那一小截是我們的最後一支蠟燭!」

passages.original: Becky gave loose to tears and wailings.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪放聲哭泣哀號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪放聲哭泣哀號。

passages.original: Tom did what he could to comfort her, but with little effect.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆盡力安慰佢,但效果甚微。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆盡力安慰她,但效果甚微。

passages.original: At length Becky said:
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒貝琪講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒貝琪說:

passages.original: “Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆!」

passages.original: “Well, Becky?”
passages.vernacular: 「點喇,貝琪?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了,貝琪?」

passages.original: “They’ll miss us and hunt for us!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋會想念我哋並尋找我哋!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們會想念我們並尋找我們!」

passages.original: “Yes, they will!
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢哋會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,他們會!

passages.original: Certainly they will!”
passages.vernacular: 當然佢哋會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然他們會!」

passages.original: “Maybe they’re hunting for us now, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者佢哋而家正在找我哋,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許他們現在正在找我們,湯姆。」

passages.original: “Why, I reckon maybe they are.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,我想或者係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,我想也許是。

passages.original: I hope they are.”
passages.vernacular: 我希望係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望是。」

passages.original: “When would they miss us, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋乜嘢時候會想念我哋,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們什麼時候會想念我們,湯姆?」

passages.original: “When they get back to the boat, I reckon.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想係回到船上嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是回到船上的時候。」

passages.original: “Tom, it might be dark then—would they notice we hadn’t come?”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,嗰時可能天黑喇——佢哋會注意到我哋冇嚟嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,那時可能天黑了——他們會注意到我們沒來嗎?」

passages.original: “I don’t know.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: But anyway, your mother would miss you as soon as they got home.”
passages.vernacular: 但無論如何,你媽媽一回到家就會想念你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但無論如何,你媽媽一回到家就會想念你。」

passages.original: A frightened look in Becky’s face brought Tom to his senses and he saw that he had made a blunder.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪臉上驚恐嘅神情使湯姆醒悟,佢睇出自己犯咗錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪臉上驚恐的神情使湯姆醒悟,他看出自己犯了錯。

passages.original: Becky was not to have gone home that night!
passages.vernacular: 貝琪嗰晚本不該回家!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪那晚本不該回家!

passages.original: The children became silent and thoughtful.
passages.vernacular: 細路哋變得沉默而若有所思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們變得沉默而若有所思。

passages.original: In a moment a new burst of grief from Becky showed Tom that the thing in his mind had struck hers also—that the Sabbath morning might be half spent before Mrs. Thatcher discovered that Becky was not at Mrs. Harper’s.
passages.vernacular: 不久貝琪新嘅一陣悲傷向湯姆表明,佢心裡嘅事都打擊咗佢嘅心——安息日早晨可能過去一半,撒切爾太太才會發現貝琪不喺哈珀太太家!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久貝琪新的一陣悲傷向湯姆表明,他心裡的事也打擊了她的心——安息日早晨可能過去一半,撒切爾太太才會發現貝琪不在哈珀太太家!

passages.original: The children fastened their eyes upon their bit of candle and watched it melt slowly and pitilessly away; saw the half inch of wick stand alone at last; saw the feeble flame rise and fall, climb the thin column of smoke, linger at its top a moment, and then—the horror of utter darkness reigned!
passages.vernacular: 細路哋把眼睛盯喺佢哋嗰截蠟燭上,睇佢慢慢無情地融化;睇到半英寸嘅燭芯最後獨自站住;睇到微弱嘅火焰升起又落下,爬上細細嘅煙柱,喺頂端停留片刻,然後——完全黑暗嘅恐怖統治喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們把眼睛盯在他們那截蠟燭上,看它慢慢無情地融化;看到半英寸的燭芯最後獨自站著;看到微弱的火焰升起又落下,爬上細細的煙柱,在頂端停留片刻,然後——完全黑暗的恐怖統治了!

passages.original: How long afterward it was that Becky came to a slow consciousness that she was crying in Tom’s arms, neither could tell.
passages.vernacular: 過咗多久貝琪才慢慢意識到佢喺湯姆懷裡哭,兩人都講不出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了多久貝琪才慢慢意識到她在湯姆懷裡哭,兩人都說不出。

passages.original: All that they knew was, that after what seemed a mighty stretch of time, both awoke out of a dead stupor of sleep and resumed their miseries once more.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋只知道,喺似乎好長嘅一段時間後,兩人從死一般嘅昏瞓中醒嚟,再次恢復佢哋嘅痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們只知道,在似乎很長的一段時間後,兩人從死一般的昏睡中醒來,再次恢復他們的痛苦。

passages.original: Tom said it might be Sunday, now—maybe Monday.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講而家可能係星期日——或者星期一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說現在可能是星期日——也許星期一。

passages.original: He tried to get Becky to talk, but her sorrows were too oppressive, all her hopes were gone.
passages.vernacular: 佢試圖讓貝琪講話,但佢嘅悲傷太沉重,佢所有嘅希望都消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他試圖讓貝琪說話,但她的悲傷太沉重,她所有的希望都消失了。

passages.original: Tom said that they must have been missed long ago, and no doubt the search was going on.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講佢哋一定早就被發現唔見喇,毫無疑問搜尋正在進行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說他們一定早就被發現不見了,毫無疑問搜尋正在進行。

passages.original: He would shout and maybe some one would come.
passages.vernacular: 佢要喊,或者有人會嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要喊,也許有人會來。

passages.original: He tried it; but in the darkness the distant echoes sounded so hideously that he tried it no more.
passages.vernacular: 佢試喇;但喺黑暗中遠處嘅回聲聽起嚟咁可怕,佢唔再試喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他試了;但在黑暗中遠處的回聲聽起來那麼可怕,他不再試了。

passages.original: The hours wasted away, and hunger came to torment the captives again.
passages.vernacular: 時辰消磨過去,飢餓又嚟折磨囚犯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時辰消磨過去,飢餓又來折磨囚犯。

passages.original: A portion of Tom’s half of the cake was left; they divided and ate it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嗰半塊蛋糕仲剩一部分;佢哋分咗食喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆那半塊蛋糕還剩一部分;他們分了吃了。

passages.original: But they seemed hungrier than before.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋似乎比以前更餓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他們似乎比以前更餓了。

passages.original: The poor morsel of food only whetted desire.
passages.vernacular: 嗰可憐嘅一小口食物只係勾起咗慾望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那可憐的一小口食物只是勾起了慾望。

passages.original: By-and-by Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 不久湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久湯姆說:

passages.original: “SH!
Did you hear that?”
passages.vernacular: 你聽到咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聽到了嗎?」

passages.original: Both held their breath and listened.
passages.vernacular: 兩人屏住呼吸傾聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩人屏住呼吸傾聽。

passages.original: There was a sound like the faintest, far-off shout.
passages.vernacular: 有一個聲音像係最微弱嘅遠處嘅喊叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一個聲音像是最微弱的遠處的喊叫。

passages.original: Instantly Tom answered it, and leading Becky by the hand, started groping down the corridor in its direction.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆即刻回應,牽住貝琪嘅手,朝佢嘅方向摸索住下走廊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆立刻回應,牽著貝琪的手,朝它的方向摸索著下走廊。

passages.original: Presently he listened again; again the sound was heard, and apparently a little nearer.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢又聽;又聽到嗰個聲音,而且顯然近咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久他又聽;又聽到那個聲音,而且顯然近了一點。

passages.original: “It’s them!” said Tom; “they’re coming!
passages.vernacular: 「係佢哋!」湯姆講;「佢哋嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是他們!」湯姆說;「他們來了!

passages.original: Come along, Becky—we’re all right now!”
passages.vernacular: 嚟,貝琪——我哋而家冇事喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,貝琪——我們現在沒事了!」

passages.original: The joy of the prisoners was almost overwhelming.
passages.vernacular: 囚犯哋嘅喜悅幾乎壓倒一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 囚犯們的喜悅幾乎壓倒一切。

passages.original: Their speed was slow, however, because pitfalls were somewhat common, and had to be guarded against.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢哋嘅速度好慢,因為陷阱相當常見,必須提防。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,他們的速度很慢,因為陷阱相當常見,必須提防。

passages.original: They shortly came to one and had to stop.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不久到咗一個,唔得不停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不久到了一個,不得不停下。

passages.original: It might be three feet deep, it might be a hundred—there was no passing it at any rate.
passages.vernacular: 佢可能三呎深,可能一百呎——無論如何無法通過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它可能三呎深,可能一百呎——無論如何無法通過。

passages.original: Tom got down on his breast and reached as far down as he could.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆趴下,盡量往下伸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆趴下,盡量往下伸。

passages.original: No bottom.
passages.vernacular: 冇底。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有底。

passages.original: They must stay there and wait until the searchers came.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋必須留喺嗰度,等搜尋者嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們必須留在那裡,等搜尋者來。

passages.original: They listened; evidently the distant shoutings were growing more distant! a moment or two more and they had gone altogether.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋傾聽;顯然遠處嘅喊叫越嚟越遠喇!再過一兩分鐘就完全冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們傾聽;顯然遠處的喊叫越來越遠了!再過一兩分鐘就完全沒了。

passages.original: The heart-sinking misery of it!
passages.vernacular: 呢令人心沉嘅痛苦!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這令人心沉的痛苦!

passages.original: Tom whooped until he was hoarse, but it was of no use.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喊到嘶啞,但冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆喊到嘶啞,但沒有用。

passages.original: He talked hopefully to Becky; but an age of anxious waiting passed and no sounds came again.
passages.vernacular: 佢對貝琪滿懷希望地講話;但經過一個焦急等待嘅世紀,再冇聲音傳嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對貝琪滿懷希望地說話;但經過一個焦急等待的世紀,再沒有聲音傳來。

passages.original: The children groped their way back to the spring.
passages.vernacular: 細路哋摸索住回到泉水邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們摸索著回到泉水邊。

passages.original: The weary time dragged on; they slept again, and awoke famished and woe-stricken.
passages.vernacular: 疲憊嘅時間拖延住;佢哋又瞓住喇,醒嚟時飢餓且悲痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 疲憊的時間拖延著;他們又睡著了,醒來時飢餓且悲痛。

passages.original: Tom believed it must be Tuesday by this time.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆相信呢陣一定係星期二喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆相信這時一定是星期二了。

passages.original: Now an idea struck him.
passages.vernacular: 而家一個念頭襲上佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在一個念頭襲上他。

passages.original: There were some side passages near at hand.
passages.vernacular: 附近有啲支通道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 附近有一些支通道。

passages.original: It would be better to explore some of these than bear the weight of the heavy time in idleness.
passages.vernacular: 探索其中啲,比無所事事地承受沉重嘅時間好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 探索其中一些,比無所事事地承受沉重的時間好。

passages.original: He took a kite-line from his pocket, tied it to a projection, and he and Becky started, Tom in the lead, unwinding the line as he groped along.
passages.vernacular: 佢從口袋裡攞出一根風箏線,綁喺一個突起上,佢同貝琪出發喇,湯姆領頭,一邊摸索一邊放線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從口袋裡拿出一根風箏線,綁在一個突起上,他和貝琪出發了,湯姆領頭,一邊摸索一邊放線。

passages.original: At the end of twenty steps the corridor ended in a “jumping-off place.”
passages.vernacular: 走咗二十步,走廊喺一個「跳下去嘅地方」結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走了二十步,走廊在一個「跳下去的地方」結束。

passages.original: Tom got down on his knees and felt below, and then as far around the corner as he could reach with his hands conveniently; he made an effort to stretch yet a little farther to the right, and at that moment, not twenty yards away, a human hand, holding a candle, appeared from behind a rock!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆跪下摸下面,然後盡量摸到手能方便夠到嘅拐角嗰邊;佢努力再往右伸啲,就喺嗰時,唔到二十碼外,一隻手,握住一支蠟燭,從一塊岩石後面出現喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆跪下摸下面,然後盡量摸到手能方便夠到的拐角那邊;他努力再往右伸一點,就在那時,不到二十碼外,一隻手,握著一支蠟燭,從一塊岩石後面出現了!

passages.original: Tom lifted up a glorious shout, and instantly that hand was followed by the body it belonged to—Injun Joe’s!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆發出一聲光榮嘅喊叫,嗰隻手即刻被佢所屬嘅身體跟隨——印第安喬嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆發出一聲光榮的喊叫,那隻手立刻被它所屬的身體跟隨——印第安喬的!

passages.original: Tom was paralyzed; he could not move.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆癱瘓喇;佢動不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆癱瘓了;他動不了。

passages.original: He was vastly gratified the next moment, to see the “Spaniard” take to his heels and get himself out of sight.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻佢好欣慰地睇到嗰「西班牙人」拔腿就跑,消失喺視線外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻他非常欣慰地看到那「西班牙人」拔腿就跑,消失在視線外。

passages.original: Tom wondered that Joe had not recognized his voice and come over and killed him for testifying in court.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆驚訝喬冇認出佢嘅聲音,過嚟殺死佢,因為佢喺法庭作證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆驚訝喬沒有認出他的聲音,過來殺死他,因為他在法庭作證。

passages.original: But the echoes must have disguised the voice.
passages.vernacular: 但回聲一定偽裝咗聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但回聲一定偽裝了聲音。

passages.original: Without doubt, that was it, he reasoned.
passages.vernacular: 毫無疑問,係咁樣,佢推論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 毫無疑問,是這樣,他推論。

passages.original: Tom’s fright weakened every muscle in his body.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅驚嚇使佢身體嘅每一塊肌肉都軟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的驚嚇使他身體的每一塊肌肉都軟了。

passages.original: He said to himself that if he had strength enough to get back to the spring he would stay there, and nothing should tempt him to run the risk of meeting Injun Joe again.
passages.vernacular: 佢對自己講,如果佢有足夠嘅力氣回到泉水嗰度,佢會留喺嗰度,乜嘢都唔能夠誘使佢再冒遇到印第安喬嘅風險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他對自己說,如果他有足夠的力氣回到泉水那裡,他會留在那裡,什麼也不能誘使他再冒遇到印第安喬的風險。

passages.original: He was careful to keep from Becky what it was he had seen.
passages.vernacular: 佢小心不讓貝琪知道佢睇到嘅係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他小心不讓貝琪知道他看到的是什麼。

passages.original: He told her he had only shouted “for luck.”
passages.vernacular: 佢告訴佢佢只係「碰運氣」喊咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他告訴她他只是「碰運氣」喊了一聲。

passages.original: But hunger and wretchedness rise superior to fears in the long run.
passages.vernacular: 但從長遠睇,飢餓同悲慘超越恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但從長遠看,飢餓和悲慘超越恐懼。

passages.original: Another tedious wait at the spring and another long sleep brought changes.
passages.vernacular: 喺泉水邊又一次乏味嘅等待同又一次長長嘅瞓眠帶嚟咗變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在泉水邊又一次乏味的等待和又一次長長的睡眠帶來了變化。

passages.original: The children awoke tortured with a raging hunger.
passages.vernacular: 細路哋醒嚟,被狂暴嘅飢餓折磨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 孩子們醒來,被狂暴的飢餓折磨。

passages.original: Tom believed that it must be Wednesday or Thursday or even Friday or Saturday, now, and that the search had been given over.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆相信而家一定係星期三、星期四,甚至星期五或星期六喇,搜尋已經放棄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆相信現在一定是星期三、星期四,甚至星期五或星期六了,搜尋已經放棄。

passages.original: He proposed to explore another passage.
passages.vernacular: 佢提議探索另一條通道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他提議探索另一條通道。

passages.original: He felt willing to risk Injun Joe and all other terrors.
passages.vernacular: 佢願意冒印第安喬同所有其他恐怖嘅險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他願意冒印第安喬和所有其他恐怖的險。

passages.original: But Becky was very weak.
passages.vernacular: 但貝琪好虛弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但貝琪非常虛弱。

passages.original: She had sunk into a dreary apathy and would not be roused.
passages.vernacular: 佢陷入咗淒涼嘅冷漠,喚不醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她陷入了淒涼的冷漠,喚不醒。

passages.original: She said she would wait, now, where she was, and die—it would not be long.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢而家要喺佢所在嘅地方等待並死去——唔會太久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她現在要在她所在的地方等待並死去——不會太久。

passages.original: She told Tom to go with the kite-line and explore if he chose; but she implored him to come back every little while and speak to her; and she made him promise that when the awful time came, he would stay by her and hold her hand until all was over.
passages.vernacular: 佢告訴湯姆,如果佢選擇,可以帶風箏線去探索;但佢懇求佢不時回嚟同佢講話;佢讓佢答應,可怕嘅時刻來臨時,佢會留喺佢身邊,握住佢嘅手,直到一切結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她告訴湯姆,如果他選擇,可以帶風箏線去探索;但她懇求他不時回來同她說話;她讓他答應,可怕的時刻來臨時,他會留在她身邊,握著她的手,直到一切結束。

passages.original: Tom kissed her, with a choking sensation in his throat, and made a show of being confident of finding the searchers or an escape from the cave; then he took the kite-line in his hand and went groping down one of the passages on his hands and knees, distressed with hunger and sick with bodings of coming doom.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆吻咗佢,喉嚨裡有窒息嘅感覺,裝作有信心找到搜尋者或從山洞逃脫;然後佢把風箏線握喺手中,手腳並用地摸索住下咗其中一條通道,被飢餓折磨,為即將來臨嘅厄運嘅預感而難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆吻了她,喉嚨裡有窒息的感覺,裝作有信心找到搜尋者或從山洞逃脫;然後他把風箏線握在手中,手腳並用地摸索著下了其中一條通道,被飢餓折磨,為即將來臨的厄運的預感而難受。

chapters.title: Chapter XXXII: Tom Tells the Story of their Escape 第三十二章:逃脫的故事

passages.original: CH Tuesday afternoon came, and waned to the twilight.
passages.vernacular: 星期二下午嚟喇,漸漸變成暮色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期二下午來了,漸漸變成暮色。

passages.original: The village of St. Petersburg still mourned.
passages.vernacular: 聖彼得堡村子仍喺哀悼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖彼得堡村子仍在哀悼。

passages.original: The lost children had not been found.
passages.vernacular: 失蹤嘅細路哋仲冇找到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 失蹤的孩子們還沒有找到。

passages.original: Public prayers had been offered up for them, and many and many a private prayer that had the petitioner’s whole heart in it; but still no good news came from the cave.
passages.vernacular: 為佢哋獻上咗公共禱告,同許許多多帶住祈求者全部心意嘅私人禱告;但山洞仍然冇傳嚟好消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為他們獻上了公共禱告,和許許多多帶著祈求者全部心意的私人禱告;但山洞仍然沒有傳來好消息。

passages.original: The majority of the searchers had given up the quest and gone back to their daily avocations, saying that it was plain the children could never be found.
passages.vernacular: 大多數搜尋者已放棄尋找,回到佢哋日常嘅職業,講好明顯細路哋永遠找唔到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大多數搜尋者已放棄尋找,回到他們日常的職業,說很明顯孩子們永遠找不到了。

passages.original: Mrs. Thatcher was very ill, and a great part of the time delirious.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾太太病得好重,大部分時間講胡話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾太太病得很重,大部分時間說胡話。

passages.original: People said it was heartbreaking to hear her call her child, and raise her head and listen a whole minute at a time, then lay it wearily down again with a moan.
passages.vernacular: 人哋講聽佢呼喚細路,抬起頭聽整整一分鐘,然後呻吟住疲憊地又放下,令人心碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們說聽她呼喚孩子,抬起頭聽整整一分鐘,然後呻吟著疲憊地又放下,令人心碎。

passages.original: Aunt Polly had drooped into a settled melancholy, and her gray hair had grown almost white.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽垂頭陷入一種固定嘅憂鬱,佢嘅灰髮幾乎變白喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽垂頭陷入一種固定的憂鬱,她的灰髮幾乎變白了。

passages.original: The village went to its rest on Tuesday night, sad and forlorn.
passages.vernacular: 星期二晚上村子悲傷淒涼地入瞓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期二晚上村子悲傷淒涼地入睡了。

passages.original: Away in the middle of the night a wild peal burst from the village bells, and in a moment the streets were swarming with frantic half-clad people, who shouted, “Turn out! turn out! they’re found! they’re found!”
passages.vernacular: 喺半夜嘅深處,村裡嘅鐘突然爆發出一陣狂亂嘅鐘聲,轉眼街上擠滿咗半穿衣服嘅瘋狂人群,佢哋喊道:「起嚟!起嚟!找到喇!找到喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在半夜的深處,村裡的鐘突然爆發出一陣狂亂的鐘聲,轉眼街上擠滿了半穿衣服的瘋狂人群,他們喊道:「起來!起來!找到了!找到了!」

passages.original: Tin pans and horns were added to the din, the population massed itself and moved toward the river, met the children coming in an open carriage drawn by shouting citizens, thronged around it, joined its homeward march, and swept magnificently up the main street roaring huzzah after huzzah!
passages.vernacular: 錫鍋同號角加入咗喧鬧,人群聚集起嚟,向河邊移動,遇到細路哋坐住由歡呼嘅市民拉嘅敞篷馬車而嚟,擠喺周圍,加入佢嘅回家行列,壯觀地橫掃主街,一聲接一聲地吼住萬歲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 錫鍋和號角加入了喧鬧,人群聚集起來,向河邊移動,遇到孩子們坐著由歡呼的市民拉的敞篷馬車而來,擠在周圍,加入它的回家行列,壯觀地橫掃主街,一聲接一聲地吼著萬歲!

passages.original: The village was illuminated; nobody went to bed again; it was the greatest night the little town had ever seen.
passages.vernacular: 村子燈火通明;冇人再去瞓覺;呢個係呢個小鎮見過嘅最盛大嘅夜晚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 村子燈火通明;沒有人再去睡覺;這是這個小鎮見過的最盛大的夜晚。

passages.original: During the first half-hour a procession of villagers filed through Judge Thatcher’s house, seized the saved ones and kissed them, squeezed Mrs. Thatcher’s hand, tried to speak but couldn’t—and drifted out raining tears all over the place.
passages.vernacular: 最初半小時,村民隊伍魚貫走過撒切爾法官嘅家,抓住獲救嘅細路哋親吻,握撒切爾太太嘅手,想講話卻講不出——然後淚雨灑滿各處地飄出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最初半小時,村民隊伍魚貫走過撒切爾法官的家,抓住獲救的孩子們親吻,握撒切爾太太的手,想說話卻說不出——然後淚雨灑滿各處地飄出去。

passages.original: Aunt Polly’s happiness was complete, and Mrs. Thatcher’s nearly so.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽嘅幸福係完整嘅,撒切爾太太嘅幾乎完整。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽的幸福是完整的,撒切爾太太的幾乎完整。
