passages.original: It would be complete, however, as soon as the messenger dispatched with the great news to the cave should get the word to her husband.
passages.vernacular: 不過,一旦被派去山洞報告大消息嘅信使把話傳畀佢丈夫,就會完整。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,一旦被派去山洞報告大消息的信使把話傳給她丈夫,就會完整。

passages.original: Tom lay upon a sofa with an eager auditory about him and told the history of the wonderful adventure, putting in many striking additions to adorn it withal; and closed with a description of how he left Becky and went on an exploring expedition; how he followed two avenues as far as his kite-line would reach; how he followed a third to the fullest stretch of the kite-line, and was about to turn back when he glimpsed a far-off speck that looked like daylight; dropped the line and groped toward it, pushed his head and shoulders through a small hole, and saw the broad Mississippi rolling by!
passages.vernacular: 湯姆躺喺沙發上,周圍有熱切嘅聽眾,講述咗呢次奇妙冒險嘅歷史,加入許多驚人嘅添加嚟裝飾佢;最後描述咗佢點樣離開貝琪出去探險;點樣沿兩條通道走到佢嘅風箏線所及嘅地方;點樣沿住第三條走到風箏線嘅最大長度,正要回頭時瞥見遠處一個像日光嘅小點;放下線摸索住朝佢走去,把頭同肩膀伸過一個小洞,睇到寬闊嘅密西西比河流過!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆躺在沙發上,周圍有熱切的聽眾,講述了這次奇妙冒險的歷史,加入許多驚人的添加來裝飾它;最後描述了他怎樣離開貝琪出去探險;怎樣沿兩條通道走到他的風箏線所及的地方;怎樣沿著第三條走到風箏線的最大長度,正要回頭時瞥見遠處一個像日光的小點;放下線摸索著朝它走去,把頭和肩膀伸過一個小洞,看到寬闊的密西西比河流過!

passages.original: And if it had only happened to be night he would not have seen that speck of daylight and would not have explored that passage any more!
passages.vernacular: 如果碰巧係夜晚,佢就睇唔到嗰個日光點,都唔會再探索嗰條通道喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果碰巧是夜晚,他就看不到那個日光點,也不會再探索那條通道了!

passages.original: He told how he went back for Becky and broke the good news and she told him not to fret her with such stuff, for she was tired, and knew she was going to die, and wanted to.
passages.vernacular: 佢講點樣回去找貝琪,告訴佢好消息,佢叫佢唔好攞呢種嘢煩佢,因為佢累喇,知道自己要死喇,而且想死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他講怎樣回去找貝琪,告訴她好消息,她叫他不要拿這種東西煩她,因為她累了,知道自己要死了,而且想死。

passages.original: He described how he labored with her and convinced her; and how she almost died for joy when she had groped to where she actually saw the blue speck of daylight; how he pushed his way out at the hole and then helped her out; how they sat there and cried for gladness; how some men came along in a skiff and Tom hailed them and told them their situation and their famished condition; how the men didn’t believe the wild tale at first, “because,” said they, “you are five miles down the river below the valley the cave is in”—then took them aboard, rowed to a house, gave them supper, made them rest till two or three hours after dark and then brought them home.
passages.vernacular: 佢描述佢點樣同佢努力並講服佢;佢摸索到真嘅睇到藍色嘅日光點時,點樣高興得幾乎死去;佢點樣從洞口擠出嚟,然後幫佢出嚟;佢哋點樣坐喺嗰度高興地哭;啲人點樣乘小艇經過,湯姆向佢哋招呼,告訴佢哋佢哋嘅處境同飢餓嘅狀態;嗰啲人起初點樣不相信呢個荒誕嘅故事,「因為」,佢哋講,「你喺山洞所在山谷下游五英里嘅河邊」——然後點樣把佢哋接上船,划到一所房子,畀佢哋晚飯,讓佢哋休息到天黑後兩三個小時,然後送佢哋回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他描述他怎樣同她努力並說服她;她摸索到真的看到藍色的日光點時,怎樣高興得幾乎死去;他怎樣從洞口擠出來,然後幫她出來;他們怎樣坐在那裡高興地哭;一些人怎樣乘小艇經過,湯姆向他們招呼,告訴他們他們的處境和飢餓的狀態;那些人起初怎樣不相信這個荒誕的故事,「因為」,他們說,「你在山洞所在山谷下游五英里的河邊」——然後怎樣把他們接上船,划到一所房子,給他們晚飯,讓他們休息到天黑後兩三個小時,然後送他們回家。

passages.original: Before day-dawn, Judge Thatcher and the handful of searchers with him were tracked out, in the cave, by the twine clews they had strung behind them, and informed of the great news.
passages.vernacular: 黎明前,撒切爾法官同同佢喺一起嘅少數搜尋者,憑藉佢哋身後拉嘅細繩線索喺山洞裡被找到,並獲知咗大消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黎明前,撒切爾法官和同他在一起的少數搜尋者,憑藉他們身後拉的細繩線索在山洞裡被找到,並獲知了大消息。

passages.original: Three days and nights of toil and hunger in the cave were not to be shaken off at once, as Tom and Becky soon discovered.
passages.vernacular: 喺山洞裡三天三夜嘅勞累同飢餓唔係即刻能擺脫嘅,湯姆同貝琪好快發現咗呢點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在山洞裡三天三夜的勞累和飢餓不是立刻能擺脫的,湯姆和貝琪很快發現了這點。

passages.original: They were bedridden all of Wednesday and Thursday, and seemed to grow more and more tired and worn, all the time.
passages.vernacular: 星期三同星期四佢哋整天臥床,似乎一直越嚟越累同疲憊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期三和星期四他們整天臥床,似乎一直越來越累和疲憊。

passages.original: Tom got about, a little, on Thursday, was downtown Friday, and nearly as whole as ever Saturday; but Becky did not leave her room until Sunday, and then she looked as if she had passed through a wasting illness.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆星期四稍微起嚟活動喇,星期五到咗鎮上,星期六幾乎完全恢復;但貝琪直到星期日才離開佢嘅房間,嗰時佢睇起嚟像係經過咗一場消耗性嘅疾病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆星期四稍微起來活動了,星期五到了鎮上,星期六幾乎完全恢復;但貝琪直到星期日才離開她的房間,那時她看起來像是經過了一場消耗性的疾病。

passages.original: Tom learned of Huck’s sickness and went to see him on Friday, but could not be admitted to the bedroom; neither could he on Saturday or Sunday.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆聽講咗哈克嘅病,星期五去睇佢,但唔能夠進臥室;星期六同星期日都唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆聽說了哈克的病,星期五去看他,但不能進臥室;星期六和星期日也不能。

passages.original: He was admitted daily after that, but was warned to keep still about his adventure and introduce no exciting topic.
passages.vernacular: 此後每天都被允許進去,但被警告對佢嘅冒險保持安靜,唔好引入任何刺激嘅話題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此後每天都被允許進去,但被警告對他的冒險保持安靜,不要引入任何刺激的話題。

passages.original: The Widow Douglas stayed by to see that he obeyed.
passages.vernacular: 道格拉斯寡婦留下嚟睇佢係咪服從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 道格拉斯寡婦留下來看他是否服從。

passages.original: At home Tom learned of the Cardiff Hill event; also that the “ragged man’s” body had eventually been found in the river near the ferry-landing; he had been drowned while trying to escape, perhaps.
passages.vernacular: 喺家裡湯姆得知卡迪夫山事件;仲有「破爛人」嘅屍體最終喺渡口附近嘅河裡被找到;佢或者係喺試圖逃跑時淹死嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在家裡湯姆得知卡迪夫山事件;還有「破爛人」的屍體最終在渡口附近的河裡被找到;他也許是在試圖逃跑時淹死的。

passages.original: About a fortnight after Tom’s rescue from the cave, he started off to visit Huck, who had grown plenty strong enough, now, to hear exciting talk, and Tom had some that would interest him, he thought.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆從山洞獲救大約兩個星期後,佢出發去睇哈克,哈克而家已經足夠強壯,可以聽刺激嘅話喇,湯姆想佢有些話會讓佢感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆從山洞獲救大約兩個星期後,他出發去看哈克,哈克現在已經足夠強壯,可以聽刺激的話了,湯姆想他有些話會讓他感興趣。

passages.original: Judge Thatcher’s house was on Tom’s way, and he stopped to see Becky.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾法官嘅家喺湯姆嘅路上,佢停下嚟睇貝琪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾法官的家在湯姆的路上,他停下來看貝琪。

passages.original: The Judge and some friends set Tom to talking, and some one asked him ironically if he wouldn’t like to go to the cave again.
passages.vernacular: 法官同啲朋友讓湯姆講話,有人諷刺地問佢係咪唔想再去山洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法官和一些朋友讓湯姆講話,有人諷刺地問他是否不想再去山洞。

passages.original: Tom said he thought he wouldn’t mind it.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講佢想佢唔會介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說他想他不會介意。

passages.original: The Judge said:
passages.vernacular: 法官講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法官說:

passages.original: “Well, there are others just like you, Tom, I’ve not the least doubt.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,仲有其他人像你一樣,湯姆,我毫不懷疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,還有其他人像你一樣,湯姆,我毫不懷疑。

passages.original: But we have taken care of that.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋已經處理喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們已經處理了。

passages.original: Nobody will get lost in that cave any more.”
passages.vernacular: 冇人會再喺嗰個山洞裡迷路喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人會再在那個山洞裡迷路了。」

passages.original: “Why?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」

passages.original: “Because I had its big door sheathed with boiler iron two weeks ago, and triple-locked—and I’ve got the keys.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為兩個星期前我用鍋爐鐵皮把佢嘅大門包上喇,並上咗三重鎖——我有鑰匙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為兩個星期前我用鍋爐鐵皮把它的大門包上了,並上了三重鎖——我有鑰匙。」

passages.original: Tom turned as white as a sheet.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆臉色變得像床單一樣白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆臉色變得像床單一樣白。

passages.original: “What’s the matter, boy!
passages.vernacular: 「點喇,細路!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼了,孩子!

passages.original: Here, run, somebody!
passages.vernacular: 呢度,嚟人,快!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡,來人,快!

passages.original: Fetch a glass of water!”
passages.vernacular: 攞杯水嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿杯水來!」

passages.original: The water was brought and thrown into Tom’s face.
passages.vernacular: 水攞嚟喇,潑到湯姆臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 水拿來了,潑到湯姆臉上。

passages.original: “Ah, now you’re all right.
passages.vernacular: 「啊,而家你冇事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,現在你沒事了。

passages.original: What was the matter with you, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 你頭先點喇,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你剛才怎麼了,湯姆?」

passages.original: “Oh, Judge, Injun Joe’s in the cave!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,法官,印第安喬喺山洞裡!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,法官,印第安喬在山洞裡!」

chapters.title: Chapter XXXIII: The Fate of Injun Joe 第三十三章:印第安喬的下場

passages.original: CH Within a few minutes the news had spread, and a dozen skiff-loads of men were on their way to McDougal’s cave, and the ferryboat, well filled with passengers, soon followed.
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘內消息傳開,一打小艇嘅人正在去麥克杜格爾洞嘅路上,載滿乘客嘅渡船不久都跟上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘內消息傳開,一打小艇的人正在去麥克杜格爾洞的路上,載滿乘客的渡船不久也跟上。

passages.original: Tom Sawyer was in the skiff that bore Judge Thatcher.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆·索亞喺載住撒切爾法官嘅小艇裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆·索亞在載著撒切爾法官的小艇裡。

passages.original: When the cave door was unlocked, a sorrowful sight presented itself in the dim twilight of the place.
passages.vernacular: 山洞嘅門打開時,喺嗰個地方昏暗嘅暮色中,一幅悲慘嘅景象呈現出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 山洞的門打開時,在那個地方昏暗的暮色中,一幅悲慘的景象呈現出來。

passages.original: Injun Joe lay stretched upon the ground, dead, with his face close to the crack of the door, as if his longing eyes had been fixed, to the latest moment, upon the light and the cheer of the free world outside.
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬直挺挺地躺喺地上,死喇,臉貼近門縫,好像佢渴望嘅眼睛一直盯住,到最後一刻,外面自由世界嘅光同歡樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬直挺挺地躺在地上,死了,臉貼近門縫,好像他渴望的眼睛一直盯著,到最後一刻,外面自由世界的光和歡樂。

passages.original: Tom was touched, for he knew by his own experience how this wretch had suffered.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆被觸動,因為佢憑自己嘅經驗知道呢個可憐蟲受咗多少苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆被觸動,因為他憑自己的經驗知道這個可憐蟲受了多少苦。

passages.original: His pity was moved, but nevertheless he felt an abounding sense of relief and security, now, which revealed to him in a degree which he had not fully appreciated before how vast a weight of dread had been lying upon him since the day he lifted his voice against this bloody-minded outcast.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅憐憫被打動,但佢仍然感到一種充沛嘅解脫同安全感,呢向佢顯示咗喺某種程度上佢以前冇充分理解嘅:自從佢對呢個嗜血嘅流浪者開口作證嗰天起,有幾咁巨大嘅恐懼重量壓喺佢身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的憐憫被打動,但他仍然感到一種充沛的解脫和安全感,這向他顯示了在某種程度上他以前沒有充分理解的:自從他對這個嗜血的流浪者開口作證那天起,有多麼巨大的恐懼重量壓在他身上。

passages.original: Injun Joe’s bowie-knife lay close by, its blade broken in two.
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬嘅鮑伊刀躺喺旁邊,刀刃斷成兩截。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬的鮑伊刀躺在旁邊,刀刃斷成兩截。

passages.original: The great foundation-beam of the door had been chipped and hacked through, with tedious labor; useless labor, too, it was, for the native rock formed a sill outside it, and upon that stubborn material the knife had wrought no effect; the only damage done was to the knife itself.
passages.vernacular: 門嘅大基樑被費力地削砍穿喇;勞動,都係徒勞嘅,因為天然岩石喺佢外面形成一道門檻,而喺嗰堅硬嘅材料上刀冇起作用;造成嘅唯一損害係刀本身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門的大基樑被費力地削砍穿了;勞動,也是徒勞的,因為天然岩石在它外面形成一道門檻,而在那堅硬的材料上刀沒有起作用;造成的唯一損害是刀本身。

passages.original: But if there had been no stony obstruction there the labor would have been useless still, for if the beam had been wholly cut away Injun Joe could not have squeezed his body under the door, and he knew it.
passages.vernacular: 但即使嗰度冇石頭嘅阻礙,勞動仍然係徒勞,因為如果樑被完全切掉,印第安喬都唔能夠把身體擠過門下,佢知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但即使那裡沒有石頭的阻礙,勞動仍然是徒勞,因為如果樑被完全切掉,印第安喬也不能把身體擠過門下,他知道。

passages.original: So he had only hacked that place in order to be doing something—in order to pass the weary time—in order to employ his tortured faculties.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢砍嗰個地方只係為了做點乜嘢——為了打發疲倦嘅時間——為了使用佢被折磨嘅官能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他砍那個地方只是為了做點什麼——為了打發疲倦的時間——為了使用他被折磨的官能。

passages.original: Ordinarily one could find half a dozen bits of candle stuck around in the crevices of this vestibule, left there by tourists; but there were none now.
passages.vernacular: 平時可以喺呢個前廳嘅縫隙裡找到半打遊客留下嘅蠟燭頭;但而家一個都冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 平時可以在這個前廳的縫隙裡找到半打遊客留下的蠟燭頭;但現在一個也沒有了。

passages.original: The prisoner had searched them out and eaten them.
passages.vernacular: 囚犯把佢哋搜尋出嚟食掉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 囚犯把它們搜尋出來吃掉了。

passages.original: He had also contrived to catch a few bats, and these, also, he had eaten, leaving only their claws.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲設法抓咗幾隻蝙蝠,都食喇,只剩下爪子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他還設法抓了幾隻蝙蝠,也吃了,只剩下爪子。

passages.original: The poor unfortunate had starved to death.
passages.vernacular: 呢個可憐嘅不幸者餓死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個可憐的不幸者餓死了。

passages.original: In one place, near at hand, a stalagmite had been slowly growing up from the ground for ages, builded by the water-drip from a stalactite overhead.
passages.vernacular: 喺近處嘅一處,一根石筍從地上慢慢生長了無數世紀,由頭頂鐘乳石嘅滴水築成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在近處的一處,一根石筍從地上慢慢生長了無數世紀,由頭頂鐘乳石的滴水築成。

passages.original: The captive had broken off the stalagmite, and upon the stump had placed a stone, wherein he had scooped a shallow hollow to catch the precious drop that fell once in every three minutes with the dreary regularity of a clock-tick—a dessertspoonful once in four and twenty hours.
passages.vernacular: 囚犯折斷咗石筍,喺殘樁上放咗一塊石頭,喺上面挖咗一個淺凹,接住每三分鐘一次以鐘表滴答般淒涼嘅規律性掉下嘅寶貴一滴——二十四小時才一甜品匙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 囚犯折斷了石筍,在殘樁上放了一塊石頭,在上面挖了一個淺凹,接住每三分鐘一次以鐘表滴答般淒涼的規律性掉下的寶貴一滴——二十四小時才一甜品匙。

passages.original: That drop was falling when the Pyramids were new; when Troy fell; when the foundations of Rome were laid; when Christ was crucified; when the Conqueror created the British empire; when Columbus sailed; when the massacre at Lexington was “news.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰一滴喺金字塔仲新時就喺落;特洛伊陷落時;羅馬奠基時;基督被釘十字架時;征服者創建大不列顛帝國時;哥倫布起航時;列克星敦屠殺定係「新聞」時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那一滴在金字塔還新時就在落;特洛伊陷落時;羅馬奠基時;基督被釘十字架時;征服者創建大不列顛帝國時;哥倫布起航時;列克星敦屠殺還是「新聞」時。

passages.original: It is falling now; it will still be falling when all these things shall have sunk down the afternoon of history, and the twilight of tradition, and been swallowed up in the thick night of oblivion.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家喺落;當所有呢啲事都沉入歷史嘅下午、傳講嘅暮色、被吞冇喺遺忘嘅濃重夜裡時,佢仍將喺落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它現在在落;當所有這些事都沉入歷史的下午、傳說的暮色、被吞沒在遺忘的濃重夜裡時,它仍將在落。

passages.original: Has everything a purpose and a mission?
passages.vernacular: 一切都有目的同使命嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切都有目的和使命嗎?

passages.original: Did this drop fall patiently during five thousand years to be ready for this flitting human insect’s need? and has it another important object to accomplish ten thousand years to come?
passages.vernacular: 呢一滴有耐心地落咗五千年,為了準備滿足呢隻匆匆人類昆蟲嘅需要嗎?佢仲有別嘅重要目標要喺未來一萬年內完成嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一滴有耐心地落了五千年,為了準備滿足這隻匆匆人類昆蟲的需要嗎?它還有別的重要目標要在未來一萬年內完成嗎?

passages.original: No matter.
passages.vernacular: 無所謂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無所謂。

passages.original: It is many and many a year since the hapless half-breed scooped out the stone to catch the priceless drops, but to this day the tourist stares longest at that pathetic stone and that slow-dropping water when he comes to see the wonders of McDougal’s cave.
passages.vernacular: 自從呢個不幸嘅混血兒挖出石頭接取無價嘅水滴以來,已有許許多多年喇,但直到今日,遊客嚟睇麥克杜格爾洞嘅奇觀時,凝視嗰塊可憐嘅石頭同嗰緩慢滴水嘅時間最長。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從這個不幸的混血兒挖出石頭接取無價的水滴以來,已有許許多多年了,但直到今天,遊客來看麥克杜格爾洞的奇觀時,凝視那塊可憐的石頭和那緩慢滴水的時間最長。

passages.original: Injun Joe’s cup stands first in the list of the cavern’s marvels; even “Aladdin’s Palace” cannot rival it.
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬嘅杯子喺山洞奇觀嘅名單上排第一;連「阿拉丁宮」都無法同佢競爭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬的杯子在山洞奇觀的名單上排第一;連「阿拉丁宮」也無法同它競爭。

passages.original: Injun Joe was buried near the mouth of the cave; and people flocked there in boats and wagons from the towns and from all the farms and hamlets for seven miles around; they brought their children, and all sorts of provisions, and confessed that they had had almost as satisfactory a time at the funeral as they could have had at the hanging.
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬被葬喺山洞口附近;人哋從七英里範圍內嘅城鎮、所有農場同小村莊乘船同馬車蜂擁而至;佢哋帶嚟細路同各種食物,並承認佢哋喺葬禮上玩得幾乎同喺絞刑時一樣令人滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬被葬在山洞口附近;人們從七英里範圍內的城鎮、所有農場和小村莊乘船和馬車蜂擁而至;他們帶來孩子和各種食物,並承認他們在葬禮上玩得幾乎與在絞刑時一樣令人滿意。

passages.original: This funeral stopped the further growth of one thing—the petition to the governor for Injun Joe’s pardon.
passages.vernacular: 呢次葬禮阻止咗一件事嘅進一步發展——向州長為印第安喬請求特赦嘅請願。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次葬禮阻止了一件事的進一步發展——向州長為印第安喬請求特赦的請願。

passages.original: The petition had been largely signed; many tearful and eloquent meetings had been held, and a committee of sappy women been appointed to go in deep mourning and wail around the governor, and implore him to be a merciful ass and trample his duty under foot.
passages.vernacular: 請願已大量簽名;舉行咗許多含淚而雄辯嘅會議,指定咗一個由多愁善感嘅女人組成嘅委員會,穿住深喪服去州長周圍哀號,懇求佢做一個仁慈嘅蠢驢、把佢嘅職責踩喺腳下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請願已大量簽名;舉行了許多含淚而雄辯的會議,指定了一個由多愁善感的女人組成的委員會,穿著深喪服去州長周圍哀號,懇求他做一個仁慈的蠢驢、把他的職責踩在腳下。

passages.original: Injun Joe was believed to have killed five citizens of the village, but what of that?
passages.vernacular: 據信印第安喬殺死咗村子裡嘅五個公民,但嗰又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據信印第安喬殺死了村子裡的五個公民,但那又怎樣?

passages.original: If he had been Satan himself there would have been plenty of weaklings ready to scribble their names to a pardon-petition, and drip a tear on it from their permanently impaired and leaky water-works.
passages.vernacular: 即使佢係撒旦本人,都會有大量軟弱嘅人準備喺特赦請願上簽名,並用佢哋永久受損漏水嘅水龍頭滴一滴淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使他是撒旦本人,也會有大量軟弱的人準備在特赦請願上簽名,並用他們永久受損漏水的水龍頭滴一滴淚。

passages.original: The morning after the funeral Tom took Huck to a private place to have an important talk.
passages.vernacular: 葬禮第二天早晨,湯姆把哈克帶到一個私密嘅地方作一次重要談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葬禮第二天早晨,湯姆把哈克帶到一個私密的地方作一次重要談話。

passages.original: Huck had learned all about Tom’s adventure from the Welshman and the Widow Douglas, by this time, but Tom said he reckoned there was one thing they had not told him; that thing was what he wanted to talk about now.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣哈克已經從威爾斯人同道格拉斯寡婦嗰度知道咗湯姆嘅全部冒險,但湯姆講佢想有一件事佢哋冇告訴佢;嗰件事就係佢而家想講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時哈克已經從威爾斯人和道格拉斯寡婦那裡知道了湯姆的全部冒險,但湯姆說他想有一件事他們沒告訴他;那件事就是他現在想說的。

passages.original: Huck’s face saddened.
passages.vernacular: 哈克嘅臉變得悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克的臉變得悲傷。

passages.original: He said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “I know what it is.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道是什麼。

passages.original: You got into No. 2 and never found anything but whiskey.
passages.vernacular: 你進咗二號房,除咗威士忌乜嘢都冇找到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你進了二號房,除了威士忌什麼也沒找到。

passages.original: Nobody told me it was you; but I just knowed it must ’a’ ben you, soon as I heard ’bout that whiskey business; and I knowed you hadn’t got the money becuz you’d ’a’ got at me some way or other and told me even if you was mum to everybody else.
passages.vernacular: 冇人告訴我係你;但我一聽到威士忌嘅事就知道一定係你;我知道你冇攞到錢,因為你一定會想辦法找到我告訴我,即使你對別人都沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒人告訴我是你;但我一聽到威士忌的事就知道一定是你;我知道你沒拿到錢,因為你一定會想辦法找到我告訴我,即使你對別人都沉默。

passages.original: Tom, something’s always told me we’d never get holt of that swag.”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,總有嘢告訴我我哋永遠攞唔到嗰筆贓物。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,總有東西告訴我我們永遠拿不到那筆贓物。」

passages.original: “Why, Huck, I never told on that tavern-keeper.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,哈克,我從冇告發嗰個旅店老闆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,哈克,我從沒告發那個旅店老闆。

passages.original: You know his tavern was all right the Saturday I went to the picnic.
passages.vernacular: 你知道我去野餐嘅嗰個星期六佢嘅旅店一切正常。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我去野餐的那個星期六他的旅店一切正常。

passages.original: Don’t you remember you was to watch there that night?”
passages.vernacular: 你不記得嗰晚你要喺嗰度守望嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不記得那晚你要在那裡守望嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh yes!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的!

passages.original: Why, it seems ’bout a year ago.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,似乎係大約一年前嘅事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,似乎是大約一年前的事了。

passages.original: It was that very night that I follered Injun Joe to the widder’s.”
passages.vernacular: 就係嗰晚我跟住印第安喬到寡婦家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是那晚我跟著印第安喬到寡婦家。」

passages.original: “You followed him?”
passages.vernacular: 「你跟蹤佢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你跟蹤他?」

passages.original: “Yes—but you keep mum.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——但你保持沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——但你保持沉默。

passages.original: I reckon Injun Joe’s left friends behind him, and I don’t want ’em souring on me and doing me mean tricks.
passages.vernacular: 我想印第安喬身後留下咗朋友,我唔想佢哋對我酸臉,耍卑鄙把戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想印第安喬身後留下了朋友,我不想他們對我酸臉,耍卑鄙把戲。

passages.original: If it hadn’t ben for me he’d be down in Texas now, all right.”
passages.vernacular: 要唔係我,佢而家喺德克薩斯,好好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是我,他現在在德克薩斯,好好的。」

passages.original: Then Huck told his entire adventure in confidence to Tom, who had only heard of the Welshman’s part of it before.
passages.vernacular: 然後哈克把佢嘅全部冒險祕密地告訴咗湯姆,湯姆以前只聽講過威爾斯人嗰部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後哈克把他的全部冒險祕密地告訴了湯姆,湯姆以前只聽說過威爾斯人那部分。

passages.original: “Well,” said Huck, presently, coming back to the main question, “whoever nipped the whiskey in No. 2, nipped the money, too, I reckon—anyways it’s a goner for us, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」哈克不久講,回到主要問題,「不管邊個喺二號房偷走咗威士忌,我想都偷走咗錢——無論如何佢對我哋係冇喇,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」哈克不久說,回到主要問題,「不管誰在二號房偷走了威士忌,我想也偷走了錢——無論如何它對我們是沒了,湯姆。」

passages.original: “Huck, that money wasn’t ever in No. 2!”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,嗰筆錢從冇喺二號房過!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,那筆錢從沒在二號房過!」

passages.original: “What!”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼!」

passages.original: Huck searched his comrade’s face keenly.
passages.vernacular: 哈克敏銳地搜索同伴嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克敏銳地搜索同伴的臉。

passages.original: “Tom, have you got on the track of that money again?”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,你又找到嗰筆錢嘅蹤跡咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,你又找到那筆錢的蹤跡了嗎?」

passages.original: “Huck, it’s in the cave!”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,佢喺山洞裡!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,它在山洞裡!」

passages.original: Huck’s eyes blazed.
passages.vernacular: 哈克嘅眼睛發亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克的眼睛發亮。

passages.original: “Say it again, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「再講一遍,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再說一遍,湯姆。」

passages.original: “The money’s in the cave!”
passages.vernacular: 「錢喺山洞裡!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「錢在山洞裡!」

passages.original: “Tom—honest injun, now—is it fun, or earnest?”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆——講真嘅,而家——係開玩笑定係認真?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆——說真的,現在——是開玩笑還是認真?」

passages.original: “Earnest, Huck—just as earnest as ever I was in my life.
passages.vernacular: 「認真,哈克——像我一生中任何時候一樣認真。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「認真,哈克——像我一生中任何時候一樣認真。

passages.original: Will you go in there with me and help get it out?”
passages.vernacular: 你願意同我進去幫忙把佢弄出嚟嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你願意同我進去幫忙把它弄出來嗎?」

passages.original: “I bet I will!
passages.vernacular: 「我打賭我願意!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我打賭我願意!

passages.original: I will if it’s where we can blaze our way to it and not get lost.”
passages.vernacular: 如果係喺我哋能做標記找到佢、不迷路嘅地方,我就去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是在我們能做標記找到它、不迷路的地方,我就去。」

passages.original: “Huck, we can do that without the least little bit of trouble in the world.”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,我哋可以毫無啲麻煩地做到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,我們可以毫無一點麻煩地做到。」

passages.original: “Good as wheat!
passages.vernacular: 「好極喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好極了!

passages.original: What makes you think the money’s—”
passages.vernacular: 你點認為錢係——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼認為錢是——」

passages.original: “Huck, you just wait till we get in there.
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,你等我哋進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,你等我們進去。

passages.original: If we don’t find it I’ll agree to give you my drum and every thing I’ve got in the world.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋找唔到,我同意把我嘅鼓同我世界上所有嘢畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們找不到,我同意把我的鼓和我世界上所有東西給你。

passages.original: I will, by jings.”
passages.vernacular: 我會,天呀。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會,天哪。」

passages.original: “All right—it’s a whiz.
passages.vernacular: 「好——太棒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好——太棒了。

passages.original: When do you say?”
passages.vernacular: 你講乜嘢時候?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼時候?」

passages.original: “Right now, if you say it.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,如果你講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,如果你說。

passages.original: Are you strong enough?”
passages.vernacular: 你夠強壯嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你夠強壯嗎?」

passages.original: “Is it far in the cave?
passages.vernacular: 「山洞裡面遠嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「山洞裡面遠嗎?

passages.original: I ben on my pins a little, three or four days, now, but I can’t walk more’n a mile, Tom—least I don’t think I could.”
passages.vernacular: 我已經能站起嚟啲喇,有三四天喇,但我走不咗超過一英里,湯姆——至少我不認為我能。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經能站起來一點了,有三四天了,但我走不了超過一英里,湯姆——至少我不認為我能。」

passages.original: “It’s about five mile into there the way anybody but me would go, Huck, but there’s a mighty short cut that they don’t anybody but me know about.
passages.vernacular: 「按任何人,除咗我,會走嘅路,到嗰度大約五英里,哈克,但有一條冇人除咗我知道嘅好短嘅捷徑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「按任何人,除了我,會走的路,到那裡大約五英里,哈克,但有一條沒有人除了我知道的非常短的捷徑。

passages.original: Huck, I’ll take you right to it in a skiff.
passages.vernacular: 哈克,我用小艇直接帶你去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克,我用小艇直接帶你去。

passages.original: I’ll float the skiff down there, and I’ll pull it back again all by myself.
passages.vernacular: 我把小艇漂下去,再獨自把佢拉回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把小艇漂下去,再獨自把它拉回來。

passages.original: You needn’t ever turn your hand over.”
passages.vernacular: 你唔使動一下手。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不必動一下手。」

passages.original: “Less start right off, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋即刻出發,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們馬上出發,湯姆。」

passages.original: “All right.
We want some bread and meat, and our pipes, and a little bag or two, and two or three kite-strings, and some of these new-fangled things they call lucifer matches.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要啲麵包同肉、我哋嘅菸斗、一兩個小袋子、兩三根風箏線,同啲佢哋稱為「路西弗火柴」嘅新奇嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要一些麵包和肉、我們的菸斗、一兩個小袋子、兩三根風箏線,和一些他們稱為「路西弗火柴」的新奇東西。

passages.original: I tell you, many’s the time I wished I had some when I was in there before.”
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你,我以前喺嗰度時,多少次希望有啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你,我以前在那裡時,多少次希望有一些。」

passages.original: A trifle after noon the boys borrowed a small skiff from a citizen who was absent, and got under way at once.
passages.vernacular: 中午剛過一會兒,男孩哋從一位不喺嘅市民嗰度借咗一艘小艇,即刻出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 中午剛過一會兒,男孩們從一位不在的市民那裡借了一艘小艇,馬上出發。

passages.original: When they were several miles below “Cave Hollow,” Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺「山洞凹谷」下游幾英里時,湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在「山洞凹谷」下游幾英里時,湯姆說:

passages.original: “Now you see this bluff here looks all alike all the way down from the cave hollow—no houses, no wood-yards, bushes all alike.
passages.vernacular: 「而家你睇呢個懸崖從山洞凹谷一路下嚟睇起嚟都一樣——冇房子,冇木材場,灌木叢都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你看這個懸崖從山洞凹谷一路下來看起來都一樣——沒有房子,沒有木材場,灌木叢都一樣。

passages.original: But do you see that white place up yonder where there’s been a landslide?
passages.vernacular: 但你睇到嗰邊嗰塊有山崩嘅白色地方嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你看到那邊那塊有山崩的白色地方嗎?

passages.original: Well, that’s one of my marks.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,嗰個係我嘅標記之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,那是我的標記之一。

passages.original: We’ll get ashore, now.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋而家上岸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們現在上岸。」

passages.original: They landed.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋上咗岸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們上了岸。

passages.original: “Now, Huck, where we’re a-standing you could touch that hole I got out of with a fishing-pole.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,哈克,我哋站嘅地方你用一根釣竿就能碰到我出嚟嘅嗰個洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,哈克,我們站的地方你用一根釣竿就能碰到我出來的那個洞。

passages.original: See if you can find it.”
passages.vernacular: 睇你能唔能夠找到。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看你能不能找到。」

passages.original: Huck searched all the place about, and found nothing.
passages.vernacular: 哈克搜遍周圍整個地方,乜嘢都冇找到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克搜遍周圍整個地方,什麼也沒找到。

passages.original: Tom proudly marched into a thick clump of sumach bushes and said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆驕傲地走進一叢茂密嘅漆樹灌木叢,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆驕傲地走進一叢茂密的漆樹灌木叢,說:

passages.original: “Here you are!
passages.vernacular: 「喺呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在這裡!

passages.original: Look at it, Huck; it’s the snuggest hole in this country.
passages.vernacular: 睇佢,哈克;佢係呢個國家最舒適嘅洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看它,哈克;它是這個國家最舒適的洞。

passages.original: You just keep mum about it.
passages.vernacular: 你保持沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你保持沉默。

passages.original: All along I’ve been wanting to be a robber, but I knew I’d got to have a thing like this, and where to run across it was the bother.
passages.vernacular: 我一直想當強盜,但我知道我得有一樣咁樣嘅嘢,而喺邊度找到係麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直想當強盜,但我知道我得有一樣這樣的東西,而在哪裡找到是麻煩。

passages.original: We’ve got it now, and we’ll keep it quiet, only we’ll let Joe Harper and Ben Rogers in—because of course there’s got to be a Gang, or else there wouldn’t be any style about it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋而家有喇,我哋要保密,只讓喬·哈珀同本·羅傑斯加入——因為當然必須有一個幫,否則就冇派頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們現在有了,我們要保密,只讓喬·哈珀和本·羅傑斯加入——因為當然必須有一個幫,否則就沒有派頭。

passages.original: Tom Sawyer’s Gang—it sounds splendid, don’t it, Huck?”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆·索亞幫——聽起嚟輝煌,唔係嗎,哈克?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆·索亞幫——聽起來輝煌,不是嗎,哈克?」

passages.original: “Well, it just does, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,確實,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,確實,湯姆。

passages.original: And who’ll we rob?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋搶邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們搶誰?」

passages.original: “Oh, most anybody.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,幾乎任何人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,幾乎任何人。

passages.original: Waylay people—that’s mostly the way.”
passages.vernacular: 攔路伏擊人——主要係呢個方式。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 攔路伏擊人——主要是這個方式。」

passages.original: “And kill them?”
passages.vernacular: 「並殺咗佢哋?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「並殺了他們?」

passages.original: “No, not always.
passages.vernacular: 「不,不總是。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不總是。

passages.original: Hive them in the cave till they raise a ransom.”
passages.vernacular: 把佢哋關喺山洞裡,直到佢哋籌到贖金。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把他們關在山洞裡,直到他們籌到贖金。」

passages.original: “What’s a ransom?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢係贖金?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼是贖金?」

passages.original: “Money.
You make them raise all they can, off’n their friends; and after you’ve kept them a year, if it ain’t raised then you kill them.
passages.vernacular: 你讓佢哋盡力從朋友嗰度籌到;你關咗佢哋一年後,如果仲冇籌到,就殺咗佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你讓他們盡力從朋友那裡籌到;你關了他們一年後,如果還沒籌到,就殺了他們。

passages.original: That’s the general way.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一般嘅方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一般的方式。

passages.original: Only you don’t kill the women.
passages.vernacular: 只係你不殺女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是你不殺女人。

passages.original: You shut up the women, but you don’t kill them.
passages.vernacular: 你把女人關起嚟,但不殺佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把女人關起來,但不殺她們。

passages.original: They’re always beautiful and rich, and awfully scared.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋總是美麗又富有,仲嚇壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們總是美麗又富有,還嚇壞了。

passages.original: You take their watches and things, but you always take your hat off and talk polite.
passages.vernacular: 你攞佢哋嘅錶之類嘅,但總是脫帽並禮貌地講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你拿她們的錶之類的,但總是脫帽並禮貌地說話。

passages.original: They ain’t anybody as polite as robbers—you’ll see that in any book.
passages.vernacular: 冇人像強盜咁有禮貌——你喺任何書裡都會睇到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人像強盜那麼有禮貌——你在任何書裡都會看到。

passages.original: Well, the women get to loving you, and after they’ve been in the cave a week or two weeks they stop crying and after that you couldn’t get them to leave.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,女人愛上你,喺山洞裡待咗一兩個星期後,佢哋唔再哭,此後你就趕不走佢哋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,女人愛上你,在山洞裡待了一兩個星期後,她們不再哭,此後你就趕不走她們了。

passages.original: If you drove them out they’d turn right around and come back.
passages.vernacular: 如果你把佢哋趕走,佢哋會轉身又回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你把她們趕走,她們會轉身又回來。

passages.original: It’s so in all the books.”
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅書裡都係咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的書裡都是這樣。」

passages.original: “Why, it’s real bully, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,真棒,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,真棒,湯姆。

passages.original: I believe it’s better’n to be a pirate.”
passages.vernacular: 我相信比當海盜仲好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信比當海盜還好。」

passages.original: “Yes, it’s better in some ways, because it’s close to home and circuses and all that.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,喺某些方面更好,因為佢靠近家同馬戲團之類嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,在某些方面更好,因為它靠近家和馬戲團之類的。」

passages.original: By this time everything was ready and the boys entered the hole, Tom in the lead.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣一切準備好喇,男孩哋進咗洞,湯姆領頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時一切準備好了,男孩們進了洞,湯姆領頭。

passages.original: They toiled their way to the farther end of the tunnel, then made their spliced kite-strings fast and moved on.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋辛苦地走到隧道嘅盡頭,然後把佢哋接起嚟嘅風箏線繫牢,繼續前進。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們辛苦地走到隧道的盡頭,然後把他們接起來的風箏線繫牢,繼續前進。

passages.original: A few steps brought them to the spring, and Tom felt a shudder quiver all through him.
passages.vernacular: 幾步把佢哋帶到泉水邊,湯姆感到一陣戰慄傳遍全身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾步把他們帶到泉水邊,湯姆感到一陣戰慄傳遍全身。

passages.original: He showed Huck the fragment of candle-wick perched on a lump of clay against the wall, and described how he and Becky had watched the flame struggle and expire.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀哈克睇停喺牆邊一塊黏土上嘅蠟燭芯碎片,描述佢同貝琪點樣睇住火焰掙扎熄滅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給哈克看停在牆邊一塊黏土上的蠟燭芯碎片,描述他和貝琪怎樣看著火焰掙扎熄滅。

passages.original: The boys began to quiet down to whispers, now, for the stillness and gloom of the place oppressed their spirits.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋而家開始安靜下嚟變成耳語,因為呢個地方嘅寂靜同昏暗壓抑住佢哋嘅精神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們現在開始安靜下來變成耳語,因為這個地方的寂靜和昏暗壓抑著他們的精神。

passages.original: They went on, and presently entered and followed Tom’s other corridor until they reached the “jumping-off place.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋繼續前進,不久進入並沿住湯姆嘅另一條走廊,直到到達「跳下去嘅地方」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們繼續前進,不久進入並沿著湯姆的另一條走廊,直到到達「跳下去的地方」。

passages.original: The candles revealed the fact that it was not really a precipice, but only a steep clay hill twenty or thirty feet high.
passages.vernacular: 蠟燭顯示出佢其實唔係懸崖,只係一座二三十呎高嘅陡黏土山。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蠟燭顯示出它其實不是懸崖,只是一座二三十呎高的陡黏土山。

passages.original: Tom whispered:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆低聲說:

passages.original: “Now I’ll show you something, Huck.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家我畀你睇點嘢,哈克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我給你看點東西,哈克。」

passages.original: He held his candle aloft and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢舉起蠟燭,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他舉起蠟燭,說:

passages.original: “Look as far around the corner as you can.
passages.vernacular: 「盡量睇拐角嗰邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「盡量看拐角那邊。

passages.original: Do you see that?
passages.vernacular: 你睇到嗰個咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看到那個了嗎?

passages.original: There—on the big rock over yonder—done with candle-smoke.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰度——喺嗰邊嘅大岩石上——用蠟燭煙畫嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡——在那邊的大岩石上——用蠟燭煙畫的。」

passages.original: “Tom, it’s a cross!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,係個十字架!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,是個十字架!」

passages.original: “Now where’s your Number Two?
passages.vernacular: 「而家你嘅二號喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你的二號在哪裡?

passages.original: ‘under the cross,’ hey?
passages.vernacular: 『喺十字架下』,係吧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『在十字架下』,是吧?

passages.original: Right yonder’s where I saw Injun Joe poke up his candle, Huck!”
passages.vernacular: 就喺嗰邊,係我睇到印第安喬把蠟燭伸出嚟嘅地方,哈克!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在那邊,是我看到印第安喬把蠟燭伸出來的地方,哈克!」

passages.original: Huck stared at the mystic sign awhile, and then said with a shaky voice:
passages.vernacular: 哈克盯住嗰神祕嘅記號一會兒,然後用發抖嘅聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克盯著那神祕的記號一會兒,然後用發抖的聲音說:

passages.original: “Tom, less git out of here!”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我哋離開呢度!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我們離開這裡!」

passages.original: “What! and leave the treasure?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢!丟下寶藏?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼!丟下寶藏?」

passages.original: “Yes—leave it.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——丟下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——丟下。

passages.original: Injun Joe’s ghost is round about there, certain.”
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬嘅鬼魂肯定喺嗰附近。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬的鬼魂肯定在那附近。」

passages.original: “No it ain’t, Huck, no it ain’t.
passages.vernacular: 「不,不喺,哈克,不喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不在,哈克,不在。

passages.original: It would ha’nt the place where he died—away out at the mouth of the cave—five mile from here.”
passages.vernacular: 佢會喺佢死去嘅地方作祟——遠喺山洞口——離呢度五英里。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它會在他死去的地方作祟——遠在山洞口——離這裡五英里。」

passages.original: “No, Tom, it wouldn’t.
passages.vernacular: 「不,湯姆,唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,湯姆,不會。

passages.original: It would hang round the money.
passages.vernacular: 佢會喺錢附近徘徊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它會在錢附近徘徊。

passages.original: I know the ways of ghosts, and so do you.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道鬼魂嘅習性,你都知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道鬼魂的習性,你也知道。」

passages.original: Tom began to fear that Huck was right.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆開始擔心哈克係對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆開始擔心哈克是對的。

passages.original: Misgivings gathered in his mind.
passages.vernacular: 疑慮聚集喺佢腦子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 疑慮聚集在他腦子裡。

passages.original: But presently an idea occurred to him—
passages.vernacular: 但不久佢想到一個主意——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但不久他想到一個主意——

passages.original: “Lookyhere, Huck, what fools we’re making of ourselves!
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,哈克,我哋把自己弄得多傻!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,哈克,我們把自己弄得多傻!

passages.original: Injun Joe’s ghost ain’t a going to come around where there’s a cross!”
passages.vernacular: 印第安喬嘅鬼魂唔會到有十字架嘅地方嚟嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 印第安喬的鬼魂不會到有十字架的地方來的!」

passages.original: The point was well taken.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲講得好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一點說得好。

passages.original: It had its effect.
passages.vernacular: 佢起咗作用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它起了作用。

passages.original: “Tom, I didn’t think of that.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,我冇想到嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,我沒想到那個。

passages.original: But that’s so.
passages.vernacular: 但係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是這樣。

passages.original: It’s luck for us, that cross is.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個十字架對我哋係運氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個十字架對我們是運氣。

passages.original: I reckon we’ll climb down there and have a hunt for that box.”
passages.vernacular: 我想我哋爬下去,找嗰個箱子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我們爬下去,找那個箱子。」

passages.original: Tom went first, cutting rude steps in the clay hill as he descended.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆先去,下降時喺黏土山上砍出粗糙嘅台階。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆先去,下降時在黏土山上砍出粗糙的台階。

passages.original: Huck followed.
passages.vernacular: 哈克跟住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克跟著。

passages.original: Four avenues opened out of the small cavern which the great rock stood in.
passages.vernacular: 從大岩石所在嘅小洞穴開出四條通道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從大岩石所在的小洞穴開出四條通道。

passages.original: The boys examined three of them with no result.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋檢查咗其中三條,冇結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們檢查了其中三條,沒有結果。

passages.original: They found a small recess in the one nearest the base of the rock, with a pallet of blankets spread down in it; also an old suspender, some bacon rind, and the well-gnawed bones of two or three fowls.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺離岩石底部最近嘅一條裡發現一個小凹處,裡面鋪住毯子嘅鋪蓋;仲有一條舊吊褲帶、啲培根皮,同兩三隻家禽啃得好乾淨嘅骨頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們在離岩石底部最近的一條裡發現一個小凹處,裡面鋪著毯子的鋪蓋;還有一條舊吊褲帶、一些培根皮,和兩三隻家禽啃得很乾淨的骨頭。

passages.original: But there was no moneybox.
passages.vernacular: 但冇錢箱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有錢箱。

passages.original: The lads searched and researched this place, but in vain.
passages.vernacular: 小伙子哋把呢個地方搜咗又搜,但徒勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小伙子們把這個地方搜了又搜,但徒勞。

passages.original: Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說:

passages.original: “He said under the cross.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講喺十字架下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說在十字架下。

passages.original: Well, this comes nearest to being under the cross.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,呢個係最接近喺十字架下嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,這是最接近在十字架下的。

passages.original: It can’t be under the rock itself, because that sets solid on the ground.”
passages.vernacular: 唔可能喺岩石本身下面,因為佢牢牢地坐喺地上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可能在岩石本身下面,因為它牢牢地坐在地上。」

passages.original: They searched everywhere once more, and then sat down discouraged.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋又搜遍各處,然後沮喪地坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們又搜遍各處,然後沮喪地坐下。

passages.original: Huck could suggest nothing.
passages.vernacular: 哈克提不出任何建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克提不出任何建議。

passages.original: By-and-by Tom said:
passages.vernacular: 不久湯姆講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久湯姆說:

passages.original: “Lookyhere, Huck, there’s footprints and some candle-grease on the clay about one side of this rock, but not on the other sides.
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,哈克,呢塊岩石嘅一邊黏土上有腳印同啲蠟燭油,但其他邊冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,哈克,這塊岩石的一邊黏土上有腳印和一些蠟燭油,但其他邊沒有。

passages.original: Now, what’s that for?
passages.vernacular: 而家,嗰個係點解?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,那是為什麼?

passages.original: I bet you the money is under the rock.
passages.vernacular: 我打賭錢喺岩石下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打賭錢在岩石下面。

passages.original: I’m going to dig in the clay.”
passages.vernacular: 我要喺黏土裡挖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要在黏土裡挖。」

passages.original: “That ain’t no bad notion, Tom!” said Huck with animation.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個主意不壞,湯姆!」哈克興奮地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個主意不壞,湯姆!」哈克興奮地說。

passages.original: Tom’s “real Barlow” was out at once, and he had not dug four inches before he struck wood.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅「真巴洛」即刻攞出嚟,佢挖咗唔到四英寸就碰到咗木頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的「真巴洛」馬上拿出來,他挖了不到四英寸就碰到了木頭。

passages.original: “Hey, Huck!—you hear that?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,哈克!——你聽到咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,哈克!——你聽到了嗎?」

passages.original: Huck began to dig and scratch now.
passages.vernacular: 哈克而家開始挖同刮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克現在開始挖和刮。

passages.original: Some boards were soon uncovered and removed.
passages.vernacular: 幾塊木板好快被揭開、移走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾塊木板很快被揭開、移走。

passages.original: They had concealed a natural chasm which led under the rock.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋掩蓋住一道通到岩石下面嘅天然裂縫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們掩蓋著一道通到岩石下面的天然裂縫。

passages.original: Tom got into this and held his candle as far under the rock as he could, but said he could not see to the end of the rift.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆鑽進去,盡量把蠟燭伸到岩石下面,但講佢睇唔到裂縫嘅盡頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆鑽進去,盡量把蠟燭伸到岩石下面,但說他看不到裂縫的盡頭。

passages.original: He proposed to explore.
passages.vernacular: 佢提議探索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他提議探索。

passages.original: He stooped and passed under; the narrow way descended gradually.
passages.vernacular: 佢彎腰穿過;狹窄嘅路逐漸下降。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他彎腰穿過;狹窄的路逐漸下降。

passages.original: He followed its winding course, first to the right, then to the left, Huck at his heels.
passages.vernacular: 佢沿住佢嘅蜿蜒路線,先向右,再向左,哈克緊跟喺後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沿著它的蜿蜒路線,先向右,再向左,哈克緊跟在後。

passages.original: Tom turned a short curve, by-and-by, and exclaimed:
passages.vernacular: 不久湯姆轉過一個短彎,喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久湯姆轉過一個短彎,喊道:

passages.original: “My goodness, Huck, lookyhere!”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅天,哈克,睇呢度!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的天,哈克,看這裡!」

passages.original: It was the treasure-box, sure enough, occupying a snug little cavern, along with an empty powder-keg, a couple of guns in leather cases, two or three pairs of old moccasins, a leather belt, and some other rubbish well soaked with the water-drip.
passages.vernacular: 真嘅係寶箱,佔據住一個舒適嘅小洞穴,同一個空火藥桶、一對皮套裡嘅槍、兩三雙舊鹿皮靴、一條皮帶,同啲被滴水泡透嘅其他垃圾喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的是寶箱,佔據著一個舒適的小洞穴,同一個空火藥桶、一對皮套裡的槍、兩三雙舊鹿皮靴、一條皮帶,和一些被滴水泡透的其他垃圾在一起。

passages.original: “Got it at last!” said Huck, ploughing among the tarnished coins with his hand.
passages.vernacular: 「終於攞到喇!」哈克講,用手喺失去光澤嘅硬幣中摸索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「終於拿到了!」哈克說,用手在失去光澤的硬幣中摸索。

passages.original: “My, but we’re rich, Tom!”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,我哋有錢喇,湯姆!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,我們有錢了,湯姆!」

passages.original: “Huck, I always reckoned we’d get it.
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,我一直認為我哋會得到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,我一直認為我們會得到。

passages.original: It’s just too good to believe, but we have got it, sure!
passages.vernacular: 太好喇,難以相信,但我哋確實得到喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太好了,難以相信,但我們確實得到了!

passages.original: Say—let’s not fool around here.
passages.vernacular: 喂——我哋別喺呢度耽擱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂——我們別在這裡耽擱。

passages.original: Let’s snake it out.
passages.vernacular: 把佢拖出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把它拖出去。

passages.original: Lemme see if I can lift the box.”
passages.vernacular: 讓我睇我能唔能夠抬起箱子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我看我能不能抬起箱子。」

passages.original: It weighed about fifty pounds.
passages.vernacular: 佢重約五十磅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它重約五十磅。

passages.original: Tom could lift it, after an awkward fashion, but could not carry it conveniently.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆能抬起,以笨拙嘅方式,但唔能夠方便地搬運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆能抬起,以笨拙的方式,但不能方便地搬運。

passages.original: “I thought so,” he said; “They carried it like it was heavy, that day at the ha’nted house.
passages.vernacular: 「我就想係咁樣,」佢講;「嗰天喺鬧鬼嘅房子,佢哋搬佢像好重似嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就想是這樣,」他說;「那天在鬧鬼的房子,他們搬它像很重似的。

passages.original: I noticed that.
passages.vernacular: 我注意到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我注意到了。

passages.original: I reckon I was right to think of fetching the little bags along.”
passages.vernacular: 我想我想到帶小袋子係對嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我想到帶小袋子是對的。」

passages.original: The money was soon in the bags and the boys took it up to the cross rock.
passages.vernacular: 錢好快裝進咗袋子,男孩哋把佢搬到十字架岩石嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 錢很快裝進了袋子,男孩們把它搬到十字架岩石那裡。

passages.original: “Now less fetch the guns and things,” said Huck.
passages.vernacular: 「而家我哋去攞槍同嘢,」哈克講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我們去拿槍和東西,」哈克說。

passages.original: “No, Huck—leave them there.
passages.vernacular: 「不,哈克——把佢哋留喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,哈克——把它們留在那裡。

passages.original: They’re just the tricks to have when we go to robbing.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋正是我哋去搶劫時要用嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們正是我們去搶劫時要用的東西。

passages.original: We’ll keep them there all the time, and we’ll hold our orgies there, too.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一直把佢哋留喺嗰度,我哋都喺嗰度舉行我哋嘅狂歡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一直把它們留在那裡,我們也在那裡舉行我們的狂歡。

passages.original: It’s an awful snug place for orgies.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係個好舒適嘅狂歡地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是個非常舒適的狂歡地方。」

passages.original: “What orgies?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢狂歡?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼狂歡?」

passages.original: “I dono.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: But robbers always have orgies, and of course we’ve got to have them, too.
passages.vernacular: 但強盜總是有狂歡,當然我哋都得有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但強盜總是有狂歡,當然我們也得有。

passages.original: Come along, Huck, we’ve been in here a long time.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,哈克,我哋喺呢度面好久喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,哈克,我們在這裡面很久了。

passages.original: It’s getting late, I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 我想晚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想晚了。

passages.original: I’m hungry, too.
passages.vernacular: 我都餓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也餓了。

passages.original: We’ll eat and smoke when we get to the skiff.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋到咗小艇再食再抽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們到了小艇再吃再抽。」

passages.original: They presently emerged into the clump of sumach bushes, looked warily out, found the coast clear, and were soon lunching and smoking in the skiff.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不久出而家漆樹灌木叢中,小心地向外睇,發現四周無人,好快喺小艇裡食午飯抽菸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不久出現在漆樹灌木叢中,小心地向外看,發現四周無人,很快在小艇裡吃午飯抽菸。

passages.original: As the sun dipped toward the horizon they pushed out and got under way.
passages.vernacular: 太陽向地平線下沉時,佢哋撐開出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽向地平線下沉時,他們撐開出發。

passages.original: Tom skimmed up the shore through the long twilight, chatting cheerily with Huck, and landed shortly after dark.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆喺漫長嘅黃昏中沿住岸邊掠過,同哈克愉快地聊天,天黑後不久上岸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆在漫長的黃昏中沿著岸邊掠過,同哈克愉快地聊天,天黑後不久上岸。

passages.original: “Now, Huck,” said Tom, “we’ll hide the money in the loft of the widow’s woodshed, and I’ll come up in the morning and we’ll count it and divide, and then we’ll hunt up a place out in the woods for it where it will be safe.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,哈克,」湯姆講,「我哋把錢藏喺寡婦柴棚嘅閣樓裡,我早晨上嚟,我哋數一數,分一下,然後我哋到樹林裡找一個安全嘅地方放佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,哈克,」湯姆說,「我們把錢藏在寡婦柴棚的閣樓裡,我早晨上來,我們數一數,分一下,然後我們到樹林裡找一個安全的地方放它。

passages.original: Just you lay quiet here and watch the stuff till I run and hook Benny Taylor’s little wagon; I won’t be gone a minute.”
passages.vernacular: 你就喺呢度安靜地躺住睇住嘢,等我跑去偷班尼·泰勒嘅小馬車;我一分鐘就回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就在這裡安靜地躺著看著東西,等我跑去偷班尼·泰勒的小馬車;我一分鐘就回來。」

passages.original: He disappeared, and presently returned with the wagon, put the two small sacks into it, threw some old rags on top of them, and started off, dragging his cargo behind him.
passages.vernacular: 佢消失喇,不久帶住馬車回嚟,把兩個小袋子放進去,上面扔啲舊破布,出發喇,喺身後拖住佢嘅貨物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他消失了,不久帶著馬車回來,把兩個小袋子放進去,上面扔一些舊破布,出發了,在身後拖著他的貨物。

passages.original: When the boys reached the Welshman’s house, they stopped to rest.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋到咗威爾斯人家時,停下休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們到了威爾斯人家時,停下休息。

passages.original: Just as they were about to move on, the Welshman stepped out and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢哋正要繼續走時,威爾斯人走出來講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們正要繼續走時,威爾斯人走出來說:

passages.original: “Hallo, who’s that?”
passages.vernacular: 「喂,嗰個係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喂,那是誰?」

passages.original: “Huck and Tom Sawyer.”
passages.vernacular: 「哈克同湯姆·索亞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克和湯姆·索亞。」

passages.original: “Good!
Come along with me, boys, you are keeping everybody waiting.
passages.vernacular: 跟我嚟,細路哋,你哋讓大家等住呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟我來,孩子們,你們讓大家等著呢。

passages.original: Here—hurry up, trot ahead—I’ll haul the wagon for you.
passages.vernacular: 嚟——快點,小跑喺前面——我替你哋拉馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來——快點,小跑在前面——我替你們拉馬車。

passages.original: Why, it’s not as light as it might be.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,佢冇該有嘅咁輕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,它沒有該有的那麼輕。

passages.original: Got bricks in it?—or old metal?”
passages.vernacular: 裡面係磚頭嗎?——定係舊金屬?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 裡面是磚頭嗎?——還是舊金屬?」

passages.original: “Old metal,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「舊金屬,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「舊金屬,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “I judged so; the boys in this town will take more trouble and fool away more time hunting up six bits’ worth of old iron to sell to the foundry than they would to make twice the money at regular work.
passages.vernacular: 「我猜係;呢鎮上嘅男孩會花更多力氣、浪費更多時間去找六毛錢嘅舊鐵賣畀鑄造廠,而唔係正常工作賺兩倍嘅錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我猜是;這鎮上的男孩會花更多力氣、浪費更多時間去找六毛錢的舊鐵賣給鑄造廠,而不是正常工作賺兩倍的錢。

passages.original: But that’s human nature—hurry along, hurry along!”
passages.vernacular: 但嗰個係人嘅本性——快點走,快點走!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那是人的本性——快點走,快點走!」

passages.original: The boys wanted to know what the hurry was about.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋想知道急乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們想知道急什麼。

passages.original: “Never mind; you’ll see, when we get to the Widow Douglas’.”
passages.vernacular: 「別管;你哋到咗道格拉斯寡婦家就知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別管;你們到了道格拉斯寡婦家就知道。」

passages.original: Huck said with some apprehension—for he was long used to being falsely accused:
passages.vernacular: 哈克有些憂慮地講——因為佢長期習慣被誤告:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克有些憂慮地說——因為他長期習慣被誤告:

passages.original: “Mr. Jones, we haven’t been doing nothing.”
passages.vernacular: 「瓊斯先生,我哋乜嘢都冇做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瓊斯先生,我們什麼也沒做。」

passages.original: The Welshman laughed.
passages.vernacular: 威爾斯人笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威爾斯人笑了。

passages.original: “Well, I don’t know, Huck, my boy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔知道,哈克,我嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不知道,哈克,我的孩子。

passages.original: I don’t know about that.
passages.vernacular: 我對此唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對此不知道。

passages.original: Ain’t you and the widow good friends?”
passages.vernacular: 你同寡婦唔係好朋友嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你和寡婦不是好朋友嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: Well, she’s ben good friends to me, anyway.”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,佢無論如何對我係好朋友。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,她無論如何對我是好朋友。」

passages.original: “All right, then.
passages.vernacular: 「咁好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼好。

passages.original: What do you want to be afraid for?”
passages.vernacular: 你仲要害怕乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你還要害怕什麼?」

passages.original: This question was not entirely answered in Huck’s slow mind before he found himself pushed, along with Tom, into Mrs. Douglas’ drawing-room.
passages.vernacular: 呢個問題喺哈克遲緩嘅頭腦中仲冇完全得到回答,佢就發現自己同湯姆一起被推進咗道格拉斯夫人嘅客廳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個問題在哈克遲緩的頭腦中還沒完全得到回答,他就發現自己同湯姆一起被推進了道格拉斯夫人的客廳。

passages.original: Mr. Jones left the wagon near the door and followed.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯先生把馬車留喺門附近,跟進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯先生把馬車留在門附近,跟進來。

passages.original: The place was grandly lighted, and everybody that was of any consequence in the village was there.
passages.vernacular: 呢個地方燈火輝煌,村子裡所有有些地位嘅人都喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個地方燈火輝煌,村子裡所有有些地位的人都在那裡。

passages.original: The Thatchers were there, the Harpers, the Rogerses, Aunt Polly, Sid, Mary, the minister, the editor, and a great many more, and all dressed in their best.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾一家喺嗰度,哈珀一家,羅傑斯一家,波莉姨媽,希德,瑪麗,牧師,編輯,仲有許多其他人,都穿住佢哋最好嘅衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾一家在那裡,哈珀一家,羅傑斯一家,波莉姨媽,希德,瑪麗,牧師,編輯,還有許多其他人,都穿著他們最好的衣服。

passages.original: The widow received the boys as heartily as any one could well receive two such looking beings.
passages.vernacular: 寡婦熱情地接待男孩哋,像任何人接待咁樣模樣嘅兩個生物所能做到嘅一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦熱情地接待男孩們,像任何人接待這樣模樣的兩個生物所能做到的一樣。

passages.original: They were covered with clay and candle-grease.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋滿身係黏土同蠟燭油。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們滿身是黏土和蠟燭油。

passages.original: Aunt Polly blushed crimson with humiliation, and frowned and shook her head at Tom.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽羞辱得滿臉通紅,對湯姆皺眉搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽羞辱得滿臉通紅,對湯姆皺眉搖頭。

passages.original: Nobody suffered half as much as the two boys did, however.
passages.vernacular: 然而冇人比呢兩個男孩受嘅苦嘅一半多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而沒有人比這兩個男孩受的苦的一半多。

passages.original: Mr. Jones said:
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯先生講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯先生說:

passages.original: “Tom wasn’t at home, yet, so I gave him up; but I stumbled on him and Huck right at my door, and so I just brought them along in a hurry.”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆仲冇喺家,所以我放棄咗佢;但我正好喺我門口撞見佢同哈克,所以我就匆忙把佢哋帶嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆還沒在家,所以我放棄了他;但我正好在我門口撞見他和哈克,所以我就匆忙把他們帶來。」

passages.original: “And you did just right,” said the widow.
passages.vernacular: 「你做得完全對,」寡婦講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你做得完全對,」寡婦說。

passages.original: “Come with me, boys.”
passages.vernacular: 「跟我嚟,細路哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「跟我來,孩子們。」

passages.original: She took them to a bedchamber and said:
passages.vernacular: 佢帶佢哋到一間臥室講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她帶他們到一間臥室說:

passages.original: “Now wash and dress yourselves.
passages.vernacular: 「而家洗漱穿衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在洗漱穿衣。

passages.original: Here are two new suits of clothes—shirts, socks, everything complete.
passages.vernacular: 呢度有兩套新衣服——襯衫、襪子,一切齊全。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有兩套新衣服——襯衫、襪子,一切齊全。

passages.original: They’re Huck’s—no, no thanks, Huck—Mr. Jones bought one and I the other.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係哈克嘅——不,唔使謝,哈克——瓊斯先生買咗一套,我買咗另一套。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們是哈克的——不,不用謝,哈克——瓊斯先生買了一套,我買了另一套。

passages.original: But they’ll fit both of you.
passages.vernacular: 但佢哋你哋兩個都合身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但它們你們兩個都合身。

passages.original: Get into them.
passages.vernacular: 穿上佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穿上它們。

passages.original: We’ll wait—come down when you are slicked up enough.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋等——你哋收拾得夠光鮮咗就下嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們等——你們收拾得夠光鮮了就下來。」

passages.original: Then she left.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她走了。

chapters.title: Chapter XXXIV: Springing a Secret 第三十四章:揭開祕密

passages.original: CH Huck said: “Tom, we can slope, if we can find a rope.
passages.vernacular: 哈克講:「湯姆,我哋可以溜,如果能找到一根繩子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克說:「湯姆,我們可以溜,如果能找到一根繩子。

passages.original: The window ain’t high from the ground.”
passages.vernacular: 窗子離地不高。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗子離地不高。」

passages.original: “Shucks! what do you want to slope for?”
passages.vernacular: 「算喇!你點解要溜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「算了!你為什麼要溜?」

passages.original: “Well, I ain’t used to that kind of a crowd.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我不習慣嗰種人群。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不習慣那種人群。

passages.original: I can’t stand it.
passages.vernacular: 我受不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我受不了。

passages.original: I ain’t going down there, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 我不下去,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不下去,湯姆。」

passages.original: “Oh, bother!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,煩人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,煩人!

passages.original: It ain’t anything.
passages.vernacular: 嗰算不咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那算不了什麼。

passages.original: I don’t mind it a bit.
passages.vernacular: 我啲都不介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一點也不介意。

passages.original: I’ll take care of you.”
passages.vernacular: 我會照顧你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會照顧你。」

passages.original: Sid appeared.
passages.vernacular: 希德出現喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德出現了。

passages.original: “Tom,” said he, “auntie has been waiting for you all the afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,」佢講,「姨媽整個下午都喺等你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,」他說,「姨媽整個下午都在等你。

passages.original: Mary got your Sunday clothes ready, and everybody’s been fretting about you.
passages.vernacular: 瑪麗畀你準備好咗星期日嘅衣服,每個人都喺為你住急。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瑪麗給你準備好了星期日的衣服,每個人都在為你著急。

passages.original: Say—ain’t this grease and clay, on your clothes?”
passages.vernacular: 喂——你衣服上呢唔係油脂同黏土嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂——你衣服上這不是油脂和黏土嗎?」

passages.original: “Now, Mr. Siddy, you jist ’tend to your own business.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,希迪先生,你只管你自己嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,希迪先生,你只管你自己的事。

passages.original: What’s all this blowout about, anyway?”
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,呢場盛宴係點回事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,這場盛宴是怎麼回事?」

passages.original: “It’s one of the widow’s parties that she’s always having.
passages.vernacular: 「係寡婦一直喺辦嘅嗰種聚會之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是寡婦一直在辦的那種聚會之一。

passages.original: This time it’s for the Welshman and his sons, on account of that scrape they helped her out of the other night.
passages.vernacular: 呢次係為了威爾斯人同佢嘅兒子哋,因為前幾天晚上佢哋幫佢擺脫咗嗰個麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次是為了威爾斯人和他的兒子們,因為前幾天晚上他們幫她擺脫了那個麻煩。

passages.original: And say—I can tell you something, if you want to know.”
passages.vernacular: 喂——如果你想知道,我可以告訴你一件事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂——如果你想知道,我可以告訴你一件事。」

passages.original: “Well, what?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, old Mr. Jones is going to try to spring something on the people here tonight, but I overheard him tell auntie today about it, as a secret, but I reckon it’s not much of a secret now.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,老瓊斯先生今晚要喺呢度向大家宣布一件事,但我今日偷聽到佢把佢當作祕密告訴姨媽,但我想而家不算乜嘢祕密喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,老瓊斯先生今晚要在這裡向大家宣布一件事,但我今天偷聽到他把它當作祕密告訴姨媽,但我想現在不算什麼祕密了。

passages.original: Everybody knows—the widow, too, for all she tries to let on she don’t.
passages.vernacular: 每個人都知道——寡婦都係,雖然佢盡力裝作唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個人都知道——寡婦也是,雖然她盡力裝作不知道。

passages.original: Mr. Jones was bound Huck should be here—couldn’t get along with his grand secret without Huck, you know!”
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯先生一定要哈克喺呢度——佢嘅大祕密冇哈克進行不下去,你知道!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯先生一定要哈克在這裡——他的大祕密沒有哈克進行不下去,你知道!」

passages.original: “Secret about what, Sid?”
passages.vernacular: 「關於乜嘢嘅祕密,希德?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「關於什麼的祕密,希德?」

passages.original: “About Huck tracking the robbers to the widow’s.
passages.vernacular: 「關於哈克跟蹤強盜到寡婦家嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「關於哈克跟蹤強盜到寡婦家的事。

passages.original: I reckon Mr. Jones was going to make a grand time over his surprise, but I bet you it will drop pretty flat.”
passages.vernacular: 我想瓊斯先生要對佢嘅驚喜大肆慶祝一番,但我打賭佢會相當平淡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想瓊斯先生要對他的驚喜大肆慶祝一番,但我打賭它會相當平淡。」

passages.original: Sid chuckled in a very contented and satisfied way.
passages.vernacular: 希德以好滿足同得意嘅方式咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 希德以非常滿足和得意的方式咯咯笑。

passages.original: “Sid, was it you that told?”
passages.vernacular: 「希德,係你講嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「希德,是你說的嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, never mind who it was.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,別管係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,別管是誰。

passages.original: Somebody told—that’s enough.”
passages.vernacular: 有人講喇——就夠喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人說了——就夠了。」

passages.original: “Sid, there’s only one person in this town mean enough to do that, and that’s you.
passages.vernacular: 「希德,呢鎮上只有一個人卑鄙到咁樣做,嗰個就係你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「希德,這鎮上只有一個人卑鄙到這樣做,那就是你。

passages.original: If you had been in Huck’s place you’d ’a’ sneaked down the hill and never told anybody on the robbers.
passages.vernacular: 如果你喺哈克嘅位置,你會溜下山,從不告訴任何人關於強盜嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你在哈克的位置,你會溜下山,從不告訴任何人關於強盜的事。

passages.original: You can’t do any but mean things, and you can’t bear to see anybody praised for doing good ones.
passages.vernacular: 你只能做卑鄙嘅事,你受不了睇到別人因為做好事被表揚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只能做卑鄙的事,你受不了看到別人因為做好事被表揚。

passages.original: There—no thanks, as the widow says”—and Tom cuffed Sid’s ears and helped him to the door with several kicks.
passages.vernacular: 好喇——唔使謝,如寡婦所講」——湯姆打咗希德嘅耳光,踢咗佢幾腳,把佢推到門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了——不用謝,如寡婦所說」——湯姆打了希德的耳光,踢了他幾腳,把他推到門口。

passages.original: “Now go and tell auntie if you dare—and tomorrow you’ll catch it!”
passages.vernacular: 「而家去告訴姨媽,如果你敢——聽日你就挨揍!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在去告訴姨媽,如果你敢——明天你就挨揍!」

passages.original: Some minutes later the widow’s guests were at the supper-table, and a dozen children were propped up at little side-tables in the same room, after the fashion of that country and that day.
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘後,寡婦嘅客人哋坐喺餐桌旁,一打細路被安置喺同一房間嘅小邊桌旁,按當時嗰個國家嘅習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘後,寡婦的客人們坐在餐桌旁,一打孩子被安置在同一房間的小邊桌旁,按當時那個國家的習慣。

passages.original: At the proper time Mr. Jones made his little speech, in which he thanked the widow for the honor she was doing himself and his sons, but said that there was another person whose modesty—
passages.vernacular: 喺適當嘅時候,瓊斯先生發表咗佢嘅小演講,其中感謝寡婦畀佢自己同佢兒子哋嘅榮譽,但講仲有另一個人,佢嘅謙虛——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在適當的時候,瓊斯先生發表了他的小演說,其中感謝寡婦給他自己和他兒子們的榮譽,但說還有另一個人,他的謙虛——

passages.original: And so forth and so on.
passages.vernacular: 如此等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如此等等。

passages.original: He sprung his secret about Huck’s share in the adventure in the finest dramatic manner he was master of, but the surprise it occasioned was largely counterfeit and not as clamorous and effusive as it might have been under happier circumstances.
passages.vernacular: 佢以佢所擅長嘅最優秀嘅戲劇方式拋出咗佢關於哈克喺呢場冒險中嘅角色嘅祕密,但佢所引起嘅驚訝大部分係偽造嘅,並不像喺更幸運嘅環境下可能會有嘅嗰樣喧鬧同熱烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他以他所擅長的最優秀的戲劇方式拋出了他關於哈克在這場冒險中的角色的祕密,但它所引起的驚訝大部分是偽造的,並不像在更幸運的環境下可能會有的那樣喧鬧和熱烈。

passages.original: However, the widow made a pretty fair show of astonishment, and heaped so many compliments and so much gratitude upon Huck that he almost forgot the nearly intolerable discomfort of his new clothes in the entirely intolerable discomfort of being set up as a target for everybody’s gaze and everybody’s laudations.
passages.vernacular: 不過,寡婦裝出相當不錯嘅驚訝,對哈克堆咗咁多恭維同感激,以致佢幾乎忘咗新衣服幾乎無法忍受嘅不適,陷入完全無法忍受嘅不適:被樹成每個人目光同讚美嘅靶子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,寡婦裝出相當不錯的驚訝,對哈克堆了那麼多恭維和感激,以致他幾乎忘了新衣服幾乎無法忍受的不適,陷入完全無法忍受的不適:被樹成每個人目光和讚美的靶子。

passages.original: The widow said she meant to give Huck a home under her roof and have him educated; and that when she could spare the money she would start him in business in a modest way.
passages.vernacular: 寡婦講佢打算喺自己嘅屋簷下畀哈克一個家,並讓佢受教育;等佢能抽出錢時,佢要以一種謙遜嘅方式讓佢開始做生意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦說她打算在自己的屋簷下給哈克一個家,並讓他受教育;等她能抽出錢時,她要以一種謙遜的方式讓他開始做生意。

passages.original: Tom’s chance was come.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆嘅機會嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆的機會來了。

passages.original: He said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “Huck don’t need it.
passages.vernacular: 「哈克不需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克不需要。

passages.original: Huck’s rich.”
passages.vernacular: 哈克好富有。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克很富有。」

passages.original: Nothing but a heavy strain upon the good manners of the company kept back the due and proper complimentary laugh at this pleasant joke.
passages.vernacular: 只有對客人哋良好禮貌嘅沉重壓力,才阻止咗對呢個愉快嘅玩笑應有嘅恰當嘅禮貌性笑聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有對客人們良好禮貌的沉重壓力,才阻止了對這個愉快的玩笑應有的恰當的禮貌性笑聲。

passages.original: But the silence was a little awkward.
passages.vernacular: 但沉默有點尷尬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沉默有點尷尬。

passages.original: Tom broke it:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆打破咗佢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆打破了它:

passages.original: “Huck’s got money.
passages.vernacular: 「哈克有錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克有錢。

passages.original: Maybe you don’t believe it, but he’s got lots of it.
passages.vernacular: 或者你哋不相信,但佢有好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你們不相信,但他有很多。

passages.original: Oh, you needn’t smile—I reckon I can show you.
passages.vernacular: 哦,你哋唔使微笑——我想我可以畀你哋睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,你們不必微笑——我想我可以給你們看。

passages.original: You just wait a minute.”
passages.vernacular: 你哋等一分鐘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們等一分鐘。」

passages.original: Tom ran out of doors.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆跑到門外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆跑到門外。

passages.original: The company looked at each other with a perplexed interest—and inquiringly at Huck, who was tongue-tied.
passages.vernacular: 客人哋帶住困惑嘅興趣互相睇——並詢問地睇住哈克,佢講不出話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 客人們帶著困惑的興趣互相看——並詢問地看著哈克,他說不出話。

passages.original: “Sid, what ails Tom?” said Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「希德,湯姆點喇?」波莉姨媽講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「希德,湯姆怎麼了?」波莉姨媽說。

passages.original: “He—well, there ain’t ever any making of that boy out.
passages.vernacular: 「佢——嗯,嗰個細路永遠搞不明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他——嗯,那個孩子永遠搞不明白。

passages.original: I never—”
passages.vernacular: 我從冇——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒——」

passages.original: Tom entered, struggling with the weight of his sacks, and Aunt Polly did not finish her sentence.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆進嚟喇,為佢袋子嘅重量掙扎住,波莉姨媽冇講完佢嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆進來了,為他袋子的重量掙扎著,波莉姨媽沒有說完她的話。

passages.original: Tom poured the mass of yellow coin upon the table and said:
passages.vernacular: 湯姆把一堆黃色嘅錢幣倒喺桌上,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆把一堆黃色的錢幣倒在桌上,說:

passages.original: “There—what did I tell you?
passages.vernacular: 「睇——我告訴你哋乜嘢喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看——我告訴你們什麼了?

passages.original: Half of it’s Huck’s and half of it’s mine!”
passages.vernacular: 一半係哈克嘅,一半係我嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一半是哈克的,一半是我的!」

passages.original: The spectacle took the general breath away.
passages.vernacular: 呢個景象讓所有人屏住咗呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個景象讓所有人屏住了呼吸。

passages.original: All gazed, nobody spoke for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 都凝視住,片刻冇人講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 都凝視著,片刻沒有人說話。

passages.original: Then there was a unanimous call for an explanation.
passages.vernacular: 然後一致要求解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一致要求解釋。

passages.original: Tom said he could furnish it, and he did.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆講佢可以提供,佢就提供喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆說他可以提供,他就提供了。

passages.original: The tale was long, but brimful of interest.
passages.vernacular: 故事好長,但充滿趣味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 故事很長,但充滿趣味。

passages.original: There was scarcely an interruption from any one to break the charm of its flow.
passages.vernacular: 幾乎冇任何人嘅打斷嚟破壞佢流動嘅魅力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾乎沒有任何人的打斷來破壞它流動的魅力。

passages.original: When he had finished, Mr. Jones said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講完時,瓊斯先生講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說完時,瓊斯先生說:

passages.original: “I thought I had fixed up a little surprise for this occasion, but it don’t amount to anything now.
passages.vernacular: 「我以為我為呢個場合安排咗啲驚喜,但而家佢算不咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以為我為這個場合安排了一點驚喜,但現在它算不了什麼。

passages.original: This one makes it sing mighty small, I’m willing to allow.”
passages.vernacular: 我願意承認,呢個讓佢顯得小得好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我願意承認,這個讓它顯得小得很。」

passages.original: The money was counted.
passages.vernacular: 錢被數喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 錢被數了。

passages.original: The sum amounted to a little over twelve thousand dollars.
passages.vernacular: 總數略多於一萬二千元。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總數略多於一萬二千元。

passages.original: It was more than any one present had ever seen at one time before, though several persons were there who were worth considerably more than that in property.
passages.vernacular: 呢比在場任何人一次見到過嘅都多,雖然有幾個人喺嗰度嘅財產價值要多得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這比在場任何人一次見到過的都多,雖然有幾個人在那裡的財產價值要多得多。

chapters.title: Chapter XXXV: A New Order of Things 第三十五章:新的秩序

passages.original: CH The reader may rest satisfied that Tom’s and Huck’s windfall made a mighty stir in the poor little village of St. Petersburg.
passages.vernacular: 讀者可以放心,湯姆同哈克嘅意外之財喺聖彼得堡呢個可憐嘅小村子裡引起咗巨大嘅轟動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讀者可以放心,湯姆和哈克的意外之財在聖彼得堡這個可憐的小村子裡引起了巨大的轟動。

passages.original: So vast a sum, all in actual cash, seemed next to incredible.
passages.vernacular: 如此巨大嘅一筆數目,全係真金白銀嘅現金,似乎近乎難以置信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如此巨大的一筆數目,全是真金白銀的現金,似乎近乎難以置信。

passages.original: It was talked about, gloated over, glorified, until the reason of many of the citizens tottered under the strain of the unhealthy excitement.
passages.vernacular: 人哋談論佢、陶醉於佢、讚頌佢,直到許多市民嘅理智喺呢種不健康興奮嘅壓力下搖搖欲墜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們談論它、陶醉於它、讚頌它,直到許多市民的理智在這種不健康興奮的壓力下搖搖欲墜。

passages.original: Every “haunted” house in St. Petersburg and the neighboring villages was dissected, plank by plank, and its foundations dug up and ransacked for hidden treasure—and not by boys, but men—pretty grave, unromantic men, too, some of them.
passages.vernacular: 聖彼得堡同鄰近村莊每一座「鬧鬼」嘅房子都被一塊板一塊板地拆開,佢嘅地基被挖掘、搜遍,尋找隱藏嘅寶藏——而且唔係男孩哋,係男人哋——其中有些定係相當嚴肅、不浪漫嘅男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聖彼得堡和鄰近村莊每一座「鬧鬼」的房子都被一塊板一塊板地拆開,它的地基被挖掘、搜遍,尋找隱藏的寶藏——而且不是男孩們,是男人們——其中有些還是相當嚴肅、不浪漫的男人。

passages.original: Wherever Tom and Huck appeared they were courted, admired, stared at.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆同哈克無論出而家邊度,都受到奉承、欽佩、注視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆和哈克無論出現在哪裡,都受到奉承、欽佩、注視。

passages.original: The boys were not able to remember that their remarks had possessed weight before; but now their sayings were treasured and repeated; everything they did seemed somehow to be regarded as remarkable; they had evidently lost the power of doing and saying commonplace things; moreover, their past history was raked up and discovered to bear marks of conspicuous originality.
passages.vernacular: 男孩哋記不起佢哋嘅話以前有過分量;但而家佢哋嘅話被珍惜、被重複;佢哋做嘅一切似乎都被認為了不起;佢哋顯然失去咗做同講平凡事嘅能力;而且,佢哋過去嘅歷史被翻出嚟,發現帶有顯著獨創性嘅標記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩們記不起他們的話以前有過分量;但現在他們的話被珍惜、被重複;他們做的一切似乎都被認為了不起;他們顯然失去了做和說平凡事的能力;而且,他們過去的歷史被翻出來,發現帶有顯著獨創性的標記。

passages.original: The village paper published biographical sketches of the boys.
passages.vernacular: 村報發表咗呢兩個男孩嘅傳記素描。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 村報發表了這兩個男孩的傳記素描。

passages.original: The Widow Douglas put Huck’s money out at six per cent., and Judge Thatcher did the same with Tom’s at Aunt Polly’s request.
passages.vernacular: 道格拉斯寡婦把哈克嘅錢以百分之六嘅利息貸出,撒切爾法官應波莉姨媽嘅要求對湯姆嘅錢都咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 道格拉斯寡婦把哈克的錢以百分之六的利息貸出,撒切爾法官應波莉姨媽的要求對湯姆的錢也這樣做。

passages.original: Each lad had an income, now, that was simply prodigious—a dollar for every weekday in the year and half of the Sundays.
passages.vernacular: 每個小伙子而家嘅收入簡直驚人——一年每個工作日一塊錢,加上一半嘅星期日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個小伙子現在的收入簡直驚人——一年每個工作日一塊錢,加上一半的星期日。

passages.original: It was just what the minister got—no, it was what he was promised—he generally couldn’t collect it.
passages.vernacular: 呢正是牧師所得嘅——不,係佢被承諾嘅——佢通常收唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這正是牧師所得的——不,是他被承諾的——他通常收不到。

passages.original: A dollar and a quarter a week would board, lodge, and school a boy in those old simple days—and clothe him and wash him, too, for that matter.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰啲老而簡單嘅日子裡,一星期一塊兩毛五足夠供一個男孩食宿同上學——都提供衣服同洗衣,就此而言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那些老而簡單的日子裡,一星期一塊兩毛五足夠供一個男孩食宿和上學——也提供衣服和洗衣,就此而言。

passages.original: Judge Thatcher had conceived a great opinion of Tom.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾法官對湯姆有咗極高嘅評價。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾法官對湯姆有了極高的評價。

passages.original: He said that no commonplace boy would ever have got his daughter out of the cave.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,冇平凡嘅男孩能把佢女兒帶出山洞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,沒有平凡的男孩能把他女兒帶出山洞。

passages.original: When Becky told her father, in strict confidence, how Tom had taken her whipping at school, the Judge was visibly moved; and when she pleaded grace for the mighty lie which Tom had told in order to shift that whipping from her shoulders to his own, the Judge said with a fine outburst that it was a noble, a generous, a magnanimous lie—a lie that was worthy to hold up its head and march down through history breast to breast with George Washington’s lauded Truth about the hatchet!
passages.vernacular: 貝琪嚴格保密地告訴佢父親湯姆喺學校點樣替佢挨咗鞭打時,法官明顯被感動;佢為湯姆為了把嗰頓鞭打從佢肩上轉到自己肩上而講嘅巨大謊言求饒時,法官爆發出美好嘅激情講,嗰個係一個高貴嘅、慷慨嘅、寬宏大量嘅謊言——一個配得上昂起頭、同喬治·華盛頓被稱讚嘅關於斧頭嘅真話並肩走過歷史嘅謊言!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪嚴格保密地告訴她父親湯姆在學校怎樣替她挨了鞭打時,法官明顯被感動;她為湯姆為了把那頓鞭打從她肩上轉到自己肩上而說的巨大謊言求饒時,法官爆發出美好的激情說,那是一個高貴的、慷慨的、寬宏大量的謊言——一個配得上昂起頭、與喬治·華盛頓被稱讚的關於斧頭的真話並肩走過歷史的謊言!

passages.original: Becky thought her father had never looked so tall and so superb as when he walked the floor and stamped his foot and said that.
passages.vernacular: 貝琪認為佢父親從冇像喺地板上嚟回走、跺腳講嗰話時嗰樣高大同卓越。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝琪認為她父親從沒像在地板上來回走、跺腳說那話時那樣高大和卓越。

passages.original: She went straight off and told Tom about it.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻去告訴湯姆呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她馬上去告訴湯姆這件事。

passages.original: Judge Thatcher hoped to see Tom a great lawyer or a great soldier some day.
passages.vernacular: 撒切爾法官希望有一天睇到湯姆成為偉大嘅律師或偉大嘅軍人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撒切爾法官希望有一天看到湯姆成為偉大的律師或偉大的軍人。

passages.original: He said he meant to look to it that Tom should be admitted to the National Military Academy and afterward trained in the best law school in the country, in order that he might be ready for either career or both.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢打算設法讓湯姆進入國家軍事學院,然後喺全國最好嘅法學院受訓,使佢準備好走任一職業或兩者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他打算設法讓湯姆進入國家軍事學院,然後在全國最好的法學院受訓,使他準備好走任一職業或兩者。

passages.original: Huck Finn’s wealth and the fact that he was now under the Widow Douglas’ protection introduced him into society—no, dragged him into it, hurled him into it—and his sufferings were almost more than he could bear.
passages.vernacular: 哈克·費恩嘅財富同佢而家受道格拉斯寡婦保護嘅事實,把佢引進咗社會——不,係把佢拖進、扔進咗社會——佢嘅痛苦幾乎超過佢所能承受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克·費恩的財富和他現在受道格拉斯寡婦保護的事實,把他引進了社會——不,是把他拖進、扔進了社會——他的痛苦幾乎超過他所能承受。

passages.original: The widow’s servants kept him clean and neat, combed and brushed, and they bedded him nightly in unsympathetic sheets that had not one little spot or stain which he could press to his heart and know for a friend.
passages.vernacular: 寡婦嘅僕人哋讓佢保持乾淨整潔,梳頭刷衣,每晚讓佢瞓喺無情嘅床單裡,床單上冇啲小汙點或污漬,係佢可以按喺心口當作朋友嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦的僕人們讓他保持乾淨整潔,梳頭刷衣,每晚讓他睡在無情的床單裡,床單上沒有一點小汙點或污漬,是他可以按在心口當作朋友的。

passages.original: He had to eat with a knife and fork; he had to use napkin, cup, and plate; he had to learn his book, he had to go to church; he had to talk so properly that speech was become insipid in his mouth; whithersoever he turned, the bars and shackles of civilization shut him in and bound him hand and foot.
passages.vernacular: 佢必須用刀叉食飯;佢必須用餐巾、杯子同盤子;佢必須學習佢嘅書,必須去教堂;佢必須講話咁得體,以致講話喺佢嘴裡變得乏味;無論佢轉向邊度,文明嘅柵欄同枷鎖把佢關住,把佢手腳綁住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他必須用刀叉吃飯;他必須用餐巾、杯子和盤子;他必須學習他的書,必須去教堂;他必須說話那麼得體,以致說話在他嘴裡變得乏味;無論他轉向哪裡,文明的柵欄和枷鎖把他關住,把他手腳綁住。

passages.original: He bravely bore his miseries three weeks, and then one day turned up missing.
passages.vernacular: 佢勇敢地忍受咗三個星期嘅痛苦,然後有一天失蹤喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他勇敢地忍受了三個星期的痛苦,然後有一天失蹤了。

passages.original: For forty-eight hours the widow hunted for him everywhere in great distress.
passages.vernacular: 四十八小時裡,寡婦好苦惱地到處找佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四十八小時裡,寡婦非常苦惱地到處找他。

passages.original: The public were profoundly concerned; they searched high and low, they dragged the river for his body.
passages.vernacular: 公眾深深關切;佢哋上下搜尋,喺河裡打撈佢嘅屍體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公眾深深關切;他們上下搜尋,在河裡打撈他的屍體。

passages.original: Early the third morning Tom Sawyer wisely went poking among some old empty hogsheads down behind the abandoned slaughter-house, and in one of them he found the refugee.
passages.vernacular: 第三天清晨,湯姆·索亞明智地到被遺棄嘅屠宰場後面啲舊空桶裡探查,喺其中一個裡面發現咗逃亡者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第三天清晨,湯姆·索亞明智地到被遺棄的屠宰場後面一些舊空桶裡探查,在其中一個裡面發現了逃亡者。

passages.original: Huck had slept there; he had just breakfasted upon some stolen odds and ends of food, and was lying off, now, in comfort, with his pipe.
passages.vernacular: 哈克喺嗰度瞓過;佢剛食咗啲偷嚟嘅零碎食物當早飯,而家舒服地抽住菸斗躺住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克在那裡睡過;他剛吃了一些偷來的零碎食物當早飯,現在舒服地抽著菸斗躺著。

passages.original: He was unkempt, uncombed, and clad in the same old ruin of rags that had made him picturesque in the days when he was free and happy.
passages.vernacular: 佢蓬頭垢面,頭髮冇梳,穿住同樣嘅破爛舊衣,呢啲衣服喺佢自由快樂嘅日子裡使佢如畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他蓬頭垢面,頭髮沒梳,穿著同樣的破爛舊衣,這些衣服在他自由快樂的日子裡使他如畫。

passages.original: Tom routed him out, told him the trouble he had been causing, and urged him to go home.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆把佢趕出嚟,告訴佢佢引起嘅麻煩,勸佢回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆把他趕出來,告訴他他引起的麻煩,勸他回家。

passages.original: Huck’s face lost its tranquil content, and took a melancholy cast.
passages.vernacular: 哈克臉上平靜滿足嘅神情消失喇,帶上憂鬱嘅色彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克臉上平靜滿足的神情消失了,帶上憂鬱的色彩。

passages.original: He said:
passages.vernacular: 佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說:

passages.original: “Don’t talk about it, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「唔好講呢個,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別說這個,湯姆。

passages.original: I’ve tried it, and it don’t work; it don’t work, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 我試過喇,不行;不行,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我試過了,不行;不行,湯姆。

passages.original: It ain’t for me; I ain’t used to it.
passages.vernacular: 不適合我;我不習慣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不適合我;我不習慣。

passages.original: The widder’s good to me, and friendly; but I can’t stand them ways.
passages.vernacular: 寡婦對我好,友好;但我受不了嗰啲方式。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦對我好,友好;但我受不了那些方式。

passages.original: She makes me get up just at the same time every morning; she makes me wash, they comb me all to thunder; she won’t let me sleep in the woodshed; I got to wear them blamed clothes that just smothers me, Tom; they don’t seem to any air git through ’em, somehow; and they’re so rotten nice that I can’t set down, nor lay down, nor roll around anywher’s; I hain’t slid on a cellar-door for—well, it ’pears to be years; I got to go to church and sweat and sweat—I hate them ornery sermons!
passages.vernacular: 佢每天早晨讓我喺同一時間起床;佢讓我洗,佢哋把我梳得亂七八糟;佢不讓我瞓柴棚;我必須穿嗰啲該死嘅衣服,讓我窒息,湯姆;唔知怎嘅,似乎冇空氣透進去;佢哋咁要命地好,我坐不下,躺不下,邊度都唔能夠打滾;我已經——嗯,似乎好幾年冇喺地窖門上滑喇;我必須去教堂,流汗又流汗——我恨嗰啲平庸嘅講道!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她每天早晨讓我在同一時間起床;她讓我洗,他們把我梳得亂七八糟;她不讓我睡柴棚;我必須穿那些該死的衣服,讓我窒息,湯姆;不知怎的,似乎沒有空氣透進去;它們那麼要命地好,我坐不下,躺不下,哪裡也不能打滾;我已經——嗯,似乎好幾年沒有在地窖門上滑了;我必須去教堂,流汗又流汗——我恨那些平庸的講道!

passages.original: I can’t ketch a fly in there, I can’t chaw.
passages.vernacular: 我喺嗰度抓不咗蒼蠅,唔能夠嚼菸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在那裡抓不了蒼蠅,不能嚼菸。

passages.original: I got to wear shoes all Sunday.
passages.vernacular: 我整個星期日必須穿鞋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我整個星期日必須穿鞋。

passages.original: The widder eats by a bell; she goes to bed by a bell; she gits up by a bell—everything’s so awful reg’lar a body can’t stand it.”
passages.vernacular: 寡婦按鈴食飯;按鈴上床;按鈴起床——一切咁可怕地規律,一個人受不喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦按鈴吃飯;按鈴上床;按鈴起床——一切那麼可怕地規律,一個人受不了。」

passages.original: “Well, everybody does that way, Huck.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,每個人都咁樣,哈克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,每個人都這樣,哈克。」

passages.original: “Tom, it don’t make no difference.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆,冇區別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆,沒有區別。

passages.original: I ain’t everybody, and I can’t stand it.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係每個人,我受不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是每個人,我受不了。

passages.original: It’s awful to be tied up so.
