passages.vernacular: 咁樣被綁住太可怕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣被綁住太可怕了。

passages.original: And grub comes too easy—I don’t take no interest in vittles, that way.
passages.vernacular: 而且食物嚟得太容易——嗰樣我對食物不感興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且食物來得太容易——那樣我對食物不感興趣。

passages.original: I got to ask to go a-fishing; I got to ask to go in a-swimming—dern’d if I hain’t got to ask to do everything.
passages.vernacular: 我必須請求去釣魚;我必須請求去游泳——我真該死地必須請求做每件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須請求去釣魚;我必須請求去游泳——我真該死地必須請求做每件事。

passages.original: Well, I’d got to talk so nice it wasn’t no comfort—I’d got to go up in the attic and rip out awhile, every day, to git a taste in my mouth, or I’d a died, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我必須講得咁好,冇啲舒適——我必須每天到閣樓上去撕扯一陣,好嘗點嘴裡嘅味道,否則我就死喇,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我必須說得那麼好,沒有一點舒適——我必須每天到閣樓上去撕扯一陣,好嘗點嘴裡的味道,否則我就死了,湯姆。

passages.original: The widder wouldn’t let me smoke; she wouldn’t let me yell, she wouldn’t let me gape, nor stretch, nor scratch, before folks—” [Then with a spasm of special irritation and injury]—“And dad fetch it, she prayed all the time!
passages.vernacular: 寡婦不讓我抽菸;不讓我喊叫,不讓我當住人打呵欠、伸懶腰或抓癢——」[然後帶住一陣特別嘅惱怒同受傷]——「仲有真該死,佢一直禱告!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寡婦不讓我抽菸;不讓我喊叫,不讓我當著人打呵欠、伸懶腰或抓癢——」[然後帶著一陣特別的惱怒和受傷]——「還有真該死,她一直禱告!

passages.original: I never see such a woman!
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過咁樣嘅女人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過這樣的女人!

passages.original: I had to shove, Tom—I just had to.
passages.vernacular: 我只好滾蛋,湯姆——我只好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只好滾蛋,湯姆——我只好。

passages.original: And besides, that school’s going to open, and I’d a had to go to it—well, I wouldn’t stand that, Tom.
passages.vernacular: 而且,學校快要開學喇,我就得去上學喇——嗯,我唔能夠忍受嗰個,湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,學校快要開學了,我就得去上學了——嗯,我不能忍受那個,湯姆。

passages.original: Looky-here, Tom, being rich ain’t what it’s cracked up to be.
passages.vernacular: 聽住,湯姆,有錢不像吹噓嘅嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽著,湯姆,有錢不像吹噓的那樣。

passages.original: It’s just worry and worry, and sweat and sweat, and a-wishing you was dead all the time.
passages.vernacular: 只係擔心又擔心,流汗又流汗,一直希望自己死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是擔心又擔心,流汗又流汗,一直希望自己死了。

passages.original: Now these clothes suits me, and this bar’l suits me, and I ain’t ever going to shake ’em any more.
passages.vernacular: 而家呢啲衣服適合我,呢個桶適合我,我再都唔好拋棄佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在這些衣服適合我,這個桶適合我,我再也不要拋棄它們。

passages.original: Tom, I wouldn’t ever got into all this trouble if it hadn’t ’a’ been for that money; now you just take my sheer of it along with your’n, and gimme a ten-center sometimes—not many times, becuz I don’t give a dern for a thing ’thout it’s tollable hard to git—and you go and beg off for me with the widder.”
passages.vernacular: 湯姆,如果唔係嗰啲錢,我永遠唔會惹上呢一切麻煩;而家你把我嗰份同你嘅一起攞去,有時畀我好錢——唔好多次,因為我對任何嘢都不在乎,除非佢相當難得——你去替我向寡婦求情。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆,如果不是那些錢,我永遠不會惹上這一切麻煩;現在你把我那份同你的一起拿去,有時給我十分錢——不要多次,因為我對任何東西都不在乎,除非它相當難得——你去替我向寡婦求情。」

passages.original: “Oh, Huck, you know I can’t do that. ’Tain’t fair; and besides if you’ll try this thing just a while longer you’ll come to like it.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,哈克,你知道我唔能夠嗰樣做。呢不公平;而且如果你再試一陣,你會鍾意嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,哈克,你知道我不能那樣做。這不公平;而且如果你再試一陣,你會喜歡的。」

passages.original: “Like it!
passages.vernacular: 「鍾意!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喜歡!

passages.original: Yes—the way I’d like a hot stove if I was to set on it long enough.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅——就像我坐喺熱爐子上足夠長時間會鍾意佢一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的——就像我坐在熱爐子上足夠長時間會喜歡它一樣。

passages.original: No, Tom, I won’t be rich, and I won’t live in them cussed smothery houses.
passages.vernacular: 不,湯姆,我唔好有錢,唔好住喺嗰啲該死嘅悶人嘅房子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,湯姆,我不要有錢,不要住在那些該死的悶人的房子裡。

passages.original: I like the woods, and the river, and hogsheads, and I’ll stick to ’em, too.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意樹林、河同桶,我都要堅持佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡樹林、河和桶,我也要堅持它們。

passages.original: Blame it all! just as we’d got guns, and a cave, and all just fixed to rob, here this dern foolishness has got to come up and spile it all!”
passages.vernacular: 真該死!正當我哋有咗槍、山洞,一切都準備好搶劫,呢該死嘅蠢事跑出嚟破壞一切!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真該死!正當我們有了槍、山洞,一切都準備好搶劫,這該死的蠢事跑出來破壞一切!」

passages.original: Tom saw his opportunity—
passages.vernacular: 湯姆睇到咗佢嘅機會——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆看到了他的機會——

passages.original: “Lookyhere, Huck, being rich ain’t going to keep me back from turning robber.”
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,哈克,有錢唔會阻止我成為強盜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,哈克,有錢不會阻止我成為強盜。」

passages.original: “No!
passages.vernacular: 「唔會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會!

passages.original: Oh, good-licks; are you in real dead-wood earnest, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 哦,太好喇;你真嘅係認真嘅嗎,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,太好了;你真的是認真的嗎,湯姆?」

passages.original: “Just as dead earnest as I’m sitting here.
passages.vernacular: 「像我坐喺呢度一樣認真。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「像我坐在這裡一樣認真。

passages.original: But Huck, we can’t let you into the gang if you ain’t respectable, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 但係哈克,如果你不體面,我哋唔能夠讓你加入幫,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是哈克,如果你不體面,我們不能讓你加入幫,你知道。」

passages.original: Huck’s joy was quenched.
passages.vernacular: 哈克嘅喜悅被熄滅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克的喜悅被熄滅了。

passages.original: “Can’t let me in, Tom?
passages.vernacular: 「唔能夠讓我加入,湯姆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不能讓我加入,湯姆?

passages.original: Didn’t you let me go for a pirate?”
passages.vernacular: 你唔係讓我去當海盜嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不是讓我去當海盜嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, but that’s different.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,但嗰不同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,但那不同。

passages.original: A robber is more high-toned than what a pirate is—as a general thing.
passages.vernacular: 強盜通常比海盜更高貴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 強盜通常比海盜更高貴。

passages.original: In most countries they’re awful high up in the nobility—dukes and such.”
passages.vernacular: 喺大多數國家,佢哋喺貴族中地位好高——公爵之類。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在大多數國家,他們在貴族中地位非常高——公爵之類。」

passages.original: “Now, Tom, hain’t you always ben friendly to me?
passages.vernacular: 「而家,湯姆,你唔係一直對我友好嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,湯姆,你不是一直對我友好嗎?

passages.original: You wouldn’t shet me out, would you, Tom?
passages.vernacular: 你唔會把我排除喺外,對吧,湯姆?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不會把我排除在外,對吧,湯姆?

passages.original: You wouldn’t do that, now, would you, Tom?”
passages.vernacular: 你而家唔會嗰樣做,對吧,湯姆?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在不會那樣做,對吧,湯姆?」

passages.original: “Huck, I wouldn’t want to, and I don’t want to—but what would people say?
passages.vernacular: 「哈克,我唔想,我都唔願意——但人哋會講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈克,我不想,我也不願意——但人們會說什麼?

passages.original: Why, they’d say, ‘Mph!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,佢哋會講:『哼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,他們會說:『哼!

passages.original: Tom Sawyer’s Gang! pretty low characters in it!’
passages.vernacular: 湯姆·索亞幫!裡面有相當下等嘅人物!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆·索亞幫!裡面有相當下等的人物!』

passages.original: They’d mean you, Huck.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋指嘅係你,哈克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們指的是你,哈克。

passages.original: You wouldn’t like that, and I wouldn’t.”
passages.vernacular: 你不鍾意嗰樣,我都不。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不喜歡那樣,我也不。」

passages.original: Huck was silent for some time, engaged in a mental struggle.
passages.vernacular: 哈克沉默咗啲時間,進行內心嘅鬥爭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈克沉默了一些時間,進行內心的鬥爭。

passages.original: Finally he said:
passages.vernacular: 最後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後他說:

passages.original: “Well, I’ll go back to the widder for a month and tackle it and see if I can come to stand it, if you’ll let me b’long to the gang, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我回寡婦嗰度一個月,試試,睇我能唔能夠忍受,如果你讓我屬於嗰個幫,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我回寡婦那裡一個月,試試,看我能不能忍受,如果你讓我屬於那個幫,湯姆。」

passages.original: “All right, Huck, it’s a whiz!
passages.vernacular: 「好,哈克,太棒喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,哈克,太棒了!

passages.original: Come along, old chap, and I’ll ask the widow to let up on you a little, Huck.”
passages.vernacular: 嚟,老夥計,我請寡婦對你放鬆啲,哈克。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,老夥計,我請寡婦對你放鬆一點,哈克。」

passages.original: “Will you, Tom—now will you?
passages.vernacular: 「你會嗎,湯姆——你而家會嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會嗎,湯姆——你現在會嗎?

passages.original: That’s good.
passages.vernacular: 嗰好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那很好。

passages.original: If she’ll let up on some of the roughest things, I’ll smoke private and cuss private, and crowd through or bust.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢放鬆啲最粗暴嘅事,我會私下抽菸、私下罵人,擠過去,否則就崩潰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果她放鬆一些最粗暴的事,我會私下抽菸、私下罵人,擠過去,否則就崩潰。

passages.original: When you going to start the gang and turn robbers?”
passages.vernacular: 你乜嘢時候開始組幫、當強盜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你什麼時候開始組幫、當強盜?」

passages.original: “Oh, right off.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,即刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,馬上。

passages.original: We’ll get the boys together and have the initiation tonight, maybe.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋把男孩哋召集起嚟,或者今晚舉行入幫儀式。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們把男孩們召集起來,也許今晚舉行入幫儀式。」

passages.original: “Have the which?”
passages.vernacular: 「舉行乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「舉行什麼?」

passages.original: “Have the initiation.”
passages.vernacular: 「舉行入幫儀式。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「舉行入幫儀式。」

passages.original: “What’s that?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼?」

passages.original: “It’s to swear to stand by one another, and never tell the gang’s secrets, even if you’re chopped all to flinders, and kill anybody and all his family that hurts one of the gang.”
passages.vernacular: 「就係發誓互相支持,永遠不洩露幫嘅祕密,即使你被砍成碎片,殺死傷害幫中一個人嘅任何人及其全家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是發誓互相支持,永遠不洩露幫的祕密,即使你被砍成碎片,殺死傷害幫中一個人的任何人及其全家。」

passages.original: “That’s gay—that’s mighty gay, Tom, I tell you.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰好棒——真嘅好棒,湯姆,我告訴你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那很棒——真的很棒,湯姆,我告訴你。」

passages.original: “Well, I bet it is.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我打賭係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我打賭是。

passages.original: And all that swearing’s got to be done at midnight, in the lonesomest, awfulest place you can find—a ha’nted house is the best, but they’re all ripped up now.”
passages.vernacular: 所有嘅發誓都得喺午夜,喺你能找到嘅最孤獨最可怕嘅地方——鬧鬼嘅房子係最好嘅,但佢哋而家都被拆喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有的發誓都得在午夜,在你能找到的最孤獨最可怕的地方——鬧鬼的房子是最好的,但它們現在都被拆了。」

passages.original: “Well, midnight’s good, anyway, Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,無論如何午夜好,湯姆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,無論如何午夜好,湯姆。」

passages.original: “Yes, so it is.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是這樣。

passages.original: And you’ve got to swear on a coffin, and sign it with blood.”
passages.vernacular: 而且你必須喺棺材上發誓,用血簽名。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且你必須在棺材上發誓,用血簽名。」

passages.original: “Now, that’s something like!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰才像話!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那才像話!

passages.original: Why, it’s a million times bullier than pirating.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,比當海盜棒一百萬倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,比當海盜棒一百萬倍。

passages.original: I’ll stick to the widder till I rot, Tom; and if I git to be a reg’lar ripper of a robber, and everybody talking ’bout it, I reckon she’ll be proud she snaked me in out of the wet.”
passages.vernacular: 我會堅持留喺寡婦嗰度直到爛掉,湯姆;如果我成咗一個正規嘅了不起嘅強盜,人人都談論,我想佢會為把我從雨裡拉進嚟而驕傲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會堅持留在寡婦那裡直到爛掉,湯姆;如果我成了一個正規的了不起的強盜,人人都談論,我想她會為把我從雨裡拉進來而驕傲。」

chapters.title: Conclusion 結語

passages.original: CH So endeth this chronicle.
passages.vernacular: 呢部編年史就此結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這部編年史就此結束。

passages.original: It being strictly a history of a boy, it must stop here; the story could not go much further without becoming the history of a man.
passages.vernacular: 既然佢嚴格講係一個男孩嘅歷史,就必須喺呢度停止;呢個故事再往下寫,就會變成男人嘅歷史。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然它嚴格說是一個男孩的歷史,就必須在這裡停止;這個故事再往下寫,就會變成男人的歷史。

passages.original: When one writes a novel about grown people, he knows exactly where to stop—that is, with a marriage; but when he writes of juveniles, he must stop where he best can.
passages.vernacular: 寫關於成年人嘅小講時,作者確切知道喺邊度停止——都就係,以婚姻;但寫少年時,佢必須喺佢最好嘅地方停止。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寫關於成年人的小說時,作者確切知道在哪裡停止——也就是,以婚姻;但寫少年時,他必須在他最好的地方停止。

passages.original: Most of the characters that perform in this book still live, and are prosperous and happy.
passages.vernacular: 書中表演嘅大多數人物仍然活住,富裕而幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 書中表演的大多數人物仍然活著,富裕而幸福。

passages.original: Some day it may seem worth while to take up the story of the younger ones again and see what sort of men and women they turned out to be; therefore it will be wisest not to reveal any of that part of their lives at present.
passages.vernacular: 有一天,重新攞起較年輕者嘅故事、睇睇佢哋成咗乜嘢樣嘅男人同女人,或者會顯得值得;因此目前最明智嘅係不透露佢哋生活嘅嗰一部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天,重新拿起較年輕者的故事、看看他們成了什麼樣的男人和女人,也許會顯得值得;因此目前最明智的是不透露他們生活的那一部分。
